aliases: Delete all chats in this workspace
features.summary: A person can list archived chats, restore them or delete them, and can delete every chat in a workspace at once after a confirmation. Cloud deletes are soft: the chat stays in Recently deleted for 30 days and can be restored on the web. Mobile Local chats and CLI or VS Code sessions are separate, device-side stores.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person control over chats they no longer want in the sidebar. Archive hides a chat but keeps it. Delete moves it to Recently deleted, where it can be restored for 30 days. A bulk action does this to every chat in the current workspace (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/bulk/route.ts:29-31, :58-80). Mobile also has a separate wipe of Local chats on the phone (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/deleteLocalChats.ts:11-24).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need a way to clean up history and to undo a mistake. The project decision record says deleted conversations were unreachable and never purged before restore was added (doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md, row 'Restore deleted conversations'). The founder-facing product definition lists privacy controls including data deletion paths (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:817).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person on Web, Desktop (the hosted web app inside Electron), Mobile (Cloud mode and Local mode), and developers on the CLI and VS Code who manage coding sessions.
problems_solved: Clearing a whole history in one step instead of deleting chats one by one.
Recovering a chat deleted by mistake, within 30 days.
Keeping the sidebar short without losing chats (archive).
Making sure public share links die with the chat (delete revokes shares) (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/bulk/route.ts:85-103).
use_cases: On Web a person opens Settings > Privacy, chooses Delete all, reads the count and the 30-day note, and confirms.
On Mobile a person with a long Cloud history taps Delete all cloud chats and confirms twice.
A person who deleted the wrong chat opens Settings > Privacy > Recently deleted on the web and restores it.
A developer runs `agi session list --archived` to see archived local sessions.

where_to_find_it: Web (and Desktop, which shows the hosted web app): Settings > Privacy has rows 'Archived chats' (Manage), 'Recently deleted' (Manage) and the bulk rows 'Archive all chats in this workspace' and 'Delete all chats in this workspace' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:641, :671-678; apps/web/features/settings/components/BulkConversationControls.tsx:94-101). The Archived chats page has a 'Delete all archived' button (apps/web/features/settings/sections/ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:226).

Mobile: Settings data controls has a row 'Archived chats' that opens the screen titled 'Archived Chats', a 'Delete all cloud chats' button, and in Local mode a 'Delete all local chats' button under 'Local chats' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:485, :460, :524; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/archived-chats.tsx:397).

CLI: `agi session list --archived`, `agi session archive <id>`, `agi session unarchive <id>`, `agi session delete <id>` act on local session files (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1936-1938, :5588-5625, :5760-5790).

VS Code: command 'Code: Archived Sessions' opens a picker with Restore, Delete and Restore all buttons (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:267-268; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/trees/sessionPickers.ts:145-185).
Chrome extension: not available (no code found in apps/extension/src for archive or bulk delete; the brief says missing).
prerequisites: Cloud actions need a signed-in account; on Mobile the app must be in Cloud mode and Cloud must be unlocked (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/index.tsx:255-275).
Web Delete all is disabled while any chat is streaming (apps/web/features/settings/components/BulkConversationControls.tsx:79, :208-212).
Restoring from Recently deleted is only offered on the web; the Mobile copy tells the person to restore on the web (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/archived-chats.tsx:339, :369).
screens_and_controls: Web Archived chats page: heading 'Archived chats', per-row Restore and Delete buttons, 'Load more', 'Delete all archived' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:87, :176-195, :204-212, :216-226).
Web bulk rows: 'Archive all' / 'Delete all' buttons that show 'Preparing…' then 'Deleting…' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:120-128).
Web confirmation dialog titled 'Delete all chats in this workspace?' with button 'Delete all chats' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:331-337).
Mobile two-step alerts: 'Delete all chats?' then 'Are you absolutely sure?' (data-controls/index.tsx:319-345).
Mobile local alert 'Delete all local chats?' with 'This cannot be undone.' (data-controls/index.tsx:370-372).
journey: Web: open Settings > Privacy and scroll to the chat history rows.
Choose 'Delete all'. The app reads the chat count from the history stats endpoint while the button says 'Preparing…' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:241-244).

Read the dialog: it names the workspace, the number of chats, says they can be restored from Settings > Privacy > Recently deleted for 30 days, and that memories learned from them stay (BulkConversationControls.tsx:51-59).
Press 'Delete all chats'. The app posts the action, removes the rows from the sidebar store and returns to /chat (BulkConversationControls.tsx:271-287).
See the notice 'Deleted N chats.' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:296-299).
To undo: Settings > Privacy > Recently deleted > Restore on a chat (apps/web/features/settings/services/conversation-data-service.ts:133-157).
feedback_and_outputs: Web success notice 'Archived N chats.' or 'Deleted N chats.' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:290-299).

Web errors: 'Finish or stop active replies before deleting all chats.', 'The chat update could not be started. Try again.', 'We could not confirm whether your chats were updated. Check your chat history before starting another bulk action.' (BulkConversationControls.tsx:38, :305-311).
Archived list failure shows 'Archived chats could not be loaded' with the note that this is not the same as having none, plus Retry (ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:121-129).
Mobile alerts 'Chats deleted' with a count, or 'Delete outcome unknown' (data-controls/index.tsx:283-310).
settings: None of these actions is a stored setting. The related stored preference 'Start new chats temporary' is a separate feature in the same Privacy page (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:700-715 area, see comment on temporary chats).

working: Web bulk route accepts only archive_all, delete_all, delete_archived, is CSRF-protected and rate limited, and soft-deletes by setting deleted_at (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/bulk/route.ts:29-31, :36-40, :58-71).
The delete runs in one transaction that also unpublishes published artifacts and removes shared_sessions rows of the deleted chats, then releases sandboxes (route.ts:88-103, :119-131).
Single chat delete is a soft delete and also revokes shares (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:38-48, :531-558).

Restore sets deleted_at to null only inside the recovery window (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/restore/route.ts:36-50; apps/web/lib/resources/lifecycle-sql.ts:58-63). The window is 30 days (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:8, :76-82).
Web lists archived chats (archived=only) and deleted chats (deleted=only) with paging (apps/web/features/settings/services/conversation-data-service.ts:73-131).
Mobile: Archived chats list, restore, delete one, delete all archived, archive all, delete all cloud chats, all through the same endpoints (apps/mobile/src/features/archived-chats/service.ts:19-157).
Mobile Local mode: Delete all local chats removes each local conversation and its draft (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/data-controls/deleteLocalChats.ts:11-24).
CLI lists archived local sessions and can archive, unarchive and delete them (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5588-5625, :5760-5790).
VS Code: archived session picker with Restore, Delete and Restore all (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/trees/sessionPickers.ts:145-185).
incomplete: The permanent purge of chats after 30 days only runs when SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED is true; the route returns 'Soft-deleted resource purge is disabled' otherwise (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-soft-deleted-resources/route.ts:14-17, :27-30). Project documents say production does not set it (doc: docs/security/security.md:1184; docs/compliance/soc2-controls.json:652). So today deleted chats are not purged on schedule, while the privacy page says a daily job deletes them (apps/web/app/privacy/page.tsx:734).
Mobile cannot list or restore Recently deleted chats; it points to the web (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/archived-chats.tsx:339, :369).
CLI: no cloud delete-all and no cloud archived list; its archived listing is of local session files (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5588-5600).
VS Code: archived list is the local runtime's threads, not cloud chats (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/trees/conversationTreeProvider.ts:117-145). Whether its Delete is permanent is unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: The soft-delete purge cron is scheduled daily at 04:10 but switched off by default (vercel.json:86-87; route.ts:14-17).
not_available: Chrome extension: archived chats and delete all (no code found; brief says missing).
CLI: delete all chats in the account (brief says missing; no bulk command found in apps/cli/src/lib.rs).

established.statement: The user can list archived chats, restore them and delete them (web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code done; Chrome missing).
One action deletes every chat (active and archived) after confirmation, and the copy states truthfully whether they can be restored (web, desktop, mobile done; CLI, Chrome missing).
Delete all uses a soft delete: rows get deleted_at set and are kept for restore.
A deleted chat can be restored for 30 days, then it is permanently deleted with its messages and search index.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; a chat or session is archived or moved to Recently deleted rather than destroyed.

acceptance_criteria: Delete all on Web with N active and M archived chats in the workspace marks N+M rows deleted_at, returns affectedCount N+M and leaves other workspaces untouched.
After Delete all, every deleted chat appears in Recently deleted and Restore brings it back with archived and pinned state unchanged.
A chat deleted more than 30 days ago is not restorable (restore returns not found) and, once the purge flag is on, its rows are removed.
Delete all is refused or disabled while a reply is streaming and shows 'Finish or stop active replies before deleting all chats.'
Deleting a chat that has a share link makes the link stop working.
Mobile Delete all cloud chats needs two confirmations and the first one says Web can restore for 30 days.
Mobile Delete all local chats removes only Local-mode chats and says it cannot be undone.
Cancelling any confirmation changes nothing.
inferred: Desktop (Electron) behaves exactly as Web because it displays the hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5) [inferred].
The purge job should be enabled in production for the 30-day promise on the privacy page to be true [inferred from docs/security/security.md:1184 and apps/web/app/privacy/page.tsx:734].
proposed: [proposed] Show Recently deleted on Mobile so restore does not need the web.
[proposed] Add `agi chats delete-all` for cloud chats with the same confirmation and soft delete.
[proposed] Turn on SOFT_DELETED_RESOURCE_PURGE_ENABLED or change the copy until it is on.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Delete all; the browser asks the server for chat counts.
Person confirms; the browser posts {action:'delete_all'} with a CSRF token.
Server checks CSRF and rate limit, soft-deletes rows, revokes share rows and published pages in one transaction.
Server tries to release each chat's code sandbox; failures are only logged.
Browser updates its sidebar store for the chats that existed at dispatch and returns to /chat.
Restore posts to the restore route, which clears deleted_at when still inside 30 days.
Daily cron hard-deletes rows past the window, unless a legal hold covers them or the purge flag is off.
Mobile Local delete runs only against the on-device chat store; no network call.
CLI archive and delete act on session files in the user config folder.

features.summary: A person can list the public or workspace-only links they created for chats, see when each expires, copy or open them, and revoke any of them. Web, Desktop, Mobile and the CLI have this. VS Code and Chrome do not. Revoking deletes the share record so the link stops working.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the account's chat share links (title, audience, expiry) and lets the person turn a link off. On Web it also lists published pages and lets the person unpublish them (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SharedLinksSection.tsx:173; PublishedArtifactsSection.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: A share link is public to anyone who has it, so the owner needs one place to see and withdraw them. The product definition lists 'shared chats' under privacy settings (doc: docs/product/definition.md:283).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who has shared a chat, on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile and CLI.
problems_solved: Forgetting which chats were shared.
Needing to cut off access after sharing by mistake.
Seeing which links have expired.
use_cases: Web: open Settings > Shared links and press Revoke on an old link.
Mobile: open Settings > Shared Links and revoke a link, with a confirmation alert.
CLI: run `agi shares` to list and `agi shares revoke <token>`.
Deleting a chat also removes its links, so the list stays accurate.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings > Shared links (page heading 'Shared links', subtitle 'Links and pages you have shared.') (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SharedLinksSection.tsx:306-310).
Mobile: Settings > Shared Links (screen title constant 'Shared Links') (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/screenTitles.ts:3; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/shared-links.tsx:303).
CLI: `agi shares` and `agi shares revoke <token> [--yes]` (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1023-1027, :1263-1273, :7349-7378).
VS Code and Chrome: not available. Chrome can create a share link but has no list or revoke (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/shareClient.ts:11).
prerequisites: Signed in to a Cloud account on every app.
CLI uses account privacy mode and needs a connection to the account (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7350-7352).
screens_and_controls: Web rows show title, audience, 'Expires <date>' or 'Expired', with Open, Copy and Revoke buttons (SharedLinksSection.tsx:421, :105-132 relative; handleCopy at :190).

Web revoke dialog 'Revoke this public link?' with text 'Anyone using the link for “<title>” will immediately lose access. This cannot be undone.' and button 'Revoke link' (SharedLinksSection.tsx:479-497).
Mobile alert 'Revoke this link?' with button 'Revoke' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/shared-links.tsx:217-236).
CLI confirmation text 'Revoke shared link <token>? Anyone who has it can no longer open the conversation. A new share gets a new link.' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7361-7366).
journey: Open the list; the app fetches GET /api/share.
Read each link; expired ones are marked.
Press Revoke; confirm in the dialog or alert.
The app sends DELETE /api/share/<token>.
On success the row disappears and a notice says 'Revoked the link for “<title>”.' (SharedLinksSection.tsx:261).
feedback_and_outputs: Web notices 'Copied the link for “<title>”.' and 'Revoked the link for “<title>”.' (SharedLinksSection.tsx:211, :261).
Web error 'Could not confirm whether the link was revoked. Reload the list to check.' (SharedLinksSection.tsx:271).

DELETE /api/share/<token> deletes the row where token and owner match, returns 404 for anyone else, and records a share_link_revoked audit event (apps/web/app/api/share/[token]/route.ts:100-146).

not_available: VS Code: no list or revoke (no code found; brief says missing).
Chrome: no list or revoke; only creating a link exists (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/shareClient.ts).

established.statement: The user can list the chat links and published pages they shared and revoke any of them.
The list comes from the account's shares through the conversation data service.
Revoking a link stops the link working: the share row is deleted and a caller who only holds the link cannot revoke it.
Shared chats are named in the privacy settings requirements.

features.summary: A person can download a copy of their account data. On Web the server prepares a zip archive and the person downloads it; Mobile can fetch a JSON export of Cloud data and also export its own on-device data; the CLI requests and downloads the archive. Importing chat history from another assistant does not exist on any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Produces a portable copy of the person's data: on Web a zip made by a background job (one or more volumes), on Mobile a JSON file shared through the phone's share sheet, on CLI zip files saved to a folder.
purpose.why_it_exists: Data rights (GDPR and India DPDP are named in the Mobile row text) and the product definition both require a data export path (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:488; doc: docs/product/requirements.md:935).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person; Mobile local export also works without an account.
problems_solved: Leaving the product with a copy of one's data.
Answering a data-access request.
Having a backup of Local chats from the phone.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Export data; browser posts POST /api/user/export with CSRF.
Server requests an archive; if one is already preparing it returns that one.
A background job gathers the user's data into zip volumes in object storage and decides email or in-app delivery.
Browser polls archive status until ready, then links to download paths.
Mobile calls GET /api/user/export (120 s timeout), validates the document and writes a temporary JSON file.
Phone share sheet hands the file to the person's chosen app; the temp file is cleaned up.
Mobile on-device export reads local SQLite stores and writes the JSON file; no network.
CLI polls the archive status and downloads each volume to disk.

aliases: Only use models that do not train on your chats
features.summary: Switches that decide where chat content may go and what is reported. 'Only use models that do not train on your chats' limits Cloud routing. 'Use my chats' and 'Use my voice' record a choice but nothing uses it today. Crash and analytics controls differ by app. Feedback-content sharing does not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person (1) keep Cloud chats and side calls away from model providers that may train on inputs, (2) record whether AGI may use chats or voice to improve its own models, and (3) choose whether crash reports, product analytics or diagnostics leave the device.
purpose.why_it_exists: Privacy expectations and the founder's decision to record opt-in choices for a possible future own model (doc: docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:55-70). The product definition names 'help improve AGI' among privacy settings (doc: docs/product/definition.md:283).
purpose.who_uses_it: Privacy-minded people on Web, Desktop (hosted web), Mobile (Cloud mode), CLI and VS Code developers.
problems_solved: Avoiding providers whose terms allow training, especially free capacity.
Keeping error reporting opt-in.
Making sure unreadable settings fail closed.
use_cases: Turn on 'Only use models that do not train on your chats' so a Free-plan Auto chat uses a no-training model.
Leave 'Use my chats' off so a future model-improvement use has no consent.
Turn on crash reports on the CLI with `agi config set crash-reports true`.
Export a redacted diagnostics file on Chrome to attach to a support request.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings > Privacy toggles 'Share crash and error reports', 'Only use models that do not train on your chats', and under heading 'Help improve <product> models' the toggles 'Use my chats' and 'Use my voice' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:54-88).

Mobile (Cloud mode, signed in): Settings > Privacy shows the same two training switches and a 'Product analytics' switch; signed out or in Local mode it shows 'AGI Cloud privacy controls' with footnote 'Model training, routing and analytics choices apply to AGI Cloud chats.' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-privacy/PrivacyCloudControls.tsx:19-47; TrainingPreferenceGroups.tsx:42-72; ProductAnalyticsConsentGroup.tsx:29).

Mobile diagnostics: the settings row that runs 'Share diagnostics?' consent then exports (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/diagnostics/shareDiagnostics.ts:13-17; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:597-602).
CLI: config keys crash-reports and product-analytics via `agi config set` (apps/cli/src/config.rs:1473-1477, :1596-1607).

VS Code: Settings webview card 'Telemetry' with 'Share usage events' and a 'Product analytics for your account' row with a Manage button (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts:1957-1985).
Chrome: Options > 'Export diagnostics' button with 'Saves a redacted bundle to attach to a support request.' (apps/extension/src/options.ts:2073-2081).
prerequisites: Web and Mobile switches need a signed-in Cloud account and read the saved value first; switches are disabled until the latest value loads (PrivacySection.tsx:395-400).
CLI crash and analytics choices count only in managed (Cloud) privacy mode (apps/cli/src/crash_reports.rs:35-43; apps/cli/src/cloud/product_analytics.rs:21-26).
screens_and_controls: Web switches with labels above; copy under 'Only use models...' says 'On Free, this keeps your chats off free models whose terms may allow training.' (PrivacySection.tsx:64).
Web note: 'Both are off unless you turn them on. Nothing is used for this today...' (PrivacySection.tsx:88).
Mobile retry button 'Retry loading model training settings' when the read fails (TrainingPreferenceGroups.tsx:77).
journey: Open Settings > Privacy.
Wait for the switches to become enabled (value loaded).
Flip a switch; the app saves it and reloads the stored value.
See 'Your privacy setting was saved.' or 'We could not confirm whether your change was saved...' (PrivacySection.tsx:349-352).
For crash reports turned off, the browser stops reporting immediately, before the save returns (PrivacySection.tsx:323).
feedback_and_outputs: Web banner after save as above; when a pending denial exists: 'Telemetry is off on this browser. Review your account setting before choosing again.' (PrivacySection.tsx:258).

Refusals when a provider may train: 'This model's provider may train on what you send. Choose another model, or turn off Only use models that do not train on your chats in Settings > Privacy.' (apps/web/lib/server/provider-training-opt-out.ts:15-16).
settings: Stored in user_settings under namespace 'privacy', keys keepOutOfProviderTraining, allowChatsForModelImprovement, allowVoiceForModelImprovement, shareTelemetry (provider-training-opt-out.ts:12-13; apps/web/lib/server/model-improvement-consent.ts:7-13).
Browser local storage keys agi.privacy.shareTelemetry and agi.privacy.pendingTelemetryOptOut (apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts:~68-69).

working: Training opt-out is read from user_settings and enforced on side calls: embeddings, transcription, speech and media are refused when the provider may train and the person opted out (apps/web/lib/server/side-call-training-policy.ts:29-37; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/embeddings/route.ts:180; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:506; apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:106; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:429; apps/web/app/api/media/video/generate/route.ts:1165).
If the opt-out cannot be read, it is treated as opted out (side-call-training-policy.ts:14-23; request-processor.ts:3615-3626).

On the Free plan, an Auto chat is moved to a no-training model when opted out, or refused if none exists (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3664-3674; provider-training-opt-out.ts:43-53).
The model catalogue route reads the opt-out (apps/web/app/api/models/catalogue/route.ts:63).
All Web toggles default to false (PrivacySection.tsx:54-86).
Crash opt-out on Web writes a local denial first so it works even when the save fails (apps/web/lib/sentry-shared.ts:81-90; PrivacySection.tsx:323).
Mobile reads and writes the three training keys with receipt checks (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-privacy/trainingPreferences.ts:1-80).
CLI crash reports: written locally on a panic and uploaded only if managed mode and opted in (or env override) (apps/cli/src/crash_reports.rs:35-50, :220).
CLI product analytics: needs managed mode, config on, and no DISABLE_TELEMETRY or DO_NOT_TRACK (apps/cli/src/cloud/product_analytics.rs:21-26).

VS Code telemetry: off by default, and also needs VS Code's own telemetry setting on (apps/extension-vscode/src/platform/config.ts:130; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/analytics/productAnalytics.ts:37).
incomplete: 'Use my chats' and 'Use my voice' record consent only; readModelImprovementConsent has no caller in apps/web outside its own file and tests (apps/web/lib/server/model-improvement-consent.ts:22; the web note says nothing is used today, PrivacySection.tsx:88). This matches the founder decision (docs/decisions/2026-11-13-founder-decisions.md:67-70).
The 'Only use models...' choice is enforced in the Free Auto chat path and on side calls; enforcement for explicit-model chats on paid plans was not established in the code read.
CLI product analytics default is on (true), unlike the Web defaults (apps/cli/src/config.rs:85-98).
Chrome has no send toggle; diagnostics are a manual redacted export (apps/extension/src/options.ts:2071-2100).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web toggles 'rememberChats' and 'locationMetadata' were removed because nothing read them (apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx:33-42).
'improveModelTraining' is retired and never reused (PrivacySection.tsx:39-42).
not_available: Feedback-content sharing choice (S85.13): not applicable on any app per brief; no control found.

steps.what_happens: Person flips a switch; the app saves the key in the privacy namespace of user_settings.
For crash reports off, the browser first writes a local denial flag and stops reporting.
On a chat turn the server reads the opt-out; unreadable means opted out.
For Free Auto turns the route swaps to a no-training model or refuses.
For a side call (embeddings, transcription, speech, media) the route checks the provider; no-training providers are always allowed, others only if not opted out.
The request then goes to the provider chosen by routing.
CLI on panic writes a small local report; on next start it uploads only when allowed.

features.summary: Controls which websites AGI may read or act in. In the Chrome extension a site must be on the person's approved list and have Chrome host permission before the assistant acts. On Desktop the person can unpair the Chrome extension, and manage allowed and blocked sites for the built-in browser pane.

purpose.what_it_does: Chrome Options keeps a list of approved sites; removing one revokes browser-control consent and Chrome's host permission for it (apps/extension/src/options.ts:1451-1478). Desktop shows the pairing between this Mac and the Chrome extension and can unpair it (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPairingSection.tsx). Desktop also keeps allowed and blocked site lists for its browser pane (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/BrowserPaneSettings.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: An assistant that can click and type on websites needs the person's explicit, revocable permission, site by site. The brief asks that the person controls which websites the assistant may read or act in and can revoke it.
purpose.who_uses_it: People using the Chrome extension or the Desktop app's browser tools.
problems_solved: Preventing action on sites the person did not approve.
Cutting off the Desktop-to-Chrome link.
Removing browser-pane approvals and blocking sites.

Press the x next to a site to revoke browser control.
On Desktop open Settings > Capabilities > Chrome and press Unpair.

features.summary: Mobile can wipe all chats, memory, settings and downloaded models stored on the phone, and sign out. Desktop has storage clean-up buttons and a Clear browsing data button for its browser pane, but no full wipe. CLI and VS Code have no wipe. Connected sources, location use, voice retention and reset personalization are not offered.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person a way to remove data the app keeps on this device. On Mobile that means everything local (apps/mobile/services/dsarExport.ts:431-472). On Desktop it means selected caches and the browser pane's cookies (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/StorageSettings.tsx:57-90; BrowserPaneSettings.tsx:39-47).
purpose.why_it_exists: Data rights and device hygiene: a person selling or handing over a phone should be able to erase local data. The row text on Mobile names GDPR and DPDP (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:488).
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users (Local and Cloud), Desktop users who want to free space or clear browser sign-ins.
problems_solved: Erasing local chats, memory, models and keys from a phone.
Freeing disk space on Desktop.
Signing out of every site in the Desktop browser pane.

Mobile Local mode: delete only local chats.
Desktop: clear web cache or old logs.

Desktop: Settings 'Storage' with 'Clean up' rows (Web cache, Old logs, Old archived sessions, Temporary command files) (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/StorageSettings.tsx:23-90; apps/web/features/settings/components/WebSettingsModal.tsx:254).
Desktop: Settings 'Browser' > 'Browsing data' > 'Clear browsing data' (BrowserPaneSettings.tsx:38-47).
CLI, VS Code, Web, Chrome: no device wipe (brief; none found).
prerequisites: Mobile wipe needs no account. It signs out all accounts as part of the wipe (dsarExport.ts:433-436).
Delete all local chats works only in Local mode (data-controls/index.tsx:366).

An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.
Mobile local wipe signs out all accounts, withdraws provider sharing, then deletes local rows in a transaction.

acceptance_criteria: After Delete everything on Mobile, no conversations, memory, instructions, settings or models remain on the phone.
The wipe requires two confirmations and the first says it cannot be undone.
The wipe signs the person out of every account.
If the wipe fails midway, the app says so and does not report success.
Delete all local chats leaves memory, settings, projects and downloaded models in place.
Desktop Clear browsing data asks first and says sign-ins are lost.
No app shows a control for location, connected sources, voice retention or reset personalization.
inferred: A Desktop wipe, if built, should reuse the confirm pattern of StorageSettings [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a Desktop 'Delete local data' that covers chats, memory and settings with the same two-step confirmation.
[proposed] Add `agi data wipe` to the CLI that removes sessions and config after confirmation, moving files to Trash first as AGENTS.md section 9 requires.

aliases: Add or remove a sign-in method
features.summary: Settings, Security on web (and desktop, which shows the web page) lists every way the account can sign in, lets the person remove one, and changes the password. Removal and some password changes need a fresh re-check. The phone lists methods and changes the password but sends add and remove to the web.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows the email address, the password state, passkeys, connected social accounts and other linked sign-in identities of the account. Lets the person connect or disconnect a social account, remove a linked identity, and set or change the password. A password change signs out every other session and device credential.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to see and control every door into the account, and to cut off a method they no longer trust. The brief states the requirement: see every way to sign in and add or remove methods; change the password with the current password or a recent re-check (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.01 and S86.02).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in account holder using the Web app, the Desktop app (which shows the hosted web screens) or the Mobile app in Cloud mode.
problems_solved: Not knowing which sign-in methods can reach the account.
Removing a method that was lost or is no longer trusted.
Locking oneself out by removing the last method (blocked by the server).
A stolen password staying useful on other devices after it is changed (other sessions and device credentials are ended).
use_cases: After losing access to a social account, the person removes that linked identity.
The person sets a password on an account that only had social sign-in.
The person suspects the password leaked, changes it, and every other device is signed out.
On the phone the person reviews which methods exist and opens the web page to add one.

established.statement: The user can see every way they can sign in (password, passkeys, social/SSO identities) and add or remove methods.
The user can change their password with the current password or a recent re-authentication, and reset a forgotten one.
The last sign-in method and the primary sign-in method cannot be removed.
Removing a method needs a re-check no older than 300 seconds.
With a password set and no second factor the current password is enough; otherwise a recent re-check is also needed.
After a password change every other session and device credential is ended; if that partly fails the person gets a 503 message.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: Every identity of the account appears on Security with an added date and a last-used date or 'Not used yet'.
Removing the only remaining identity returns the 'only way left to sign in' message and nothing is deleted.
Removing the primary identity returns the 'registered under' message.
Removing a removable identity asks for confirmation, then a re-check older than 300 seconds triggers the step-up prompt, then the row disappears and an identity_unlinked notice is sent.
A new password shorter than 8 characters is refused; a wrong current password gives 'Your current password is not correct.'.
After a successful password change the other sessions in the session list are gone and device credentials are revoked.
On the phone the 'Add or remove a sign-in method' row opens the web Security page.
inferred: [inferred] A removed linked identity should also stop working for sign-in at once; the server deletes the mapping row and clears the identity cache (identities/route.ts:99).
[inferred] The Desktop app has no separate code for this; it shows the web screens (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
proposed: [proposed] Show last-used time on the Email and Password rows too.
[proposed] Let the phone remove a linked identity in the app with the same step-up used for sessions.

steps.what_happens: The web page loads the identity list and provider list from the server.
The person presses Remove and confirms; the browser sends DELETE with a CSRF token and an optional step-up token.
The server checks CSRF, rate limit, input shape, then step-up, then runs the locked delete that refuses the last or primary identity.
The server clears the identity cache and emits the identity_unlinked event, which audits and notifies the holder.
Connect and Disconnect of a social account run through the identity provider's own client library in the browser.

features.summary: Passkeys let the person sign in with the device unlock instead of a password. On web and desktop the Security page can add, rename and remove passkeys through the identity provider. The phone lists passkeys and security keys and can remove keys of Advanced Account Security, but adding happens on the web.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the account's passkeys with added and last-used dates, adds a new passkey, renames one (1 to 50 characters) and removes one after a confirmation.
purpose.why_it_exists: Passkeys resist phishing better than passwords. The brief requires that the user can add, see, rename and remove passkeys (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any account holder with a browser that supports passkeys; phone users who want to review or remove keys.
problems_solved: Passwords that can be phished or reused.
Not knowing which devices hold a passkey.
A lost device whose passkey must be removed.
use_cases: Add a passkey on a laptop, then sign in with fingerprint.
Rename 'Passkey' to 'Work laptop'.
Remove the passkey of a lost phone.
On the phone, review the passkey and security key list.

where_to_find_it: Web and Desktop: Settings, Security, panel 'Passkeys' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx:246).
Mobile (Cloud mode only): Account security, row 'Passkeys and security keys' opening a page of the same title (account-security/PasskeysSection.tsx:25, index.tsx:637-650).

Web: a browser that supports passkeys; otherwise the panel says 'This browser cannot create passkeys. Use a browser with passkey support to add one.' (PasskeysPanel.tsx:365-366).

screens_and_controls: Web: button 'Add a passkey'; per row a rename control and 'Remove' (PasskeysPanel.tsx:350-495).

Remove dialog: 'Remove <name>?' with 'You will no longer be able to sign in with this passkey on any device that synced it. You can add it again later.' and button 'Remove passkey' (PasskeysPanel.tsx:307-310).
Mobile: list of keys (kind label 'Passkey' or 'Security key'), 'Remove' per Advanced Account Security key, row 'Add a passkey or security key' (value 'Web') (PasskeysSection.tsx:195-250).
journey: Open Settings, Security, Passkeys.
Press 'Add a passkey'; the browser shows its own passkey prompt; confirm with fingerprint, face or PIN.
The list reloads with 'Added <date> · Not used yet'.
To rename, use the rename control, type a name, save.
To remove, press 'Remove', confirm.

Errors: 'This passkey could not be changed.' and the uncertain-outcome text 'The passkey change outcome could not be confirmed...' (PasskeysPanel.tsx:49, 262).

established.statement: The user can add, see, rename and remove passkeys for their account.

features.summary: Two-step sign-in adds a code from an authenticator app at every sign-in. Backup codes are one-time spares. The switch AGI_AUTHENTICATOR_ENROLLMENT must be 1 for setup and backup codes; turning off or regenerating needs a recent re-check. Available on web, desktop and phone.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the account holder start authenticator setup, confirm it with a 6-digit code, receive one-time backup codes, replace those codes, and turn two-factor off. A workspace may require two-factor from its members.
purpose.why_it_exists: A password alone is weak. The brief requires a second factor that can be turned on and off, and recovery codes that can be viewed, downloaded and regenerated (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.04 and S86.05).
purpose.who_uses_it: Account holders; workspace admins who require two-factor for members.
problems_solved: Stolen passwords.
Losing the authenticator app (backup codes).

Setup: step-up two_factor.enable, refuses when already enrolled, creates a secret sealed with an envelope, stores a pending row in user_two_factor and returns secret and otpauth_url (setup/route.ts:28-86).

features.summary: An optional stricter mode. After at least two passkeys or security keys, saved recovery keys, an emailed code and a passkey confirmation, every sign-in needs a passkey or security key and email recovery stops. Turning on signs out other devices. It is managed on web and desktop; the phone only opens the web page.

purpose.what_it_does: Enrolls the account into a mode where sessions and device credentials must prove themselves with a passkey or security key, issues ten one-time recovery keys with a 48-hour recovery wait, emails an undo link valid 48 hours, and turns the mode off on request.
purpose.why_it_exists: People at higher risk need protection that survives a hijacked email or password. The brief requires a hardened mode that tightens account security beyond defaults (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.26).
purpose.who_uses_it: Individual account holders at higher risk. Not available to accounts managed by an organization or on a domain an organization verified.
problems_solved: Account takeover through email or password reset.
Stolen refresh credentials on linked devices.
Unattended recovery by an attacker (48-hour hold).
use_cases: A journalist enrolls with two security keys.
After losing a key the person starts recovery with a recovery key and completes it 48 hours later.
An attacker enrolled the account; the owner follows the emailed link to turn it off within 48 hours.
A passkey-required refusal appears in an app and the person verifies with a passkey.

Sign-out of every other session and device credential at enrollment, and denial of pending device codes (service.ts:595-619).

Turn off with a passkey assertion (service.ts:764-780; enrollment/route.ts:55-72).

established.statement: The user can turn on a hardened mode that tightens account and agent security beyond defaults.
Enrollment needs at least two passkeys or security keys including one that works across devices.
Turning on signs out every other session and device credential and emails an undo link valid 48 hours.
Recovery starts with a recovery key and unlocks after 48 hours.
Undo cleanup runs under a 120-second lease and a partial cleanup asks the person to open the link again.
Not available to organization-managed or verified-domain accounts.

acceptance_criteria: With one passkey, enrollment is refused with 'Add at least 2 passkeys or security keys...'.

Turning off with a valid passkey assertion clears enrollment; with no assertion it fails.
Opening the undo link twice after success returns the 'expired or already used' message.
An organization-managed account gets 'not available for an account your organization manages'.

steps.what_happens: The person adds keys, generates recovery keys and requests an email code.
The browser creates a passkey assertion with the browser's WebAuthn prompt.
The server re-checks step-up, availability, key count and email, consumes the assertion and the code, promotes the recovery keys and arms the undo link in one transaction.
The server revokes device refresh credentials, denies approved device codes, ends other identity sessions, marks this session verified and emails the undo link.
On later requests the API gate checks enrollment and per-session verification; unverified sessions get PASSKEY_REQUIRED.
The email message is sent by the notification service.

data.synced: Server only; a cache of enrollment (300 s) and session verification lives in the key-value store
data.retained_or_deleted: Undo link 48 h; verification up to 7 days or the session lifetime; recovery hold 48 h (contract file).

features.summary: Lists the account's signed-in sessions with device, place and times, ends one, ends all (needs a re-check), and signs out this device. Full on web, desktop and phone. The CLI, VS Code and Chrome can only sign out their own device and cannot list or end other sessions.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows each active session with device, OS, browser, place and times, with the current one first. Ends a single session, ends every session and device credential, and signs out the current device on each app.
purpose.why_it_exists: If a device is lost or a login looks wrong, the person must be able to cut it off. The brief requires seeing sessions (device, place, last active) and ending any, signing out the current device, and one action to sign out everywhere (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.06, S86.09, S86.10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in account holder on any app.
problems_solved: A forgotten login on a shared computer.
A suspected account compromise.
Old sessions living beyond the account lifetime policy.
use_cases: Revoke one unknown session.
Use 'Log out of all devices' after a lost phone.
Sign out of the CLI on a shared machine.
Sign out of the Chrome extension and clear the saved autofill profile.

features.summary: Settings, Account, Linked devices lists the CLI, VS Code, Chrome, desktop and phone linked to the account, renames them and unlinks them, which revokes their credentials. The Desktop app also pairs with the Chrome extension and a phone. The phone's pairing screen is switched off in the current build.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows every app linked to the account with state (Signed in or Signed out), last seen and capabilities; renames or unlinks a device and revokes its credential, sessions and mobile tokens. On Desktop, pairs and unpairs the Chrome extension, and connects or disconnects a phone for Remote Control.
purpose.why_it_exists: A lost or retired device must lose access. The brief requires seeing trusted or linked devices and removing trust, and seeing devices paired for remote use and unpairing them (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/086-security-and-connected-access-settings.md, S86.07 and S86.08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Account holders who sign in from the CLI, VS Code, Chrome, desktop or phone; Desktop users who drive a browser or phone remotely.
problems_solved: A lost laptop still holding a credential.
Not knowing which apps are signed in.
Leftover pairing of a browser or phone to a desktop.
use_cases: Unlink a retired laptop's CLI.
Rename 'Mac' to 'Office Mac'.
Unpair Chrome from the Mac.
Disconnect a phone from Remote Control.

steps.what_happens: The panel fetches the device list; the server unions three queries for the user and caps at 200.
Unlink: CSRF and rate limit, validate uuid and options, tell the device and live sessions to drop remote work, then in one transaction revoke refresh credentials and delete registration rows.
The server ends the device's identity session, writes audit events device_trust_revoked and session_revoked, and notifies the holder.
The device discovers the revocation the next time it connects and signs out.
Desktop Chrome pairing: the extension submits a code to a local bridge on the Mac; unpair clears the pairing and uninstalls the native host manifest.
Phone pairing for Remote Control uses a code scanned on the phone and a relay service; relay not traced.

features.summary: AGI tells the signed-in person, in the app and by email, when something security-related happens on the account: a new sign-in, a password change, a two-factor change, replaced backup codes and similar. The person can stop the emails in Settings, Notifications, unless Advanced Account Security is on. Built on web (and the web screens shown in Desktop).

purpose.what_it_does: When a security-relevant act happens, the server records an in-app notification with a link into Settings and, if email is allowed and configured, sends a plain email with the same text. One catalogue defines the title, message, severity and the Settings section each notice opens (apps/web/lib/services/identity-events/catalogue.ts:4-32, 49-60).
purpose.why_it_exists: So an account holder can spot a takeover quickly. Each notice says what to do if the act was not theirs (apps/web/lib/services/identity-events/catalogue.ts:47). The product requires every surface to make trust boundaries knowable (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 4.4).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in account holder on web and Desktop (Desktop shows the hosted web app). Account holders with Advanced Account Security cannot turn email notices off in effect.
problems_solved: A person does not notice a stranger signing in.
A password or two-factor change made by an attacker goes unseen.
A person wants fewer emails but still wants in-app alerts.
use_cases: Someone signs in on a new browser; within minutes the owner sees 'A new sign-in to your account' in the app and gets an email.
The owner changes their password; a 'Your password was changed' notice appears and is emailed.
The owner regenerates backup codes; a notice says the old codes no longer work.
The owner switches Security alerts email to Off; later notices still show in the app.

Notices appear in the notification bell on web (apps/web/features/notifications/components/NotificationBell.tsx) and each opens a Settings section (apps/web/lib/services/account-activity-notifications.ts:47).

For emails: the server needs RESEND_API_KEY and AGI_NOTIFICATIONS_FROM_EMAIL set (names only) (apps/web/lib/services/notification-email-service.ts:10-15).

Advanced Account Security needs email.' (NotificationsSection.tsx:66-72).
One select per row with options Off and Email (NotificationsSection.tsx:98-115).

working: Catalogue of 27 security notice kinds with title, message, severity, settings section and audit type (apps/web/lib/services/identity-events/catalogue.ts:4-32).

New-sign-in notice: first sighting of a session younger than 15 minutes raises new_sign_in once per session across processes using a key-value claim (apps/web/lib/server/session-sightings.ts:14, 23-47); called from the auth layer (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:199, 478, 520).

Password change and backup-code regeneration announce a change after the change succeeds (apps/web/app/api/settings/password/route.ts:98-105; apps/web/app/api/settings/2fa/backup-codes/route.ts:65-72) through announceTwoFactorChange (apps/web/lib/server/two-factor-security-events.ts:26-36).
Each notice is stored once per dedupe key and emailed only when newly stored (account-activity-notifications.ts:33-54; apps/web/lib/services/notification-service.ts:58-96).
Email is skipped when the person opted out unless enrolled in Advanced Account Security (account-activity-notifications.ts:75-96).
Notification failure never stops the audit write (apps/web/lib/services/identity-events/index.ts:68-77).
Device sign-in approval and account-compromise containment record in-app notices (account-activity-notifications.ts:98-139).
incomplete: Nine catalogued notices are raised by nothing: new_device, new_location, passkey_added, passkey_removed, api_key_created, api_key_revoked, identity_linked, sso_connection_changed, account_deletion_scheduled (apps/web/lib/server/__tests__/security-event-coverage.test.ts:56-66).
The device-approval and compromise-containment notices are in-app only; no email is sent for them (account-activity-notifications.ts:98-139).
Email is silently not delivered when the transport variables are not set; the result is 'not_configured' and nothing is logged as a failure (notification-email-service.ts:145-151, 168).

established.statement: The user is told about security-relevant events (new sign-in, password or 2FA change, new device) and can control how.
A new-sign-in notice is sent the first time a session is seen, if it started within the last 15 minutes.
Password and two-step changes send a change notice.
Each notice is recorded once per dedupe key, then emailed.
Email is skipped when the person has opted out, unless Advanced Account Security is on.
A failed preference lookup logs a warning and sends no email.
Every surface must make trust boundaries knowable to the person.

acceptance_criteria: After signing in on a new session younger than 15 minutes, exactly one 'A new sign-in to your account' notice appears, and a second request on the same session creates no second notice.
Changing the password creates one 'Your password was changed' notice and, with email on, one email whose subject is that title.
With Security alerts set to Off and no Advanced Account Security, a security act creates the in-app notice and no email.
With Advanced Account Security enrolled and the preference Off, the email is still sent.
A session older than 15 minutes seen for the first time creates no notice.
If the preference lookup throws, the in-app notice exists, no email is sent and a warning is logged.
Replaying the same event with the same reference creates no duplicate notice or email.
inferred: [inferred] Because dedupe is per user, event and reference, two real password changes only produce two notices if each carries its own reference; the emit function generates a random reference when none is passed (identity-events/index.ts:72).
[inferred] The 15-minute window means a long-lived session first seen later does not alert.
proposed: [proposed] Raise the nine unraised notices or remove them from the catalogue so the promise matches the behaviour.
[proposed] Show on the Security alerts row that email cannot be turned off under Advanced Account Security, instead of only in Delivery details.
[proposed] Email the device-approval and compromise notices, or state why they are in-app only.

steps.what_happens: A request arrives with a session; the auth layer calls noteSessionSighting and the work runs after the response.
The identity provider is asked when the session started; older than 15 minutes means no notice; otherwise a key-value claim with a session-lifetime expiry decides whether this is the first sighting.
emitIdentitySecurityEvent records a risk observation, tries the notice, then writes an audit record.
The notice is inserted in public.notifications with a dedupe key identity:<event>:<ref>; a duplicate stops the flow.
The profile email and the opt-out are read; Advanced Account Security enrolment overrides an opt-out.
The email is sent through the email transport with an idempotency key.
The person opens the bell or the email link and lands in Settings.

steps.what_happens: The surface calls GET /api/connectors with the session.
The server reads active connections, OAuth grant summaries (with granted scopes) and custom connectors and returns them with grantedPermissions sentences.
The person presses Disconnect; web sends DELETE /api/connectors?connectorId= with a CSRF token.
The server checks CSRF, rate limit and workspace access, cancels pending authorizations, captures and revokes stored tokens.
Tokens are revoked at the third-party vendor when possible.
Saved tool permissions are cleared and a connector_removed audit event is written.
The response carries success and an optional vendor notice, which the surface shows.

features.summary: A developer on a paid plan creates a key for AGI's public API, picks what it may do, sees it masked afterwards and revokes it. Web and Desktop create, list and delete; the CLI lists and revokes but sends creation to the browser. Personal access tokens do not exist.

steps.what_happens: The person fills the New Key dialog and submits; the browser sends POST /api/settings/api-keys with CSRF.
The server validates, resolves the entitled plan tier, checks project and the 20-key cap.
A step-up check requires recent sign-in proof, then rate limit api-keys-create applies.
A key is generated; only its hash and prefix are stored; the raw key is returned once with HTTP 201.
Audit event and developer webhook event are written.
Revoke: DELETE with CSRF and rate limit api-keys-delete; owner check; revoked_at set.
A caller of the public API sends the key; the server checks format, hash, expiry, revocation and scope.

features.summary: Sets how much the agent asks before acting, with per-tool Allow, Ask or Deny choices that win over the default. The default is saved on the account, enforced on every cloud turn and resume, and capped by workspace policy. Saved per-tool choices can be reviewed and removed. There is no single withdraw-everything action.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores an account default of ask every time, auto-approve read-only, or skip approvals, plus per-tool verdicts for each connector, and applies both when the agent wants to run a tool (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:48-70; apps/web/app/api/connectors/permissions/route.ts:30-34).
purpose.why_it_exists: Agents can read, send and delete things in other services. The person decides how much to trust them. The product requires approval prompts for connector writes, computer use and similar actions (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who lets the agent use tools: web, Desktop, phone, CLI, VS Code, Chrome.
problems_solved: Being asked about every harmless read.
An agent deleting or sending something irreversible without asking.
A member skipping a workspace's approval rules.
use_cases: Choose 'Run read-only actions without asking' so searches run but writes still ask.
Set a connector tool to Deny so it never runs.
Try to give 'Always' to a delete tool and be told it will always ask.
Reset all permissions for one connector.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Capabilities, section 'Tool approvals' with three radio options; above it Local access and below it Approval history (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:213-219; apps/web/features/settings/components/ToolApprovalDefaultsPanel.tsx:92-153).

Web: Settings, Connectors, open a connector, 'Tool permissions' (apps/web/features/connectors/hooks/useConnectorsSettingsAdapter.tsx:95, 1245-1253). Each tool shows Allow, Ask or Deny; the draft names (Always allow, Needs approval, Blocked) are database values, not button labels (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:64-92).
Desktop: the same hosted web Settings; the Desktop runtime has its own permission decisions (see F086-11).
Phone: Settings, 'Action approvals' with the three options, 'Recommended' on the ask option, and an approval history (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/auto-approve.tsx:30-80).
CLI: during first-run setup 'Default permission mode' offers Default, Auto, Plan (apps/cli/src/onboarding.rs:737-772, 960-969); an organization policy can pin it.
VS Code: a local runtime permissionMode of ask, auto, plan or bypass exists in its protocol (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:978); UI control not opened.
Chrome: an approval policy lists always-ask reasons (apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/approvalPolicy.ts:1-20); the default-mode control was not opened.

Skip approvals is offered only when no workspace the person belongs to forbids it (tool-approval-policy.ts:34-44, 74-88).
Per-tool choices need a connected connector.

Heading 'Tool approvals', helper 'Default for tool actions. Per-tool choices in Connectors win.' (ToolApprovalDefaultsPanel.tsx:101-108).

established.statement: The user can review the approvals they chose to remember and remove any of them.
The user can set the default approval posture (ask every time, auto-approve safe, autonomous) and it is enforced.
One action withdrawing every optional grant is not applicable.
The default is saved in account settings and read on each turn and on resume.
If the default cannot be read, the agent asks before every action.
Skip approvals is offered only where the workspace allows it; a member cannot skip by switching workspace.
A critical tool cannot get a standing allow; the server answers 422 critical_tool_always_asks.
Removing a per-tool rule advances a generation and revokes that connector's session grants in the same transaction.
Approval prompts show action, target, tool, risk, scope and choices.

acceptance_criteria: Changing the default on web is visible on the phone in Cloud mode and applies to the next agent turn.
With Ask before every action, a read tool waits for approval.
With read-only auto-approve, a read tool runs and a write tool asks.
A member of a workspace that forbids Skip approvals sees that option disabled with the workspace note and the runtime acts as ask every time.
Setting Allow on a critical tool returns 422 critical_tool_always_asks and stores nothing.
Resetting a connector's permissions removes its saved verdicts and revokes in-conversation grants.
Making the default unreadable (database error) leads to approval being required.
A Deny verdict blocks a tool even under Skip approvals.
inferred: [inferred] The cloud default of Skip approvals for a never-set account conflicts with the fail-closed principle in AGENTS.md section 6; it may be intended or not, so it needs a decision.
[inferred] Lockdown mode (a separate panel) can force gating regardless of the policy (hostedToolRunsUnasked takes lockedDown, tool-approval-policy.ts:26-32).
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether a never-configured account should start on Ask; if so change CLOUD_ACCOUNT_DEFAULT_TOOL_APPROVAL_POLICY and its tests.
[proposed] Show one 'Saved approvals' list per surface with the same wording.
[proposed] Map CLI and VS Code modes to the three account policies in one shared table.

steps.what_happens: The person picks a default; the page saves namespace tool-approvals to the account and optimistically updates, restoring on failure.
On every chat turn and on resume the server reads user_settings and resolves the policy against every organization the person belongs to.
Per-tool verdicts for the connector are loaded for the model if it supports tools.
The tool loop runs, asks, or refuses per policy; critical tools always ask.
Removing a verdict runs one transaction: bump generation, revoke session grants, delete rows; then an audit event.
On the phone in Local mode the choice is stored on the device and no server call is made.
In the CLI the mode is written to the local config file.

aliases: Local folders, websites, apps, clipboard and screen
features.summary: Controls what AGI may use on the person's own computer. Desktop lists approved folders, remembered answers (apps, clipboard) and system permission status; Chrome keeps an approved-sites list backed by real browser host permission; the CLI limits file reach to the folder it runs in plus added folders. Screen access has no dedicated preference.

purpose.what_it_does: Asks before the agent touches an app, reads the clipboard through copy and paste keys, or uses a folder, remembers the answer for this session or for good, and lets the person review and remove it. Desktop also shows the status of operating-system permissions (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/permissionManager.ts:107-189, 299-313; apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:195-235).
purpose.why_it_exists: An agent that can click and type on a person's computer can reach anything signed in. The person must decide, and be able to take it back (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.7).
purpose.who_uses_it: People using Desktop computer use or folders, the Chrome extension on sites, and the CLI in terminals.
problems_solved: The agent controlling an app the person did not intend.
Silent clipboard reads.
Unclear why screen capture fails on macOS.
Chrome access to sites the person never approved.
use_cases: Allow the agent to control one app for this session, and refuse another app for good.
Remove a remembered 'Always allowed' answer so Desktop asks again.
Add a folder with 'Add a folder' and later 'Remove access'.
Approve a site in Chrome options and later remove it, which also removes the host permission.

where_to_find_it: Desktop (and web): Settings, Capabilities, 'Local access' with 'Folders' and 'Commands' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/LocalAccessSection.tsx:37-55, 213).

Desktop: Settings, General desktop settings, then 'Permissions' with 'Your answers' and a system privacy settings group (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx imports DesktopPermissionsSection; DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:28-37, 195-235).

Chrome: extension Options, permissions section, 'Approve a site so the assistant can act on it, and remove it any time.' with Add and a list ('No sites allowlisted yet.') (apps/extension/src/options.ts:1337-1345, 1403-1412).
CLI: --add-dir, /add-dir, /remove-dir and /trust grant (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:409-411; apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:332-380; apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:7389).
Phone, VS Code: not applicable here.
prerequisites: Desktop: the Electron host (host check useElectronHost); settings are hidden otherwise (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:195).

Screen, accessibility and microphone permissions at operating-system level (SYSTEM_PERMISSION_KINDS: Screen Recording, Accessibility, Microphone) (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-privacy.ts:3, 10-20).
Chrome: Add must run from a real click so Chrome can show its permission prompt (apps/extension/src/features/options/site-allowlist.ts:86-97).
screens_and_controls: Desktop answer rows: label plus hint 'Allowed until you quit the app', 'Allowed once', 'Always allowed', 'Refused until you quit the app' or 'Always refused'; button 'Remove' or 'Ask again' (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:87-99, 165-181).

System rows: status text Allowed, Not allowed, Not asked yet, Blocked by your organization, Not needed on this computer, and an 'Open System Settings' button when action is needed (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:48-85).
'Refresh' button on the system group.
Run-time prompt 'Permission required': 'Allow <app> to control <name>?' with Deny, 'Allow this session' and 'Never allow' (permissionManager.ts:356-389; applicationControl.ts:104-120).
Clipboard prompt for copy and paste key combos: Deny, 'Allow this session', 'Always allow' (permissionManager.ts:360-366; computerUseSteps.ts:58-73).
'Check this step' warning dialog for password-field typing with Deny and 'Allow once' (computerUseSteps.ts:84-117).
Folders: 'Add a folder'; remove with a confirmation 'Remove access to <name>?' and button 'Remove access' (LocalAccessSection.tsx:55-56 and the section's remove handler).
journey: The agent wants to click in an app.
Desktop shows the permission prompt naming the app and what it can do.
The person chooses Deny, Allow this session or Never allow; closing the dialog grants nothing.
Later the person opens Settings, Permissions, sees the answer, and presses Remove or Ask again.
For folders the person adds one with the system chooser and removes it with confirmation.
In Chrome the person opens the current tab's origin in Options, presses Add, accepts Chrome's prompt, and removes it later from the list.
feedback_and_outputs: Row hints state how long an answer lasts.
'Permissions could not be read from the app.', 'That answer was not removed.', 'That app was not added to Refused apps.' (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:38-40).
Folder messages: 'Approved folders could not be read.', 'That folder was not approved.', 'That folder was not removed.' (LocalAccessSection.tsx:51-53).
macOS only: dialog 'Screen recording permission needed' once per run when capture is denied or restricted (apps/desktop/electron/screenshot.ts:39-50).
Agent receives a plain refusal text when a step is refused (applicationControl.ts:70-72).
settings: Desktop decisions file desktop-permissions.json under the app's user-data folder (permissionManager.ts:49-50).
Chrome storage key agi_site_allowlist and a user site blocklist (apps/extension/src/background/policy.ts:187; options.ts:1170-1177).
CLI additional roots list for the session (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6080-6083).

working: Desktop remembers granted or denied decisions per capability and scope: session decisions in memory, 'always' decisions persisted atomically; a corrupt store means everything asks again (permissionManager.ts:34-104, 127-150).

High-risk capabilities (computer use, application control, shell, remote host, browser internals, destructive git) never get a permanent grant from the prompt; only 'Never allow' can be permanent, as a refusal (permissionManager.ts:360-395; packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/capabilities.ts:66-73).

Each run step re-checks application permission and clipboard permission before acting, and a closed prompt or a stopped run leaves the app untouched (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/applicationControl.ts:121-133; computerUseSteps.ts:119-135).
The agent may not control AGI's own window (applicationControl.ts:135-146).
Settings list answers and revoke them; application answers are handled in a separate refused-apps flow (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:195-216).
Folders: list, pick and revoke roots; revoking stops work in that folder first (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/dispatcher.ts:2312-2321; apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/runtime-client.ts:123-165).
Chrome approves a site only with a Chrome host-permission grant and removes it on delete (site-allowlist.ts:86-120).
CLI adds and removes extra working directories and lists them (claude_parity.rs:332-380).
incomplete: Screen sharing preferences: there is no dedicated control; only the Screen Recording system row and the one-time macOS dialog exist (DesktopPermissionsSection.tsx:48-85; screenshot.ts:39-50). The brief points at DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:47, which holds only labels and imports.
The draft cited apps/cli/src/tui/tui_app.rs:3868 for CLI folders; that line is input handling. CLI folder access is --add-dir, /add-dir, /remove-dir and /trust (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:409-411).
'Allowed once' appears in the hint text but one-time decisions are excluded from the review list (permissionManager.ts:299-313).
disconnected_or_disabled: Tauri desktop settings (apps/desktop/src) are internal; the public Desktop shows web settings (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
not_available: The macOS-only screen dialog is not shown on other platforms (screenshot.ts:40).
Phone, VS Code: not applicable (brief).

established.statement: The user can choose which local folders AGI may read or write, see the list and remove access.
The user can choose which websites AGI may read or act on and remove them later.
The user can choose which desktop applications AGI may control and revoke that.
The user controls whether AGI may read the clipboard and can review or withdraw that permission.
The user can set preferences for whether and how AGI may see the screen.
A refused or closed prompt leaves the app untouched.
Each run step re-checks the application and clipboard permission before acting.
On macOS with screen capture blocked, Desktop shows a one-time explanation dialog.
Browser actions on new or sensitive domains and computer-use actions with consequences need approval prompts.

acceptance_criteria: A step aimed at an app with no answer shows the permission prompt and does not run until the person chooses.
Choosing Deny, closing the dialog or stopping the run leaves the app untouched and the answer is Refused until quit.
Choosing 'Never allow' records Always refused and a later step on that app is refused without a prompt.
Removing an answer in Settings makes Desktop ask again.
Pressing copy or paste key combinations the first time asks about the clipboard; refusing blocks the key press.
In Chrome, Add triggers Chrome's host-permission prompt and Remove deletes the host permission and list entry.
With macOS screen capture denied, a capture shows the explanation dialog once per run.
Removing a folder asks first and stops work in that folder.
inferred: [inferred] Brief item S86.22 is only partly met because the person cannot set preferences, only view the OS state.
[inferred] 'Always allow' for the clipboard is consumed as single use after the step (consumeSingleUse, computerUseSteps.ts:72), so a standing clipboard grant may behave per use; confirm in tests.
proposed: [proposed] Add a Screen sharing row that explains what capture is used for and links to the OS setting.
[proposed] Show CLI added folders in the settings of Desktop when the CLI runs from Desktop.
[proposed] Show remembered site answers in the same list as app answers on Desktop for the paired browser.

features.summary: On the phone, Settings, Permissions shows whether AGI may use the microphone and the camera, reading the answer from the operating system. If not yet asked, the person can trigger the system prompt; if denied, an Open Settings button leads to the device settings. AGI cannot change device permissions itself.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists device permissions with their current level and opens a detail screen per permission that reads the system status, offers the system request when undecided and sends the person to device Settings otherwise (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/Detail.tsx:50-107, 154-167; registry.ts:51-79).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to see and change what the app can use. The operating system owns the decision; AGI shows the truth and a path to change it.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every phone user, especially those using voice input or document scanning.
problems_solved: Voice or camera does nothing and the person does not know why.
Not knowing what is allowed.
Stale status after changing it in device Settings.
use_cases: Check the microphone is allowed before dictating.
Allow the camera so a document can be scanned.
After denying by mistake, tap Open Settings and re-enable.
Return from device Settings and see the new status.

where_to_find_it: Phone: Settings, Safety and security, 'Permissions', then 'Microphone' or 'Camera' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/permissions/index.tsx:180-191; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:727).
Other apps: not applicable; Desktop shows Microphone in its system permission rows under F086-11 (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/desktop-privacy.ts:3).
prerequisites: The phone app. No sign-in or plan requirement found in the permissions code.
iOS also lists Speech Recognition, Photos & Files, Reminders and Face ID; Notifications and Calendar on both platforms (registry.ts:251-259).
screens_and_controls: List row per permission: label, access level label (Never, Ask, While using, Always), accessibility text '<label> permission. Access level: <level>. Tap to manage.' (index.tsx:49; types.ts:20-25; registry.ts:276-284).

Detail: title, headline (Access Granted, Not Requested, Access Denied), description ('Used for voice input and audio recording.' or 'Used for photo capture and document scanning.'), explanation, one action button, note 'AGI can’t change device permissions for you.' (Detail.tsx:154-167, 254-322; types.ts:27-37; registry.ts:163-189).
journey: Open Settings, Safety and security, Permissions.
Tap Microphone or Camera.
Read the status.
If 'Not Requested', tap 'Allow Microphone' or 'Allow Camera' and answer the system prompt.
If denied, tap 'Open Settings' and change it in the device settings.
Return to the app; the status refreshes on its own.
feedback_and_outputs: Headline and colour change when granted (Detail.tsx:222-235).
Read failure text: 'Could not read this permission from your device. The status shown may be out of date.' (Detail.tsx:27-28, 71-72).
Request failure text: 'Your device could not process the request. Try again, or open Settings.' (Detail.tsx:29-30, 102-103).
Alert 'Could not open Settings' if the OS settings page cannot open (Detail.tsx:32-36).
settings: The decision itself lives in device Settings; the app stores only the last observed status (apps/mobile/stores/permissionsStore.ts:9-13, 42-61).

working: Status is read when the screen gains focus and again whenever the app returns to the foreground (Detail.tsx:56-84).
Microphone status uses the camera module's microphone permission calls; camera status uses its camera permission calls (registry.ts:51-59, 71-79).
Unrecognised status values are shown as denied; only 'granted' counts as allowed (registry.ts:45-49, 272-274).
A request is possible only while undecided; otherwise the button opens device Settings (Detail.tsx:155-167).
A repeat press while a request is running is ignored (Detail.tsx:94-96).
Last observed status is saved with persisted storage (permissionsStore.ts:42-61).
iOS usage descriptions for the camera and microphone are declared in the app config (apps/mobile/app.config.js:75-76, 170-173).
incomplete: The draft cited detail.tsx; the file is Detail.tsx.
The OS 'restricted' state (parental or device policy) is not told apart from 'denied' (registry.ts:45-49 maps every non-granted, non-undetermined value to denied).
Access-level wording (Never, Ask, While using) does not map exactly to what the OS offers; 'Ask' is shown for an unasked permission (registry.ts:276-284).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found in the code
not_available: Android shows no Speech Recognition, Photos, Reminders or Face ID row (registry.ts:251-259).
Other apps: not applicable.

proposed: [proposed] Show 'Restricted by your device' separately from denied.
[proposed] Say on the Microphone screen that on-device speech recognition on iOS also needs the Speech Recognition permission.
