features.summary: The Workspace console Overview page on web (and desktop through the hosted web app) shows an owner or admin a live security posture list with recommendations. A diagnostics panel on the Policy page explains what one member may use and why a request would be allowed or refused. Mobile shows a trimmed posture list.

purpose.what_it_does: Overview: reads the workspace's real configuration from the database on each load and lists signals in groups (Identity, Provisioning, Access, AI controls, Data, Residency and keys, Audit), each marked Enforced, Stated position or Not configured, plus Recommended next steps (workspace-posture-service.ts:33, WorkspacePostureOverview.tsx:171). Diagnostics: for a chosen member, optionally a feature, an app surface and a country, it returns the member's effective policy, the rules that turned things off, and an allow or refuse decision with a plain reason (policy/diagnose/route.ts:20-31,61-70; WorkspacePolicyDiagnostics.tsx:115).
purpose.why_it_exists: A security reviewer reads a posture page as a list of controls, so the page separates what the server enforces from what is only recorded (workspace-posture-service.ts:22-32). Diagnostics lets an admin answer 'why can this person not use X' without guessing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins on a Team or Enterprise plan. Members are refused by the server.
problems_solved: An admin cannot tell which controls actually bind and which are only notes.
An admin cannot tell why a member is blocked when defaults, roles, groups and personal exceptions all apply.
A security team needs one page to check sign-in, provisioning, sharing, retention, keys and audit setup.
use_cases: An admin opens Overview before a security review and follows a Recommended link to verify a domain.
An admin picks a member and the Code feature on the Desktop app and reads why it is refused.
An admin on the phone checks seats and posture rows without opening a laptop.

where_to_find_it: Web: console at /workspace, nav section 'Workspace', link 'Overview' with hint 'Security posture and recommendations' (WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:38-47). Reached from Settings through the 'Workspace administration' pointer (WorkspaceConsolePointer.tsx:28).
Web diagnostics: console 'Policy' page (/workspace/policy), card 'Explain a member's policy' (WorkspaceFeatureControls.tsx:564; WorkspacePolicyDiagnostics.tsx:115).
Desktop: the Electron main window loads the hosted web app (electron/main.ts:1065-1067), so the same pages apply [inferred]. Whether the window offers a route to /workspace is unknown.
Mobile: Settings > Workspace screen, section 'Seats and invitations' followed by one group per posture group (WorkspaceAdministration.tsx:366-420; settings/workspace.tsx:664-667).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available.
prerequisites: Signed in, current terms accepted, age check passed, account active (workspace/layout.tsx:25-35).
A shared workspace selected; otherwise 'No workspace selected' (WorkspaceConsoleShell.tsx:100).

Role owner or admin for the page frame (WorkspaceConsoleShell.tsx:10,107), Team or Enterprise plan (team-admin-access.ts:70-84), and the audit.read permission for the posture data (posture/route.ts:43-48). Diagnostics also needs policy.manage (diagnose/route.ts:40-44).
screens_and_controls: Overview header: workspace name, 'Read live from this workspace's configuration on <time>' and a count of items needing attention (WorkspacePostureOverview.tsx:219-240).
'Recommended' card with a button per recommendation; group cards with rows showing a state mark, value, an enforcement badge and a link arrow.
Footnote explaining 'Stated position'.
Diagnostics form: Member select, 'Feature to check (optional)', 'From' app select, 'Country code (optional)', and an 'Explain' button (WorkspacePolicyDiagnostics.tsx:128-195).
Mobile rows: 'Seats', pending invitations, 'Invite by email', posture rows, and recommendation rows that open the web in an in-app browser (WorkspaceAdministration.tsx:371-427).
journey: Open Settings, choose 'Workspace administration', or go to /workspace.
Read the header and the Recommended card.
Open a group row link to fix an item (for example Members, Identity, Policy).
To explain a member: go to Policy, scroll to 'Explain a member's policy', choose the member, optionally a feature, app and country, press Explain.
Read 'Allowed.' or 'Refused.' with the reason, the policy revision, any rules that turned things off, and reasoning, country and app limits.
feedback_and_outputs: Loading skeleton cards; error card 'We could not load your workspace posture' with 'Try again'.
Card 'You do not administer this workspace' for a refusal (WorkspacePostureOverview.tsx; use-workspace-posture.ts:64).
Diagnostics result line 'Allowed.' or 'Refused.' plus reason; 'Nothing is turned off for this person.'; 'This workspace has no policy yet.'
Mobile: error row 'Workspace administration could not load' with value 'Retry'.
settings: The posture reflects Policy, Models, Connectors, Identity, Data and Audit pages; it has no settings of its own.
Posture data is cached in the browser for 60 seconds (use-workspace-posture.ts:71).

working: Posture route: rate limit, user-scoped database, membership check, Team/Enterprise check, audit.read check, live read, admin-data-access log (posture/route.ts:33-57).

Posture service reads organizations, members, invitations, SSO, directory sync, SCIM tokens/users/groups, shared items, audit events, legal holds, audit destinations, spend limit, connector and model policy counts (workspace-posture-service.ts:193-300).
Each signal carries enforcement 'enforced', 'stated' or 'unconfigured' (workspace-posture-service.ts:33).
Diagnose route validates the query, confirms the person is a member, and returns effective controls plus a decision with Cache-Control private, no-store (diagnose/route.ts:46-71).
Web UI for both (WorkspacePostureOverview.tsx, WorkspacePolicyDiagnostics.tsx) and mobile posture list (WorkspaceAdministration.tsx).
incomplete: The overview does not show the plan name; the plan is used only for retention (workspace-posture-service.ts:354) and a 'Seats' row exists (workspace-posture-service.ts:487-499).
Diagnostics explains only a feature ask or a managed-compute ask; model, connector, sharing or export requests cannot be chosen (diagnose/route.ts:61-65).
Mobile shows state and value but not the enforcement badge or detail text (administration.ts:30-36).
disconnected_or_disabled: Desktop: the internal desktop source has a workspace policy hook that hides sidebar features, but the public Electron window shows the hosted web app (desktop/src/features/v3/useWorkspacePolicy.ts:53-64; electron/main.ts:1065-1067).
not_available: CLI: no console or command for posture or diagnostics found; a search of cli/src, extension/src and vscode for the posture and diagnose endpoints found none (search result).
VS Code and Chrome extension: not applicable.

established.statement: An administrator opens an organization overview that summarises the workspace from live data.
An administrator can see the effective policy for a member or request and why an action was allowed or refused.
Owner/admin/member permissions are enforced through direct API requests and the UI.
Enterprise admin, audit, policy and SSO/SCIM controls are required before broad managed compute.

acceptance_criteria: A member who calls GET /api/settings/organization/posture directly gets 403 and no posture data.
An admin on a Team or Enterprise plan sees the posture with a generated-at time, and a second open after a configuration change shows the change (after the 60 s cache).
A row whose value is only recorded shows 'Stated position', not 'Enforced'.
Diagnostics for a member with a feature turned off returns 'Refused.' with a reason and lists the rule that turned it off.
Diagnostics for a person who is not a member returns 'That person is not a member of this workspace.'
If the database cannot read the policy, the decision is a refusal with code workspace_policy_unavailable, not 'allowed'.
inferred: The Overview should state the plan and licensed seats; the brief's S87.01 asks for plan, but the page shows only a 'Seats' row [inferred from workspace-posture-service.ts:487].
A non-admin on mobile should not see an error row; the admin section is shown by plan, not role (settings/workspace.tsx:340,664) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Let diagnostics also explain model, connector and sharing asks, since those are refused by other gates.
[proposed] Show the enforcement badge on mobile rows.
[proposed] Show a distinct 'Team or Enterprise plan required' card instead of the generic 'You do not administer' card for a subscription refusal.

steps.what_happens: Admin opens /workspace; the server layout checks the session, terms, age eligibility and account state, then looks up the workspace role.
The page frame is chosen from the role: unavailable, no workspace, not an administrator, or the console.
The browser calls GET posture with its bearer token; a 403 becomes the 'You do not administer' card.
The route applies a rate limit, resolves the user-scoped database, requires membership, Team/Enterprise entitlement and audit.read.
The service runs its database reads in parallel and builds signals and recommendations; the access is logged as admin data access.
For diagnostics, the form calls GET diagnose; the route needs policy.manage, checks the member exists, builds an ask, and diagnoseMemberPolicy returns effective controls and a decision.
On mobile, the screen loads invitations and posture together and shows them as rows.

purpose.why_it_exists: A shared workspace needs a controlled way to add and remove people within the seats paid for, and to hand over the one owner role without leaving the workspace ownerless.

Ownership cannot be left without an owner.

Remove a departing member and read the cleanup report.

established.statement: An administrator can list the workspace members with name, email and role.
Invite by email with a role, see pending invitations, renew and revoke them, and the invitee can accept.
See licensed, used and available seats; members consume and release seats; seats can be added.
The owner can hand ownership to another member after confirmation, with the server moving the owner role atomically.
Invite acceptance, expiry, seat limits, role changes and member removal preserve isolation; removing access closes later reads.

acceptance_criteria: Inviting with role owner is refused by the schema (400).
A second invitation to an address with a pending one returns a conflict telling the admin to resend.
An invitation older than 7 days cannot be accepted and shows as expired.
Accepting while signed in as a different email is refused.
With no seats available, creating or accepting is refused with the seat message.
Removing a member returns a revoked-credentials summary and the member's next request is refused.
Ownership transfer leaves exactly one owner; a non-Primary-Owner gets 403.
inferred: Revoking a pending invitation frees nothing if invitations hold no seat; the hint text should match behaviour [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Make the seat hint match the real rule, or reserve a seat per pending invitation.
[proposed] Show cleanup warnings on mobile removal instead of only a generic alert.

steps.what_happens: Admin submits email and role; the route validates (role admin, member or viewer), checks Team plan and members.manage, applies the role ceiling.
A transaction locks the workspace members, expires old invitations, refuses existing members and duplicate pending invitations, and inserts a hashed token with a 7-day expiry.
An email is sent through an outside email service when possible; the response carries the token and delivery result so the admin can copy the link.
Invitee opens the link, signs in with the invited address; accept updates the invitation and inserts the member in one transaction, then provisions the seat's usage ledger.
Role change or removal: lock, authority check, owner invariant, update or delete; removal then revokes credentials.
Ownership transfer: step-up check, lock, Primary Owner check, successor check, owner role moved atomically, audit event.
Mobile calls the same endpoints, wrapping the transfer in a step-up prompt.

features.summary: On the Identity page an owner claims a company email domain with a DNS TXT record, then sets up a SAML or OIDC single sign-on connection for it, and connects an identity provider over SCIM so members are created, updated and removed automatically. SSO and SCIM need the Enterprise plan. Requiring SSO for everyone is not available.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates an SSO connection for a domain and issues a verification challenge; verifies ownership by looking up a TXT record; activates the connection through the sign-in service (Clerk) only after the domain is verified; creates first-sign-in (JIT) members for verified domains; lets an admin add a directory sync connection, mint SCIM bearer tokens and map groups to roles; and serves SCIM Users and Groups to the provider.
purpose.why_it_exists: Companies want staff to sign in with their own identity provider and want joiners and leavers handled by their directory, not by hand.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners (SSO, domain) and owners/admins (directory sync) on Enterprise.
problems_solved: Proving a company controls a domain before routing sign-in for it.
Manual onboarding and offboarding.
Stale access after someone leaves the company.
use_cases: Owner adds company domain, publishes the TXT record, verifies, and activates SAML.
Admin connects an identity provider, copies the token once.
Provider disables a user; membership, tokens and keys end.
New staff sign in through SSO and join as a default role (JIT).

Desktop: hosted web pages [inferred].
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not available.

Owner role to create, verify or delete SSO connections (sso/route.ts:208-214; verify-domain/route.ts:65).
Owner or admin for directory sync (directory-sync-access.ts:65).
Access to DNS for the domain and to the identity provider.
screens_and_controls: SSO panel: 'Add connection' with fields 'Email domain', 'Protocol', 'Display name', 'IdP metadata URL' or 'OIDC discovery URL' and 'OIDC client ID'; 'OIDC client secret' (SSOPanel.tsx:600-762).
Status labels 'Domain not verified', 'Domain verified', 'Ready to activate', 'Active' (SSOPanel.tsx:33-50).
DNS record rows 'Record type', 'Record name', 'Record value' and buttons 'Verify domain' and 'Reissue challenge' (SSOPanel.tsx:409-481).
Service provider rows 'ACS URL', 'SP entity ID', 'SP metadata URL'.

journey: Open Identity, press 'Add connection', enter domain, protocol and provider details.
Copy the DNS TXT record shown and publish it at your DNS host.
Press 'Verify domain'. If it fails, read the reason; wait for DNS and retry, or 'Reissue challenge' if expired.
Activate the connection so sign-in is routed for that domain.
Under Directory sync add a connection, create a token (name, optional expiry) and copy it once into the identity provider.
Map directory groups to roles; watch 'Recent IdP activity'.
feedback_and_outputs: Verify failure messages: record not found, mismatched value, challenge expired, lookup failed (verify-domain/route.ts:131-156).
Success: 'verified' with next step configure and activate.
Token shown once on creation.
Notice that removing a user at the provider ends their membership, tokens, keys and sessions (WorkspaceIdentityPanels.tsx:79-84).
settings: Challenge lifetime 7 days (domain-verification.ts:10).
JIT default role (member or viewer) and the on/off flag are stored on the connection (jit-provisioning.ts:11,41-58); where they are edited was not found.

working: Domain verification with expiry, constant-time compare, distinct reasons (domain-verification.ts:88-132).
Already-verified connection returns success without re-checking; no challenge returns 409 NO_CHALLENGE (verify-domain/route.ts:112-128).
Activation refused until the domain is verified (sso/[id]/route.ts:283-290).
JIT membership only for active, verified connections with JIT enabled and a matching email domain; seat shortage is refused and audited (jit-provisioning.ts:50-60,108-126).
Directory connection create, token mint (name, optional future expiry, audit event) (directory-sync/route.ts:75-200; tokens/route.ts:52-130).
SCIM requests need a valid token, an unlocked tenant, an active connection, a token issuer who still administers the workspace, and Enterprise (scim-auth.ts:44-120).
Rejected or failed SCIM requests are logged as sync events (scim-route.ts:30-56).
incomplete: Requiring SSO is not available: an active connection adds a route and members with passwords can still use them (WorkspaceIdentityPanels.tsx:92-95).
Group-scoped sharing and budgets from directory groups are not available (WorkspaceIdentityPanels.tsx:96-99).
Sign-in routing by domain is performed by the outside sign-in service after activation; the routing itself was not read.
disconnected_or_disabled: Connections stay dormant ('Ready to activate') until activated (SSOPanel.tsx:43-46).
not_available: CLI, mobile, VS Code, Chrome: no screens. Mobile brief status n/a.

established.statement: An administrator claims a company domain, publishes a DNS TXT challenge, and the product verifies ownership before routing sign-in for that domain.
A workspace owner configures a SAML or OIDC connection for a verified domain, and members on that domain sign in through the identity provider.
An administrator connects an identity provider over SCIM (connection and bearer token), and the provider creates, updates and deprovisions members.
SSO/SCIM are part of the enterprise path.

acceptance_criteria: Verify with no record returns 409 reason no_record; with a different token returns token_mismatch.
Verify on a verified connection returns verified true without a DNS lookup.
Activating an unverified connection returns 409.
A user whose email domain differs from the connection domain is not auto-joined.
A SCIM call with a revoked token returns 401; with a token whose issuer left returns 403.
A SCIM call on a non-Enterprise workspace returns 403.
Deactivating a user via SCIM removes the membership and revokes credentials.
inferred: Sign-in routing is delegated to the sign-in service and works only if its connection is active [inferred from sso/[id]/route.ts:281-345].
proposed: [proposed] Add 'Require SSO' enforcement with an owner break-glass path.
[proposed] Show JIT role settings on the Identity page if missing.

steps.what_happens: Owner creates a connection; input is validated, URLs checked, a challenge token with expiry is stored.
Owner publishes the TXT record at their DNS host.
Verify: the server asks DNS for the TXT record, compares in constant time, and stamps domain_verified_at.
Activation registers or toggles the connection at the outside sign-in service.
A first sign-in through the provider triggers JIT membership if active and verified.
Admin mints a SCIM token (shown once); the provider sends SCIM calls with it; every call is authenticated and checked.
Provider sends the user inactive or deletes it; membership is deleted (never an owner) and credentials revoked.

features.summary: Admins create workspace API keys for automations. Each key belongs to a service principal (a non-human account), carries limited scopes and an optional expiry up to one year, is shown once, and can be revoked. Disabling a principal stops all its keys. Keys can reach only a short list of admin endpoints.

purpose.what_it_does: Mints keys whose secret begins with a fixed admin-key prefix, stores only a hash, binds each key to a principal whose maximum scopes cap what the key can do on every call, and lets automations read the audit trail, list and manage members and invitations, and read usage (admin-api-keys.ts:19,108-130,191-235; route-access.ts:24-114).
purpose.why_it_exists: Automations need administrative access that does not depend on one person's login and can be limited and revoked.
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners and admins with identity.manage (create, revoke, disable); automations as callers.
problems_solved: Scripts using a person's session.
Keys that die when their creator leaves.
Over-broad automation access.
use_cases: Nightly job exports the audit trail to a SIEM or archive.
HR system invites and removes member and viewer accounts.
Finance reads the per-member usage report.
Admin disables a principal after an incident.

established.statement: An administrator creates non-human service accounts with bounded permissions and keys that outlive their creator, and can disable them or revoke their keys.
An administrator issues scoped, expiring API keys for automations through a documented API, and can revoke them.
Workspace API keys require an active Team or Enterprise subscription.

acceptance_criteria: A key created by an admin still works after that admin is removed from the workspace.
A revoked key returns 401 on its next call.
A key whose principal is disabled returns 401; enabling restores it.
A key asking for a scope its creator does not hold is refused at creation.
A key cannot call an endpoint missing from the access table or the members-only endpoint.
A key cannot assign admin roles.
An expired key returns 401.
inferred: 'Expiring' is only optional today; the brief's Should says expiring [inferred gap].
proposed: [proposed] Require an expiry, or warn on 'No expiry'.
[proposed] Let admins create a principal without a key.

Step-up confirmation is required, then a transaction finds or creates the principal and inserts the key hash.
The raw key is returned once; only a SHA-256 hash is stored.
The automation calls an endpoint with the bearer key; the key is verified, plan and IP allow-list checked, scope compared to the route table.
Revoke sets revoked_at; principal disable makes verification fail.

features.summary: Admins choose which providers and models members may use, switch product features on or off with exceptions for roles, groups or people, and set connector tool rules (always allow, needs approval, blocked). The server refuses what is blocked and refuses when the policy cannot be read. The CLI honours only the hooks feature and MCP controls, plus web site rules.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves a model policy (allowed and blocked providers and models) and refuses blocked models on managed chat and other model routes with a reason (model-policy/route.ts:80-240; model-policy.ts:227-273); saves feature switches and exceptions that every gate reads (WorkspaceFeatureControls.tsx; managed-compute-gate.ts:205); and saves connector, plugin, MCP host, web domain and tool rules, with the strictest of workspace and member rules winning (connector-policy/route.ts; connector-tool-permissions.ts:503-540).
purpose.why_it_exists: Organisations must control which AI providers see their data, which features exist for staff, and which actions an AI agent may take.
purpose.who_uses_it: Owners and admins with policy.manage.
problems_solved: Staff using unapproved providers or models.
Risky features such as computer use or remote control being open to all.
Agents writing to connected apps without approval.
use_cases: Block one provider for the whole workspace.
Turn off Computer use for everyone but one group.
Mark every write tool of a connector as 'Needs approval'.
Explain to an employee why a model is refused.

An administrator switches product features on or off (with exceptions) and each switched-off feature is refused wherever it runs.
An administrator decides which tools members and agents may use (allow, block or require approval) and the tool loop enforces it.

Model, connector and sharing policy preserve isolation.

A connector write tool set to 'Blocked' is not offered to the model; set to 'Needs approval' it pauses for approval.
The CLI refuses hooks when the workspace turns hooks off and when the policy is unknown.
Saving a model in both lists returns 400.
inferred: Desktop and web parity on feature switches is by the shared server gates because the Electron window shows the hosted app [inferred].

steps.what_happens: Admin saves a model policy; the route checks Team plan and policy.manage, validates against the catalog, writes with a privileged connection, and records an audit diff.
A member sends a chat; the request processor resolves the model, then evaluates the workspace model policy and refuses with 403 and a code, or 503 if unreadable.
Auto routing filters the plan against the policy before picking a model.

steps.what_happens: A gated feature request calls the workspace feature gate; an unreadable policy is a refusal.
On a chat turn, the member's saved tool verdicts and the workspace tool rules are merged, stricter wins; denied tools are not offered and ask-level tools pause for approval.
The CLI fetches the effective policy hourly, seals it on disk, and refuses hooks or MCP servers when the workspace disallows or the policy is unknown.
Own-key or Local turns on a device do not pass these server gates; no on-device enforcement of model policy was found.

features.summary: Workspace admins decide which connectors (including custom ones), plugin keys, MCP hosts and websites members may use, and publish a private plugin catalogue to members. The web server enforces this at connect, install and chat-tool time. The desktop shows the same hosted screens. The CLI only partly honours it.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets an owner or admin set allow and block lists for connectors, allow or block custom connectors, set approved plugin keys and MCP server hosts, set allowed and blocked websites and per-tool rules, and publish plugins or single skills to the workspace so members get them as required, installed by default, available, or hidden (WorkspaceConnectorPolicy.tsx:221, WorkspacePlugins.tsx:32-52, connector-policy/route.ts:104).
purpose.why_it_exists: A company needs to say which outside systems and add-ons its people may connect to company data, and to give them vetted add-ons without sending them to the public directory (connector-policy-gate.ts:21-40 comment, WorkspacePlugins.tsx:415).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins (permission policy.manage) edit; every member of the workspace is governed by it and can read the policy to learn why an integration is missing (connector-policy/route.ts:80-86, plugins/route.ts:62-70).
problems_solved: A member connecting a connector the company forbids before any credential is exchanged (connector-policy-gate.ts:139,216).
Unvetted plugins being installed (install-gate.ts:21-50).
No private place to distribute company plugins and skills (plugins/route.ts:62).
use_cases: An admin blocks one connector and switches custom connectors off.
An admin approves only three plugin keys; other installs are refused.
An admin uploads a plugin .zip and marks it Installed by default for all members.
An admin retires a plugin so every member loses it at once (WorkspacePlugins.tsx:394).

where_to_find_it: Web: Workspace console at /workspace, Controls section, links 'Connectors' (/workspace/connectors) and 'Plugins' (/workspace/plugins) (WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:90,108). Page titles 'Connectors' and 'Plugins' (connectors/page.tsx, plugins/page.tsx:14).
Desktop: [inferred] the same hosted web screens, because the public Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). No Electron code that loads /workspace was opened.

Members: the Plugins area of the app lists workspace plugins (WorkspacePlugins.tsx:415 text 'Members find these under Plugins'); data comes from GET /api/plugins/organization (plugins/organization/route.ts:16).
Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: no screen found.

screens_and_controls: Connectors page: 'Custom connectors' switch labelled 'Allow custom connectors' (WorkspaceConnectorPolicy.tsx:633); 'Catalog connectors' list with per-connector allow/block toggles and per-tool choices 'Member decides', 'Always allow', 'Needs approval', 'Blocked' (lines 418-423, 669); 'Approved plugins' and 'Blocked plugins' lists (221,230); 'MCP server hosts' (261); 'Allowed sites' and 'Blocked sites' (388,397); button 'Save policy' (797).

journey: Open Workspace > Connectors.
Choose a catalog connector and mark allowed or blocked, toggle custom connectors, add plugin keys, MCP hosts and sites.
Select 'Save policy'; the page sends PUT /api/settings/organization/connector-policy.
Open Workspace > Plugins and upload a plugin or skill .zip; files are scanned, then published.
Pick Required, Installed by default, Available to install or Not available for each plugin, optionally per group.
Members open Plugins and see only what the workspace offers; a blocked connector is missing from their tools.
feedback_and_outputs: Error text 'Could not update connector policy. Try again.' (WorkspaceConnectorPolicy.tsx).
Validation messages when an item is both allowed and blocked (connector-policy/route.ts:146).
Refusal texts from the shared evaluator, for example 'Your workspace administrator has blocked the "x" connector.' (policy.ts:28-60).
Each save writes an admin_policy_changed audit row (connector-policy/route.ts:166-180, plugins/route.ts:84-95).
settings: Feature switches 'skills' and 'plugins' on the Policy page (WorkspaceFeatureControls.tsx:40-41) turn the whole capability off for the workspace.

working: Web connection gate: connect, OAuth start/callback, credentials, custom creation and bank-link routes call evaluateConnectorPolicyForUser, which refuses blocked, not-listed and disallowed custom connectors before any credential exchange (connector-policy-gate.ts:139-215; callers listed under app/api/connectors/*).
Web plugin install gate refuses a plugin key that is blocked or not on a non-empty approved list, and checks dependencies (install-gate.ts:21-50, connector-policy-gate.ts:216).

Web chat-turn tool list drops blocked connectors and fails closed with an empty list when the policy cannot be read (user-connector-tools.ts:1920-1945); capability loading fails closed too (user-connector-tools.ts:1977-2000).
Chat requests refuse with 403 feature_disabled when the workspace turned a feature off, and plugin loading is skipped when the plugins switch is off (request-processor.ts:3730,3745).

Private catalogue: admins publish plugins and single skills, set install preference per plugin and per group, retire plugins (plugins/route.ts:62,114); members read their list (plugins/organization/route.ts:16, organization-plugin-service.ts:384); required plugins cannot be turned off by members (organization-plugin-service.ts:418).
The catalogue uses its own tables, separate from the user's public-directory installs (organization-plugin-service.ts:143-181 versus installed-skills.ts:90-105).
Desktop: [inferred] shows the web screens; no separate code.
incomplete: Per-item skill allow list: only plugin keys have allow/block lists; skills are controlled by the 'skills' feature switch and by plugin membership. No per-skill list found (connector-policy/route.ts:119-129).

CLI: the workspace connector policy is read and evaluated (claude_parity.rs:2105,2354) but the production caller found only refuses the GitHub-app install help text (claude_parity.rs:753) and applies website rules to web search and fetch (site_rules.rs:107).
CLI MCP servers: refused when the workspace turned MCP off or restricts the list (workspace_policy.rs:371,409; mcp/mod.rs:301).
disconnected_or_disabled: CLI evaluate_plugin_access is defined but its only callers found are in tests (claude_parity.rs:2412, 4295); the CLI plugin loader does not apply the workspace plugin lists.
CLI managed.rs plugin policy is a local signed-plugin requirement from a device file, not the workspace allow list (managed.rs:29, plugins.rs:254-300).
Connectors are gated by connectorsReleased() before policy, so unreleased connectors answer 'coming soon' (connector-policy-gate.ts:144-150).
not_available: Mobile: no connector or plugin policy screen or enforcement found.
VS Code and Chrome: none found.
CLI private marketplace: no code that reads the workspace catalogue.

established.statement: A blocked connector is not offered in the tool list and cannot be connected.
Skill and plugin allow lists are enforced at install time and at request time.
A workspace curates a private catalogue separate from the public directory that members browse and install.
An empty allow list means unrestricted, not deny-all; block beats allow.
A policy that cannot be read must not become an unrestricted connection.

acceptance_criteria: With connector X blocked, connecting X returns a refusal naming X and no credential is stored.
With a non-empty approved plugin list, installing an unlisted plugin key is refused with the 'not on the approved list' reason.
With custom connectors off, creating a custom connector is refused even if its id is on the approved list.
A blocked connector's tools do not appear in a chat turn's tool list for a member.
A plugin set to Not available is absent from a member's Plugins list; a Required plugin cannot be turned off by the member.
Saving a policy where one item is both allowed and blocked is refused with a validation message.
Every policy save and plugin publish writes an admin_policy_changed audit row.
inferred: The CLI should apply workspace plugin and connector lists for managed sessions, matching web [inferred from brief S87.17 'CLI done' versus the code].
A per-skill list is needed if 'per item' in S87.17 means skills [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Wire evaluate_plugin_access into the CLI plugin install and load path and cache it with the existing sealed policy cache.
[proposed] Add a skill-level allow list or state clearly that skills follow their plugin.

features.summary: Admins see what the workspace shares (projects, conversations, artifacts, connectors), set per-member project access or stop sharing, and use one Policy switch, 'Public sharing', that blocks new public share links and artifact publishing. A second switch, 'Memory', turns account memory off for every member. Web and the hosted desktop screens only.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows shared items and who can open them, lets owners, admins and project owners change per-member access or stop sharing, and lets admins switch public sharing and workspace memory on or off (OrganizationSharingSection.tsx:195-555, WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:457,474).
purpose.why_it_exists: Companies need control over what leaves the workspace and over what the assistant remembers about members.
purpose.who_uses_it: Admins and sharing managers (permission sharing.manage) and project owners (content.share) for projects; owners and admins with policy rights for the switches (org-sharing-service.ts:91-110).

Not knowing who can open a shared project.
Account memory keeping workspace content the company does not want kept.
use_cases: Admin turns Public sharing off before an audit; members get a refusal on new links.
Admin removes one member's access to a shared project.
Admin selects 'Stop sharing' on a project so everyone loses it.
Admin leaves Memory off for a regulated workspace.

established.statement: An admin sees every project shared with the workspace, sets per-member access and can stop sharing.
Members cannot create new external share links while sharing outside the workspace is off.

With Public sharing off, POST /api/artifacts/publish returns 403 and nothing is stored.

With Memory off, a member's chat turn receives no memory context even if their personal memory is on.
With no policy row, memory is off for workspace members.
'Stop sharing' on a project removes it from the shared list and members lose access; an audit row project_unshared exists.
A plain member cannot change per-member access on a project they do not own.

features.summary: Admins set a retention window and a nightly sweep deletes older chats (except held ones), request a data-region move, connect a customer encryption key, and restrict access by IP range. IT can push managed settings to the Chrome extension and CLI. The key currently seals only audit-stream secrets. Rollout channels do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Sets how long workspace conversations are kept and deletes older ones when enforced; records a request to move workspace data to another region; lets an Enterprise workspace enroll, rotate, replace and revoke its own KMS key; refuses requests from outside listed IP ranges; and lets a device-management file configure the extension and CLI (WorkspacePolicySection.tsx:521-560, 694; WorkspaceDataRegion.tsx:123; WorkspaceEncryptionKey.tsx:257-334; managed-schema.json).
purpose.why_it_exists: Companies must meet retention, residency, key-control and network rules and must deploy tools centrally.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins; the owner only may revoke a key (keys-access.ts:58); platform operators complete region cutovers (admin/data-region/route.ts:38); IT teams deploy device files.
problems_solved: Chats kept forever.
No control over network origin of requests.
Customer wants its own key control.
IT cannot configure extension or CLI per device.
use_cases: Set 90 days and enforce, with a dry run first.
Request a move to another region once it is provisioned.
Enter office CIDR blocks so only that network reaches the workspace.
IT pushes a site allow and block policy to the Chrome extension.

steps.what_happens: Admin saves retention and IP settings; server validates and refuses a self-lockout.
Cron calls the sweep; server lists enforced orgs, reads holds, deletes in batches of 500 excluding holds, records the sweep and an audit row.
Admin requests a region move; server checks Enterprise and provisioning, stores the request, audits it.
Platform operator performs the data copy outside this code and calls the completion endpoint, which switches the region.
Every authenticated request passes the IP check against stored CIDRs using the client IP.
Key calls go to the customer's KMS service to validate, wrap and unwrap; data keys cached and dropped on revoke.
Chrome and CLI read their managed files from the device on start and on change.

features.summary: A public help centre on the web app with a search box that finds articles as you type, plus small links inside settings screens (web, mobile, VS Code, Chrome) that open the article for that screen. Desktop and the extensions open the web help centre. CLI has no help search.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person search help articles (the page /help calls the search API /api/help/search) and browse them by collection. Settings screens carry a link such as 'How memory works' that opens the matching article. Retrieval is a keyword ranking (BM25) over a built help corpus, with no model call (comment: apps/web/app/api/help/search/route.ts:16-24).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a person can solve a problem without writing to support, and so every screen that needs explaining points at one canonical article. The brief states 'Users can search a help centre and open matching articles' and 'Screens that need explaining link straight to the matching help or docs article' (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/088-support-trust-and-policy-product.md, S88.01 and S88.02).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any visitor (the /help page and the search API are public and need no sign-in: no auth call in apps/web/app/api/help/search/route.ts:47-96) and any signed-in user in a settings screen.
problems_solved: People cannot find the article that explains a setting.
An empty search result looks the same as a broken index; the API reports corpus 'available' or 'unavailable' so the page can say which (apps/web/app/api/help/search/route.ts:64-72).
Searching help must keep working when the support assistant is turned off (route comment, apps/web/app/api/help/search/route.ts:16-24).
use_cases: A user opens Help and types 'billing' to find the plans article.
A user in Settings, Memory clicks 'How memory works' and lands on the memory article.
A person on the phone app taps 'How plans and billing work' style links and reads the article in an in-app browser.
On a non-help screen the account menu 'Get help' opens /help pre-searched for that area (apps/web/lib/support/help-entry-points.ts:93-96).

where_to_find_it: Web: account menu, 'Get help' submenu, 'Get help' item opens /help; on routes under billing, work, connectors, workspace or admin it opens /help with a prefilled query (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx:91-97, apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:514, apps/web/lib/support/help-entry-points.ts:93-96). Also Settings, Help, link 'Help center' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/HelpSection.tsx:31-36).

Web contextual links: 'How memory works', 'How plans and billing work', 'How privacy controls work', 'Sessions, email and API keys', 'Choosing a model and effort', 'Learn more about usage limits', 'How workspaces work', 'How voice works', 'How sharing works', 'How account security works' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:244, BillingSection.tsx:718, PrivacySection.tsx:423, AccountSection.tsx:440, GeneralSection.tsx:518, UsageSection.tsx:1285, TeamSection.tsx:669, VoiceSection.tsx:78, SharedLinksSection.tsx:312, SecuritySection.tsx:237).

established.statement: Users can search a help centre and open matching articles.
Screens that need explaining link straight to the matching help or docs article for that feature.
Search says so when the index is not available (corpus 'unavailable', HTTP 503) instead of showing an empty list.
Search is rate limited under 'help-search'.

acceptance_criteria: Typing one character does not start a search; two or more does, after about 250 ms.
Typing a second query while the first is in flight leaves only the second result on screen.
With the index unloaded, the page shows the 'Search is not answering right now' text, not 'Nothing here covers that yet'.
A query with no match shows 'Nothing here covers that yet' and the support address.
Each web contextual link opens the article named in its docId (for example 'How memory works' opens /help/memory).
From the phone app, searching for a purchase topic returns no purchase article.
The 61st search within a minute from one caller is refused by the rate limiter.

Mobile and extension help links should keep opening the same article id as the web link [inferred from shared docId values].
proposed: [proposed] Add in-app help search on mobile, CLI and the extensions, or state the web-only choice in the product docs.
[proposed] Make the About 'Help Center' row use the same helper as Settings so one place owns the address.

steps.what_happens: Person types a query; the page waits 250 ms, aborts any earlier request and calls GET /api/help/search.
Server applies the 'help-search' rate limit, validates the query, picks the phone or web view of the corpus.
Server ranks chunks with BM25, keeps the best chunk per article and returns title, path, category and snippet; the response is cacheable for 60 seconds.
If the corpus cannot load, the server logs the reason and answers 503 with corpus 'unavailable'.
Opening a contextual link on mobile or desktop launches the in-app or system browser on the hosted article.

features.summary: People can send a bug report, and can produce a diagnostic bundle (build, platform, language, time zone, recent errors) that our server redacts. On web the bundle can be reviewed and downloaded before sending. Mobile asks first with a confirm dialog. CLI, VS Code and Chrome save a redacted file to attach to support.

purpose.what_it_does: Collects technical context on the device, posts it to /api/support/diagnostics (or inside a ticket) where the server validates and redacts it, and returns a summary and file name the user can read, download or share (apps/web/app/api/support/diagnostics/route.ts:18-45).
purpose.why_it_exists: Support needs build and platform context to act, and users need to see what leaves the device (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/088-support-trust-and-policy-product.md, S88.04 and S88.07).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in user reporting a fault; support staff reading the stored bundle.
problems_solved: Bug reports without build or platform details.
Secrets inside recent error text: the server is the only redactor (apps/web/lib/support/diagnostics/export.ts:6-10, apps/web/lib/support/diagnostics/schema.ts:10-17).
Query strings or share tokens in a page path are cut (apps/web/lib/support/diagnostics/schema.ts:20-27).

Phone user opens Settings, 'Export Diagnostics' and shares the file by the system share sheet.
CLI user runs the doctor command with the export option and attaches the file.
VS Code user picks 'Export diagnostics' in the Help menu.

acceptance_criteria: Pressing 'Review diagnostics' shows a summary and enables 'Download diagnostics'.
The downloaded file name starts with 'agi-diagnostics-web-'.

A page path with a query string comes back without the query string.
A bundle with the wrong shape to the export route is refused; the same bundle in a ticket still creates the ticket without diagnostics.
On mobile, Cancel in the dialog sends nothing.
The CLI prints the summary and the written path, and the file holds only the listed fields.
A signed-out user in Chrome sees 'Sign in first...'.

proposed: [proposed] Always show the redacted summary before a ticket or report is sent on web and mobile, not only on request.
[proposed] Let mobile 'Report App Issue' attach the same bundle behind its own preview.

features.summary: A person sends general feedback, a bug or a feature request from inside web, desktop, mobile, CLI or VS Code. The web and CLI send to /api/feedback, mobile Cloud to /api/mobile/feedback; both store a row in the feedback table. Chrome has none. Mobile in Local or own-key mode opens an email instead.

purpose.what_it_does: Collects a typed message (and on web an optional screenshot) plus app version, platform and page, and stores it as a row in public.feedback (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:37-38,260-279). The same route also stores response ratings, AGI Work task feedback and safety-refusal reports.
purpose.why_it_exists: Users must be able to send general feedback and feature requests from inside the product and have them stored for the team (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/088-support-trust-and-policy-product.md, S88.05 and S88.06).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any user, signed in or not on the web route (getOptionalAuthUser: apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:356); the product team reads the table.
problems_solved: Ideas and complaints reach the team with context.
Ratings and refusal reports stay traceable to a message (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:148-199).
use_cases: A web user chooses 'Feature request' and describes a missing option.
A phone user sends 'Bug Report' from 'Report App Issue'.
A CLI user types /bug the diff view hangs.
A web user hits 'Report issue' on a safety refusal notice.

where_to_find_it: Web: account menu, 'Get help' submenu, 'Send feedback' (apps/web/shared/components/layout/AccountMenuItems.tsx:105-108, apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:515). The dialog is mounted with a hidden trigger at apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:619 and apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7217. The message-level controls open the 'task' variant (AGI Work feedback) (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:3826) and the safety-refusal variant 'Report issue' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/ChatMessageList.tsx:1973).
Desktop: Help menu, 'Send Feedback' sends the host command that opens the same dialog (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts:557, apps/web/features/desktop-host/hooks/use-host-commands.ts:65-67).
Mobile: Settings, Support, 'Report App Issue' (also in About) (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:875-885, apps/mobile/app/(app)/about.tsx:283-310).
CLI: slash commands /feedback, /feedback feature, /bug (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:194-212).

VS Code: command 'Code: Send Feedback' (agi-workforce.sendFeedback) and Help menu '$(feedback) Send feedback' (apps/extension-vscode/package.json:320-323, apps/extension-vscode/src/features/help/helpMenu.ts:37).
Chrome extension: none found.
prerequisites: Web and desktop: none for a general report (anonymous allowed); sign-in is required for ratings (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:298).
Mobile: Cloud mode to post; otherwise email (apps/mobile/src/features/feedback/index.tsx:86,105-112).

CLI and VS Code: signed in; CLI refuses Local and own-key (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:373-381, apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs:123-129); VS Code replies 'signed-out' without a token (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/feedback/submitFeedback.ts:34-35).
screens_and_controls: Web dialog 'Share feedback': types 'General feedback', 'Something is broken', 'Feature request'; optional screenshot with 'Capture screen' and 'Upload image'; 'Details' (up to 10,000 characters); buttons 'Cancel', 'Send feedback' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:18-22,330-428).
Safety variant 'Report an incorrect refusal' with 'Submit report' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:263-267,415-423).

Mobile screen 'Report App Issue': type buttons 'Bug Report', 'Feature Request', 'General Feedback'; text field up to 2,000 characters; button 'Submit Feedback' or 'Email Feedback' (apps/mobile/src/features/feedback/index.tsx:31-35,248,306).
CLI usage text (apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs:37).
journey: 1. Open the feedback entry for the app.
2. Pick the type.
3. Type the message (web may add a screenshot).
4. Send.
5. See the thank-you message, or the error and try again.
feedback_and_outputs: Web: 'Thanks, your feedback was sent.' or 'Thanks, your report was recorded.'; a note if the screenshot could not be stored (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:306-317).
Mobile: alert 'Thank You!' / 'Your feedback has been submitted.', or 'Submission Failed' (apps/mobile/src/features/feedback/index.tsx:124-131).

CLI: 'Bug report sent to the AGI Workforce team. Thank you.' style lines; too long: 'the description is N characters and the limit is 10000. Press Up to edit it, shorten it by M characters and send it again.' (apps/cli/src/cloud/feedback.rs:53-62,83-92).
settings: None.

working: Web: dialog posts to /api/feedback with anti-forgery token; stores row; screenshot up to 4 MiB stored in private object storage when configured (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:165-215, apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:47-86).

incomplete: The brief flags web and desktop 'mount' as unfinished; the code shows the dialog mounted with a hidden trigger in WebAppShell and WebChatPage, so the general entry is reachable (apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:619). The two cited message-level mounts open other variants. Whether the brief's flag refers to something else is unknown.

Web stores the chosen type only inside the subject text ('Feature request · Web chat'); there is no separate type field (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:178-184, apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:116-119).

established.statement: Users can send general product feedback from inside the product and it is stored for the team.
Users can submit a feature request from inside the product and it is stored.
The web route stores the row in public.feedback.
Ratings need a message id; task feedback needs a run id; safety refusal reports need message id and finish reason.
A CLI message over 10,000 characters is refused with the number of characters to cut.

acceptance_criteria: Sending general feedback on web returns success and a row appears in public.feedback with source 'web'.
A safety-refusal report without a message id is rejected with a 400.
A response rating without a rating or message id is rejected.
On mobile in Cloud mode, 'Submit Feedback' stores a row with source 'mobile'.
On mobile in Local mode, the button reads 'Email Feedback' and opens a mail draft.
The CLI in Local mode prints 'nothing is sent to your AGI cloud account in this mode'.
A 10,001-character CLI message is refused and not clipped.
inferred: Feedback should never carry the user's conversation text; the dialog says prompts and content are not attached [inferred from apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerFeedbackDialog.tsx:393-399].
proposed: [proposed] Add a Chrome extension feedback entry.
[proposed] Store the feedback type as its own field on web.
[proposed] Let mobile Local mode store feedback only with explicit consent, or label email as the only path.

Mobile outside Cloud mode instead opens the phone's mail app with a draft to the support address.

features.summary: When a request or chat turn fails, the person sees 'Reference: <id>'. The id is the server request id also written to the server log, so support can find the matching log line. It is shown only on failure and only if the server gave one. Web, mobile, CLI and VS Code show it; Chrome display was not found.

purpose.what_it_does: The web error handler puts the request id in every error body and in the response header (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:91-116,346). Chat clients keep the id from the failed stream and append it to the failure text (apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts:164-190, apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/messageStreamError.ts:158-199).
purpose.why_it_exists: When a request fails the user can quote one id to support (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/088-support-trust-and-policy-product.md, S88.08).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any user who sees a failed chat turn or an error page, and support staff searching logs.
problems_solved: Support cannot find the failing request from a vague description.
A success must show nothing to report (comment at apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts:164-168).
use_cases: A user copies 'Reference: abc' from a failed reply into a ticket.
A CLI script reads the 'reference' field of the JSON error result (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:471-474).
A VS Code user sees 'Reference' after a failed chat message.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: the notice under a failed reply, e.g. 'This turn didn't complete... Reference: <id>' (apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts:179-190). Web error page: 'Reference for support: <id>' and 'Error ID' with the text 'Please include this ID when contacting support.' (apps/web/app/error.tsx:56, packages/ui/i18n/locales/en/errors.json:239-243).
Desktop: same web app in the window [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5].
Mobile: failure notice in chat ends with 'Reference: <id>' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/messageStreamError.ts:199).
CLI: 'Reference: <id>' on its own line in the failure hint, and the 'reference' key in --json results (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:1052-1058, apps/cli/src/errors.rs:471-474).
VS Code: chat error headline with 'Reference' (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/errorPresentation.ts:350-353,488).
Chrome extension: not found in apps/extension/src.
prerequisites: A failed request or turn that carried an id from the server.
screens_and_controls: No control; it is text in the error notice. Web error page also shows an id label.
journey: 1. A chat turn or request fails.
2. The notice shows the usual explanation and 'Reference: <id>'.
3. The person copies it into a ticket or email (F088-02).
4. Support searches the server log for that id.
feedback_and_outputs: Text 'Reference: <id>' appended to the failure message; nothing on success; nothing when the server gave no id.
settings: None.

working: Web server: every wrapped API response gets the request id header; error bodies carry requestId (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:91-116,247-256,346).

Web chat client: reads requestId from the stream error or errorRequestId in message metadata and appends 'Reference: ...' only when present (apps/web/features/chat/lib/turn-error-notice.ts:164-190,226,304; apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:655-681).
Upstream provider rejections log the correlation id and return it in the error shape (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/upstream-error-copy.ts:244-275).
Mobile: reference appended only when the server logged one (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/messageStreamError.ts:158-199).
CLI: reference in hint and JSON result; a test asserts the line ends 'Reference: req_7f3a' and is absent without an id (apps/cli/src/errors.rs:1494-1500).
VS Code: typed failure carries requestId and the headline adds it (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/errorPresentation.ts:298,350-353).
incomplete: Chrome: the stream chunk type carries a requestId field (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatHandler.ts:166,934), but no place that displays 'Reference' to the user was found in apps/extension/src; so the brief's 'chrome done' is not confirmed.
Desktop has no separate display; relies on the hosted web app [inferred].
not_available: Public API 'api done' in the brief: header is set by the wrapper (apps/web/lib/error-handler.ts:346) but not documented elsewhere in files read.

established.statement: When a request fails, the user sees a reference id they can quote to support.
The id is the one the server already put in its own log line for the failure; shown only on failure.
If the server gave no id, no reference is shown.

acceptance_criteria: A failed web chat turn with a requestId shows 'Reference: <id>' in the notice.
A successful turn shows no reference.
A failed turn with no requestId shows no reference text.
The API response for an error carries the same id in body and header.
The CLI --json error result has a 'reference' value when the engine gave one.
The id found in the UI matches a server log line's requestId.
Mobile shows the id only when the server logged one.
inferred: Local-mode failures on device have no server log, so no id applies [inferred; not verified in code].
proposed: [proposed] Show the id in the Chrome extension side panel.
[proposed] Offer a copy button on the reference text.

established.statement: Users can see current service status from the product, fed by live health checks.
During an incident, users see a notice in the product describing the problem and its status.
Users are told about planned maintenance before and during it, inside the product.
The product shows a list of currently known issues with status or workaround.
A health check that takes longer than 3 seconds is treated as no answer, so no incident notice is shown.
The notice list is read every 5 minutes and on window focus.

acceptance_criteria: With the chat database check failing, /api/status/notices returns an incident notice with scope 'product' and link '/status'.
With only billing failing, the notice has scope 'billing' and does not show in the product-wide stack.
With a window starting in 48 hours, a maintenance notice with 'Details' linking /maintenance is returned; with one starting in 80 hours, none.
A dismissed notice stays hidden after reload in the same browser session and returns in a new session.
If the health read takes over 3 seconds, no incident notice is returned.
After a failing check clears, a 'working again' notice appears for about an hour.
The mobile About 'Service Status' row opens the status page.
inferred: Local and own-key chats run on the device or a provider directly, so a hosted outage banner may be misleading for them; the status page says Local and BYOK work does not depend on our servers (apps/web/app/status/page.tsx:243-246) [inferred relevance].
proposed: [proposed] Show the same notice feed in mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome.
[proposed] Add a known-issues list with status and workaround, owned by one content source.
[proposed] Hide hosted-outage banners for chats that use Local mode.

steps.what_happens: Browser requests GET /api/status/notices on mount, every 5 minutes and on window focus.
Server reads cached health checks, racing a 3 second timer; no answer means no incident notices.
Server decides which scopes are blocked, records last failing time in the key-value store and reads recovery state.
Server adds a maintenance notice if the configured window is within 72 hours or under way.
Response is cacheable at the edge for 60 seconds (stale 60).
Client validates the list, drops stale dismissals, filters by scope and shows banners.

steps.what_happens: Web: the banner component reads the last-seen date from browser storage, compares it with the newest release entry bundled in the web build, and shows the card if newer.
Web: the picker decides the Leaving label from the model's deprecation date and the current clock.
Web: opening a chat compares its saved model with the selectable catalog and builds the substitution.
Web import: dry-run parses the text on our server, flags duplicates against the user's live memories, writes nothing.
Web import: commit filters excluded subjects, applies memory write policy, then inserts and reports counts.
Web import: the user sends the prompt to the other assistant and pastes the answer; that step is outside our product.
Mobile: compares the stored version with the app version on start and shows a toast; the What's new action opens a web page.
CLI: background task fetches the latest release from our servers, stores it in memory, and either pushes an update notice or the unseen notes and writes release-notes-seen.
CLI migrate reads files under the home Claude folder and writes into the AGI config folder.

features.summary: A web page where anyone, signed in or not, files a data request (access, correction, erasure, withdrawal, nomination, grievance) and gets a reference. features.summary: Four ways to push back. A person can report a harmful answer, report copyright, trademark or impersonation on shared content, appeal an answer refused for safety, or appeal an account suspension. established.statement: A user can report a harmful or problematic response from where it appears, and it reaches moderation.
Anyone can report copyright infringement or impersonation in hosted content and get a reference.
When a response is refused for safety, the user can appeal or report it from that notice.
A suspended user is told why and can appeal from where they are blocked, with a way to follow it.
Web report is an alias of the mobile route with one handler.
Notices never remove content; removal is the admin takedown route.

acceptance_criteria: Posting a web report creates a content_reports row with metadata source web.
Posting the same reportId twice creates one row.
A copyright notice for a URL that resolves to nothing returns not found and stores nothing.
A copyright notice returns a reference starting IP- and the target stays published.
A signed-in suspended user's appeal creates one ticket with the appeal subject; a second message appends to it while open.
A signed-out appeal returns 202 for a matching and a non-matching email alike.
Safety appeal without message id or finish reason is rejected.
inferred: Web users should be able to choose a reason and add a note, as mobile users can. [inferred]
Mobile should have a native appeal. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a reason list and note to the web report.
[proposed] Add a native mobile appeal thread.
[proposed] Link copyright reporting from mobile shared items.

steps.what_happens: Web posts the report with a CSRF token and generated report id.
Server checks CSRF and the mobile-content-report rate limit, validates, inserts or ignores a duplicate.
Mobile saves the report on the device first, then tries the server; offline or Local mode keeps it on the device and asks consent before one send.
Copyright intake resolves the URL, records the notice, logs a security event, emails operators.
Operator and appeal receipt emails go through the email provider.
Signed-in appeal opens or appends to a ticket with the appeal subject and emails staff.
Signed-out appeal passes a bot challenge, then files after the response is sent.

features.summary: On every web API request, the server turns the verified sign-in subject into one AGI account id and then refuses the request if the account is locked, in recovery, suspended, banned, or deleted. A scheduled deletion is still allowed so the person can cancel it. Clerk is the only identity provider the code can select.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps a provider sign-in (a subject string) to one AGI account id, reads the account's standing, and either lets the request through or answers 403 with a reason and a recovery path. The provider sits behind one interface so the rest of the web app never talks to Clerk directly (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts:1-53).
purpose.why_it_exists: The account must outlive the sign-in method, and a closed account must stop working everywhere at once. One check at the API layer covers Web, Desktop, Mobile, CLI and both extensions because they all call the same API [inferred from the shared API layer].
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person, indirectly. Support and security staff rely on it to make lock, suspend and delete real.
problems_solved: A suspended or erased person cannot keep using a stale session or a stale provider callback (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:179-212).
A locked person gets a path to fix it (password reset) and a suspended person gets an appeal path, instead of a bare error (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).

Swapping the identity provider needs one adapter and an environment change, not edits at each call site (apps/web/lib/server/identity.ts comment on getIdentityProvider; packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:36-53).
use_cases: A suspended person opens the web app and sees a suspension notice with an Appeal link instead of their chats.
A person whose account was erased tries to sign in again through a leftover provider session and is turned away.
A person with a scheduled deletion signs in and can still open Settings to cancel the deletion.
An operator replaces the identity provider by adding an adapter in the factory switch.

where_to_find_it: No control. It runs on every request on the server (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:244-282).

The denial notice titles come from ACCOUNT_DENIAL_NOTICE: 'This account is locked' (action 'Reset your password'), 'Finish recovering this account' ('Continue recovery'), 'This account is suspended' ('Appeal this suspension'), 'This account has been deleted' ('Back to sign-in') (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:32-37).
Recovery pages named in code: /auth/reset-password and /appeal (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:27-28).
prerequisites: A verified sign-in through the hosted identity provider (the only selectable provider is 'clerk') (packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1).
An account profile row; an identity row is linked on first sign-in if the account exists (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:158-168).
screens_and_controls: No screen owns this feature. Clients show the 403 body: message, reason, recoveryPath (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:111-117).
On a device sign-in refresh the denial is returned as error 'account_unavailable' with an optional recovery_url (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts, account_unavailable branch).
journey: The person acts in any app; the app sends a request with a session cookie or bearer token.
The server verifies the token with the identity provider and resolves the subject to an account id.
The server reads the account status (cache first, database second).
If the status is locked, recovery_pending, suspended, banned or deleted the server answers 403 ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE with the reason and recovery path.
Otherwise the request proceeds; a scheduled deletion does not block it.
feedback_and_outputs: 403 with code ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE, reason one of locked, recovery, suspended, deleted, and recoveryPath (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:111-117).
503 'Unable to verify account status. Please try again shortly.' when the lookup fails twice (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:279-282).
Locked message names /auth/reset-password; suspended message cites section 11 of the Terms and says a person reviews every appeal (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:75-95).
settings: AGI_IDENTITY_PROVIDER selects the provider; unset means clerk; any other value throws a config error (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:11-34).
ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN (1, true or on) allows requests when the status lookup fails; default is fail closed (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:269-278).

working: Subject-to-account resolution with a 5 minute key-value cache, database fallback, and an 'erased' outcome distinct from 'unknown' (apps/web/lib/server/identity-account.ts:179-212; apps/web/lib/server/request-context-cache.ts:10).

Seven stored statuses; deletion_scheduled and deleted are derived from a deletion date and an erasure tombstone, and erasure outranks everything (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:1-9, 61-66; apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:12-34).
Denial decisions for locked, recovery_pending, suspended, banned (reported as 'suspended'), deleted (apps/web/lib/auth/account-status.ts:72-100).
Status lookup is cached, retried twice, each try bounded to 2000 ms, and fails closed with 503 (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:109-120, 244-282).
An erased subject is logged as an auth failure 'erased_account' and refused (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:293-303).
An unattended-run query refuses owners whose status is a denying one, derived from the same vocabulary (apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:46-52).
incomplete: The brief says adapters cover password, social, passkey and SSO (brief S89.02). The code has one adapter only, Clerk (packages/platform/identity/src/factory.ts:47-52; packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1). SSO connection code at apps/web/lib/server/sso/clerk-enterprise-connections.ts was not opened [unknown how it ties to the adapter].
Sign-in-completion check fails open on a lookup error, by design, leaving the route gate as the fail-closed layer (apps/web/lib/auth/account-lifecycle.ts:38-46).
disconnected_or_disabled: ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN turns fail-closed into fail-open when set (apps/web/lib/api-auth.ts:269-278). Its production value is unknown.
not_available: A second identity provider: not available in the code (packages/platform/identity/src/types.ts:1).
Per-app behaviour: none recorded; the brief marks every app n/a (brief S89.01).

established.statement: A server-side account service maps every authenticated identity to one AGI account record and enforces account state (active, locked, pending deletion) on each request.
Authentication is delegated to identity-provider adapters (password, social, passkey, SSO) behind one server interface that verifies sessions and fetches users.
Security behaviour fails closed.
A lockout is self-service and a suspension is not; they must not share a message; a scheduled deletion stays allowed.

acceptance_criteria: A locked account gets 403 reason 'locked' with recoveryPath '/auth/reset-password' on any authenticated API route.
A suspended or banned account gets 403 reason 'suspended' with recoveryPath '/appeal'.
A deleted or erased account gets reason 'deleted' with recoveryPath null.
An account with a deletion date but status active is allowed.
When the status lookup fails twice, the request gets 503 unless ACCOUNT_STATUS_FAIL_OPEN is set.
After erasure, a stale provider session for the old subject is refused and logged as 'erased_account'.
inferred: Because every client calls the same web API, one check protects all six apps [inferred]; Local-mode work that never calls the API is not covered by it [inferred].
A cached 'allowed' answer can outlive a new lock for the cache window; the length of the status cache is not in the files read [inferred, unknown TTL].
proposed: [proposed] Add a second adapter behind the factory, or reword brief S89.02 to say Clerk is the single provider, so the brief and code agree.
[proposed] Record which clients render the denial notice titles, per app, so the notice is checked on all six.

steps.what_happens: A client sends a cookie or bearer token; the server verifies it with the identity provider.
The subject is resolved to an account id: cache read, else a database join of identities and erasure_tombstones; an unmapped subject resolves only where the subject is the stored user id.
If the identity row is missing but the account exists it is linked and an identity_linked audit event is written; otherwise last_authenticated_at is touched.
The account status is read from cache or from profiles plus tombstone, bounded to 2000 ms and retried once.
A denying status throws a 403 ACCOUNT_UNAVAILABLE error with reason and recovery path.
The client shows the notice and the recovery link.

features.summary: Lets a person list signed-in sessions and devices, end one or all of them, rename or unlink a device, and stop remote work on it. Command-line and editor sign-ins keep working through rotating refresh tokens; reusing a token revokes its whole family. Devices announce themselves by heartbeat.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides (1) a session list and revoke endpoints backed by the identity provider, (2) a device registry with rename, unlink and stop-remote-work, (3) a rotating device refresh token with replay detection, and (4) a heartbeat that records each client's surface, system, version and capabilities.
purpose.why_it_exists: A person must be able to end a lost or unknown sign-in, and long-lived device sign-ins need credentials that die if copied.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person using Settings; the CLI, VS Code extension, Desktop, Mobile and Chrome extension through their heartbeats and refresh calls.
problems_solved: A stolen refresh token is detected on second use and the family is revoked (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:153-176).
A person can sign out everywhere, including device credentials, in one step (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:189-250).
Sessions older than the lifetime rule end even though the provider keeps renewing them (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts:96-140).
use_cases: A person loses a phone and unlinks it as lost from Linked devices.
A person clicks 'Log out of all devices' after a suspicious sign-in.
A CLI session refreshes its access token every few days without a new browser sign-in.
A team admin removes a member and that member's workspace device tokens die (see F089-06).

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Security section has the rows 'Active sessions' (links to Account) and 'Log out of all devices' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx).
Web: Settings, Account shows the session list; the Linked devices panel has buttons 'Rename' and 'Unlink' (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:321-356).
Desktop: Settings, Account tab, 'Active sessions' with 'Log out of all devices' (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/tabs/Account/CloudAccountControls.tsx:164-178).
Mobile: Account security screen, section 'Sessions' with 'Session timeout' and 'Log out of all devices' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/index.tsx:679-754).
CLI and extensions: heartbeat and refresh run in the background; no screen found.

You will need to sign in again.', confirm button 'Log out everywhere' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SecuritySection.tsx:82-85).
Unlink: confirm title 'Unlink <device>?' with confirm button 'Unlink device' (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:333-337).

Per-session revoke: DELETE /api/settings/sessions/{sessionId} (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts).

The app calls GET /api/settings/sessions and GET /api/settings/devices.
The person picks a session or device and confirms.

The list refreshes; for revoke-all the current session also ends and the person signs in again.
