working: Session list: one page of 100, with total count and truncated flag; sessions past the lifetime bounds are ended while listing and an audit event is written (apps/web/lib/server/session-revocation.ts:46-62; sessions/route.ts:96-176).

Revoke all: rate limit, CSRF, step-up; ends every other session in batches of 10 with up to 3 attempts per session under provider rate limits, then the current session, then device refresh credentials and Ask-from-Siri tokens; emits all_sessions_revoked (sessions/route.ts:189-270; session-revocation.ts:20-27, 93-135).
Single-session revoke route exists (sessions/[sessionId]/route.ts:73).
Device list merges registrations, device-code sign-ins and legacy desktop and mobile rows, max 200, with presence and live-credential flags (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/route.ts:141-246).
Device rename, unlink (options lost, logoutAll) and stop remote work (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts:431-433).
Refresh rotation inside one transaction with row lock; replay finishes the family as compromised, notifies the owner, writes a critical audit event (refresh/route.ts:153-176, 270-300).
Refresh refuses with account_unavailable, terms, or age-review without destroying the family (refresh/route.ts:182-216).
Developer access token lives 7 days; refresh token 30 days (apps/web/lib/server/developer-token.ts:11; apps/web/lib/server/device-refresh-token.ts:5).
Heartbeat upsert keyed on user, surface, install id; first sighting sends a new-device notice (heartbeat/route.ts:24-100).

Heartbeat clients exist on Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and the web desktop-host (apps/desktop/src/services/deviceRegistryHeartbeat.ts; apps/mobile/src/features/device-registry/heartbeat.ts; apps/cli/src/device_registry.rs; apps/extension-vscode/src/features/device-registry/deviceHeartbeat.ts; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/deviceHeartbeat.ts).
incomplete: The first-draft claim that DELETE /api/settings/sessions revokes 'all other sessions' is wrong: it ends every session including the current one (sessions/route.ts:243-270).
Refresh gate for terms only withholds accounts that never accepted, because no binding revision is set (apps/web/lib/server/terms.ts:20; see F089-04).
Session list is capped at 100 rows; the remainder is only counted (session-revocation.ts:46-62).
disconnected_or_disabled: Device sign-in can be toggled in Settings (DeviceSignInToggle component exists); how it gates the refresh route was not traced (apps/web/features/settings/components/DeviceSignInToggle.tsx).
not_available: A session list on the web Security section itself: it only links to Account (SecuritySection.tsx).
Pairing a second device (S89.22) belongs to another feature and is not described here.

established.statement: A session service lists a user's active sessions and revokes one, all others, or all.
Device credentials use rotating refresh tokens with reuse detection, and can be revoked per device or all at once.
A device registry records each signed-in client (surface, OS, version, capabilities, last seen) and lets the user rename or unlink it.
Heartbeat never turns remote work back on by itself; only pairing again does.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/settings/sessions returns at most 100 sessions, a totalCount and truncated true when more exist.
DELETE /api/settings/sessions without CSRF or step-up is refused and ends nothing.
DELETE /api/settings/sessions ends all sessions including the current one and all device refresh credentials.
Using a refresh token twice returns invalid_grant the second time and every later token in that family also fails.
A heartbeat cannot set remote control back to true once stop-remote-work turned it off.
Renaming a device to an empty or 121-character name is refused with the 1 to 120 character message.
A provider 429 during revoke-all produces a 502 'try again to finish' message with counts.
inferred: Web (the only surface not registering) shows as surface 'web' in the list [inferred from the comment in sessions/route.ts:63-70].
Heartbeat is a Cloud-mode feature on the CLI; the other apps' gating by mode is unknown.
proposed: [proposed] Show a clear 'also signs this device out' note next to revoke-all on every app, as the confirm text does on web and desktop.
[proposed] Trace heartbeat gating in Local mode on Desktop and Mobile and add a test like the CLI one.

steps.what_happens: The app calls the sessions or devices endpoint with its credential and CSRF token for writes.
The server lists sessions from the identity provider and joins device_registrations to add OS and surface.
Revoke-all checks rate limit, CSRF and step-up, ends other sessions through the provider in batches, then the current one, then revokes device refresh credentials and writes a security event.
A device sends a refresh token; the server hashes it, locks the family row, checks account status, terms and age review, inserts a new token, marks the old one used, and returns a new access token.
A used token presented again revokes the family, records compromise, notifies the owner and writes a critical audit event.
A client sends a heartbeat every 45 seconds (Desktop) or 5 minutes (others); the server upserts the registration.

A consent and terms store records which Terms version each user accepted and their consents, and blocks use until current Terms are accepted.
A revision of Terms is announced ahead of time and continued use accepts it; only a material change with an effective date forces acceptance.
Documentation availability and account availability are kept separate.

features.summary: A person has a personal workspace and may belong to team workspaces. They pick the active one, and data and policy follow it. A team owner on a team plan can create one workspace, rename it, transfer ownership, and schedule its deletion with a 14 day cooling period that can be cancelled.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the person's workspaces, saves and resolves the active one (a request header beats the saved choice), and lets team admins create and change an organization; the owner can schedule deletion and cancel it.
purpose.why_it_exists: Teams need shared data and shared rules separate from a person's own account, with seat limits and a safe way to delete a team.
purpose.who_uses_it: Team owners and admins; every team member when switching workspace.
problems_solved: Data and policy are scoped to the chosen workspace; a request for a workspace the person is not in is refused (apps/web/lib/services/active-workspace-service.ts:63-84).
A team cannot be deleted by accident: owner only, typed confirmation, legal holds block, 14 day cooling (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:475-575).
Seats cannot exceed the licence (apps/web/lib/services/organization-seat-service.ts:76-90).
use_cases: An employee switches from personal to the company workspace in the account menu.
A manager on a team plan creates the company workspace.
The owner schedules deletion, then cancels within 14 days.
Mobile sends an active-workspace header on each request.

where_to_find_it: Web: account menu workspace switcher; Settings, Team (apps/web/app/settings/team/page.tsx); workspace console at /workspace (nav groups Workspace, People, Controls, Records; links Overview, Members, Roles, Identity ...) (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:38-132).

Desktop: cloud team section (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/cloud/CloudTeamSection.tsx) using /api/settings/organization and /organization/active (apps/desktop/src/api/cloudAccountSettings.ts:662-686).
Mobile: team feature calling /api/settings/organization, /organization/active, transfer-ownership (apps/mobile/src/features/team/service.ts:68-176).
prerequisites: Creating a workspace needs an active plan with team administration (Team, Team Premium or Enterprise plan ids team, team_premium, enterprise) (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:362; apps/web/app/api/settings/team/team-admin-access.ts:63-75).
The person must not already own a workspace (organization/route.ts:244-258).
Deleting needs ownership of the active workspace (organization/route.ts:490).
screens_and_controls: Switch: PUT /api/settings/workspaces with a workspace id or the personal selector (workspaces/route.ts:56-102).
Header selector that wins over the saved choice (active-workspace-service.ts:63-84).
Delete confirmation must match the workspace name or slug (organization/route.ts:505-514).
Cancel deletion: POST /api/settings/organization/deletion/cancel (owner only).
journey: Person opens the switcher; the app lists workspaces (GET /api/settings/workspaces).
Person picks one; the app PUTs the choice; the server saves it and caches it.
Later requests resolve the workspace from header or saved choice.
To delete, the owner types the workspace name; the server checks legal holds and schedules erasure 14 days out.
The owner can cancel any time before the date.
feedback_and_outputs: List: workspaces, activeWorkspaceId, activeOrganizationId, scope 'organization' or 'personal' (workspaces/route.ts:36-50).
Switch result: workspaceId, activeOrganizationId, scope.
Refusals: 'Invalid Managed Cloud workspace selector' (validation), 'You are not a member of that workspace' (403).
Create refusals: 'You already own a workspace. Switch to it from the account menu.', 'Your purchased seats could not be verified...' (503).

Delete message: 'Workspace deletion scheduled. Everything in this workspace will be permanently deleted in 14 days. Cancel from the workspace deletion page, under Settings, Workspace, any time before then to keep it.' with scheduledFor (organization/route.ts:572-576).

Cooling period: ORGANIZATION_DELETION_COOLING_PERIOD_DAYS = 14 (apps/web/lib/server/organization-deletion.ts:10).

List memberships and account workspaces (active-workspace-service.ts:155-181; workspaces/route.ts:30-50).
Switch inside a transaction with an advisory lock; membership checked; value and cache written (workspaces/route.ts:75-90; active-workspace-service.ts:168-232).
Create organization: team-admin gate, one owned workspace, purchased seats read from billing, advisory lock, transaction (organization/route.ts:227-346).
Delete: owner only, name or slug confirmation, legal-hold check, one pending schedule, audit event organization_deletion_requested (organization/route.ts:475-575).

established.statement: An organization service creates, updates, transfers and deletes organizations (workspaces for teams) with owners and seats.
A workspace service lists a user's workspaces (personal and team) and switches the active one, scoping data to it.
A selector that is not a valid id is refused with a validation error; a non-member is refused as forbidden.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and names the consequence; permanent removal happens only from an explicit user action that names what is lost.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/settings/workspaces returns personal scope when no organization is active.
PUT with a workspace the caller is not in returns 403 'You are not a member of that workspace'.
A request header with a valid member workspace id overrides the saved choice for that request.
A user who already owns a workspace gets 409 on POST /api/settings/organization.
A non-owner calling DELETE /api/settings/organization is refused.
DELETE with a wrong name or slug confirmation schedules nothing.
DELETE with an active legal hold is refused with the hold count message.
After scheduling, deletion status shows pending true and canCancel true until the date.
inferred: A scheduled-deletion workspace keeps working until the date [inferred; the enforcement job was not read].
Seat counts come from billing; a workspace without a subscription shows 'unprovisioned' [inferred from seatSource].
proposed: [proposed] Document in the brief that creation needs a team plan and one owned workspace per account.
[proposed] Trace and test the workspace header on CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

features.summary: Admins on a team plan invite people by email, change roles, remove members, manage groups, and build custom roles. Nobody can grant a permission they do not hold themselves. Removing a member also cuts off that member's workspace sessions, device tokens and API keys. Invitation tokens are stored only as hashes.

purpose.what_it_does: Adds, changes and removes members; creates, resends, revokes and accepts invitations; manages workspace groups and group roles; defines built-in and custom roles and checks permissions with an escalation ceiling.
purpose.why_it_exists: A team needs controlled access: who is in, what they can do, and a guarantee that delegation cannot raise anyone above the person delegating.
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins; people holding custom roles; invitees.
problems_solved: A role holding only members.manage cannot promote someone to a role with more permissions than the actor (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/membership-role-ceiling.ts:22-36).
A leaked invitation database does not reveal usable links (hash only) (apps/web/lib/services/organization-invitation-service.ts:20-37).
A removed member loses live access, not only the seat (apps/web/lib/services/deprovision-service.ts:176-250).
use_cases: An admin invites a colleague as viewer; the colleague accepts from the email link.
An owner creates a custom role 'Billing reader' with a few permissions and gives it to a member.
An admin builds a workspace group and sets its members and roles.
An admin removes a leaver and sees how many sessions, device tokens and keys were revoked.

where_to_find_it: Web: workspace console links 'Members' (/workspace/people), 'Roles' (/workspace/roles), 'Identity' (/workspace/identity) (WorkspaceConsoleNav.tsx:51-67); Settings, Team (/settings/team).
Web Roles page cards 'Roles' and 'Additional roles' (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceRoles.tsx:237-243, 482-486).
Mobile: team administration for invitations, role change, remove, transfer (apps/mobile/src/features/team/administration.ts:98-187; service.ts:132-185).
Desktop: cloud team section (apps/desktop/src/api/cloudAccountSettings.ts:723-773).
prerequisites: A team plan (team, team_premium, enterprise) for team administration (team-admin-access.ts:63-75).
Admin or a role holding the needed permission (for example roles.manage, members.manage).
An available licensed seat to add or accept (organization-seat-service.ts:76-83).
screens_and_controls: Role editor labels 'Role name', 'Permissions. You can only grant what your own role holds.', buttons 'Create role' and 'Save role' (WorkspaceRoles.tsx:158-211).
Additional roles card text: 'A member keeps their membership role and gains every permission of each role checked here.' (WorkspaceRoles.tsx:484-486).
Invitation roles allowed: admin, member, viewer (organization/invitations/route.ts:40-44).
Group card: workspace groups are editable; groups from an identity provider are read-only with 'Change it there.' (organization-role-service.ts:530-537 conflict message).
journey: Admin opens Members and enters an email and role.
Server checks the role ceiling, seat room, creates a 7 day invitation, emails the link.
Invitee opens the link and accepts or declines.
On accept the server adds the membership, makes that workspace active, and writes a member_joined audit event.
Admin later changes a role or removes the member; removal triggers deprovisioning.
feedback_and_outputs: Invitation created: 201 with invitation, inviteToken and delivery result (organization/invitations/route.ts:92-125).

Refusals: 'The <Role> role carries permissions you do not hold yourself: ...' (membership-role-ceiling.ts:50-57); 'You cannot grant permissions you do not hold yourself: ...' and 'Only the Primary Owner can hold ..., so no role can carry it.' (organization-role-service.ts:86-107).
Removal result lists revoked sessions, device tokens, API keys and warnings (team/[memberId]/route.ts:90-98).
Card error line 'Could not complete this workspace role action. Try again.' (WorkspaceRoles.tsx:104).

working: Two route families: /api/settings/team (list, add, role change, remove, invitations create, list, resend, revoke, accept) and /api/settings/organization/{members,invitations,groups,roles} which also accept workspace API-key callers (organization/invitations/route.ts:55-90).

Invitation: random 32-byte token, SHA-256 hash stored, expiry, resend count, revoke, list pagination; accept supports decline (organization-invitation-service.ts:20-37; team/invitations/accept/route.ts:60-99).
Role changes and removals need team admin access and CSRF; removal runs deprovisionMember (team/[memberId]/route.ts:38-100).

Deprovision revokes provider sessions only when the workspace was the member's active one, workspace device refresh families, Ask-from-Siri tokens, and workspace API keys, reporting errors as warnings (deprovision-service.ts:100-250).
Groups: workspace-source groups stored in scim_groups can be created, renamed, deleted, given members and roles; directory groups are read-only (organization-role-service.ts:516-640).
Custom roles: create, update, delete with permission ceiling and primary-owner-only permission guard (organization-role-service.ts:86-250).
Membership role ceiling check on invite and role change (membership-role-ceiling.ts:22-60).
Seat ceiling and last-owner protection become friendly 409 errors (organization-seat-service.ts:76-100).

established.statement: A membership service adds, changes and removes members, and removal revokes that member's workspace access and credentials.
An invitation service creates, lists, expires, revokes and accepts invitations with hashed tokens.
A group service manages groups of members and maps groups to roles.
A role/permission service defines built-in and custom roles, checks member permissions, and prevents escalation beyond the actor's own rights.
Never weaken permissions or trust boundaries to make a change pass.

acceptance_criteria: An invitation token is never stored; only its SHA-256 hash is in organization_invitations.
An invitation older than 7 days cannot be accepted.
An 11th resend of one invitation is refused.
A member holding members.manage but not a role's permissions cannot assign that role (403 with the permission list).
Creating a custom role with a permission the actor lacks returns 403 naming it.
A permission only the primary owner may hold returns a validation error saying so.
Removing a member ends that member's workspace device tokens and API keys and reports counts.
Removing or demoting the last owner returns the 'Transfer ownership' conflict.
Adding a member beyond licensed seats returns the 409 seat message.

A member removed from workspace A keeps personal-account sessions [inferred from deprovision comment on sessionsBelongToWorkspace].

features.summary: A server-side gate that applies a workspace's saved rules (managed compute, feature access, surfaces, second-factor requirement, IP allow-list, retention flags, product analytics) to each request, scoped to the workspace the person is using. If the workspace or its policy cannot be read, the request is denied, not treated as having no policy.

purpose.what_it_does: Resolves the caller's active workspace, reads the layered workspace policy (plus per-member overrides), and asks a pure evaluator one question about the request. It answers allowed, denied with a code, or 'unscoped' when no policy governs the request (apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-gate.ts:205-310). Separate helpers answer second-factor, IP allow-list, zero-data-retention, secret-handling and product-analytics questions across all governing workspaces (organization-policy-gate.ts:409-610).
purpose.why_it_exists: A buyer is told the workspace policy binds regardless of which client sent the request. A route that skips the gate makes that false (apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/workspace-policy-coverage.test.ts:19-26). The brief requires every data access to be scoped to the caller and workspace and to apply feature access, MFA, IP allow-list and retention (S89.16, doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/089-account-and-access-components.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins set the policy; every member's requests on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome are governed by it when they reach the web server. The gate itself is called by server routes, not by people.
problems_solved: A workspace with an unreadable policy would silently behave as ungoverned; the gate denies instead (organization-policy-gate.ts:192-197).
A caller could pick a workspace they do not belong to; the gate denies with 'workspace_not_accessible' (organization-policy-gate.ts:216-223).
A delinquent enterprise contract could still buy managed compute from personal scope; the funding organization's billing hold is checked first (organization-policy-gate.ts:199-203, 134-167).
Product analytics could be collected against a workspace's wishes; any governing workspace that forbids them blocks collection (organization-policy-gate.ts:501-513).
use_cases: An admin turns managed compute off for a workspace; a member's chat request to the managed route is refused with 'managed_compute_disabled' (apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/organization-policy-gate.test.ts:206).
An admin requires second-factor sign-in; a member without it is refused on gated routes (apps/web/lib/mfa-policy-gate.ts:1-48, organization-policy-gate.ts:464-499).
An admin sets an IP allow-list; a request from another network is refused with 'ip_not_allowed' (apps/web/lib/ip-allow-list-gate.ts:18-30, 56-66).
The database is down during a policy read; the request is refused with 'workspace_policy_unavailable' and a message telling the person to retry (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:82-88).

where_to_find_it: No screen belongs to the gate itself; the person only sees a refusal message in whichever app made the request [inferred from gate returning a decision with a reason, organization-policy-evaluator.ts:75-104].

Admins edit the policy through GET and PATCH /api/settings/organization/policy and read the effective result at /api/settings/organization/policy/effective (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts:334-335; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/effective/route.ts).
Admins read the security posture through GET /api/settings/organization/posture (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/posture/route.ts:66).
prerequisites: The person is signed in and (for workspace scope) a member of the workspace they select (organization-policy-gate.ts:211-224).
An admin has saved a policy; before that the workspace is ungoverned by design (organization-policy-gate.ts:185-190).
Changing policy needs the 'policy.manage' permission (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts:225-226). Reading posture needs 'audit.read' (posture/route.ts:44-48).
screens_and_controls: Exact admin screen labels for the policy editor: unknown, not traced in this pass.

Refusal text seen by the person: 'We could not confirm your workspace security settings, so this request was stopped. Try again in a moment, and contact your workspace administrator if it keeps happening.' (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:85-86).
Not-a-member text: 'You are not a member of the selected workspace. Choose a workspace you belong to, then try again.' (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:101-102).
Billing-unreadable text on purchases: 'We could not confirm your workspace billing status, so this purchase was stopped. Try again in a moment.' (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:93-94).
journey: 1. The person acts in an app (for example sends a managed chat turn).
2. The app calls a web route; the route calls the gate with the person's id, a question (the 'ask') and the request (organization-policy-gate.ts:205-210).
3. The gate resolves the active workspace; a failed read is retried once (organization-policy-gate.ts:61-71, 213-215).
4. It reads the billing state and the layered policy, applies per-member overrides, and the evaluator decides (organization-policy-gate.ts:248-310).
5. If allowed the route continues; if denied the route returns the reason and code.
6. Failure path: unreadable data produces 'workspace_policy_unavailable' and a log line '[org-policy] ... request denied' (organization-policy-gate.ts:265-269).
feedback_and_outputs: A decision object with allowed, code, reason, obligations and organizationId (organization-policy-gate.ts:57-59).

Decision codes include managed_compute_disabled, feature_disabled, region_not_allowed, surface_not_allowed, mfa_required, billing_read_only, billing_past_due, workspace_policy_unavailable, workspace_not_accessible (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:42-61).
Errors for MFA and IP: 403 with reason 'mfa_required' or 'ip_not_allowed' (mfa-policy-gate.ts:19-26; ip-allow-list-gate.ts:18-24).
Info and error log lines carry the prefix '[org-policy]'.
settings: Workspace policy fields read by the gate: requireMfa, ipAllowList, allowProductAnalytics, zeroDataRetentionOnly, secretHandling, retentionDays, requireLocalToByokPreview, per-surface sync switches (organization-policy-gate.ts:486,510,542,593; organization-policy-evaluator.ts:114-132).
Request-country header name 'x-vercel-ip-country' feeds region rules (organization-policy-gate.ts:51).

working: The gate retries each read once, then denies with 'workspace_policy_unavailable' (organization-policy-gate.ts:48,61-71,264-269).

A purchase ask (credit top-up, seat purchase) is decided on the billing hold alone when only the policy is unreadable; an unreadable billing hold denies the purchase (organization-policy-gate.ts:93-117, 264-276; organization-policy-evaluator.ts:110-112).
Selected-workspace failures below HTTP 500 are denied as 'workspace_not_accessible' (organization-policy-gate.ts:216-223).
Unknown second-factor requirement throws service-unavailable (organization-policy-gate.ts:490-496).

Product analytics: any governing workspace that disallows them returns false, and any read error in the caller collects nothing (organization-policy-gate.ts:501-513; apps/web/lib/server/product-analytics.ts:29-37).
IP allow-list: cached; on read failure the last known list is enforced, and with none known the request is denied (organization-policy-gate.ts:566-596).
Secret handling falls back to the strictest mode ('block') when unreadable (organization-policy-gate.ts:50,419-424,440-444).
A coverage test names every managed-compute route and fails if one stops calling the gate (apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/workspace-policy-coverage.test.ts:34-60).
incomplete: Whether retentionDays is enforced by purge jobs is not established here; the gate only returns it as an obligation (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:114-118). unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: An organization with no saved policy is deliberately answered 'unscoped' (allowed) so existing organizations are not switched off (organization-policy-gate.ts:185-190, 278).
not_available: No desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome code evaluates policy locally; they rely on the web server [inferred: the gate imports server-only modules, organization-policy-gate.ts:1].

established.statement: A resource-authorization layer scopes every data access to the caller and active workspace and applies workspace policy (feature access, MFA, IP allow-list, retention).
An unreadable workspace or policy is not 'no policy'; each read is retried once, then the request is denied as workspace_policy_unavailable, except a purchase that depends only on the billing hold.
A request against a workspace the person cannot access is denied with an explicit decision.
If the second-factor requirement is unknown, the request fails.
Product analytics are blocked if any governing workspace forbids them.
Every managed-compute route must ask the workspace policy.

acceptance_criteria: With no saved policy, a managed-compute ask in that workspace returns allowed with code 'unscoped'.
With managed compute switched off in a saved policy, the ask returns allowed=false with code 'managed_compute_disabled'.
If the policy read fails twice, a non-purchase ask returns 'workspace_policy_unavailable'; a credit top-up with no billing hold is allowed.
If the billing state cannot be read after one retry, a seat purchase is denied.
A selected workspace the caller is not a member of is denied with 'workspace_not_accessible', not treated as personal scope.
If any governing workspace has product analytics off, the analytics check returns false.
If one governing workspace's policy is unreadable and none requires MFA, the MFA check throws service-unavailable.
inferred: Per-surface rules are a configuration control, not a security boundary, because the surface comes from a client-supplied header (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:139-143). [inferred from the code comment]
Cloud mode is governed; Local mode never reaches the gate [inferred: Local inference does not call web routes].
proposed: [proposed] Add a test that lists every route that serves workspace data and fails if it never calls a gate, beyond the managed-compute list.
[proposed] Record in the posture response which gate calls failed closed in the last day, so admins can see unavailable-policy denials.

steps.what_happens: A web route receives a request from any app and calls the gate with the user id and an ask.
The gate resolves the active workspace from the request, retrying once on failure.
It reads billing state and the layered policy from the database, retrying once each.
It applies per-member overrides when the policy has any.
The pure evaluator returns allowed or a denial code; denials are logged.
The route allows the request or returns the denial to the app.

data.retained_or_deleted: Held in server memory; lifetime unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The gate does not call a model or provider. It decides whether a model call may start, and managed-compute asks are the main case (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:23-24). Model and provider restrictions per workspace live in a separate model-policy gate (apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/model-policy-gate.test.ts exists) and are not covered here.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account. Personal scope (no active workspace) is ungoverned for policy except for the funding organization's billing hold (organization-policy-gate.ts:199-203).
access_and_usage.permissions: Reading and changing policy needs 'policy.manage' (policy/route.ts:225-226); posture needs 'audit.read' and team-admin access (posture/route.ts:44-48). The gate itself applies to every member.
access_and_usage.subscription: Billing hold states (read-only, past due) can deny managed compute and purchases (organization-policy-evaluator.ts:55-56). Which plan allows workspace policy editing was not established here. unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: The gate does not meter usage. Rate limits on the admin routes use the 'settings-org' keys (posture/route.ts:33).
access_and_usage.flags: none found in the gate. Tenant lockdown is checked in the directory-sync path, not here.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model specific.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in this gate; provider rules sit in the model-policy gate.

features.summary: Lets an owner connect a company identity provider (SAML or OIDC), prove ownership of the email domain with a DNS record, and switch on just-in-time membership. A separate SCIM 2.0 service lets the company directory create, update and turn off users and groups with a bearer token. Both need an Enterprise plan.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores SSO connections as inactive drafts with a domain challenge, registers them in the hosted identity provider (Clerk) when activated, grants membership at first sign-in from a verified domain, and exposes a first-party SCIM 2.0 server under /api/scim/v2 (apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts:175-306; apps/web/lib/server/sso/jit-provisioning.ts:39-127; apps/web/app/api/scim/v2/Users/route.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: Enterprise buyers need single sign-on and automatic joiner, mover and leaver handling from their directory (S89.17, S89.18 in doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/089-account-and-access-components.md; doc: docs/compliance/directory-sync.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners (create, delete connections), owners and admins (list, token minting), and the customer's identity provider calling SCIM with a token. End users meet it only as the enterprise sign-in.
problems_solved: Someone claiming a domain they do not own: creation is a draft, activation needs a DNS TXT proof (apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts:220-229, apps/web/lib/server/sso/domain-verification.ts:43-47).
Leavers keeping access: deactivating a user through SCIM revokes membership and credentials (apps/web/lib/server/scim/scim-provisioning-service.ts:777-783).
Directory sync running during an incident: a locked-down workspace refuses SCIM (apps/web/lib/server/scim/scim-auth.ts:60-70).
Hostile IdP input: URLs, metadata and attribute mapping are validated before storing (apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts:52-103).
use_cases: An owner adds a SAML connection for example.com, publishes the TXT record, verifies it, then activates it.
A new employee signs in through SSO and is added as 'member' automatically on first sign-in.
The directory sends POST /Users for a new hire; a pending row is created and linked when the person signs in.
The directory sends active=false for a leaver; their seat and credentials are removed.

where_to_find_it: Web: the SSO panel in team settings (apps/web/features/settings/sections/team/SSOPanel.tsx) with labels 'Domain not verified', 'Domain verified', 'Ready to activate', 'Reissue challenge', 'Remove connection', 'Record type', 'Record name', 'Record value', 'ACS URL', 'SP entity ID', 'SP metadata URL' (SSOPanel.tsx:35-44,409-450,496,576).

Web admin: directory sync page with 'Connections', 'SCIM tokens', 'Group role mapping', 'Recent IdP activity', and provider choices 'Microsoft Entra ID' and 'Google Workspace' (apps/web/features/admin/pages/DirectorySyncAdminPage.tsx:66-67,420,506,601,661).
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no screen found for configuration; they only sign in through the hosted flow [inferred, no UI file found by search].
prerequisites: An Enterprise plan on the workspace: other plans get 403 'SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED' (apps/web/lib/server/sso/sso-access.ts:20-22,60-71) and SCIM answers 403 'Directory sync requires an active Enterprise subscription' (scim-auth.ts:111-122).
Owner role to create, verify, delete a connection (admin/sso/route.ts:211-218,339-346); owner or admin to list (route.ts:121-128).
The deployment's Clerk instance must have enterprise connections enabled, or the call returns 503 not-provisioned (clerk-enterprise-connections.ts:140-144 offset; admin/sso/route.ts:356-358).
A SCIM token minted by an owner or admin (apps/web/app/api/admin/directory-sync/tokens/route.ts:52).
screens_and_controls: SSO panel fields: email domain, SAML metadata URL or XML, OIDC discovery URL, client id, client secret (SSOPanel.tsx:118-124,527,611).
Validation messages: 'Enter a company domain, such as example.com.', 'Use an HTTPS metadata URL from your identity provider.' (SSOPanel.tsx:118-122).
Error messages: 'Could not create the SSO connection.', 'Domain verification failed.', 'Could not remove the connection.' (SSOPanel.tsx:295,477,582).
journey: 1. Owner opens the SSO panel and enters domain and SAML or OIDC details; POST /api/admin/sso stores an inactive draft and returns 'nextStep: verify_domain' with a TXT record (admin/sso/route.ts:295-301).
2. Owner publishes the TXT record under '_agiworkforce-sso' and calls verify; a successful lookup sets domain_verified_at (verify-domain/route.ts:94-190; domain-verification.ts:6-8).
3. Owner activates the connection with PATCH /api/admin/sso/{id}; the server creates or updates the connection in Clerk (admin/sso/[id]/route.ts:281-345).
4. Owner turns on just-in-time provisioning and picks 'member' or 'viewer' as default role (admin/sso/[id]/route.ts:46-47).
5. A user signs in; on the first /api/me call the server provisions membership (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:165-173).
6. For SCIM, an admin mints a token; the directory calls /api/scim/v2/Users and /Groups with 'Authorization: Bearer'.
7. Removal: DELETE deactivates by default or hard-deletes with hard=true (admin/sso/route.ts:308-376).
feedback_and_outputs: 201 with connection view and domain instructions on create.
409 'Domain ... is already configured for SSO' on duplicate (admin/sso/route.ts:247-250).
SCIM responses use content type application/scim+json with Bearer challenge on 401 (scim-protocol.ts:48-61).
SCIM create returns 201 with a Location header (apps/web/app/api/scim/v2/Users/route.ts:44-56).

Audit events sso_connection_created, sso_connection_deactivated, sso_connection_deleted, sso_jit_membership_granted, sso_jit_membership_refused (admin/sso/route.ts:281-293,396-408; jit-provisioning.ts:88,110).
settings: jit_provisioning_enabled and jit_default_role per connection (admin/sso/[id]/route.ts:46-47).
Group role mapping on the directory sync page (DirectorySyncAdminPage.tsx:601).
The challenge lasts seven days (domain-verification.ts:10).

working: Create, list, patch, verify, reissue and remove SSO connections with validation and audit (apps/web/app/api/admin/sso/route.ts; verify-domain/route.ts; [id]/route.ts).
SAML connections are created in Clerk with IdP-initiated sign-in off and subdomains off (clerk-enterprise-connections.ts:157-162 approx).
JIT joins only active, domain-verified, JIT-enabled connections, matched by exact domain or subdomain, and refuses with an audit event when no seat is free (jit-provisioning.ts:28-37,49-60,103-123).

SCIM Users and Groups: GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE (apps/web/app/api/scim/v2/Users/[userId]/route.ts:22-59; Groups/[groupId]/route.ts:22-59), plus discovery routes ServiceProviderConfig, Schemas, ResourceTypes.
SCIM auth order: rate limit, bearer token, lockdown check, connection active, token issuer still admin, Enterprise plan (scim-route.ts:10-22; scim-auth.ts:42-122).
SCIM errors are returned as SCIM error bodies with status, detail and scimType (scim-protocol.ts:55-77).
Failed and rejected SCIM requests are recorded as sync events (scim-route.ts:33-52).
incomplete: SCIM POST creates a pending record when no account exists; no account is created and no invitation is sent (doc: docs/compliance/directory-sync.md:50-70). Membership is granted at the person's next sign-in or on a later PUT/PATCH.
Exact SCIM error shapes for every failure were not traced beyond the ScimError class.
disconnected_or_disabled: SSO needs the Clerk Enhanced Authentication add-on; without it the code returns 'not_entitled' (clerk-enterprise-connections.ts:1-5 of the excerpt).
Directory sync is disabled for a locked-down workspace or a disabled connection (scim-auth.ts:60-87).
not_available: No configuration UI on desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome [inferred; no UI file found by search].

established.statement: Admins can configure SSO connections (SAML/OIDC) with domain verification and just-in-time provisioning.
A SCIM adapter creates, updates and deactivates users and groups from the customer's IdP.
Connections are created in the hosted identity provider; the SAML form refuses IdP-first sign-in.
Only the email domain or a subdomain matches a connection.
SCIM user lists are filtered and paged; a create returns 201 with a location header.
SCIM is a first-party service; POST /Users always returns a real resource and a pending user is linked at sign-in.

acceptance_criteria: A new SSO connection is stored with is_active=false and returns a TXT record to publish.
Creating a second connection for the same domain returns 409.
A non-owner calling POST /api/admin/sso is refused.
A user signing in with a verified-domain enterprise account joins as the connection's default role once, and a second sign-in reports 'already_member'.
A SCIM request without a valid bearer token gets 401 with a Bearer challenge.
A SCIM request for a workspace not on an Enterprise plan gets 403.
SCIM POST /Users returns 201 and a Location header ending in /Users/{id}.
SCIM active=false removes the membership and revokes credentials.
inferred: JIT only runs when the person signs in through the web identity handshake (/api/me), so a user who never calls it is not provisioned [inferred from apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:165-173].
SCIM runs only against Cloud; Local mode has no accounts [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show on the SSO panel when a connection is draft, verified and active in one status line with the failing step.
[proposed] Document every SCIM error shape in docs/compliance/directory-sync.md.

steps.what_happens: Owner submits a connection; the server validates the domain, URLs, metadata and mapping, stores an inactive draft with a challenge token, and writes audit events.
Owner publishes a DNS TXT record at their DNS host.
The server resolves the TXT record over DNS and marks the domain verified.
Activation calls the hosted identity provider to create or update the enterprise connection.
A user signs in at the company IdP through the hosted provider; the app then calls /api/me and the server inserts an organization_members row with source sso_jit.
The customer directory calls SCIM; the server authenticates the token, applies the change in scim_provisioned_users and membership, records a sync event.

features.summary: Two kinds of programmatic credentials. Workspace service principals are non-person identities with capped permissions and keys that an admin issues and can disable. Personal API keys belong to a person, are stored as a hash with a prefix, may expire, and can be revoked. Personal access tokens do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Issues, lists, scopes and revokes credentials for automation. A workspace key always belongs to a service principal whose scopes are a ceiling (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/admin-api-keys/route.ts:203-250). A personal key is created for a user with scopes, optional expiry and optional project (apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:71-163).
purpose.why_it_exists: Automation must not borrow a person's identity, and a lost key must be stoppable at once (apps/web/lib/server/service-principal.ts:27-31,189-192). The brief requires bounded scopes, hashed expiring keys and revocation (S89.19, S89.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace admins with 'identity.manage' (workspace keys); any signed-in person on a plan with the managed API capability (personal keys); the support assistant for key regeneration.
problems_solved: An automation acting for a person: refused by assertInteractiveMemberActor (service-principal.ts:87-95).
A key with more power than its maker: scopes must be held by the creator (admin-api-keys/route.ts:122-131).
Key theft: the raw key is shown once and only a hash and prefix are stored (api-key-service.ts:214-228).
Too many keys: 20 active per person (api-keys/route.ts:26,105-109).
use_cases: An admin creates a workspace key for a nightly compliance export with a narrow scope and 90-day expiry.
An admin disables a service principal and all its keys stop.
A developer creates a personal key with the allowed scopes to call the managed API.
A person regenerates a leaked key; the old key is revoked and a new one issued in one step.

where_to_find_it: Web workspace console: 'New workspace API key', fields 'Key name' and 'Workspace API key expiry', and 'Disable principal' (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceApiKeys.tsx:57,253-263; WorkspaceServicePrincipals.tsx:157).
Web personal settings: the 'API keys' control in the Account section (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AccountSection.tsx:458); help link 'Sessions, email and API keys' (AccountSection.tsx:440).
Other apps: no screen found [inferred from search]. Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome can use a key as a client but the creation screens are on web.
Personal access tokens: no screen; the service does not exist (S89.21 'not applicable anywhere').
prerequisites: Personal key creation needs a plan with the 'managed_api' capability, otherwise 403 SUBSCRIPTION_REQUIRED with an upgrade link (api-keys/route.ts:84-92).
Creation needs a step-up check with action 'api_credential.reveal' (api-keys/route.ts:111-117; admin-api-keys/route.ts:133-139).
Workspace keys need the 'identity.manage' permission (admin-api-keys/route.ts:112-117).
screens_and_controls: Error text: 'Could not create this API key. Try again.', 'Could not revoke this API key. Try again.', 'Could not load workspace API keys.' (WorkspaceApiKeys.tsx:165,331,340).
Personal key list shows name, key_prefix, scopes, project, created, last used, expires (api-keys/route.ts:39-50).
Workspace key limits: scopes 1 to 16, expiry in days or none (admin-api-keys/route.ts:49).
journey: 1. Person opens API keys, enters a name, picks scopes and an optional expiry.
2. The app posts to /api/settings/api-keys with a CSRF token; the server checks the plan, the project, and the 20-key cap.
3. The server asks for step-up verification, then applies the 'api-keys-create' rate limit (api-keys/route.ts:111-120).
4. The server stores the hash and prefix and returns the full key once with status 201.
5. The server records an audit event 'api_key_created' and queues a webhook 'api_key.created' (api-keys/route.ts:133-154).
6. Later: revoke with DELETE /api/settings/api-keys/{keyId}; already revoked returns a 'already revoked' message (api-keys/[keyId]/route.ts:44-66).
7. Workspace path: POST /api/settings/organization/admin-api-keys makes or reuses a service principal and returns the key once; DELETE revokes it; PATCH on service-principals disables a principal.
feedback_and_outputs: 201 with api_key (masked) and full_key (once).
Validation message 'You may not have more than 20 active API keys at once' (api-keys/route.ts:106-108).
Refusal naming the missing scope: 'This workspace API key is not scoped for X. It carries Y.' (service-principal.ts:105-107).
Audit events api_key_created, api_key_revoked, admin_api_key_created, admin_api_key_revoked, admin_policy_changed for principal disable.
settings: Idempotency-Key header on workspace key creation (admin-api-keys/route.ts:119,185-195).
Principal scope ceiling (max_scopes) and disabled_at (service-principal.ts:41-50).

working: Service principal helpers: actor prefix 'service_principal:', interactive-actor refusal, scope check naming the missing scope, ceiling check, create, list, read, disable (apps/web/lib/server/service-principal.ts:14-211).
Workspace key route: list, create (step-up, creator's own permissions bound the scopes, idempotent mint in one transaction), revoke (admin-api-keys/route.ts:104-296).
Principals route: GET and PATCH only (service-principals/route.ts:88-89).
Personal key route: list, create with plan gate, step-up, rate limit, 20-key cap, project check, audit and webhook (api-keys/route.ts:52-166).
Hashing with argon2id and an 8-character-style public prefix pattern 'sk_live_<16 hex>' (api-key-service.ts:9-21,53-60).
Verification skips revoked, expired or archived-project keys and updates last_used_at (api-key-service.ts:244-293).
Rotation: transaction, lock the row, refuse if project or metadata changed, revoke old and insert new (api-key-service.ts:145-197).
incomplete: Personal key rotation has no settings route: the only caller found is the support assistant action (apps/web/lib/support/actions/executors/regenerate-api-key.ts:32-40; registry). The first draft listed rotation under /api/settings/api-keys, which is not what the code shows.
There is no 'create service principal' route; a principal is created as a side effect of creating a workspace key without a principal id (admin-api-keys/route.ts:229-236).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found
not_available: Personal access tokens: not available on any app (S89.21).
Key creation screens on desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not found.

established.statement: A service principal cannot perform an action that acts for a person.
A service principal may use only the scopes it holds; a call outside them is refused naming the missing scope.
Scopes requested for a principal above its ceiling are refused.
Each person may have at most 20 active keys.
Creating a key needs step-up and a rate limit.
Keys are stored as a hash plus a prefix.
A project that does not exist or is archived is refused.
Admins can create service accounts with bounded scopes and credentials; the API-key service issues hashed, expiring, revocable keys; personal access tokens are not applicable.
New personal keys require at least one managed API scope.

acceptance_criteria: Creating a 21st active personal key returns a validation error.
Creating a personal key without a recent step-up is refused.
The create response includes full_key once, and the list never does.
A workspace key request for a scope the admin does not hold returns 403 listing the refused scopes.
Using an existing principal with a scope above its ceiling returns 403 naming the principal.
A disabled principal cannot receive a new key.
Rotating a key whose project was archived is refused and the old key stays active.
A key that is revoked or past expiry fails verification.
inferred: Disabling a principal stops all its keys because key verification joins the principal [inferred from service-principal.ts:189-192 comment; the verifying query was not opened].
Local mode needs none of these credentials [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a settings route and button for personal key regeneration so it is not only reachable through the support assistant.
[proposed] Apply the rate limit before the database count and step-up on personal key creation so refused callers cost less.

steps.what_happens: The app posts a create request with CSRF token and chosen scopes.
The server checks plan capability, project, and active key count.
The server requires step-up verification, then applies the rate limit.
A new raw key is generated, hashed with argon2id, stored with its prefix; the raw key is returned once.
Audit event and webhook event are queued.
A client later sends the key; the server finds the row by prefix, checks revoked, expiry and project, verifies the hash and updates last_used_at.

features.summary: Links a phone to a signed-in computer or account with a short code and QR, so the phone can follow and steer coding sessions (Remote Control). The web server checks the account, plan and switches, the relay mints credentials, and the relay refuses a claim from a different account. It needs Cloud and a paid plan; mobile v1 hides it.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a pairing session on the relay through POST /api/pair/initiate, lets the phone claim it through POST /api/pair/claim, and keeps the pairing bound to one account (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:47-175; apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:47-173; services/signaling-server/src/pair-token.ts:95-105).
purpose.why_it_exists: The relay has no way to verify a user token, so the web server establishes the account and tells the relay; this stops a scanned QR joining a stranger's desktop (claim/route.ts:37-46).
purpose.who_uses_it: A person with a desktop (Electron desktop shows the hosted web page; CLI; VS Code extension) and a phone. The brief calls it the remote-device pairing service (S89.22).
problems_solved: Joining another person's desktop with a guessed or shared code: refused with 'pairing_belongs_to_another_account' (claim/route.ts:134-147).
Pairing when the plan, workspace policy or the switch forbid it: refused before any relay call (initiate/route.ts:66-67).
Pairing that works without the relay: refused with 503 (initiate/route.ts:69-80).
Stale pairings piling up: the relay sweeps them (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:425-435).
use_cases: A developer starts Remote Control on the desktop web app, shows a QR, and approves a phone to read diffs and steer a session.
The CLI starts a pairing and prints a QR for the phone.
The VS Code extension asks for a pairing and shows a prompt naming the phone before it can steer sessions (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts:87-92).
A phone enters a typed code on its own and claims it through the gateway.

where_to_find_it: Web (also the Electron desktop window): section headed 'Remote Control' with text 'Pair your phone to follow Code sessions running on this computer: approve steps, read diffs, test results and new files, and steer the next turn.' (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx:37-39).

Mobile: Settings screen titled 'Remote control' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/remote-control.tsx:181), but it renders 'FeatureUnavailable' with feature 'Remote' because the companion flag is false (remote-control.tsx:131; apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:16).
CLI: remote control module starts a pairing against /api/pair/initiate and prints a QR (apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs:24,241-280; claude_parity.rs:1834).
VS Code: remote-control feature service (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts).
Tauri desktop store also calls /api/pair/initiate (apps/desktop/src/stores/connectionStore.ts:692). Chrome extension: no pairing code found.
prerequisites: Signed in on the host device (initiate/route.ts:55-61).

A plan with the 'remote_control' capability; otherwise the web shows 'Remote Control comes with paid plans.' and the API returns 'plan_upgrade_required' (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:9-15 of the plan check; RemoteControlSection.tsx:50).
Workspace policy allows the 'remote_control' feature and the switch is on (remote-control-gate.ts:44-62).
Server configured with relay address and internal secret (initiate/route.ts:69-80).
Mobile: the companion feature flag on, which is off in v1 (v1FeatureFlags.ts:16).
screens_and_controls: Pair button and Stop control in RemoteControlSection; failure text 'Pairing could not start.' (remote-pairing.ts:5; RemoteControlSection.tsx:47-48).
Disconnect text: 'Your phone disconnected. It reconnects on its own while Remote Control is on. To pair a different phone, stop Remote Control and pair again.' (RemoteControlSection.tsx:44).

Phone messages: 'This QR code was made by an older Desktop version. Update AGI Workforce on Desktop, generate a new code, and scan it again.' and 'The 12-character code alone can no longer secure this connection. Scan the QR code in the pairing window on Desktop.' (apps/mobile/services/manualPairing.ts:23-26).
journey: 1. Host starts pairing; POST /api/pair/initiate with CSRF, rate limit 'device-link' and the standing check.
2. The server calls the relay's POST /pairings with the internal secret and the account id; relay returns a 12-character code, expiry, URLs and a pair token for the initiator (index.ts:703-760).

3. The host shows a QR. The web server's own response has qrData 'agiw:<code>' (initiate/route.ts:171) but desktop, CLI and web compose an 'agiw3:' payload that adds a pairing secret (apps/web/features/remote-dispatch/lib/browser-pairing.ts:5; apps/cli/src/remote_control/mod.rs; apps/desktop/src/stores/connectionStore.ts).
4. The phone scans or types the code; it posts to /api/pair/claim with its session.
5. The server asks the relay to claim with role 'mobile' and the account id; the relay refuses with 403, 404 or 409 when not allowed (claim/route.ts:125-147).
6. The phone gets a pair token and relay address and connects over a secure WebSocket (connectionStore.ts:1010-1035).
7. VS Code asks the person to confirm the phone before it may steer.
feedback_and_outputs: Initiate returns code, expiresAt, expiresIn, qrData, signaling URLs, pairTokens for the initiator (initiate/route.ts:167-174).

Claim errors: 'pairing_not_found' 404, 'pairing_role_in_use' 409, 'pairing_belongs_to_another_account' 403, 'Signaling server unavailable' 503, 'Failed to claim pairing session' 502 (claim/route.ts:122-152).
Audit events remote_pairing_initiated and remote_pairing_claimed, with a failure outcome for rejected claims (claim/route.ts:135-170).

established.statement: A pairing service links a second device to a signed-in desktop or account with a short code and binds it to the account.

Missing relay URL or secret returns 503 'Pairing is not configured'.

claim of an unknown or expired code returns 404 'pairing_not_found'.
A second phone claiming the same pairing gets 409 'pairing_role_in_use'.
A claim code that is not 12 letters or digits returns 400 'Invalid pairing code'.
An unreachable relay returns 503 'Signaling server unavailable' and is logged.

steps.what_happens: Host app asks the web server to start a pairing.
The web server checks session, CSRF, rate limit, plan, policy and the switch.
The web server calls the relay with a shared internal secret to create a pairing with the account id.
The relay stores the pairing and issues the initiator's pair token.
The host shows the code and QR; the phone scans it.
The phone posts to /api/pair/claim; the web server asks the relay to claim with the account id.
The relay compares accounts, rotates the credential and returns a token; the phone then opens a WebSocket to the relay.

features.summary: Lets a person download their data and delete their account, and lets an owner delete a workspace. Deletion is scheduled with a cooling period, cancellable, then a nightly job erases every store, refuses when a legal hold applies, leaves a tombstone, and reports which stores succeeded or failed.

purpose.what_it_does: Exports account data through GET and POST /api/user/export and archive routes, schedules account deletion through DELETE /api/user/delete-account, schedules workspace deletion through DELETE /api/settings/organization, and runs scheduled erasure through cron routes (apps/web/app/api/user/export/route.ts:3456-3458; apps/web/app/api/user/delete-account/route.ts:616-617; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:582; vercel.json:90-96).
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to take and remove their data; a legal hold must stop erasure; the product must show what is kept and why (S89.23; doc: docs/compliance/legal-hold-and-ediscovery.md:37-60).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person (account export and deletion); workspace owners (workspace deletion); compliance staff reading the retention manifest.
problems_solved: Half-erased accounts: each store reports success or failure and a failed store is retried (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:440-460; deletion-manifest.ts:584-612).
Erasing under a legal hold: the whole erasure is refused (account-erasure.ts:893-976; organization-erasure.ts:285-306).
Orphaned stored files and backup copies: files and backup copies are deleted (account-erasure.ts:763-820).
Re-creation of an erased subject: a tombstone row remembers it (account-erasure.ts:1203-1215).
use_cases: A person requests their data export and downloads the archive.
A person deletes their account, changes their mind within the cooling period and cancels.
An owner deletes a workspace; 14 days later the job erases it and cancels its seat subscription.
An account under a legal hold requests deletion; the job keeps all data and reports the hold.

where_to_find_it: Web: Account section with controls 'Delete account' and the notice 'Account deletion scheduled' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/AccountSection.tsx:466,510).

prerequisites: Signed in. Delete needs CSRF, a rate limit 'user-data-delete' and a step-up check (delete-account/route.ts:386-389,462).
A paid plan must be settled first: the route refuses with a message when a plan change is scheduled or a subscription must be handled (delete-account/route.ts:500-510).
Workspace deletion: owner with the right permission (organization route; not traced in detail).
screens_and_controls: Cancel control while the schedule is still cancellable (can_cancel in delete-account/route.ts:348).
Refusal text example: 'Your <plan> plan has a scheduled change, so nothing was deleted. Keep your current plan in Settings > Billing, then delete your account.' (delete-account/route.ts:503-504).
Error text: 'Account deletion could not be scheduled. Nothing was deleted. Please try again, or contact <support email> if this persists.' (delete-account/route.ts:533-536 region).
journey: 1. Person opens Account settings and chooses 'Delete account'.
2. The server checks sign-in, CSRF, rate limit and step-up, then schedules deletion for 24 hours later by setting deletion_scheduled_for on the profile (delete-account/route.ts:481,523-529).
3. The page shows 'Account deletion scheduled' with a cancel option until the time arrives.
4. The nightly job purge-deleted-accounts picks due accounts and runs the erasure (cron route; schedule '7 4 * * *' in vercel.json).
5. Erasure checks legal holds, media jobs, deletes files and rows, anonymises financial records, records a tombstone and a report.
6. A failed store leaves the profile for the next run; a success removes the profile.
7. Workspace: DELETE schedules 14 days ahead; cancel at /api/settings/organization/deletion/cancel; job purge-deleted-organizations erases it ('12 4 * * *').
feedback_and_outputs: Erasure report with counts per store, anonymised stores, complete flag and profileRetained (account-erasure.ts:440-460).
Deletion status values pending, blocked, partial, complete with human reasons (deletion-manifest.ts:563-612).
Held report text: 'Subject is under an active legal hold; data preserved.' or 'Legal hold status could not be read, so nothing was erased: ...' (account-erasure.ts:950-957).
Audit event deletion_blocked_by_legal_hold (doc: docs/compliance/legal-hold-and-ediscovery.md:61-65).
settings: Account deletion delay is 24 hours (delete-account/route.ts:481); workspace delay is 14 days (apps/web/lib/server/organization-deletion.ts:10).
Retention manifest: apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts RETENTION_MATRIX.

working: Account erasure refuses under a member, custodian or workspace legal hold, and refuses when the hold cannot be read (account-erasure.ts:893-933).

Knowledge object files, avatar, feedback screenshots and media are deleted with their backup copies; untracked knowledge ledger rows must be settled or the erasure throws (account-erasure.ts:763-857).
A tombstone row is opened, advanced and closed (account-erasure.ts:1203-1260).
Organization erasure refuses under an active legal hold and when the seat subscription cannot be canceled, keeping the workspace for the next run (organization-erasure.ts:285-350).
The deletion manifest lists each store with retention and a deletion path (deletion-manifest.ts:289-518).
Export has tests that it covers personal data and matches the erasure inventory (apps/web/app/api/user/export/__tests__/export-matches-erasure-inventory.test.ts).

established.statement: An export/deletion coordinator produces the user's export and erases account and organization data across every store, honouring legal holds and recording what is retained.
Account erasure deletes stored files and their backup copies and leaves a tombstone.
Organization erasure is blocked by an active legal hold; data is kept and the report says so.
If the seat subscription cannot be ended, the workspace is kept and the report says why. (The first draft called this a billing hold; the code reports a failed subscription cancellation.)
Untracked knowledge ledger rows block erasure until settled.
A held deletion is recorded, not only refused; a hold placed before the delete wins.
A pairing in the relay lasts at most eight days including the sweep.

acceptance_criteria: Deleting an account sets deletion_scheduled_for about 24 hours ahead and nothing is erased immediately.
Cancelling before the time clears the schedule.
The purge job erases a due account with no hold and removes its files.
The purge job on a subject with an active hold erases nothing and reports the hold.
If the hold query fails, nothing is erased.
A workspace deletion schedules 14 days ahead and the cancel route reverses it.
Organization erasure keeps the workspace when the seat subscription cannot be canceled.
The export matches the erasure inventory: every personal table is exported or listed as not exported with a reason.
inferred: Local-mode data on the device is not touched by the coordinator [inferred: it runs only on the server].
Per-store retention such as audit logs follows the manifest, not this feature's code [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show the person which stores are pending in the account screen using DeletionOutcome.
[proposed] Provide export and deletion entry points on mobile for store review expectations.

features.summary: Platform staff can read a workspace's data only under a grant that has a reason, a ticket, a purpose, named scopes, a limited window and approval by a second operator. Every request, decision, read, refusal and expiry is written to a hash-chained trail the workspace can read.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides request, approve, deny and revoke actions on support access grants, a gate that refuses reads no live grant covers, an expiry sweep, and a verifier for the hash chain (apps/web/app/api/admin/support-access/route.ts; apps/web/lib/server/support-access-service.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: Customers must be able to trust that staff cannot read their data without their knowledge; the brief requires a recorded reason, second operator, time limit and logging (S89.24; doc: docs/compliance/soc2-controls.json AC-04).
purpose.who_uses_it: Platform operators on the allow-list, workspace owners and admins who read their own grants and events, and auditors.
problems_solved: One person granting themselves access: refused in code and by a database constraint (support-access-service.ts:489-491 area; migration 0229).
Open-ended access: the window defaults to one hour and is capped at eight hours (support-access-service.ts:58-59).
Edited logs: each event hashes the previous one, so removal or edits are detectable (support-access-service.ts:342-369).
Silent refusals: a refused read is recorded before the error (support-access-service.ts:705-726).
use_cases: An operator opens a ticket-based grant to read a workspace's conversations to debug an issue; a colleague approves for one hour.
A security investigation grant allows reading data that a normal support grant withholds (Google user data).
An operator lists background jobs across workspaces and sees content only for workspaces a live grant covers.
An auditor verifies the trail for a workspace.

where_to_find_it: Web admin API only: GET and POST /api/admin/support-access (apps/web/app/api/admin/support-access/route.ts:94-215). No admin screen for it was found by search [inferred].
Workspace owners and admins read their own grants and events through database row policies (apps/web/db/neon/0229_support_access_grants.sql header comment); a screen for this was not found.
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: none.
prerequisites: The caller's id is on the platform operator allow-list set by the PLATFORM_ADMIN environment setting; otherwise every platform-admin surface answers 404 (apps/web/lib/auth-guards.ts:26-50).
A desktop device token is refused for this surface (auth-guards.ts:40-42).
CSRF token and rate limit 'admin-security' on writes (route.ts:96-100).
screens_and_controls: Request body: action 'request', organizationId, reason (at least 20 characters), ticketRef (3 to 128 characters), purpose (support, security, abuse, legal, customer_consent), scopes (conversations, files, projects, connectors, billing, audit_logs, workspace_settings, background_jobs) (route.ts:34-41; support-access-service.ts:14-34,61-64).
Decision body: action approve, deny or revoke, grantId, optional ttlMs up to eight hours (route.ts:43-47).
List query: organizationId, status, limit, and action=verify to check the trail (route.ts:94-135).
journey: 1. Operator A posts action 'request' with reason, ticket, purpose and scopes; a pending grant and a 'requested' event are written; response 201.
2. Operator B posts action 'approve'; the server refuses if B is the requester, sets the expiry as the smaller of the chosen window and eight hours from the request, and appends 'approved'.
3. While the grant is live, the gate allows reads in its scopes for operator A only; each read appends an 'accessed' event with row count.
4. The grant ends by expiry sweep (cron route), revoke, or deny; the trail records it.
5. Anyone may verify the chain with GET action=verify.

Error 'A break-glass grant needs a second operator: the requester cannot approve their own access.' (support-access-service.ts:489-491).

established.statement: Administrative access to customer data requires a recorded reason, a second operator's approval, a time limit, and is logged.
Approval by the requester is refused.
The window defaults to one hour and is at most eight hours.
Expired grants move to an expired state in the trail.
Each event is written to a hash chain.
Every grant creation writes an audit event; each data read is also recorded.
Operator access to a workspace's data requires a grant the workspace can see in a hash-chained trail.

acceptance_criteria: A request with a reason shorter than 20 characters is refused.
The requester approving their own grant is refused.
An approved grant's expiry is never more than eight hours after the request.
A read under no live grant throws SupportAccessDeniedError and writes a 'refused' event first.
A read by another operator using a colleague's grant is refused.
After revoke or expiry the same read is refused.
Changing any trail row makes verify report the broken entry.
Unapproved background-job listing shows no content for a workspace without a grant.

Workspace-visible trail depends on row policies in migration 0229 [inferred from its header].
proposed: [proposed] Add a workspace-facing screen listing grants and events.
[proposed] Make a failed trail append fail the read for operator reads, not only log it.
[proposed] Resolve the single-operator limitation recorded in the control register before claiming operation.
