features.summary: The server keeps every Cloud chat and every message of it, scoped to the signed-in user and the active workspace. Apps create, list (paged), open, update and soft-delete chats, and append messages. The mobile app, Chrome side panel, CLI and Tauri desktop reach the same routes. Web and mobile screens differ in how they page.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores each Cloud chat as a row in web_conversations and each turn (a user question or an assistant answer) as a row in web_messages, and exposes create, list, read, update, soft-delete and message append through server routes (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:330-331; apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:590-592; apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/route.ts:155-156).
purpose.why_it_exists: So history is durable and the same chat can be listed, opened and continued from any app signed in to the account (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/090-conversation-and-synchronization-components.md, S90.01 and S90.02; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:775 row W02).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people using Cloud mode on web, mobile, the Chrome side panel, the CLI and the internal Tauri desktop. Engineers and testers use the routes as the contract for chat history.
problems_solved: History lost when a device or browser tab is closed.
A chat started on a phone cannot be continued on the web without a shared store.
Long histories need paging so a list or a chat does not load everything at once.
Retried saves must not duplicate a message (the insert is idempotent on the client message id: apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/message-thread.ts:33-45).
use_cases: Send a first message on web: a chat row is created and the message is saved to it.
Open the chat list on mobile, tap Load older chats, and older chats append.
Open a saved chat on web: the client fetches the messages in pages of up to 500 until none are left.
Delete a chat: it is soft deleted and disappears from the list on every device.

where_to_find_it: Web: the chat list in the sidebar and the chat page at /chat/[id] (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:7152 passes onLoadMoreSessions; apps/web/shared/components/layout/WebAppShell.tsx:575).
Web Desktop (Electron) shows this same hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: the chats list screen (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx) with controls labelled Load older chats (:832) and Retry loading chats (:816).
Chrome side panel: creates Cloud conversations through the shared client (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:9080).
CLI: pushes and pulls chat records through the sync route (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs:13, :294-332).
Tauri desktop (internal): CloudRuntime lists conversations with the shared client (apps/desktop/src/runtime/CloudRuntime.ts:1737).
prerequisites: A signed-in account; every route resolves the user and workspace through getUserScopedDb (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:36).
Cloud mode. On the Tauri desktop the Cloud persistence client throws unless the app is in managed Cloud mode with an account session (apps/desktop/src/lib/cloudChatPersistence.ts:49-62).
For mobile cloud sync: the cloudChat feature flag, cloud app mode and a cloud account (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:98-105).
screens_and_controls: Sidebar list rows (web) built from the chat store (apps/web/shared/components/layout/sidebar-session-rows.ts:34).
Mobile list with Load older chats button, Loading chats and Loading older chats indicators (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/ChatsListScreen.tsx:816-874).
Mobile chat menu: Share, Rename, Pin/Unpin, Move to project, Duplicate, Mark as read/unread, Archive, Delete (apps/mobile/src/features/conversation-actions/useConversationActions.ts:262-300).
Web conversation title menu opened by the button labelled Conversation options (apps/web/features/chat/components/ConversationTitleMenu.tsx:140).
journey: Person types and sends the first message in a new chat.
The client creates the chat (POST /api/chat/conversations) with a client-chosen id, title and model, or the server generates an id (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:275-300).

The client saves each turn with POST /api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages; the server inserts the row and moves the visible leaf to it (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:101-134).
The chat appears in the list only after it has at least one live message (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:82).
Later the person opens the list on another device; the first page loads, and older pages load on request.
Opening a chat loads its messages in pages until all are read (web: apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:729-766).
feedback_and_outputs: Mobile list failure text: Chats could not be refreshed. Check your connection and try again. (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:468-531).
A chat deleted or no longer owned answers Conversation not found (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:123-125).

On the Free plan a spent daily allowance answers HTTP 429 with a message saying how many chats or messages Free accounts can save a day and that they return after midnight UTC (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:180-187, :355-381).

During a planned maintenance window a new chat is refused with New chats are paused for planned maintenance until <time>. Try again after it ends. (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:202-209).
Create returns 201 with the conversation; a reused id that now belongs to a deleted or foreign chat returns 409 conversation_unavailable (route.ts:305-323).
settings: Page sizes are contract constants: default 50, maximum 100 chats per page, maximum 500 messages per conversation read (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversations.ts:87-89).
Title cap comes from conversation-contract.json titleMaxLength (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversation-contract.json:2).
Message content cap 100,000 characters on write and 1,000,000 stored (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversations.ts:19-20).

working: Create chat with idempotent upsert on a client id, scoped to user and workspace (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:270-300).
List chats: pinned first then newest, filtered by project, title text (q), archived and deleted filters (route.ts:60-136).
The list accepts a keyset cursor or an offset and returns nextCursor, nextOffset and hasMore (route.ts:71, :103-106, :154-160).
Read one chat with messages by limit and offset, with an ETag carrying the server version (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:91-168).
Separate keyset-paged message list route GET /api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/route.ts:45-97).
Append a message, idempotent on a client id; the assistant role stores the model (messages/lib/message-thread.ts:33-45; persist-message.ts:91-99).

Soft delete of a chat sets deleted_at, clears the cached compaction summary, revokes shares and published artifacts of that chat and releases the sandbox (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:38-50, :533-558, :577).
Restore route exists for soft-deleted chats (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/restore/route.ts; exact behaviour not opened).
Mobile lists with a cursor when one is returned, otherwise offset (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatMessageStore.ts:468-531).
CLI pushes chat title, model, project and text messages through /api/chat/sync (apps/cli/src/cloud/chat.rs:294-332).
incomplete: Web paging uses offset only: the sidebar list reads limit and offset (apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:196, :552). The brief's keyset paging is therefore only used by mobile among the clients I opened.
The message-only keyset route GET .../messages has no caller in the web hook I read; web opens a chat through GET .../[id] by offset (useConversations.ts:729-766). Other callers unknown.

A POST message stores role, content, model (assistant only), metadata and parent; its insert does not write provider or token counts (message-thread.ts:33-45). The read routes return provider and token columns (messages/route.ts:68), so where those are written is not established here (unknown).
A chat with no live message is hidden from the list (route.ts:82), so a just-created empty chat does not appear until its first message is saved.
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile cloud sync engine only runs when the cloudChat feature flag is true, the app is in cloud mode and a cloud account exists (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:98-105).
The Tauri desktop persistence client is blocked in Local and own-key modes by design (apps/desktop/src/lib/cloudChatPersistence.ts:6-12, :49-55).

The migration headers for the parent column, drafts and star/archive columns still say NOT YET APPLIED (apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:4; 0219_conversation_drafts.sql:3; 0059_conversation_star_archive.sql:13). The routes select those columns, so applied status in each environment is unknown.
not_available: VS Code extension: its managed chat client is used for projects and artifacts clients (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/projects/projectsClient.ts:72; artifactsClient.ts:95); a saved-chat list was not found in the files I opened (unknown).
Local mode chats are not stored on the server by design; where web Local chats are stored on the device was not opened (unknown).

established.statement: S90.01: conversations are durably stored per user and workspace, created, listed with keyset paging, read, updated and soft-deleted through a server API.
S90.02: each turn is durably stored against its conversation with role, content, model, usage and metadata, and can be listed and appended.

Create, send, edit, regenerate, branch, archive, restore and delete must keep conversation and message lineage after reload; double submission or reconnect must not create duplicate turns; failed persistence must be visible and recoverable.
History paging must not skip a row when an item is removed or restored before the next page loads; deleted, temporary, foreign-account and inaccessible-workspace content stays excluded.
Temporary chats are not stored.

acceptance_criteria: A message POSTed to a chat is returned by the next read of that chat, with the same id when a client id was supplied.
Sending the same message id twice leaves one row.
A chat with 120 messages opens complete on web; the page loop ends when hasMore is false.
The list returns pinned chats first, then newest, and following nextCursor never repeats or skips a chat on mobile.
A deleted chat is absent from the list, from a read (404) and from message save.
A Free account at its daily chat or message limit receives HTTP 429 with the free_daily_* code; a paid account is not refused by that check.
A user cannot read or write another user's or another workspace's chat (404).
inferred: [inferred] The brief's 'platform done' for all apps means the server routes are done; per-app screens were assessed separately above.
[inferred] A malformed cursor silently restarts from the first page because decodeKeysetCursor returns null for bad input (apps/web/lib/identity/pagination.ts:45-57; route.ts:71).
proposed: [proposed] Move the web list and open-chat hooks to cursor paging, matching the brief and mobile.
[proposed] Return 400 for a malformed cursor instead of restarting.
[proposed] Show a visible error when a Free allowance is spent while the composer is sending (not verified how web shows it).

steps.what_happens: Client builds a create request (id, title, model, project, temporary flag).
Server checks the user, CSRF, rate limit, maintenance window, project ownership and the Free daily chat allowance, then upserts the row.
Client saves each turn; server locks the thread when the chat is branched, inserts the message with a parent and moves the active leaf.
After an assistant message is saved, artifact indexing is scheduled in the background.
A list read runs a scoped SQL query ordered by a pinned-first text key and returns a cursor.
The client renders the page and requests the next page from nextCursor (mobile) or nextOffset (web).
Delete sets deleted_at in one transaction with share and published-artifact revocation, then releases the sandbox session.

data.what: Chat row: id, owner, workspace, title, model, route, project, pinned, starred, archived, temporary flag, active leaf, draft, instructions, timestamps, server version, deleted_at
data.synced: Yes: read by every app through the routes and the sync pull
data.retained_or_deleted: Soft delete sets deleted_at; restorable within a recovery window named RESOURCE_RECOVERY_WINDOW_DAYS (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:74-83); the window length was not read.

data.what: Message row: id, chat, role, content, model, provider, token counts, metadata, parent
data.retained_or_deleted: A single message delete is a hard delete (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/message-thread.ts:370-380); a whole-chat delete is soft.

data.what: On-device chats in mobile Local mode
data.synced: No; Local chats never leave the device (apps/mobile/src/features/conversation-actions/useConversationActions.ts:103-106)
data.retained_or_deleted: Delete from this device cannot be restored (same file, delete alert).

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Saving and listing chats calls no model. The assistant message stores the model name it was given. Which model answers is decided elsewhere (SYS-chat-turn-pipeline). Free plan allowance counting is a database count, not a provider call.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account is required on every route; rows are scoped to user_id and the active workspace (organization_id) (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:78-80).
access_and_usage.permissions: Owner-only: every query filters on user_id and workspace. A foreign or missing chat answers 404. The sync route also passes a workspace policy gate named chat_sync (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:551; apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:262-282).
access_and_usage.subscription: The Free plan has a hard daily cap on chat creates and message writes; other plans have no hard limit from this check (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:389-390). Entitlement is resolved from the plan tier (same file:523-537). Linked to SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Free daily caps: 1000 message writes and 100 conversation creates per UTC day (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:485-486); counted from the tables, not a separate meter (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:131-148). If the count cannot be read the write is allowed (tier-unit-quota-service.ts:391-404). Rate limits use named buckets chat-conversation-list, chat-conversation-read, chat-conversation, chat-message.
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile: FEATURES.cloudChat (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:100). Server: maintenance window for new chats (route.ts:202). No flag found for the web routes.

features.summary: Edits and regenerations are kept as sibling messages under one parent, and the chat records which path is visible. A fork copies the chat up to a chosen message into a new chat linked to its source. Web and mobile can fork; web shows a version pager on turns.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a chat as a tree through web_messages.parent_id, records the visible path in web_conversations.active_leaf_message_id, and creates forked chats that copy messages up to a fork point and are linked in conversation_branches and conversation_branch_messages (apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql:36-53; apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:194-479).
purpose.why_it_exists: Replacing a regenerated answer or an edited question in place destroys the earlier one; the product contract says in-place replacement is not acceptable when later turns depend on the old message (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:417-429).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who regenerate answers, edit earlier questions, or want to try another direction without changing the original chat.
problems_solved: Lost earlier answers after Regenerate.
Lost later turns after editing a question.
No way to explore a side path without altering the source chat.
Duplicate forks from a retried request (idempotent request id).
use_cases: Regenerate an answer and page back to the first one.
Edit the opening question and keep both versions with their own replies.
Branch a chat from a message to try a different model or direction.
Duplicate a whole chat on mobile (fork from the last message).

established.statement: S90.03: regenerations and edits of a turn are kept as versions (siblings of one parent) and the visible version is recorded so users can page between versions.
S90.04: conversation lineage is a graph: messages form a parent tree and forks create a new conversation linked to its source message.
Edits and retries preserve a branch graph with parent id, branch id, version ordinal, active branch pointer, provenance, trust transition and previous/next UI; in-place replacement is not acceptable.
Edit, regenerate and branch must preserve lineage after reload.
A retried fork returns the same branch.

acceptance_criteria: Regenerating twice leaves three sibling answers under one parent and a pager 3 of 3.
Reloading keeps the selected version visible.
Switching versions does not reorder the sidebar.
Editing the first message creates a root sibling group and both versions keep their replies.
A fork from message M copies the chat up to M, opens as a new chat titled (branch), and leaves the source unchanged.
Posting the same fork requestId twice yields one new chat.
A parent id from another chat is refused with Parent message not found.
Deleting a response with followers asks for confirmation and, after confirming, moves the reader to a surviving sibling.
inferred: [inferred] A fork carries the visible path, not every variant, because with variants only lineage rows are copied (conversation-branch-service.ts:395-397).

[inferred] The fork lands in the active workspace default, since the insert omits organization_id and the column default is current_app_org_id() (apps/web/db/neon/0110_active_workspace_content_scope.sql:50) while the source is read by user only (conversation-branch-service.ts:226-248); confirm.
proposed: [proposed] Copy parent_id mapping in forks so the new chat keeps its own tree.
[proposed] Count copied messages against the Free allowance, or document why one is requested.
[proposed] Store a version ordinal if the product contract requires it.

steps.what_happens: Client saves a sibling turn with parentId.
Server locks the chat row, checks the parent belongs to the chat, converts a linear chat once, inserts, and sets the leaf.
Client pages versions locally and writes the choice with PUT activeLeafMessageId.
Fork: server checks allowance, locks the source, verifies the fork point, checks branch capacity, inserts the new chat, the relation and the copied messages with new ids in one transaction.
After commit, copied assistant messages are indexed for artifacts in the background.
Client opens the new chat.

features.summary: One update route changes a chat's title, model, route, project, pinned, starred, archived, temporary flag and visible leaf, and saves each change. A pinned chat sorts first. A stale-version write is refused with 412 when the caller sends If-Match. The star flag exists in the store, but no control that sets it was found.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person organise chats and set per-chat options, and persists each change on the server so every device sees it (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:170-514).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long histories need pin and archive to stay usable, and a chat needs its own model, project and temporary state (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/090-conversation-and-synchronization-components.md, S90.08 and S90.12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with more than a few chats; workspace members who file chats into projects; people using temporary chats for private questions.
problems_solved: Important chats buried by newer ones.
Clutter from old chats without deleting them.
Losing the chosen model or project on another device.
Two devices overwriting each other's metadata (guarded by an optional version check).
use_cases: Pin a chat so it stays at the top of the sidebar.
Archive a finished chat and restore it later from Archived chats.
Move a chat into a project.
Turn on a temporary chat so nothing is saved.

features.summary: A new chat first gets a title cut from the first question on the server. Then a model may write a short title in the background and replace it, but only if the title is still the cut one. Titles for temporary and on-device-model chats stay on the device. The person can rename at any time.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a new chat a readable title in two stages: a cut of the first question (50 characters plus ...) saved with the message, then a model-written title of at most 60 characters saved if the title is unchanged (apps/web/lib/chat-title.ts:7-26; apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:169-208; generate-title.ts:324-346).
purpose.why_it_exists: So the sidebar is readable without typing a name and never shows a blank row (generate-title.ts:3-11).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who starts a chat; engineers maintaining titles and cost.
problems_solved: Untitled rows in the sidebar.
A slow or failing provider blocking message save (the title runs after the response).
A background title overwriting a name the person typed.
use_cases: Send a first question; the sidebar shows the cut question, then a short title within seconds.
Rename right after; the generated title does not replace it.
Use a temporary chat; the title is cut on the device only.

features.summary: The web composer keeps unsent text on the chat row so it survives a reload and shows on another device. Saves wait 1.5 seconds, retry, and use a revision check. If two devices differ, a Compare dialog asks which to keep. Temporary and device-model chats never sync a draft. Mobile keeps drafts on the phone only.

purpose.what_it_does: Saves the text in the composer per chat, locally and on the server (draft, draft_updated_at on web_conversations), and restores it when the chat opens (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-conversation-draft-sync.ts; apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:783-788).
purpose.why_it_exists: A half-written message was lost by closing a tab and never reached another device (apps/web/db/neon/0219_conversation_drafts.sql:3-10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users switching tabs or devices mid-message.
problems_solved: Lost text on reload.
Text typed on a laptop not visible on another browser.
Two tabs silently overwriting each other (revision check and conflict dialog).
use_cases: Type, close the tab, reopen the chat: the text is there.
Start a message on one computer, finish it on another.
Two tabs edit the same draft: a dialog compares them.

where_to_find_it: Web composer in every saved chat (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx; sync hook mounted at apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1972).
Conflict dialog titled Choose which draft to keep (apps/web/features/chat/components/DraftConflictDialog.tsx:68).
Electron Desktop shows the same hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: on-device draft store only (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:1-20).
prerequisites: Signed in, saved Cloud chat (a uuid chat id on the server).
Not a temporary chat; no model on the device selected; the chat holds no device-model turns (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:73-83).
screens_and_controls: Composer text box.
Toast with a Retry button after three failed saves: This draft couldn't sync to your other devices. Retry when ready. (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:247-253).
Toast with a Compare button: This draft changed elsewhere. Your text is still here, but has not synced. (:282-288).
Dialog headings Here and Elsewhere, buttons Use the other version and Keep this version (DraftConflictDialog.tsx:75-92).
journey: Person types; the text is parked in the chat store and browser storage.
After a 1500 ms pause the hook sends PUT with draft and the last revision seen.
Server stores the text and returns a new revision; the hook marks it saved.
On another device, opening the chat reads the draft and fills an empty composer.
If the text was changed elsewhere, the save returns 409 with the other text; the toast offers Compare.
Person picks a side; Keep this version resends over the other's revision; the other version replaces the local text and empties the conflict.
feedback_and_outputs: Silent on success.
Retry toast after 3 automatic attempts with delays of 3 s then doubling (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:25-26, :241).
Conflict toast and dialog as above.
A failed save is never shown as saved (conversation-draft.ts:169-195).
settings: Draft cap 20000 characters and debounce 1500 ms from conversation-contract.json (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversation-contract.json:3-4).

working: Server stores draft and draft_updated_at without touching updated_at or server_version (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/route.ts:212-274).

Compare-and-swap: the write applies only when the client's revision matches the stored one; otherwise 409 with the current draft and revision, unless the stored text already equals the new text (route.ts:221-270).
Revision rises at least one millisecond per write (route.ts:224-229).
Per-chat save queue, session-bound requests, revision tracking (apps/web/features/chat/services/conversation-draft.ts:120-199).
404 means the chat is not on the server yet; the hook waits until it is listed (conversation-draft.ts:174; hook:221-228).
Opening a chat copies the server draft into an empty composer; a local draft or a pending clear wins (apps/web/lib/hooks/useConversations.ts:783-788).
Temporary chats: the SQL writes null (route.ts:223-228); the client does not send for them (hook:73-83).
Empty draft clears the server copy and uses a clear token so it is not resurrected (hook:155-177; conversation-draft.ts:163).
incomplete: For a temporary chat the server answers saved: true with a null revision after nulling the draft, rather than refusing [inferred from route.ts:219-272]; the client never sends it.
Drafts are saved only when the chat has a uuid id and exists on the server; a brand new unsaved chat uses browser storage only (hook:158; test useConversationDraftSync.test.tsx:193).
disconnected_or_disabled: Server draft sync is switched off while a device model is selected or when the chat holds device turns (use-conversation-draft-sync.ts:73-83).
Migration 0219 header says NOT YET APPLIED; applied status unknown (0219_conversation_drafts.sql:3).
not_available: Server drafts on mobile: the mobile draft store has no server call (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/draftStore.ts:1-60 imports MMKV and account epoch only); no mobile draft route use found by search.
Drafts in CLI, Chrome and VS Code: not found (unknown).

features.summary: Three separate functions. Search finds words in chat titles and messages on the server (web) or on the phone (mobile). Export builds Markdown, JSON, HTML, PDF or Word files in the browser from an open chat. Import adds text memories from pasted ChatGPT, Claude or similar output; it does not import chats.

purpose.what_it_does: Search: substring match on titles and message text, plus an index search for artifacts, code sessions and projects, through GET /api/search (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:245-626). Import: a two-step dry run and commit that writes memory items, not chats (apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:55-195).
purpose.why_it_exists: People must find old conversations, take a transcript out of the product, and bring what other assistants know about them (doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:780 row W07; doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/090-conversation-and-synchronization-components.md S90.09, S90.10, S90.22).

Memory import persists and affects the next applicable turn; temporary chats neither read nor write memory.

Searching from one workspace does not return another workspace's chats.

proposed: [proposed] Add a chat history import (ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini export files) that creates chats through the existing save route with the Free allowance applied.

features.summary: A signed-in person turns a saved Cloud chat into a read-only copy with a random link. The server checks the copy against the stored chat, strips local paths and secrets, and sets an expiry of 1, 7 or 30 days. The owner can refresh, limit to the workspace, or revoke it. (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:77-83)

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a frozen, cleaned copy of a saved chat under a 24-character random token. Anyone with the link can open /share/<token> and read it until it expires or is revoked, unless the owner limited it to their workspace. The owner can list, refresh, change audience, and revoke links. (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:553-612; apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:100-123)
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to show an answer to someone else without giving access to their account. The copy is a snapshot, so later edits do not leak. The brief states the rule: sharing freezes a sanitized snapshot under a token that can be viewed, listed, changed in visibility and revoked (brief S90.11). Competitor guidance asks the product to explain snapshot versus live sharing, recipient access, revocation and sensitive-content review (doc: docs/product/competitive-guidance.md:276).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person with a saved Cloud chat (Web, Mobile, Chrome, and the internal Tauri desktop shell call the create endpoint). Readers need no account for a public link. Workspace admins gate external sharing by policy. (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:578; apps/mobile/src/features/shared-links/service.ts:105; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/shareClient.ts:70)
problems_solved: Showing a chat to a colleague or client without screenshots.
Stopping a link that was sent to the wrong person (revoke).
Keeping private data out of a shared copy (local paths and credentials are removed or the share is refused). (apps/web/app/api/share/route.ts:127-135,334-372)
Keeping an old link from outliving the chat: deleting a chat through sync removes its share rows. (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:696-697)
use_cases: Share an answer with a teammate for 7 days, then let it expire.
Limit a link to everyone in the workspace instead of anyone with the link.
Update an existing link after the chat grew, so the same URL shows the new messages.
Revoke every live link to a chat from the phone's Shared Links screen.

features.summary: Cloud answers stream to the screen as server-sent events with a keep-alive line every 2 seconds of silence. Agent events carry a versioned envelope and a sequence number, and are journalled for runs. If a connection drops, Web replays the saved answer after its cursor, and Desktop, Mobile and CLI follow the run journal after their last sequence.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams a turn's text and agent events to the client, validates each envelope, and lets a client pick up after a drop without repeating what it has already shown. Two recovery paths exist: replay from the saved assistant turn by character cursor (plain chat) and replay of journalled run events after a sequence number (agent runs). (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/resume/stream/route.ts:40-95; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1218-1246)
purpose.why_it_exists: Long answers cross flaky networks and proxies. Without keep-alives and resume, a drop loses or duplicates text. The brief requires an event gateway with heartbeats and resume, one versioned envelope, and a journalled cursor so a client can resume without duplicates (brief S90.13, S90.14, S90.15).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone chatting on Cloud: Web, Mobile, the Tauri desktop shell, CLI, VS Code and Chrome read the same envelope. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3241-3285; apps/desktop/src/api/cloudApi.ts:1225-1250; apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:363-368; apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_turns.rs:1050-1060; apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:1308; apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/cloudAgentClient.ts:470)
problems_solved: Idle connections dropped by proxies (keep-alive comment every 2 s). (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/sse-heartbeat.ts:6,29-40)
Duplicate text after reconnect (sequence ledger and character cursor). (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:1650-1668,3273-3284)
Half-shown answers when frames are lost (gap blocks settling until replay). (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3241-3245,3771-3777)
Run state lost on app close (journal in cloud_agent_events). (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:35)
use_cases: Watch a long answer type out, then lose Wi-Fi briefly; the rest fills in.
Close the laptop during an agent run and reopen: Desktop or Mobile follows the run after its last sequence.
A proxy drops an idle research stream; keep-alives prevent it.
A client missing a frame stops settling and asks for the saved remainder.

where_to_find_it: Every Cloud chat on Web (hosted app, also inside Electron Desktop), Mobile, CLI, Chrome side panel and VS Code. Resume is automatic; there is no control. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3771-3777)
The only visible cue found on Web is a 'reconnecting' stream phase while resume runs. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3040-3049)
prerequisites: A Cloud turn (Managed Cloud route).
For Web plain-chat resume: the conversation is not temporary, the turn is not a continuation, and no durable run handle exists. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3045)
The server must have saved the assistant turn; if it has not yet, the client retries up to 3 times, 500 ms apart. (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:1672-1673,3012-3016)
screens_and_controls: No dedicated control. The chat shows streaming text, then a 'reconnecting' phase, then the final answer or an error.
journey: Person sends a message.
Server opens an SSE response with no-cache headers and keep-alive lines; frames carry envelopes with sequence numbers.
If the connection ends early or a gap in sequence is seen, the Web client posts the last sequence and delivered character count to /runs/<turnId>/resume/stream.
The server sends only the unseen text and a finish frame, then [DONE].
The client appends the remainder and settles the answer.
For agent runs, Desktop, Mobile and CLI instead fetch GET /runs/<runId>?after=<sequence> pages and replay them.

The brief's cursor/replay store points at the run journal; the plain-chat resume route reads the saved assistant message, not the journal. (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/resume/stream/route.ts:66-74)

established.statement: A gateway streams a turn's events as server-sent events with agent-run headers, heartbeats and a resume path.
Stream events use one versioned envelope that the server encodes and every client decodes and validates.
Events are journalled with a sequence cursor so a client can re-read after a cursor or resume a dropped stream without duplicates.
Keep-alive interval is 2 seconds.
Resume sends only the unseen part of the saved answer.

acceptance_criteria: An idle 5 s gap in a stream contains at least two ': keepalive' lines.
Dropping the connection at 40 characters then resuming with cursor characters=40 yields only the rest, with no repeated text.
A resume for a turn id that belongs to another account returns 404 not_found.
A resume body with a negative number returns 400 resume_cursor_invalid.
A skipped sequence number stops the Web client from finishing until replay completes.
GET run?after=N returns only events with sequence greater than N, in order.
A second write of the same (run, sequence) does not create a duplicate row.
inferred: Every client that renders agent events should dedupe by sequence, as Web, Desktop, Mobile and CLI do. [inferred]
Resume should be offered on every Cloud surface; today only Web, Desktop, Mobile and CLI have replay code. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Name one owner for the two envelopes (StreamEnvelope and AgentEventEnvelope) in docs.
[proposed] Stamp the first-leg stream so gap detection covers plain chat from the first byte, if it is not already.

features.summary: Cloud chats, messages and artifacts move between devices through one pull and push endpoint using a server version counter. A push names the version it was based on; the server applies it, accepts an exact repeat, or returns the server copy as a conflict. Deletes are tombstones. Old or new protocol versions are refused with a clear message.

purpose.what_it_does: GET /api/chat/sync returns changes after a cursor (up to 500 chats, 1000 messages, 500 artifacts). POST /api/chat/sync applies a device's changes using a base version, returns applied rows and conflicts with the current server copy, and advances a cursor. Deletes set deleted_at and flow as ordinary changes. (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:54-56,105-220,542-917)
purpose.why_it_exists: The same account chat must look the same on Web, Mobile and other apps, and edits made offline must not be lost or overwrite newer changes. The brief states the rules: base version apply/conflict/idempotent, cursor pull/push, offline queue, tombstones, and a version floor (brief S90.16, S90.17, S90.19, S90.21, S90.23). Product docs name Account Cloud as the continuity domain shared by Web, Mobile Cloud, Desktop Cloud and eligible Chrome Managed Cloud. (doc: docs/product/suite.md:64-72)
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in Cloud users on Mobile (full engine), Chrome (pull of conversations), CLI (push of sessions, pull of history), and the Web app (artifact sync). (apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:1068-1077; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/conversationSync.ts:865; apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:326-360; apps/web/features/chat/services/artifact-cloud-sync.ts:60,114)
problems_solved: Same chat on two devices.
Edits made offline are queued and sent later (Mobile).
A delete on one device is not undone by another device's later push.
Old apps are told to update instead of failing to parse.
Pages never skip rows: the cursor stops at the lowest unfinished table frontier. (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:958-998)
use_cases: Write on the phone, open Web and see it.
Edit in a tunnel; changes push when the phone reconnects.
Delete a chat on Web; it disappears on the phone after the next pull.
Run a CLI session; it appears in the account history.

established.statement: Client pushes carry a base version; server applies, rejects as conflict, or treats as idempotent; clients reconcile conflicts with the server copy.
Conversations, messages and artifacts changed on one device appear on the user's other devices through cursor pull and push.
Changes made offline are queued durably and reconciled when connectivity returns.
Deletions become tombstones that advance the cursor, reach other devices, and are not re-created by a later push.
Clients declare a version; the server refuses too-old or too-new clients with an update-required answer instead of a parse failure.
Normal synced chat is shared by Web, Mobile Cloud and public Electron Desktop; Chrome mirrors only chats whose every turn is Managed Cloud; CLI and VS Code stay local unless explicitly handed off.
Unknown-provenance or Local/BYOK-mixed Chrome conversations stay browser-local.
Temporary chats are never synced.

acceptance_criteria: A message written on Mobile appears on a second signed-in client after one sync interval.
Pushing with a stale base version returns a conflict containing the current server row and does not overwrite it.
Repeating an identical push returns applied, not a conflict.
A chat deleted on device A is absent on device B after pull, and a later push from B of the same chat does not recreate it.
With 600 changed chats, the first pull returns 500 and hasMore true, and the second returns the rest with no missed row.
A push with protocolVersion 1 returns 426; one above the server's returns a validation error.
A temporary chat created on Mobile never appears in a pull.
Airplane-mode edits on Mobile are sent after reconnect and survive an app restart.
inferred: Free-plan daily creation caps apply to sync pushes, so a Free user can be refused on sync. [inferred from assertFreeDailyAllowance]
Local mode on Mobile and Desktop must never sync to Cloud without an explicit fork. (doc: AGENTS.md section 6)
proposed: [proposed] A visible 'Sync paused' state with the reason on every app that syncs.
[proposed] A pending-changes count on Mobile while offline.
[proposed] Document the Tauri desktop sync tables as unused or wire them.

steps.what_happens: A local change marks the chat or message dirty and stores it in the persisted queue.
The 30 s timer or a foreground event starts a sync if Cloud mode and signed in.
Push sends items with baseVersion and protocolVersion 2.
Server checks CSRF, rate limit, workspace policy, protocol, free-plan allowance, then applies each batch in SQL.
Server returns applied versions, conflicts and a cursor; the device clears applied items and adopts server copies of conflicts.
Pull fetches changes after the cursor in pages; the device applies deltas and stores the safe cursor.
Deleted rows come as deleted_at and are applied as tombstones.

features.summary: One generated catalog of models, providers, provider routes, capabilities, plan tiers, aliases and lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement). A developer edits curated JSON and runs the sync command. Web, Mobile, the extensions and the server read the compiled output through one TypeScript module; Desktop's Rust code reads a generated mirror.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds every model fact in JSON under packages/ai/model-registry/catalog, compiles it into a registry plus models.json, and exposes lookups (alias to canonical id, provider display, routes, capabilities, tier access, lifecycle) through packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts (packages/ai/model-registry/scripts/compile.mjs:37, :54, :57; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1446).
purpose.why_it_exists: So no surface keeps its own copy of model ids, prices, capabilities or plan limits, and a model swap never needs a consumer edit (doc: AGENTS.md section 4; packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1-18).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers and operators edit and sync it. Every app and the server read it. End users see only the result: the models in the picker, plan locks, and retirement notices.

established.statement: One compiled model registry is the source every surface and the server read for model facts.
A provider registry records each provider (display, defaults, governance, hosts).
A provider-route registry records every model x provider route with harness, trust modes, retention, cache class and price.
A capability registry records intrinsic and route-dependent capabilities per model.
Model aliases resolve to canonical model ids everywhere.
Model lifecycle (stage, deprecation, retirement, replacement) is managed and enforced.
The model catalog is generated and is the only place a model id may be a literal; never hand-edit models.json.
AGI never claims a model or provider can do something if capability metadata does not prove it.

acceptance_criteria: After editing the curation file and running pnpm sync:models, pnpm sync:models:check passes and models.json changed only through the generator.
Resolving a provider api model id, an alias and a canonical id returns the same canonical id.
A model whose deprecation date is in the past is not selected by Auto and is refused when pinned, on every plan and trust mode.
The picker shows a plan lock for a model the plan does not include, using the tier policy from the catalog.
A message stored with a retired model id still shows a model name.
An inline model id literal in app code fails pnpm check:model-id-literals.
inferred: [inferred] The picker hides or locks models by the same tier policy the server uses, because both read model-catalog.ts.
[inferred] A retired model should show a successor on every app, as Mobile does; only Mobile is evidenced.
proposed: [proposed] Show the retirement notice and replacement on web and extensions, the way Mobile does.
[proposed] Add a test that every surface picker reads the retirement label from one shared helper.

steps.what_happens: Developer edits catalog JSON and runs the sync command.
Compiler validates the catalog and writes registry.json, registry.ts, models.json and the Rust mirror files.
Apps import the compiled data at build time; the server and routing package read the same registry in process.
At request time the server resolves the incoming model id to the canonical id and reads tier, routes and lifecycle from it.
Picker rows are built from the same catalog on the person's device, with plan locks from the tier policy.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The catalog describes every provider route (managed cloud, own key, local harnesses) but does not call any provider itself; compile.mjs may refresh synced data from outside sources only in its refresh mode (packages/ai/model-registry/package.json scripts: refresh).

access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Each route carries trust modes (managed_cloud, byok, local) and each provider has governance data (packages/contracts/types/src/model-catalog.ts:1066, :143-152).

features.summary: Turns the model choice into one model and one route. 'Auto' means the server classifies the task and picks a model the plan allows and the budget can afford. A named model must be used or refused with a reason. Cloud Code sessions send an explicit model with each agent turn, but clients may substitute it first.

purpose.what_it_does: resolveAutoRoute takes a selection (Auto alias or a model id), task type, plan, trust mode and runtime profile and returns a selected model plus route and fallbacks, or an 'unavailable' code with reasons (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1722). classifyTaskLocally and classifyTaskFamily label the request (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts:137; packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts:173).
purpose.why_it_exists: So people can leave the choice to the product (cost, plan, capability aware) or pin a model and be sure it is the one that answers (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:294-296; packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json:566).
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who sends a message. Developers read the routing package. Operators tune routing through catalog policy and environment switches.
problems_solved: Choosing a model per message by hand.
A pinned model silently answered by a different model.
Sending a message to a model the plan does not include.
Spending more than the account budget allows.
use_cases: Free or paid person leaves the picker on Auto and sends a coding question; the server classifies it and picks a coding-capable model.
Person pins a model in the picker; the same model answers or the request is refused with a reason.
Person on a lower plan pins a higher-plan model and gets a 403 'not available' error naming the plan.
Cloud Code session starts an agent turn with the chosen model.

journey: Person picks Auto or a model.
Person sends a message; the client sends the selection as the request's model field.
Server classifies the task and builds a routing request from plan, budget, health and policy (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:94).
Router returns a selected model and route, or unavailable.

Auto route explanations such as 'the model you picked cannot handle this request' (packages/contracts/types/src/auto-route-explanation.ts:10).
settings: Model picker selection; Auto profile on Mobile; Cloud Code turn mode.

Operator switches AGI_ROUTING_TASK_FAMILY_STAGE, AGI_ROUTING_OBSERVED_HEALTH, AGI_ROUTING_CANARY, AGI_ROUTING_SHADOW: on unless set to 0, false or off (packages/ai/routing/src/routing-stages.ts:11-18; packages/ai/routing/README.md:66-80).

working: Auto aliases (auto, auto-economy, auto-balanced, auto-premium) map to profiles; continuity policy has preserveExplicitSelection true (packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/routing-policies.json:566).

Named selection: unknown id returns unknown_selection; ineligible returns explicit_model_ineligible or model_not_available_in_region; a pinned route that is unhealthy or lacks a credential returns explicit_route_ineligible (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1752-1850).
Pinned model is not replaced by the router; only a client-set flag can turn a capability mismatch into Auto (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1819-1840).

Server chat path never sets that flag, so a named model is not swapped for Auto there (apps/web/lib/server/managed-cloud-routing/routing-request.ts:94-130, no fallbackToAuto field; admission.ts:253 sets it false when exactSelection).
Auto order honours plan slots, budget (isAffordable) and prompt fit (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1677-1686).
Plan gate for named models returns 403 model_not_available with requiredTier (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:5330-5350).
Schema rejects an empty model string (request-processor.ts:591).
Cloud Code agent route rejects missing model, a model not in the catalog, and a model not on the plan (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/agent/route.ts:136, :148, :164).

Local classifier covers task types coding, reasoning, agentic, multimodal, long_context, computer-use, image_generation and more (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts:137-247); 12 task families (packages/ai/routing/src/task-family.ts:68-81).
incomplete: Cloud Code clients replace the chosen model before sending: resolveCloudCodeAgentModel keeps the selection only if it supports tools, else picks a coding model from a family chain or the plan default, with no message (packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code-agent-model.ts:13-40). Used by web (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx:464), Mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/cloud-code/CloudCodeSessionScreen.tsx:243; CloudCodeSessionsScreen.tsx:373) and VS Code (continueInCloud.ts:120). The server then receives the replacement as if chosen.

Mobile and Chrome resolve routes client-side with fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch true (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/cloudDispatchRouting.ts:94; apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedChatRouting.ts:55). Mobile's resolver is called only by image-request and unreadable-image helpers per grep, so its effect on the model actually sent is unknown.
Explicit selection fallback plan holds one route per provider with no 4-route cap (packages/ai/routing/src/auto.ts:1506-1513) while Auto plans cap at 4 (auto.ts:757, :1620).

Order of plan check versus routing refusal for a higher-plan pinned model: the route decision at request-processor.ts:4912 runs before the plan gate at :5330, and the 403 test shows the plan error is reachable; which case yields 422 versus 403: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Task-family stage is gated by an environment switch (on by default) (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4621; packages/ai/routing/README.md:66-69).
not_available: CLI routing: unknown, not read.
Desktop-specific routing: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so no separate routing; Tauri routing code is retained internal (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

established.statement: A model router resolves Auto and explicit selections to a model and route.
A task classifier labels each request for routing.
An explicitly selected model is enforced end to end (never silently replaced).
Stronger models are not the default because they are stronger; routing weighs intent, capability, quality, latency, privacy, reliability, context and total cost.
Nothing silently routes a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud.

acceptance_criteria: Auto message from a plan-allowed account is served by a model that plan allows and the response carries the resolved model header.
A pinned model is either the serving model or the request is refused with a code; the served model never differs.
A pinned model above the plan returns 403 with code model_not_available and the required plan name.
An empty model value is rejected; an unknown name returns an error, not a different model.
Cloud Code: the model shown in the composer equals the model in the request body of the agent turn, or the person is told about the change.
Auto never picks a model whose estimated cost exceeds the remaining budget when a budget is set.
inferred: [inferred] A tool-less model chosen in Cloud Code should be refused with a message, in line with S91.23, not swapped.
proposed: [proposed] In Cloud Code, show a notice when the chosen model cannot run the agent and ask the person to confirm the replacement.
[proposed] Drop fallbackToAutoForCapabilityMismatch from Mobile and Chrome client resolution, or surface it as a notice.
[proposed] Cap explicit-selection fallback plans at the same limit as Auto.

steps.what_happens: Person picks Auto or a model and sends; the client puts the selection in the request's model field.
Server validates the schema, classifies the task and task family, estimates input tokens and reads the account budget.
Server builds a managed-cloud routing request and calls resolveAutoRoute.
On 'unavailable', server checks workspace model policy and answers 403 or 422; otherwise it carries the decision on.
For a named model, server checks the plan and answers 403 model_not_available with requiredTier if not allowed.
Cloud Code: the client resolves the agent model and posts it; the server validates it against the catalog and plan and runs the turn.

features.summary: Server code that takes one chat request, picks the provider adapter built by a factory, supplies the deployment's provider key, and translates messages, images, documents, tools and structured-output requests into that provider's format. Calls happen on our servers for managed cloud; the web chat endpoint is the entry for every app.

purpose.what_it_does: The chat completions route admits the request, routes it, then asks ADAPTER_PROVIDERS for a builder per provider. Each builder creates a ProviderAdapter (id, auth, catalog, stream) through a shared factory with server credentials (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-providers.ts:126-246; apps/web/lib/services/provider-adapter-service.ts:313; packages/contracts/types/src/provider-adapter.ts:595).
purpose.why_it_exists: So every provider is called the same way, keys stay on the server, and each vendor's wire format is handled in one adapter.
purpose.who_uses_it: All apps through the chat endpoint; engineers adding providers.
problems_solved: Different vendor request formats.
Attachments a vendor cannot read.
Strict tool schemas required by some vendors.
Keys leaking to clients.
use_cases: Send a message with an image and a PDF to a vendor; each becomes the vendor's image and document block.
Ask for JSON output; the request carries the response format only if the route supports it.
Model uses tools; schemas are normalised per vendor.
A free promoted turn uses its reserved credential instead of the shared key.

working: Factory: one build function per provider through buildServerProviderAdapter; bespoke providers listed at adapter-providers.ts:126 plus protocol and gateway routes (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-providers.ts:240-246).

Credential broker: resolveServerProviderApiKey reads the first set environment key from a per-provider list; static key wins over the Vercel OIDC token (apps/web/lib/services/provider-adapter-service.ts:55-66, :117-126).
Base URL from environment is validated against an allow-list; a bad host is ignored with a warning (apps/web/lib/services/provider-adapter-service.ts:128-146).

Reserved free-turn credential: only the Anthropic builder applies it, and it throws if the credential is not configured (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-factory.ts:27-39, :66-74).

Canonical request: wire id per provider, tools split into function and raw vendor tools, response format kept only when the model supports JSON and the route lists that format (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/canonical-request.ts:126-210).

Anthropic translation: image (base64 or URL), PDF to document, text-like files to text, tool and tool-choice mapping, cache-breakpoint plan (packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/translate.ts:102-135, :227-245, :336).
Strict OpenAI tool schemas: additionalProperties false at the top, empty required lists (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/openai-tool-schema.ts:3-57).
Structured outputs on the Anthropic route filter schemas with unsupported keywords (packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/translate.ts:296).
OpenRouter requests carry a price ceiling from the route sheet, and routers always use zero-retention (canonical-request.ts:145-170).
incomplete: Strict-schema and structured-output rules differ per provider; I read Anthropic and the shared OpenAI helper only. Other providers' translate files not read.

Coordinator spans several code paths (single stream, tool loop, research loop), each calling createFailoverPlan (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:603, :1051, :1254, :1365); I read the single-turn stream path only.
The brief's route.ts:359 is the dispatch function, not a single coordinator class.
disconnected_or_disabled: Provider 'workers-ai' is built through the factory package but I did not find it in the server's adapter list; unknown.
not_available: Own-key (BYOK) calls through this server path: unknown; the path here uses deployment keys (provider-adapter-service.ts:117-126).
Local runtime adapters (ollama, lmstudio) exist as packages and desktop lists them as dependencies, but no import in apps/desktop/src was found (grep); how they are used is unknown.

established.statement: One coordinator admits, routes, meters and dispatches each inference request.
Providers implement a common adapter interface selected by a factory.
A credential broker supplies each adapter with the right server credential per provider.
Canonical requests are translated into each provider wire format.
Images and documents are translated into each provider multimodal format.
Tool schemas are translated per provider (including strict-schema normalisation).
Structured-output requests are translated to each provider native structured-output feature.
Security behaviour fails closed; Rust and desktop egress use host-owned policy; secrets never committed.

acceptance_criteria: Every provider id in the managed list has one adapter built by the factory and a mapError.
A base URL environment value on a non-allow-listed host is ignored and a warning is logged.
An image sent to a model without vision returns 400 model_no_vision before any provider call.
A PDF reaches Anthropic as a document block; an unsupported file type on a route yields an unsupported-input classified error.
A tool schema with an empty object and no required list is sent with required [] for strict OpenAI routes.
A promoted free turn uses its reserved credential, or fails with a clear error if it is not configured.
inferred: [inferred] Reserved-credential handling should apply to every provider that can serve a promoted turn; code applies it to Anthropic only.
proposed: [proposed] Add a table in docs listing, for each provider, its document, image and strict-schema behaviour, generated from adapters.
[proposed] Move reserved-credential handling into the shared factory function.

features.summary: Turns each provider's stream into one chunk format, peeks at the first chunk so a start error can still be handled, stops a silent stream after 90 seconds, bounds the time to first token and the whole stream by the turn's budget, and carries the person's stop to the provider call.

purpose.what_it_does: Each provider adapter translates its stream into StreamChunk values wrapped in an idle watchdog; the server peeks the first chunk, arms first-token and stream deadlines, forwards the client's abort signal, and settles billing for a stopped turn (packages/ai/providers/anthropic/src/index.ts:130; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-factory.ts:132-185; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/provider-deadlines.ts:86-139).
purpose.why_it_exists: Apps read one stream format; a hung provider must not hold a server function open; Stop must really stop.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats; operators watch timeouts.
problems_solved: Different vendor stream shapes.
Hung upstream holding a request.
Provider continuing to run after the person stopped.
Errors surfacing after the person already saw text.
use_cases: Person watches text appear and presses stop.
Provider never answers; the turn ends with a time-out error and may move to another route.
Provider goes quiet mid-answer; the stream ends after 90 seconds of silence.
Person closes the tab; the provider call aborts.

Idle watchdog default 90 seconds, error name StreamIdleTimeoutError (packages/ai/provider-runtime/src/watchdog.ts:1-12); used by the adapters for anthropic, deepseek, google, groq, lmstudio, minimax, moonshot, ollama, openai, openrouter, perplexity, qwen, vercel-gateway, zhipu and the OpenAI-compatible adapter that xai and nvidia use (grep of withStreamIdleWatchdog under packages/ai/providers; xai/src/index.ts:27).
First chunk peek: an error first chunk is mapped to an Error with status and thrown before streaming starts (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-factory.ts:161-182).
First-token deadline 25s per call inside a 40s turn budget; stream deadline equals the tool-loop budget (apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:5, :10-14; provider-deadlines.ts:58-64, :241-290).
Client abort forwards to the provider call through the armed signal (provider-deadlines.ts:86-101); route passes request.signal (route.ts:1270-1276).
Cancelled streams: partial answer persisted; tokens already produced are billed as completed (stream-transform.ts:131-139, :715-750, :939-953).
Heartbeat wrapper around the SSE body (stream-transform.ts:~957 withSseHeartbeat).

steps.what_happens: Server builds the adapter and starts the provider stream with a first-token and stream deadline.
Adapter opens the vendor stream with the abort signal; vendor sends events.
Watchdog turns 90 seconds of silence into an error; server peeks the first chunk.
Chunks are re-encoded into the SSE response for the app; heartbeat keeps it alive.
When the person stops, the app closes the request; the abort reaches the provider and billing settles.

features.summary: When a provider call fails, the error is classified. Safe failures are retried on the same route or moved to another route; some classes never rotate. Outcomes are written to a health store so bad routes are skipped. Failed or refused turns release their usage reservation.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps provider errors into one category list, retries start-of-stream failures on the same route within a time budget, plans fallbacks, rotates routes in createFailoverPlan, records outcomes to a health store and refunds failed reservations (packages/ai/provider-runtime/src/errors.ts:33, :817; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/provider-deadlines.ts:198-239; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/managed-failover.ts:386; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:195, :363).
purpose.why_it_exists: Providers fail often. People should usually not notice, and a failure must not cost them credits or silently spend more elsewhere.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every chat user (invisible); operators read health and failures.
problems_solved: Transient 5xx and overloads.
Rate limits and spent quotas on one key.
Bad credentials.
Retrying doomed requests and wasting the turn budget.
Spending on another paid provider when an account runs out of money.
use_cases: Provider returns an overload at stream start: same route retried after backoff.
A key is rejected: other routes on that provider are skipped and another provider is tried.

steps.what_happens: Adapter yields an error chunk or throws; the first chunk is peeked and mapped to an Error with status, Retry-After and classification.
Same-route retry waits with backoff if the class and budget allow.

If still failed, createFailoverPlan.next decides: never-rotate classes stop; free lane re-enters its stage; same-route transient retry; OpenRouter route-retry for the same model; then the next admissible candidate.
Each failure is written as a health outcome to the key-value store, which ranking reads next time.
If no route is left, the reservation is settled as failed and the error is returned.

features.summary: Before sending, the server estimates tokens and fits the conversation into the model's window. It drops old turns, summarises them when allowed, and shortens only what may be shortened. Policy messages and the latest user message are never cut; a latest message that cannot fit is refused. Dense scripts count as about one token per character.

purpose.what_it_does: Estimates tokens per message (planContextTrim, estimateTokens), plans which old messages to drop, replaces them with a summary or a marker, shrinks unprotected text, and refuses a turn whose latest user message cannot fit (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-window.ts:135; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-compaction.ts:411; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6703-6752).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long chats must keep working and a request must not overflow a model window and fail at the provider.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every cloud chat user in long conversations; operators.
problems_solved: Overflow errors from the provider.
Losing the user's current question.
Cutting policy rules off the end of a system prompt.
Under-counting CJK text.
use_cases: A long chat on a small-window model: oldest turns are summarised.
A temporary chat: oldest turns are dropped with a marker (no summary stored).
A pasted document too big for the model: the person gets 'This message is too long for the selected model'.
Failover to a model with a smaller window is skipped if the fitted conversation does not fit.

In-model markers: '[Earlier messages in this conversation were omitted to fit the model context window.]' or a fenced summary (context-window.ts:16; context-compaction.ts:70-80).
settings: AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED: summarising is on unless set to 0, false or off (context-compaction.ts:38, :60-62). No person-facing setting found.

working: Estimator: characters times a per-provider ratio and a tokenizer drift factor from the catalog; default 1 token per 3.5 characters (packages/ai/routing/src/classify.ts:106-125).
Message estimate adds 800 tokens per multimodal part and 4 per message (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts:12-13, :22-32).
Budget: window minus reply allowance minus 2,048 reserve, at least 1,024 (model-compatibility.ts:10-11, :47-53).
Plan: drop oldest whole groups, tool results stay with their assistant turn, last user turn protected (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-window.ts:135-196).
Protected: the latest user message and policy or format system messages are never shrunk; the dynamic reference block behind the cache boundary may be cut (context-window.ts:45-60).
Dense script floor (CJK, kana, Hangul ranges) counted at about one token per character, applied to the latest user message (context-window.ts:71-100, :102-120).

Compaction: model-written summary of dropped turns, stored per conversation and reused when the coverage digest still matches; falls back to the mechanical trim on any failure; not used for temporary chats or when disabled (context-compaction.ts:411-476; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-compaction.ts:369-372).
Latest user message that cannot fit: turn is refused 400 message_too_long and the reservation is released at zero cost (request-processor.ts:6728-6752).
Failover candidates are skipped when the fitted conversation exceeds their window (managed-failover.ts:567; context-window.ts:374-381).
incomplete: Protected overflow (policy messages too large): logged as a warning and the payload is sent whole, not refused (context-window.ts:237-245; context-window.test.ts: 'sends the policy whole and reports the overflow'). The first draft said overflow is always reported to the person; only the latest-user-message case is.
Dense-script floor applies to the latest user message only; older messages use the normal estimate (context-window.ts:102-120).
The estimator is a character ratio, not a tokenizer; accuracy per model: unknown.
Estimator lives under apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/model-compatibility.ts yet is imported by the server; a boundary concern [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Summarising can be switched off by AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED.
not_available: Local-mode context fitting on device: unknown; Mobile on-device models declare their own contextWindow (packages/contracts/types/src/on-device-models.ts:22).

features.summary: On the web Cloud chat endpoint, the server reads token counts (input, output, cache, reasoning) from each provider stream, prices them, settles the managed usage reservation, and writes spans, metrics and a routing trace with route, latency, cost and outcome. A failed call is settled at zero cost but still records its outcome. Server-side only.

purpose.what_it_does: Collects usage numbers from every provider response on the web Cloud chat endpoint, turns them into a billed cost and a provider cost, settles the usage reservation, and emits telemetry (spans, metrics, a routing-decision trace row) naming model, provider, route, latency and outcome. (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-usage.ts:28; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:334; apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:44)
purpose.why_it_exists: Cloud (managed) inference is billed and capped, so every call needs exact usage; operators also need to see which route served a turn and whether it failed. The brief requires usage numbers on every call and an outcome even on failure. (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/091-model-and-inference-components.md S91.16, S91.31)
purpose.who_uses_it: The billing and quota system uses the numbers to settle reservations; operators read costs, routing and rollout views; engineers read spans and logs. People see their own usage only through account or plan meters, which this brief did not read.
problems_solved: Charging the wrong amount: tokens, cache reads and writes, reasoning tokens and provider-reported cost all feed the price (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-usage.ts:5-17).

Double billing after a crash: the reservation is marked 'provider started' before the provider call, and an expired lease is refunded as 'outcome_unknown' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:533; apps/web/db/neon/0056_managed_usage_request_lifecycle.sql:9).

Not knowing why a turn failed or which route served it: spans, a trace row and a turn-outcome metric carry route, provider, model and error code (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:44,126).
use_cases: A user sends a chat turn in Cloud mode; the stream ends with a usage chunk; the server prices it and settles the reservation.
A user presses Stop mid-answer; the turn is still billed on estimated tokens if any text was delivered (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:107-165).
An operator opens the Costs tab and explains one request: served route, fallback, cost, cache tokens (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:230).

where_to_find_it: Web: no person-facing screen in this feature. Operators: admin dashboard tabs 'costs', 'routing' and 'rollout' (apps/web/features/admin/pages/OperatorDashboardPage.tsx:38-60); the Costs panel has the headings 'Cost breakdown, last 24 hours' and 'Explain one request' (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:230).
Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: nothing found in this feature; these apps send chat to the web endpoint in Cloud mode [inferred]; Local and own-key paths were not read, so unknown.
prerequisites: Cloud mode (managed) on the web chat endpoint; the code throws 'billing_protocol_error' if a managed turn has no reservation (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:313-318).
Operator views need a platform admin (requirePlatformAdmin) (apps/web/app/api/admin/observability/route.ts:33).
screens_and_controls: Costs panel: dimension tabs route, model, user, tenant; table columns Requests, Cache hit, Actual, Retail, Value, Fallbacks, p50 / p95 (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:230-262).
Explain form: fields 'Account id' and 'Idempotency key', button 'Explain' (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:290-310).
journey: A person sends a Cloud turn (not visible to them as telemetry).
Server reserves usage, then marks provider started, then calls the provider.
Stream usage chunks are folded into one accumulator.
On finish the server prices the usage and settles the reservation as completed or failed.
Telemetry rows and spans are written; an operator later reads them in the admin Costs or Routing tabs.
feedback_and_outputs: Operator: tables, 'Reading the breakdown…' spinner, error 'Could not load the cost breakdown.', empty text 'No provider cost event was recorded in the last 24 hours…' (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:195-228).
Person: a quota warning header may be sent when credits run low (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6190).
settings: No user setting found for this feature. Server settings names only: AGI_ROUTING_TRACE_RETENTION_DAYS, AGI_ROUTING_TRACE_RETENTION_BATCH (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:27-28).

working: Usage accumulator keeps the highest input and output counts and the last cache, reasoning and provider-reported cost values (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-usage.ts:28-62).

Non-stream and stream paths both settle the managed reservation with token, cache, reasoning and server-tool usage (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/response-builder.ts:143; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:334).
Provider-reported cost is used only if within a 0.1x to 10x band of the catalog estimate (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:210-218).
Failed attempts are settled at zero cost with the outcome and error class (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:212-223).
A client Stop with delivered text is settled as completed on estimated tokens (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:134-165).
Provider-started mark is persisted before the provider loop; failure to mark refunds and returns an error (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:526-553).
Routing decision trace row written fire-and-forget, then completed with outcome, error_code, ttft, duration, cost (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:44,126).
Spans via withSpan with domain 'model', redaction, OTel bridge and metrics (apps/web/lib/observability/span.ts:76; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:1465).
Stage-0 CPST fields (task outcome, retries, fallback, route plan id, task family) added to the settlement usage (apps/web/lib/cpst-telemetry.ts:52).
incomplete: CPST verifier result is always 'skipped' and task outcome is never 'success' (only 'abandoned', 'failure' or 'unknown') (apps/web/lib/cpst-telemetry.ts:35-42,57).
The successful non-stream trace outcome is persisted without ttft, duration or cost (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/response-builder.ts:266).
disconnected_or_disabled: Trace pending-map is in process memory, bounded to 2,000 entries; an outcome for an evicted or other-instance decision is skipped (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:98,170).
not_available: No per-app status in the brief; Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome usage telemetry for Local and own-key modes was not read: unknown.

established.statement: Token usage (input, output, cache, reasoning) is extracted from each provider response.
Each inference emits telemetry (spans, usage, cost, route, latency, outcome).
A failed call must still record its outcome.
Managed usage is marked started before the provider call so a crash cannot double-bill.

acceptance_criteria: A completed Cloud turn leaves a managed usage row with input, output, cache and reasoning counts and a cost.
A provider error before output leaves the reservation released at zero cost with the error class recorded.
A turn stopped by the client after text was delivered is billed (not refunded).
A routing_decision_traces row exists for the request id with kind 'served' and a final outcome.
Killing the server after the provider-started mark leaves the row in provider_started and a later recovery refunds it as outcome_unknown; the same idempotency key cannot start a second provider call.
The Costs panel shows the request's route, fallback flag, actual cost and cache tokens.
inferred: Telemetry write failures must never fail or delay the turn (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:164 comment states this) [inferred as requirement].
Names of provider and model in spans are redacted of secrets before leaving the process [inferred from redactAttributes in span.ts].
proposed: [proposed] Record ttft, duration and cost on the successful non-stream trace outcome too.
[proposed] Persist the pending-trace map or reconcile uncompleted traces so multi-instance deployments do not lose outcomes.
[proposed] Produce a 'success' task outcome and a real verifier result once a verifier seam exists.
