steps.what_happens: Request admitted; managed usage is reserved with an idempotency key (the request id), estimated cost and a lease.
Routing decision is persisted as a trace row (non-blocking).
Reservation marked provider_started before the provider call; on failure the reservation is refunded and an error returned.
Provider call; stream chunks of type 'usage' fold into the accumulator.
Settlement: price tokens, server tools and cost source; finalize reservation as completed or failed.
Trace outcome and turn metric recorded; delivery marker set for non-failed turns.

data.what: Managed usage request row (tokens, cache, reasoning, cost, status, attempt outcome, error class)
Routing decision trace (route, provider, model key, cohort, outcome, error code, ttft, duration, cost, prompt stamps)
data.retained_or_deleted: purged by the hourly rollout cron after the retention window (default 30 days); account erasure deletes the subject's rows (apps/web/db/neon/0212_routing_decision_traces.sql:25-27; apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:34)

data.what: Provider cost event with cache read/write units

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The usage chunk comes from whichever provider adapter served the turn; fields vary per provider (cache write 1h, reasoning, reported cost, search and code-execution counts are optional) (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/adapter-usage.ts:5-17). Pricing comes from the catalog via LLMCostCalculator (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/response-builder.ts:115).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account needed for managed Cloud turns; operator views need a platform admin (apps/web/app/api/admin/observability/route.ts:33).
access_and_usage.permissions: Admin endpoints require requirePlatformAdmin and the 'admin-operator' rate limit (apps/web/app/api/admin/observability/route.ts:30-33).
access_and_usage.subscription: This feature is the metering side of the subscription: plan tier, credits and quota features are passed to the reservation (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6148-6170). Per-plan rules are owned by SYS-subscriptions-entitlements-and-usage.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Reservation lease defaults to 900 seconds, bounded 60 to 3600 in the database function (apps/web/db/neon/0056_managed_usage_request_lifecycle.sql:130). Pending trace map limit 2,000 (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:98).
access_and_usage.flags: Flag variants are stored on the trace row (flag_variants) and joined into the cohort label (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/routing-decision-trace-service.ts:105). No flag turns this feature off: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Optional usage fields (reasoning, cache write 1h, fast speed, server tools) depend on what the provider reports; missing fields stay undefined.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Free trial and free lane turns settle through a separate path (settleFreeTrialRequest) (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/stream-transform.ts:262).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not read for Desktop or Mobile local inference; this web pipeline does not run on the device. Whether Local turns record any usage on the device: unknown.

features.summary: Server prompts live in code as a versioned manifest resolved by id. A flag can pick a version for a person; the release ledger gates it. Prompt caching is applied on routes that support it and refused for Temporary Chat and zero-retention turns. Operators read cache hit rates in the admin Costs tab.

purpose.what_it_does: Resolves each server prompt by id and version, stamps the used version on cost and routing rows, builds a tenant-scoped prompt cache plan per turn, and lets operators read cache hit rates and cache tokens by route, model, user or tenant. (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-registry.ts:75; packages/contracts/types/src/prompt-cache-plan.ts:142; apps/web/lib/services/route-cache-observability-service.ts:143)
purpose.why_it_exists: Prompts need identity, A/B selection and rollback without a database, and repeat turns should be faster and cheaper without leaking cached content across tenants or out of private turns. (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-manifest.ts:18-33; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2815-2822)
purpose.who_uses_it: The chat pipeline on every Cloud turn; engineers who add prompt versions; operators who watch cache numbers. People see only faster, cheaper repeat turns.
problems_solved: A shipped prompt is never rewritten, so a stamped ledger row always means one text (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-manifest.ts:32).
A stale flag cannot take a surface down: an unknown version falls back to the pinned one (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-registry.ts:55-56).
A Temporary Chat or zero-retention workspace never leaves a cached prefix (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2829-2836).
Two workspaces never share a cache key because the key folds in organization, user, prompt version and toolset (packages/contracts/types/src/prompt-cache-plan.ts:152-170).
use_cases: An engineer adds version 2 of the chat system prompt, opens flag prompt.<id> variant v2 to staff first, and rolls back by moving the pin.
A user in a long chat sends a follow-up and the stable system prefix is read from cache.
A user in Temporary Chat sends a turn and no cache control is attached.
An operator opens the Costs tab by route and sees the cache hit rate drop after a prompt change.

where_to_find_it: Web: no person-facing screen. Operators: admin tab 'costs', column 'Cache hit', and the 'Explain one request' item 'Cache read / write tokens' (apps/web/features/admin/components/OperatorCostsPanel.tsx:238,326).
Other apps: no screen found; prompt resolution and caching are server-side so the other apps see only the result [inferred].
prerequisites: Cloud mode on web chat endpoint [inferred].
Operator view needs a platform admin.
screens_and_controls: Costs panel tabs route, model, user, tenant; Cache hit column is cache-hit requests divided by requests (apps/web/lib/services/route-cache-observability-service.ts:131).
Temporary chat flag on a conversation; no cache control in the UI.
journey: Engineer adds a prompt version to the manifest and a release record.
Flag prompt.<id> with variant vN selects it for a subject if the release ledger admits it.
User sends a turn; the server resolves the prompt and stamps id@version.
Server decides cache use from surface, Temporary Chat and zero-retention.
Provider reports cache tokens; operator reads them later.
feedback_and_outputs: Operator table columns and explain fields (Cache hit, Cache read / write tokens).
Log warning '[prompt-flags] a prompt flag selected a version the release ledger does not open to this subject; serving the pinned version' (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-variants.ts:17).
settings: Flag key prefix 'prompt.' with variants named v<number> (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-flags.ts:21-24).
Environment name AGIWORKFORCE_CACHE_RETENTION ('long' enables 1h cache on eligible hosts) (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/anthropic-payload-policy.ts:107).
Request field use of prompt cache: default on for non-API surfaces, off for API unless asked (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2834).

working: Registry resolves by id with pinned, variant or rollout selection and never throws on an unknown variant (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-registry.ts:75-100).
Flag-selected variants checked against the release ledger and audience (internal staff) (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-flags.ts:60-75; apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-release.ts:16-28).
Stamp 'id@version' stored in prompt_ids on provider_cost_events and routing_decision_traces (apps/web/db/neon/0214_prompt_manifest_stamps.sql:24-32; apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-stamp.ts:12).
Cache plan: Temporary Chat outranks zero retention; either makes the turn non-cacheable (packages/contracts/types/src/prompt-cache-plan.ts:94-100,142-150).
Turn-level decision combines the request flag and the privacy class (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2829).
Anthropic adapter applies ephemeral cache control to the system blocks, with 1h only on eligible hosts (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/anthropic-payload-policy.ts:103-125).

Cache hit rates, cache read/write tokens, fallback counts and latency per route, model, user, tenant, last 24 hours by default (apps/web/lib/services/route-cache-observability-service.ts:143; apps/web/app/api/admin/observability/route.ts:44).
A shadow mirror (extra copy of a turn to a candidate model) is refused for the same private turns (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2851).
incomplete: The staged-rollout path 'rollouts' in resolvePrompt is only exercised by its test; no production caller passes 'rollouts' (grep over apps/web found only prompt-registry.ts and prompt-rollout.test.ts).
disconnected_or_disabled: Staged prompt rollout by traffic fraction exists but is not connected to a caller (apps/web/lib/prompts/prompt-registry.ts:37-47,63-72).
not_available: Cache numbers on non-web apps: none found. Cache behaviour for OpenAI-type routes is in packages/ai/providers/openai/src/translate.ts (referenced, not read in detail): unknown.

established.statement: Prompts are versioned in a registry and resolved by id and version.
Prompt caching is applied where routes support it and suppressed for private turns.
Operators can see cache hit rates and cache token usage per route, model and tenant.
A staged rollout can select a newer version for a share of requests.
Prompts stay in code; a shipped version is never rewritten.

acceptance_criteria: resolvePrompt with no variant returns the pinned version and stamp id@pinned.
A flag variant v2 returns version 2 only if the release ledger admits it; otherwise pinned and a warning is logged.
A variant naming a missing version serves the pinned version.
A turn in a Temporary Chat has usePromptCache false and no cache control reaches the provider.
A zero-retention workspace turn has usePromptCache false.
With a rollout fraction f and a request id, the same request id always lands on the same side, and about f of ids get the new version.
The Costs tab shows non-zero Cache hit for a route that served repeat turns.
inferred: The temporary chat flag also stops saving the chat; the brief states this but the code reviewed here only shows its effect on caching and shadow mirroring [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Connect staged rollouts to the release ledger canary record so a fraction rollout of a prompt can run in production.
[proposed] Show cache hit rate per prompt stamp, since stamps are already stored.

features.summary: An hourly server job compares each canary and shadow model with the promoted model in the same slot, writes benchmark rows per model, cohort and slot, and alerts on-call by page and email when quality, latency or cost is worse. It alerts only; it does not block a rollout itself. Operators read results in the 'rollout' admin tab.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads the last full hourly window of routing traces, computes per-cohort failure rate, p50 and p95 latency and cost per request, stores them, raises alerts, and purges old traces. (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:72; apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:80)
purpose.why_it_exists: A new model should not widen to everyone before there is evidence it is not worse than the promoted one. A promotion carries evidence of its shadow and canary stages. (apps/web/db/neon/0212_routing_decision_traces.sql:21-23; doc: docs/architecture/provider-routing.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Operators and on-call engineers. Not used by people in the apps.
problems_solved: Silent regressions in a candidate model's failure rate, latency or cost.
No record of how each lifecycle stage performed.
Alert floods: a candidate is judged only against the control in the same slot and window, with a minimum sample size (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:140-150).
use_cases: A canary model fails 8 points more often than control; on-call is paged once for six hours.
An operator opens the 'Model rollout' tab to see slots with a canary or shadow and recent benchmarks.
A shadow model's cost per request is over 1.5x control and an alert is sent.

where_to_find_it: Web admin dashboard, tab 'rollout', heading 'Model rollout' (apps/web/features/admin/components/ModelRolloutPanel.tsx:48; apps/web/features/admin/pages/OperatorDashboardPage.tsx:487).

working: Cron route returns 401 'Unauthorized' without a valid cron authorization (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:73-76).
Scheduled hourly at minute 5 (vercel.json:182-183).

Benchmark rows upserted per model, lifecycle stage, cohort, slot and window start; rows without a lifecycle stage are skipped (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:213-240).
Alerts for quality, latency and cost compared with control (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:140-200).

Alert dedup by claim key slot, cohort, candidate model and kind, 6 hours; if the store errors the alert is still sent; if no store, all alerts are sent (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:57-71).
Claims are released and 500 returned when neither page nor email reached anyone (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:140-142).
Read-only admin API and panel list stages (observed health, canary, shadow), slots and the 100 latest benchmarks (apps/web/app/api/admin/model-rollout/route.ts:55-70).
Also purges expired routing traces and semantic decision traces (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:93-97).
incomplete: The job alerts only. No code found that blocks or reverses a rollout from these results; the operator pulls a canary by hand with the routing kill switch (apps/web/app/api/cron/evaluate-model-rollout/route.ts:126).
Quality is measured as failure rate only, not answer quality (apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/rollout-evaluation-service.ts:111).
disconnected_or_disabled: Canary and shadow stages depend on stage switches (observedHealthRankingEnabled, canaryRoutingEnabled, shadowMirroringEnabled); their current values were not read (apps/web/app/api/admin/model-rollout/route.ts:61-65).

established.statement: A model evaluation service scores models and cohorts and gates rollout.
The scheduled job must pass the cron authorisation check or it is refused with 401.
Each window writes benchmark rows per model, cohort and slot.
Alerts are sent once per claim key; if the claim store is down, the alert is sent anyway.
The hourly job compares candidate cohorts with the promoted model and pages on call.

acceptance_criteria: GET without the bearer secret returns 401 and writes nothing.
With traces in the window, model_rollout_benchmarks gets one row per model, lifecycle stage, cohort and slot; rerun updates it, not duplicates.
A candidate below the minimum sample count raises no alert.
A candidate with failure rate more than 5 points above control raises a 'quality' alert.
A second run within 6 hours with the same condition does not page again.
If the claim store throws, the alert is still sent.
If neither page nor email is delivered, response is 500 and claims are released.
inferred: 'Gates rollout' in the brief means evidence plus alert for a human; no automatic gate was found [inferred from reading the job and service].
proposed: [proposed] Let promotion tooling refuse a widen when the last window shows an open alert for that slot.

[proposed] Add a semantic quality score beside failure rate (a semantic assessment service exists in the same folder, apps/web/lib/services/model-rollout/semantic-response-assessment-service.ts, not wired here as read).

aliases: Tool access (Auto / On demand / Always available)
features.summary: Every platform tool is declared once with four risk labels (what it does, whether it can be undone, whether it returns other people's content, whether it can send data out). Undeclared tools count as the riskiest kind. With many connected tools, only a budgeted, relevant set of schemas is sent; the rest sit behind a 'load_connector_tools' directory the model can query. Web server only.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds the one table that says, for each AGI platform tool, its action class (read, write, delete, execute, external_send), whether the effect is reversible, whether it returns untrusted content and whether it opens an outbound path (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-metadata.ts:101). Connector tools (GitHub, Gmail, Outlook and others) have their own tables (tool-metadata.ts:863). Separately, it picks which connector tool schemas go to the model each turn and lists the others in a directory tool (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-schema-loader.ts:116).
purpose.why_it_exists: Risk was once guessed from tool names; the file header says a name guess misclassifies send_email, post_comment and similar tools as harmless (tool-metadata.ts:1-12). Sending every connector schema also grows the prompt without limit, so a byte budget bounds it (tool-schema-loader.ts:27-30).
purpose.who_uses_it: The model (it sees the offered tools). The approval gate and the loop read the labels. The person only sees the effect: fewer tool prompts for safe tools, more prompts for risky or unknown ones, and a Tool access setting.
problems_solved: A tool nobody classified cannot slip through as harmless: it resolves to an irreversible write with an egress path (tool-metadata.ts:876-882).
Prompt size stays bounded when many connector tools are connected (tool-schema-loader.ts:116-163).
A tool the ranking missed is still reachable: the model can load it by name or keyword (tool-loop.ts:3982-4027).
use_cases: A user with Gmail, GitHub and Outlook connected asks to summarise a pull request; only tools matching the words of the request are sent first, the rest are listed in the directory.
An MCP server adds a tool nobody declared; it is treated as an irreversible write and asks every time.
A user picks 'Always available' in Capabilities so every connector tool schema is sent from the start (up to the larger budget).

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Capabilities section, heading 'Tool access' with options Auto, On demand, Always available; shown only when the server lists the 'toolAccess' switch as available (apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx:23-35,172-190).
Mobile: Settings, Capabilities, Tool access options with the same three labels (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/capabilities/toolAccessPreferenceService.ts:21-37).
Desktop: the public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app, so the web screen applies (AGENTS.md section 5, doc: AGENTS.md).
CLI: has its own tool list with deferred tools and a 'tool_search' tool, a separate implementation (apps/cli/src/tool_search.rs:123,465; apps/cli/src/platform/runtime/tool_catalog.rs:134-175).
VS Code extension and Chrome extension: no tool-list code found in the files searched; unknown.
prerequisites: Hosted chat (Cloud mode) with at least one connector or MCP tool connected; with none, only built-in tools are offered and no directory tool appears (tool-schema-loader.ts:174-175).
The Tool access control is hidden unless the account's available switches include 'toolAccess' (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:172).
screens_and_controls: Tool access radio group: 'Auto' (AGI chooses for you), 'On demand' (load tools when needed; more steps, lower accuracy), 'Always available' (ready from the start; fewer messages, better accuracy) (CapabilitiesSection.tsx:23-35).

features.summary: Tool calls from a model stream or from saved messages are turned into one shape (id, name, arguments). Before anything runs, the arguments get a shallow schema check: valid JSON, required keys, top-level types and fixed value lists. A bad call is refused with a reason sent back to the model, and does not ask the person first. Web server path.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads streamed tool-call fragments and stored assistant messages into PendingToolCall objects with id, qualified name and parsed arguments, flagging text that is not JSON (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2163-2190,3026-3057). It then checks arguments against the tool's declared input schema (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/tool-argument-validation.ts:74-108).
purpose.why_it_exists: Models sometimes send arguments that are missing a required field or have the wrong type. Refusing early with a clear reason lets the model fix the call instead of running a tool on bad input.
purpose.who_uses_it: The tool loop on every call; the model sees the rejection text. The person is not asked to do anything.
problems_solved: Broken JSON from a model no longer runs a tool (tool-argument-validation.ts:78).
Missing required fields and wrong types are caught before execution (tool-argument-validation.ts:84-106).
A bad call does not trigger an approval prompt (tool-loop.ts:7498-7510).
use_cases: A model calls a connector tool without a required 'owner' field; the call is refused with 'missing required argument "owner"'.
A model sends a number where a string is declared; the refusal names the argument and type.
A provider streams arguments in pieces; they are joined and parsed once at the end.

The error text goes back to the model: 'Tool "X" was not run because its arguments were rejected: ... Call it again with arguments that match its schema.' (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/tool-argument-validation.ts:110-115).

working: Streamed fragments are joined per call index and capped at 256 K characters (262,144) by slicing; extra text is dropped silently (tool-loop.ts:535,2137-2146).

At most 32 tool calls are read per step; calls without a name are skipped; a repeated id is replaced with a new UUID (tool-loop.ts:2163-2190; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-call-limits.ts:2).
Arguments that fail JSON.parse become { _raw: text } with argsMalformed true (tool-loop.ts:2171-2186,3038-3046).

Malformed arguments are refused, not run: toolArgumentProblem returns 'the arguments were not valid JSON' first (packages/ai/provider-protocol/src/tool-argument-validation.ts:78). The code comment on PendingToolCall that says the call still runs on raw text is out of date (tool-loop.ts:910-917).

The schema check covers: required keys present; each given property matches its top-level declared type; each given value is in a primitive enum list. null is allowed for optional keys (tool-argument-validation.ts:84-106).
Schemas using anyOf, oneOf, allOf, not, $ref or if are skipped, and unknown extra properties are not rejected (tool-argument-validation.ts:13,80,96-105).
Sandbox execution tools use their own schemas through the same function (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:177-182,312-315).
The same check also runs for the voice tool runner through executeOfferedToolCall (tool-loop.ts:3656-3700).
incomplete: Validation is shallow: no nested objects, array item types, min/max, patterns or additionalProperties (tool-argument-validation.ts:1-108).
The 256 K cap applies to streamed parsing only; parseAssistantToolCalls (saved messages) has no cap (tool-loop.ts:3026-3057).

Platform tools other than execution tools: which have schemas in externalToolSchemas is limited to the offered MCP/connector tool list, so built-in tools such as web search are not checked by this map (tool-loop.ts:4038-4042); whether they self-validate was not checked.

features.summary: The hosted chat runs the model, then its tool calls, then the model again, until it finishes or hits a step or time limit. Read-only calls may run side by side (4 at once only if the route supports it); everything else runs one at a time. Stop ends the stream and tools in flight. Shared checks decide empty, blocked, cancelled or cut-off turns.

purpose.what_it_does: runToolLoop streams a provider step, executes the tool calls, adds results to the conversation and repeats, within a step budget and a wall-clock budget (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:6697-6740). A dispatcher routes each call to its executor: search, fetch, sandbox code, Office files, skills, connectors, device steps and others (tool-loop.ts:2400-3020). A separate research loop covers Deep Research (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/research-loop.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: Answers often need several tool calls in a row. The loop keeps this bounded in steps, time and concurrency, and settles every turn in a known end state.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every hosted chat user whose model calls tools, scheduled agent runs and voice tools; the CLI has its own Rust engine.
problems_solved: Runaway loops: a step limit pauses the run with a checkpoint instead of failing (tool-loop.ts:7910-7960).
Slow serial reads: independent read-only calls can run together (tool-loop.ts:5398-5403,5729).
Hung tools: each call has a deadline (apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:8).
Blank answers: one shared definition of empty or cut-off turns (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/turn-completeness.ts:1-60).

Read-only calls (declared read class) run first with concurrency 4, but only if the serving route's harness marks parallelToolCalls as implemented; otherwise concurrency is 1 (tool-loop.ts:5385-5403; packages/ai/model-registry/catalog/harnesses.json:39).
Mutating and undeclared calls run one at a time after the read-only batch, and each is checked for a stop request first (tool-loop.ts:5738-5747).

Step limit: with a step-budget checkpoint handler the run pauses durably and only a resume that raises the limit continues; without one the turn ends with error code max_agent_steps_reached (tool-loop.ts:7910-7973).
Wall-clock limit: with an invocation checkpoint handler the run checkpoints and a caller continues (tool-loop.ts:6739-6760).
Cancel: checked at loop start, before each mutating call and in other points; the signal is combined into each tool call's own abort signal (tool-loop.ts:4201-4204,5538-5542,6697-6700).
Each call has its own timeout and abort; a timed-out write reports unknown outcome and tells the model not to retry (tool-loop.ts:1702-1745,5721-5727).

Error text from tools is fenced as untrusted data; connector results use a sealed envelope; fetched pages and stored pages are fenced (tool-loop.ts:2200-2240; apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts mcp_tool_result).

established.statement: The runtime loops model call, tool calls, results, model until done, within step and time limits.
Independent parallel-safe calls run concurrently; unsafe ones one at a time.
Cancelling a run stops the model stream and in-flight tools and settles the run as cancelled.
One evaluator decides whether a turn finished, came back empty, was blocked, cancelled or cut off for every path that persists a turn.
A single dispatcher routes each call to its executor.
Tool outputs are normalised into a bounded, redacted result with an error flag before reaching the model.
Dependency-aware execution is not applicable anywhere.

acceptance_criteria: A chat with default settings stops after 10 steps by pausing (with a checkpoint handler) or by error code max_agent_steps_reached (without).
Two read-only calls in one step run together only when the route supports parallel tool calls; otherwise one after another.
A write call never runs at the same time as another call.
Pressing stop before a mutating call starts produces 'was not run: the user stopped this run before it started' for that call.
A tool exceeding 120 s returns a timeout message to the model; a write returns an unknown-outcome message.
A turn with no text, no tool call, no file and no card counts as empty and is not saved as a blank answer.
A cancelled finish reason is classed as cancelled.
inferred: Order of results follows read-only first then mutating, not the model's original order [inferred from tool-loop.ts:5729-5747].
A tool-heavy run gets 100 steps only in AGI Work mode [inferred from tool-loop.ts:901-905].
proposed: [proposed] Show the person why a run is serial (route lacks parallel support).
[proposed] Wrap every tool result in one untrusted envelope and test it.

steps.what_happens: Loop reads limits, checks cancel and pause, applies steer messages and the time budget.
A provider step is streamed through the shared adapter table; an empty step may rotate to another route.
Tool calls are parsed, gated and validated (F092-02, F092-05).
Read-only calls run with concurrency up to 4 (or 1), then mutating calls in order; each is run under a timeout and an abort signal.
Individual executors call outside services (web search, page fetch, connectors, sandbox).
Results are secret-checked, emitted as events and appended; the loop continues or ends.
Device-step tools are paused and sent to the person's own device to run, then results return.

features.summary: When a tool returns more than 100,000 bytes, the first part goes to the model and the rest is kept for 24 hours under a reference id; the model reads it in 40,000-character pages with the read_tool_result tool. Older results trimmed from long chats are kept the same way. Needs a key-value store; otherwise the result is just cut.

purpose.what_it_does: referenceOversizedToolResult checks the secret policy, stores the full result (up to 900,000 characters) under a random reference and returns the first 100,000 bytes plus a note telling the model how to read the rest (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-result-store.ts:153-215). readStoredToolResult returns a page of up to 40,000 characters wrapped as untrusted data (tool-result-store.ts:262-337).
purpose.why_it_exists: Long tool output would fill the model's context. Keeping it by reference lets the model fetch only what it needs, and lets it re-read results that were trimmed from history.
purpose.who_uses_it: The model, through a reader tool. The person is not given a control; what they see of the notice is unknown.
problems_solved: Oversized sandbox, connector and MCP results no longer flood the context (tool-loop.ts:2850-2860,2905-2925,3005-3020).
Results trimmed from a long chat remain readable (tool-loop.ts:1657-1700).
Secrets in stored results are checked before storage and on read (tool-result-store.ts:158-160,299-304).
use_cases: A sandbox command prints a large log; the model reads page two with offset 40000.
A connector returns a big document; the first part is shown and the model asks for more.
In a later turn the model re-reads a result trimmed earlier.

features.summary: For each tool call the server decides run, ask or refuse using a nine-row table: saved Deny first, saved Allow unless untrusted content plus private data plus an outbound path meet, then the account default. A call that needs a person pauses the run in a stored checkpoint; a decision from any device resumes it, only for the exact calls asked.

purpose.what_it_does: resolveToolCallGate walks a frozen table of nine ranks and returns allow, ask or deny with a machine reason (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-call-gate.ts:68-160). Calls that must ask are saved with the messages and arguments in a checkpoint row and the stream ends; the approve endpoint claims the row and resumes the loop (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts:200-230; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1908-2000).
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can act on real accounts. The person must control risky actions, and a prompt-injection that tries to send private data out must not run silently. D-2026-09-15-01 sets the default posture: read-only tools run without asking and writes, sends and similar keep asking (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md:40-46).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every hosted chat user whose model calls tools; workspace admins (autonomous approvals can be disabled for members); scheduled and unattended runs.
problems_solved: Risky or unknown tools cannot run without a decision (tool-metadata.ts:1070-1081).
Private data cannot be sent out after untrusted content without asking, even if the tool was saved as 'allow' (tool-call-gate.ts:86-92).
An approval answered on one device cannot be replayed or answered twice (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1930-1995).
Unattended runs do not hang on a question nobody can answer (tool-call-gate.ts:146-157).
use_cases: Model wants to post a GitHub comment; a card asks Allow or Deny.
User sets a connector tool to Always allow; later a page with hidden instructions makes the model call the same tool with data; the trifecta rule asks again.
A scheduled agent hits a trifecta call and is denied, or pauses if the run can pause.
User starts a task on the web, approves from a phone.

prerequisites: Signed-in account; a turn that offers a tool needing approval.
For 'Skip approvals' the workspace must allow autonomous approvals (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-approval-policy.ts:29-41).
screens_and_controls: Tool card: 'This tool requires approval before execution.' or the high-risk notice 'Private data from this chat could be sent outside AGI. Check where it goes before you allow it.' (ToolCallCard.tsx:404-408; tool-approval-policy.ts:34-35).
Buttons Allow, Allow for this chat, Deny.
Account default radio group 'Default approval for tool actions'.
journey: The model calls a tool.
Server gates each call (F092-05 table); calls with bad arguments are dropped first (F092-02).
If any call must ask, approval events are sent and the run is saved in a checkpoint; the stream ends in a paused state.
The person sees cards with Allow and Deny.
The client posts decisions to /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve with the run id.
Server claims the checkpoint under a lease, checks that the decisions match exactly the pending calls, records an audit event per decision, and resumes the loop.
Approved calls run with the stored arguments; denied calls give the model a denial message; the run continues.
feedback_and_outputs: Events 'approval-requested' and 'approval-resolved' per call (tool-loop.ts:7822-7835,6551-6561).

Errors: 400 'Approval decisions do not match the pending tool calls.', 410 'This approval request expired and can no longer be resumed.', 404 'Pending approval not found.', 409 'This approval is already being resumed.' (approve/route.ts:90-155).
Audit event 'tool_approval_decided' per decision (approve/route.ts:629-642).
settings: Account default policy: ask_every_time, auto_approve_read_only, autonomous; an unset website account resolves to autonomous, unreadable settings to ask_every_time (packages/contracts/types/src/tool-approval-policy.ts:3-13; apps/web/shared/types/toolApprovalPolicy.ts:44-52; docs/security/security.md section 1.1).
Per-tool saved levels allow, ask, deny; a critical tool cannot be saved as always allow (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/connector-tool-permissions.ts:45-61).
Workspace key allowAutonomousToolApprovals (tool-approval-policy.ts:84).

working: Nine-rank gate: 1 saved deny; 2 device step with a device host allowed; 3 saved allow with trifecta escalates; 4 saved allow; 5 saved ask; 6 manual mode with a policy auto-approved tool allows; 7 manual mode asks; 8 trifecta escalates; 9 otherwise allow (tool-call-gate.ts:68-128; doc: docs/security/security.md section 1.1).

Trifecta is true when untrusted content is in context or arrives in the same batch, a sensitive source is reachable, and the tool creates an egress path; an undeclared tool counts as egress (tool-call-gate.ts:130-136; tool-metadata.ts:876-882).
Escalate means ask when attended; deny when unattended unless the run can pause and the caller allows it (tool-call-gate.ts:146-157; tool-loop.ts:3841-3846).

In 'auto' approval mode the account policy is not consulted (rank 6 needs manual mode) but a saved deny and the trifecta still apply (tool-call-gate.ts:68-128). The mode is manual when any MCP or connector tool is offered or any tool is not auto-approved by the policy (tool-loop-routing.ts:144-151).

Policy auto-approval: under auto_approve_read_only only declared, read, reversible, no-egress tools run unasked, plus flagged web search, fetch and sandbox code; autonomous allows all non-destructive tools; ask_every_time allows none; device steps and browser commands never auto-approve (tool-metadata.ts:1083-1100).
Checkpoint save validates the pending calls (1 to 32), event cursor continuity and a complete approval boundary, or throws (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1416-1470).

Claim: only a pending checkpoint younger than 24 hours; decisions must name exactly the pending call ids; the row moves to 'resuming' under a lease token; a second answer gets a conflict 'already answered on another device' (cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1908-2000). The approve route passes a 86,400 second lease (approve/route.ts:227).
Resumed approved calls use the stored pending call arguments and are still blocked if the tool has since been denied (tool-loop.ts:6563-6590).
Migration 0062 table with states pending, resuming, resolved, failed, one active row per run, row-level security (apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:8-60).
Input and device checkpoints reuse the same table with checkpoint_kind (apps/web/db/neon/0148_mrtr_input_checkpoint.sql:19-20; cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2090-2700).
incomplete: There is no separate per-call decision table; per-call outcomes are kept as the 'approval-resolved' event in the run journal and the audit event 'tool_approval_decided', while the checkpoint row holds only the run-level state (0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:22-24; approve/route.ts:629-642).

Which unattended callers set unattendedEscalationPauses: the scheduled executor builds a tool plan with the approval policy (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:222-300), but whether it can pause was not confirmed.
Voice tools use their own table with a 'requiresApproval' flag and the same policy (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:215-240); equivalence with the gate not verified.
disconnected_or_disabled: Autonomous policy is ignored when the workspace forbids it (tool-approval-policy.ts:29-41,86-96).
not_available: VS Code approval UI: none found.
A reject-with-reason beyond optional 'guidance' text: guidance exists but its UI was not opened (approve/route.ts:236-250).

established.statement: A policy evaluator decides allow, ask or deny for every tool call from the account policy, saved per-tool levels and the lethal-trifecta rule, on every path that runs tools.
Pending approval requests are persisted with the exact calls, messages and request so any device can answer them later.
Each approval decision is recorded per call with outcome and the checkpoint is resolved exactly once.
A decision applies only to the exact pending calls; mismatched or stale decisions are refused and resumed calls use stored arguments.
Requests for human input queue durably and the run resumes when answered.

In the default read-only mode, sandboxed code, web search, page fetch and other non-mutating tools run without asking; external writes, purchases, messages, destructive actions, credential changes and consequential commands on the user's machine keep asking.
Approval prompts are required for connector writes, shell and file operations outside safe defaults, and must show action, target, provider/tool, risk, scope and choices.

acceptance_criteria: A saved Deny blocks the call under every policy and the result says it is blocked.
A saved Allow runs unasked unless untrusted content, a reachable private source and an egress tool all hold; then it asks.
Under 'Run read-only actions without asking', web search and a read tool run unasked; a write tool asks.
An unattended run refuses a trifecta call, or pauses if it can checkpoint.
Approving on a second device after the first answered returns a conflict.
Sending decisions that miss or add a call id returns 400 and runs nothing.
A checkpoint older than 24 hours returns 410.
A resumed approved call runs with the arguments saved at pause.
inferred: Approval mode 'auto' is used when the turn offers only tools the policy auto-approves; combined with rank 9, those run unasked [inferred from tool-loop-routing.ts:144-151].
The 'allow once' and 'always allow' choices go through the scoped-approval planner (approve/route.ts:236-250,340-470) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a per-call decision table or explicit journal query so 'recorded per call' is one lookup.
[proposed] Show the person which rule row asked (reason code) on the card.

steps.what_happens: Server loads the account policy and per-tool levels for the turn.
Each call is run through the gate with the turn context (mode, policy, unattended, device host, untrusted content, sensitive source).
Deny: refusal result. Allow: run. Ask: events and checkpoint saved, stream ends paused.
The person's device shows cards; decisions are posted to the approve endpoint.
Server validates the request, claims the checkpoint under a lease, writes audit events, rebuilds the request from stored messages and resumes the loop.
Approved calls run; denied calls give the model a denial message; the loop continues with the model provider.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The gate is model-neutral. Model route is restored from the saved request on resume (approval-checkpoint-request.ts:20-60).

features.summary: Each tool call leaves a trace: the audit log gets a row for platform tool runs, and connector calls add a row with outcome and duration that the person can read as 'Recent calls'. Retry-unsafe calls are claimed for 15 minutes so a retried step does not run twice. GitHub comment and review writes whose outcome is unknown are checked on GitHub.

purpose.what_it_does: recordToolCallAudit writes a security audit event for each tool outcome (completed, failed, blocked, handed off, sent to device) (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:3514-3540). meterConnectorCall inserts a connector_call_events row without waiting (apps/web/lib/connectors/health.ts:281-300; apps/web/lib/services/connector-call-log-service.ts:52-75). runToolCallOnce claims a key in the key-value store before a retry-unsafe call (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-idempotency.ts:164-204). The GitHub write path checks GitHub after an unknown outcome (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:413-458).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to know what the agent did with their accounts, a retry must not post or send twice, and a timeout must not leave the truth unknown.
purpose.who_uses_it: People reading a connector's recent calls; the loop on every retry-unsafe call; admins reading the audit log.
problems_solved: Duplicate writes after a retry or resume (tool-idempotency.ts:1-12).
Silent connector failures: three failures in a row mark a connector not responding (connector-call-log-service.ts:37).
A GitHub timeout no longer leaves the model guessing (user-connector-tools.ts:413-458).
use_cases: User opens a connector and reads 'Recent calls' with outcome and duration.
A step is retried after a lost connection and the same write is not repeated.
The model posts a GitHub comment, GitHub times out, the server checks and reports whether it landed.

where_to_find_it: Web Connectors: 'Recent calls' list inside the connector's Tool Permissions panel (apps/web/features/connectors/components/ConnectorCallLog.tsx:31; ToolPermissionsPanel.tsx:377).
Mobile: connector call log screen (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/ConnectorCallLog.tsx; apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts).
Desktop public app: hosted web app (AGENTS.md section 5).
CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no call log screen found.
prerequisites: Signed-in account; Cloud mode connector calls.
Migration 0223 applied: its header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only', so whether the table exists in each environment is unknown (apps/web/db/neon/0223_connector_call_events.sql:4).
screens_and_controls: 'Recent calls' list: connector, tool, outcome (succeeded, failed, blocked), duration, time; text 'What it was asked and if it answered. Repeated failures mark it as not responding. Arguments and results are never recorded.'; loading 'Reading the call log'; error 'The call log could not be read.' with Retry (ConnectorCallLog.tsx:31-39).
journey: A connector tool call runs.
The executor times it and writes a log row in the background.
The person opens the connector's permissions panel.
The page calls GET /api/connectors/calls with the connector id and limit.
The list shows the latest calls newest first.
feedback_and_outputs: Empty list text: 'This connector has not been called yet, so there is nothing to show.' (ConnectorCallLog.tsx:33).
GitHub unknown outcome messages: 'It is safe to try again.' or 'Check ... before trying again, so it is not posted twice.' (user-connector-tools.ts:436-451).
Idempotent replay messages: 'already ran for this step and was not run again', 'outcome is unknown' (tool-idempotency.ts:60-82).
settings: AGI_TOOL_IDEMPOTENCY_WINDOW_MS, default 900,000 ms, minimum 1,000 (tool-idempotency.ts:16-20,45-58).
Call log read limit: default 50, maximum 100 (apps/web/app/api/connectors/calls/route.ts:16; connector-call-log-service.ts:40).

working: Audit event per tool outcome with tool name, category, status and duration; eventType tool_executed, browser_action or computer_use_action (tool-loop.ts:3500-3540).
Every call result path in the loop awaits auditToolCall (tool-loop.ts:5820-5830).
Connector calls log succeeded, failed or blocked with duration; the insert is not awaited and a failure only logs a warning (connector-call-log-service.ts:46-75).
GET /api/connectors/calls returns the signed-in user's rows, rate limited, no arguments or results (apps/web/app/api/connectors/calls/route.ts:18-35; 0223 table columns).

Idempotency: every tool except a short safe list is 'unsafe' and is claimed before running; a replay returns the settled result or 'already ran'; a claim that cannot be written refuses the call; no key-value store means the call runs unguarded (tool-loop.ts:932-943; tool-idempotency.ts:164-204).
The idempotency key is built from the request key, step, tool call id, user and organization and resume round (tool-loop.ts:5695-5702).
Settled results above 16 KB store only 'settled' (tool-idempotency.ts:31).

GitHub post_issue_comment and post_pull_request_review: on GitHubWriteOutcomeUnknownError the server lists recent comments or reviews since the start time and returns landed, not landed, or could not confirm (user-connector-tools.ts:413-458,499-540; apps/web/lib/github-app.ts:994-1090).
incomplete: Reconciliation covers only the two GitHub write tools; other external writes have no outcome check (user-connector-tools.ts:499-540).

The first-draft claim 'receipt of every tool action the user can read' is partly met: platform tools go to the audit log, connector calls to the call log; no screen for the audit log of platform tools was examined.
The 'surface' column of connector_call_events is not filled by meterConnectorCall callers seen (user-connector-tools.ts:2753-2760).

The idempotency 'safe' list is a name list in the loop and does not use the metadata retrySafety field, so a read tool like web search is also claimed (tool-loop.ts:932-943; tool-metadata.ts:961-969).
disconnected_or_disabled: Idempotency guard is skipped when the durable workflow passes its own toolExecutor (tool-loop.ts:5703-5716).
not_available: Reconciliation for non-GitHub writes (mail, calendar, messages).
A user-facing receipt screen for platform tool actions.

established.statement: Every tool action leaves a durable receipt (who, which tool, when, outcome) the user can later read.
Retry-unsafe tool calls are remembered by an idempotency key so a retried step does not run them twice.
When an external action's outcome is unknown, the runtime checks the external system and records the real outcome before retrying or reporting.
Approval prompts and logs: the product requires logs for connectors.

acceptance_criteria: A connector tool call adds a row with outcome and duration visible in Recent calls.
A failed log insert does not fail the tool call.
A retried step with the same key does not run an unsafe tool twice and says it already ran or its outcome is unknown.
With the store unreachable on claim, an unsafe call is refused with a message to the model.
A GitHub comment that times out but landed reports success once.
A GitHub comment that timed out and did not land says it is safe to try again.
If GitHub cannot be checked, the message says the outcome could not be confirmed.
An account with no connector calls sees the empty message.
inferred: Because the log write is fire-and-forget, a lost row is possible without an error [inferred from connector-call-log-service.ts:46-52].
Idempotency for web search and other reads costs a key-value write per call [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Extend reconciliation to other external writes (mail, calendar).
[proposed] Add a person-facing activity log for platform tool actions.
[proposed] Use metadata retrySafety to choose which calls to claim.

steps.what_happens: A tool call is settled; the loop writes an audit event with status and duration.
For a retry-unsafe call, the loop claims an idempotency key in the key-value store before execution.
The connector call runs against the outside provider; start time is taken.
A call row is inserted in the background.
On a GitHub timeout or 5xx, the server asks GitHub for recent comments or reviews since the start time.
The person opens Recent calls; the page fetches the endpoint.

features.summary: On our servers, each Cloud agent turn is saved as a run with its ordered events, tool and model results, approval checkpoints and (in Work mode) a plan. The turn runs in a durable workflow, so it can outlive the connection. A sweep every 15 minutes ends runs whose worker has gone, marking them failed or cancelled with a reason.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps the state of a Managed Cloud agent turn on the server instead of in the open request. It stores the run row (state, model, last event number, cancel request), every event in order, a receipt for each model call and tool call (including its result), versioned approval checkpoints that hold messages and pending tool calls, and a Work plan row. A reaper then settles runs that nothing is driving any more. (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9-39; apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:19-39; apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:9-35; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:90)
purpose.why_it_exists: A long agent task must not die when a tab closes, a phone loses signal or a server invocation ends. Events are stored by sequence number so Web, Desktop and Mobile can reconnect and replay the same activity. (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:1-7) Operation receipts stop a retried step from repeating a paid or changing action. (apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:1-7)
purpose.who_uses_it: A person using Cloud (managed) agent turns in chat or Work mode on the web app, and the other apps that follow a run through the shared run client. Engineers and support read the tables when a run looks stuck. (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-agent-runs-client.ts:528; apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3095)
problems_solved: A closed tab or dropped connection does not end the turn: the durable workflow keeps running and the client can follow it again from the last event number it saw (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/route.ts:50-58).

A crash leaves a run in a live state; the reaper moves it to failed (or cancelled if the person had asked to stop) and writes an error event saying why (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:110-125, 56-70).
A retried step does not repeat a model or tool call because a completed operation replays its stored result (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:304-307).
A tool that was waiting for approval can resume later from a saved checkpoint (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1416).
use_cases: Start a long Work task, close the tab, return later and see the run's events replayed.
A server invocation ends mid-turn; about 18 minutes later the reaper settles the run so the conversation is no longer blocked.
A turn pauses for tool approval and resumes from the stored checkpoint within the 24 hour window.
An engineer looks up a stuck run in cloud_agent_runs and its operations to see the last step.

where_to_find_it: No screen of its own. It sits behind chat and Work turns in the web app; the reconnect state shows as a stream phase named 'reconnecting' in the web chat code (apps/web/lib/hooks/useChatStream.ts:3095).

Run follow code exists in Desktop (apps/desktop/src/runtime/CloudRuntime.ts:700), Mobile (apps/mobile/services/streaming.ts:478), the Chrome extension (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/managedRunControl.ts:435) and the VS Code extension (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/cloud-tasks/cloudRunClient.ts, matched by search, not read).
CLI: not found. The CLI has no call to the hosted run endpoint (search for completions/runs in apps/cli/src found nothing).
prerequisites: A Cloud (managed) turn that carries a managed-usage or free-trial reservation. A turn with neither cannot start durably and runs request-scoped (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow-input.ts:560-611; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:1001-1018).
The kill switch AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS must not be set to 0, false or off (apps/web/lib/workflows/durable-initial-turns.ts:5-19).
screens_and_controls: Stop control: sets cancellation_requested_at on the run (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1174).
Pause and resume of a run are served by sub-routes of the run endpoint (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/pause, /resume, /steer, /archive: directory listing).
journey: 1. The person sends an agent turn; the server creates the run row keyed by the request idempotency key (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:899-901; apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:23-25).
2. The server starts the durable workflow and waits for its first event; if that fails it falls back to a request-scoped stream (route.ts:946-1018).
3. In Work mode a plan row is opened first (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts:74-76).
4. Each model call and tool call is claimed, run and stored as an operation receipt; events are appended in order (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:238-338).
5. If the connection drops, the client calls the run endpoint with the last event number and replays what it missed (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs/[runId]/route.ts:50-58).

6. If the turn needs approval, a checkpoint is saved and the run waits; the workflow continues in a new invocation when a turn passes the invocation limit (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts:81-85).
7. At the end the run is settled and the stream closed; if the worker died, the reaper settles it (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:90).
feedback_and_outputs: Replayed events in the chat or task view.

On an orphaned run the person sees: 'This turn did not finish: the run working on it ended before it could report back.' with code run_abandoned and retryable true (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:32-33; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-termination.ts:12, 38-45).
If the person had asked to stop: 'You stopped this turn, and the run working on it ended before it could report back.' (cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:34-35).
Response headers X-AGI-Tool-Loop: durable and X-AGI-Workflow-Run-Id (route.ts:983-984).
settings: AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS (kill switch; durable on unless set off) (apps/web/lib/workflows/durable-initial-turns.ts:5)
AGI_DB_LOW_POWER (sweep skipped outside the first 15 minutes of each hour) (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:5-18)
No user-facing setting found.

working: Run and event journal with per-user isolation (row level security) (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:56-70).
Operation receipts with leases, replay limit of 5 and result storage (apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:19-39; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-execution-service.ts:25).

Versioned approval checkpoints holding request, messages and 1 to 32 pending calls, claimed once under a lease; 24 hour expiry constant (apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:19-34; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:457).
Durable workflow loop that continues in new invocations until the turn settles (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow.ts:77-91).

Reaper: runs in states queued, planning, running, resuming idle for 1100 seconds (800 s invocation limit + 300 s lease) go to failed, or cancelled if a stop was requested; also cancels the workflow run; batches of 200, up to 25 batches, 240 s budget (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:13-18, 28, 110-125; apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:16; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-execution-service.ts:23).
Cron route with secret check, scheduled at minutes 10, 25, 40, 55 of each hour (apps/web/app/api/cron/reap-agent-runs/route.ts:13-31; vercel.json:70-71).
Work plan row opened for Work mode runs and settled at the end (apps/web/lib/workflows/steps/work-plan-steps.ts:18-65).
incomplete: Plan steps are not written during the run. The workflow opens the plan with no steps and only settles its status; no caller creates steps or revises the plan (apps/web/lib/workflows/steps/work-plan-steps.ts:29-36; apps/web/lib/services/work-plan-service.ts:365-370; search found no other caller of createWorkPlan outside the service). The in-run step list is still tracked in the tool loop (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:3880).
The brief says a run holds 'a lease'. The runs table has no lease column. Leases are on operations and checkpoints only (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9-29; 0063:25-27; 0062:25-26).
The reaped run is marked state failed with code run_abandoned on its error event. There is no state named abandoned (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-reaper.ts:112, 67).
Whether the migration for the plan tables (0237) is applied is not shown: its header reads 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0237_work_plans.sql:3).
disconnected_or_disabled: Request-scoped fallback: when the durable start fails, stalls or is switched off, the turn runs inline and dies with the connection (apps/web/lib/workflows/durable-initial-turns.ts:12-15; route.ts:1001-1018).
not_available: CLI: no use of the hosted run journal found. The CLI keeps its own sessions (search of apps/cli/src for the run endpoint found nothing).

Local mode and own-key: a durable turn needs a managed-usage or free-trial reservation, so a turn without one runs request-scoped (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-workflow-input.ts:605-611). Whether an own-key turn carries a reservation: unknown.

established.statement: Runs are stored with state, events and a lease.
Plans and steps are stored and updated as the run goes.
A checkpoint holds messages, pending calls and the request; a run can resume from it.
Tool calls and their results are stored durably with the run so a paused or resumed turn and the transcript can read them.
A reaper sweep settles runs whose invocation has ended so they do not hang; an orphaned run is marked with a reason.
Client reconnection on each app is not established by the brief.

acceptance_criteria: Closing the tab during a Work run does not stop it; reopening shows the events from where the client left off.
A run with no activity for more than 1100 seconds in a worker-held state is set to failed (or cancelled if stop was requested) by the next sweep, and an error event with code run_abandoned is added.
A run waiting for a person (awaiting_input, awaiting_approval, paused) is never reaped.
A completed operation replayed with the same key returns the stored result and does not run the tool again.
A second approval checkpoint can be saved for the same run only after the first is resolved (one active per run).
With AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS set to off, a turn still answers but runs request-scoped.
Work mode run ends with its plan row settled (completed, failed or cancelled).
inferred: The run should be listed and re-openable after a reload on every app that shows cloud tasks [inferred from the shared run client in several apps].
Plan steps should appear in work_plan_steps as the run proceeds, since the table, the status function and the revision schema exist [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Write plan steps and their status changes from the tool loop into work_plan_steps so the stored plan matches what the run shows.
[proposed] Add a run lease column or document that operation leases are the only leases.
[proposed] Show the person a clear 'resumed' or 'ended' state on each app after reconnecting.

steps.what_happens: Chat route creates the run row and event cursor for the turn
Route starts the durable workflow and waits for the first event within a time budget; on failure it cancels and runs inline
Each model and tool call is claimed under a lease, run, and its result stored
The model call goes to the chosen provider
Events are appended and streamed to the client; the client reconnects with the last sequence
On a tool needing approval a checkpoint is saved; the person's answer resumes it
The reaper updates stalled runs and cancels the workflow run

features.summary: A Cloud agent run gets a limit set: 20 dollars of model spend, 500 tool calls and 6 hours of wall clock. Before each durable model or tool call the server checks these, and stops the run when one is passed or when the same tool call would be made a fifth time in a row. The stopping cap is recorded.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates one budget row per Managed Cloud run and checks it before each durable operation. It refuses on time, tool-call count, repeated identical tool call, or spend, and writes the refusal code on the row. (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-budget.ts:23-34, 234-287; apps/web/db/neon/0258_cloud_agent_run_budgets.sql:35-70)
purpose.why_it_exists: The cloud runtime metered a run only after it settled, so a loop or runaway spend showed up only on the invoice. The CLI engine already had a spend cap and a loop stop. (apps/web/db/neon/0258_cloud_agent_run_budgets.sql:3-10)
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person running a Cloud agent turn gets it automatically; engineers read the refusal code when a run stops. No setting for the person was found.
problems_solved: A run that loops on one tool is stopped on the fifth identical call (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-budget.ts:19, 265-272).
A run cannot spend without end: provider calls are refused once observed spend reaches the cap (cloud-agent-budget.ts:275-284).
A run cannot go on for days: refused after 6 hours (cloud-agent-budget.ts:251-256).
The reason survives the process: the first refusal code is stored (cloud-agent-budget.ts:161-175).
use_cases: An agent keeps calling the same search with the same input; on the fifth try the run stops with a message.
A research run reaches its spend cap and stops before the next model call.
A run left waiting for hours is refused its next step after 6 hours of wall clock.
Support reads refusal_code to explain why a run ended.

where_to_find_it: No screen or control. The person sees only the stop message in the run's result. Where the message appears on each app: not verified.
prerequisites: A Cloud agent run on the durable workflow. Inline (request-scoped) fallback runs are not checked: the check lives in executeCloudAgentOperation, which is called only from workflow code (apps/web/lib/workflows/cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:262; search of apps/web for callers found workflow files only).
screens_and_controls: None found. The cap values are not editable by the person.
journey: 1. A run starts and works normally.
2. Before each model call or tool call, the server claims the operation, then checks the budget (cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:253-262).
3. If a cap is passed, the operation is marked failed with the refusal, a warning is logged, and a fatal error ends the step (cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:263-282).
4. The workflow's failure step writes an error event, a failed task state and a stop event (apps/web/lib/workflows/steps/fail-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:55-75).
5. The person sees a failed run with an error message.
feedback_and_outputs: Spend: 'This run reached its spend limit of <credits>, so AGI stopped before spending more.' (cloud-agent-budget.ts:281)
Tool calls: 'This run reached its limit of 500 tool calls, so AGI stopped instead of running another one.' (cloud-agent-budget.ts:262)
Time: 'This run reached its time limit of <minutes> minutes, so AGI stopped instead of starting another step.' (cloud-agent-budget.ts:254)
Loop: 'AGI was about to make the same tool call for the 5th time in a row, so this run was stopped instead of looping.' (cloud-agent-budget.ts:270)
Whether this exact text reaches the person: the failure step maps the error through a provider error classifier, so it is not established (fail-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:34-39).
settings: Defaults are constants: 20 dollars, 500 calls, 6 hours (cloud-agent-budget.ts:23-27). No setting or flag found. Loop threshold 5 mirrors the CLI engine, checked by a test (cloud-agent-budget.ts:14-19).

working: Budget row created on first use with the defaults, including for older runs (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-budget.ts:121-147).
Checks run in order: time, then for tool calls the count and repeat loop, then for model calls the spend (cloud-agent-budget.ts:251-284).
Spend is measured from recorded provider usage for the run, priced by its provider and model (cloud-agent-budget.ts:177-195).
The refusal is recorded once (first wins) and the operation is failed with it (cloud-agent-budget.ts:165-175; cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:263-282).
A replay of an already-claimed step returns its receipt and is not refused (cloud-agent-operation-executor.ts:259-262).
Table checks keep the numbers valid and tie a budget to its owner (apps/web/db/neon/0258_cloud_agent_run_budgets.sql:35-70).
incomplete: The code does not reserve the spend up front. It reads spend so far and refuses only when the cap is already reached, so one provider call can overshoot (cloud-agent-budget.ts:275-284). The brief's wording 'reserved up front' is therefore not what the code does.

The table allows subagent refusal codes (depth, fan-out, attempt) and has parent and depth columns, but the service accepts only four codes and has no subagent logic (apps/web/db/neon/0258_cloud_agent_run_budgets.sql:49-52 vs apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-budget.ts:29-34).
No code outside the budget service reads refusal_code or the codes (search of apps/web app, lib, features found none), so the UI cannot show the cap by name.
disconnected_or_disabled: Scheduled unattended runs do not go through this check: scheduled-agent-executor.ts calls the tool loop directly and does not use executeCloudAgentOperation (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:595-640).
Request-scoped fallback turns are not budgeted (see prerequisites).
not_available: CLI: uses its own cost cap and loop stop (apps/cli/src/cost_ledger.rs; crates/agiworkforce-agent-core/src/runaway.rs:14), not this table.
Desktop, Mobile, Chrome, VS Code: no budget logic of their own found; they follow the hosted run.

established.statement: Defaults per run: spend 20 dollars (stored as micro-dollars), 500 tool calls, 6 hours wall clock.
The same call made 5 times in a row stops the run.
The spend check happens before each provider operation.
Each refusal is recorded with its code.
A refused operation returns a stop message and the run ends.
The brief's Should line says each run has a budget reserved up front and enforced before every operation; the code enforces but does not reserve.

acceptance_criteria: A new run gets a budget row with 20,000,000 micro-dollars, 500 tool calls and 21,600,000 ms.
The fifth identical tool call in a row (same fingerprint) is refused with code tool_loop; a different call at the same count is allowed.
The 501st tool call is refused with code run_tool_call_cap.
A provider call after observed spend reaches the cap is refused with code run_cost_cap.
Any operation after 6 hours is refused with code run_time_cap.
Only the first refusal code is kept on the row.
A refused operation shows as failed in cloud_agent_execution_operations and the run ends in failed state.
A replayed completed operation is returned and not refused.
inferred: The person should be told which cap stopped the run, in words, on every app [inferred from the message texts written for it].
Scheduled and inline runs should have the same caps [inferred from the stated purpose: one envelope for the runtime].
proposed: [proposed] Put the refusal code on the error event so each app can show a clear title and a link to what to do next.
[proposed] Apply the check to inline fallback and scheduled runs.
[proposed] Reserve an estimate before a provider call, or document that overshoot by one call is accepted.
[proposed] Let a plan or the person set the cap.

steps.what_happens: The workflow wraps a model or tool call in executeCloudAgentOperation and claims the operation
For a newly acquired operation, the budget row is read or created and checked
Tool-call count and last four input hashes are read from the operations table (current operation excluded)
For model calls, run usage is read and priced for the run's provider and model
On refusal: refusal code written, operation failed, warning logged, fatal error thrown
Workflow failure step writes error, failed state and stop events

features.summary: People set up a task that runs on its own at a set time, once or repeating. A cron endpoint every 15 minutes claims due runs in waves of 10 and stops at 55 seconds. Each run uses the tool loop without a person present. Tools that would need asking are withheld, or the run pauses for approval.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores scheduled tasks and their runs, finds those that are due, runs the agent for each with a time limit, and records the result. It runs with the person's Tool approvals rules: tools allowed without asking run; others are not offered or cause a pause that the owner can approve later. (apps/web/app/api/cron/run-schedules/route.ts:14-72; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:2471-2520; apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:237-372, 595-640)
purpose.why_it_exists: People want a daily briefing or weekly summary without opening the app. A run with nobody present cannot ask permission, so it needs rules for that. (apps/web/lib/server/tools/schedule-tool.ts:42-44; apps/web/db/neon/0308_schedule_run_approval.sql:3-8)
purpose.who_uses_it: People on a plan that allows scheduled tasks: basic 3, pro 5, max 15, max_15x 25, team 10 tasks; free, byok and local-only 0 (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:562-700). Plan display names may differ from these keys.
problems_solved: Repeat work can be set once and runs by itself.

A run cannot do an action that needs a person without that person knowing: it pauses and waits for approval for up to 24 hours (apps/web/db/neon/0308_schedule_run_approval.sql:3-8; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:79).
A claimed run whose worker died is recovered through lease expiry (schedule-service.ts:2487-2489).
Spend cap on the account pauses schedules with reason credit_cap_reached (schedule-service.ts:1794, 2144).
use_cases: A daily morning briefing task.
A weekly summary of a project's files using the project context.
A one-time reminder set from chat with the create_schedule tool.
A recurring task that stops and asks the owner before sending data out.

where_to_find_it: Web: route /chat/schedules, page heading 'Scheduled', button 'Create a task', search 'Search scheduled tasks' (apps/web/app/chat/schedules/page.tsx; apps/web/features/schedules/components/SchedulesPage.tsx:967, 1010, 1065). Also a section inside a project (apps/web/app/chat/projects/[id]/page.tsx:44).
Chat: the create_schedule tool, described as 'set up a task that runs on its own at a set time' (apps/web/lib/prompts/chat-system-prompt.ts:423; apps/web/lib/server/tools/schedule-tool.ts:16).
CLI, Mobile: files that call the schedules API exist (apps/cli/src/schedules.rs; apps/mobile/src/features/schedules/service.ts); screens and labels not read.
Chrome extension page lists 'Scheduled tasks' (apps/web/app/chrome-extension/page.tsx:74).
prerequisites: A plan with a non-zero scheduled task limit; otherwise the page shows 'Scheduled tasks are available on Basic and higher plans.' (SchedulesPage.tsx:306, 1076).
Managed compute access for schedules must allow the run (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:915-935).
screens_and_controls: Create a task, More ways to create a task, templates, status filter, project filter, share link (SchedulesPage.tsx:1010, 1024, 1206, 1235, 1537).

Form note: 'Scheduled tasks are swept <cadence>, so the shortest supported interval is <minimum>.' (apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleForm.tsx:358-359; sweep interval 15 minutes: packages/platform/utils/src/scheduling/schedule-time.ts:259).
journey: 1. Create a task by form or by asking in chat (create_schedule: name, prompt, recurrence once/daily/weekly/monthly, time) (schedule-tool.ts:42-60).
2. The task saves, checked against the plan's task limit (schedule-service.ts:877, 994).
3. The cron sweep claims due runs (apps/web/app/api/cron/run-schedules/route.ts:47-52).
4. The executor checks secrets, access policy, route and tools, then runs the tool loop with unattended settings (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:861-935, 595-640).
5. The result is saved with status success, failed, timeout, cancelled or awaiting_approval (schedule-service.ts:350).
6. If a step needs approval, the run waits; the owner approves or denies and it resumes (0308 migration).
feedback_and_outputs: Run history with status (apps/web/app/api/schedules/runs/route.ts).
Skipped-run text such as 'Scheduled execution skipped: <reason>' for secret handling or access denial (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:890, 920).
When search or code tools are withheld the run's result says which step was skipped and points to Settings, Capabilities, Tool approvals (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:374-425).
Expired approval: 'Nobody approved or denied the step this run was waiting on within 24 hours, so the run stopped. Resume the schedule to run it again.' (schedule-service.ts:79).
settings: Settings, Capabilities, Tool approvals (named in the withheld-tool note) (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:424).
AGI_DB_LOW_POWER (sweep paused outside minutes 0 to 14 of each hour) (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts).
Per-task: recurrence, retry settings, missed-run policy run_once or skip (schedule-service.ts:102, 2076).

working: Cron endpoint checks the secret, skips under low power, runs up to 5 waves of 10 claims (limit 50 per sweep) and stops after 55 seconds of budget; each wave has a 40 second run timeout (apps/web/app/api/cron/run-schedules/route.ts:14-72; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:478).
Cron runs every 15 minutes (vercel.json:49-51).
Before claiming, expired approvals are stopped and expired claims recovered (schedule-service.ts:2481-2487).
Claim leases the run for the timeout plus 5 seconds (schedule-service.ts:2490-2492).
The run goes through the tool loop with unattended true and escalation pauses (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:619-620).
Tools needing approval under the owner's rules are not offered for the provider-native search or code tools, and a note says so (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:264-327, 374-425).
A run can pause awaiting_approval and resume (apps/web/db/neon/0308_schedule_run_approval.sql:21-35; schedule-service.ts:1957).
Retries with backoff up to 5 attempts (schedule-service.ts:77-80, 1643).
Entitlement and managed-compute access are checked at run time (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:903-935).
incomplete: Each scheduled run is cut off at about 40 seconds (the wave timeout becomes the run timeout) and ends with status timeout, so long tasks do not 'run to completion' (route.ts:16, 47-52; schedule-service.ts:2323).

The brief says anything that would need asking is refused. The code withholds some tools and pauses others for approval; it does not refuse outright (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:619-620, 374-381; 0308 migration).
Scheduled runs do not use the per-run budget or the durable run journal (F092-07, F092-08); they use their own run table scheduled_task_runs (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:595-640).
disconnected_or_disabled: Low-power skip: when AGI_DB_LOW_POWER is 1 the sweep returns skipped db_low_power outside the first 15 minutes of each hour (apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:15-18).
not_available: Free, byok and local-only plans: limit 0, so no scheduled tasks (billing-catalog.ts:590-640).
Local mode: no on-device scheduler found in the files read. The CLI has its own cron tools (apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/mod.rs:1196 'cron_create'); not examined further.

established.statement: A cron endpoint with a secret check claims due runs in waves of 10 and stops at a sweep budget of 55 seconds.
Tools run only if the unattended gate allows them; anything that would need asking is refused.
Low-power cron skip can pause the sweep.
A durable scheduler starts scheduled agent runs on time and runs them to completion unattended.

acceptance_criteria: Calling the cron route without the secret returns 401 and runs nothing.
With 25 due runs, one sweep claims 10, 10, then 5 and stops (drained true).
A task on a plan with limit 0 cannot be created; the page shows the plan message.
A task whose tool needs approval under the owner's policy either has the tool withheld with a note or pauses as awaiting_approval, and never runs it silently.
An unanswered approval is stopped after 24 hours with the message above.
A run that exceeds its time limit is recorded as timeout and may retry up to the configured attempts.
With AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1 at minute 30 the route answers skipped db_low_power.
inferred: A scheduled run should be able to run longer than 40 seconds if the product wants long agent tasks [inferred from the brief's 'to completion'].
proposed: [proposed] Run long scheduled tasks on the durable workflow so they get journal, budget and recovery.
[proposed] Tell the owner in a notification when a run pauses for approval.

Expired approval waits are stopped and expired claims recovered
