features.summary: A named agent is a saved set of instructions, tools and model. In the CLI it is a markdown file under .agiworkforce/agents or .claude/agents, managed with /agents. The web app also has a hosted Agents page backed by the user_agents table. The old /api/agents/execute route answers 410. The CLI has a subagent manager; the hosted run has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person define a reusable agent (name, description, instructions, model, tools) and run chats or tasks as that agent. In the CLI an agent file overrides the session's model, tools, turn cap, permission mode and system prompt. On the web a built agent can be published, shared and run in chat or on a schedule. The CLI can also run named agents as child sessions. (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:25-47, 6-11; apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:1-30; apps/cli/src/subagent.rs:575-590)
purpose.why_it_exists: People repeat the same instructions in every chat. Competitor products offer reusable agents. (apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:3-10)
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers on the CLI; people on web who build and share agents with a workspace.
problems_solved: Reuse instead of re-pasting instructions.
Narrow what an agent may do: a CLI agent can only narrow, never widen, the session's permission mode (apps/cli/src/agents.rs:2384-2437).
Share an agent with a workspace with published versions (apps/web/db/neon/0370_user_agents.sql:15-24).
use_cases: In the CLI, /agents create <name> and edit the file, then run with --agent <name>.
A model in the CLI lists installed agents through the agent tool and asks the foreground orchestrator to run one.
On web, build an agent on /chat/agents, publish it and start a chat as it.
Run a scheduled task as a chosen agent (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:896-901).

features.summary: Per-turn context assembly is the server step that decides which memory, past-chat, project-instruction and project-file items go into one chat turn. It checks the user's switches, workspace policy and ownership, applies per-source size caps, and stores a manifest of what was included or left out. It runs for the web chat endpoint and the Free chat path.

purpose.what_it_does: For each chat turn the server builds a list of context sources (account memory, past chats, project instructions, project knowledge files, other chats in the project), refuses classes the user or workspace has switched off, drops duplicates and stale items, applies per-source character caps, and records a manifest of what was included and excluded and why (packages/platform/context-engine/src/engine.ts:162-321; apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:105-243).
purpose.why_it_exists: Without one gate, each loader would do its own permission and policy checks, and nobody could explain afterwards why the assistant knew something; the engine comment says the checks are the engine's, not each loader's (engine.ts:157-161; apps/web/db/neon/0252_context_manifests_and_source_policy.sql:6-11).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who chats through the managed Cloud chat endpoint gets it without choosing anything; engineers and support use the manifest to explain a turn [inferred from the stored table].
problems_solved: A switched-off setting or a temporary chat cannot leak personal context into a turn (engine.ts:115-132).
A failing source cannot break the whole turn (engine.ts:134-144).
The same fact stated by memory and by a past chat is sent once (engine.ts:215-220).
A turn can be explained after the fact from stored counts and ids, without keeping the text (types.ts:116-120).
use_cases: A user with Memory on asks a question and relevant saved memories are added.
A user in a project asks about an uploaded file and the project instructions, matching file passages and sibling chats are added.
A user starts a temporary chat and no memory or past chats are added.
A scheduled agent run assembles memory and recent chats through the same engine (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:446-472).

where_to_find_it: Web: no screen of its own; the effect appears in every Cloud chat. The switches that feed it are in Settings, Memory: 'Search past chats' and the memory switch (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:409-416).
Desktop (Electron) shows the hosted web app, so it gets the same server assembly [inferred from AGENTS.md section 5, doc: AGENTS.md].
Mobile: when the execution mode is cloud the server assembles context (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2800).
CLI, VS Code extension, Chrome extension: not established; no call to this engine was found in those folders. unknown.

features.summary: Instruction order places the parts of a model's system message in a fixed ranking: system, developer, project, personalized, memory, untrusted content. Memory and untrusted content are marked as reference only. A helper reports any lower layer placed above a higher one. The web chat endpoint sorts its blocks with it.

purpose.what_it_does: Defines six instruction layers, maps every context source class to one of them, sorts prompt blocks by layer with a stable order inside a layer, and defines a conflict table saying what happens to the losing layer (packages/contracts/context/src/instruction-precedence.ts:11-18,48-63,125-136,156-172).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a lower layer such as a recalled memory or a fetched page cannot sit above, or act as, a higher one; the header comment says every surface orders by this and nothing else decides which instruction wins (instruction-precedence.ts:9-10).
purpose.who_uses_it: The chat server code, tests and the desktop device-side copy; people only feel the effect when project or personal instructions change an answer.
problems_solved: Prompt injection through memory or fetched content being treated as commands (instruction-precedence.ts:22-26,37-44).
Two modules ordering the same layers differently (precedenceDisagreements, lines 202-216).
A source class whose trust does not fit its layer (instructionLayerTrustMismatches, lines 219-224).
use_cases: A project instruction beats the person's custom instruction when they conflict.
A recalled memory saying 'ignore previous rules' is treated as data.
A fetched web page placed after memory in the prompt.
A test fails if a new source class has no layer.

features.summary: When a chat is too long for the model's window, the server drops the oldest turns and, for saved non-temporary chats, replaces them with a short model-written summary kept on the conversation. The summary is reused only while a digest of the covered messages still matches. On any failure it falls back to a plain trim.

purpose.what_it_does: Plans which old messages to drop, asks a managed model to summarize them (up to 24,000 characters in, 2,000 out), saves the summary with a coverage digest on web_conversations, and substitutes it for the dropped span as a fenced note (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/context-compaction.ts:40-42,152-275,411-476).
purpose.why_it_exists: So long conversations keep going instead of failing, while keeping facts from early turns, and so an edited or deleted message cannot live on in a stale summary (migration 0282 header, apps/web/db/neon/0282_compaction_summary_coverage.sql:3-12).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone with a long Cloud chat thread; no control is shown.
problems_solved: Prompt exceeds the model window.
Withdrawn words coming back through a cached summary (0282:5-12).
Paying for a summary that will not help because the newest message cannot fit (context-compaction.ts:438).
Instructions hidden in dropped content being laundered into plain text (context-compaction.ts:68-85).
use_cases: A long research chat that outgrows the window keeps its early decisions.
A user deletes a message inside the summarized span; the next turn rebuilds the summary.
A temporary chat gets a plain trim only.
A later turn extends the stored summary with only the newly dropped messages.

where_to_find_it: Web Cloud chat: no control; a fenced note in the prompt marks dropped history. Visible only to the model.
Mobile and Desktop in Cloud mode use the same endpoint (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2800) [inferred for desktop from AGENTS.md section 5].
CLI, VS Code, Chrome extension: not established. unknown.

screens_and_controls: None. The 'switch' in the draft is a server setting, not a user control (context-compaction.ts:38,59-62).
journey: The person keeps chatting in a long thread.
The server estimates the prompt against the model window and plans a trim (context-compaction.ts:414).
If messages would be dropped and the chat qualifies, the server looks for a stored summary that still matches (lines 335-353).
If none, it calls a managed model to summarize the dropped span, billed as background usage (lines 212-253).
It stores the summary and substitutes it for the span (lines 368-377, 459-468).
The model answers with the summary in place of the old turns.
feedback_and_outputs: The model sees a fenced block 'Earlier messages summarized to fit the model context window.' or, on plain trim, the dropped-history marker (context-compaction.ts:74-85; context-window.ts:16-17).
If the newest message cannot fit, the turn is refused with a 'message too long' response (request-processor.ts:6730-6755).
settings: Server env AGI_CONTEXT_COMPACTION_ENABLED: off, false or 0 disables summaries (context-compaction.ts:59-62).
No per-user setting found.

working: Plan, summarize, store, reuse and extend (context-compaction.ts:277-380).
Digest covers message ids, row versions and dropped-text fingerprints, so edits, deletes and branch switches invalidate it (lines 126-150,343-348).
Fallback to plain trim for temporary chat, no conversation id, kill switch, newest-message overflow, or any error (lines 433-441,469-475).
Secrets redacted before the summary call (lines 170-181).
Summary of untrusted tool content uses a separate fence tag (lines 68-85).
Reservation released when the provider fails (lines 258-273).

disconnected_or_disabled: Migration 0164 and 0282 headers: 0282 is titled 'Migration 0280' inside the file; apply state unknown (0282:2).
not_available: No user-visible control or indicator for compaction on any app searched.
No local-model summary path: the summary always calls a managed route (lines 164-168).

established.statement: When a conversation outgrows the window, older turns are compacted into a summary and the turn continues.

features.summary: Recall finds earlier chats and project files that match the current question and adds short passages to the turn. Past chats need the 'Search past chats' switch and are skipped in temporary chats. Project files use the search index for large files and per-request passage picking otherwise. Failures are reported to the model as degraded recall.

Project files: for files over 16,000 characters, asks the index for passages; otherwise picks passages per request (project-context-service.ts:339-350; project-knowledge-retrieval.ts:27-65).
purpose.why_it_exists: So the assistant can use what the person said before and what their project files say, without sending everything every turn; the budget is small (past-chat-context-service.ts:28-43; project-context-service.ts:79-93).

features.summary: The indexer cuts project files, library files, chats, artifacts, reports and developer sessions into overlapping text chunks and stores them with a text-search column and, when possible, an embedding vector. Embedding is a metered call. If it fails, chunks stay keyword-searchable and indexing retries with growing delays. A cron sweep every ten minutes starts the work.

purpose.what_it_does: Claims a pending retrieval document, loads its source text, cuts it into 1,400-character windows with 200 overlap (max 400 chunks), embeds the chunks in metered batches, writes chunks and settles the document status in one transaction (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-index-service.ts:417-436,479-518,658-785; packages/platform/data-layer/src/search/chunk.ts:10-15).
purpose.why_it_exists: Search by meaning and by keyword needs a prepared copy of the content; 0202 says nothing was embedded before so there was no semantic or hybrid retrieval on managed cloud (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:6-10).

features.summary: This is search over a person's own indexed content. It merges keyword matches from a full-text index with meaning matches from a vector index, re-scores the merged list, and returns passages. It is used by the chat server for recall and by the web 'Search your workspace' dialog. Without vectors it answers by keyword alone and says so.

purpose.what_it_does: Builds a full-text query and, when an index with embeddings exists, a query vector; runs both inside the caller's user and workspace; merges ranks (reciprocal rank), re-scores on term coverage, exact phrase and title, removes near-duplicates and caps hits per source (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-search-service.ts:444-529; packages/platform/data-layer/src/search/rank.ts:5-95).
purpose.why_it_exists: Keyword search misses meaning and vector search misses exact terms; combining them gives better passages for chat and for the search dialog (0202 header lines 6-10).
purpose.who_uses_it: The chat server (past chats, project files, attached files, research file sources) and web users of the global search dialog.

features.summary: Web search lets the AGI Workforce assistant look up current facts on the public web during a chat turn. On the web app it is ambient: on whenever the chosen model has a search route. The server decides when a search is required, runs it through one configured provider, caps and meters the calls, and returns numbered sources.

purpose.what_it_does: On Cloud turns, the server gives the model a web_search tool (or the provider's own built-in search), decides whether a search is mandatory for the message, runs the search through the configured provider adapter, and returns up to 5 results as fenced, untrusted, numbered sources [apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts:54-58, 493-550; apps/web/lib/web-search/required-search.ts:186-262].
purpose.why_it_exists: Models answer from training data that goes stale. Search gives current, citable facts, and the per-call limits and charges keep the cost of a bought search call bounded [apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:25-31 comment].
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone chatting with Cloud models on web, mobile, Chrome and the Desktop window that shows the web app; also automated callers (API, CLI, VS Code in Cloud mode, AGI Work, Deep Research, scheduled runs), which are billed differently [apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:45-64].
problems_solved: Stale or invented answers on recent events
Answers with no sources on turns whose point is current information (required search) [apps/web/lib/web-search/required-search.ts:210-216 comment]
Unbounded provider spend from a free plan [apps/web/lib/web-search/search-budget.ts:25-31]
Prompt injection through search snippets (results are fenced as untrusted data) [apps/web/lib/web-search/web-search-tool.ts:539-549]
use_cases: Ask 'who is the current head of a company' and get a sourced answer; the office-holder pattern forces a search [apps/web/lib/web-search/required-search.ts:110-125]
Type /search followed by a question to force a search on the web composer [apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:3190-3205]
Run an AGI Work task that needs outside facts; search is mandatory there [apps/web/lib/web-search/required-search.ts:190]
A model without built-in search still searches through the platform tool [apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2520-2530 comment]

The + menu row labels are listed at ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:147-200 and none is Web search; the 'Deep Research' row at ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1305-1311 is a different feature. Web search is ambient and follows model support [apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:1690-1698].

Paid and automated calls reserve a charge before the call, then settle or release it; a refused reserve (HTTP 402 or 429) stops the call; any other hold failure lets the call run and queues the charge [search-budget.ts:199-272, 404-428; tool-loop.ts:5020-5075].

A query planner decides when and what to search (required-search detection, research query plan).
Results from any provider are normalized into one source shape (id, url, title, provider, dates).
Web search and code execution stay separately capability-, deployment-, policy- and trust-gated, and web search is not an intrinsic model capability.
Web search and page fetches ask before running unless policy allows; the founder decision on making them read-only is pending.
Local, own-key and Cloud stay separate; nothing routes a Local chat to Cloud silently.

steps.what_happens: The web composer keeps web search on only when the selected model has a search route, and /search marks the turn as search-requested.
The request carries web_search and search_requested to the chat completions route.
The server checks canUseWebSearch and a kill switch; if off, web_search and web_fetch are cleared for the turn.
The server classifies whether a search is required and offers the tool: native search for providers that have it, otherwise the platform web_search function when a backend key exists.
When the model calls web_search, the loop checks the per-turn budget, then decides free window, charge or refusal, and reserves a charge.
executeWebSearch calls the first configured provider; on failure it tries the next.
Results get missing titles filled by fetching the page, are ranked, numbered against the turn's source list, fenced and sent to the model; sources stream to the client.
The call is settled against the hold; sources are collected from the stream and saved with the message.

features.summary: Reading a web page lets the assistant fetch one public http or https address and return its readable text, title, description and date, with HTML, PDF and Office files supported. Every hop is checked so private or internal addresses are refused. Pages are cut at a size limit, fenced as untrusted, and capped per turn.

purpose.what_it_does: url_fetch downloads one public URL, reduces it to text, and returns title, text, a short description and a date when the page declares them [apps/web/lib/url-fetch/url-fetch-tool.ts:486-684].
purpose.why_it_exists: Search snippets are short. The model needs the page itself to quote or check a claim, and a fetch from a server must not become a way to reach internal networks [apps/web/lib/url-fetch/guarded-fetch.ts:91-100; apps/web/lib/egress-policy.ts:289-300].
purpose.who_uses_it: The model (tool call) on Cloud turns, the Deep Research loop, and the title and redirect helpers that reuse the guarded fetch [apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2730-2751; research-loop.url-fetch.test.ts; web-search-tool.ts:803-830].
problems_solved: Server-side request forgery to private addresses
Redirect chains that end somewhere unsafe
Huge or binary responses
Page text trying to instruct the model
use_cases: A user pastes a link and asks for a summary
The model follows a search result to read the full article
A Deep Research run reads a PDF report
A project domain rule limits reading to approved sites

where_to_find_it: No dedicated screen. The user pastes a link or asks to read a page; the explicit-fetch phrasing turns web_fetch on [apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:988-990].
The page appears as a source chip on the answer (url_fetch sources carry a tool tag) [tool-loop.ts:1458-1470 comment].
Mobile and Chrome: web_fetch flag sent to the managed route [apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/freeTrialClient.ts:1604].
CLI has its own web_fetch tool [apps/cli/src/features/exec/tools/web/mod.rs:536].
prerequisites: Cloud mode with web search or web fetch allowed for the turn (the same capability gate clears both) [request-processor.ts:5249-5252].
A streaming request: url_fetch is offered only when the request streams [request-processor.ts:2634].
screens_and_controls: No control of its own; follows the web search gate and the per-chat site rules (research domain policy).
journey: 1. The user pastes a URL or asks to read a page.
2. The model calls url_fetch with the address.
3. The server checks the address and every redirect, then downloads within limits.
4. Text is extracted and fenced as untrusted content.
5. The model answers; the page shows as a source.
feedback_and_outputs: On success: 'Fetched <url>', title and text inside an untrusted-content fence [url-fetch-tool.ts:705-720].
On failure: 'Fetch failed (<code>): <message>' to the model [tool-loop.ts:2737-2740].
Truncation note: '[Content truncated: showing the first 20,000 of N extracted characters.]' [url-fetch-tool.ts:673-681].
Budget text when the turn has fetched its allowed pages [url-fetch-tool.ts:32-37].
settings: Per-chat allowed or denied sites from the Deep Research plan card or workspace rules (domain policy) [url-fetch-tool.ts:560-570].

working: Only http and https; embedded user name or password is refused; cookie and authorization headers are never sent [apps/web/lib/url-fetch/guarded-fetch.ts:67, 91-95].
Each hop is resolved and checked as public before the request; redirects are followed manually up to 5, each re-checked [guarded-fetch.ts:107-205].
Private and internal addresses refused by the egress policy, which also pins the checked addresses for the request [apps/web/lib/egress-policy.ts:271-300].
Limits: 10 s, 1.5 MB (10 MB for documents), 20,000 characters returned, 5 redirects; 5 reads per chat turn, 15 per AGI Work turn [url-fetch-tool.ts:30-46; tool-loop.ts:4673-4677].
Content types: HTML, XHTML, plain text, Markdown, JSON; PDF and Word, Excel or PowerPoint files go through a document reader [url-fetch-tool.ts:46-55, 499-512, 601-628].
Title, description and publication date are read from the page's own metadata for HTML [url-fetch-tool.ts:684-700].
Domain policy: a URL outside allowed sites is refused, and a redirect that leaves the allowed sites is refused with a clear message [url-fetch-tool.ts:560-570, 588-600].
Character set check: an undecodable declared encoding returns unsupported_content_type [url-fetch-tool.ts:650-658].
Page text is fenced, with '<' escaped so it cannot close the fence [url-fetch-tool.ts:705-720].
incomplete: The same extraction helpers are used for titles in search results, but a failed metadata fetch silently leaves the field empty [web-search-tool.ts:733-775].
disconnected_or_disabled: Where the provider has its own fetch tool (Anthropic route), the platform can attach that native tool instead of url_fetch; the provider then reads the page outside our address checks [request-processor.ts:2603-2620].
url_fetch is not offered on non-streaming requests [request-processor.ts:2634].
not_available: No per-call charge for url_fetch was found in the tool loop (none found).
Internal Tauri build has a separate scrape and fetch implementation (not traced) [apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/core/llm/tool_executor/search_tools.rs:439].

established.statement: A web-fetch service reads a given URL and returns its text for the model.
URLs are resolved safely: only public http(s) hosts, no credentials, redirects re-checked, private or internal addresses refused.
Fetched pages are reduced to readable text with title, description and date extracted.
Security behavior fails closed; desktop and server egress go through the egress policy.

acceptance_criteria: A URL with a user name or password is refused.
A hostname that resolves to a private address is refused after lookup.
A redirect to a private address is refused even when the first URL is public.
A page over the character cap returns the first 20,000 characters and a truncation note.
A page with no readable text returns an error naming the address.
The sixth page read in one chat turn is refused with the budget message.
A PDF under the document cap returns its text.
inferred: Per-call spend is not charged because no charge code was found; confirm this is intended [inferred from absence in tool-loop.ts:2730-2751].
proposed: [proposed] Apply the same address checks when a provider-native fetch tool is used, or state that the provider does the reading.
[proposed] Add per-call limits for documents to the same turn ledger as pages.

steps.what_happens: The model or the user's explicit request triggers url_fetch with an address.
The address is checked for scheme, credentials, length and the site policy.
The host is resolved and checked public, then fetched with redirect handling set to manual.

Text is extracted, cut, fenced and returned; the page joins the turn's sources.

features.summary: Citations are the numbered source links under an answer. The server numbers them in the order sources were shown, saves them with the message, and replaces Google routing redirects with publisher addresses. Project-file citations can point to a page or heading. A grounding checker that verifies claims against sources is not built for chat or research.

features.summary: Deep Research is a long, paid-tier research run on Cloud. It drafts a plan the user reviews, runs bounded search and read rounds, stops on budgets, completed plan or a round with no new sources, then writes a cited report. The run is saved and can be paused, resumed, cancelled or retried.

purpose.what_it_does: Server-side loop: plan, user approval, gathering rounds with web search, page reads, optional files and connectors, then a synthesis turn that always runs on what was gathered; the report and its sources are saved [apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/research-loop.ts:1-52, 3088-3110, 3363-3395].
purpose.why_it_exists: One reply cannot cover a question that needs many sources. A durable report survives a closed tab or a failed run [apps/web/db/neon/0094_research_reports.sql:1-18].
purpose.who_uses_it: Paid-plan users on web, mobile and the internal desktop build [doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:63]. Not on CLI, VS Code or Chrome [same doc, lines 277-279].
problems_solved: Shallow answers to broad questions
Lost work when a run fails
Unreviewed spend (the plan is approved first)
Reports with no sources
use_cases: Compare options in a market with a cited report
Re-run a past report for current sources
Limit a run to named sites or the user's own files
Resume an interrupted run

journey: 1. Turn on Deep Research and send a question.
2. The server writes a plan and pauses at 'Review the plan to start searching' [research-loop.ts:3098-3110].
3. The user edits and presses 'Start research' (or 'Cancel').
4. Rounds of search and page reads run with progress.
5. A cited report is written and saved; a notification is sent [research-run-options.ts:74-97].
6. The user can pause, resume, retry, or save the report.
feedback_and_outputs: Status events: planning, awaiting_approval, searching, synthesizing, complete, error [research-loop.ts:446-520; mobile researchRunState.ts:19-28].
Status line 'Research complete' or 'Research complete, but the report could not be saved' [research-loop.ts:3583-3586].
Gaps list: planned questions the report does not answer [ResearchPlan.tsx:35 copy; research-loop.ts:590-631].
settings: Environment values: AGI_RESEARCH_MAX_ITERATIONS, AGI_RESEARCH_MAX_SEARCHES, AGI_RESEARCH_BUDGET_MS, AGI_RESEARCH_MAX_PARALLEL_TOOL_CALLS, AGI_RESEARCH_MAX_QUERY_REWRITES; AGI_NATIVE_SEARCH_MAX_USES [research-loop.ts:1771-1790, 171-227; request-processor.ts:2558-2561].
Deliverable defaults: full-report, prose, 0 minimum sources, stop when no new sources [packages/contracts/types/src/research.ts:286-292].

working: Capability check refuses Deep Research for non-paid tiers on the server and the composer disables it with an upgrade state [request-processor.ts:5221; billing-catalog.ts:355; ChatComposerNew.tsx:1620-1627].

Defaults: 6 iterations, 12 searches, 4-minute budget, 3 parallel tool calls, 4 query rewrites; each is read from an environment value within a range (iterations 2 to 8, searches 3 to 15, budget 30 s to 10 min, parallel 1 to 8, rewrites 0 to 12) [research-loop.ts:178-184, 227, 1771-1795].
A planning turn runs when there are at least 3 iterations; the last iteration is always synthesis [research-loop.ts:1796-1810].

Stop rules, as coded: (a) the model says READY_TO_REPORT AND every planned query is searched or dropped AND the minimum source count is met; (b) search budget reached; (c) time budget reached; (d) diminishing returns, meaning the latest round added zero new sources, only when the deliverable asks for it and no planned query is pending [research-loop.ts:3363-3395]. The 0.5 coverage threshold is not a stop rule; it labels gaps after the report [research-loop.ts:590-631]. The first draft was wrong on this.
Each search in a round goes through search admission: automated callers are charged; a refused or failed hold skips the search [research-loop.ts:1811-1845].

Cancellation is checked at boundaries from the client abort or a durable cancel flag; a cancelled run is stored as interrupted with what it gathered so a retry can resume [research-loop.ts:2034-2050; research-run-options.ts:11-14].
Pause, steer and resume exist (pause request, steer messages, resume with approved steps and prior sources) [research-loop.ts:2078-2100; research-run-options.ts:98-112; ResearchActivity.tsx:531-675].

Report save is an upsert on (user, request), retried 3 times; completed status sets completed_at; failed or interrupted rows keep an honest error [research-loop.ts:188-189, 1984-2024; research-report-service.ts:212-296; 0094_research_reports.sql:52].
Approved runs start as a durable workflow when durable turns are enabled and the transport is healthy; otherwise the request-scoped loop runs [route.ts:634-700].

Sources can include the user's own files and connected apps; allowed and denied sites are enforced at ingestion and in the reader [route.ts:604-626; research-sources.ts:56-66; research-loop.ts:855-880].

established.statement: Research runs store their evidence (sources, citations, status, cost) durably.
A research orchestrator runs plan, search rounds, stop rules, synthesis, cancellation and resume.
A report generator synthesizes the final report in the requested deliverable format with citations.

Review the plan before approved work begins; cancellation stops new side effects; resume an interrupted report without rerunning completed actions unnecessarily; allowed source controls are enforced, not just prompted; reports reopen with sources intact.
Deep Research is generally available on web, desktop and mobile, absent on CLI, VS Code and Chrome.

acceptance_criteria: A Free account cannot start Deep Research; the composer shows an upgrade state and the server refuses.
A paid account sees a plan first and no search runs until 'Start research'.
A run stops at 12 searches or 4 minutes by default and still writes a report.
A round that finds no new source ends gathering when the box is ticked and no planned query is pending.
Cancelling mid-run stores status interrupted with the gathered sources and a retry can resume.
A completed run has a saved row with status completed, citations and sources_consulted.
With sites restricted, no source outside them appears in the report.
If the save fails three times, the status line says the report could not be saved.

Free-plan refusal happens at two layers (capability and route) [route.ts:567; request-processor.ts:5221].

steps.what_happens: The composer sends the question with research on; the server checks the paid capability and the model.
The server starts a research cloud-agent run row and, for the first pass, writes a plan and stops for approval.
The user edits and approves the plan; the approved steps return with the next request.
Gathering rounds run searches and page reads (native provider search or the platform tools), within the budgets, and aggregate sources.
Synthesis writes the report; the loop saves the row and notifies the user.
The client lists and reopens reports through the reports API.

features.summary: After a normal chat turn in Cloud mode, AGI Workforce's server reads what the person wrote, picks out short personal facts (name, job, home, preferences), and saves them as memories. Duplicates are merged and a newer fact about the same single-valued topic replaces the old one. Each memory records its source chat and turn.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns ordinary chat statements such as 'I live in Berlin' into saved account memories without the person asking. The facts are later read back into replies (see F094-05). Mobile Local mode and the CLI have their own on-device versions of the same idea (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/consolidation.ts:176; apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:1-30).
purpose.why_it_exists: The project requires memory that is inspectable, editable and shared across Cloud chat contexts, with provenance on every entry (doc: docs/product/definition.md:200; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:28-31). Learning from chats is how the assistant stops asking the same questions again.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who has persistent memory turned on and chats in Cloud mode (Web, the Desktop window that shows the hosted web app, Mobile Cloud, CLI Managed sessions, Chrome extension and VS Code when they use Managed Cloud).
problems_solved: The person does not have to repeat their name, job, location or preferences in every chat.
The same fact is not stored twice, and a corrected fact (new city, new employer) replaces the old one instead of piling up.
The person can see where a learned fact came from and delete it.
use_cases: A person writes 'My name is Priya and I work at a bank.' The server saves two short facts after the reply.
A person who lived in Pune writes 'I live in Oslo'. The new residence fact replaces the old one; the old one is kept as history and can be restored.
A person turns off 'Save memories from chats'. Nothing is learned unless they say 'remember ...'.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Memory. Toggles 'Persistent memory', 'Save memories from chats', 'Include sensitive topics in memory', 'Allow memory generation from tool-assisted chats' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:316,395,419,432).

Web and Desktop (Electron shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5): learned facts appear in the memory list with the note 'Learned from "<chat title>"' or 'Learned from a chat' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MemoryEditor.tsx:574-588).
Mobile: Settings > Memory ('Cloud Memory' in Cloud mode, 'Memory' in Local mode) (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory.tsx:709).
CLI: account memory is cached from /api/memory/sync and shown in a TUI memories widget (apps/cli/src/cloud/memory.rs:1-8; apps/cli/src/tui/widgets/memories_settings.rs). Depth not read.
VS Code and Chrome extension: account memory clients list the saved memories (apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/accountMemoryClient.ts:1-40; apps/extension/src/background/memory-bridge.ts).
prerequisites: Signed in, Cloud mode (managed storage). A Local or BYOK turn is refused by the eligibility gate (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:654-662).
'Persistent memory' on. The server reads it as off unless the saved capability is exactly true (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:277-280).
'Save memories from chats' on (default on once memory is on) (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:278-279).
The workspace has not turned memory off (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:611-616).
screens_and_controls: Switch 'Persistent memory' (master).
Switch 'Save memories from chats' (disabled while master is off; hint 'Turn on persistent memory to change this.') (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:59,395-403).
Switch 'Include sensitive topics in memory' and 'Allow memory generation from tool-assisted chats'.
Per-chat memory override: the request field memory_enabled=false skips reading and learning for that chat (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:712).
Memory list with 'Learned from' origin line, pin and delete buttons (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MemoryEditor.tsx:346,375).
journey: Turn on 'Persistent memory' in Settings > Memory.
Chat normally and state a fact in a sentence that is not a question, for example 'I live in Lisbon.'
The assistant replies as usual.
After the turn completes, the server extracts up to 5 facts and writes them as source 'auto' memories linked to the chat and turn.
Open Settings > Memory to see the new entry labelled 'Learned from <chat title>'. Pin, edit or delete it there.
If a replaced fact was wrong, open the replaced-memories list and restore it (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/restore/route.ts:20).
feedback_and_outputs: No toast or banner appears for learning. The only visible result is the new row in Settings > Memory [inferred: no client code reads the learning result].
The row shows 'Learned from <chat>' with a link to the chat when the chat still exists (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MemoryEditor.tsx:574-588).
Server logs 'Managed auto-memory turn recorded' with extracted and inserted counts (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:128-137).
settings: capabilities.memory (master), capabilities.generateFromHistory, capabilities.allowToolAssistedGeneration, capabilities.includeSensitiveTopics stored in user_settings (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:258-282).
settings.memory.excludedTerms (never-remember list, max 50 terms, min 3 chars) and settings.memory.suppressedSources (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:283-300,1343-1367).
Workspace policy allowMemory (Workspace > Policy) (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:39).
Server env AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION: model-assisted extraction is on unless set to 0, false, off or no (apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:79-82).

working: Pattern extraction: 21 English phrase patterns ('my name is', 'I live in', 'I prefer', 'remember that', ...). A clause must be 2 to 120 characters; questions and task-only reminders about tab/window ids are skipped (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:19-45,69-87,89-120).

Model-assisted extraction, on by default, re-reads the turn after the response on a cheap utility route, keeps the pattern result as fallback, is capped at 5 facts, and is skipped for zero-data-retention turns (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:41-57,145-186; apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:48-82).

Learning gate: memory master on, generate-from-history on, not temporary, per-chat override not false, surface not 'api' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2392-2406). Personalization=false forces memory_enabled=false (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:3523).

A tool-assisted turn learns nothing unless 'Allow memory generation from tool-assisted chats' is on (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6451-6455; apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:148-153). A turn holding Google user data is skipped (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:97-109).
Never-remember terms and the 'auto' suppressed source stop a candidate (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1355-1377).

Write gate: prohibited content (credentials, payment cards, other prohibited categories) is always refused; temporary chat refused; sensitive topics refused unless the person asked or opted in; workspace memory off refused; non-managed trust refused (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:570-668).

Merge and supersede in one SQL statement: a normalised key (lower-case, punctuation stripped, 'user's X' read as 'my X', 'user is' as 'I am') finds a duplicate; the merge keeps pin and the longer-lived expiry (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:399-403,742-858).

Supersession applies to five single-valued topics only: name, residence, employer, role, origin (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:612-619). Rank is pinned 2, person-written 1, auto 0; a rival of higher rank makes the new fact land already superseded (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:405-407,805-814).

Provenance: source_conversation_id, source_turn_id and a provenance JSON (creator account, agent id, trust mode, conversation, turn) are written with the row (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:476-505,825-856).

Mobile Local mode learns on the device into SQLite with the same patterns, 5 per turn, dedupe and topic supersede (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/consolidation.ts:64,176-215; apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/localMemoryWriter.ts:25-75).
CLI: a session summary is extracted on session end and merged per trust boundary (Local, BYOK, Managed) into files under memories/ (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:1-30).
incomplete: Contradiction handling covers only five topics; any other changed fact (for example a changed favourite food) is stored beside the old one until the person deletes it (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:612-619).

Provenance JSON stores creator, conversation, turn, agent and trust mode only; the migration comment also lists model, provider route, prompt version and tool invocations, which this writer does not fill (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:494-505; apps/web/db/neon/0285_user_memories_provenance.sql:40).

Memory source labels 'chrome', 'vscode' and 'cli' can be written by commands but are not in MEMORY_SOURCES, so they cannot be hidden with the suppressed-sources setting (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:40-49; apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:317).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web, Desktop and Mobile Local or own-key turns never write to the account memory table: the eligibility gate refuses any non-managed trust mode (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:654-662).
The API surface never learns (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:2404).
not_available: Languages other than English for pattern extraction: patterns are English phrases (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:19-45). The model path may cover more; its language behaviour is unknown.
Agent-specific memory (S94.14) is missing in the brief and was not looked for here (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/094-memory-and-personalization-components.md S94.14).

established.statement: A component extracts candidate facts from ordinary turns for memory.
Each memory records where it came from (conversation, turn, writer).
Duplicate memories are merged instead of stored twice.
A newer contradicting fact supersedes the older memory.
Temporary chats neither read nor write memory.
Every memory entry exposes provenance, last update, edit, exclusion, export and deletion; sensitive categories require explicit controls.
Saved memory and referenced chat history are separate controls.

acceptance_criteria: With memory and 'Save memories from chats' on, a Cloud chat turn 'I live in Lisbon.' creates one memory 'User lives in Lisbon' with source auto and a source chat link.
The question 'Do I live in Lisbon?' creates no memory.
In a temporary chat, with 'Save memories from chats' off, with the per-chat memory override off, or on the API surface, no memory is created.
Saying 'my favorite color is teal' and later 'the user's favorite color is teal' leaves one memory.
Saying 'I live in Pune' then 'I live in Oslo' leaves Oslo active and Pune superseded and restorable; if Pune was pinned, Oslo lands already superseded.
A card number or password in the text is never stored, even when the person says 'remember'.
A failure in learning does not fail the chat turn.
inferred: Learning should not be visible to the person at the moment it happens; the list is the only place it shows [inferred from absence of any client feedback code].
Local and own-key turns on Web should have an on-device equivalent of learning, as Mobile Local has [inferred from the three-mode rule].
proposed: [proposed] Show a small non-blocking note under the reply when a new memory was saved, with an undo link, as the leading assistants do.
[proposed] Extend contradiction topics beyond five or let the model flag a conflict, with a test per topic.
[proposed] Fill model, provider route and prompt version into the provenance JSON the migration already allows.

steps.what_happens: The person sends a chat message from an app in Cloud mode; the request carries optional memory_enabled and personalization flags.
The server reads the workspace and user memory policy; a temporary chat gets a disabled policy; a read failure continues the turn without memory.
The server strips inlined files, code fences and explicit remember/forget commands from the user text, checks the learning gate, and extracts up to 5 pattern candidates.
The model replies. If the turn used tools and tool-assisted learning is off, candidates are dropped.

On a completed turn the recorder either persists pattern candidates, or (flag on and source text present) re-reads the turn with a utility model after the response and persists those, falling back to patterns on any failure.
The utility-model call is a provider call on a managed route, reserved as background usage under quota feature memory_extraction.
Each candidate is checked against never-remember terms, the project of the conversation is looked up, then written through writeConsolidatedMemory (eligibility gate, merge, supersede, provenance).
Mobile and other clients later pull the new row through /api/memory/sync.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Pattern extraction uses no model. Model-assisted extraction calls a cheap managed utility route chosen by the server, never the person's chosen model, so it works the same whichever chat model is selected; it needs a managed route and is skipped otherwise (apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:4-13,115-120). Own-key (BYOK) and Local turns are not written to Cloud memory. No model identifiers are written here.

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account; rows are keyed by user_id and read through a user-scoped database (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:50).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy allowMemory can switch memory off for all members (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:611-616). No role check for the person's own memories was found.
access_and_usage.subscription: No plan check found in the learning path. The model extraction call receives the plan tier and is metered as background usage under quota feature memory_extraction (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:176; apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:50). Exact limits per plan: unknown.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: At most 5 auto facts per turn (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:72). Clause 2-120 chars (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:11-12). Model extraction: 256 output tokens, 6 s timeout (apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:66,74). Create API content max 20,000 chars (packages/contracts/types/src/memory-wire.ts:1).
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_MODEL_MEMORY_EXTRACTION (server env, default on). User switches: memory, generateFromHistory, allowToolAssistedGeneration, includeSensitiveTopics.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Works with any chat model because learning runs on the user text and a separate utility model; no capability of the chat model is needed (apps/web/lib/services/model-memory-extraction.ts:12).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Zero-data-retention turns are not sent to the utility route (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:41-52). Turns with health-space projects or Google data force a no-training route (apps/web/lib/services/managed-auto-memory-service.ts:176-178).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Web: a local-model turn does not write to account memory [inferred from the managed-trust gate at apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:654-662]. Mobile Local learns into an on-device store, needs the memory switches on, and does not sync (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/consolidation.ts:66-78). CLI Local writes Local-boundary files on the device (apps/cli/src/memory_pipeline.rs:1-12). Whether sign-in is required for Mobile Local memory: unknown.

Model extraction runs after the response using the framework's after hook; outside a request scope it is left to settle. Pattern persistence is awaited inside the success hook.
Persistence failure is logged as a warning and the chat completion stays successful; an ineligible write is counted as excluded.
Idempotent id per user, scope and normalised fact so two concurrent turns insert one row; no retry loop for failed writes.
Only a 'completed' outcome learns.
Disabled policy; nothing learned.
Model extraction times out at 6 s and falls back to pattern facts. Offline client behaviour on Web: not handled in the code (not searched).
Switches carry aria-labels; the origin line is a text link. Mobile Local uses its own store and Alert dialogs.

features.summary: The person types 'remember that ...' or 'forget ...' in chat. The app sends the sentence to the memory command route, which saves or searches the memory, and the person sees a short receipt. A forget always shows what would be deleted and waits for a confirmation. The assistant is told the outcome so it does not claim more.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the person a direct, reliable way to add or remove a memory by talking, with an honest receipt, instead of hoping passive learning notices (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:122-131 comment).
purpose.why_it_exists: An explicit ask should get policy checks, a clear answer and a way to undo or confirm, which silent extraction does not give (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:122-131). Unrecoverable deletion must ask first (doc: AGENTS.md section 9).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person chatting in Cloud mode on Web (and Desktop, which shows the web app), Mobile (own flow), and the Chrome extension client.
problems_solved: Passive learning misses or refuses facts; a command is deterministic.
There was no chat path to delete a memory before this.
The assistant could claim 'I forgot that' when nothing was deleted; the outcome note prevents it.
use_cases: 'Remember that I use TypeScript.' The memory is saved and a toast says 'Saved to memory: ...'.
'Forget my old address.' A dialog lists the matching memories; the person confirms and they are deleted.
'Remember my card number is ...' is refused with the reason.

where_to_find_it: Web chat composer (WebChatPage) and the Desktop window showing the hosted web app (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2628-2640).
Mobile chat: runs as a status step on the assistant message, with its own Alert dialog (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/memoryCommands.ts:224-270).
Chrome extension: runAccountMemoryCommand client exists (apps/extension/src/features/cloud-bridge/memoryClient.ts:156). Where it is called: not read.
prerequisites: Cloud mode and a signed-in session with the cloud memory controller ready; otherwise the toast 'Cloud memory is unavailable until your account and workspace are ready. This command was not sent to memory.' appears (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-explicit-memory-commands.ts:121-128).
Not a temporary chat and not a local-model turn on Web (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2628-2630).
Memory on for a remember to be stored (refusal reason memory_disabled otherwise) (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:81-88).
screens_and_controls: The chat composer only. No special button.
Confirmation dialog titled 'Forget this memory?' or 'Forget N memories?' with button 'Forget' (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-explicit-memory-commands.ts:176-186).
Mobile Alert 'Forget this memory?' with 'Cancel' and 'Forget' (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/memoryCommands.ts:209-221).
journey: Type 'remember that I am vegetarian' or 'forget my old address' and send.
The hook tests the text for the words remember, forget or memory and posts it to /api/memory/commands.
For remember: a toast shows the server message, for example 'Saved to memory: ...'.
For forget: the server finds matches; the dialog lists them and says chats stop using them and it cannot be restored.
Choose 'Forget' to send the request again with confirmed=true; the toast confirms the deletion. Cancel keeps everything.
The chat message itself still goes to the model with a note of the outcome so the assistant answers in one sentence.
feedback_and_outputs: Toast text comes from the server message first, else from fixed receipts: 'Saved to memory.', 'Already in memory, so nothing changed.', 'Not saved: a pinned memory on the same topic takes priority.', 'Not saved: memory is off, or this is something memory does not keep.', 'Deleted the matching memories.', 'No saved memory matched, so nothing was deleted.', 'Waiting for your confirmation before anything is deleted.' (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-explicit-memory-commands.ts:25-33,105-113).
Success toasts for stored, already_known, forgotten; neutral toast for others (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-explicit-memory-commands.ts:34,105-113).
Failure toast 'Memory did not answer, so it is unknown whether anything was saved or deleted. Check Memory in Settings.' (apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-explicit-memory-commands.ts:23).
settings: Same switches as F094-01: Persistent memory, Include sensitive topics, never-remember list (Settings > Memory > 'Never remember').
Workspace memory policy.

working: Parsing: remember patterns ('remember that X', 'remember: X', 'remember this: X', 'remember X') and forget patterns ('forget about X', 'forget that X', 'stop remembering X', 'delete my memory about X', 'forget my X'); questions starting with do, does, did, can, what, why ... are not commands; subject 2-120 chars (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:132-212).
Server route: CSRF, rate limit 'chat-conversation', body validated, conversation temporary flag read from the database not from the caller (apps/web/app/api/memory/commands/route.ts:19-52).

Remember goes through the same eligibility gate plus the never-remember list; sensitive facts are allowed when the person asked (userRequested) but prohibited categories are not (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:95-120; apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:570-668).

Forget: ILIKE search of visible memories (min 3 chars, max 25 matches, scoped to the chat's project visibility), then every forget with at least one match returns confirmation_required until confirmed=true (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:60-64,157-176; packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:340-388).
Delete is a tombstone with blanked text; the route logs only memory ids (apps/web/app/api/memory/commands/route.ts:68-80; apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:391).

The chat request carries memory_command so the model gets a one-sentence outcome note on web, desktop and mobile surfaces (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:36,292-303; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:6239-6242).

Model-callable tools save_memory, search_memory, forget_memory are added when the user asks about memory, on streamed, tool-capable, non-temporary chats (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1116-1152; apps/web/lib/server/tools/memory-tools.ts:19-23).
Mobile Local mode runs the same handlers against the on-device store; Cloud mode posts to the server route (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/memoryCommands.ts:180-200).
incomplete: The forget search is a plain substring match on the subject (and extracted phrasing); it does not understand meaning, so 'forget my job' finds only text containing those words (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:66-68,157-176).
A remember command cannot carry an expiry; the store port passes no expiresAt (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:122-141).
disconnected_or_disabled: Web hook is skipped in temporary chats and for local-model turns, although the server allows a forget in a temporary chat (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:2628-2630; apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:73-74).
Mobile skips commands in temporary chats (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2961).
not_available: CLI and VS Code chat commands for remember/forget through this route: not found in files read; VS Code has a chat participant that reads memory but command handling was not located.
No undo for a deleted memory by design (confirmation text says it cannot be restored).

established.statement: A handler performs explicit remember/forget commands and reports the result.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence.
Add, edit, pin, exclude, pause, delete and import persist and affect the next applicable turn.
Temporary chats neither read nor write memory.

acceptance_criteria: 'Remember that I am vegetarian' on Web shows a success toast and a new memory appears in Settings > Memory.
'Do you remember my name?' is not treated as a command.
'Forget my address' with one match opens a dialog naming that memory; Cancel deletes nothing; Forget deletes it and a toast says 'Deleted the matching memories.' (or the server message).
A forget with no match says nothing was deleted.
If the memory route fails, the toast says it is unknown whether anything changed and nothing is shown as saved.
A remember that hits a pinned memory on the same topic says it was not saved.
inferred: A forget confirmation should also appear for a single match, because the handler asks whenever matches exist [inferred from packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:352-358]; the first draft said 'more than one'.
Commands should work in temporary chats for forget, as the server comment says [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Show forget in temporary chats on Web and Mobile, since the server allows it.
[proposed] Let a remember carry 'for 30 days' as an expiry using the existing expiresAt rules.
[proposed] Use meaning-based matching for forget with the confirmation list as the safety net.

steps.what_happens: The composer calls runExplicitMemoryCommand with the message and the current conversation and project ids. The hook returns early unless the text contains remember, forget or memory words.
POST /api/memory/commands with CSRF and rate limit; the server reads the conversation's temporary flag and health-space project from the database.
parseExplicitMemoryCommand finds the first command sentence; remember runs checkEligibility then store; forget runs find then (if confirmed) remove.
The response carries status, message, requiresConfirmation and matches; the hook shows a toast or the confirmation dialog, and a confirmed forget is posted again with confirmed=true.
The chat message is sent to the chat route with memory_command {kind,status}; the server adds a note so the model reports the real outcome in one sentence.
Mobile Local mode: the same handlers run against SQLite on the phone, with no server call.

features.summary: The person sees every saved memory with its topic, source and update date, can add, edit, pin and delete memories, and can delete all of them. Pinned memories come first and win conflicts. A deleted memory leaves only an empty marker so other devices drop it, and it disappears from replies at once.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the person inspect and control account memory: list, add, edit, pin or unpin, delete one or all, restore a replaced memory (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:41,107,192; apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts:76,152; apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/restore/route.ts:20).

steps.what_happens: The Settings screen asks the cloud memory controller for the list; it calls GET /api/memory.
Pin sends PUT /api/memory/{id} with {pinned}; the server updates the row and returns it; the controller swaps it into the list.
Delete sends DELETE /api/memory/{id}; the server sets is_deleted, blanks content, category and import key.
Other devices pull deltas where deleted or expired rows come back as is_deleted true and drop the entry.
The next chat turn reads only active rows, so a deleted memory cannot be injected.

features.summary: A memory can have an end date. Expired memories stop appearing in replies at once. A daily job at 03:05 UTC marks expired memories deleted, then merges duplicates and replaces stale conflicting ones, in bounded batches. It needs no person to run it, and a run that cannot finish continues the next day.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps account memory tidy: hides then removes expired memories, merges leftover duplicates and resolves leftover conflicts on a schedule (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-memories/route.ts:15-41).
purpose.why_it_exists: Memories with an expiry must stop being used and be removed on schedule; maintenance must run without user action (S94.10, S94.15). Workspace retention can force an end date (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:674-684).
purpose.who_uses_it: The system; people see the effect (shorter, cleaner memory).
problems_solved: Temporary facts (a trip, a project) do not stay forever.
Concurrent writes that left duplicates are cleaned up.
Old stale facts about name, residence, employer, role and origin stop competing.
use_cases: A memory created through the API with expiresAt 30 days ahead disappears from replies after that date and is blanked at the next daily run.
A workspace with enforced retention caps new memory lifetimes.
Two copies of 'I live in Rome' written at the same time are merged overnight.

where_to_find_it: No screen. It is a server job configured in vercel.json (vercel.json:106-107).
The effect shows in Settings > Memory on every app (entries vanish; replaced entries appear under 'Replaced memories').
prerequisites: A memory with expires_at set, or duplicate or conflicting rows. Expiry can be set by POST or PUT /api/memory with expiresAt (future, within 3,650 days) or imposed by workspace retention (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:416-430,674-684).
screens_and_controls: None in the UI read. Expiry has no control in the shared editor (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/MemoryEditor.tsx).
journey: A memory is saved with an expiry (API) or retention is enforced.
At the expiry time every read path stops returning it.
At 03:05 UTC the job blanks it (soft delete) in batches.
Then it merges duplicates and supersedes stale same-topic rows.
Other devices see the deletion at next sync.
feedback_and_outputs: No user-facing message. The route returns JSON {expired, remaining, consolidation:{merged, superseded, remaining}} and logs 'Memory expiry sweep completed' and 'Memory consolidation completed' (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-memories/route.ts:22-35).
settings: Workspace memory retention (retentionDays, retentionEnforced) in the workspace policy; enforcement flag recorded since migration 0138 (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:668-673).
Cron schedule in vercel.json.

working: Cron GET /api/cron/expire-memories at '5 3 * * *' (vercel.json:106-107), maxDuration 300 s, protected by verifyCronRequest (401 otherwise) (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-memories/route.ts:11-21).
Sweep: batches of 500, up to 200 batches, 240 s budget; sets the tombstone assignments on rows with expires_at <= now (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:884-917).
If the sweep ends with rows remaining, it logs a warning, skips consolidation and returns consolidation null (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-memories/route.ts:28-31).

Consolidation: duplicates first (batch 500, up to 50 batches, 40 s) then stale conflicts; a duplicate keeper takes the stronger rank and the longer expiry (or none) (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:931-1082).
Errors return HTTP 500 'Internal server error' and log 'Memory expiry cron failed' (apps/web/app/api/cron/expire-memories/route.ts:36-41).
Reads check expires_at at query time, so expiry is immediate even before the job runs (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:375-381).
incomplete: Consolidation topics are the five in MEMORY_CONFLICT_TOPICS only (packages/ai/agent-core/src/memory.ts:612-619).
Imported memories are deduped by import key only at write time; the job later merges near duplicates (apps/web/lib/memory/import-store.ts:33-75).
disconnected_or_disabled: Nothing is switched off. Whether the cron is enabled in the production Vercel project is not recorded in files read.
not_available: No user control to set an expiry in the UI, and a remember command cannot set one (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:122-141).
No hard removal of expired rows; they remain as blank tombstones.

established.statement: Memories with an expiry date stop being used and are removed on schedule.
Background jobs maintain memory (expiry, consolidation) without user action.

acceptance_criteria: A memory whose expires_at has passed is not returned by chat, list, export, import preview or sync as active, even before the cron runs.
After the 03:05 UTC run, expired rows have empty text and is_deleted true.
With more than 500 expired rows the sweep continues in batches until a short batch or its ceiling.
If the sweep hits its ceiling, consolidation is skipped for that run.
A request without the cron secret gets 401 and nothing changes.
A database failure returns 500 and is logged.
inferred: A person-set expiry in the past is refused by the API ('expiresAt must be in the future') [inferred from apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:416-430].
proposed: [proposed] Alert when 'remaining' is true on consecutive days.
[proposed] Add a metric for rows swept and merged per run.
[proposed] Add an expiry choice to Settings > Memory.

steps.what_happens: Vercel calls GET /api/cron/expire-memories on the schedule with the cron credential.
The sweep updates up to 500 due rows per statement to is_deleted true with text, category and import key cleared, repeating up to 200 times or 240 s.
If rows remain, return with consolidation null; otherwise run consolidation.
Duplicate merge: group active rows by user, project, workspace and normalised key; keep the highest rank then newest; extend the keeper's expiry to the longest; tombstone the rest.
Stale supersede: among active rows matching a conflict-topic prefix, keep one per topic and mark the others superseded_by it.
Clients learn of the changes at the next /api/memory/sync pull.

features.summary: For each Cloud chat turn the server loads the account's saved memories, keeps those that fit the chat (not deleted, expired, superseded, hidden by source, or from another workspace or project), ranks them by word overlap with the request with pinned ones first, and adds up to 30 to the model's system context.

purpose.what_it_does: Makes replies use what the person saved. It selects, ranks, trims and fences memory text and adds it as a system message, and returns citations so apps can show which memories were used (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1128-1213,1281-1302,1315-1317; apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:216-239).
purpose.why_it_exists: Saved memory is only useful if the right facts reach the model, within a size budget, without leaking across projects or workspaces (doc: docs/product/definition.md:200-203; doc: docs/product/experience-contract.md:547-558).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every Cloud chat user with memory on; also local-model turns on Web through the local-context route.
problems_solved: Replies stay personal without the person repeating facts.
Project-only facts do not appear in unrelated chats.
Memory off at account or workspace level really stops reading, not only writing.
use_cases: Ask 'plan my week' and the assistant already knows the person works night shifts.
Inside a project set to its own memory only, account facts are not used.
A local-model chat on Web gets the person's memory text through /api/memory/local-context.

where_to_find_it: Automatic in every Cloud chat on Web, Desktop (hosted web app), Mobile Cloud, CLI Managed, VS Code and Chrome extension when they use Managed Cloud.
Project setting on Web: a switch in the project settings dialog for using account memory (apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx:78,387; label text not read).
Mobile chat shows a 'memory used' chip (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MemoryUsedChip.tsx).
Settings > Memory scope table: 'Account', 'Workspace', 'Project' with meanings (apps/web/features/settings/sections/MemorySection.tsx:43-55).

journey: The person sends a message in a Cloud chat.
The server reads the policy and the active memories for the account, workspace and project.
It ranks them against the message, trims to limits and adds one fenced system message.
The model answers using them.
The response header and message metadata list memory citations so the app can show which were used (packages/contracts/types/src/memory-wire.ts:9-10).
feedback_and_outputs: Citations: id and an excerpt of up to 240 chars per memory (packages/contracts/types/src/memory-wire.ts:10,160-175).

settings: capabilities.memory, per-chat memory_enabled, personalization, project uses_global_memory, workspace allowMemory, memory.suppressedSources, memory.excludedTerms (those apply to writes).

working: Policy gate: if the policy is not enabled, nothing is read ('memory_disabled') (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1143-1146).

Query: user's rows that are active (not deleted, not superseded, not expired), source not in the suppressed list, project scope predicate, workspace predicate, and free of Google user data; ordered pinned then updated; limit 500 candidates (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1148-1186).

Scope: loose chat reads global rows only; project reads its own plus global unless the project opted out (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1085-1089,1264-1279). An unreadable project falls back to global only.

Ranking: words of 3+ chars, weight log((N+1)/(df+0.5)); sort pinned first, then score, then original order; without query words the query order stays (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1091-1126). Top 30 are kept (line 67).

Formatting: each memory cut to 1,000 chars, total 8,000 chars, category kept, output JSON inside a fenced untrusted-content block (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1281-1302). The block is added as the first system message (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1315-1317; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4343-4346).
Memory is one source of the context resolution engine with a budget of 8,000 chars (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:1228-1262).

Failures: a policy read failure logs 'Managed memory load failed; continuing without account memory'; a context failure continues without memory, unless a project context was required, in which case the turn is not sent (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4152-4160,4254-4268).

Web local-model turns fetch /api/memory/local-context (instructions, memory text, citations) and add it to the local prompt when personalization is on and the chat is not temporary (apps/web/app/api/memory/local-context/route.ts:12-28; packages/contracts/types/src/memory-wire.ts:182-205).

Mobile Cloud: the server assembles context (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2800-2803). Mobile Local: top 5 on-device facts, up to 50 facts, 1,000 chars each, 8,000 total, fenced (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:2805; apps/mobile/src/features/memory/services/personalContext.ts:16-33).
CLI: a Managed session's prompt carries the cached account memory for the linked project; Local and BYOK sessions do not (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:908-925).
VS Code adds up to 50 account facts per turn to the chat input (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/chat-participant/chatParticipant.ts:367-370; apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/memoryStore.ts:30).
incomplete: Ranking is word overlap only; a shadow relevance experiment runs but changes nothing (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4907-4912).
Memory sources from 'cli', 'vscode', 'chrome' cannot be suppressed by source (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:317).
Mobile Cloud's own relevance function in the persisted store is used for the offline path (apps/mobile/src/features/memory/store.ts:589-619).
disconnected_or_disabled: Own-key (BYOK) turns: whether the server injects account memory for own-key provider routes was not established; the CLI explicitly gives none to BYOK sessions (apps/cli/src/cloud/mod.rs:913-915).
The brief's code line numbers for request-processor (1278, 2904) no longer match the file; current lines are cited here.

established.statement: Saved memories are retrieved into the model context for a turn, scoped and filtered.
Retrieved memories are ranked by relevance to the current request.
A resolver decides whether personal, workspace or project memory applies to a turn.
Project-only facts stay in their project; temporary chats neither read nor write memory.
Memory scopes: Cloud global, Cloud project, Work-project, Mobile local, developer workspace; each entry needs scope and provenance.
Nothing may silently route a Local chat to BYOK or managed cloud; a Local-to-BYOK move is an explicit fork with consent.

acceptance_criteria: With memory on, a Cloud reply uses a saved fact relevant to the question.
With memory off (account, workspace, or per-chat), the request contains no memory block.
A project-only memory never appears in a loose chat; with the project set to its own memory, global memories do not appear in that project.
A pinned memory outranks an unpinned one with higher word overlap.
A deleted, expired or superseded memory is never injected.
No more than 30 memories and 8,000 characters are added, each at most 1,000 characters.
If the memory read fails, the chat still answers.
inferred: On Web, sending account memory to a local model happens only on the person's own device after sign-in; this should be disclosed as the account memory leaving the Cloud for the device [inferred from apps/web/app/api/memory/local-context/route.ts].
Own-key turns should follow an explicit rule for account memory; not established.
proposed: [proposed] Add embedding-assisted ranking behind the existing shadow experiment once it shows gain.
[proposed] Show memory citations on Web replies as Mobile does.
[proposed] Add the CLI, VS Code and Chrome sources to the suppressible sources.

steps.what_happens: The chat request arrives; personalization=false forces memory_enabled=false.
The memory policy (workspace and user) is read in parallel with attachments; a temporary chat gets a disabled policy; a failure becomes 'unreadable' and the turn continues without memory.
resolveInteractiveTurnContext loads memory with the last user message as the query, the project scope, suppressed sources and workspace.
Rows are read (500 candidates), ranked, cut to 30, formatted to at most 8,000 chars, fenced as untrusted data.
The block is inserted as a system message and citations are attached to the response.
The provider model receives the request and answers.
Local-model turn on Web: the browser or desktop app fetches /api/memory/local-context and builds the local prompt on the device.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Memory is added as plain system text, so any chat model that accepts a system message can use it. Memory tools (search_memory) need a tool-capable model (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:1123-1130). No model identifiers are written here.

features.summary: The person can download all saved memories as a JSON file, and can bring in memories from another assistant by pasting or uploading text, previewing the items, choosing which to import and committing. Duplicates are skipped and blocked items are reported. A full account data export also lists memories.

purpose.what_it_does: Exports active memories of the current workspace as memories-<date>.json and imports a list of memories from text in bulk (apps/web/app/api/memory/export/route.ts:52-107; apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:55-176).

purpose.who_uses_it: People switching from another assistant, or taking a copy of their data.
problems_solved: No need to retype what another assistant knows.
The person owns a portable copy of their memories.
Imports cannot sneak in blocked content.
use_cases: Copy the provided prompt, run it in another assistant, paste the answer into the dialog and import selected items.
Export before deleting all memories.

working: Import dry-run (default mode): needs non-empty text, parses it, rejects text over 200,000 chars, marks items already present in the same workspace, returns up to 500 items with a truncation flag (apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:55-85; packages/contracts/types/src/memory-import.ts:3-4,82-106).

Import commit: 1 to 500 non-empty strings; each is checked against the never-remember list, then the write policies (eligibility gate with userRequested true), then inserted with an import key; duplicate keys per user, source and workspace are skipped (apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:90-150; apps/web/lib/memory/import-store.ts:33-75).

features.summary: Account memory has three guards. A person can switch off whole sources of memory (auto-captured, web, desktop, mobile). They can list words memory must never keep. A temporary chat is kept out of memory, past-chat recall, search and history. The server enforces all three. Web and mobile show the controls.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person decide what the account memory may contain and what it may use in replies. (1) Source choices: a suppressed source stays saved but is left out of answers (apps/web/features/settings/components/MemoryExclusions.tsx:295). (2) A never-remember list: a new memory containing a listed term is refused on write (apps/web/lib/services/memory-write-service.ts:44).
