purpose.why_it_exists: Memory is only trustworthy if people can bound it. Competing assistants offer memory controls and incognito chats; this feature gives AGI Workforce the same, with the rule kept on the server so every app obeys it. [inferred] (the project's AGENTS.md section 10 says the leaders are the reference, doc: AGENTS.md)
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who uses memory on the web, mobile (Cloud mode), VS Code or CLI, and anyone who starts a temporary chat. Workspace admins also gate memory as a whole (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:640).
problems_solved: A person does not want a client name, address or health detail remembered.
A person wants memories from one device or from automatic capture ignored without deleting them.
A person wants a throwaway chat that leaves no trace in memory, search or history.
Secrets and card numbers must never end up in stored memory.
use_cases: Add 'my home address' to Never remember so that no later chat can save it.
Tick 'Suppress: Automatically captured from chats' to answer only from memories the person saved by hand.
Start a temporary chat to ask a private question; it is not saved to history and is skipped by memory and search.
Run `memory never --add salary` in the CLI so the web and mobile apps also refuse memories that mention it.

working: Terms list: normalised on read (trim, lower-case, minimum 3 characters, maximum 50, duplicates dropped) (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:283-297).

Suppressed sources are normalised to the known set mobile, desktop, web, auto (managed-memory-context-service.ts:317-333) and applied in the SQL read of memories as `coalesce(source,'web') <> all(...)` on every load (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1152-1177).

The chat turn loads suppressed sources before building memory context, for any turn that includes memory (apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:145-157). If memory context cannot be assembled the turn continues without memory (turn-context-service.ts:322-327; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/request-processor.ts:4253-4262).

Suppressed sources are also honoured by the model memory tools (apps/web/lib/server/tools/memory-tools.ts:203-220) and by live voice (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/lib/live-voice-context.ts:275-283) and by the browser-local turn context endpoint (apps/web/app/api/memory/local-context/route.ts:25; turn-context-service.ts:419).
Suppressing 'auto' also stops automatic capture: persistManagedAutoMemoryFacts returns zero inserts (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1372-1379).

Never-remember list applied on every write path: manual create (apps/web/app/api/memory/route.ts:148), edit (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/route.ts:110), restore (apps/web/app/api/memory/[id]/restore/route.ts:40), bulk import (apps/web/app/api/memory/import/route.ts:116), device sync push (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:170), explicit remember commands and model tool saves (apps/web/lib/services/memory-commands.ts:112-123; memory-tools.ts:296-298), and automatic capture (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1371-1396).

If the list cannot be read, single writes and batch writes are refused with an internal error and an error log (memory-write-service.ts:35-42). A sync push that only deletes is never blocked (memory/sync/route.ts:180-182).

Credential, payment card, government identifier, biometric, precise location, criminal history and immigration status content is refused for every write through writeConsolidatedMemory, regardless of the list or of an explicit ask (managed-memory-context-service.ts:570-584,721-742; packages/contracts/context/src/memory-content-policy.ts:1-9). Sensitive topics (health, ethnicity, religion, politics, orientation, gender identity, union membership) are refused unless the person asks explicitly or turns on 'Include sensitive topics in memory' (managed-memory-context-service.ts:613-622).

Temporary chat, server side: memory context is not loaded (turn-context-service.ts:121-124); automatic learning is off (request-processor.ts:2392-2404); the memory tool is not offered (request-processor.ts:1123-1146); past-chat recall is off (turn-context-service.ts:127-128); a temporary conversation is excluded from past-chat queries (apps/web/lib/services/past-chat-context-service.ts:256,345,523), from the search route (apps/web/app/api/search/route.ts:324,359,375), from the retrieval index (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-search-service.ts:270,363), from memory sync origin links (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:72) and from the recap (apps/web/lib/services/reflect-service.ts:327).

History: persisting a message into a temporary conversation is refused with 'Messages in a temporary chat are not saved.' (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/persist-message.ts:80; apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:9); the assistant turn is not persisted server side (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/assistant-turn-persistence.ts:253-257); the conversation list hides temporary conversations (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:81).
A purge job deletes temporary conversations older than 30 days unless a legal hold applies (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-temporary-chats/route.ts:23,45; vercel.json:26).

Mobile screen with load retry, save error and cloud-only visibility (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/memory-exclusions.tsx:75-110,237-249). VS Code and CLI edit the term list through the same preferences endpoint (apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/memoryExclusions.ts:77; apps/cli/src/cloud/personalization.rs:330-362).

Desktop Local-mode temporary chat: never written to SQLite, and the native runtime skips memory for it (apps/desktop/src/features/chat/useTemporaryChat.ts:11-16; apps/desktop/src/runtime/TauriRuntime.ts:775-778).
incomplete: Scheduled runs and the Slack assistant build their memory loader without suppressed sources, so a suppressed source is still read there (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:431-436; apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:189-194). The default passed is an empty list (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1152).

The memory namespace is saved as free-form data; the server does not validate terms on save, only on read. A term shorter than 3 characters sent from VS Code is saved but silently dropped on read; VS Code does not check the length (apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/memoryExclusions.ts:62-66; managed-memory-context-service.ts:286-297). The 100-character term limit exists only in the web and mobile inputs (MemoryExclusions.tsx:197; memory-exclusions.tsx:23).
The term match is a plain case-insensitive substring match, with no word boundary (managed-memory-context-service.ts:353-359).

established.statement: Suppressed sources are read on every memory load, so a suppressed source is not used in replies; enforcement is in the read path.
A memory whose text contains a never-remember term is refused on write with a message naming the term; an unreadable list refuses the write.
Credential and payment-instrument patterns are refused on write regardless of the list.
Temporary chats are excluded from past-chat queries, search, retrieval search, memory sync and the history save; the recap also excludes them.
established.source: S94.20 (brief); apps/web/lib/temporary-chat-policy.ts:13-21 (the policy comment lists which code keeps each clause)

established.statement: The project says its web apps follow the leaders' memory and incognito behaviour and that stricter rules win when sources disagree.

acceptance_criteria: With 'auto' suppressed, a memory saved by automatic capture is not in the model context of the next web chat turn, and no new automatic memory is stored.
With a term 'salary' listed, 'Remember that my salary is high' is refused and the reply names 'salary'; the same text through import and sync push is also rejected.
With the list unreadable (simulated read failure), a manual memory save fails with the 'nothing was saved' message and no row is created.
A memory text containing a card number or 'password is ...' is refused even when the never-remember list is empty.
In a temporary chat, nothing is added to memory, the conversation does not appear in the conversation list or in /api/search, and sending a message save to history returns the 'not saved' conflict.
Removing a term or un-suppressing a source takes effect on the next turn without restart.
Terms under 3 characters are rejected in the web and mobile UI with the 'Enter at least 3 characters' message; the 51st term is refused.
inferred: The same account lists should apply to every client that talks to account memory, because the list lives in account settings and the VS Code placeholder says 'on every client' (apps/extension-vscode/src/memory/memoryExclusions.ts:51). [inferred]
Suppression should also apply to unattended runs, because the brief says the choice 'is enforced'. [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Pass loadSuppressedMemorySources into scheduled runs and the Slack assistant loaders.
[proposed] Validate the memory preference namespace on save (min and max length, count) so all clients get the same answer.
[proposed] Add never-remember and source controls to the desktop Cloud-mode Memory tab and to the Chrome extension, or state why not.

steps.what_happens: The person edits the list or a source box in Settings; the app saves it as the 'memory' preference namespace.
On a chat turn the server reads the memory switches, then (if memory is included) the suppressed sources and project scope, and builds memory context from user_memories excluding suppressed sources.
A temporary conversation skips memory and past-chat loading and writes no context manifest.
After the turn, automatic capture extracts at most 5 candidate facts, drops those matching a listed term, applies content and policy checks and writes survivors with source 'auto'.
A manual, imported, synced or tool-saved memory passes the never-remember check, then writeConsolidatedMemory applies the content and policy gate before the row is stored.
Search, past-chat recall, retrieval and the conversation list add is_temporary = false filters; saving a message to a temporary conversation is refused.
A nightly job deletes temporary conversations older than 30 days unless held.
Desktop Local mode: a temporary chat is answered by the native runtime with a temporary history and never written to the local database.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider takes part in enforcing these rules; they run in plain database queries and pattern checks on our servers. The chosen model only sees the memories that passed them. Memory facts for automatic capture are extracted by pattern code (request-processor.ts:2415); whether a second, model-based extractor also runs is covered by a separate feature and is unknown here.

features.summary: After a chat turn the server tells the app which saved memories it put in front of the model, and the app shows them: a 'Show sources' panel with 'Memory · N' on the web, a 'Memory · N' chip on mobile. Past chats used are listed too. The server sends the list in a response header, and the app saves it with the message.

purpose.what_it_does: Records which memories (and past chats) were placed in the model's context for a reply, so the person can see where an answer may have come from. The list is built from the memories actually loaded for the turn, then trimmed to what survived the final prompt fit (apps/web/lib/services/turn-context-service.ts:216-218; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/reference-citations.ts:68-77).
purpose.why_it_exists: Recall is otherwise invisible. The past-chat component says so in its own comment: without it the reader cannot tell a remembered fact from an invented one (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/CitationPastChats.tsx:15-19).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who use memory and want to check or manage what shaped an answer; testers checking that memory is used only when allowed.
problems_solved: Trust: the person can see which memories were in play.

Correctness: no memory is cited when memory was off, the chat was temporary, or the text was cut by the prompt fit.

features.summary: Reflect is a recap of a person's chat activity over 30 days, 3 months, 6 months or a year: totals, active days, topics, four pattern notes and ongoing work, built without a model. Separately, a schedule lets a person choose which sources each run may read: project, saved memories, the web, and chats from the last 24 hours.

purpose.what_it_does: Reflect: builds counts, topics and plain observations from the person's saved chats and describes patterns without scoring (apps/web/lib/services/reflect-service.ts:127-275). Scheduled-run context: before an unattended run, the server builds only the context the schedule allows (project, memory, recent chats) (apps/web/lib/services/scheduled-agent-executor.ts:409-520).
purpose.why_it_exists: To give people a look back at how they use the product, and to let routines such as a morning brief draw on what they worked on, with the person in control of the sources.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with memory on (Reflect) and people with a paid schedule allowance (scheduled runs).
problems_solved: People forget what they worked on across many chats.
A morning brief needs recent work and memory but must not read what the person did not allow.
An unattended run must not use sources the person left unticked.
use_cases: Open Reflect and pick 'Past 3 months' to see topics and ongoing work.
Create the 'Daily briefing' schedule that reads recent chats, memories and the web.
Untick 'The web' on a schedule so it cannot search.
Turn off 'Search past chats' so the recent-chats source gives a notice instead of text.

Schedules (desktop): a similar block with project, saved memories and the web only (apps/desktop/src/features/schedules/DesktopScheduleAccessFields.tsx:29-38).

Reflect shows a headline, stats (total chats, active days, most active day, peak hour), a daily activity chart, topics with percentages, four notes and 'ongoing work' (reflect-service.ts:127-275).

Schedule sources checkboxes: 'Project instructions and files' (only when the schedule has a project), 'Saved memories' (helper 'Read only while memory is on in Settings.'), 'The web', 'Recent chats' (helper 'Your chats from the last 24 hours. Read only while Search past chats is on in Settings.') (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:30-60).
journey: Reflect: open Settings > Reflect; the page builds the recap when opened (copy: 'Built only when you open this page.') (ReflectSection.tsx:88-90).
Choose a range or press 'Refresh'.
Read the summary, stats, topics and notes; open an ongoing chat from the list.
Schedules: open the schedule form, tick sources, save.
At run time the server loads only the ticked sources and runs the task; the result is shown in the schedule's run history.
feedback_and_outputs: Loading: 'Building your recap...' (ReflectSection.tsx:127-130).
Memory off: 'Memory is off. Turn on Memory and Save memories from chats to create a recap.' (ReflectSection.tsx:138-142).
Empty: 'No conversation activity yet' / 'There are no eligible conversations in your <range>.' (reflect-service.ts:196-205).
Summary body ends 'This recap describes patterns without scoring them.' (reflect-service.ts:250).
Mobile error: 'Reflect could not load. Check your connection and try again.' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/reflect.tsx:104).

Scheduled run notices given to the model: 'The user had no chats in the last 24 hours...' or 'The user’s recent chats were not available to this run...' (apps/web/lib/services/past-chat-context-service.ts:51-55).
settings: capabilities.memory and capabilities.generateFromHistory (Reflect gate).
capabilities.searchPastChats (recent-chats gate) and capabilities.memory (memory source gate) (managed-memory-context-service.ts:255-281).
Schedule sources {project, memory, web, recentChats} with defaults project, memory, web true and recentChats false (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/schedules.ts:96-101).

working: GET /api/reflect validates range (default 30d) and timezone, is rate limited under 'settings-activity', and returns 409 'memory_required' when memory is off (apps/web/app/api/reflect/route.ts:15-41).

The recap reads up to 1,000 of the person's non-deleted, non-temporary conversations created in the range, in the person's workspace, skipping chats that carry a cloud agent run (reflect-service.ts:296-345). It uses the first five user messages per chat as a sample, classifies a topic, and builds four notes named delegation, description, discernment and diligence (reflect-service.ts:144-180,215-247). No model is called.
'sampled' is true and the count is given when there are more chats than the sample (reflect-service.ts:273-274).
Ongoing work lists chats that span more than one day or have at least 3 user messages (reflect-service.ts:102-120).

The Reflect screen exists on web, desktop and mobile with loading, memory-off and error states (apps/web/features/settings/sections/ReflectSection.tsx; apps/desktop/src/features/settings/cloud/CloudReflectSection.tsx:114-119; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/reflect.tsx:40-45).
Schedule creation takes sources and stores them; missing sources fall back to defaults (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:632-670,766; scheduled-agent-executor.ts:926).

A scheduled run builds context only from ticked sources: project (needs the project), memory (policy-checked, project-scoped), recent chats (24 hours, up to 6 chats, 2 messages each, 3,000 characters, excluding temporary and deleted chats) (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:409-520, 1003-1004; past-chat-context-service.ts:38-43,523-527).
Recent chats are read only when 'Search past chats' is on; otherwise the run gets the 'not available' notice (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:438-440,492-495).
An empty result gives the fixed empty notice; an unreadable result gives the fixed unavailable notice (past-chat-context-service.ts:51-55; scheduled-agent-executor.ts:486-495).
Memory in a scheduled run is skipped entirely when memory is off, because the memory policy is handed to the loader (managed-memory-context-service.ts:1138-1146).
incomplete: Scheduled runs do not apply suppressed memory sources and do not rank memories by relevance (no query is passed) (scheduled-agent-executor.ts:431-436). See F094-07.
The Slack assistant uses the same memory loader without suppression (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:189).
Reflect topics come from a fixed classifier; observations are templates, not model text (reflect-service.ts:215-247).
Desktop schedule form lacks the 'Recent chats' source (DesktopScheduleAccessFields.tsx:30-38); mobile has no source picker (only the daily brief template sets sources).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile daily brief is available only when the schedules flag is on and the plan allows scheduled tasks (dailyBrief.ts:56-58).
Connectors in schedules show 'coming soon' when connectors are not released (ScheduleAccessFields.tsx:106-120).
not_available: Reflect: no CLI, VS Code or Chrome screen found.
Recap by day or week: not offered; only 30d, 90d, 180d, 365d (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/conversations.ts:104).

established.statement: A recap is produced only when the memory-enabled setting is on; otherwise 'memory-disabled'. Temporary chats are excluded. Insights describe patterns without scoring; long lists are sampled and the recap says so.
A scheduled run's context is built only from the sources the schedule selected; 'Recent chats' is read only while Search past chats is on.
Empty recent chats gives a fixed notice saying there were no chats in the last 24 hours; an unavailable read gives a fixed unavailable notice.

acceptance_criteria: With memory off, GET /api/reflect returns 409 memory_required and the screen shows 'Memory is off'.
With memory on and 3 chats in range, the recap totals match and a temporary chat is not counted.
With more than 1,000 chats the recap says it is sampled.
A schedule with only 'The web' ticked gets no memory, project or recent-chats text in its system prompt.
A schedule with 'Recent chats' ticked and 'Search past chats' off gets the unavailable notice, not chat text.
A schedule with 'Recent chats' ticked and no chats in 24 hours gets the empty notice.
A deleted or temporary chat never appears in the recent-chats text.
Changing the range reloads the recap.
inferred: Reflect should honour suppressed sources only if it used memories; it uses chats, so the question does not arise. [inferred]

The recap should drop messages the person deleted; the query filters deleted messages (reflect-service.ts:307-313) and a test covers withdrawn turns (apps/web/lib/services/__tests__/reflect-withdrawal.test.ts). [inferred from test titles]
proposed: [proposed] Offer day and week ranges, as the brief's wording suggests.
[proposed] Pass suppressed sources and the run's goal as a query to the scheduled-run memory loader.
[proposed] Add 'Recent chats' to the desktop form and a source picker on mobile.
[proposed] Make Reflect available on CLI or state why not.

steps.what_happens: Reflect: the app calls GET /api/reflect with range and the device time zone.
Server reads user settings to check memory and generateFromHistory; if off returns 409.
Server queries chats and user message samples, builds the recap with plain code and returns it with Cache-Control private, no-store.

features.summary: Sends a file to private storage on our servers and creates its record only after the server has re-read and checked the bytes. A file over 4 MiB goes up in parts that resume after a dropped connection. A chat file over 25 MiB goes through a separate checked intake. Web, desktop, mobile, CLI and Chrome call the same routes.

purpose.what_it_does: Moves a chosen file from the device into private object storage, then registers it as a chat attachment (a media_assets row) or a project source (a project_knowledge_files row). No row exists until the server has read the stored bytes back and finished its checks (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:302; apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-files.ts:299).
purpose.why_it_exists: A client cannot be trusted to say what a file is or how big it is. Splitting the upload from the registration lets the server verify size, type, checksum, plan limits and safety before the file can be listed, searched or sent to a model [inferred from the route flow]. Part uploads exist so large files survive weak networks (test: apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/__tests__/resumable-upload-interruption.test.ts).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in person who attaches a file to chat, adds a source to a project, or uploads from the Library. The CLI also uses the same routes (apps/cli/src/cloud/attachments.rs:11-12).
problems_solved: A mislabelled or oversized file never becomes a record, because the row is written last (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:461).
A dropped connection does not lose a big upload: the client asks which parts are stored and sends only the rest (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:121-129).
Plan size, daily-count and storage limits are enforced on the server before any byte is accepted (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:132; apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts:169).
use_cases: Attach a PDF to a chat message.
Add a spreadsheet as a project source (the checksum is required).
Upload a 300 MiB document to chat on a phone over a weak network and resume after a drop.
Drop a file into the Library on the web app.

where_to_find_it: Web: chat composer attachments (the control label was not read) and the Library page, New menu labelled 'Add to the library' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:2010; apps/web/app/chat/library/page.tsx:17). Library uploads call uploadChatAttachments with declineLargeFiles (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:180).

Desktop: chat attachments use the shared client (apps/desktop/src/services/desktopCloudAttachments.ts:30). The desktop Library passes no uploadFiles, so no upload entry there (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx:157-210).
Mobile: chat attachments via its own client (apps/mobile/services/api.ts:695-702, 822) and parted upload (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/upload/partedChatUpload.ts:153).
CLI: chat attachments and project sources (apps/cli/src/cloud/attachments.rs:11-12; apps/cli/src/cloud/knowledge.rs:12).
Chrome extension: side panel and computer-use file upload use the shared client (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10283; apps/extension/src/features/computer-use/userFileUpload.ts:217).
VS Code extension: no call to these upload routes found.
prerequisites: A signed-in Cloud account. The Chrome side panel shows a sign-in message when there is no managed-cloud owner (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:10270-10278).
Object storage configured on the server, or the route fails (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:87).
A supported file type: images, PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, text or code (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:95-99).
screens_and_controls: Composer attachment picker (web, desktop, mobile, Chrome): labels not read.
Library 'New' button opening the 'Add to the library' menu (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:2010).
Upload error text under the Library toolbar, default 'That upload did not finish.' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:839).
CLI: attach by path in a chat; labels not read.
journey: 1. The person picks or drops a file.
2. The client computes a SHA-256 checksum (apps/web/features/chat/services/chat-attachment-upload.ts:509; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-chat-attachments-client.ts:193).
3. Up to 4 MiB: the client asks POST /api/uploads/presign for a place to put the bytes, PUTs the bytes, then calls POST /api/uploads/chat-attachment/complete (or the project register route).

4. Over 4 MiB: the client opens a part session with POST /api/files/uploads, sends 5 MiB parts, and calls complete on the session (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/resumable-uploads.ts:79; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/upload-contract.json:3-4).
5. After a drop the client calls GET on the session; the server lists stored parts and the client sends the missing ones.

6. Over 25 MiB in chat (up to 500 MiB): the client opens a chat-large-file session; complete returns an intake that the server checks in the background (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:385-410).
7. The client receives the attachment (id, name, type, url) or a refusal message.
feedback_and_outputs: Attachment object {id, name, mimeType, byteCount, type, url '/api/files/<id>'} (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:262-275).
Refusals are validation errors with fixed text, for example 'Uploaded file size does not match the selected file.' (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:343).
A closed session answers 'This upload is no longer open. Start it again to finish the file.' (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:104).
An old project client gets 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:77).
settings: None found for the upload itself. Plan limits come from the billing catalog (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:564-710).

working: Presign validates kind (avatar, knowledge-file, chat-attachment), name, type and size, then returns a private upload URL valid 300 seconds, or a same-origin relay URL when direct upload is not allowed (apps/web/app/api/uploads/presign/route.ts:38, 95, 192).

Complete re-reads the stored bytes under the declared size, checks type and checksum, reuses an identical file the user already holds, checks storage, scans, runs the workspace data policy, re-seals the bytes and only then inserts the row (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:302-470).

Resumable sessions: create (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/route.ts:218), progress/list parts (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:121), sign parts (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/parts/route.ts:33), relay parts in 4 MiB segments (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:204), complete (:425), abort (:552).

Chat large files: admission, an intake row written under a per-user lock, daily large-file bytes refunded on failure, and a workflow started on complete (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/route.ts:74-215; apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:385-410). A sweeper cron exists (vercel.json:66).

Shared client picks parts above the relay segment size and falls back to presign when resumable upload is unavailable (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-chat-attachments-client.ts:193-215).
incomplete: Project sources: the 'second step' is the register route, not the chat complete route (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/route.ts:68) or finishKnowledgeFile for parts (apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/[uploadId]/route.ts:343). The brief names only the chat complete route.
disconnected_or_disabled: Large chat files need a client with a hasher and a server that offers them; otherwise the client throws or the server answers 'Files this large aren't available yet.' (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/managed-cloud-chat-attachments-client.ts:226-233; apps/web/lib/server/attachment-allowance.ts:50). The Library declines large files (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:180).
not_available: VS Code: no upload client found.
Local (on-device) uploads: no on-device equivalent found in the code opened; the routes are our managed service.

established.statement: Uploads run as a two-phase session: presign a private object, then complete it server-side with checks before a record exists.
Large uploads can be sent in resumable parts and resumed after interruption.
Duplicate project sources are refused by checksum and total storage is bounded.

acceptance_criteria: A file with an unsupported type is refused at presign with 'Chat supports images, PDFs, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and text or code files.'
A project-source presign without a checksum returns 409 UPLOAD_PROTOCOL_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.
If the byte count stored differs from the declared count, the stored object is deleted and no row is created.
A 12 MiB file interrupted after two parts resumes by sending only the missing parts, and finishes with one attachment.
Calling complete twice for the same file returns the same attachment and creates one row.
A request that would exceed plan storage is refused before the row is written.
Cancelling a part session leaves no stored object and no row.
inferred: Every app that attaches files should apply the same limits as the server; the CLI does not receive server-announced limits and uses compiled ones (apps/cli/src/cloud/attachments.rs:26).
proposed: [proposed] Record in one place which app screens trigger each upload path, so testers can map gestures to routes.
[proposed] Fix the brief's line anchors, several do not match the files.

steps.what_happens: Client hashes the file and picks the path by size (over 4 MiB: parts).
Presign or session create: auth, CSRF, rate limit, type and size check, plan admission, storage URL.
Bytes are sent to private object storage, directly or through a same-origin relay route.
Complete re-reads stored bytes, verifies size, type and checksum, scans, seals, inserts the row, deletes the staging object.
Large chat file: complete starts an intake workflow; the sweeper cron retries stuck ones.

features.summary: Checks the real bytes of an upload: executable signatures, type confusion, active content in PDFs and SVGs, credential material, a known-bad hash list and the workspace data policy. Then asks a self-hosted virus scanner. Any failure refuses the file and deletes its bytes. Required in production unless an operator opts out.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs structural inspection, credential scanning, an external malware scan and the workspace data policy on uploaded bytes before a record is created (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:601-611; apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:348-440).
purpose.why_it_exists: Stored files are later served, shared and read by models. A file full of secrets or an executable behind a picture name would otherwise be kept and distributed (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:190-200 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every uploader indirectly; security owners and operators who deploy the scanner (doc: docs/security/upload-scanning.md).
problems_solved: Mislabelled executables and active content are refused.
Credentials are not stored and fed to models.
A scanner outage fails closed instead of admitting unscanned bytes (services/upload-scanner/README.md; apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:418-431).
use_cases: Someone uploads a .png that is really a ZIP: refused.
A text file containing a private key: refused.
The virus engine is down: uploads fail with a retry message.
A password-protected archive: refused with a message to remove the password.

where_to_find_it: Nothing to open. Refusals appear wherever a file is attached: web, desktop, mobile, CLI and Chrome show the error text from the server [inferred from the shared routes].
prerequisites: An upload in progress (F095-01).
screens_and_controls: No controls. The person sees an error message.
journey: 1. The person uploads a file.
2. On complete, the server scans.
3. If refused, the bytes are deleted and the person sees a fixed message.
4. The person removes the problem and uploads again.
feedback_and_outputs: 'This file could not be attached because its contents failed a safety check.' (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:57-58 region, SAFETY_CHECK_REFUSAL_MESSAGE).
Password protected: 'This file is password protected, so its contents could not be checked. Remove the password and upload it again.' (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:482).
Scanner trouble: "We couldn't check this file for safety. Try again later." (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:487).
Too complex: 'This file is too complex for us to check for safety...' (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:490).
settings: Operator settings by name: UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_URL, UPLOAD_SCAN_WEBHOOK_TOKEN, UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-450); scanner side UPLOAD_SCAN_SOURCE_HOSTS, MAX_SOURCE_SCAN_BYTES (services/upload-scanner/src/config.ts).

working: Structural inspection and credential scan on chat attachments, then external scan, then the workspace data policy (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:397-440).
Same scan on project sources (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:359).

Large chat files: head inspection in the intake workflow plus a scan job posted to the scanner's v2 route (apps/web/lib/server/chat-file-intake/steps.ts:14-17, 802; apps/web/lib/security/source-scan-client.ts:196-203).
Known-illegal-media hash list blocks and records a moderation event (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:348-364).
Scanner service: constant-time bearer auth, 411 without length, 413 over cap, 503 on timeout or clamd failure, health probe with signature age (services/upload-scanner/src/server.ts:89,103-150,188).
Production requires a configured scanner unless UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:408-415).
incomplete: Brief says 'platform partial': complete once the scanner is deployed and the two environment values are set (S95.06). Whether it is deployed is not shown in the code: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Audio dictation skips the external scan on purpose (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:469-472).
If UPLOAD_SCAN_REQUIRED=false and no URL, only structural checks run and a warning event is logged once (apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:433-440).
not_available: Quarantine: refused bytes are deleted, not kept (apps/web/lib/server/chat-attachment-completion.ts:415).
On-device scanning on any app: none found.

established.statement: Uploaded bytes are inspected for real type, active content and executables, not only the declared MIME.
Uploads are malware-scanned and unsafe files are quarantined or rejected.
Every route that materialises user bytes runs the same scanner; a failing file is deleted and never registered; production requires the external scanner.

acceptance_criteria: A ZIP declared as image/png is refused.
A PDF with a launch action is refused.
A text file with a recognised private key format is refused; a high-entropy string alone is logged, not refused.
With the scanner down in production, the upload is refused with the retry message and no row exists.
A file larger than the scanner cap gets 413 from the scanner and is refused.
A refused chat attachment leaves no staging object.
A password-protected PDF is refused with the password message.
inferred: The credential scan reads only the first 256,000 bytes of text [inferred from CREDENTIAL_SCAN_BYTES, apps/web/lib/security/upload-scan.ts:173; use not confirmed].
proposed: [proposed] Correct docs/security/upload-scanning.md:45, which says an unconfigured production refuses with external_scanner while the code returns scan_unavailable.
[proposed] Decide whether to keep refused files for review (quarantine) or confirm deletion as the policy.

features.summary: Turns uploaded files into things a model and a person can use. PDFs, Office files, notebooks and text give their text. Scanned PDF pages are read by a vision model on a metered managed route. The Library draws a small WebP preview of pictures on request. Pictures are shrunk at request time for models.

purpose.what_it_does: Extracts text and page anchors for project sources (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:286), reads scanned pages through a model (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:97), prepares chat files in steps (apps/web/lib/server/chat-file-preparation), makes a model-sized copy of pictures (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/model-image.ts:63) and renders Library thumbnails (apps/web/lib/server/library-thumbnail.ts:51).
purpose.why_it_exists: Models read text and images, not file formats. A scan has no text layer, so without OCR the file would be listed but unanswerable (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:121-130 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: People asking questions about attached files or project sources, and anyone browsing the Library.
problems_solved: Scanned PDFs become searchable text.
Large pictures fit provider limits without changing the stored file (model-image.ts comment).
The Library shows previews without storing derivatives.
use_cases: Ask about a scanned contract added to a project.
Attach a spreadsheet and ask for totals.
Browse picture thumbnails in the Library.
Attach a large photo to chat.

where_to_find_it: No dedicated screen. Triggered by upload and by asking about a file in web, desktop, mobile, CLI and Chrome chat (trigger screens not opened).

Thumbnails: Library grid on web and desktop (shared view, packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx); mobile library uses a thumbnail hook (apps/mobile/src/features/library/useLibraryThumbnail.ts:2).
prerequisites: A Cloud account, a supported file, a plan with a vision-capable managed route for scans [inferred].
screens_and_controls: Library tile image; project source row summary; 'Ask about this file' composer in the viewer (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1349).
journey: 1. Upload a document.
2. The server extracts text; a scanned PDF page is sent as an image to a model.
3. The text is saved on the source row with a note when a model read it.
4. Ask a question; the model uses the text.
feedback_and_outputs: Row note: 'Some pages of this document had no text layer, so their text was read from the scan by a model and may contain mistakes.' (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:30).
Withheld notice when privacy settings block every vision route (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:79).
Errors such as 'This PDF has more scanned pages than project knowledge extraction reads. Split it and upload the parts.' (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:173-176).
settings: Privacy setting that keeps content away from providers that may train (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:102-115).

working: PDF text with page anchors, Office, notebook and plain text extraction for project sources (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-extraction.ts:286-419).
OCR through an admitted managed vision route with a usage reservation and finalization (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:102-200).

Chat file preparation readers for PDF, Office, spreadsheet, delimited and text, with OCR page files (apps/web/lib/server/chat-file-preparation/derived-keys.ts:86; apps/web/lib/server/tools/file-search-tool.ts:613).
Thumbnail route renders a 640 px WebP from jpeg, png, webp or gif up to 30 MiB, auto-rotated (apps/web/lib/server/library-thumbnail.ts:6-9,51; apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/thumbnail/route.ts:50-104).
Library list adds thumbnail_uri only when the file qualifies (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts:76).
Model picture copy: decode, resize and re-encode until it fits; stored file unchanged (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/model-image.ts:63).
incomplete: Extracted text is stored on project_knowledge_files (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-files.ts:393), but where anchors are stored is not shown in the insert I read: unknown.
Brief says thumbnails are 'missing' (S95.13); code has them. The brief is stale.
disconnected_or_disabled: Scans can be withheld when no no-training route exists (apps/web/lib/server/scanned-document-text.ts:79,102-115).
not_available: Stored thumbnails: none, each request renders again (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/thumbnail/route.ts:103 no-store).
Metadata stripping on stored images: none found at upload; thumbnails go through sharp [inferred that sharp drops metadata by default].
Previews for non-image files as generated files: not applicable per brief S95.12; text preview is served by /api/files/[id]/text (route folder exists).
On-device OCR: none found.

established.statement: Document parsers extract text from PDFs and office files for use by the model.
Scanned (image-only) pages are OCR-ed.
Images are preprocessed (resize, normalise, strip metadata) before storage or model use.
Thumbnails are generated for files.
Extracted text and anchors are stored for reuse.

acceptance_criteria: A text PDF added to a project has extracted text and page anchors.
A scanned PDF gets text with the OCR note and a usage reservation.
A scan for an account that opted out of training providers is stored without text and the person is told why.
A 40 MiB PNG gets no thumbnail (404 Thumbnail not available).
A 2 MP JPEG gets a WebP thumbnail with long edge 640 or less.
A PDF over the page limit is refused with the 'Split it' message.
The Library list carries thumbnail_uri only for qualifying pictures.
inferred: Costs of OCR should appear in the person's usage like other managed calls (reservation with plan tier).
proposed: [proposed] Update the brief rows for S95.09 and S95.13 to partial.
[proposed] Cache thumbnails if render cost matters; today none.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: OCR uses a managed route admitted for task type multimodal with the account's plan; the provider is whatever routing admits (SYS-model-catalog-and-routing). Picture shrinking and thumbnails use the sharp library, no model.

features.summary: A list of a person's files and generated items with type, size, origin and conversation, with search, tabs, sort, Recently deleted and a meter of storage used against the plan. Web, desktop and mobile have a screen; the CLI can list. Storage counts Library files and project sources together.

purpose.why_it_exists: Gives people one place for uploads and generated files and a clear view of how much storage the plan allows. Matches the leaders' Library [doc: docs/product/requirements.md:182].
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web, desktop, mobile and CLI.

Delete or restore files.
See storage and download use.
use_cases: Search for a PDF by name.
Open Recently deleted to restore a file.
See '1.2 GB of 4 GB file storage used'.
List library items from the CLI.

established.statement: File metadata (owner, type, size, source, conversation, lifecycle) is stored per file.
A Library catalog lists a user's files with filters, sort and search.
Storage use is accounted against the plan allowance.
Deleted files move to trash and can be restored within a window (30 days).

acceptance_criteria: A new upload appears in All and Uploads within one reload.
A file attached in a temporary chat never appears.
Deleting a file moves it to Recently deleted; restore brings it back.
A file deleted over 30 days ago is not listed in Recently deleted.
On a plan with a limit, an upload that would exceed it is refused with the plan message and the meter is unchanged.
Free users see the storage line as the Library shows it (see the owner's Free usage decision in memory; not a repo source).
Search 'report' returns files whose name or prompt contains it, case-insensitive.
Signed-out hosts show a sign-in state, not an empty library.
inferred: Meter and enforcement should use the same sum (they do: sumFileStorageBytes).
proposed: [proposed] Make the docs matrix agree with the code for web and CLI.
[proposed] Show per-app status lines in the brief.

features.summary: There is no folder hierarchy for files. The web Library shows projects as folders. Project sources can be copied from Google Drive and refreshed by hand, and the link to the origin is stored as an external reference. There is no scheduled sync and no live link to outside files.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the Library show project containers as folders (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:88-170), stores one record per outside resource a source came from (apps/web/db/neon/0322_external_resource_references.sql:28), imports Drive files into a project (apps/web/lib/server/project-drive-import.ts:121) and re-reads them on request (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/[fileId]/refresh/route.ts:31).
purpose.why_it_exists: People keep files in Drive and in projects. The reference keeps identity, version and access apart from the copied bytes (migration 0322 header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users adding Drive sources to projects.
problems_solved: Know where a source came from.
Update a source when the Drive file changes.
use_cases: Add a Drive document to a project.
Refresh it after edits in Drive.
Open a project from the Library folder row.

where_to_find_it: Web Library: project rows shown as folders, 'create folder' goes to the Projects page (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx:143-148).

Web project sources: Add sources modal with a Drive picker and a refresh button (apps/web/features/projects/components/AddSourcesModal.tsx; apps/web/features/projects/lib/google-drive-picker.ts; apps/web/features/projects/components/SourcesPanel.tsx:26,90-116).
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no folder or Drive-import screen found. Desktop has an unrelated Cloud storage panel (apps/desktop/src/features/cloud/CloudStoragePanel.tsx:61), not checked.
prerequisites: Cloud sign-in; Google Drive connected; connectors released (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/google-drive/route.ts:39); an owned, non-archived project.
screens_and_controls: Library folder rows and picker for 'Add to project' (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/library/LibraryView.tsx:1474,1888-1917).

2. Add sources, pick up to 10 Drive files.
3. The server downloads each, runs the normal upload checks and creates a source linked to a reference.
4. Later press refresh; the server compares versions and adds a new version only if changed.

features.summary: Keeps older versions of files (project knowledge files, published artifacts, and, in code only, generated files) and lets the owner of a project share it with their organisation as read-only or with named editors. Web and mobile have a sharing screen; versions have no per-file history screen found for files.

purpose.what_it_does: Two linked jobs. First, versioning: a re-uploaded project file with the same name becomes a new version and the old one is marked superseded (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-files.ts:394, :425); a published artifact keeps an append-only history that can be listed, read and restored (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:871, :971, :500; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/versions/route.ts:34); a generated file can point at the file it replaced and at the file it was made from (apps/web/lib/server/generated-file-persist.ts:95, :56). Second, sharing: a project owner or sharing manager shares a project with the organisation and sets per-person access (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:305, :405).
purpose.why_it_exists: Migration 0257 says a file had no history and no parent, a republish overwrote the earlier version, and nobody could answer where an export came from (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:2-20). Sharing exists so a team can work from one project's instructions and files while chats stay private (apps/web/features/settings/sections/OrganizationSharingSection.tsx:196).
purpose.who_uses_it: Project owners, organisation owners and admins, members with the share right, invited editors, and anyone who republishes an artifact. [inferred] from the permission checks (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:91).
problems_solved: A newer upload of a same-named project file no longer destroys the old row; it is superseded, not deleted (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:197-218).
Raising a project's default access can never silently give the whole organisation edit rights; edit is a per-member grant (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:213-217).
A member later moved to Viewer cannot keep using an old edit grant, because the right is checked again on every read (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:264-266).
A health space cannot be shared (apps/web/lib/services/org-sharing-service.ts:361).
use_cases: Owner shares a research project with the workspace so every member can read its files.
Owner shares a project 'with people I choose' and grants two colleagues Can edit.
User re-uploads a corrected spec with the same file name; the project uses the new one and the old is kept as a superseded version.
User restores an earlier published version of an artifact.

So media_assets rows get version 1 in practice [inferred from a code search of apps/web].

Migration 0257 file header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:4). Whether it is applied is not recorded in the files read; the product memory notes a later migration number in production, so the header is probably stale [inferred].

No restore route for an older project knowledge file version or an older generated file version was found (only DELETE and GET on the file route: apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/knowledge-files/[fileId]/route.ts:96-97).
disconnected_or_disabled: file_lineage is written only when a caller passes parentFileId; no such caller found, so the lineage table is likely empty in practice [inferred].

established.statement: File versions are kept (supersede chain, published versions, lineage).
Files and file-bearing resources can be shared (org sharing, publish links) under access control.
Sharing checks the organisation permission before a write.
Shared projects: members with access read instructions and files; Can edit lets them change it; chats stay private.

acceptance_criteria: Re-uploading a same-named file to a project makes the newest row version N+1, the previous row has superseded_at set, and the file list shows only the newest.
Sharing a project as a member without sharing.manage who does not own it returns 403 'Only the project's owner or someone who manages sharing...'.
Sharing with audience 'invited' sets default access none; 'workspace' sets read.
Granting write to a Viewer-role member is refused with the Viewer message.
A plan with project limit 0 refuses sharing with a validation error; at the limit, sharing returns a conflict.
Unsharing a project that is not shared returns 404 'That project is not shared with your organization'.
Each share, access change and unshare writes an audit event.
Republishing an artifact adds a version row and restore creates a new version rather than editing history.
inferred: Generated files should get versions when the model edits an earlier file, which needs callers to pass supersedesFileId [inferred from the unused parameter].
Shared project file access should also hide files of a deleted or archived project (see archived retrieval rules, apps/web/db/neon/0244_archived_resources_leave_ai_retrieval.sql) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Pass supersedesFileId and parentFileId from the tool loop and sandbox file sweep so edits and exports record versions and lineage.
[proposed] Add a per-file version history screen and restore route for project knowledge files and generated files.
[proposed] Correct or remove the 'NOT YET APPLIED' header in migration 0257 once its state is confirmed.

features.summary: Deleting a Library file hides it and keeps it for 30 days under 'Recently deleted', where it can be restored or deleted permanently. A daily job then erases stored bytes and rows, plus indexes and lineage built from them. A legal hold stops erasure. Web, Desktop and Mobile call the same server routes.

purpose.what_it_does: Soft delete sets deleted_at on a media asset (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:693); restore clears it only inside 30 days (:711-724); permanent delete erases bytes and row, but only for a file already in the trash (:756-803); a daily cron purges files older than 30 days with their bytes and derived records (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-deleted-media/route.ts:165-224).
purpose.why_it_exists: Users need to undo mistakes, and the company must eventually remove bytes and everything derived from them. The deletion policy file states the 30-day window once for every caller (apps/web/lib/resources/deletion-policies.ts:8, :222-262). AGENTS.md section 9 requires that removed files go to a recoverable state first.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in user of the Library on web, Desktop or Mobile; operators who run the cron; legal-hold administrators.
problems_solved: Accidental deletion is recoverable for 30 days.
Stored bytes do not stay forever after deletion.
Search index rows, lineage edges and generation jobs do not outlive their file.
A preserved record under legal hold is not destroyed (route.ts:249-266).
use_cases: User deletes a file, opens Recently deleted and restores it.
User permanently deletes a file from Recently deleted after a confirmation naming the loss.
Cron purges a file deleted 31 days ago and its index and lineage rows.
User removes a project source file and the source stops appearing in answers.

established.statement: Deleted files move to trash and can be restored within a window.
Expired trash and retention windows are purged, including stored objects.
Derived resources (indexes, jobs, lineage, thumbnails) are cleaned up with their source.
Deleting a source file withdraws everything derived from it (index chunks, context).
An irreversible action asks first and names the consequence; an agent never destroys user data on its own; removal goes to a recoverable state first.

acceptance_criteria: Delete moves the file to Recently deleted and it disappears from the main list and from /api/files/{id} (404).
Restore inside 30 days brings it back; after 30 days restore returns success false.
Permanent delete on a live file does not remove it; on a trashed file it erases object and row.
The cron removes objects and rows older than 30 days and reports counts; a file under legal hold is counted as heldFromPurge and kept.
If object deletion fails, the row is kept for the next run.
After purge, file_lineage edges naming the file on either side are gone.
Cron without valid secret returns 401 and touches nothing.
inferred: A user-facing confirmation exists for both delete types on the shared Library view [inferred from useConfirmAction use at LibraryView.tsx:731-756].
The window shown in confirm text should come from the same constant as the server window [inferred]; the text hardcodes 30 days.
proposed: [proposed] Make permanent=true on a live file either soft delete first or return a clear error rather than success false.
[proposed] Give project source files a restore route and a Recently deleted view.
[proposed] Read the window in client text from a shared contract constant.

steps.what_happens: User confirms Delete; the client sends DELETE /api/media?id=<uuid> with a CSRF token.
Server validates the id, rate limits, and sets deleted_at on the user's row in the active workspace.
A database trigger drops the file's search index document.
Restore clears deleted_at when it is still inside 30 days.
Permanent delete: in one transaction lock the trashed row, refuse if held, delete the stored object, delete the row, then delete derived records.
Daily cron selects assets deleted over 30 days ago that are not held, deletes objects from object storage, deletes rows whose objects went, then removes lineage edges and cascades.
Object bytes live in the private bucket of the object-storage provider; deletion is a call to that outside service.

features.summary: Download serves a Library file only to its owner in the active workspace, with safe headers and a monthly download allowance. Export data (web) builds a zip of account JSON plus library and project files for a 24-hour link; desktop and mobile export JSON only. Conversion has no endpoint; it is a LibreOffice command the model runs in a sandbox.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams or redirects file bytes after an access check (apps/web/app/api/files/[id]/route.ts:194-347); builds a downloadable archive of the account's data and files in background jobs (apps/web/lib/server/data-export-archive.ts:508-720); lets the assistant convert office files in a code sandbox using an installed LibreOffice (apps/web/lib/e2b/execution-tools.ts:31-33).
purpose.why_it_exists: People must be able to take their files and data out (data portability), and users of generated documents want other formats such as PDF. Access checks stop other accounts reaching private bytes.
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in user downloading a Library file; account owners requesting a data export; users asking the assistant for a PDF or other converted file.
problems_solved: Bytes are never served without a per-request access check and a 404 for another workspace.
Browser-executable types (html, svg, xml) are forced to download so they cannot run on the app origin (apps/web/lib/security/served-bytes.ts:41-55).
Large exports do not run in one request; they are split into volumes of about 1 GiB and processed in jobs (data-export-archive.ts:48, :597-720).
Unreadable files are listed in unavailable-files.json instead of failing the whole export (data-export-archive.ts:55).
use_cases: User clicks Download on a PDF in the Library.
User presses 'Export data' in settings and later opens the zip link or emailed link.
User asks the assistant to turn a Word file into a PDF; the model runs soffice in its sandbox.
User on Desktop exports Cloud account data as a JSON file.

established.statement: Downloads are authorised per request against owner/workspace and served with safe headers.
Exports are packaged (archive of files and metadata).
Files can be converted between formats server-side.
Execution boundaries must be stated from code; sandboxing and code execution depend on an AGI harness, not on the model.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-out request to /api/files/{id} returns 401; another account's id returns the same 404 as an unknown id.
A trashed file returns 404.
An html or svg file is served as attachment with application/octet-stream.
Responses carry Cache-Control private, no-store and X-Content-Type-Options nosniff.
When the monthly download allowance is used up the file is refused with the plan message.
POST /api/user/export returns 202 with a preparing archive; a second request while preparing returns the same archive.
The archive contains export.json, files/library and files/projects entries, and unavailable-files.json when a file cannot be read.
An archive link works for 24 hours and then answers that it has expired.
inferred: Server-side conversion is intended to be done by the sandbox, not a separate service [inferred from the code found].
Desktop and mobile JSON export is intended to be partial compared with the web archive [inferred]; the brief says archive of files and metadata.
proposed: [proposed] Add a dedicated, metered convert action or at least record derivation 'conversion' lineage for sandbox outputs.
[proposed] Offer the file archive on Desktop and Mobile, or link to the web export.
[proposed] Correct the brief's code pointers for S95.22.

steps.what_happens: Client requests the file; server rate limits, checks sign-in and looks up the file for this user and workspace.
Server checks the download allowance, streams bytes from private object storage and records egress.
Object storage holds the bytes; large chat uploads are sent by a signed URL straight from storage.
Browser saves the blob.
Export request: server collects account data, stages export.json in private storage, enqueues the build job.
Build job streams library and project files into zip volumes through a multipart upload to private storage, then schedules expiry and the ready email.
Email is sent through the notification email service when configured and verified.
Conversion: the model calls a code tool; the command soffice runs in a remote E2B sandbox, and output files are persisted as generated files.

features.summary: A metadata-only list of every artifact an account's assistant messages have produced. The server writes one row per artifact when an assistant message is saved. The web gallery, the web and phone project Artifacts tabs, the CLI and the VS Code tree read it, so a new device sees artifacts it never opened. It holds no artifact content.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores id, title, type, language, source conversation, source message and time for each artifact found in assistant message markdown, and serves the caller's rows newest first, optionally limited to one project (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/index/route.ts:39-106; apps/web/db/neon/0121_artifact_index.sql:37).
purpose.why_it_exists: Web artifacts are re-derived from message text, so a device only knew artifacts from chats it had rendered. The index fixes discovery without copying content (apps/web/db/neon/0121_artifact_index.sql header; doc: docs/architecture/derived-state.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web (gallery and project panel), phone (project tab), CLI (artifacts list) and VS Code (artifacts tree). Engineers use it as the account's artifact registry.
problems_solved: Gallery showed one artifact after clearing local storage while the account had four (apps/web/db/neon/0121_artifact_index.sql header)
Project views could not list artifacts from chats never opened on this device (apps/web/features/projects/components/ProjectArtifactsPanel.tsx:28)
No second copy of content to drift from the message (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/index-artifacts.ts:40-48)
use_cases: Open /gallery on a new laptop and see every artifact the account made
Open a project and see all artifacts from its chats
Run the CLI artifacts list command to find an artifact id to show or publish
Browse artifacts in the VS Code Artifacts tree

established.statement: A server-side registry records every artifact (id, type, title, source conversation/message) for the account.
The index holds metadata only, never content; rows are keyed by the deterministic derived id so they merge with locally derived artifacts.
Rows are written by the server when an assistant message is saved; indexing never fails or delays the save.
Each user sees only their own rows (row-level security).
Default page 200, maximum 500.
Artifacts carry id, title, type and source message or session.

acceptance_criteria: After an assistant message with a renderable block is saved, one row exists with the same id the client derives
The row has no content column and title is at most 200 characters
GET /api/artifacts/index returns only the caller's rows, newest first, default 200, maximum 500; limit 501 returns a validation error
projectId returns only artifacts whose source conversation is in that project; a non-uuid projectId is rejected
Deleting a conversation removes its artifacts from the list
A forced indexing failure still saves the message
Signed-out web gallery shows its empty state without a network call
inferred: Local-mode chats that never reach the server have no index rows; the index is Cloud-side only [inferred from the table being server-side and written by server routes]
A reader that needs content must fetch the message and derive it [inferred from packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-index.ts:13-18 comment]
proposed: [proposed] Add a cursor so accounts with more than 500 artifacts can page
[proposed] Add a one-time rebuild job from messages for history older than migration 0121
[proposed] Show index rows on the phone main Artifacts screen

steps.what_happens: An assistant message is saved on the server (single, bulk, keep, edit, sync push, managed turn, branch)
Artifacts are derived from the message text with the shared derivation under the policy stored in message metadata
Old rows for the message are deleted and the new rows inserted in one unnest statement; errors are logged only

The client merges rows with locally derived artifacts by id

features.summary: A server copy of artifacts whose content was edited or authored on a device, with an append-only version table. Web and phone push and pull these through the chat sync endpoint in Cloud mode. Re-derivable artifacts are not pushed. The server keeps versions, but no API to read one back or restore it was found; restore works on the local copy.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds one current row per edited artifact (content, title, type, version, pin, tags, soft-delete) and writes a version row each time a push is applied (apps/web/db/neon/0039_artifact_cloud_sync.sql:40,59; apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts:366-374,886).
purpose.why_it_exists: An edited artifact can no longer be re-derived from its message, so it needs a server copy to follow the account across devices (apps/web/db/neon/0039_artifact_cloud_sync.sql:12-22).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people who edit artifacts on web or phone in Cloud mode; the sync engine on each client; support staff reading data exports.

established.statement: A server store keeps each artifact's successive versions so any version can be read back or restored.
Only non-re-derivable (edited or authored) artifacts are stored; re-derivable ones are never pushed.
Version rows are append-only keyed by artifact and version; current row is last-writer-wins; history unions.
Rows are isolated per user; Managed Cloud only, Local and own-key artifacts never pushed.
Artifacts must have version history and retention behaviour.

acceptance_criteria: Edit an artifact on web; it appears on the phone after sync with the same content
Pushing with a stale base version returns a conflict containing the server's current row
A second push of the same version number does not duplicate the version row
A temporary conversation's artifact is never pushed
User B cannot read user A's artifact or version rows
Deleting the account removes both tables' rows for the user
A stored version can be read back through an API [not met today]
inferred: Local and own-key conversations stay off the account because the client filters them (artifacts-store.ts:1059-1072) [inferred]
proposed: [proposed] Add a read endpoint listing versions and returning one
[proposed] Make the restore action write back through sync so history is server-complete
[proposed] Record a version row for every applied edit even if the client did not bump the number

features.summary: On web, a person can comment on a passage, slide, page element or whole artifact, reply, resolve, and send open comments or a selected passage to the assistant as an edit request. Comments are private to the account; there is no multi-person editing. Selection edits are prompts sent through normal chat, not a server service.

features.summary: A server tool lets the model create real Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV files from structured input, store them and attach them to the answer. It runs in the web chat loop (composer Output menu, or detected request) and in live voice sessions. Bad input returns a readable error to the model, not an empty file.

purpose.what_it_does: Validates a strict request, builds the file with libraries on the server (or edits an attached Word or Excel file), checks the package, stores it as a generated file and returns a file link (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts:126-209,930-1076; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2562-2606).
purpose.why_it_exists: People ask for a file, not text about a file; models cannot write these binary formats themselves.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people in web chat (and the phone chat, which sends the same flag) and in live voice.

features.summary: HTML, React and SVG artifacts show live in a frame served from a separate sandbox origin that cannot reach the app's cookies or storage. A strict policy blocks network calls. If the origin is unset, equal to the app, or silent, the preview falls back to a restricted same-page frame. An element picker lets the person select a part of the preview.

purpose.what_it_does: Posts artifact source to a static renderer page in a cross-origin frame; the renderer shows html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text or code and reports ready, done or error (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:881-910; apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:146-433).
purpose.why_it_exists: Model-written code is untrusted; running it on the app's origin would hand it the person's session (apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:153-157 comment).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone previewing an artifact on web; the Chrome extension side panel; the Tauri desktop build; published artifact pages.
