features.summary: A published HTML or React app on the web can keep small text key-value data between visits, either private to one signed-in viewer or shared by everyone who can open the app. The server enforces key rules, size limits and who may read or write. Only the web app runs this.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives a published HTML or React app four calls, get, set, delete and list, on window.agi.storage. Each call reaches the server, which saves text rows in the table published_artifact_storage. Personal rows belong to one signed-in viewer. Shared rows are visible to everyone who may open the app (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:283, apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:78, apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:3).
purpose.why_it_exists: A generated page has no backend of its own. Without a platform store, a to-do list, a score board or a poll would forget everything on reload. The migration comment says the table holds 'Key-value text a published HTML or React artifact keeps between visits' (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:130).
purpose.who_uses_it: Two people. The app author writes code that calls window.agi.storage, usually by asking the assistant to build it. The viewer opens the published link, signs in and sees their saved state next time. The publisher can also inspect and clear the shared data in the Sites page (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteDataTab.tsx:231).
problems_solved: Published pages lose state on reload.
Authors cannot run a database for a small generated app.
Viewers cannot keep private data in a shared app without it leaking to other viewers.
One viewer or app cannot fill the database without bound (value and per-scope size limits).
use_cases: A habit tracker app keeps each viewer's checkmarks as personal data.
A team poll keeps vote counts as shared data.
A notes app saves a draft as JSON text under one key.
The owner opens Sites, Data and clears shared data after a bad test.

where_to_find_it: Web only. There is no menu item. The storage is used by the code inside a published HTML or React app opened at /shared-artifact/<token> (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:62).
Web, owner view: sidebar entry 'Sites' (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:125), open a site, tab 'Data' (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteDetail.tsx:280).
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: no runtime. A published app opens in the system browser, where the web page serves it (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:405-409).
prerequisites: The artifact is published and its kind is html or react (apps/web/db/neon/0372_published_site_viewers.sql:72).

The viewer is signed in. A signed-out viewer gets a banner 'Create an account or sign in to use this app's AI and saved data.' with buttons 'Create an account' and 'Sign in' (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:274).

The sandbox origin must be configured. The runtime bridge lives in the sandbox page (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:242, apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:158). A known-flaws row says production did not set NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN when it was written (audit/registers/known-flaws.md:57). Current setting is unknown.
The viewer can open the app: public, own app, shared with a workspace they can read, or invited by email (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72).
screens_and_controls: No screen for the viewer. The app's own code decides what to show.

Sites page, Data tab: heading 'Shared data', text 'Saved by the app for every visitor to see.', a size summary, table columns Key, Value, Size, Updated, button 'Clear shared data' (disabled when empty), empty text 'Nothing shared yet.' (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteDataTab.tsx:241).
For other app kinds the Data tab says 'Only apps built as HTML or React can save data between visits.' (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteDataTab.tsx:231).
journey: The author publishes an HTML or React artifact (see F096-09).
The viewer opens the link and signs in if the app needs saved data.
The app calls window.agi.storage.set(name, jsonText, shared). Values must be text, so objects need JSON.stringify (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:289).
The server saves the row and returns the saved key and value.
On the next visit the app calls get or list and shows the saved state.
The owner may open Sites, Data, and click 'Clear shared data' to remove shared rows.
feedback_and_outputs: A call resolves with {key, value, shared}, null for a missing key on get, {key, deleted, shared} on delete, or {keys, prefix, shared} on list (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:113).

Refusals come back as readable messages: 'Keys are 1 to 200 characters with no spaces, slashes or quotes, and values are text.' (400), 'A saved value can be up to 4 MB.' (413), 'This app's shared data is at its 20 MB limit.' or 'Your data in this app is at its 20 MB limit.' (413), 'This app uses connected apps, so it cannot save data that other people can read.' (403), 'This app is no longer available.' (404) (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:60-115).
Without a sign-in the call fails with "Sign in to use this app's AI and saved data." (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/artifactRuntimeClient.ts:57).
settings: No user setting found in the code for storage.

Server limits are code constants: per value, per scope, key pattern and list size (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:8-11, apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:99).
Rate limit bucket name 'artifact-storage' (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:55); its numbers were not read, unknown.

working: Route api:POST /api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage handles get, set, delete, list with token check, CSRF, active-account check, rate limit, schema check and a runnable-app check (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:46-78).

Table with key check (1-200 characters, no whitespace, slash, backslash or quotes), a 5 MiB value check, unique index per app, scope and key, and row-level security on all four verbs (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:3-20).

Who may run an app is decided by two database functions. Their latest definition allows public apps, the owner, workspace members for 'organization' apps, and invited emails for 'invited' apps; only html and react kinds (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72-151).

Write admission takes an advisory lock, requires read committed isolation, sums existing bytes in the scope and inserts only if the total fits within the scope limit (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:208-258).
List returns up to 1,000 keys in order, optionally by prefix (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:276-296).

The sandbox page installs a frozen window.agi object with complete and storage, and posts each call to the parent page, which validates it and forwards to the server (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:313, apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:272, apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:123).
Unpublish deletes the rows through a foreign key with on delete cascade (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:5).
Owner data view and clear: api:GET and api:DELETE /api/artifacts/publish/[token]/data (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/data/route.ts:62-63) with the Sites 'Data' tab.
incomplete: The refusal of shared writes for connector apps calls the database function app_published_artifact_uses_connectors, which is defined in migration 0391. That file's header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0391_artifact_runtime_usage_cap.sql:4, :316). Whether production has it is unknown.

The migration comment says the allowance is 5 MB per row and 20 MB, but the route enforces a 4 MB value limit from the contract constant while the database check allows 5 MiB (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:85, packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:10, apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:17).
disconnected_or_disabled: If the sandbox origin is not configured the page falls back to an inline frame with no bridge; a request without a host is answered with a message that AI and saved data are not available (apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:158, apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:277-281). Whether the fallback frame installs window.agi at all was not found; unknown.
not_available: Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no storage runtime (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:405-409).
No per-viewer storage listing for the owner: the owner sees shared rows and only their own personal rows (apps/web/lib/services/published-site-data-service.ts:8-14).
No binary or object storage; values are text only (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:56).

established.statement: Generated apps can persist data in a backend store provided by the platform.
Only HTML and React apps can use storage; other kinds are refused.
Personal data belongs to one signed-in viewer; shared data is visible to everyone who can open the app.
Shared storage is refused for apps that use connected data when the writer is not the owner.
Unpublishing deletes the app's stored rows.
Over-limit writes return a clear 413 message.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-in viewer of a public html app can set, get, list and delete a personal key and sees the same value after a reload.
A key containing a space, slash, backslash or quote is refused with status 400 and the key message.
A value over 4 MB returns 413 'A saved value can be up to 4 MB.' and nothing is saved.
A write that would push one scope past 20 MB returns 413 with the 'limit' message; a smaller write in another scope still works.
A viewer cannot read another viewer's personal key; both can read the same shared key.
A markdown, svg, mermaid, text or code publication returns 404 'This app is no longer available.' from the storage route.
After the owner unpublishes the app, its rows no longer exist in published_artifact_storage.
A non-owner write with shared=true on an app bound to connected apps returns 403 shared_storage_with_connectors.
inferred: Changing the audience from public to workspace or invited should make existing rows unreachable for people who lose access, because every policy calls app_can_run_published_artifact [inferred].
The 20 MB limit applies per scope (one shared pool plus one pool per viewer), not per app, because the admission query sums bytes by app and scope owner [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Align the 5 MB wording in the migration comments and brief with the 4 MB enforced value limit.
[proposed] Add a record of when migration 0391 was applied so the shared-write refusal can be trusted.
[proposed] Let the owner see per-viewer usage totals without reading private values.

steps.what_happens: The app code calls window.agi.storage.get, set, delete or list. The sandbox page turns it into a runtime request.
The sandbox page posts the request to the app page. The page checks the origin and shape of the request.
The host checks the viewer is signed in. If not, it shows the sign-in banner and fails the call.
The browser posts to the storage route with a CSRF header.
The server checks token format, CSRF, active account, rate limit and the request schema, then finds the runnable app.
The server reads, writes, deletes or lists in the database under the viewer's row-level security. Writes take an advisory lock and check the scope total.
The answer goes back through the page to the sandbox, and the app's promise resolves or rejects.

data.what: Key, text value, byte count, who updated it, timestamps, owner (null for shared)
data.synced: Held only on the server; every device of the same viewer reads the same rows after sign-in
data.retained_or_deleted: Kept until the app deletes the key, the owner clears shared data, the app is unpublished (cascade), or the viewer's profile is removed (cascade on owner_user_id) (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:5-6)

data.what: AI consent flags stored in the browser by the same runtime hook (not storage rows)
data.retained_or_deleted: Until the person answers again or clears browser data (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:48-76)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model or provider takes part in storage calls. Storage is plain database reads and writes. The sibling call window.agi.complete does use a model; see F096-08.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account is required even for a public app, because the database functions return nothing when there is no current user (apps/web/db/neon/0395_published_artifact_audience_revocation.sql:72-90). The account must be active (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/storage/route.ts:54).
access_and_usage.permissions: Viewer must be allowed to run the app: public, owner, workspace member for an organization app, or invited email for an invited app. Personal rows are limited to the viewer; shared rows to anyone who can run the app (apps/web/db/neon/0325_published_artifact_storage.sql:70-110). Only the owner may call the data view and clear routes.
access_and_usage.subscription: none found in the code. The storage route does not read the plan or entitlement.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Key 1-200 characters; value up to 4 MB enforced by the route; database check at 5 MiB; 20 MB per scope; list returns up to 1,000 keys; request body ceiling is twice the value limit plus 64 KB (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:8-13). Rate limit bucket 'artifact-storage' per user. Storage use is not billed or counted as AI usage.
access_and_usage.flags: No flag on the storage route. The sandbox origin variable decides whether the bridge exists. AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED gates AI only, not storage (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:6).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable. No model is involved.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Publishing is refused for artifacts not made in managed cloud mode, so a Local artifact cannot become a published app that uses this store (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:267; mobile alert 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish', apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:300). Storage itself always runs on our servers; no on-device storage version exists.

features.summary: A published web app can ask the model to answer a prompt and, if allowed, let the model use the viewer's connected apps through server-held tools, without the page seeing credentials. It exists in the web code but is switched off: connectors are 'coming soon' and AI in apps needs a server flag. The brief calls it missing.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a published HTML or React app call window.agi.complete(prompt, {connectors}). The server runs one model completion for the signed-in viewer, optionally with tools from the viewer's own connected apps, and returns text. Credentials stay on the server. The viewer must say Allow before any call (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/route.ts:74, apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx:133).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants artifacts to read connected-service data without exposing credentials (S96.18) and a viewer sign-in path to those services (S96.19). The code implements a tool-using completion rather than a raw data proxy [inferred].
purpose.who_uses_it: App authors on a paid plan who build an app that summarises mail, tickets or notes. Viewers who open the app and approve the access. Reviewers who check that public links never reach connected apps.
problems_solved: A generated page cannot hold secrets, yet needs live data.
A public link must never let a stranger spend or read someone's connected apps.
Viewers need to see and limit which tools the app may use.
Spend by AI calls inside apps must be reserved and counted against the viewer's plan.
use_cases: A published dashboard summarises the viewer's own issue tracker.
A workspace-shared app drafts text with AI only, with no connectors.
A viewer declines tools they do not trust and the app still runs without them.
A publisher tries to share a connector app publicly and is refused.

where_to_find_it: Web only. In the published page at /shared-artifact/<token> an 'AI permission' panel appears when the app first asks for AI (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx:57).
Own chat: live artifacts have a separate owner-side route api:GET/POST /api/artifacts/live (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/live/route.ts); its UI labels were not read, unknown.
Other apps: no runtime; a published app opens in the system browser (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:405-409).
prerequisites: Server flag AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is on, else 'AI in apps is not available yet.' (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:6, apps/web/lib/artifact-ai.ts:3).

For connectors, connectors must be released. The shipped constant is 'coming_soon', so they are refused with 'Connectors are coming soon.' (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14, apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:122).
The viewer is signed in and on a plan with the artifact_connectors capability: pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium or enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341,361).
The publication is not public: visibility must be workspace or invited (apps/web/db/neon/0383_published_artifact_connector_audience.sql:33).
The app was published bound to connected apps, otherwise 'This app was not published with connected apps, so it cannot use yours.' (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/route.ts:67).
screens_and_controls: 'AI permission' panel with, for each connected app, a legend and a tool list with checkboxes, 'Checking your connected apps' while loading, an error line if the list fails, and buttons 'Allow' and "Don't allow" (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx:57-140).
After granting, a review control lets the viewer reopen the choice (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:300).
Sign-in banner 'Create an account or sign in to use this app's AI and saved data.' with 'Create an account' and 'Sign in' (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/PublishedArtifactView.tsx:274).
journey: The publisher shares the app to a workspace or invited people (not public).
The viewer opens the link and signs in.
The app calls window.agi.complete with optional connector ids.
The page asks 'AI permission'; the viewer chooses tools and clicks 'Allow'.
The browser posts the prompt to the server with an idempotency key.
The server checks switches, plan, policy, moderation and limits, picks a route, runs the model (and tools) and returns text.
The app shows the text.
feedback_and_outputs: Response is {text} (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:32).

Readable refusals: 'You chose not to let this app use AI.', 'You chose not to let this app use your connected apps.', 'Your connected apps could not be listed for this app.', 'Your plan cannot use connected apps from published apps.', 'Connected apps in published apps are available on <plan labels>.', and the public-share message (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:15-17, apps/web/lib/services/artifact-connector-gate.ts:26-34).
Turn limit messages: 429 when all concurrent AI responses are busy, 403 when the plan excludes AI in apps (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:60-90).
settings: Consent is remembered per viewer, link and exact code revision in browser storage, so republished code asks again (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:79-100).
Connector tool permissions and approval policy are read per user (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:373-381).
Server setting names: AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED (flag) and the connector release constant.

working: Three routes exist: complete, connectors and storage under api:POST /api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/ (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]/complete/route.ts:74, connectors/route.ts:47).

The connectors route lists, per connector, whether it is connected and which tools are available, needing approval or blocked (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:44-72; apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:432).

Connector use is refused on public publications by a database function that returns true only when the audience is not public (apps/web/db/neon/0383_published_artifact_connector_audience.sql:33; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:620).
Setting visibility to public is refused with a conflict if the app uses connectors (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:176-179).
Publishing an artifact that has a live binding starts it as 'invited' instead of 'public' (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:440).

Completion pipeline: switch check, coarse release check, public-share check, workspace privacy policy, entitlement and managed compute access, connector gate, moderation, content safety, secret handling, route selection, model and provider policy, egress policy, concurrent-turn slot, then the reserved and finalised usage record (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:116-285; apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:629-760).
Google data fails closed: a run offered a Google connector tool runs only on a model that keeps inputs out of training (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:665-671).
Owner-side live artifacts store a binding of connectors and allowed tools (apps/web/lib/services/artifact-runtime-service.ts:948).
incomplete: Per-app metering of AI calls is coded in managed-usage-request-service with database function reserve_artifact_runtime_usage_microusd, defined in migration 0391 which is marked not applied (apps/web/lib/services/managed-usage-request-service.ts:785-804; apps/web/db/neon/0391_artifact_runtime_usage_cap.sql:4).

The viewer 'sign-in bridge' is only account sign-in to AGI plus Allow; no flow to connect a new service from inside the published page was found. The connectors list reports connected true or false (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-runtime.ts:63). What the UI shows for connected false was not read, unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Connectors are switched off by the constant CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE = 'coming_soon' (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14).
AI in apps is switched off unless AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is on; its production value is unknown (apps/web/lib/server/artifact-ai-switch.ts:6).
not_available: No credential-free raw data proxy: the page cannot query a connector directly, only through a model completion [inferred].
Not on desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code or Chrome (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:405-409).
Not for public links by design (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:109).

established.statement: A proxy lets artifacts read connected-service data without exposing credentials.
A bridge lets a viewer of a shared app sign in to that app's connected services.
Connector-based apps cannot be shared publicly.
Connector runs pass through managed compute access and entitlement checks.
Connectors are not released yet and AI in apps is off by default.

acceptance_criteria: With connectors unreleased, a complete call naming one connector returns 403 connectors_coming_soon.
With the AI flag off, any complete call returns 403 artifact_ai_off with 'AI in apps is not available yet.'
A complete call with connectors on a public publication returns 403 connectors_not_on_public_share.
A viewer on a plan without artifact_connectors gets 403 plan_upgrade_required naming the plan labels.
A viewer who clicks "Don't allow" gets the declined message and no server call is made.
A viewer who is not the owner calling connectors on an app not bound to connected apps gets 403 connectors_not_declared.
A completion reserves and then finalises a usage record; a failed run releases the reservation.
Republishing changed code asks for AI permission again.
inferred: The brief status 'missing' is out of date for the web platform: routes, tables and UI exist, only switched off [inferred].
Viewer sign-in to services probably relies on the viewer's own connections made in the connectors page, not on a flow inside the published page [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Update the brief status of S96.18 and S96.19 to 'partial, disabled'.
[proposed] Add an in-page 'Connect this app' link when a connector reports not connected.
[proposed] Record the live state of the release constant and the AI flag in one status page for testers.

steps.what_happens: App calls window.agi.complete; the sandbox page relays it to the host.
Host checks sign-in, then shows the 'AI permission' panel or uses stored consent for this exact code revision.
Browser fetches connector and tool descriptions for the panel.
Browser posts the prompt, connector ids and allowed tools with an idempotency key.
Server runs the gates: AI flag, connector release, public-share block, workspace policy, plan entitlement, moderation, safety, secret handling.
Server picks a model route allowed for the plan, checks model and egress policy and takes a concurrent-turn slot.
Server reserves usage, runs the completion or tool loop against the model provider, using the viewer's connector tools, then finalises usage.
Text returns to the page and then to the app.

The run is on our servers and Local or own-key origin artifacts are refused for owned runs (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/artifact-completion.ts:59-67). features.summary: On the web, a person publishes an artifact to a durable link, chooses who may open it (anyone with the link, their workspace, or invited emails), updates it, unpublishes it, and restores earlier versions. The server screens content and operators can take it down. Mobile and CLI can publish too. Desktop only saves a local file.

purpose.what_it_does: Copies an artifact into the published_artifacts table under a 24-character token and serves it at /shared-artifact/<token>. Republishing keeps the same link and adds a version. The owner can rename it, change its audience, invite viewers, list and restore versions, view and clear app data, and unpublish (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:168, apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:196-197).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants generated pages to be reachable by others without hosting work (S96.20), with audience control (S96.23), moderation (S96.25) and rollback (S96.26).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who makes an artifact in chat and wants to share it. Workspace members who receive a link. Platform moderators who handle takedowns and reports.
problems_solved: A chat artifact is private to its conversation.
Links must not be guessable.
Owners need to revoke or roll back.
Illegal or abusive content needs a takedown path.
Connector apps must stay off public links.
use_cases: Publish an HTML landing page and send the link.
Share a dashboard with the workspace only.
Invite three reviewers by email.
Restore the previous version after a bad edit.
A moderator removes a reported page.

where_to_find_it: Web chat artifact panel: menu item and button 'Publish' (shows 'Publishing…' while busy), with the accessible name 'Publish artifact to a public link' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2308,2924), plus 'Share artifact' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2774).
Web sidebar 'Sites' opens /chat/sites; a site has tabs 'Settings' and 'Data' (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:125, apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteDetail.tsx:279-280).
Web public page /shared-artifact/<token> (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:62).

Mobile: full-screen artifact 'Publish' with alert 'Publish to a public link?'; Sites screen 'Sites' with chips 'Yours' and 'Shared with you' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:285-293, apps/mobile/src/features/sites/SitesScreen.tsx:180,225).
CLI: agi artifacts publish, unpublish, audience, published (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:3877-4020).
Desktop: local file only; no hosted publishing (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:13-15).
VS Code and Chrome: no publish; VS Code lists artifacts and opens a published link (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:116-118).
prerequisites: Signed in to AGI Cloud. Mobile offers 'Sign in to AGI Cloud to publish' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:303).
The artifact kind is html, react, svg, mermaid, markdown, text or code (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:61).
Content is 1 to 1,000,000 characters (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:50).
The artifact came from a managed-cloud chat; otherwise publishing is refused (packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifacts.ts:267).
Workspace policy allows external sharing for public audience (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-publication-policy.ts:67).
The conversation belongs to the caller and is not deleted.
screens_and_controls: Audience choices: 'Anyone with the link', 'Your workspace', 'Only people you invite' (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteSharingOptions.tsx:8-10).
Workspace share confirm label 'Share with workspace' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1339).

Site card menu 'Unpublish' and a copy-link button; Settings tab sections 'Versions', rename, audience, invited viewers (apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteCard.tsx:93-116, apps/web/features/sites/components/SiteSettingsTab.tsx:319).
Public page shows 'Published <date>' and a report-content link (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:92).
Unavailable page for bad or revoked links; invite-only page for invited links the viewer cannot open (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:69-82).
journey: Open an artifact in chat and click Publish.
The server screens the title and content, strips or blocks secrets according to policy, and saves the page.
A share link appears; copy it.
Choose the audience in the panel or on the Sites page; for invited, add email addresses.
Edit the artifact and click Publish again: same link, new version if the content changed.
On Sites, open Settings, Versions, and restore an earlier version.
Choose Unpublish to remove the link for everyone.
feedback_and_outputs: Publish returns 201 with token, shareUrl, version, kind, title, sandboxed, visibility and workspace info (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:108-125).

Refusals: validation text when the usage policy is violated ('This artifact cannot be published because it violates the AGI Workforce usage policy.'), 409 when the user already has the maximum of 200 publications ('You already have 200 published artifacts. Unpublish one before publishing another.'), 403 when the conversation is not theirs (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:413-416; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-publication-policy.ts:18-24).
Unpublish of a token that is not the caller's gives 404 'Published artifact not found' (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:75).
Audit event 'share_link_updated' is recorded on publish and restore (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:103).
settings: Audience (public, organization, invited) per publication.
Workspace external-sharing policy and secret-handling policy shape what is allowed (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-publication-policy.ts:67-85).
Rate-limit buckets 'share-create' and 'share-view'; numbers unknown.

working: Publish and list: api:POST and api:GET /api/artifacts/publish with CSRF, rate limit, schema check, sharing gate, moderation, outbound inspection, upsert, version record, audit (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts:42-125).
Token is 18 random bytes in base64url, 24 characters; format enforced everywhere by one regex (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:107,289).
Same artifact republishes to the same row through unique (user_id, artifact_id) (apps/web/db/neon/0095_published_artifacts.sql:68; apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:421).

Per-user cap MAX_PUBLISHED_PER_USER equals 200, checked under an advisory lock (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:59,413; packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/artifact-index.ts:132).

Three audiences: public, organization, invited. The page reads public rows first, then workspace and invited rows through row-level security (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:28-45; apps/web/db/neon/0372_published_site_viewers.sql:25).
An artifact with a live binding starts as 'invited' (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:440).

Update: PATCH changes title or audience; going public is refused if the app uses connectors and checked against the external sharing gate (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/route.ts:176-186).

Unpublish: DELETE removes the row, which cascades to versions, viewers, shares and storage (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:563; apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:53).

Version history and restore exist: versions list, read, and restore that republishes the old snapshot under the same token (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/[token]/versions/[version]/route.ts:46-133). An unchanged republish does not add a version (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:871).

Moderation: platform admin takedown deletes a public row and content reports have a review queue; the public page links 'report' (apps/web/app/api/admin/takedown/route.ts:36,113; apps/web/app/api/admin/content-reports/route.ts:60,132).

Mobile publishing and Sites screens call the same endpoints (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/services/artifactPublishing.ts:60-292). CLI publish, audience, unpublish call the same routes (apps/cli/src/cloud/artifacts.rs:451-585).
incomplete: Published pages have no expiry and views are not counted or audited (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:44-47).
Per-app AI metering depends on migration 0391, marked not applied (apps/web/db/neon/0391_artifact_runtime_usage_cap.sql:4).
The sandbox origin variable may be unset in production, which affects script apps (audit/registers/known-flaws.md:57).
disconnected_or_disabled: Mobile publishing in Local mode is blocked with 'Switch to AGI Cloud to publish' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/ArtifactFullScreen.tsx:299-300).
not_available: Custom domains: no code found (S96.22 missing).
Deployment history as a build log: not present; the version list is the only history (brief says not applicable).
Hosted publishing on desktop, VS Code and Chrome (apps/desktop/src/features/artifacts/publishAdapter.ts:13-15; docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:116-118).
Per-app views metering (S96.24) (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:47).

established.statement: A service deploys generated sites and apps to a hosted URL.
Deployment history is not applicable.
Custom domains are missing.
Access to a published app is authorized per its audience (public vs workspace).
Per-app metering of views, compute and AI calls is missing.
Published content is screened and can be reported and taken down by moderators.
A controller unpublishes and restores earlier versions.
Links use an unguessable 24-character token; republish keeps the link; no expiry; per-user cap returns a conflict.
Mobile and CLI publish go through the managed cloud route only; the picked mode must be Cloud.

acceptance_criteria: Publishing the same artifact twice returns the same token and the second version number only if content changed.
A 25-character or malformed token returns the unavailable page and 404 from the API.
With audience 'Only people you invite', a signed-out visitor sees the invite-only page, and an invited email opens the app.
Unpublish by a non-owner token returns 404 and does not delete.
Publishing the 201st artifact returns 409 with the cap message.
Publishing text that the moderation check rejects returns a validation error and nothing is saved.
Restore of version N makes the live page equal version N and records a new version.
After a platform takedown the link shows the unavailable page.
inferred: Moderators can only act on public rows through the takedown route's target lookup; whether workspace and invited rows can be taken down was not read [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add per-publication view counts if S96.24 is wanted.
[proposed] Update the brief: S96.21 has a version list and S96.24 has partial AI metering.
[proposed] Offer hosted publish on desktop through the web route.

steps.what_happens: The person clicks Publish. The client picks the kind and sends artifact id, title, content and conversation id.
Server checks CSRF, the share-create rate limit and the body schema.
Server checks external sharing policy, runs the usage-policy check on title and content, then outbound content inspection for secrets.
In one transaction the server takes a per-user lock, checks the cap, upserts the row, and records a version unless unchanged.
Server writes an audit event and returns the share URL.
A visitor opens the link. The server reads public rows, else workspace or invited rows by the visitor's session, and renders the page, running script kinds in the sandbox frame.
Unpublish deletes the row and everything that cascades from it.

data.what: Title, kind, language, full content (up to 1,000,000 characters), token, visibility, owner, source conversation, version
data.synced: Server only; web, mobile and CLI read the same rows
data.retained_or_deleted: No expiry; removed by unpublish, takedown, or unpublish of the source conversation (apps/web/lib/services/published-artifact-service.ts:581)
Kept until the publication is deleted; no pruning found

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model takes part in publishing. Moderation and secret inspection are code checks on our servers (the moderation and outbound-content-inspection modules were called but their rules not read, so whether they call an outside service is unknown).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account to publish, list, change or unpublish. Reading a public page needs no account; workspace and invited pages need sign-in (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx:28-45).
access_and_usage.permissions: Only the owner (user_id) may update, restore or unpublish; row-level security enforces it. Public reads are by token. features.summary: The brief calls both a template registry and a design-system asset registry missing. On the web there is a smaller per-account version: built-in document and deck templates, saved templates, and saved brand kits (three colours, two fonts, a voice note). There are no shared company registries and no logos or font files.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a web user start a document or presentation from a built-in or saved template, save a document or deck as a template, and save brand kits that restyle decks. Items are stored per account in studio_library_items (apps/web/db/neon/0373_studio_library_items.sql:19, apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/templates/NewArtifactMenu.tsx:14).
purpose.why_it_exists: Migration 0373 says a document or deck could not be kept to start new ones from, and there was nowhere to keep a brand's colours, fonts and voice (apps/web/db/neon/0373_studio_library_items.sql:3-9).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users who write documents and decks and want repeatable starts or a consistent look.
problems_solved: Starting from a blank page every time.
Re-entering brand colours and fonts.
Keeping house style across decks.
use_cases: Start a 'Meeting notes' document from a built-in template.
Save a finished board deck as 'Board' and start the next one from it.
Create a brand with accent colour and serif headings and apply it to a deck.
Delete an old saved template.

Web artifact menu item 'Save as template' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:2441).
Brand kit dialog from a deck ('New brand') (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/library/LibraryDialogs.tsx:111; empty-state text at :276).
Other apps: not found in the code searched; unknown.
prerequisites: Web, signed in, and an open conversation (the menu returns nothing without a conversation id) (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/templates/NewArtifactMenu.tsx:58).
To save, a document or presentation artifact.
screens_and_controls: Dialog 'Save as template' with a name field and save button (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/library/LibraryDialogs.tsx:77).
Brand kit dialog with colours, fonts and a voice note, limited to the fields in the schema (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/studio-library.ts:25-32).
Library manager dialog titled via 'Templates and brands' listing saved items with delete (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/library/LibraryDialogs.tsx:250).
journey: Open the artifact panel in a chat.
Choose 'New from template' and pick a built-in or saved template; a new artifact opens with its content.
Edit it.
Choose 'Save as template', name it, save; toast says 'Saved as a template. Find it under New from template.'
In a deck, create a brand and apply it as a theme.
feedback_and_outputs: Toast success 'Saved as a template. Find it under New from template.' and error 'The template was not saved' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/library/LibraryDialogs.tsx:64-67).
Limit error becomes a conflict message when 100 items of a kind exist (apps/web/lib/services/studio-library-service.ts:73).
Brand themes appear beside the built-in deck themes (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:600-607).
settings: None besides the saved items. The 100 per kind limit is a code constant.

working: Built-in templates in a static client list: documents (blank, meeting notes, project brief, product requirements, weekly update, research summary, blog post, press release) and a presentation 'Pitch deck' (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/templates/artifact-templates.ts:17-206).

Saved items API: api:GET and api:POST /api/artifacts/library with kind filter, CSRF, rate limit, validation and a 100-per-kind limit; api: DELETE on /api/artifacts/library/[itemId] (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/library/route.ts:60-61, apps/web/lib/services/studio-library-service.ts:10).
Three kinds: document_template, deck_template, brand (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/studio-library.ts:9).

Template payload: title up to 200 characters and content up to 200,000 characters; brand payload: background, text and accent as #rrggbb, heading and body font from sans, serif, mono, and a voice up to 2,000 characters (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/studio-library.ts:15-32).
Rows are private to the account with forced row-level security (apps/web/db/neon/0373_studio_library_items.sql:30-38).
Brand to deck theme conversion (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/presentation/deck-themes.ts:112).
incomplete: Templates cover only documents and decks; no templates for html, react or other artifact kinds were found.
not_available: A shared or workspace-wide template or brand registry: none found; rows belong to one user.
Logos, font files or image assets: the brand schema has none (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/studio-library.ts:25-32).
Fonts beyond three families sans, serif, mono.
Use by generated html or react apps as design tokens: no route or injection found.
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: not found in the code searched; unknown.

features.summary: The server-side pieces behind AGI Workforce media and realtime voice: durable image and video generation jobs, mask checks, storage, AI-generated marking, speech-to-text, text-to-speech, and the live voice session broker. Several brief items (post-processing, transcoding, thumbnails, music, audio overview, consent store) have no code.

purpose.what_it_does: This page covers the 30 items of the area that no named feature owns. The built parts are all Cloud (our managed service) code in apps/web. Image generation and editing run as durable queued jobs against the OpenAI, Google and Stability image routes (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:315-420). Video runs as a provider task (Google, Runway, OpenRouter) that is polled and reconciled until done (apps/web/lib/services/video-provider-output-service.ts:300-310). Finished media is written to private storage and marked as AI-generated (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-executor.ts:766). Audio has three server routes: transcription (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:852), read-aloud speech (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:53) and a live voice session broker over WebRTC (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:555-565).
purpose.why_it_exists: Image and video work outlasts one HTTP request, costs money, and can fail at the provider. A durable job with one billing reservation means a closed tab does not abandon paid work and a retry does not charge twice (apps/web/db/neon/0226_durable_image_generation_jobs.sql:1-15). Voice needs server-held provider keys, per-plan limits and tool approval, so the browser never holds a long-lived key (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:126-148).
purpose.who_uses_it: People using AGI Workforce Cloud on web, mobile, desktop and CLI who generate images or video, dictate, hear replies read aloud or talk live. Engineers and testers maintaining the media and voice pipeline.
problems_solved: Image or video work lost when the person closes the tab (apps/web/db/neon/0226_durable_image_generation_jobs.sql:1-15).
Paying twice on retry: one idempotency key and one reservation per job (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:709-745).
Masks that do not match the source image are rejected with a plain message before any provider spend (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/edit-mask.ts:90-102).
Generated images carry a machine-readable AI-generated mark (apps/web/lib/server/generated-media-provenance.ts:34-37).
use_cases: A person asks for an image, closes the tab, and finds the finished image in their media library later.
A person draws a region on an image and asks for an edit; the server checks the mask is a PNG with transparency and the same size.
A person starts a video; the server polls the provider or accepts a signed provider callback until the file is stored.
A person talks to the assistant live; the server opens a provider session, bills in one-minute blocks and lets the voice run approved tools.

where_to_find_it: Web: voice call surface VoiceModeSurface in chat (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:38-60); image and video pages at /features/images and /features/video are marketing pages with tests (apps/web/app/features/images/page.test.tsx) [inferred].
Mobile: voice screen apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:326); live voice client apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/liveVoiceSession.ts.
Desktop: dictation in apps/desktop/electron/voiceDictation.ts; hook useVoiceTranscription posts to /api/voice/transcribe (apps/desktop/src/hooks/useVoiceTranscription.ts:650).
CLI: apps/cli/src/voice.rs (push-to-talk, three backends) and apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs (image generation) (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-9; apps/cli/src/cloud/image.rs:1,21).
VS Code: no voice, a webview has no microphone (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:328).

Chrome extension: voice side panel apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/voice.ts (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:329); it reads results from a browser speech recogniser (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/voice.ts:218-220).
prerequisites: A signed-in account; 18 and over, enforced by an adult-eligibility gate on image and live voice routes (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:30-40; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:184-193).
Cloud mode: managed-compute access, organization policy, spend limit and model policy gates pass (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:44-80).
Storage and provider keys configured on the server; otherwise availability is reported off (apps/web/lib/server/media-storage.ts:77-93) [inferred].
Live voice needs microphone permission and WebRTC support in the client (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:447-480).
screens_and_controls: Voice call surface labels: 'Share your camera', 'Stop sharing your camera', 'Stop the task', 'Try again', 'Continue in text', 'Upgrade', 'Tap to hear the assistant', 'Do not send that', 'Reconnecting, attempt', 'Continue that session' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:38-60).
Image mask drawing: RegionSelector component (apps/web/features/chat/components/RegionSelector.tsx:59).
Image result card: ImageGenerationCard (apps/web/features/chat/components/ImageGenerationCard.test.tsx names it).
journey: Image: the client posts a prompt to /api/media/image/generate with an Idempotency-Key; the server runs gates, reserves credit and returns 202 with a queued job (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:709-879).
The client polls /api/media/image/status; the job is driven by a background queue or by that poll (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-drive-queue.ts:33-55).
The finished images appear in the media library with an AI-generated header (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/managed-image-generation.ts:961-967).

Live voice: the browser creates a WebRTC offer, posts it to /api/voice/live/sessions, receives the provider's answer and talks (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:488-519; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:612-619).

The call is billed in one-minute blocks and can be extended or closed through the session routes (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:20-28; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/[sessionId]/extend/route.ts).
feedback_and_outputs: Image job statuses: queued then terminal; error text is categorised, for example 'The image provider did not respond before the request deadline. Please try again.' (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:104-125).
Mask errors: 'The mask must be a PNG image...', 'The mask needs transparency...', size mismatch text (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/edit-mask.ts:90-102).
Voice: call time, status line, reconnect banner, 'Weekly limit reached' and 'Monthly limit reached' messages (apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:261-262).
Speech route returns audio bytes, or 204 in one branch (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:244-255).
settings: Voice, language, pace and reasoning level are sent when a live session is created (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:149-166).
Memory switch for the call: memoryEnabled (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:154).
Read-aloud device voice is remembered in local browser storage (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:104-110).
Settings page for voice: apps/web/app/settings/voice/page.test.tsx and apps/web/features/settings/sections/VoiceSection.test.tsx exist.

working: Image generation and edit adapter for three image providers, with output structure checks for PNG, JPEG and WebP (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-generation-provider.ts:315-420, 795-830) (S97.01, S97.02).
Mask validation: PNG, alpha, same size as source (apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/edit-mask.ts:90-102) (S97.04).

Durable image jobs with attempts, cancellation, exhaustion and settlement; drive handed to a queue kind 'media-generation.image-attempt' (apps/web/lib/jobs/job-handlers.ts:363; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-drive-queue.ts:33-55) (S97.05).

Video reconciliation by workflow with 10-second poll, 2-minute provider submission grace, 5 failure limit (apps/web/lib/services/video-job-reconciliation-service.ts:47-51; apps/web/lib/workflows/video-generation-workflow.ts:27-35) (S97.06).

Completion by signed OpenRouter webhook plus status polling for image and video (apps/web/app/api/media/video/openrouter-webhook/route.ts:40-100; apps/web/app/api/media/video/status/route.ts:75; apps/web/app/api/media/image/status/route.ts) (S97.07).
Bounded video download: 256 MB cap, mp4, webm and quicktime types (apps/web/lib/services/video-provider-output-service.ts:20-22) (S97.08).
Private object storage and a media_assets catalogue (apps/web/lib/server/media-storage.ts:248; apps/web/db/neon/0036_media_assets.sql:9) (S97.09).

AI-generated provenance: claim built per image, embedded in the bytes, stored in asset metadata and sent as response headers (apps/web/lib/compliance/ai-act.ts:58-86; apps/web/app/api/media/image/lib/image-job-executor.ts:755-766; apps/web/lib/server/generated-media-provenance.ts:34-37) (S97.14).

Transcription: 25 MB cap, MIME and header checks, provider speech-to-text, metered with reserve and settle (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:398-460, 603-810); /api/voice/transcribe wraps it with a dictation kill switch (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:29) (S97.16).
Read-aloud: server speech route (4,000 characters max, metered) and a browser speech fallback in useTTS (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:48-53; apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:338-379) (S97.17).

Live voice broker: posts the browser's WebRTC offer to the provider with instructions, voice, tools and a restricted list of client events, and returns the answer (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:130-148, 555-565) (S97.18, S97.20).

established.statement: A server adapter turns an image prompt into generated images through a real provider and hands them to the media job.
A server adapter edits a source image, with an optional mask, through a provider edit endpoint.
Masks are validated and normalised (size, alpha) before they reach the provider.
Image and video generations run as durable queued jobs that a background worker drives to completion.
Provider-side jobs are polled and reconciled until terminal, with results persisted and failures settled.
Job completion is picked up by provider webhooks and by status polling.
Finished outputs are downloaded (bounded, typed) and written to private object storage catalogued per user.
Image outputs are post-processed server side (resize, format, upscale, background removal); videos are transcoded; thumbnails or contact sheets exist.
Generated media carries provenance metadata (AI-generated, provider, model, time, hash) stored with the asset and served with it.
A store records consent for using a person's likeness or voice.
A server transcription service turns uploaded audio into text, metered per request; a text-to-speech service serves read-aloud and voice replies.
A broker creates realtime voice sessions, with live audio over WebRTC; when the user speaks over a reply, playback stops and state stays consistent.
Voice turns can call product tools under the user's approval policy; a voice request can be handed to a durable task; sessions are persisted so they can be audited and resumed.
Mic affordance gives dictation or shows exactly why voice is unavailable; if live voice is not v1, the app says unavailable without broken controls.
Local inference on mobile and desktop is free of any paid subscription; every subscription capability connects to one AGI Subscription system.

acceptance_criteria: Posting an image prompt with an Idempotency-Key returns 202 and a queued job; repeating the same key does not create a second job or a second reservation.
A mask that is not PNG, has no alpha, or differs in size from the source gets a 422 with code invalid_mask_image and no provider call.
A signed webhook with a bad signature gets 401 and a malformed one 400; a good one returns 202 and nudges the video job.
A finished image is stored privately, its bytes carry the AI-generated mark, and the file route returns the generated-by headers.
An audio file over 25 MB gets 413 and an unsupported type 415.
Creating a live voice session for a Free-plan account without allowance, or over a spend cap, returns a refusal and no charge.
Closing a live session settles the reserved blocks and sets voice_sessions.status to closed.
A voice tool call that needs approval does not run until approved.
inferred: Local and own-key modes should not call these managed routes; image, video and live voice are Cloud only here [inferred from the managed-compute gates, apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:44-60].
Interruption handling should be tested on real calls because the code does not show it [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add server post-processing (thumbnail first) so the library does not serve full-size originals as previews.
[proposed] Mark speech output as AI-generated and fix the stale audio line in the compliance table.
[proposed] Wire onVisualFrame to a real frame sender or remove the camera control from the surface.

steps.what_happens: Client posts an image prompt; server checks CSRF, rate limit, sign-in, age gate, managed-compute, organization policy and spend limit.
Server validates the source and mask, reserves credit under an idempotency key and writes a queued image job.
A queue entry or the client status poll drives the attempt; the provider is called once per attempt.
The image provider generates or edits the image.
Server hashes bytes, builds a provenance claim, embeds it, stores the object and settles the reservation.
Video task is created at the provider; a workflow polls every few seconds or a signed webhook nudges it; output is downloaded and stored.
Audio upload is checked and sent to the transcription provider; the bytes are dropped after, nothing stores them.

Browser creates a WebRTC offer; server forwards it to the live voice provider with instructions and tools, records a voice_sessions row, returns the answer; audio then flows browser to provider directly.
Voice tool calls come back to our server for approval-checked execution.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The live voice, speech and transcription models are chosen by routing slots, not by the person (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:177-183; apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:102). Speech and transcription currently require OpenAI models (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:103; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:500). Image providers are OpenAI, Google and Stability; video providers are Google, Runway and OpenRouter. A backend model is chosen by plan for live voice tool work (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:540-560).

access_and_usage.account: Signed-in account on all routes; image and live voice also need the adult-eligibility gate (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:30-40; apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:184-193). Transcription also accepts an API key with inference:write scope (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:297).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace policy, web-domain policy for voice fetch, tool approval policy for voice tools (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:62-70, 118-125). Microphone permission on the client.
access_and_usage.subscription: Image routes check the canUseImages capability (apps/web/app/api/media/image/generate/route.ts:100-110) and managed compute access. Live voice checks entitlements and tier unit quota (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:50-58). Free plans get a monthly voice-seconds allowance from the tier policy (apps/web/lib/voice/free-voice-allowance.ts:47-52).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Image: reservation per job, rate limit 'image-generation'. Transcription: reserve and settle by tokens or duration, 25 MB cap, rate limit 'audio-transcription'. Speech: 4,000 characters, rate limit 'voice-speech'. Live voice: one-minute billing blocks and a 10-minute lease (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-billing.ts:20-28). Values are in code constants; plan numbers come from the tier policy.
access_and_usage.flags: Dictation kill switch DICTATION_CAPABILITY (apps/web/lib/feature-flags/kill-switches.ts:33); canUseImages capability; video provider release policy (apps/web/lib/server/video-provider-release-policy.ts); OPENROUTER_WEBHOOK_SECRET env var name for the webhook (apps/web/app/api/media/video/openrouter-webhook/route.ts:41).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Speech and transcription slots must resolve to live OpenAI models or the route throws or refuses (apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:103; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:500). Live voice slot must resolve to a live managed provider (apps/web/app/api/voice/live/sessions/route.ts:177-183).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: A privacy setting that keeps content away from providers that may train blocks transcription, speech and live voice with a 403 (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:506-516; apps/web/app/api/voice/speech/route.ts:106-111). Only Runway has a verified video cancel operation (apps/web/lib/services/video-provider-output-service.ts:314). Some regions are blocked on transcription with 451 (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:276-285).
access_and_usage.local_mode: These server routes are Cloud only. In Local mode no image, video or live voice route is used. Browser speech is a no-server fallback for read-aloud (apps/web/lib/hooks/useTTS.ts:338-379); mobile read-aloud uses the device speech engine (apps/mobile/src/features/voice/services/tts.ts:1); the CLI can use a local whisper binary (apps/cli/src/voice.rs:1-9). Whether these need sign-in is unknown.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person on a paid plan link an outside service (mail, files, tickets) to AGI Workforce through that service's own sign-in page. The server keeps the grant. In code today only 13 services are released, and a second account of the same service still overwrites the first.

purpose.what_it_does: A server-side registry lists every connector with its sign-in scheme, risk class and release state. The person starts a sign-in, approves the outside service's consent screen, and returns to the app. The server checks the one-time state value, exchanges the code, and stores an encrypted grant. A database schema also exists to hold several accounts per service, each with a label, a scope (personal, work, service) and one default.
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant can only act in a person's mail, files or tickets with that person's own consent. The server holds the grant so every app uses one sign-in instead of each app keeping its own token (S98.01, S98.02, S98.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in person on a plan that includes connectors, on the web app (Settings, Connectors). Mobile, CLI, Desktop and VS Code are clients of the same server routes (see user_experience).
problems_solved: One sign-in per service instead of pasting keys into each app.
The consent scope is capped per service, so a connector cannot quietly ask for more than reviewed.
A work mailbox and a personal mailbox could be kept apart (schema only today; the connect flow does not create a second account).
use_cases: Connect a project-tracker service so the assistant can read tickets in chat.
Reconnect a service after its authorization expired.
See which account a connector is signed in as (the account label).
Link a work and a personal account of one service (not working end to end today; see gaps).

journey: 1. Open Settings, Connectors and pick a service in the directory.

2. Choose Connect. The web calls GET /api/connectors/oauth/start with the connector id; the server checks release, workspace access and policy, then returns an authorize URL (oauth/start/route.ts:222-300).
3. The browser goes to the outside service and the person approves consent.
4. The service redirects to /api/connectors/oauth/callback with state and code.
5. The server validates state, consumes the pending record, checks the policy again, exchanges the code and stores the encrypted grant (finish-authorization.ts:43-224).
6. The person is sent back to the return path (default /connectors) with a connector id and a status such as 'connected' (callback/route.ts:32-41, 79).
7. Mobile: the app opens the sign-in in an in-app browser session and posts state and code to /api/connectors/oauth/complete (apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:272-303; callback/route.ts:43-52).
feedback_and_outputs: Redirect status codes: connected, denied, failed, invalid_state, unavailable, reauthorize, registration_rejected (finish-authorization.ts:29-35, 65-80).
Start statuses: not_configured, policy_blocked, scope_reconsent, credential, open, unavailable, error (oauth/start/route.ts:67-76).

When a wider scope set is requested than a stored grant holds, the start response carries status scope_reconsent and the added scopes; the flow still proceeds to the consent screen (oauth/start/route.ts:318-323, 381-386).
An audit event 'connector_added' is recorded on success (finish-authorization.ts:128-139, 211-222).
settings: CONNECTOR_OAUTH_PROVIDERS_JSON, CONNECTOR_OAUTH_<ID>_CLIENT_ID and _CLIENT_SECRET, CONNECTOR_OAUTH_REDIRECT_BASE_URL, CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (names only) (apps/web/.env.example:405-420; docs/development/connectors-setup.md).
Workspace connector policy and the 'canUseConnectors' kill switch (connector-capability.ts:31-42).

working: Registry of about 90 connector records with auth scheme, risk class, release state and surfaces (apps/web/lib/connectors/catalog.ts:161-275).
OAuth start with PKCE and a random 64-hex state, pending record with a 600-second life (pkce.ts:12-26; oauth-store.ts:11, 52).
Callback rejects a missing or malformed state with status invalid_state and returns to /connectors (callback/route.ts:66-69).
Callback hands an app-originated state to the mobile app instead of processing it in the browser (callback/route.ts:43-52).
Code exchange and grant storage happen inside one transaction that checks the pending authorization was consumed (oauth-store.ts:254-277).
Scope ceilings per connector drop requested scopes that are not on the reviewed list (oauth-scope-allowlist.ts:24-40; scopes-escalation.ts:23-41).

Schema for several accounts per connector exists: account_key, account_label, account_scope (personal, work, service), is_default, one live default per connector (db/neon/0253_connector_accounts.sql:30-67).
A scoped read only returns the named account; an unscoped read returns the default first (oauth-store.ts:492-514).
Account label is taken from the id token claims email, preferred_username or upn when present (lib/connectors/accounts.ts:13-31).
GET /api/connectors/{connectorId}/accounts lists accounts (accounts/route.ts:30-40).
incomplete: Multi-account connect is not wired. createPendingAuthorization is called without an account key from the start route and from MCP discovery (oauth/start/route.ts:353-370; mcp-discovery.ts:242), and the callback stores the grant with only an account label, so the key falls back to 'default' and a second sign-in to the same service overwrites the first (finish-authorization.ts:171-185; oauth-store.ts:294-320, normalizeConnectorAccountKey in accounts.ts:5-9). The brief marks S98.11 as done; the code does not support that.

The 'unqualified call uses the default, a scoped call never resolves to another account' rule is implemented in the store read (oauth-store.ts:492-514), but resolveConnectorAccessToken takes no account argument and always reads the unscoped default (oauth-access.ts:84-97), so no caller can scope a call.
grantRequiresReconsent exists but has no non-test caller; the start route uses scopeEscalation directly and only reports scope_reconsent (scopes-escalation.ts:48-55; oauth/start/route.ts:318-323).
No set-default route or control was found.

established.statement: A server-side registry defines every connector: id, auth scheme, endpoint, risk class and release state (S98.01).
A store keeps each user's connected accounts and grants per connector (S98.02).
The OAuth callback validates state, exchanges the code and stores the grant (S98.03).
Requested scopes are capped per provider and a wider scope set forces fresh consent (S98.06).
When several accounts exist for a connector, the runtime selects the right one per task (S98.11).
A request scoped to a personal account must never resolve to a work account.
Setup readiness is distinct from authorization; never mark a provider connected from a redirect alone. Connectors stay at coming_soon except the exact released ids.

acceptance_criteria: A callback with no state or a state that is not 64 hex characters redirects to /connectors with status invalid_state and stores nothing.
A state that was already used, expired (600 s) or belongs to another user returns invalid_state.
A released connector with valid consent ends with status connected and one encrypted grant row; the account label shows in 'Connected account'.
A connector id not in the released list returns status unavailable and no code is exchanged.
A Free-plan account is refused with plan_upgrade_required before any credential is exchanged.
Requested scopes outside the reviewed ceiling are dropped from the authorize URL.
Connecting a second account of the same service keeps both (currently fails: see gaps).
Cancelling at the consent screen returns status denied.
inferred: [inferred] The mobile in-app flow must produce the same stored result as the browser flow, since /oauth/complete reuses finishConnectorAuthorization.
[inferred] Account selection per task needs the model or the person to name an account; the contract has no such argument today.
proposed: [proposed] Pass accountKey and accountScope from the start route into createPendingAuthorization and from the pending record into the upsert, with a stable key such as the provider account id.
[proposed] Add an accountKey option to resolveConnectorAccessToken and the tool executor, plus a set-default route and control.
[proposed] Call grantRequiresReconsent where a stored grant is used, or delete it.

steps.what_happens: Person chooses Connect in the directory; the app calls the start route.
Server checks release, region, token storage, workspace access and connector policy (email, plan, kill switch, org policy).
Server filters scopes against the ceiling, makes PKCE and state, and stores a pending authorization (10 minutes).
Person approves on the outside service's consent page.
Outside service redirects to the callback; server validates state, consumes the pending record, re-checks release and policy.
Server exchanges the code at the service's token endpoint and writes the grant with encrypted tokens.
Server records a connector_added audit event and redirects with status connected.

features.summary: Keeps connector sign-ins working after the first connect. Tokens are sealed in the database, refreshed once when several requests need the same expiring token, and reported as needing reconnect when the outside service refuses them. Health and a call ceiling come from a log of recent connector calls.

purpose.what_it_does: Encrypts access and refresh tokens at rest and opens them only when a call needs them. Refreshes a token that is about to expire, using a database row lock and an in-process share so concurrent requests refresh once. Records every connector call and derives a health state, a circuit that pauses a failing connector, and a per-minute call ceiling.
purpose.why_it_exists: Tokens are secrets and they expire. Without a coordinator, two requests refresh at once and one loses its token. Without health, a person cannot tell a dead connector from a slow one (S98.04, S98.05, S98.10).
purpose.who_uses_it: The platform for every connector call; people see its results as 'Needs reconnecting', a Reconnect notice or a paused-connector message.
problems_solved: Plain-text tokens in the database.
Double refresh races that revoke a still-good grant.
A silent dead connector with no explanation.
use_cases: A mailbox token expires overnight; the next chat request refreshes it without the person noticing.
The vendor revokes access; the person gets a 'Reconnect <name>' notification.
A connector fails three calls in a row; further calls are paused with a message that names the wait.
A person opens the connectors list and sees which connectors are not responding.

where_to_find_it: Web: 'Needs reconnecting' under 'Connected account' (ConnectorAccountSummary.tsx:30); notification titled 'Reconnect <name>' targeting Settings, Connectors (oauth-access.ts:39-54); outcome announcer action label 'Reconnect' (features/connectors/components/ConnectorOutcomeAnnouncer.tsx:33).
CLI: 'agi connectors' shows 'needs reconnecting: open <url>' or 'connected since <date>, <health>' (apps/cli/src/cloud/connectors.rs:176-205).
Mobile: connect card in chat and connector detail screen (labels unknown).
Health data: GET /api/connectors/health (app/api/connectors/health/route.ts:17-32) and per-connector 'health' in GET /api/connectors (route.ts:333-360).
prerequisites: A connected connector (F098-01).
CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY set; without it connect is refused (custom-connector-crypto.ts:31-41; oauth/start/route.ts:222-224).
screens_and_controls: No dedicated health screen was found; health shows as a state on the connector entry (health values: connected, needs-reauthorization, not-responding, connectable, not-configured, unsupported-here; packages/client/client-runtime/src/connectors/policy.ts:134-145).
Reconnect link or button starts F098-01 again.
journey: 1. Person uses a connector in chat.
2. The server reads the grant and decrypts the token (oauth-access.ts:95-108).
3. If it expires within 60 seconds, one refresh runs under a row lock (oauth-access.ts:35, 116-121, 173-199).
4. On success the new tokens are saved and the call goes ahead.
5. If refresh is refused, the grant is revoked, the person is notified, and tools answer 'reauthorization required' (oauth-access.ts:197, 258-263).
6. The person reconnects from Settings or the link.
feedback_and_outputs: Notification 'Reconnect <name>': 'The <name> authorization expired or was revoked, so its tools stop working until you connect it again.' (oauth-access.ts:46-52).
Paused message: '<name> failed its last N calls, so calls to it are paused for Ns. Nothing was sent.' (health.ts:242).
Rate message: 'has taken N calls in the last minute, which is this account's ceiling of 60...' (health.ts:253).
Unreachable message from connectorUnreachableMessage (oauth-access.ts:464).
settings: CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (name only).

Constants: expiry skew 60 s, health window 1 hour, call ceiling 60 per 60 s, failure streak 3, recency 30 min, backoff 2 s doubling to 5 min (oauth-access.ts:35; health.ts:33-38; connector-call-log-service.ts:37-38).

working: Token sealing with a purpose bound into the authentication tag (custom-connector-crypto.ts:47-58; oauth-store.ts:294-345).

Decryption failure on read throws ConnectorGrantDecryptionError, which access resolution turns into reauthorization-required with reason 'undecryptable' (oauth-store.ts:441-446, 516-545; oauth-access.ts:98-105).
One refresh per user, connector and account key inside a process (oauth-access.ts:136-150), plus a database 'for update' row lock across processes (oauth-store.ts:461-490).
A second waiter that finds a fresh token after the lock returns it without refreshing (oauth-access.ts:210-212).
A lock wait that is cut returns status 'unreachable' (retry later), not reauthorization (oauth-access.ts:185-191; oauth-store.ts:448-452, 470-480).
Dead refresh (invalid grant), no refresh token, or rejected discovered grant revokes the row and sends a once-a-day-deduplicated notification (oauth-access.ts:215, 229, 258-263, 39-54).
Transient failures (5xx, 408, 429, network) give 'unreachable' and keep the grant (oauth-access.ts:166-171, 264-267).
Health summary: responding, degraded (failure ratio above 0.25), not-responding (3 straight failures within 30 minutes), unknown with no calls (health.ts:42, 128-135).
Circuit: closed, open, half-open with exponential wait (health.ts:74-78, 165-174); gate refuses a call when open or at 60 calls a minute (health.ts:227-264).
'blocked' calls (refused by this platform) never count against the provider (health.ts:84-86).
Calls are logged to table connector_call_events and metered (health.ts:280-298; db/neon/0223_connector_call_events.sql).
incomplete: The brief describes states 'healthy, needs reauth, failing'; code has two systems: call-log health (responding, degraded, not-responding, unknown) and the list health that adds needs-reauthorization from grant state (health.ts:42; app/api/connectors/route.ts:341-359). needsReauthorization in the list is true only when there is no refresh token and the access token has expired (oauth-store.ts:575-583).
The in-process refresh share is per server instance; cross-instance safety relies on the row lock [inferred from oauth-access.ts:37 and oauth-store.ts:461].
Health is computed from the last 100 log rows within an hour (health.ts:40, 300-310).
disconnected_or_disabled: Nothing probes a connector on its own; health only changes when calls are made (health.ts:28-32).
not_available: Local mode and apps' own token storage: none; mobile, CLI and VS Code do not hold connector tokens (they call the server).

established.statement: Connector tokens and credentials are stored encrypted and decrypted only for use (S98.04).
A coordinator refreshes expiring tokens once, even when several requests need the token at the same time (S98.05).
A health monitor tracks each connection's state (healthy, needs reauth, failing) (S98.10).
Security behaviour fails closed; a secret is never committed.

acceptance_criteria: A stored token is never readable as plain text in connector_oauth_grants.
Ten concurrent requests for an expired token cause one call to the token endpoint.
A refresh that the vendor rejects as an invalid grant revokes the grant and creates one notification per connector per day.
A 503 from the token endpoint leaves the grant intact and returns 'unreachable'.
After three failed calls within 30 minutes the connector reports not-responding and the next call is refused with the paused message.
The 61st call in one minute to one connector is refused with the ceiling message.
A grant that cannot be decrypted asks for reconnect instead of crashing.
inferred: [inferred] Because key rotation uses a key ring, an old ciphertext must still open after a new key is added (loadKeyRing, envelope.ts:296).
[inferred] The hourly health window means a quiet connector reads 'unknown', not 'healthy'.
proposed: [proposed] Align the brief's three states with the code's names, or expose one combined state.
[proposed] Add a scheduled probe so a dead connector is found before a person asks.

steps.what_happens: A tool call asks for an access token for a user and connector.
Server reads the grant row and decrypts tokens with the key ring.
If the access token expires within 60 s, one refresh starts under a row lock in a transaction.
The vendor's token endpoint answers; new tokens are sealed and saved, or the grant is revoked.
The call outcome is logged to connector_call_events and checked against the circuit and ceiling for later calls.
