execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model is involved. The outside service's token endpoint is called for refresh.

access_and_usage.account: Runs for the signed-in user who owns the grant; all queries are by user id.
access_and_usage.permissions: Call log table uses row-level security by user (0223 migration); org call data is stored with an optional organization id.
access_and_usage.subscription: None found in the code for refresh and health themselves; the plan gate applies when a connector is used (see F098-03).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Per-connector ceiling 60 calls per 60 s, circuit after 3 failures, backoff 2 s to 5 min (health.ts:33-38). Each non-blocked call is also recorded as infrastructure cost (health.ts:290-297, recordConnectorCall in lib/services/infrastructure-cost).
access_and_usage.flags: None specific. The key ring env name is CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Refresh requires the vendor's token endpoint to accept the stored refresh token; behaviour differs per vendor (invalid_grant versus transient).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not applicable. These tokens live on our servers; local inference does not use them.

features.summary: Lets the assistant use a connected service from a chat turn. The server builds the tool list for the signed-in person, applies login, plan, policy and approval rules, calls the service, and logs the outcome. A built-in Microsoft 365 adapter exists but is off: those ids are not released and need vendor app settings.

purpose.what_it_does: For each chat turn the server lists the tools of the connectors the person has connected (remote MCP servers, a GitHub adapter, bank accounts, and a Microsoft Graph adapter for Outlook, OneDrive, SharePoint and Teams). It runs a call with the person's own token, asks for approval where the rules say so, and returns the result to the model. A separate POST route proxies MCP operations (call tool, read resource, get prompt, tasks) for the web UI.
purpose.why_it_exists: The assistant must act inside services where the person already works, with that person's permissions, under server-held credentials and rules (S98.07, S98.14).
purpose.who_uses_it: A person on a paid plan chatting on the web (and Desktop, which shows the hosted web app). Mobile, CLI and VS Code reach the same server chat; their own connector tool handling beyond reconnect notices is unverified.
problems_solved: Reading mail or files without copy and paste.
Sending or creating items only after approval.
One gateway so tokens never reach a browser or device.
use_cases: 'Summarize unread mail from my manager' using the mail adapter.
'List my events for tomorrow'.
'Read this document from my drive as text'.
Approve or deny a send_mail request before it leaves.

where_to_find_it: Web chat: connector tools are used by the assistant during a turn once a connector is connected and released; the composer plus menu lists connector options (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ComposerPlusMenu.tsx imports hasReleasedConnectors).

Connector tool permissions (deny / ask / allow per tool) are read by loadConnectorToolPermissions (app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/connector-tool-permissions.ts); the settings control for them is not read.

CLI: reconnect notices from tool results (apps/cli/src/cloud/connectors.rs:16-85).
VS Code: 'Code: Show Connectors' view and 'Manage connectors on web' (package.json:723-734; surfaces/index.ts:245-249).
prerequisites: Connector connected and released (F098-01).
Paid plan with connectors capability; kill switch open; workspace policy allows the connector (connector-capability.ts:44-84).

For the Microsoft adapter: the owner registers an Entra app and sets client ID and secret for outlook, onedrive, sharepoint and teams (apps/web/.env.example:405-417; docs/development/connectors-setup.md).
screens_and_controls: Chat approval prompt for tools that need approval.
Tool permission levels deny, ask, allow per connector tool (mcp/route.ts:49-59).
journey: 1. Person asks for a task that needs a connected service.
2. The server loads the tool list for that person (user-connector-tools.ts:2437-2600).
3. The model picks a tool; the server checks release, circuit and ceiling, and screens outgoing content (user-connector-tools.ts:2757-2795).
4. For send or create tools, the person approves when asked (tool-metadata.ts:827-846).
5. The server gets a token (refresh if needed), calls the service, and returns text to the model.
6. The model answers; the outcome is logged.
feedback_and_outputs: Tool results appear in the reply; blocked or failed calls return a plain message such as 'Nothing was sent.'
Authorization-required result with a reconnect link when the grant is missing or expired (microsoft-graph.ts:789-808).
For tools that return an interactive app, a card is added (see F098-04).
settings: Per-tool permission level (deny, ask, allow).
Workspace connector policy.
CONNECTOR_OAUTH_OUTLOOK_CLIENT_ID and _CLIENT_SECRET etc. (names only) for the Microsoft adapter.

working: Gateway route POST /api/connectors/{connectorId}/mcp: CSRF check, rate limit, body size limit, user scope, permission level, approval gate for non-allow or critical tools, then call, with audit event data_accessed or tool_executed (app/api/connectors/[connectorId]/mcp/route.ts:25-146).
A call needing approval returns approvalRequired and runs only when the body carries approved: true (mcp/route.ts:57-59).
Read operations: readResource, getPrompt, taskGet; task operations check the task was bound to this user (mcp/route.ts:78-121).
Tool catalog per user, including first-party adapters (user-connector-tools.ts:2437-2600).
Executor checks release, then the circuit and ceiling gate, then screens outgoing content before the call, and logs each outcome (user-connector-tools.ts:2737-2800).

Microsoft Graph adapter code: Outlook search_mail, read_mail, list_events, send_mail, create_event; OneDrive search_files, read_file; SharePoint search_sites, search_files, read_file; Teams list_chats, read_chat_messages, list_teams, list_channels (catalog.ts:175-190, 257-261; microsoft-graph.ts:25, 297-834).
send_mail and create_event are classed external_send, not reversible, at most once (tool-metadata.ts:827-846); the tool text says the person approves every send (microsoft-graph.ts:410, 448).
Graph errors: 401 gives authorization expired, 403 gives insufficient scope, unreachable gives a try-again message (microsoft-graph.ts:795-816).
incomplete: Microsoft adapter is marked partial in the brief; saving Outlook drafts needs a broader scope that is not admitted (area brief S98.07 unfinished note).
Which approval prompt the chat shows for external_send under each policy was not read; the classification exists but the 'always asks under every policy' claim is from the brief only.
The executor and the tool list always use the default grant; no account choice (oauth-access.ts:84-97).
disconnected_or_disabled: All of this is off by release state: outlook, onedrive, sharepoint, teams, gmail, slack, github and others are not in the 13 released ids (connector-release.ts:14-34; user-connector-tools.ts:2083, 2492, 2537).

Free plan: tools withheld (connector-capability.ts:44-67).
not_available: Local mode: none for cloud connectors. Device-local connectors (filesystem, terminal, browser automation, screen vision, local model runtime) are run by the desktop runtime, not this gateway (catalog.ts:125-137).
Private-network bridge is missing (S98.15).
Connector search and index worker is missing (S98.08).

established.statement: Provider-specific adapters implement connector behaviour for each supported provider (S98.07, status partial).
A server-side gateway proxies MCP operations for a user, applying auth and permissions (S98.14).
send_mail and create_event are external sends and ask under every policy.
Connector release is selective: the full-launch switch stays coming_soon.
Web search, memory, MCP and similar features are route or harness features, not intrinsic model capabilities.

acceptance_criteria: A POST to the gateway without a CSRF token is refused.
A tool set to deny returns forbidden.
A tool that needs approval returns approvalRequired and does not call the service until approved:true is sent.
A critical-risk tool asks even when its level is allow.
send_mail is never executed without an approval step.
A Free account sees no connector tools.
An expired grant returns an authorization-required result with a reconnect path, not a crash.
Each executed call writes a connector_call_events row.
inferred: [inferred] The gateway route is used by the interactive-app card (F098-04) and Settings catalog views, not by the model loop, which uses the executor.
[inferred] Any model provider can use connector tools because the tool loop is server side.
proposed: [proposed] Add one test that proves approval for external_send under every policy mode.
[proposed] Pass the chosen account into the executor once multi-account works.

steps.what_happens: Chat turn starts; server checks release, plan tier and kill switch for connectors.
Server builds the tool list from connected grants and first-party adapters.
Model (through the chosen provider route) asks for a tool call.
Executor checks release, circuit and ceiling, then screens the arguments for secrets.
Approval is requested for non-allow or critical tools; with approval the call runs.
Server resolves the token (refresh if needed) and calls the vendor API or MCP server.
Outcome logged and metered; text result returned to the model; audit event written on the gateway route.

features.summary: Talks to MCP servers: lists their tools, resources and prompts and calls tools. The web server uses a TypeScript client; the CLI and Tauri desktop use a Rust crate. When a tool returns an interactive app, the web chat shows it in a sandboxed card; mobile shows plain text.

purpose.what_it_does: Connects to any MCP server (remote over HTTP or SSE, or local over stdio in the CLI and Tauri desktop), negotiates the protocol revision, lists capabilities and calls tools. In web chat, a tool that returns an app resource is shown as a card in a separate sandbox origin, and calls from the app go back through the gateway.
purpose.why_it_exists: MCP is the shared way to add tools and rich results from outside vendors without custom code per vendor (S98.12, S98.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who add an MCP server or custom connector, and anyone whose connector returns an interactive result.
problems_solved: One client for many servers.
Safe display of third-party interactive content.
Honest fallback to plain text when no safe sandbox exists.
use_cases: Add a vendor's MCP server by URL from the connectors page.
Use a CLI-configured stdio MCP server in a terminal session.
See a chart or form from a tool as a card in chat.
Click inside the card and approve a follow-up tool call.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, Connectors, add by URL or from the directory; public /connectors/mcp-directory page 'Browse the MCP directory' (app/connectors/page.tsx:33; app/connectors/mcp-directory).
Web chat: card titled '<tool name> interactive result', text 'Loading MCP App…', buttons 'Allow once' and 'Deny' (McpAppCard.tsx:147-236, 440).
Mobile: plain result text; messages 'This MCP App result expired or is unavailable.' and 'The tool returned no text to show.' (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:12-13).
CLI: 'agi mcp add/list/remove' style commands (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:5112-5388) [command names not fully read].
Desktop (Tauri): commands mcp_list_servers, mcp_connect_server, mcp_call_tool (apps/desktop/src-tauri/src/sys/commands/mcp.rs:781-999). The public Electron Desktop shows the hosted web app.
VS Code and Chrome: unknown.
prerequisites: For web remote servers: connector released, paid plan, connect done (F098-01, F098-03).
For apps: NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN set to an https origin different from the app origin in production (McpAppCard.tsx:111-118; lib/validate-env.ts:461-490).
CLI and Tauri: a stdio command or URL configured locally.
screens_and_controls: Add-by-URL form with optional bearer token or OAuth client ID and secret (docs/development/connectors-setup.md).
Card controls: 'Allow once' and 'Deny' for tool calls and for device permissions (camera, microphone, location, clipboard) the app asks for (McpAppCard.tsx:54-80, 196-236).
journey: 1. Person adds a server or has one connected.
2. Server connects, negotiates, and lists tools, resources, prompts (packages/tools/mcp/src/connect.ts:655-760).
3. A tool call returns a result with an app resource; the server saves the payload and the chat shows a card (tool-loop.ts:2968-3000).
4. The browser fetches the payload, reads the app HTML through the gateway, and loads it in a sandbox frame on the dedicated origin (McpAppCard.tsx:225-255).
5. Calls from the app go to the gateway; non-allowed tools ask first (McpAppCard.tsx:283-300).
6. If anything is unsafe or missing, the plain tool result is shown with a reason.
feedback_and_outputs: 'Loading MCP App…' while loading.
"This app can't be displayed here, so the tool's result is shown instead." when no separate sandbox origin exists (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/mcp-app.ts:3-4).
"This app's content is too large to display." over 2 MB (mcp-app.ts:1-2).
Device ask sentence: 'This app wants to use your camera ...' (McpAppCard.tsx:74-80).
settings: NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN (name only; .env.example:868).
Per-tool permissions (F098-03).
CLI MCP server config files and OAuth store (apps/cli/src/mcp/).

working: Rust client: list_tools, list_resources, list_resource_templates, read_resource, call_tool (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/client.rs:151-223); transports stdio, HTTP, SSE (client.rs transport kinds at 230-262; transport/ folder).
Rust discovery: probes server/discover, classifies modern, legacy or silent servers and reports an unsupported revision (client.rs:288-390).
Rust OAuth flow helpers: protected-resource and authorization-server discovery, dynamic registration, PKCE, refresh (crates/agiworkforce-mcp/src/oauth/flow.rs:147-672).
Rust response cache for list calls (cache.rs:16 lists prompts/list among cached methods).

TypeScript client used by the web server lists tools, resources, resource templates and prompts with item limits and error capture, and exposes callTool, readResource, getPrompt, and tasks (packages/tools/mcp/src/connect.ts:395-430, 655-760, 815-895).
Web card: separate sandbox origin required in production, 2 MB cap, CSP from the app's metadata, device-permission prompts, approval for tool calls (McpAppCard.tsx:54-144, 283-300).
Payload saved for 30 days, up to 2 MB, in table mcp_app_payloads; payload route returns it to its owner (mcp-state-store.ts:10-60; app/api/mcp-apps/payload/[payloadId]/route.ts).
incomplete: The Rust client has no prompts/list or prompts/get method; prompts are only referenced in cache keys and input-required rules (client.rs:33; cache.rs:16, 241). The brief says the client lists prompts (S98.12). The web's TypeScript client does list and get prompts (connect.ts:733, 889).

Apps render only on web chat. Mobile shows result text (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:1-40). Desktop (Tauri), VS Code and Chrome handling of app cards: unknown; a search found no card code there.
The brief cites tool-loop.ts:2147 for the host bridge; the card is built near tool-loop.ts:2968-3000 (stale reference).
disconnected_or_disabled: Interactive apps are off in production without a dedicated sandbox origin (McpAppCard.tsx:111-118).
Web connectors are off except released ids (F098-01).
not_available: Local mode for remote servers: only stdio servers on the device are local; HTTP servers need the network.
Private-network reach from cloud (S98.15 missing).

established.statement: An MCP client runtime connects to servers and lists and calls their tools, resources and prompts (S98.12).
A host bridge renders MCP App resources in a sandbox and relays calls between widget and server (S98.16).
Interactive apps load in a separate sandbox origin; production refuses a same-origin sandbox.
Rust protocol types flow one way into TypeScript; a Rust client and a TypeScript client both exist.

acceptance_criteria: Connecting to a test server lists its tools, resources and prompts (web) or tools and resources (Rust).
A server that publishes only a newer unsupported revision gives a clear 'unsupported revision' error.
With no dedicated sandbox origin in a production build, the card shows the plain result and the explanatory sentence.
An app resource over 2 MB shows the too-large sentence.
An app asking for camera shows the device sentence and no access until 'Allow once'.
A tool call from the app for a non-allowed tool asks before running.
The payload route refuses another user's payload id.
inferred: [inferred] Mobile cannot host the sandbox, so plain text is the product choice there.
[inferred] A prompts method on the Rust client would be needed for CLI parity with web.
proposed: [proposed] Add list_prompts and get_prompt to the Rust client or change the brief wording.
[proposed] Decide card behaviour for Tauri desktop, VS Code and Chrome.

steps.what_happens: Server (web) or process (CLI, Tauri) connects to the MCP server and negotiates the protocol revision.
Client lists tools, resources, prompts (TypeScript) or tools and resources (Rust).
A tool call returns a result that names an app resource; the web server saves the payload and emits a card.
The browser loads the payload, reads the resource via the gateway, and opens the sandbox frame on another origin.
Calls from the app go through the gateway with approval; the host relays results to the frame.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: No model is needed to connect or list. A model decides to call tools through the normal tool loop. Remote MCP servers are outside services; their content is untrusted and is fenced or sanitized (connect.ts sanitizeCatalogText; lib/connectors/mcp-untrusted-text.ts).

access_and_usage.subscription: Web remote servers: paid plan with the connectors capability (F098-03). Local stdio: none found in the code read.
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Catalog item limits per capability (connect.ts CATALOG_ITEM_LIMITS), 2 MB app cap, request payload cap, timeouts (config.rs McpTimeouts).
access_and_usage.flags: NEXT_PUBLIC_MCP_APP_SANDBOX_ORIGIN; release gate for web connectors.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not model dependent for connection; tool use depends on the model route's tool support [inferred].
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Server must speak a supported MCP revision; some need pre-registered OAuth clients (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Local stdio MCP servers run on the device in the CLI and Tauri desktop. Remote servers in Local mode: whether the product routes them is not verified. Web card requires a browser and our server gateway.

features.summary: Runs the CLI as an MCP server on standard input and output, so another AI client can list and call the CLI's local file, search, shell, git and language-server tools. It lists a fixed set of tools, refuses any tool not listed, and needs no sign-in or model.

purpose.what_it_does: 'agi mcp-server' reads one JSON line at a time, answers initialize, ping, server/discover, tools/list and tools/call, and runs each call through the CLI's normal tool executor with approval prompts refused.

features.summary: Accepts signed events from outside services and turns them into work. A generic connector endpoint checks a per-trigger signature. A separate GitHub endpoint checks GitHub's signature, ignores duplicate deliveries, and can start an automatic pull request review. Slack, Gmail and Calendar have their own receivers.

purpose.what_it_does: POST /api/webhooks/connectors/{triggerId} verifies an x-agi-signature over the timestamp and body, then queues the event for the trigger that owns that secret. POST /api/github/webhook verifies x-hub-signature-256, records the delivery id once, and routes events to event triggers, an automatic review, or a mention-driven task.
purpose.why_it_exists: Lets outside systems start automations without polling, and lets the GitHub App review pull requests (S98.09).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who create an event trigger (web: Schedules, Triggers panel) and owners who install the GitHub App.
problems_solved: Polling delays.
Forged requests: bad signatures get 401.
Repeat deliveries: duplicates are acknowledged without reprocessing (GitHub).
use_cases: A build system posts a signed event that starts an agent task.
GitHub sends a pull request opened event and a review is queued.
A teammate mentions the bot in a comment and a task runs.
Rotate a trigger's secret after a leak.

where_to_find_it: Web: Schedules, Triggers panel; source choice 'Anything else (signed webhook)' with the note 'You get a URL and a signing secret to post events to.'; source label 'Webhook' (apps/web/features/schedules/components/ScheduleTriggersPanel.tsx:88-103).
Web: regenerate action titled 'Regenerate the signing secret for <name>?' with 'Signing secret: ...' shown once (ScheduleTriggersPanel.tsx:308, 414-419).
Developer webhooks panel (outgoing, separate): features/developers/components/WebhooksPanel.tsx (not this feature).
GitHub: installed through the GitHub App; webhook URL is set on the App by the owner.
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome, Desktop: server only; the brief and code show no receiver on devices.
prerequisites: Signed-in person who owns the trigger (signing-secret route).
EVENT_TRIGGER_SIGNING_SECRET set on the deployment (connector route returns 503 'Connector events are not configured' otherwise) (trigger-signatures.ts:5, route.ts:75-80).
For GitHub: GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET set, a verified installation, and PR review enabled on it (github route.ts:64-80; route.ts:329-352).
screens_and_controls: Create trigger, copy URL and signing secret, regenerate secret, delete trigger (ScheduleTriggersPanel.tsx:300-360).
GitHub App settings page at GitHub (outside).
journey: 1. Person creates a trigger with source 'Anything else (signed webhook)'.
2. The panel shows the URL and a signing secret once.
3. The outside service signs each request: HMAC over '<timestamp>.<body>' sent as x-agi-timestamp and x-agi-signature, within 5 minutes.
4. The server verifies, parses the JSON (needs string 'id' and 'type'), and queues work.
5. The sender gets {received, matched, queued} or a retryable 503.
feedback_and_outputs: 200 {received:true, matched, queued} (connector route.ts:123-127).
401 'Invalid signature'; 400 'Body must carry an id and a type'; 413 'Payload too large' (128 KB); 503 with Retry-After 10 when queueing fails (route.ts:44-120).
GitHub: 200 with duplicate:true on a repeat, 401 on a bad signature, review: queued (github route.ts:123-129).
settings: EVENT_TRIGGER_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, GMAIL_PUBSUB_AUDIENCE, GMAIL_PUBSUB_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_EMAIL, GOOGLE_CALENDAR_CHANNEL_SECRET, GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET, GITHUB_PR_REVIEW_MONTHLY_CAP, GITHUB_BOT_LOGIN (names only) (trigger-signatures.ts:5-9; github route.ts:50, 59).

working: Connector route: rate limit bucket trigger-webhook, uuid check, 128 KB body cap, salt read, signature check with a 300 s window, JSON object check, id and type check, ingest, 503 on queue failure (webhooks/connectors/[triggerId]/route.ts:35-128).

Per-trigger secret is derived from the deployment secret, the trigger id and a rotation salt; rotating the salt invalidates the old secret (trigger-signatures.ts:47-86; db/neon/0387_event_trigger_signing_salt.sql; trigger-service.ts:413, 438).
Constant-time comparison in both signature checks (trigger-signatures.ts:14-18; github-app.ts:349-360).

GitHub route: rate limit github-webhook, signature check (401 when secret missing or wrong), router for ping, ignored and invalid events, delivery de-duplication, automation events into triggers, installation-deleted cleanup, mention tasks limited to OWNER, MEMBER or COLLABORATOR, automatic PR review on opened, reopened, synchronize, ready_for_review for non-drafts (github/webhook/route.ts:64-300).
Review budget: 5-minute debounce while a review is pending and a rolling 30-day cap (default 100, from GITHUB_PR_REVIEW_MONTHLY_CAP) per installation (route.ts:57-61, 356-420).
Review gates: workspace code policy, managed compute policy, managed compute private beta flag, plan tier lookup (route.ts:462-486, 543).
Release of the delivery receipt when processing fails so a redelivery is processed (route.ts:171-178; delivery-dedup.ts:57).

Slack, Gmail and Calendar receivers exist with their own verification (verifySlackSignature trigger-signatures.ts:24; Gmail Pub/Sub token check in app/api/webhooks/gmail/route.ts; calendar channel token trigger-signatures.ts:90).
incomplete: The connector route does not itself record the delivery id; duplicate handling happens inside ingestTriggerEvent, which returns outcome 'duplicate' (trigger-ingest.ts:37, 372). The brief only claims de-duplication for GitHub.
PR review also depends on a managed compute private beta flag; when it is off, reviews are skipped with a log line (github route.ts:477-483).
The brief item 'rate limits per route' is true in code, but limits are per IP and fail open if the limiter store is down (rate-limit.ts:464-478).
disconnected_or_disabled: Connector events are refused when EVENT_TRIGGER_SIGNING_SECRET is unset (route.ts:75-80).
GitHub webhook returns 401 for every request when GITHUB_WEBHOOK_SECRET is unset (route.ts:73-80).
Automatic review off unless the installation has pr_review_enabled and a verified owner (route.ts:329-352).
not_available: Receivers on mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome and Desktop: none; server only.
Local mode: none; an outside service must reach our server.

established.statement: Signed webhooks from external providers are received, verified and routed (S98.09).
Connector triggers reject a bad signature with 401.
The code-host webhook rejects a bad signature with 401 and acknowledges a duplicate delivery without reprocessing.
Security behaviour fails closed.

acceptance_criteria: A connector POST with a wrong signature returns 401 and queues nothing.
A POST with a timestamp older than 300 seconds is rejected.
After regenerating a trigger's secret, the old signature fails and the new one works.
A body over 128 KB returns 413.
A GitHub POST without a valid x-hub-signature-256 returns 401.
Sending the same GitHub delivery id twice processes it once and answers duplicate:true.
A non-draft pull request opened event queues a review only when the installation has review enabled.
With the signing secret unset, connector events return 503 not configured.
inferred: [inferred] A sender must retry on 503 because the route asks for redelivery.
[inferred] Because the rate limit is per IP, a shared sender IP could share the 300 per minute budget.
proposed: [proposed] Document the signing format for sender developers on the trigger panel.
[proposed] Add a replay test for the connector route's duplicate outcome.

steps.what_happens: Outside service sends a signed POST to our server.
Server applies a per-IP rate limit and body cap.
Server reads the trigger's salt and verifies the signature against the derived secret.
Server validates payload shape and calls ingestTriggerEvent, which matches triggers, filters, de-duplicates, applies run caps and enqueues a job.
For GitHub, the server also may schedule a PR review or a mention task after the response, using an installation token from GitHub.
A model reviews the diff through managed compute and comments are posted to GitHub.

features.summary: Two planned platform pieces that do not exist yet. One would sync connector content in the background and index it for search. The other would let cloud connectors reach services on a customer's private network. The code read has neither. The brief and audit ledger both mark them missing. No app can use them.

purpose.what_it_does: Nothing today. The brief says a background worker should sync and index connector content so it can be searched (S98.08), and a bridge should let cloud connectors reach services on a customer's private network (S98.15). Both are marked missing on the platform (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/098-integration-and-extensibility-components.md).
purpose.why_it_exists: Planned so connected apps (mail, files, chat) could be searched without a live call each time, and so company-internal servers could be used by cloud connectors. No product document read explains the reason further, so the reason is unknown beyond the brief's 'Should' lines.
purpose.who_uses_it: Nobody yet. Intended users would be people with connected accounts and organizations with internal services [inferred].
problems_solved: None today.
Intended: searching connector content without a live call each time [inferred from S98.08].
Intended: reaching private services from cloud connectors [inferred from S98.15].
use_cases: Intended: search across a connected mail or file account from chat.
Intended: a cloud connector reaching an internal tool server behind a company firewall.
Today, in place of these: connectors are called live, and cloud connector endpoints that point at private or internal addresses are refused (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:643-652).

where_to_find_it: Not available on web, desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code extension or Chrome extension. No screen, command or setting exists for either piece in the code read.
prerequisites: Not applicable. Nothing to use.
screens_and_controls: None found in the code. A search for connector indexing terms in apps/web/lib, apps/web/app and the database migrations found only the public connector directory refresh, which lists available servers and does not index a user's content (apps/web/lib/connectors/directory/ingest.ts:1-25).
journey: No journey exists. A person who connects an account gets live connector calls only; the brief lists no sync step.
feedback_and_outputs: None. No 'last synced' time is shown: a founder decision lists 'no sync time' among connector extras that are not built (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md).
settings: None found.

working: Cloud connector endpoints are checked against an SSRF policy (a block on private and internal addresses) before the catalog is read and again at execution (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:643-652). This is the opposite of a private-network bridge and is not part of the missing feature.
not_available: Connector search/index worker: missing on every app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/098-integration-and-extensibility-components.md S98.08; doc: audit/missing/098-integration-and-extensibility-components.md).
Private-network bridge: missing on every app (same brief S98.15; same audit file; the ledger row has rollup 'missing', audit/ledger/ecosystem-capability-ledger.jsonl:3052).

No connector content table found: no migration with an index or embedding table for connector content was found by searching apps/web/db/neon for index, embedding, ingest and crawl terms next to 'connector'.

established.statement: A background worker syncs and indexes connector content so it can be searched (S98.08).
A bridge lets cloud connectors reach services on a customer's private network (S98.15).
Both items are planned for build wave 5, on the platform.

acceptance_criteria: When built, connector content for a connected account is indexed in the background and a search returns results without a live provider call.
When built, an index entry is only visible to the account that owns it.
When built, disconnecting a connector removes its indexed content.
When built, a cloud connector can reach a registered private service only through the bridge, and the existing block on private addresses stays on for every other path.
Until built, no app shows a control that claims either capability.
inferred: Indexed content is personal data and must follow the trust boundaries in AGENTS.md section 6: Local content never goes to a managed index without an explicit, labelled fork [inferred].
A private-network bridge needs customer-side software or an outbound tunnel, because the cloud cannot dial into a private network [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Decide first whether the index is per user or per workspace, and write it as a decision record under docs/decisions before building.
[proposed] Treat private reach as an organization admin feature with its own policy switch and audit events, like the existing plugin and connector policy gates.

features.summary: A hosted list of plugins (packs of skills and connector needs). A signed-in web account can install one, which also installs the plugins it needs, then update, turn off or remove it. A person can also add a public GitHub marketplace, and a daily job refreshes the public directory. The CLI can browse and install too.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists plugins from three sources (built-in registry rows, a cached public directory snapshot, and the person's own marketplaces). Installs a built-in plugin for one account after resolving its dependencies, records which permissions the person approved, offers updates with a diff, and removes plugins. Lets a person register a public GitHub repository as a marketplace and refresh it.
purpose.why_it_exists: Plugins bundle skills and connector needs so a workflow can be added in one step, as ChatGPT and Claude do (doc: docs/product/requirements.md lines 1560-1568 list install, enable or disable, update, uninstall, namespacing and marketplace or source controls).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on web and the CLI; desktop users are sent to the web to manage plugins.
problems_solved: Finding packs of skills without hand-copying files.
Pulling in the plugins a pack depends on automatically.
Keeping installed plugins current, and noticing when an installed version was stopped.
Using a team's or publisher's own plugin catalog.
use_cases: Browse GET /api/plugins and install a built-in pack from the web directory.
Update an installed plugin after approving any new permissions it asks for.
Add a public GitHub marketplace on the account and install a plugin from it with the CLI (agi marketplace get plugin@marketplace).
Remove a plugin; if other plugins depend on it, choose to remove them too.

where_to_find_it: Web: marketing page /plugins and /plugins/[id] (apps/web/app/plugins/page.tsx:1-80); in-app plugin management lives under settings section 'plugins' (apps/web/features/settings/lib/web-settings-sections.ts:78) and the directory UI labels 'Install', 'Installed', 'Required', 'Turned off', 'Built in', 'Partners', 'Marketplace' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:81-103). Exact navigation path inside the app was not traced: unknown.

CLI: 'agi plugin' (list, install, info, login, configure) and 'agi marketplace' (add, sources, remove, browse, get, show, recommend, search) (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:941-945, 2340-2372).

Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: no plugin install found; the matrix says absent for all three (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:372-381). Note the capability table lists canUsePlugins true for mobile (packages/contracts/types/src/capabilities.ts:120) while the matrix says false; code is the higher source, and no mobile install code was found.
prerequisites: A signed-in account. Plugin routes use a user-scoped database session (apps/web/app/api/plugins/installations/route.ts:43).
The workspace must allow the 'plugins' feature (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-gate.ts:11-33).
Browsing GET /api/plugins needs no sign-in found in the route (apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:51-94).
screens_and_controls: Directory tabs 'Built in', 'Partners', 'Marketplace' and group headings 'Built-in packs', 'Partner plugins', 'Marketplace plugins' (apps/web/features/directory/constants.ts:90-103).
Buttons and states 'Install', 'Installed', 'Desktop and CLI', 'Coming later' (same file, lines 81-85).
Desktop 'Manage plugins' button, with an error line 'Could not open your plugins.' if the browser cannot open (CloudPluginsSection.tsx:10,45).
CLI: 'agi marketplace show plugin@marketplace' previews what a plugin adds, the connections it needs and the permissions it asks for (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2362-2364).
journey: Open the plugin directory and search or filter (search, verified, worksWith, source, category, publisher, status, sort, limit, cursor; apps/web/app/api/plugins/route.ts:30-42).

Open a plugin and choose Install. The server resolves dependencies, checks policy for the plugin and each dependency, then checks version, signature, digest and scan (installations/route.ts:58-85; plugin-installation-service.ts:303-336).
If a dependency is missing or its version clashes, the install is refused with a message naming the plugin (plugin-dependencies.ts:182-206).
The page receives the installation and the list of dependencies installed with it (installations/route.ts:117).
Later, the updates list shows a newer version with a diff; the person names any new permissions and applies the update (updates/route.ts:26-79; plugin-lifecycle.ts:656-745).
To turn off or remove, the server refuses if other plugins depend on it unless the person agrees to include them (installations/[id]/route.ts:49-135).
To add a catalog: register a public GitHub repository URL; refresh it later (marketplaces/route.ts:42-76; marketplaces/[id]/refresh/route.ts).

Install with dependency resolution: breadth-first, depth at most 8, at most 32 plugins, version ranges checked for conflicts (apps/web/lib/services/plugin-dependencies.ts:6-7,118-169; plugin-installation-service.ts:255-301).
A plugin whose dependencies cannot be read is not installed (plugin-installation-service.ts:204-206).
A built-in plugin may depend only on built-in plugins; a dependency in another marketplace is refused (plugin-installation-service.ts:269-274).
Dependencies are installed before the root, inside the same install call (plugin-installation-service.ts:346-367).
Update offers and apply, including repairing an installation pinned to a suspended or deprecated version (plugin-lifecycle.ts:592-745).
Remove: delete the row, with a dependents check (plugin-installation-service.ts:434; installations/[id]/route.ts:104-135).

Daily refresh of the public directory snapshot by cron at 06:08 UTC (vercel.json:157-160; apps/web/app/api/cron/refresh-plugin-directory/route.ts:17-40).
CLI browse, show, get and search of account marketplaces (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:2340-2372; apps/cli/src/cloud/marketplaces.rs:5,81-82).
incomplete: User-registered marketplace sources refresh only when a person calls the refresh route. The only caller of refreshMarketplaceSource is that route (apps/web/app/api/plugins/marketplaces/[id]/refresh/route.ts:36); no cron or job was found for them. The daily cron refreshes the public directory, a different store.
Registry installs only work for plugins marked web-installable with an embedded manifest (plugin-installation-service.ts:190-197); others return PLUGIN_NOT_INSTALLABLE.

The brief names plugin-lifecycle.ts:603 for update and removal; at HEAD update offers start at line 592, apply at 656, and removal lives in plugin-installation-service.ts:434 and the DELETE handler. The brief predates HEAD.
disconnected_or_disabled: Migration 0232 (signing, scan table, approved permissions) carries a header 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0232_plugin_package_signing_and_permission_review.sql:4). Whether it is applied in each environment is unknown; code reads plugin_package_scans and approved_permissions, so installs would fail without it.
not_available: Mobile, VS Code extension and Chrome extension: no plugin install (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:372-381).
Desktop: no in-app install; it opens the web (CloudPluginsSection.tsx:38-41).
Marketplaces from non-GitHub hosts: refused, 'Only public github.com repository URLs are supported.' (plugin-marketplace-service.ts:520-523).

established.statement: A registry lists available plugins with versions and metadata (S98.17).
Installing a plugin resolves and installs the plugins it depends on (S98.19).
Plugins can be installed, updated to a newer version and uninstalled (S98.20).
A marketplace service registers plugin catalogs and keeps them refreshed (S98.25).
Plugin requirements: install, enable/disable, update, uninstall, namespacing, marketplace or source controls, and included MCP servers, skills, hooks, subagents and prompts.

acceptance_criteria: GET /api/plugins returns entries with total and filters; an invalid query returns 400 INVALID_QUERY.
Installing a plugin that depends on two others installs the two others first and returns them in 'dependencies'.
Installing a plugin with an unreadable dependency list installs nothing and names the plugin.
An update that adds a permission the member has not approved is refused until the member names it.
Removing a plugin that others depend on is refused with the dependents named, unless the person agrees to remove them too.
A marketplace refresh that fails keeps the old entries and marks the source 'error' with the message.
A suspended version cannot be installed and shows its reason.
inferred: Update and removal should be offered on every app that shows installed plugins; today only the web and CLI do [inferred from matrix].
A user-registered marketplace should refresh without a manual call to meet 'keeps them refreshed' [inferred from S98.25 and the lack of a job].
proposed: [proposed] Add a scheduled refresh for user-registered marketplace sources, bounded by a per-run budget like the directory ingest.
[proposed] Show update offers in the desktop and CLI plugin screens so the web is not the only place to learn about one.

steps.what_happens: The person opens the directory or runs a CLI command. The client calls GET /api/plugins (or the marketplace routes).
The server reads built-in rows from the database and the cached public snapshot, merges and filters them, and returns a page.
On Install the server checks the csrf token, a rate limit, the workspace 'plugins' gate and the per-plugin policy.
It resolves dependencies, checks the dependency policy, then for each plugin checks suspension, signed digest, scan record and permissions, then writes the install rows.
A workspace audit event 'plugin_installed' is written for each dependency and the root.
Registering a marketplace fetches the manifest from raw GitHub with a 10 second timeout, validates, scans and stores it in one transaction.
Once a day the cron refreshes the public directory snapshot from public marketplace manifests and listings.

features.summary: Checks before a plugin runs. A package must match its signed digest and have a passing content scan, or install is refused. New permissions need the member's approval. An organization admin can publish plugins to the workspace and set who gets them. Separate publisher identity checking is not built; human review stands in for it.

purpose.what_it_does: Verifies a plugin package's digest and Ed25519 signature against trusted public keys, scans package text for dangerous patterns with fixed rules, records the verdict by content hash, holds back installs that need new permissions, and lets a workspace admin publish plugins and choose per plugin whether members must have it, get it by default, can choose it, or cannot see it. Community submissions get a human approve, reject or suspend step.
purpose.why_it_exists: Plugins carry instructions and connectors that act with the person's access, so a bad package could leak secrets or act without approval. The checks fail closed so a missing check never reads as a pass. Organizations need a controlled way to roll plugins out.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person installing a plugin (the checks run silently); workspace admins with the policy.manage permission; platform reviewers who handle community submissions.
problems_solved: Tampered or unsigned packages being installed.
Prompt-injection, secret-stealing and destructive text hidden in skill files.
A plugin update quietly gaining new permissions.
Organizations unable to push approved plugins to members.
use_cases: A member installs a registry plugin; an unsigned copy is refused with 'is not signed'.
An admin uploads a plugin archive to the workspace and sets it 'Required'.
A member uploads their own plugin; a 'review' scan finding needs them to acknowledge it.
A reviewer suspends an approved community plugin.

established.statement: Plugin packages are validated (manifest, integrity, signature) before they can be installed (S98.18).
Publishers have verified identities and installs check a package came from its publisher (S98.26); status 'not applicable anywhere'.
An organization can distribute approved extensions to its members (S98.27).
Extension packages are scanned for dangerous content and blocked or flagged before install (S98.28).
Extensions are evaluated (quality or safety runs) before or after publication (S98.29).
Publisher identity is checked in the owner's review of each submission, as ChatGPT's app review does.
Security behaviour fails closed; never weaken validation or guards to make a change pass.

acceptance_criteria: An unsigned non-builtin registry plugin cannot be installed and the message says it is not signed.
A signature that matches no configured key is refused as signature_invalid.
A package whose scan has never run is refused with scan_missing.
A package with a 'block' finding cannot be uploaded or installed; a 'review' finding installs only after the content hash is acknowledged.
An update that adds a permission leaves the installation off until approved.
A member cannot turn off a 'Required' workspace plugin.
Publishing a workspace plugin needs policy.manage; without it the route refuses.
inferred: Evaluation should include a run against sample prompts to meet 'quality/safety runs' [inferred from S98.29 wording].
Marketplace plugin files, not only the manifest, should be scanned before install [inferred from S98.28].
proposed: [proposed] Pass the downloaded artifact digest into the install check so hash_mismatch protects real downloads.
[proposed] Write the publisher review steps into a runbook under docs/runbooks and record who reviewed each submission, so S98.26 has evidence.

steps.what_happens: On install of a registry plugin the server builds an integrity claim from the stored digest, signature and source.
It checks the digest and verifies the signature with Ed25519 against each configured public key; a builtin first-party pack skips the signature.
It reads the stored scan record by digest; missing or non-pass refuses.
It compares declared permissions with those the member approved before; an expansion disables the install and raises a review.
On workspace publish the archive is parsed, scanned with the same rules, hashed, stored in a transaction, and an audit event is written.
A member's enabled workspace plugins become skills in the skills list.

features.summary: Two lists. The server lists the skills a person can use, including ones from installed plugins, and serves a skill's bundled files for preview or download. The CLI builds one slash command list from built-in commands, skills, plugin commands and custom command files. Mobile, desktop, Chrome and the CLI read the server skills list.

purpose.what_it_does: GET /api/skills returns built-in, plugin, workspace, personal and installed-directory skills with source, version, required tools and connectors. GET /api/skills/[name]/files/[...path] returns one bundled file as text or as a download. In the CLI, the command registry merges built-in commands, skills, plugin command files and custom command files so the palette, help and slash handling agree.
purpose.why_it_exists: A skill is a saved procedure the model can follow; people need to see which are available and load its scripts and references when used. The CLI needs one command list so a name means one thing.
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone using skills on web, mobile, desktop or Chrome; CLI users typing slash commands; plugin authors adding commands.
problems_solved: Knowing which skills are on and where each came from.
Previewing or downloading a skill's files safely.
Name clashes between commands and skills.
Plugin and project commands showing up beside built-in ones.
use_cases: Open the skills list and pick a skill; its source shows as built-in, plugin or personal.
Preview references/guide.md inside a skill.
In the CLI type / and find a plugin's command next to /help.
Add a markdown file to .agiworkforce/commands and run it as a slash command.

where_to_find_it: Web: skills list reads GET /api/skills; the public page /skills is linked from the site map (apps/web/app/sitemap-page/page.tsx:36); in-app skill screens not opened: unknown.

steps.what_happens: The app sends GET /api/skills with the person's session.
The server rate-limits (bucket 'skills-catalog-read'), opens a user-scoped database session, and checks whether the workspace allows plugins.
It reads the built-in skills from the .agents/skills folder shipped with the server (cached 60 s), filtered by product audience, plus extra layers from SKILLS_LAYERS.
It adds installed directory skills and personal skills, de-duplicates and returns the list.
A file request resolves the skill, then reads the file with realpath containment and a size ceiling, and returns text or an attachment.
The CLI syncs account skills into a local folder and discovers local skills; the TUI builds the slash registry on the device.
Running /name resolves skill, then plugin command, then custom command and sends the expanded prompt to the model as the next message.

features.summary: In the CLI, a person can list commands in ~/.agiworkforce/hooks.json to run at set moments, such as before or after a tool call. A hook can block the action, stop the run, rewrite tool input or output, or add context. User hooks run in the OS sandbox unless turned off; plugin hooks always do.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs user, plugin and organization-managed commands at 35 named events in the CLI (for example PreToolUse, PostToolUse, SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, Stop). The hook gets a JSON description on standard input. Its output or exit code can block the action, stop the loop, rewrite tool arguments, add up to 4 KB of context or replace tool output.
purpose.why_it_exists: Lets people and teams enforce rules and automate around the agent: guard dangerous commands, format after edits, redact secrets, log activity. The event names follow Claude Code's so existing habits carry over (doc comment in apps/cli/src/features/hooks/hooks.rs:140-148; doc: docs/product/requirements.md line 1428-1430 lists hooks among plugin contents).
purpose.who_uses_it: CLI users and developers; organization admins through a managed policy; plugin authors who ship hooks.
problems_solved: Stopping an unsafe tool call before it runs.
Automating checks after edits.
Scrubbing secrets from tool output before it is stored.
Centrally controlling which hooks may run in an organization.
use_cases: Block 'git push' with a PreToolUse hook scoped by if: Bash(git push*).
Run a formatter after every edit with a PostToolUse hook.
Inject project context before each prompt with BeforePromptBuild or UserPromptSubmit.
An admin turns hooks off for the workspace.

Config file ~/.agiworkforce/hooks.json (hooks.rs:928-930). The home folder can be changed with the AGIWORKFORCE_HOME setting (apps/cli/tests/coverage_wave2_hooks_agi_events.rs, set_var line).

Not on web, desktop, mobile, VS Code or Chrome: none found. The app server can add and remove hooks for a connected client (apps/cli/src/app_server/surfaces.rs:1194,1207); which client calls it was not traced: unknown.

The brief cites hooks.rs:1155 as dispatch and chat.rs:260; at HEAD run_hooks is at hooks.rs:1395 and the PreToolUse handling at agent/chat.rs:284-322; line 1155 is inside hook matching and chat.rs:260 is tool-argument error code. The brief predates HEAD.

Hooks, skills, plugins and subagents are in scope; plugins include hooks.

Never weaken guards or trust boundaries; a guard that did not finish must not read as a guard that allowed.

A blocking hook that times out blocks; a non-blocking one does not.

steps.what_happens: The CLI loads hooks.json (checks owner and mode on Unix), appends plugin hooks, applies the managed policy.
At an event the agent code builds a HookInput and calls run_hooks.
run_hooks filters hooks by matcher and if rule, and returns nothing if the workspace policy disallows hooks.
Each hook starts as a shell line or a program with arguments, sandboxed or on the host, with the JSON on standard input and a timeout.
Output and exit code are turned into block, stop, updated input, context or replaced output; results are combined with Blocked over Stop over Continue.
For a signed-in account the CLI reads the workspace policy from our servers to learn whether hooks are allowed.

features.summary: One coding-session service, the AGI CLI's developer-session host, owns coding threads, turns, approvals and history. The CLI, VS Code and Desktop talk to it over a shared JSON protocol. Cloud Code sessions are listed beside local ones but cannot take turns there. Mobile reaches it only through the relay [inferred].

purpose.what_it_does: Holds the state of coding sessions (called threads) in one place: the list of threads, each thread's messages, status, working folder, branch, worktree, trust mode and the single client allowed to write to it. Clients start turns, stream output, steer, interrupt, approve actions and resume threads through one wire protocol. (apps/cli/src/app_server/developer_host.rs:2341, crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:1)
purpose.why_it_exists: So that every coding surface shows the same session instead of each keeping a private copy. The protocol file says it is shared by AGI CLI and AGI for VS Code, and v8 exists so an editor client rides the CLI instead of keeping a second copy of each surface. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:1, :32-35)
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers using the AGI CLI, the AGI VS Code extension and the Desktop app's coding view. Engineers building clients against the protocol. The mobile phone reaches desktop coding sessions through the relay (see F099-99).
problems_solved: Two clients no longer drift apart on the same session: one writer lease decides who may send turns, and others can take over or release it (thread/writer/takeover, thread/writer/release).
A session started in one app can be resumed, forked, searched, archived, pinned or rewound from another.
Cloud Code sessions for the same GitHub repository show up in the local thread list, so the person sees all work for a repository in one place.
use_cases: Start a coding thread in the CLI, then reopen it in the VS Code sidebar and continue it.
Open Desktop's coding view, which starts the AGI CLI as its runtime and lists the saved sessions for a folder.
Interrupt a running turn, answer an approval request, then resume after restart.
See a cloud Code session next to local threads and be told to continue it on the web or with agi code teleport.

where_to_find_it: CLI: the command agi app-server (transport stdio, ws, or a bind address such as 127.0.0.1:8788). The ordinary agi chat and TUI use the same host [inferred]. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6700-6760, :870)

Web, Mobile, Chrome: no direct use found. Web only receives cloud sessions; mobile uses the relay. [inferred]
prerequisites: The AGI CLI binary must be present and new enough; Desktop refuses a runtime below its minimum version and says to update the AGI CLI or point Settings at a current binary. (apps/desktop/electron/runtime/developerSessionService.ts:1322-1356)
A WebSocket server needs the environment variable AGI_APP_SERVER_TOKEN, otherwise it refuses to start. (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:6727-6737)
Listing cloud sessions needs a signed-in account (agi login) and a git origin remote that is a GitHub repository. (apps/cli/src/app_server/cloud_threads.rs:34-41, :88-97)

journey: 1. A client starts the host (agi app-server) or Desktop spawns the CLI as a child process.

2. The client sends initialize with its protocol version and gets the server's version and capabilities; an unsupported version is refused with code -32005. (crates/agiworkforce-protocol/src/developer_session.rs:36-44)
3. The client sends thread/start (or thread/list then thread/resume).

5. The host streams turn/output_delta and turn/agent_event; approvals are requested with approval/requested.
6. The turn ends with turn/completed, turn/failed or turn/interrupted.

established.statement: One coding-session service owns session state for every client. Status in the brief: platform done.
The wire protocol is stable and shared by the CLI and VS Code; every v8 method is additive.
Local, own-key and managed cloud are separate trust boundaries; nothing may silently route a Local session to another boundary.

acceptance_criteria: A thread started through the host from one client appears in thread/list from a second client for the same folder.
Only the writer-lease holder can send turn/start; another client must take over or release first, and thread/writer_changed is emitted.
A client announcing an unsupported protocol version is refused at initialize with error code -32005.
A WebSocket server started without AGI_APP_SERVER_TOKEN does not start.
A cloud thread (id prefix cloud:) appears in the list only when signed in and the repository matches, and turn/start on it is refused with the continue-on-web message.
A turn with more input items than the limit is rejected with an invalid-request error.

features.summary: One shared catalog names every plan (Local Mode, Local Mode + BYOK, Free, Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise), how it is sold, and its price. One server resolver then answers what an account may use right now. Checkout, usage limits and every app read these two sources.

purpose.what_it_does: Defines each plan tier, its label, its USD and INR price and interval, whether it can be bought self-serve, by seat upgrade, by contract, or not at all, and the catalog version a subscription was sold under (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:166-231; packages/contracts/types/src/billing-plan-catalog.ts:18-29). A server resolver combines the account's own subscription row, a workspace seat and the payment status into one answer: plan, entitled yes or no, source, and a denial reason (apps/web/lib/services/entitlement-resolution.ts:211-228, 384-413).
purpose.why_it_exists: So that checkout, pricing pages, usage limits and every app agree on what a plan is and what an account holds. A subscriber keeps the catalog version they bought under, so a later reprice is visible and never silent (billing-plan-catalog.ts:12-18; doc: docs/product/commercial.md section Grandfathered Plans And Catalog Versions).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every server enforcement point (chat gate, quota checks, checkout), the web pricing and billing screens, and indirectly every app that shows a plan. Engineers and testers use it as the single source for 'what does this plan allow'.
problems_solved: Two services computing two different answers about the same user (the resolver says every entitlement question resolves in one place, entitlement-resolution.ts:213-216).
A reprice silently changing what an existing customer agreed to (plan_catalog_version kept per subscription, billing-plan-catalog.ts:12-18).
Hard-coded plan names and prices in each client (clients import the catalog from @agiworkforce/types, apps/web/app/billing/UpgradeWelcome.tsx:6).
use_cases: A visitor compares plans on the pricing page, then starts checkout for one.
A team member with no subscription of their own gets the workspace plan through a seat (entitlement-resolution.ts:376-413).
A person whose card failed is served as Free with a billing notice header instead of being locked out (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:343-352).
A withdrawn plan sends a new buyer to its successor while an existing subscriber keeps the plan they bought (billing-plan-catalog.ts:31-35, 94-110).

where_to_find_it: Web: pricing page at /pricing (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:969, 915), upgrade chooser at /upgrade (apps/web/app/upgrade/UpgradeChooser.tsx:96), and Settings > Billing (apps/web/features/settings/sections/BillingSection.tsx:650).
Desktop (Electron): shows the hosted web app, so the same web screens; Stripe pages open in the system browser (apps/web/features/billing/services/stripe-payments.ts:46-57).

Mobile: Settings 'Subscription' screen shows the current plan and 'Compare plans'; with the build flag off it shows no purchase control (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/screenTitles.ts:2; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-billing/index.tsx:351-360, 550).
CLI: /pricing and /upgrade print or open the web pricing URL (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs:219, 785-797).
Chrome extension: menu entries open /pricing in a tab (apps/extension/src/side_panel.ts:12083, 14139).
VS Code extension: no plan screen found in this read; usage-limit errors carry the plan message (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:875-882). A plan or purchase entry is unknown.
prerequisites: A signed-in account to see the account's own plan; the catalog itself is public data on the pricing page.
To buy a paid plan: the paid-upgrade gate must allow the account (see F100-04).
screens_and_controls: Pricing page: one card per plan with its label from the catalog (apps/web/app/pricing/page.tsx:915); Team has a monthly or yearly cadence toggle, because only Team and Team Premium have yearly prices (billing-catalog.ts:200-216; doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md).
Upgrade page headed 'Upgrade' with 'Usage this period' and a recommended plan (apps/web/app/upgrade/UpgradeChooser.tsx:96, 131, 196).
Order panel: 'Order details', 'Payment method', and a 'Subscribe to <plan>' button (apps/web/features/billing/components/UpgradeOrderPanel.tsx:320, 508, 584).
Enterprise is contract priced and has no self-serve price (billing-catalog.ts:226-230).
journey: Open the pricing page and read the plan cards.
Choose a plan; the catalog says whether it is self-serve, seat upgrade, contract only or free (billing-plan-catalog.ts:61-67).

If self-serve, continue to the order panel and checkout (see F100-04). If contract only, the buyer is sent to sales: checkout answers 'is no longer sold self-serve. Contact sales to buy it.' (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:219-225).
After purchase the resolver reads the new subscription and every app sees the new plan.
feedback_and_outputs: Plan label and monthly price on the confirmation screen, with renewal or trial end (apps/web/app/billing/UpgradeWelcome.tsx:65-75, 96-110).
A notice for yearly Pro subscribers that nothing changes for them (billing-plan-catalog.ts:56-59).
For a lapsed paid plan the API still serves the turn as Free and sets header X-AGI-Billing-Notice with the subscription status (auth-gate.ts:68, 343-352).
settings: Plan data has no per-user setting; it is code in the shared package plus Stripe price ids read from environment variables named STRIPE_PRICE_* (apps/web/lib/pricing.ts:54-110).
Regional price display depends on the country header and the Stripe price currency options (apps/web/lib/server/localized-pricing-service.ts:97-138; apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:230-231).

working: Catalog of ten tiers (local-only, byok, free, basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise) with labels Local Mode, Local Mode + BYOK, Free, Basic, Premium, Max, Ultra, Team, Team Premium, Enterprise (billing-catalog.ts:5-14, 166-231).
Sellability is computed per plan: withdrawn, contract_only, seat_upgrade, self_serve or free_of_charge (billing-plan-catalog.ts:61-67). Catalog version is 4 (billing-plan-catalog.ts:18).
Pro yearly billing is withdrawn for new sales as of 2026-09-27 and existing yearly subscribers are grandfathered (billing-plan-catalog.ts:43-59).
Legacy tier names hobby and pro_plus fold into basic and max (billing-catalog.ts:1029-1041).

Stripe price ids are mapped from plan, interval and currency to named environment variables for USD and INR (apps/web/lib/pricing.ts:54-110); other currencies are derived from the Stripe price's currency options (apps/web/lib/server/localized-pricing-service.ts:97-138).

Checkout opens for a price only when the Stripe amount equals the published amount and the tax behavior matches the currency; otherwise it stays closed with a warning (localized-pricing-service.ts:140-180).
If the Stripe price lookup fails, the page serves the catalog USD price and checkout stays closed (localized-pricing-service.ts:43-59).

Resolver precedence: own entitled paid row, then a workspace seat, then the user's own lapsed or free row, then none (entitlement-resolution.ts:376-413). A seat counts only if the seat rank is within licensed seats and the owner's subscription is entitled (entitlement-resolution.ts:104-120).

A user with no subscription row at all resolves as Free, entitled false, denial entitlement_missing; a lapsed or unpaid row resolves as Free with denial payment_required (entitlement-resolution.ts:289-302, 304-321).
Every denial is recorded as a capability denial event (entitlement-resolution.ts:273-279).
Plan resolution for a subscriber uses the catalog version they were sold under (apps/web/lib/services/plan-catalog-service.ts:70).
incomplete: The withdrawn-plan table is empty, so withdrawn sellability and successor routing have no live data yet (billing-plan-catalog.ts:36-41).
Plan visibility per surface lists only web, desktop and mobile; there is no entry for CLI, VS Code or Chrome (billing-catalog.ts:233-246). Whether that is deliberate is unknown.
Only USD and INR have configured Stripe price ids; any other currency depends on currency options set in Stripe, which this read could not inspect (pricing.ts:54-110).
disconnected_or_disabled: Paid purchase of any plan is gated for accounts that are not already paying (see F100-04); the catalog is shown but purchase is not open to everyone (apps/web/lib/server/billing-waitlist-access.ts:33-54; doc: docs/product/commercial.md section Paid Acquisition Gate).
not_available: Enterprise has no self-serve price or checkout (billing-catalog.ts:226-230; checkout/route.ts:219-225).
CLI, VS Code and Chrome show no plan comparison screen of their own; they open the web pricing page (claude_parity.rs:785-797; side_panel.ts:12083). VS Code entry unknown.

established.statement: A single plan catalog defines each plan's tier, capabilities and limits and is what checkout and enforcement read.
A price catalog maps each plan, interval and currency to a real charged price that pricing and checkout use.
One service resolves what an account is entitled to (plan, seat, grace) and every enforcement point asks it.
A subscription keeps the catalog version it was sold under; moving a subscriber off it needs at least 30 days notice, takes effect at renewal, and states the right to cancel first.

established.statement: One user has one billing owner (Stripe, Apple or Google) and one effective entitlement across all surfaces.

established.statement: Public plan names and prices are owned by billing-catalog.ts; display-name changes keep stored plan identifiers.

acceptance_criteria: Every tier in the catalog has a label, a sellability value and the current catalog version, and listPlanCatalog returns all ten.
A new buyer asking for a contract-only or seat-upgrade tier gets no purchasable plan; a withdrawn tier maps to its successor.
An account with no subscription row resolves as Free, entitled false, denial entitlement_missing; an account with a lapsed paid row resolves as Free with denial payment_required.
A workspace member with no own paid row inherits the workspace plan only while the owner's subscription is entitled and the member's seat rank is within licensed seats.
Asking with includeSeats false returns only the user's own plan.
When Stripe cannot return a price, the pricing page shows the catalog USD price and the checkout call for that price is refused.
inferred: The catalog is meant to be the only place plan prices and labels are written, so a client that restates them is a defect [inferred from AGENTS.md section 4 and the shared import pattern].
Local and own-key use needs no entitlement; the plans local-only and byok exist at price 0 only as labels [inferred from billing-catalog.ts:167-177 and checkout/route.ts:178-182].
proposed: [proposed] Add CLI, VS Code and Chrome to the plan surface list, or document why they are excluded.
[proposed] Publish the current plan and catalog version in one read endpoint so each app can show it without a local copy.

steps.what_happens: A person opens the pricing page; the page reads plan labels and prices from the shared catalog in the web bundle.
For localized prices the server maps the country to a currency, looks up the Stripe price (cached ten minutes) and marks the price checkout-ready only if amount and tax behavior match.
Stripe returns the price and its currency options.
On any gated request the server resolves the entitlement: own subscription row, then workspace seat, then free or none, and builds one bundle with plan, status, entitled and denial reason.
The chat gate calls the resolver and, for a lapsed paid plan, serves the turn as Free with a billing notice header.
The app reads the plan from the account and shows it.
