features.summary: Stops usage that the plan or budget does not allow. Managed requests are checked against rolling 5-hour, weekly and monthly windows, request rate, concurrent responses and spend caps before a model runs. A refused request says which limit was hit and, where known, when it resets.

purpose.what_it_does: Refuses or admits each managed Cloud request using plan windows (rolling session, weekly, flagship weekly, billing period), request rate limits shared across server instances, a per-plan count of concurrent responses, daily and monthly unit quotas, and three kinds of spend cap (workspace block, workspace policy cap, personal cap on extra credits).
purpose.why_it_exists: Managed usage costs real money per call, so each account must be held to what its plan pays for, and a workspace owner must be able to cap spend (S100.04, S100.11, S100.12, S100.13 in the area brief).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person using Cloud mode on any app; workspace owners and admins who set budgets; engineers who tune plan limits.
problems_solved: One person exhausting shared capacity or running unlimited parallel responses.
Surprise spend on a workspace or on personal extra credits.
Unclear refusals: each refusal has a code, text and reset context (managed-usage-request-service.ts:402-467, 560-598).
use_cases: A Premium user sends many long chats and hits the rolling 5-hour limit; the reply names it and offers the reset time.
A Free user with one concurrent response sends a second message while the first still streams and is told to stop or wait (turn-slot.ts:34-48).
A workspace admin sets a monthly limit with mode Block; members' managed turns are refused with over_cap until the month resets or the cap is raised.
A person turns on usage credits and sets a personal Monthly spend limit for extra usage.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Usage with cards 'Plan usage limits', 'Credit balances', 'Resets', 'Monthly spend limit' and meters 'Current session', 'This week', 'Most capable models', 'This billing period' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:414, 491, 710, 1312-1396; packages/contracts/types/src/usage-vocabulary.ts:37-59).
Web workspace console: a spend limit card with an enforcement select that offers Notify and Block (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:189, 264-270).
Desktop: the same web screens in the hosted app.
Mobile: refusal is shown in the chat screen as a paywall presentation (apps/mobile/app/(app)/chat/[id].tsx:511; apps/mobile/services/failureCopy.ts:60).
CLI: refusal text with the limit name and reset (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:217; apps/cli/src/models/streaming.rs:217).
VS Code: a usage-limit error with a reason and recovery (apps/extension-vscode/src/utils/api.ts:875-882).
Chrome: side panel maps limit codes to a session or weekly window (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/usageWindows.ts:42-53).
prerequisites: A signed-in account using Managed Cloud. Local and own-key use are not metered by this server path [inferred, see access_and_usage].
To set a workspace limit: a team admin with the policy.manage permission (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:68-79).
screens_and_controls: Usage meters per window with urgency levels at 90 and 95 percent (usage-vocabulary.ts:14-17).
Workspace spend limit: monthly cap in credits, enforcement Notify or Block, alert threshold percent (spend-limit route PutSchema; WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:264-270).
Personal Monthly spend limit: a whole number of credits (apps/web/app/api/settings/spend-limit/route.ts:25-29).
Free accounts see 'Upgrade for higher capacity' instead of plan meters (UsageSection.tsx:1313).
journey: Send a message in any app.
The server checks rate, then resolves the plan, then the workspace budget, then takes a turn slot, then reserves usage against the windows.
If any check refuses, the app shows the refusal text and, for plan windows, the reset time and a suggested alternative model.
Otherwise the turn runs (see F100-03).
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal texts for the 5-hour, weekly, flagship weekly and monthly windows (managed-usage-request-service.ts:431-467).
Refusal text names the limit (for example 'Your 5-hour usage limit') and mentions usage credits where relevant (managed-usage-request-service.ts:513-558).
limitContext with resetsAt and an alternative model is attached when readable (managed-usage-request-service.ts:573-596).

Concurrent limit: HTTP 429 code concurrent_turn_limit_reached with headers X-AGI-Concurrent-Turn-Limit and X-AGI-Concurrent-Turns-Active (turn-slot.ts:14-47). Limiter down: HTTP 503 with Retry-After 30 (turn-slot.ts:20-32).
Request rate: HTTP 429 RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED with reset time and Retry-After (rate-limit.ts:1234-1296).
settings: Workspace spend limit (cap, enforcement, alert threshold).
Personal Monthly spend limit.
Usage credits on or off (usageCreditsEnabled, managed-usage-request-service.ts:715).

working: Plan window refusals map decision codes to HTTP 429 or 402 and error codes rolling_five_hour_limit_reached, rolling_weekly_limit_reached, flagship_weekly_limit_reached, insufficient_credits (managed-usage-request-service.ts:402-467).

Rolling windows are 5 hours and 7 days (apps/web/lib/server/capability-limit-resets.ts:7-8). Session, weekly and flagship caps come from the plan and catalog version (apps/web/lib/server/managed-usage-policy.ts:168-182; packages/contracts/types/src/managed-usage-limits.ts:31).
Clients classify limit codes into kinds with upgrade and reset hints (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:864-1022).
Rate limits use a shared Redis store with a per-instance fallback, and production refuses to start without Redis credentials (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:20-32, 1150-1226).
Tier scaling of rate limits exists for chat, image, video, voice and transcription keys by the plan's concurrent turn count (rate-limit.ts:934-966).
Concurrent responses use a Redis sorted-set slot per turn with a 360 second age-out; a plan with limit 0 is refused; no limit means no slot (rate-limit.ts:1306-1420; turn-slot.ts:109-163).
Every agent-turn entry point takes the slot through withManagedTurnSlot, including approve and resume routes (turn-slot.ts:96-108; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/route.ts:1486).

Free daily caps and monthly metered units (video seconds, voice minutes, computer use) are resolved from the tier policy and enforced by assertTierUnitAllowance (apps/web/lib/services/tier-unit-quota-service.ts:51-75, 298).

Workspace budget gate: mode Block with spend at or over the cap refuses with code over_cap, HTTP 402; Off and Notify admit (spend-limit-service.ts:161-200; apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:511-545).

Workspace policy cap: a monthlySpendCapCents in the organization policy refuses at reservation with organization_spend_cap_reached, HTTP 402, and fails closed when the policy or spend cannot be read (managed-usage-request-service.ts:338-399).
Personal limit: a ceiling on credits used past the plan, enforced in the database at admission, and a failure to read it fails the reservation (apps/web/db/neon/0378_personal_spend_limit.sql:11-25).
Artifact (published app) calls are capped per app per 5 hours (managed-usage-request-service.ts:473-478 refusal artifact_runtime_limit_reached; reservationError at 440-444).
incomplete: The workspace block gate decides from a 60 second cached sum, so a workspace can overshoot by about one window of spend (apps/web/lib/services/spend-limit-service.ts:51-58).

The workspace block gate fails open when its state cannot be read (spend-limit-service.ts:171-180; managed-compute-gate.ts:517-523), while the policy cap fails closed; the two behave differently by design or by accident, which is unknown.
The rate limit for the main chat route does not pass the plan tier, so tier scaling does not apply there [inferred: auth-gate.ts:274 calls withRateLimit without a plan argument].
disconnected_or_disabled: AGI_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE widens limits and is ignored in production runtimes (rate-limit.ts:46-62).
not_available: Whether the CLI, VS Code and Chrome apps send every refusal code to the person with the reset time is not established; they classify limit codes but per-app wording was not compared.

established.statement: Per-plan limits and quotas (rolling windows, unit quotas) are resolved from the plan and applied when a request is admitted.
A shared rate-limiting service limits requests per user, route and plan across instances.
A concurrency limiter caps simultaneous managed turns per account according to plan.
A budget manager holds spending limits and stops managed usage when a budget is reached.
Managed Free is open in public alpha and the credit controls must keep pace with Free usage.
The max_15x plan has no rolling 5-hour cap; a zero ceiling means zero permitted usage.
established.source: doc: docs/product/commercial.md (Plan Presentation And Usage Windows)

established.statement: Rate limits are configuration, not constants.

acceptance_criteria: A managed request that would exceed the rolling 5-hour cap is refused with HTTP 429 and code rolling_five_hour_limit_reached, and the response context carries a reset time when readable.
The weekly, flagship weekly and monthly windows each refuse with their own code and text.
With a plan concurrency of N, the (N+1)th simultaneous turn gets HTTP 429 concurrent_turn_limit_reached and a plan with no concurrency is refused with the upgrade message.
When the slot store is down and policy is fail-closed, the turn gets HTTP 503 with Retry-After 30.
A workspace in Block mode over its cap gets code over_cap; switching to Notify or raising the cap frees it at once because the cache is dropped on save.
A personal cap stops credit use past the plan ceiling at admission.
Exceeding a route's request rate gives HTTP 429 with a retry time.
inferred: The 5-hour and 7-day window lengths should be configuration, not literals, per AGENTS.md section 8 [inferred; they are constants at capability-limit-resets.ts:7-8].
A turn slot must be released on every end path including client abort [inferred from turn-slot.ts:55-69].
proposed: [proposed] Make the workspace Block gate fail closed or document why it fails open.
[proposed] Pass the plan tier into the chat route rate limit so tier scaling applies there.
[proposed] Compare the refusal wording on all six apps in one table test.

steps.what_happens: The app sends a chat request with a bearer token to the managed chat endpoint.
Server applies the per-IP and per-user request rate limits against the shared Redis store.
Server resolves the plan (see F100-01), serving a lapsed plan as Free.
Server takes a concurrent-turn slot for the plan or refuses with 429 or 503.
Server checks the workspace budget gate and, on reservation, the workspace policy cap.

Server reserves estimated cost through a database function that holds the session, weekly and flagship caps under a per-user lock and returns a decision such as acquired, session_limit or weekly_limit.
On refusal the server reads the reset time and a standard-model alternative and returns the refusal.
Redis holds the rate counters and turn slots.

data.synced: Shared across server instances; not synced to devices

Deleted with the account or by deletePersonalSpendLimit (spend-limit-service.ts:350-360)

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The rolling limits count cost, and the flagship weekly cap applies when the chosen model is flagged flagship, so model choice affects which window is charged (managed-usage-request-service.ts:792-799). The refusal can suggest a standard model (PLAN_LIMIT_WINDOWS alternative, lines 473-501). Which models are flagship is owned by SYS-model-catalog-and-routing.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account with a bearer token or API key (auth-gate.ts:172-186).
access_and_usage.permissions: Setting a workspace limit needs team admin access and the policy.manage permission (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/spend-limit/route.ts:68-79). The personal limit needs only the account holder (settings/spend-limit/route.ts:43-60).
access_and_usage.subscription: Limits come from the plan the resolver returns. Free accounts hold the Free window and caps; lapsed paid plans are served as Free (auth-gate.ts:343-352). Concurrent responses by plan: product limits table (billing-catalog.ts:580-731).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Windows: 5 hours, 7 days, billing period (capability-limit-resets.ts:7-8; usage-vocabulary.ts:37-59). Free daily caps and monthly units are in FREE_DAILY_CAPS and the tier policy (billing-catalog.ts:484-490; tier-unit-quota-service.ts:51-75). The numbers live in configuration, not in this feature.
access_and_usage.flags: AGI_RATE_LIMIT_SCALE (non-production only), AGI_RATE_LIMIT_CLIENT_IP_SOURCE, Redis credentials (rate-limit.ts:20-62, 1066-1080). Feature flags for limits: none found in this read.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Flagship models draw on a separate weekly share (FLAGSHIP_OF_WEEKLY_BUDGET_RATIO, managed-usage-limits.ts:27). Free users are limited to free models in the plan line 'A usage allowance, free models only' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/plans/index.tsx:57-60).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: none found in the code for plan limits; provider cost is tracked separately (see F100-03).
access_and_usage.local_mode: none found in the code: these checks run only on the server's managed Cloud path. The local-only and byok plans have unlimited concurrent turns in the limits table (billing-catalog.ts:583-615). Whether local or own-key turns reach any of these checks is unknown; see SYS-local-inference and SYS-execution-boundaries.

states_and_edge_cases.behaviour: Security-sensitive keys fail closed (block 60 seconds); others fail open with a warning. A quota-exhausted store falls back to per-instance counting.
Follows the Redis outage policy: fail-open admits with no recorded slot, fail-closed returns 503 Retry-After 30.
The slot is released only when the stream ends, errors or is cancelled.
Refusal is sent without context.
Block gate treats the request as ungoverned; the policy cap returns 503 billing_unavailable.
409 idempotency_in_progress, idempotency_replay or idempotency_conflict.
Refusal text changes to offer turning credits on or buying more where the account can.

states_and_edge_cases.behaviour: not handled in this feature's code; limiter calls race an 800 ms timeout and treat a slow limiter as unavailable.
Usage meters carry an aria-label such as '<label> usage' or 'usage unavailable'.

scenarios.name: Hit the rolling 5-hour limit
steps: Use an account on a paid plan in a test environment.
Send managed turns until the 5-hour cap is reached.
Read the next response in web, CLI and mobile.
scenarios.expected: HTTP 429 code rolling_five_hour_limit_reached; text names the 5-hour limit; reset time shown when available.

scenarios.name: Concurrent response ceiling
steps: On a plan with concurrency 1, start a long streaming reply.
Send a second message before it ends.
Stop the first reply and retry.
scenarios.expected: Second send gets 429 concurrent_turn_limit_reached with the active and limit headers; after stopping the first it succeeds.

scenarios.name: Workspace Block cap
steps: As admin with policy.manage, set a small monthly cap with enforcement Block.
Have a member send managed turns until spend passes the cap.
Raise the cap.
scenarios.expected: Member turns are refused with 402 over_cap, then admitted at once after the cap is raised.

steps: Make the turn slot store unreachable in a non-production environment with fail-closed policy.
Send a managed turn.
scenarios.expected: HTTP 503 with Retry-After 30 and code concurrency_limiter_unavailable.

scenarios.name: Personal cap on extra credits
steps: Turn on usage credits and set a personal Monthly spend limit.
Use credits past the plan until the limit is reached.
scenarios.expected: Admission refuses further credit use; the plan windows still apply.

features.summary: Every metered Cloud model call is recorded in a durable ledger. Before the call an estimated cost is held; afterwards the hold becomes the real cost, or is released if the call failed. A scheduled job recovers holds whose turn vanished. Cost is tagged by user, workspace, chat, key, schedule and app.

purpose.what_it_does: Reserves an estimated cost in microUSD under an idempotency key, moves the request through provider-started and client-delivered states, finalizes it at the billed cost with the provider cost kept separately, releases failed or stranded holds, and attributes each request to who and what caused it (managed-usage-request-service.ts:738-1306).
purpose.why_it_exists: So balances and windows can always be recomputed from a ledger, a retried request is never charged twice, a failed reply is not charged, and the company can see what each call cost it versus what the customer was billed (S100.05 to S100.10 in the area brief).
purpose.who_uses_it: The chat pipeline, voice, artifacts, scheduled tasks and API keys on the managed path; finance and operations people reading usage and cost reports.
problems_solved: Double charging on retry (idempotency keys, managed-usage-request-service.ts:403-425).
Charging for failed replies (failed outcome records zero for both amounts, line 1166-1168).
Quota held forever by a dead turn (recovery cron, recover-reservations/route.ts:34-92).
Hidden margin loss (provider cost recorded separately, lines 1166-1169, 1262-1289).
use_cases: A normal chat turn reserves, streams, then finalizes at the real token cost.
A turn fails midway: the hold is released and nothing is billed.
A turn is recovered after a stall and then delivers: a late settlement bills the delivered work (managed-usage-request-service.ts:1087-1139).
A published app (artifact) makes AI calls: they are capped per app and cannot be billed to usage credits (line 763-769).

CLI, VS Code, Chrome and mobile show limits and balances through their own usage views; the ledger itself has no screen on them.
prerequisites: A Managed Cloud request. Reservation needs a user id, an idempotency key, a request hash, a provider and model, and a plan tier (managed-usage-request-service.ts:738-760).
screens_and_controls: Usage history grouped by a chosen dimension, with aria-label 'Group usage history by' (UsageSection.tsx:1110).
'Credit balances' lists Bonus credits and Purchased credits (UsageSection.tsx:430-431).

journey: Person sends a message.
Server reserves an estimated cost; if refused the person sees a limit message (F100-02).
Model streams the reply; the server marks provider started and client delivered.
On success the reservation is finalized at the real cost; on failure it is released.
Balances and meters update; if the stall left a hold, the recovery job releases it.
feedback_and_outputs: Updated meters and balances.
An 'extra usage' message when fast mode needs usage credits that do not cover the message (managed-usage-request-service.ts:427-432).

working: Reservation through three database functions chosen by funding: plan windows with limits, extra usage on credits, and artifact runtime (managed-usage-request-service.ts:781-868).
Idempotency key parsed and replays refused with distinct codes (lines 403-425, 777).
Provider steps extend a reservation inside one request (reserveManagedUsageProviderStep, line 941).
Lifecycle transitions mark_managed_usage_provider_started and mark_managed_usage_client_delivered (lines 1043-1071).
Finalization calls finalize_managed_usage_request_microusd with outcome completed or failed; failed bills zero for billed and provider cost (lines 1140-1230).
Late completion after recovery is billed through a separate durable settlement, and an undelivered recovery absorbs provider cost visibly with an error log (lines 1087-1139, 1243-1274).
Provider cost and what the customer was billed are separate fields, and a served route can differ from the reserved route (lines 1140-1200, 1276-1289).

Attribution: schedule run, conversation, API key (lines 614-712), plus workload, project id and session id (apps/web/lib/billing/usage-attribution.ts:4-8), organization id (line 742) and artifact subject key (line 763).

Stranded reservations: a cron every 15 minutes releases them and drains the settlement queue, and also releases expired Free reservations and settles abandoned voice sessions (apps/web/app/api/cron/recover-reservations/route.ts:34-92; vercel.json:74-76).
The recovery job skips itself in low-power mode (recover-reservations/route.ts:40-41; apps/web/lib/server/cron-low-power.ts:17).
Refunds reverse credits: plan allowance and purchased credits are revoked in proportion to a refunded charge (apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/refund-events.ts:147-216).
incomplete: The ledger is the table managed_usage_requests plus credit tables; the brief calls it append-only, but whether rows are updated in place by the lifecycle functions was not checked: the service runs update statements against managed_usage_requests (managed-usage-request-service.ts:614-712), so 'append-only' is not established.
The usage reporting and export (S100.24) and the cost-of-goods ledger were not read for this page.
disconnected_or_disabled: A late settlement that is rejected leaves the cost absorbed and is only logged (managed-usage-request-service.ts:1115-1128).
not_available: No per-app difference: all apps share the server path. A ledger entry for Local or own-key turns: unknown.

established.statement: Each metered operation records a usage event (who, what model, how much, cost) into durable storage.
An append-only usage ledger holds every reservation, settlement and release so balances and windows can be recomputed.
Before a metered operation runs its estimated cost is reserved against the account's limits and balance.
After an operation the reservation is settled at actual cost and credits are deducted exactly once.
Unused or failed reservations are released, stranded ones recovered, and refunded purchases reverse their credits.
Costs are attributed to account, project, feature and model, and provider cost is kept separately from what the user is billed.
Allowance and purchased balance are distinct entitlements.
established.source: doc: docs/product/commercial.md (Allowance And Purchased Balance Are Distinct Entitlements)

established.statement: A cost of goods ledger exists.

acceptance_criteria: Sending the same idempotency key and body while a request is in progress returns 409 idempotency_in_progress; after it finishes returns 409 idempotency_replay; a different body returns 409 idempotency_conflict.
A completed request settles once at the actual cost; a failed request leaves billed and provider cost at zero and the hold released.
A reservation whose turn disappears is released by the recovery cron within its schedule and the user's window frees.
A request that completes after its lease was recovered is billed once through the late settlement or logged as absorbed.
An artifact call is refused when billed to usage credits, and refused when the per-app cap is reached.
A refunded top-up or plan charge revokes the matching credits in proportion, and a repeat of the same webhook revokes nothing more.
Each finalized request carries attribution fields where known (conversation, API key, schedule run, workload, project, session).
inferred: Settlement being idempotent by key is what makes overlapping cron runs safe [inferred from recover-reservations/route.ts:26-31 comment].
Balances are derived from the ledger and credit tables, not stored only as counters [inferred from the area brief; not verified in SQL].
proposed: [proposed] State in the brief whether the ledger is append-only or a lifecycle table, and align the wording.
[proposed] Add a page-level reconciliation that proves the sum of settlements equals the sum of credit deductions for a period.

steps.what_happens: The chat pipeline estimates the cost and calls reserve with an idempotency key and request hash.
A database function takes a per-user lock, checks caps and balance and writes the reservation row, returning a decision.
Attribution fields are written onto the row.
The server calls the model provider and streams the reply; lifecycle marks are written.
On end, finalize writes the billed cost and records the provider cost and served route.
If auto-reload applies and cost was positive, a reload check is triggered.
Every 15 minutes the cron recovers stale reservations and drains the settlement queue.

features.summary: Lets an eligible web account buy a plan on Stripe's hosted checkout, then keeps the stored plan in step with Stripe through signed, de-duplicated webhooks. A daily job compares billed plans to Stripe and emails a report. Stripe Tax calculates tax. New paying customers are currently gated by an access code or flag.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a Stripe subscription checkout for a verified account, returns the person to a page that waits for the webhook, applies subscription events in order, and compares billed plans to the catalog once a day (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/cron/reconcile-billed-plans/route.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a payment turns into a plan on every app, double billing is prevented, and drift between Stripe and the stored plan is noticed (S100.14 to S100.16, S100.20).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users who upgrade or buy Team seats, and operations staff who receive divergence reports. The desktop app reuses the web flow and opens Stripe in the browser.
problems_solved: Two live subscriptions for one customer (guard at checkout/route.ts:391-428).
Webhooks arriving twice or out of order (idempotency and event ordering, idempotency.ts:8-49; db.ts:1086-1100).
Silent drift between the stored plan and what Stripe bills (daily comparison, cron/reconcile-billed-plans/route.ts:71-160).
Wrong or missing tax (tax-policy.ts:98-112).
use_cases: A Free user with an access code chooses Premium and pays by card.
A buyer in India pays in INR with tax included in the price.
A webhook for an async bank payment arrives later and only then grants the plan (handlers.ts:89-111).
Operations receives an email when a stored plan differs from the Stripe price (reconcile cron lines 115-145).

where_to_find_it: Web: /upgrade and /upgrade/<plan> order screen, button 'Subscribe to <plan>' (apps/web/features/billing/components/UpgradeOrderPanel.tsx:584); Settings > Billing 'Payment' section (BillingSection.tsx:938).
Desktop: same screens; the 'Checkout opened in your browser. Pay there, then come back' notice (apps/web/features/billing/services/stripe-payments.ts:30-36).
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: do not sell through Stripe; CLI and Chrome open the web pricing page (claude_parity.rs:789-797; side_panel.ts:14139). Mobile store purchases are F100-05.
prerequisites: Signed in; an email is optional but used if available (checkout/route.ts:191-202).

The upgrade gate must allow the account: a live paid subscription, or the upgrades-open flag, or AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1, or a beta_redemptions row (billing-waitlist-access.ts:33-54; checkout/route.ts:297-310).
STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED not set off, and STRIPE_SECRET_KEY present (checkout/route.ts:58-62, 178-182).
screens_and_controls: Upgrade waitlist dialog: 'Join upgrade waitlist' and 'Have an access code?' (apps/web/features/billing/components/UpgradeWaitlistDialog.tsx:149, 161).
Order panel sections 'Order details', 'Payment method', 'Due today', 'Subtotal', 'Tax', 'Total due today' and 'Tax is calculated at checkout.' (UpgradeOrderPanel.tsx:320, 360, 391-446).
Stripe hosted checkout with terms-of-service consent, promotion codes, full billing address and tax ID collection (checkout/route.ts:517-523; tax-policy.ts:98-112).
Confirmation page /billing with 'Confirming checkout.' or 'You're all set.', 'Start chatting' and 'View billing' (apps/web/app/billing/UpgradeWelcome.tsx:96-166).
journey: Pick a plan on the upgrade page and press 'Subscribe to <plan>'.
The browser calls POST /api/checkout with plan, interval and an idempotency key.
If the gate refuses (403 code from WAITLIST_ACCESS_REQUIRED_CODE), the waitlist dialog opens.
On success the server returns a Stripe URL; the app remembers the pending session and opens it (stripe-payments.ts:222-253).
Pay on Stripe; Stripe returns to /billing?success=true&session_id=...
The server verifies the session belongs to the user; the page polls the account until the plan is active, up to 30 seconds (UpgradeWelcome.tsx:14-15, 77-90).
If it takes longer, the page says to check Billing and that the person was not charged twice (line 112-114).
feedback_and_outputs: 'Paid upgrades are opening in stages. Join the waitlist or enter an access code to continue.' when gated (billing-waitlist-access.ts:11-12).
'This account already has an active subscription with our payment provider. Open Billing to manage it...' on a double-billing refusal (checkout/route.ts:70-71).
'Paid-plan checkout is not available yet. Local and BYOK are free.' when switched off (checkout/route.ts:178-182).
A notification 'Your payment did not go through' on a failed invoice (handlers.ts:57-66).
settings: Trial and promotion codes in checkout (allow_promotion_codes true, checkout/route.ts:522).
Stripe billing portal for payment methods and cancellation (stripe-payments.ts:189).

working: Checkout creates a subscription-mode Stripe session with catalog version in metadata, terms consent, promotion codes, automatic tax, tax ID collection and required billing address (checkout/route.ts:460-523; apps/web/lib/billing/tax-policy.ts:98-112).
Price comes from the localized price selection and is refused when Stripe's amount or tax behavior does not match the catalog (checkout/route.ts:231-237; localized-pricing-service.ts:140-180).

Refuses if Stripe already bills a live subscription for the stored customer, if another checkout just completed, or if the billing owner is another channel (checkout/route.ts:312-314, 391-428, 486-492, 551-559).
If the stored Stripe customer no longer exists, drops it and creates a fresh one (checkout/route.ts:396-413).
Open earlier checkouts for the same user are expired before a new one is created (checkout/route.ts:468-492).
CSRF token, rate limit key 'checkout', deadline and circuit are applied (checkout/route.ts:173-189, 610-616).

Webhook: rate limit, signature check with a 60 second tolerance (400 on wrong or missing signature, logged as an invalid signature), idempotency by event id through a database function, then dispatch and mark succeeded in one transaction (stripe-webhook/route.ts:33-95; lib/verify.ts:15-51; lib/idempotency.ts:8-70).

Subscription created, updated and invoice events update plan and status; an older event cannot overwrite a newer one, and a canceled subscription is not resurrected (handlers.ts:135-165; db.ts:1086-1111).
Async-payment checkouts grant the plan only on async_payment_succeeded (handlers.ts:89-113).
Cancellation sets the plan to free and ends enterprise contracts (handlers.ts:176-221).

Daily job at 01:11 compares billed plans against Stripe, logs, emails a report, and re-queues review if the email cannot be sent; it repairs nothing (vercel.json:174-175; cron/reconcile-billed-plans/route.ts:71-160).
Top-ups use the same tax parameters (apps/web/app/api/billing/top-up/route.ts:250).
incomplete: Tax on mid-cycle plan changes through /api/upgrade was not found in that route; tax handling there is unknown (apps/web/app/api/upgrade/route.ts).
disconnected_or_disabled: Paid acquisition is gated: without the upgrades-open flag, AGI_BILLING_WAITLIST_OPEN=1 or a redeemed code, a non-paying account gets HTTP 403 (checkout/route.ts:297-310; doc: docs/product/commercial.md Paid Acquisition Gate).
STRIPE_CHECKOUT_ENABLED set to 0, false or off closes checkout (checkout/route.ts:58-62).
Pending checkout confirmation component renders nothing; it only polls and redirects to /billing (apps/web/features/billing/components/PendingCheckoutConfirmation.tsx:16-70).
not_available: Stripe checkout on mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome: none found; they send the person to the web (side_panel.ts:14139; claude_parity.rs:789).

established.statement: A checkout adapter creates a payment-provider checkout for any eligible user and returns them to a verified result.
Subscription state is kept in sync with the payment provider, in order, with periodic reconciliation.
A webhook endpoint verifies provider signatures, processes each event exactly once and handles the billing event types.
Tax is calculated by an integrated tax engine for every charge, including tax IDs and reverse charge.
Paid upgrades stay behind the access gate; the presence of working checkout code does not open paid purchasing.
established.source: doc: docs/product/commercial.md (Payment Guidance, Paid Acquisition Gate)

established.statement: One billing owner per user; a second channel loses while the first is entitled.
established.source: doc: docs/product/commercial.md (Subscription Ownership Across The Suite)

established.statement: Yearly billing is withdrawn for individual plans; checkout refuses it with a message naming the cadence sold.

acceptance_criteria: A gated account posting to /api/checkout gets 403 with the waitlist access code; after opening the flag or redeeming a code it receives a Stripe URL.
A customer with a live Stripe subscription cannot start a second checkout and sees the active-subscription message.
A webhook with a wrong signature returns 400 and is logged; the same valid event delivered twice processes once.
An older subscription update delivered after a newer one does not change the stored plan or status.
After paying, /billing shows 'Confirming checkout.' and then 'You're all set.' with the right plan, without a manual refresh, within 30 seconds in the normal case.
Tax is computed on the Stripe session for USD and the INR price includes tax; tax ID entry is offered.
The daily reconcile job returns the number examined and diverged and emails a report when a divergence exists.
inferred: A webhook failure returns 500 so Stripe retries, because the event is marked failed (stripe-webhook/route.ts:77-95) [inferred from Stripe retry behaviour].
The pending-confirmation component and the /billing page together make the return trip trustworthy, because /billing only accepts a session id that belongs to the user (app/billing/page.tsx:16-41).
proposed: [proposed] Make the reconcile job able to repair, or add a runbook step for each drift type.
[proposed] Show tax and total on the order panel before the Stripe page, in every currency.

steps.what_happens: The person presses Subscribe; the browser posts plan and interval with a CSRF header and a fresh idempotency key.
The server checks CSRF, the on/off switch, rate limit and the plan-change gate, then validates the request and resolves the purchasable plan.
The server asks Stripe for the price and checks amount and tax behavior.
The server applies the acquisition gate, the billing-owner rule, finds or creates the Stripe customer, and refuses if Stripe already bills a subscription.
The server expires earlier open checkouts, creates the Stripe session and records a checkout_started audit event.
The person pays on Stripe's page in the browser; Stripe calculates tax.
Stripe sends events; the server checks the signature, de-duplicates and updates the subscription row in one transaction.
The return page verifies the session and the app polls the account until the plan is active.
Once a day the cron compares each billed subscription to Stripe and emails a report.

features.summary: Lets the mobile app sell plans and credit top-ups through the Apple App Store and Google Play. The server checks each store receipt, records the grant and tells the store it was delivered. It is off in the current mobile build, and also off on the server unless a deployment switch is set.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists store products for an account, verifies a purchase receipt with Apple or Google, grants the matching plan or credits once, acknowledges the purchase with the store, and processes store renewal and refund notifications (apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap/catalog/route.ts; verify/route.ts; lib/server/mobile-iap-store-verification.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: Phone stores require their own billing for in-app digital sales, and the account must still have one plan across all apps (doc: docs/product/commercial.md, Subscription Ownership Across The Suite; S100.17).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on iPhone or Android when selling is turned on; operations who configure store products.
problems_solved: Granting a plan for an unverified or reused receipt (receipt bound to one account, verify route test returns 403 for a receipt bound elsewhere, apps/web/app/api/mobile/iap/verify/__tests__/route.test.ts:245-255).
A purchase left unacknowledged and auto-refunded by Google (verify/route.ts:28-51).
Two billing owners for one account (catalog hides plans while another channel bills, catalog/route.ts:175-179).
use_cases: A signed-in iPhone user buys a subscription in the app; the server verifies it and the plan appears on every app.
A paying user buys a credit top-up in the app.
After reinstalling, the user taps Restore purchases and unfinished purchases are processed.
With selling off, the person sees a message that nothing was charged.

working: Catalog endpoint returns enabled false with a named reason when the deployment switch is off, no products are registered, the kill switch is on, deletion is scheduled, store consent was withdrawn, or another channel bills the plan (mobile-iap-catalog.ts:127-150; catalog/route.ts:59-186).
Catalog also creates or reads a per-user app account token used to bind purchases (catalog/route.ts:159-169).
Product id maps are validated: unknown keys, duplicate store ids and a missing Google base plan are errors (mobile-iap-catalog.ts:63-114).

Verify validates the body, resolves the product, requires an existing app account token, verifies with the store, records the grant, then acknowledges Google purchases after the grant is committed; an acknowledgement failure is logged and the result is still returned (verify/route.ts:53-114).
A purchase that was charged but cannot be granted files a refund request (apps/web/lib/services/mobile-iap-ledger-service.ts:319-368).
Apple and Google renewal and refund notifications have their own routes (app/api/mobile/iap/apple-notifications/route.ts; google-notifications/route.ts).
The mobile app has the purchase hook, restore flow and catalog parse tests (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/useMobileIap.ts; __tests__).
incomplete: Verify does not itself re-check the deployment switch or the kill switch; it resolves the product from the configured maps, so with the switch off no product resolves and the call is refused (verify/route.ts:65-66; mobile-iap-catalog.ts:127-157 resolveMobileIapProduct reads maps only). Whether a stale map would let a verify through while the catalog says off was not established.

The brief lists a waitlist redemption requirement for the catalog; the catalog and verify routes do not read beta_redemptions and their tests assert they do not (catalog/__tests__/route.test.ts:156-159; verify/__tests__/route.test.ts:242-245).
disconnected_or_disabled: The mobile build flag nativePurchases is false: the app shows no purchase, upgrade, top-up or restore control and the store connection is not opened (apps/mobile/src/features/billing/storePurchases.json:2-10; nativePurchaseAvailability.ts:3; cloud-billing/index.tsx:351).
MOBILE_IAP_ENABLED is off unless set to 1, true or yes (mobile-iap-catalog.ts:53-56).
Docs confirm mobile v1 sells nothing in the app (doc: docs/product/commercial.md, Launch Posture and Paid Acquisition Gate).

steps.what_happens: The Subscription screen asks the server for the catalog with platform and storefront.
The server decides if selling is enabled, checks the kill switch, deletion and consent state, and the subscription owner, and creates the app account token.
The person pays in the store's own sheet.
The app posts platform, product id and purchase token to verify.
The server verifies the receipt with Apple or Google, checking it is for this account's token.
The server records the grant (plan or credits), or files a refund request if it was charged but cannot be granted.
The server acknowledges a Google purchase, writes an audit event and returns the result; the app finishes the transaction.

features.summary: Shows a person their recent Stripe invoices and receipts, lets them request a refund on a payment, and applies refunds and card disputes to the plan and credits. Simple cases refund automatically; the rest go to staff. A won dispute restores the plan and credits; a lost one ends the held plan.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists the account's latest 24 invoices with links to the receipt and PDF; accepts customer refund requests and decides them by rule or sends them to an operator; reverses credits for refunded charges; places a hold on the plan and revokes credits when a dispute opens and restores or finalizes them when it closes.
purpose.why_it_exists: Customers need receipts and a fair way to get money back, laws give statutory withdrawal rights in some countries, and card disputes must not leave credits spendable that the money no longer backs (S100.18, S100.19; apps/web/lib/services/billing-refund-service.ts:389-420).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying customers (invoices, refund request form); operations staff (refund operations page); Stripe and the card networks as event sources.
problems_solved: No proof of payment (Invoices and receipts page).
Refund requests handled by hand every time (automatic settlement for statutory and unused cases, billing-refund-service.ts:713-775).
Credits spent after a refund or lost dispute (credit reversal, refund-events.ts:147-216; dispute-events.ts:166-265).
use_cases: A customer opens Invoices and receipts to download a PDF for expenses.
A customer in the EEA or UK requests a refund within 14 days and is refunded in proportion to unused credits.
A customer who never used the plan asks within 7 days and is refunded automatically.
A bank dispute opens: the plan goes on hold and credits are revoked until it closes.

where_to_find_it: Web: /billing/invoices headed 'Invoices and receipts', with 'Back to billing' on small screens (apps/web/app/billing/invoices/page.tsx:26, 22-24); Settings > Billing has an 'Invoices' section (BillingSection.tsx:1056).
Web: refund request form on the refund policy page with 'Choose a payment…', 'Choose a reason…' and 'Your requests' (apps/web/app/refund-policy/RefundRequestForm.tsx:261, 283, 328).
Web admin: Refund operations page (apps/web/features/admin/pages/RefundOperationsPage.tsx).
Desktop: same web pages. Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no invoice or refund screen found; mobile store purchases are refunded by the store (billing-refund-service.ts:1107-1151).
prerequisites: Signed in; a Stripe customer on the account for invoices and refunds (billing-invoice-service.ts:54).
Staff with admin access for operator actions (api/admin/billing-refunds).
screens_and_controls: Invoice table with columns Date, Invoice, Total, Status, Receipt (InvoiceList.tsx:127-140).
Messages 'Loading your invoices', 'No invoices yet. A paid plan produces one each billing period, and it appears here.', and 'Try again' on error (InvoiceList.tsx:70-110).
Refund form fields: payment, reason, details (RefundRequestForm.tsx:252-299).
journey: Open Billing, then Invoices and receipts; the page loads invoices from the server.
Download the PDF or open the hosted receipt.
To ask for a refund, open the refund form, choose the payment and a reason, add details, and send.
The server records the request and may refund at once or leave it pending for review; the person is notified of the decision.
The plan and credits change follow the refund.
feedback_and_outputs: A message when invoices are not available, or older invoices exist in the billing portal (InvoiceList.tsx:98-122).
A status heading after a refund request (RefundRequestForm.tsx:238).
A notification of the decision: card refund takes 5 to 10 business days, store refund goes to the store payment method (billing-refund-service.ts:560-566).
A notification 'Your plan and credits are back' when a dispute is won (dispute-events.ts:431-441).
settings: None for the person; refund windows are 14 days statutory and 7 days for unused plans, set in apps/web/lib/billing/refund-requests.ts:1-2.

working: Invoices are read live from Stripe for the stored customer, newest first, at most 24, with line items; store and organization invoices are excluded (billing-invoice-service.ts:29, 38-102; invoices/page.tsx:28-30). Rate limit key billing-invoices (api/billing/invoices/route.ts:14).
Customer refund requests: GET lists requests and refundable charges; POST files a request with CSRF, rate limit and an audit event refund_requested (api/billing/refund-requests/route.ts:48-137).

Assessment: billing-error reasons go to review; statutory withdrawal in the EEA and UK within 14 days refunds the unused share; an unused plan or top-up within 7 days with no earlier discretionary refund refunds in full; otherwise review (billing-refund-service.ts:389-420; refund-requests.ts:1-2).
Automatic settlement retries safely and leaves the request pending if Stripe refuses or is unfinished (billing-refund-service.ts:713-775).
Operator tools: issue a refund, decline, record a store refund, look up an account (billing-refund-service.ts:890-1181; api/admin/billing-refunds/route.ts:228-229).

On a refunded plan charge the current period's plan allowance is revoked in proportion and a full refund ends the entitlement; on a refunded top-up purchased credits are revoked (refund-events.ts:147-250, 251-342).

Dispute opened: plan moves to past_due with cancel at period end, collection is paused, credits are revoked and recorded; won disputes restore credits and lift the hold; lost disputes end the plan (dispute-events.ts:166-265, 379-451, 483-528).
Refund and dispute events arrive on the same webhook as checkout (handlers.ts:305-324).
Refunds also reverse referral rewards (handlers.ts:307, 316).
incomplete: Early fraud warnings are only recorded; what to do about them is undecided (handlers.ts:325-365).
A refunded plan's Stripe subscription is left alone unless an operator cancels it; the code notes this in a warning (refund-events.ts:239-244).
disconnected_or_disabled: Refunds need Stripe configured, else the form route says 'Refunds are not available in this deployment.' (refund-requests/route.ts:92-96).
not_available: Invoice or refund screens in the mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome apps: none found. Store invoices: not listed (invoices/page.tsx:28-30).

established.statement: An invoice service produces and lists invoices for each account with downloadable documents.
Refunds and disputes are processed end to end: issued, reflected in plan and credits, and reversed when a dispute is won.
Refund and chargeback policy and a dispute reserve are launch requirements for managed credits.
Legal copies the leaders and the stricter wins; statutory withdrawal rights apply in the EEA and UK.

acceptance_criteria: The invoice page lists up to 24 invoices newest first with Date, Invoice, Total, Status and Receipt, and says when older ones exist.
With no Stripe customer the page says 'No invoices yet.'; with Stripe not configured it says invoices cannot be shown.
A refund request for a payment not on the account is refused with 404 'That payment is not on your account.'
A request inside the withdrawal window from an EEA or UK billing country is assessed statutory_withdrawal and refunded at the unused share.
A fully refunded plan charge for the current period revokes the plan and revokes credits; a repeat webhook delivery revokes nothing more.
A dispute opening revokes credits and holds the plan; a won dispute restores the credits and the plan; a lost one leaves them revoked and ends the plan.
Each refund request filing writes a refund_requested audit event.
inferred: An operator decision must also notify the customer; the code returns customerNotified for that purpose [inferred from billing-refund-service.ts:1107-1181].
Statutory country lists should come from one shared EEA list [inferred from the import of EEA_COUNTRY_CODES, billing-refund-service.ts:23].
proposed: [proposed] Add an invoice list for store-billed customers or link to the store receipt.
[proposed] Decide the rule for early fraud warnings and record it in docs/product/commercial.md.

steps.what_happens: The invoices page requests the list from the server.
The server looks up the stored Stripe customer and asks Stripe for the invoices.
A refund request is posted; the server checks CSRF, rate limit and that the charge belongs to the account, assesses it and may refund through Stripe at once.
Stripe processes the refund and later sends charge.refunded.
The webhook revokes credits in proportion and ends the entitlement for a fully refunded current period, in one transaction with de-duplication.
A dispute event revokes credits, pauses collection in Stripe and moves the plan to past_due; the close event restores or finalizes.
The person gets a notification of the outcome.

features.summary: Lets people redeem Stripe promotion codes when they subscribe or upgrade, and lets any signed-in person share a referral link. A friend who joins gets a trial and bonus credits after their first payment. The referrer earns bonus credits after a 14-day hold. Staff can also run usage-limit promotions and grant goodwill credits.

purpose.what_it_does: Four separate mechanisms sit under this name. (1) Promotion codes: Web checkout is a Stripe-hosted page that is created with promotion codes switched on (apps/web/app/api/checkout/route.ts:522); the in-app upgrade flow takes a code, checks it against Stripe and prices the upgrade with it (apps/web/app/api/upgrade/route.ts:259-349). (2) Referrals: each account can get one referral code and link, a /r/<code> visit stores a cookie, sign-up attaches the new account to the code, the friend's first paid invoice converts it, and a daily job pays the referrer after a hold (apps/web/lib/services/referral-service.ts:197-520; apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/referral-events.ts:114-195). (3) Bonus credits: a grant table with sources referral_referrer, referral_friend and promo (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:11). (4) Usage-limit promotions: platform admins define time-boxed limit resets or uplifts for paid plans (apps/web/lib/services/usage-limit-promotion-service.ts:84-129; apps/web/app/api/admin/usage-promotions/route.ts).
purpose.why_it_exists: To grow sign-ups through invitations, to let sales and marketing discount a plan, and to give staff a controlled way to give credits or extra allowance. The brief says a promotion service should create and apply promo codes, bonus credits and invite grants, and a referral service should issue codes, attribute sign-ups and grant rewards (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.22, S100.23).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in account (referral link, promotion code at checkout or upgrade), referred friends, platform admins (usage promotions, goodwill credits), and finance or support staff who read the operator tools.
problems_solved: A person with a discount code can use it on a Stripe checkout or on a plan upgrade.
A person can invite friends and earn credits only when the friend really pays.
Abuse is limited: disposable emails, email aliases, same network, same device and same card are refused, and refunds or disputes claw the reward back.
Staff can give a bounded, expiring promotion without editing code.
use_cases: A new user opens a friend's /r/<code> link, signs up, starts the paid plan with a 7-day trial, pays, and both receive bonus credits.
An existing subscriber upgrades a plan, types a promotion code, sees the discounted preview and confirms.
A person opens Settings, Referrals, copies the invite link or shares it.
A platform admin saves a time-boxed limit-reset promotion with a cost ceiling.

established.statement: A promotion service creates and applies promo codes, bonus credits and invite grants to accounts.
A referral service issues referral codes, attributes sign-ups and grants rewards.
Referral rewards follow the leaders and stricter policy wins; product and policy calls follow ChatGPT and Claude.
Referral terms are linked at checkout when a referral trial applies.

acceptance_criteria: Visiting /r/<valid code> redirects to /r/welcome and sets an httpOnly agi_referral cookie lasting 30 days; an invalid code redirects to sign-up with no cookie.
A sign-up within 24 hours through a code is stored as signed_up; the same account cannot be attributed twice.
A friend sign-up with a disposable email, the referrer's email alias or the referrer's network is stored as blocked.

The friend's first paid invoice sets the referral to converted and adds bonus credits to the friend; the referrer receives credits only after the 14-day hold and only under the monthly and yearly caps.
A refund or dispute on the qualifying invoice revokes both grants and marks the referral clawed_back.
An upgrade with an expired, fully redeemed or non-applying code is refused with a plain message and the plan is unchanged.
The Referrals page shows the code, link, counts and a state for each friend, and shows an error with retry when loading fails.

[inferred] Bonus credits are spent only on Cloud usage because they sit in the managed credit ledger (apps/web/lib/services/bonus-credit-service.ts:164-200).
proposed: [proposed] Write an audit event for referral reward grants, clawbacks and promotion applications; none is written today.
[proposed] Show the referral link on mobile and in the VS Code extension, or document that they are web-only.
[proposed] Add an in-app promotion-code field to first checkout, matching the upgrade panel.

aliases: Seats, team admin and admin API
features.summary: Tracks how many paid seats a workspace has and how many are used, lets admins invite members within that limit, and lets admins run the workspace through scoped API keys. Enterprise workspaces can also sync users from their identity provider through SCIM. Everything is on the web and server; no other app was found to manage seats.

purpose.what_it_does: Seat service: the organizations table holds licensed_seats and a trigger-maintained seats_consumed, with a database check that seats used cannot pass seats licensed (apps/web/db/neon/0085_organization_seats_lifecycle.sql:24-60; apps/web/lib/services/organization-seat-service.ts:30-60). Stripe webhook code writes purchased seats onto the organization (apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/seats.ts:90-200). Invitations are created, listed and expired by the Team settings API (apps/web/app/api/settings/team/invitations/route.ts:60-160). Admin API: workspace API keys with the prefix agiadm_ act as service principals with scopes (apps/web/lib/server/admin-api-keys.ts:19, 95-130; apps/web/lib/server/compliance-caller.ts:36-85). SCIM: a bearer token acts for one workspace and provisions users and groups (apps/web/lib/server/scim/scim-auth.ts:30-120).
purpose.why_it_exists: So teams pay for the number of people they have, admins cannot add past that number, and large customers can manage people from their own identity system. The brief asks for a seat service that tracks purchased seats, assigns and enforces them, and an authenticated, scoped administrative API (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.21, S100.26).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins (Team or Enterprise plan), automation that holds a workspace API key, and identity providers calling SCIM.
problems_solved: Prevents more members than paid seats, even when two admins act at once (database check).
Lets an admin invite someone who has no account yet.
Lets automation read audit data and manage members with only the permissions it was given.
Lets an identity provider create, update and remove members automatically.
use_cases: An owner invites a colleague by email with role member and sees seats used go up.
An admin creates a workspace API key with the audit.read scope to export the audit trail from a script.
An identity provider calls /api/scim/v2/Users to provision a new hire.
An owner at the seat limit is told to free a seat or buy more.

established.statement: A seat/license service tracks purchased seats, assigns them to members and enforces the count.
Organization admins can manage their workspace programmatically through an authenticated, scoped administrative API.
Invitations list and create require team admin access; list expires pending invites and returns seat state.
A destructive or irreversible action asks first and names the consequence.
Every subscription capability connects to one AGI Subscription system.

acceptance_criteria: An admin on a Team plan can create an invitation; a member without members.manage is refused.
When seats used equals seats licensed, a new invitation or acceptance is refused with the 'no licensed seats available' message.
The invitation list marks expired invitations before returning and includes licensed, used and available seats.
A workspace API key for a workspace that lost its Team entitlement is refused with 'require an active Team or Enterprise subscription'.
A key scoped only for one permission is refused on a route needing another.
A request with a bearer token that is not a workspace key is refused and never falls back to the cookie session.
A SCIM request with a bad token gets 401; for a locked-down workspace gets 403 and a sync.denied event; on a non-Enterprise plan is refused.
inferred: [inferred] Seats consumed count active members plus pending invitations, because accepting an invitation must release its seat before taking one (apps/web/db/neon/0085_organization_seats_lifecycle.sql:36-45).
[inferred] The same permission model applies to people and keys, because routes declare one permission per route (apps/web/lib/server/service-principals/caller.ts:36-60).
proposed: [proposed] Show seats and invitations in the desktop and mobile apps as a link to the web page.
[proposed] Allow usage analytics export for workspace keys with billing.read scope.
[proposed] Document the SCIM Enterprise-only rule beside the Team plan page.

features.summary: Shows a person how many credits they used over time, by product area and by model, and lets them download the records as CSV. Workspace admins see the same for the whole workspace, by day, member, model, provider, workload or project, and can export it. All of it reads the managed usage ledger, so it covers Cloud usage only.

purpose.what_it_does: Personal history: GET /api/usage/history groups settled managed usage by day, week or month and breaks it down by product area and model, with an optional workload filter (apps/web/app/api/usage/history/route.ts:36-61; apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:197-250). Personal export: GET /api/usage/export returns CSV of up to 10,000 records (apps/web/app/api/usage/export/route.ts; apps/web/lib/services/account-usage-history-service.ts:30). Workspace: GET usage-analytics and its export route return totals and breakdowns for admins (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/usage-analytics/export/route.ts:55-120).
purpose.why_it_exists: People need to see what their credits paid for and finance teams need to reconcile it. The brief asks that usage reporting aggregates the ledger by time, model and feature for accounts and workspaces, with export (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.24).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any signed-in Cloud user for personal usage; workspace admins with the billing.read permission on a Team or Enterprise plan for workspace usage; API callers with the usage:read scope.
problems_solved: Explains where credits went.
Gives finance a file that matches the dashboard.
Lets scripts and the CLI read the same history.
Warns when part of the breakdown was cut off.

An admin opens the workspace Usage page, selects 30 days and presses 'Export daily CSV'.

features.summary: Stores a signed enterprise agreement per workspace: committed seats, term, payment terms, purchase order, payment method policy and support tier. Stripe subscription and invoice events keep a billing-contract record in sync, and admins can record bank payments or end a contract. Creating agreements has no screen or caller in the code read.

purpose.what_it_does: A versioned agreement store keeps each commercial agreement as a new row that supersedes the last (apps/web/lib/services/enterprise-contracts/agreement-store.ts:193-358). Stripe webhooks sync a billing-contract summary and invoice records from subscriptions and invoices (apps/web/app/api/stripe-webhook/lib/handlers.ts:127-160; apps/web/lib/services/enterprise-billing-service.ts:359-556, 707-810). Invoicing code computes invoice positions, checks them against the agreement and records offline payments idempotently (apps/web/lib/services/enterprise-contracts/invoicing.ts:144-330). The workspace console shows contract terms and invoices (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceEnterpriseContract.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: Enterprise customers buy by contract, pay by invoice or transfer and need purchase order numbers. The brief says enterprise contracts (committed seats, invoicing terms, PO, offline payment) are stored and drive billing (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.25).
purpose.who_uses_it: Sales and staff who author agreements, workspace admins with billing.read who read them, and operators with billing.contracts.manage who report offline payments or end a contract.
problems_solved: Keeps the signed terms as the record, with history of amendments.
Stops payment methods the contract does not allow.
Lets a bank payment be recorded once, even if the form is submitted twice.
Lets support priority follow the contracted support tier.
use_cases: An admin opens the workspace billing page and reads term, committed seats, payment terms and purchase order.
An operator reports a wire payment against an invoice with a bank reference.
Sales records an amendment that raises committed seats.
A contract ends and the workspace is returned to the self-serve state.

features.summary: Lets a signed-in person open a support ticket, see their tickets and read and answer the thread. Priority comes from the contracted support tier. Staff see a queue, reply (the customer gets an email) and can escalate. Web has a tickets panel in Help settings and mobile has Support screens in Cloud mode. Other apps link out.

purpose.what_it_does: POST /api/support/tickets creates a ticket with the person's reply email, message, optional diagnostics and optional live-handoff id; GET lists the person's tickets; GET and PATCH on a ticket read the thread, add a reply or close it (apps/web/app/api/support/tickets/route.ts:28-80; apps/web/app/api/support/tickets/[ticketId]/route.ts). Staff list, read, reply and escalate through staff routes (apps/web/app/api/support/staff/tickets/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/support/tickets/[ticketId]/escalate/route.ts).

The brief says cases are created with account context, routed to staff and threaded with replies (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in customers; support staff who are platform admins; on-call engineers paged for urgent escalations.
problems_solved: A bug report reaches staff with redacted diagnostics.
Enterprise customers are not queued behind free visitors.
Customers get an email when staff reply.
A resolved ticket reopens when the customer answers.
use_cases: A user on web opens Settings, Help, fills 'What happened' and presses 'Raise ticket'.
A mobile user in Cloud mode raises a ticket from Support.
A staff member replies and marks the ticket resolved.

features.summary: Writes a durable record when someone does something that matters, such as starting a checkout, changing a plan, inviting a member or creating a key. Workspace admins can browse the audit trail and export it as JSONL, unless the workspace policy switches export off. Every export, allowed or denied, is itself recorded.

purpose.what_it_does: recordAuditEvent writes to security_audit_logs and, when the event has an organization, to the workspace trail enterprise_audit_events through a database function (apps/web/lib/security-audit.ts:610-731). The workspace audit route lists events and the export route streams them as JSONL (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/audit/route.ts; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/audit/export/route.ts:50-155). Audit logs cannot be updated or deleted by the runtime role (apps/web/db/neon/0043_audit_log_immutability.sql; 0123_audit_log_immutability_trigger.sql).
purpose.why_it_exists: So billing and admin actions can be reviewed later, by customers and by staff. The brief asks that commercial and administrative actions write durable audit events that can be queried later (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/100-commercial-and-administrative-components.md S100.28).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins with audit.read, security reviewers, workspace API keys scoped to audit.read, and staff investigating incidents.
problems_solved: Shows who changed a plan, a role, a key or a seat.
Lets a customer take its audit trail into its own tools.
Lets a policy stop bulk export.
Proves that exports themselves were requested.
use_cases: An admin filters by outcome denied and by severity warning on /workspace/audit.
An admin presses 'Export JSONL' and gets agi-audit-<org>-<date>.jsonl.
A script with an audit.read key pulls the trail nightly.
An owner turns off 'Allow audit export' and later export attempts are refused and logged.

features.summary: A shared package of zod schemas (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts) names each request and response body once, so the server and the apps read the same shape. Golden JSON examples let the CLI's Rust code check itself against the same data. 141 client-called web routes still have no shared schema and sit on a shrinking baseline list.

purpose.what_it_does: Declares one schema per wire message (device sign-in, sync of chats, memory and projects, connectors, notifications, managed media, usage and billing figures) in shared packages, and guards that fail the build when a client-called route or a Rust client drifts from them (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/device-authorization.ts:9; scripts/check-route-shared-contracts.mjs:1; scripts/check-cli-wire-parity.mjs:28).
purpose.why_it_exists: Two sides that each write their own copy of a body shape disagree after the first change on either side. The route guard says only a schema both sides import survives such a change (scripts/lib/route-shared-contracts.mjs:1-8). The architecture overview has a 'Shared Contracts' section and says to read from shared contracts instead of surface-local copies (doc: docs/architecture/overview.md:31,108).
purpose.who_uses_it: Engineers who add or change an API field; the web server routes; the Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome and VS Code TypeScript clients; the Rust CLI through its own struct mirrors. End users never touch it.

Rust CLI structs that drift from the TypeScript schema (scripts/check-cli-wire-parity.mjs:28)
Clients that guess at a body that does not match

features.summary: One shared vocabulary for durable event names, message content-block kinds, error codes with classes and retry rules, primary-key rules and notification categories. Guards check emitters, block readers, error use and key names. The brief's error-definition cites point to a 31-line file; the real owner is error-taxonomy.ts.

purpose.what_it_does: Defines names once: domain events as namespace.object.verb (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/domain-events.ts:20-61), message block kinds (packages/contracts/types/src/conversation.ts:15), error classes with a retry flag (packages/contracts/types/src/error-taxonomy.ts:15-58), key rules (packages/contracts/types/src/identifier-contract.json) and notification categories (packages/contracts/types/src/notifications.ts:11).
purpose.why_it_exists: Without one list each app names things its own way, and a new block kind reaches an old build as an empty bubble. The code says a kind added to the list reaches an older build as an unknown block it degrades (packages/contracts/types/src/conversation.ts:9-14).
purpose.who_uses_it: Engineers; the web audit pipeline; Web, Desktop, Mobile, Chrome and VS Code renderers; the Mobile notification feed.
problems_solved: Two names for the same event (a closed verb list makes synonyms impossible, packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/domain-events.ts:10-19)
Unknown content blocks dropped silently
A storage outage and a defect arriving as one status (packages/contracts/types/src/error-taxonomy.ts:1-6)
Primary keys that encode a name, address or file name (packages/contracts/types/src/identifier-contract.ts:1-9)
use_cases: A workspace admin removes a member; the audit event member_removed becomes workspace.member.revoked (apps/web/lib/audit-domain-events.ts:25)
A model replies with a block an old Chrome build cannot draw; the client lists it among unknownBlocks and degrades it (packages/contracts/types/src/client-capability-manifest.ts:145-164)
A request fails with a class that says 'not retryable'; the client reads the flag instead of guessing (packages/contracts/types/src/error-taxonomy.ts:87)
A Mobile user opens the notification feed and each row carries a shared category and severity (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/notifications.ts:9-18)

established.statement: One authentication client (sign-in, device flow, token refresh) is shared by every client surface.
Every client calls the server through the same API client modules.
One streaming client (SSE reading, reconnect, event parsing) is shared by every client.
Device refusals are pending, slow_down, denied, expired, invalid, account unavailable or terms acceptance required, and a review refusal must point to the acceptance URL.
Every SSE reader in a client module is either the shared reader or recorded with its owner; the record only shrinks.
Account approval signs the device into the account; Local mode needs no account access.

acceptance_criteria: The token route answers pending until approval, then a bearer token with a positive lifetime
slow_down makes the next poll at least 5 seconds slower
A device whose account must accept terms shows the acceptance link and does not sign in
A stream cut mid-answer on Mobile shows a lost-connection error, never a finished answer
A frame over the limit is refused under every chunk split
A new hand-written SSE splitter in a client file fails check:sse-readers
A device-start reply with a verification URL on another origin is refused

features.summary: A shared message queue holds follow-ups sent while an answer streams; VS Code caps it at 20, the shared default is 100 per priority lane. A shared reducer builds agent activity. A shared sync package handles cursors, deltas and tombstones. Task states map to board stages; Chrome reads that map to cancel scheduled runs.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps conversation state moves in shared code: a priority message queue (packages/client/client-runtime/src/queue/messageQueueManager.ts), an activity reducer (packages/client/client-runtime/src/agentActivity.ts:484), a sync package for cursors, conversation, message, memory, project and settings deltas and tombstones (packages/client/sync/src), and one task-state to board-stage map (packages/contracts/types/src/cross-device.ts:413-431).
purpose.why_it_exists: A client that drops a deleted row keeps no record the deletion reached it, so its next push re-creates the row (packages/client/sync/src/tombstones.ts:1-6). Each client inventing its own queue or lifecycle names makes states disagree.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who type follow-ups mid-answer, use more than one device, or schedule runs; engineers.

features.summary: Tools, approvals, skill manifests and the local coding-session protocol are each declared once. The tool registry guard has an empty undeclared list. Approval request and resume bodies are shared. Skill manifests are tested against one golden file in TypeScript and Rust. The coding-session protocol is generated from Rust and CI checks drift.

purpose.what_it_does: Declares every first-party tool with risk facets in one table (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-metadata.ts:101), shares approval request and resume schemas (packages/contracts/cloud-contracts/src/tool-approval-resume.ts:34), parses SKILL.md manifests in one package checked against a golden file (packages/tools/skills/src/__tests__/manifest-fixtures.test.ts), and generates TypeScript protocol types from Rust (scripts/generate-protocol-types.mjs).

purpose.who_uses_it: People who approve or deny assistant actions, install skills, or use VS Code or Desktop with a local runtime; engineers.

features.summary: One package owns colours, radii, type and motion values for every screen. A shared web component library, a shared string catalogue and a mobile primitive layer sit on top. Each surface renders Markdown itself with some shared helpers. Guards fail the build when a screen uses an unknown token or a raw mobile control.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the six apps one source for visual values (colour, corner radius, type, motion), one catalogue of translated strings, a shared web component library for Web and Desktop, a native component layer for Mobile, and shared Markdown helper code (fence classification, math and task-list plugins, source normalisation) that each surface plugs into its own renderer. Guards in scripts/ enforce the rules (packages/ui/design-tokens/package.json; packages/ui/ui/package.json; packages/ui/i18n/package.json; scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs; scripts/check-mobile-primitives.mjs).
purpose.why_it_exists: The product competes with Claude and ChatGPT, so chat must look and read the same on every app. A private copy of a colour or string drifts. The design-tokens package describes itself as 'the only sanctioned source of color, spacing and type values' (packages/ui/design-tokens/package.json:4). AGENTS.md section 4 forbids hardcoding design values (doc: AGENTS.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Engineers who build screens on any app; testers who compare a screen with the design; people using the apps, who see consistent text, colour and corners.
problems_solved: Colour or radius drift between Web, Chrome side panel, VS Code panel and Mobile.
A stylesheet referring to a custom property nobody defined, which leaves the element unstyled (scripts/check-css-tokens.mjs).
Mobile touch targets built from raw platform controls that skip theme, type scale and accessibility role (scripts/check-mobile-primitives.mjs:3-8).
Translated strings that exist in one language but not in another (scripts/check-i18n-parity.mjs).
use_cases: An engineer changes a brand colour once in packages/ui/design-tokens and Web, Chrome, VS Code and Mobile pick it up.
A tester opens a Markdown answer in the Chrome side panel and in the VS Code panel and checks that code fences, task lists and math render the same way.
A person switches the app language on Mobile and every screen reads in that language.
An engineer adds a Mobile button and must use the Button or PressableBox primitive or the guard fails.

prerequisites: None for the person. For an engineer: run pnpm check:css-tokens, pnpm check:mobile-primitives and pnpm check:i18n-parity (package.json:145,175,424).
screens_and_controls: Web and Desktop (hosted web): components from @agiworkforce/ui, for example Button, Dialog, Sheet, Switch, Tabs, Tooltip, ConfirmAction (packages/ui/ui/src/primitives/).
Mobile: Text, Button, PressableBox, Card, Input, Switch, Badge, Skeleton, Separator (apps/mobile/components/ui/).
Chrome side panel and options page: its own DOM helpers plus tokens from getExtensionTokensCss (apps/extension/src/tokens.ts:1-30; apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/dom.ts).
VS Code panel: its own HTML built in webviewContent.ts, with agiVsCodeCssVars as the fallback behind host theme variables (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/sidebar-webview/webviewContent.ts:191).
journey: 1. A person opens an app. The app loads its stylesheet or token map from the design-token package.
2. Screens draw from shared primitives (Web, Desktop, Mobile) or from the surface's own controls (Chrome, VS Code).
3. Text comes from the shared catalogue through i18next (Web, Desktop, Mobile), through the shared VS Code catalogue (VS Code), or through the browser extension message file (Chrome).
4. An assistant answer is turned into the surface's own display by that surface's Markdown renderer.
5. For an engineer: the guards run in the guard chain and fail on a broken token, raw control or missing translation (package.json:397).
