features.summary: Artifacts made in chat run in a sandboxed frame loaded from a separate origin under a strict content policy. A published artifact gets a public link; its page can ask the viewer to allow AI and connected apps. Connected apps are off today: connectors are marked coming soon.

purpose.what_it_does: Two parts. (1) The sandbox: interactive artifacts (HTML, React and similar) render in an iframe on a separate sandbox origin with a content policy that blocks network calls (packages/contracts/types/src/artifact-csp.ts:17-45; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/artifact-components/ArtifactSandboxFrame.tsx:146-168). (2) Hosting: a published artifact is served at /shared-artifact/[token] and may call runtime routes for AI completions, storage and connected apps (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime).
purpose.why_it_exists: Artifacts run code written by a model, so it must not reach the user's session or the network. Publishing lets a person share a working app by link, like the leaders' artifact sharing (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:189-190).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who create artifacts and people who open shared links, signed in or not.
problems_solved: Run generated code safely.
Share an app by link.
Let a published app use AI and, later, connected apps with the viewer's consent and plan.
use_cases: Open a shared artifact link and use the page.
A published app asks to use AI; the viewer allows it.
An owner publishes a dashboard that reads the viewer's connected app, after consent (currently blocked).

where_to_find_it: Web: chat artifact panel (shared UI), published page at /shared-artifact/[token] (apps/web/app/shared-artifact/[token]/page.tsx), titled '<title> - AGI' or 'Published artifact - AGI'.
Desktop, VS Code, Chrome: artifact panel from the shared unified-chat package (AGENTS.md section 5) [inferred]; the published page is web only.
Mobile and CLI: have artifact lists or commands (matrix lines 49, 187), but the published page and runtime routes are web.
Connected apps in artifacts: Present on web and api only (doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:81).
prerequisites: Viewing a public link needs no sign-in (page.tsx:25-35). Using AI inside the app needs sign-in (usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts, 'Sign in' action in PublishedArtifactView.tsx:285) and the server switch AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED.
Connected apps: connectors released (currently not), a plan with artifact_connectors, workspace policy, and each connector connected in Settings, Connectors.
screens_and_controls: Published page with the artifact in a frame and a report-content link (page.tsx).
Consent box labelled 'AI permission': text 'This app wants to use AI with your account...' with buttons 'Allow' and "Don't allow" and per-tool checkboxes (ArtifactConnectorConsent.tsx:50-140).
Unavailable page for a bad or revoked link; invite-only page for invite-only artifacts (page.tsx:76-95).
journey: 1. Open /shared-artifact/<token>. 2. The server looks up a public row, then workspace or invited rows (page.tsx:25-45). 3. The page renders the artifact in the sandbox frame (PublishedArtifactView.tsx:321-325). 4. If the app asks for AI, the consent box appears; the choice is remembered per exact revision of the code in the browser (usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:37-85). 5. On Allow, the page calls the runtime routes; the server runs the gates and the model call (artifact-completion.ts:112-310). 6. The answer returns to the app.
feedback_and_outputs: Refusal texts: 'This app is no longer available.', 'AI in apps is not available yet.', 'Connectors are coming soon.', 'Connected apps in published apps are available on <plans>.', 'This app was not published with connected apps, so it cannot use yours.', 'Remove sensitive credentials before sending.' (several files).
Client messages: 'You chose not to let this app use AI.', 'You chose not to let this app use your connected apps.' (usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:14-18).
settings: Server: NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN (empty in .env.example:676), AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED (artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8).
User: Settings, Connectors; tool approval choices decide which tools an app may use (artifact-completion.ts:259-270).

working: Sandbox frame in the shared UI: sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin allow-modals' on a separate origin, a handshake timeout of 3 seconds, and a fallback frame if the origin is missing or fails (ArtifactSandboxFrame.tsx:11, 148, 160-168).
The origin helper refuses the app's own origin so scripts cannot reach the session (apps/web/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:150-175; packages/ui/unified-chat/src/lib/artifact-sandbox.ts:209-218).

Content policy: default none, scripts from four named script hosts plus inline, connect-src none, frame-src self for the renderer and none for the fallback, object and base none (artifact-csp.ts:17-45).
The renderer page carries the same policy in a meta tag, kept identical by a test (infrastructure/sandbox/index.html:50-58; packages/contracts/types/src/__tests__/artifact-csp.test.ts).
Published page and routes: connectors, complete, storage under apps/web/app/api/artifacts/runtime/[token]; publish route apps/web/app/api/artifacts/publish/route.ts.

Gate order for AI completion: AI switch, connectors released, public-share rule, workspace privacy, managed compute access, connector plan gate, moderation, content safety, secret handling, route selection, model policy, egress policy, turn slot (artifact-completion.ts:112-310).
incomplete: The web published page uses its own SandboxedIframe, whose sandbox attribute is 'allow-scripts allow-same-origin' with no 'allow-modals' on the sandbox-origin path, and 'allow-scripts allow-modals' on the fallback (apps/web/features/chat/components/SandboxedIframe.tsx:399, 427). The brief describes only the shared-UI frame.

The infrastructure sandbox host also sets a response header policy with a shorter script and style host list than the meta policy (infrastructure/sandbox/vercel.json header; index.html:55-58). Both apply [inferred: the browser enforces both]; whether this difference is intended: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Connectors are switched off: CONNECTOR_RELEASE_STATE is 'coming_soon' (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14), so the gate returns 403 connectors_coming_soon (artifact-connector-gate.ts:20-25; artifact-completion.ts:121-123).

AI inside published apps is off unless AGI_ARTIFACT_AI_ENABLED is set to a true spelling (artifact-ai-switch.ts:5-8); the AI-off answer is 403 artifact_ai_off 'AI in apps is not available yet.' (artifact-ai.ts:1-3).
If NEXT_PUBLIC_SANDBOX_ORIGIN is empty (as in .env.example), the sandbox falls back to an opaque srcDoc frame (artifact-sandbox.ts:158-175).
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no published-app runtime; connected apps in artifacts exist on web and api only (surface-feature-matrix.md:81).

established.statement: Interactive artifacts run in a sandboxed iframe with a restrictive content policy. Platform status: done.
Generated applications are hosted at a public URL with the runtime they need. Platform status: done.
The frame uses sandbox allow-scripts, allow-same-origin and allow-modals and loads from a separate sandbox origin.
established.source: S102.31 Should line; verified at ArtifactSandboxFrame.tsx:148 and artifact-sandbox.ts:158

established.statement: The content policy sets connect-src to none and frame-src to self (for the renderer; none for the same-page fallback).
The connector route checks connectors are released and the plan allows artifact_connectors; failure codes connectors_coming_soon (403) and plan_upgrade_required (403).
Three surfaces enforce the artifact policy and must not drift: renderer, web fallback and unified-chat fallback.
Artifacts need an id, a relationship to the conversation, and live in the web, desktop and mobile artifact model.

acceptance_criteria: A published artifact's script cannot call fetch or open a connection to any host (connect-src none).
The frame cannot read the cookies or storage of the app's own origin; configuring the sandbox origin equal to the app origin makes the app use the opaque fallback.
A revoked or malformed link shows the Unavailable page, not a 404 page.
A viewer who is not signed in sees the sign-in prompt before the AI consent.
With connectors in coming_soon state, a request with connectors returns 403 connectors_coming_soon.
With connectors released and a plan below Pro, the same request returns 403 plan_upgrade_required naming the plans.
Changing the published code asks for consent again.
Public shares cannot use connectors (403 connectors_not_on_public_share).
inferred: A script host removed from the contract list must also be removed from the renderer meta tag and the fallbacks (test enforces byte equality) [inferred from the artifact-csp.ts header comment].
Consent decisions must be per account and per revision [inferred from usePublishedArtifactRuntime.ts:68-85].

steps.what_happens: A visitor opens /shared-artifact/<token>; the server validates the token and reads a public row, then workspace or invited rows with the cookie user.
The browser loads the page and creates the sandbox iframe from the sandbox origin, then posts the artifact to it; if the handshake fails within 3 seconds it falls back to a same-page srcDoc frame.
The sandbox host serves a static renderer with the content policy.
steps.evidence: infrastructure/sandbox/vercel.json (separate host); index.html:50-58 [host is a separate deployment: sandbox.agiworkforce.com per index.html:9]

steps.what_happens: Artifact code asks the parent for runtime work through postMessage; the parent, not the sandbox, calls our API with the viewer's session.

The server runs the gates (AI switch, connectors released, public-share rule, policy, compute access, plan, moderation, safety, secret handling), picks a model route, checks model and egress policy, takes a turn slot and runs the completion.
The model provider answers; the text returns to the page.

features.summary: The server-side records of who a person is and which of their devices are signed in. One profile row per account, a map from sign-in provider identity to account, a device registry filled by app heartbeats, and rotating refresh-token families that let one device or all devices be signed out. All of it runs on our servers.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores the account profile (profiles table), the link from a sign-in provider subject to the account (identities table), one registry row per signed-in install of a desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome or mobile app (device_registrations), and device refresh-token families that rotate on each use and are revoked on sign-out, unlink or replay (apps/web/db/neon/0002_profiles.sql:1; apps/web/db/neon/0174_identities.sql:1; apps/web/db/neon/0207_device_registrations.sql:23; apps/web/db/neon/0080_device_refresh_token_rotation.sql:1). GET /api/me assembles the account the apps display (apps/web/app/api/me/route.ts:325).
purpose.why_it_exists: So an account is recognised the same way on every app, the person can see which machines are signed in and cut one off, and a stolen refresh token cannot be used quietly. Brief items S103.01 and S103.02 require these records to be durable, owned by one canonical record and classified for export and erasure (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person on every app; support and admins read it indirectly through account and device lists.
problems_solved: Recognising the same person across apps and across sign-in providers (apps/web/db/neon/0174_identities.sql:1)
Showing which device is which and whether it is awake (apps/web/db/neon/0207_device_registrations.sql:1)
Ending a lost or compromised device's access, including a refresh token that is used twice (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:153)
Making sure erasure and export know every table that holds account data (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:122,173)
use_cases: A person signs the CLI in on a laptop; later the Linked devices list shows it with its operating system and last seen time.
A person loses a phone and unlinks it as lost; its refresh family is finished for good.
A refresh token is replayed by an attacker; the whole family is revoked, a critical audit event is written and the owner is notified.
A desktop app opens settings and reads the profile name, plan and billing owner from /api/me.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings > Linked devices panel, headed 'Linked devices', with row buttons 'Rename' and 'Unlink' (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:374,341,356). Settings pages exist at /settings/account, /settings/profile and /settings/security (apps/web/app/settings).

Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome, Mobile: no visible control found in this pass. Each posts a heartbeat that appears in the web list (apps/desktop/src/services/__tests__/deviceRegistryHeartbeat.test.ts; apps/cli/src/device_registry.rs; apps/extension-vscode/src/__tests__/deviceHeartbeat.test.ts; apps/extension/__tests__/device-heartbeat.test.ts; apps/mobile/src/features/device-registry/__tests__/heartbeat.test.ts). The visible labels inside those apps: unknown.
prerequisites: A signed-in account. Heartbeat and refresh need a valid session or device credential (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:22).
Device sign-in uses the device authorization flow (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/code, approve, token).
screens_and_controls: Linked devices list with rename and an Unlink button; Unlink asks 'Unlink <device>?' with the confirm label 'Unlink device' (apps/web/features/settings/components/LinkedDevicesPanel.tsx:333-336).
The unlink call accepts options lost and logoutAll (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts). Whether the panel exposes those two choices: unknown, not opened.
Sessions list and revoke through /api/settings/sessions (apps/web/app/api/settings/sessions/route.ts).
journey: 1. The person starts sign-in on a device (device code route).
2. They approve it in the web app (approve route).
3. The device exchanges the code for an access token and a refresh token (token route).
4. The app sends a heartbeat with its install id, operating system, version and capabilities; the server creates or updates its registry row.
5. When the access token expires the app calls refresh; the server swaps the refresh token for a new one.
6. In Linked devices the person can rename or unlink; unlinking revokes the refresh family and removes the registry row.
feedback_and_outputs: Heartbeat answers with the device id and the next heartbeat interval (apps/web/app/api/devices/heartbeat/route.ts:22).
First time a device is seen the account gets a new-device notice (notifyNewDeviceRegistered in the heartbeat route).
Refresh refusals carry specific errors: terms acceptance required with a link, age review required, account unavailable with a recovery link (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:153).

Refresh rotates the token inside a transaction with a row lock, marks the old one used, and treats a reused token as a replay: the family is finished as compromised, an audit event 'refresh_family_compromised' (critical) is written and a notice is sent (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:153).
Refresh is withheld, without revoking the family, when terms need accepting or the 18-and-over decision is missing (apps/web/app/api/auth/device/refresh/route.ts:153).

Unlinking a device revokes its credential family, optionally as lost (compromise recorded) and optionally everywhere, and deletes the registry rows (apps/web/app/api/settings/devices/[deviceId]/route.ts).
Logout revokes the developer session family by refresh token (apps/web/app/api/auth/logout/route.ts).
profiles, identities, device_registrations and the refresh tables are named in the erasure and export manifest (apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:122,161-163,223).

Sessions and devices (registrations, refresh tokens, revocations) are durably stored and classified.
A refresh token that was already used must not be accepted again; the family is finished as compromised.
Presence is derived from last_seen_at when read, never stored, so a silent device cannot stay online.

acceptance_criteria: After a heartbeat from each of the five device apps, one row exists per user, app and install id and a second heartbeat updates it without a duplicate.
Using the same refresh token twice returns an error the second time and the first rotated token no longer works.
Unlinking a device makes its refresh token fail on the next refresh.
A refresh for an account whose terms are not accepted is refused with the acceptance link and the same token works after acceptance.
GET /api/me for a new account returns plan, name and billing owner and never another account's data.
Every table named in the identity and device group appears in the deletion manifest.
inferred: Local-only use of an app without sign-in should create no account or device rows [inferred; no code path found that registers without a credential].
proposed: [proposed] Show the device list, with last seen time, in the desktop, mobile, CLI and extension settings, not only on web.
[proposed] Record a revocation row so the person can see when and why a device was cut off.

features.summary: The server records for workspaces (organizations), who belongs to each with which role, the workspace policy, and each person's personal preferences. Every change to policy, roles or role grants adds one revision to a per-workspace counter, so clients can tell whether they are looking at the latest state. All of it runs on our servers.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores organizations and their members with roles owner, admin, member or viewer (apps/web/db/neon/0015_organizations.sql:1), custom roles and grants, the admin policy and related policies, and a per-user preferences document (apps/web/db/neon/0028_user_settings.sql:7).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a team can run under shared rules (privacy mode, sync per app, memory, sharing, retention) with a recorded history of rule changes, and so one person's personal settings follow them across apps. Brief items S103.03, S103.04 and S103.05 require durable storage and classification (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Workspace owners and admins, members, and any person using personal settings.
problems_solved: Knowing who may change workspace rules (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts:226)
Stopping two admins from silently overwriting each other, using one revision counter with If-Match (apps/web/lib/server/workspace-revision.ts)
Finding every workspace table at workspace erasure (apps/web/lib/server/organization-erasure.ts:33)
Keeping personal settings per account, grouped by page (apps/web/db/neon/0028_user_settings.sql:7)
use_cases: A person creates a workspace and becomes its owner.
An admin turns off memory for the workspace; the policy revision number goes up.
An admin gives a member a custom role; the same counter records it.
A person changes a personal setting on one app and the same value is read on another.

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings pages /settings/team, /settings/general, /settings/privacy and the admin console (apps/web/app/settings; apps/web/features/admin/pages/AdminConsolePage.tsx). Exact visible labels of the workspace policy screens: unknown, not opened.

Desktop, Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: they read workspace policy through the API (policy flags allow_cli_cloud_sync, allow_vscode_cloud_sync, allow_chrome_cloud_sync exist in apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-service.ts:376). Visible screens: unknown.
prerequisites: Signed-in account.
Creating a workspace: the person must not already own one (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:302).
Changing policy needs the permission policy.manage (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts:226).
screens_and_controls: Create, rename, delete workspace (POST, PATCH, DELETE on /api/settings/organization).
Members list and per-member role or removal (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/members/[userId]/route.ts).
Roles and groups screens (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/roles).
Policy read and patch (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts).
Personal preferences read and save by namespace (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts).
journey: 1. Person creates a workspace; the server inserts the organization and an owner membership and makes it the active workspace.
2. Owner invites or manages members and assigns roles.
3. Admin opens policy, reads it with its revision, edits and saves with the revision they saw.
4. Server stores the new policy and the revision counter moves up.
5. Other admins and clients see the new revision on their next read.
feedback_and_outputs: Creating a second workspace by the same owner returns: 'You already own a workspace. Switch to it from the account menu.' (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:302).
A person without permission gets: 'Your workspace role does not allow changing workspace policy.' (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/policy/route.ts:226).

Policy responses carry canManagePolicy, currentUserRole and revision, and the x-workspace-revision header with an ETag like W/"wsrev-N" (policy/route.ts:192-206; apps/web/lib/server/workspace-revision.ts).
Member role changes write the audit event 'member_role_changed' (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/members/[userId]/route.ts).
settings: Admin policy fields: default privacy mode, allowed privacy modes, managed compute, chat sync surfaces, per-app cloud sync, audit export, retention days and enforcement, external sharing, memory (apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-service.ts:376).
Extra policy fields stored in metadata: secret handling, MFA, monthly spend cap, zero data retention, product analytics, IP allow list, controls (organization-policy-service.ts:376).
Personal preferences by namespace, with a stored version number (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts).

working: Workspace creation inserts organizations and an owner row in one transaction and sets the active workspace (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/route.ts:321).
upsertOrganizationPolicy writes the admin policy and clears the cached IP allow list for that workspace (apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-service.ts:376).

A database trigger appends one revision row for every write to the admin, model and connector policies, overrides, roles, member roles and group roles (apps/web/db/neon/0201_workspace_policy_layers_and_revisions.sql:112-165).
The policy read reports the latest revision (apps/web/lib/services/organization-policy-service.ts:70; apps/web/lib/server/workspace-revision.ts).
If-Match with the revision tag is honoured; a caller that sends none, or '*', is allowed (apps/web/lib/server/workspace-revision.ts).
Custom roles are created, updated and deleted with a check that the actor cannot grant permissions they do not hold (apps/web/lib/services/organization-role-service.ts:86).
Deleting a role can reassign its members and groups to a replacement role (apps/web/lib/services/organization-role-service.ts:236).
Preferences are stored as one jsonb document per user in namespaces (apps/web/db/neon/0028_user_settings.sql:7).
Workspace erasure lists members, policies, overrides and revisions (apps/web/lib/server/organization-erasure.ts:33,83,84).
incomplete: Preferences GET and PUT also gate on workspace memory and tool-approval policy, so a preference can be refused by workspace rules (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts). The full list of namespaces: unknown.
disconnected_or_disabled: Migration 0201 (revisions) carries the header 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0201_workspace_policy_layers_and_revisions.sql:4). Code reads organization_policy_revisions already, so a database without it would fail the policy read. Applied state: unknown.
not_available: Revision history is only a counter with source table and actor; no stored copy of the old policy values was found (0201 table has revision, source, changed_by_user_id).

established.statement: Organizations/workspaces are durably stored and classified.
Memberships and role grants are durably stored and classified.
User preferences and workspace policy (with revision history) are durably stored and classified.
Every write to policy, roles or role grants appends one row to organization_policy_revisions.
Policy changes require the policy.manage permission.

acceptance_criteria: Create a workspace: one organization row and one owner member row exist and it is the active workspace.
A second create by the same owner is refused with the 'already own a workspace' message.
A member without policy.manage who patches policy gets a 403.
After a policy patch, the revision in the next read is higher by at least one.
A patch with an old If-Match tag is refused (behaviour on mismatch: confirm in the route test).
Workspace erasure removes member and policy rows (organization-erasure test).
inferred: A role change and a policy change both bump the same counter, so a client holding an old revision sees a conflict for either [inferred from workspace-revision.ts comment].
proposed: [proposed] Keep the previous policy values with each revision so an admin can see what changed and restore it.
[proposed] Show the revision number and author in the policy screen.

features.summary: The server records of chats: conversations and messages, message versions and forked branches, a per-turn record of what context was sent to the model, and saved memories with versions for conflict-safe sync. Temporary chats carry a flag and are purged after 30 days. Local-mode chats are not written here unless the app syncs.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps conversations (web_conversations) and messages (web_messages) with tree parents for message versions, copies a conversation into a branch from a chosen message, records a context manifest for each turn, and stores memories with a server version so apps can sync them (apps/web/db/neon/0001_mvp_chat.sql:3; apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:194; packages/platform/context-engine/src/manifest-store.ts:55; apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:211).
purpose.why_it_exists: So chat history survives devices and sessions, a person can try another answer without losing the first, the product can show what context shaped a turn, and what the assistant remembers is the same on every app. Brief items S103.06, S103.07, S103.09 and S103.10 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person who chats in Cloud mode; sync clients (mobile, CLI, VS Code) for memory.
problems_solved: Losing chats between devices (apps/web/app/api/chat/sync/route.ts)
Overwriting a newer memory edit from another device (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:211)
Two devices creating the first message variant at once (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/message-thread.ts:29)
Chats meant to be temporary living forever (apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-temporary-chats/route.ts)
use_cases: Start a chat on web and continue on mobile in Cloud mode.
Branch from an earlier message to try a different question.
Edit a message and flip between versions.
Save a memory on the phone and see it on web.

where_to_find_it: Web: /chat (history and composer), Settings > Memory, Settings > Archived chats, Settings > Deleted chats (apps/web/app/settings/memory; apps/web/features/settings/sections/ArchivedChatsSection.tsx:87; apps/web/features/settings/sections/DeletedChatsSection.tsx:60). Composer text 'Temporary chats never read or save memory.' (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:6137).

journey: 1. Person sends a message; the conversation is created or updated (POST /api/chat/conversations).
2. The turn is assembled and a context manifest is written.
3. Messages are stored; editing creates a variant; Branch calls the fork service.
4. A memory is saved on any app; the app pushes it with the version it saw.
5. Server applies it or returns the current server copy as a conflict.
feedback_and_outputs: Creating a conversation in a missing or archived project returns 'Project not found' (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:238).
A conversation that is gone returns 409 'This conversation is no longer available. Start a new conversation.' (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:238).
Memory push answers applied, conflicts (with the current server copy), rejected (with reason and message) and a cursor (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:211).
Branch limits: 'This message already has the maximum number of branches'; 'This conversation already has the maximum number of forks' (apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:279).
settings: Temporary chat (privacy settings; apps/web/features/settings/sections/PrivacySection.tsx).
Memory switches and workspace memory policy (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:721).

working: Create conversation checks the project belongs to the user and workspace, is not archived or deleted; a temporary chat cannot join a project (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:238).
Create counts against a free daily allowance for conversation creates (assertFreeDailyAllowance, apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/route.ts:238).
Message insert is idempotent on the client message id and cannot touch another conversation's message (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/message-thread.ts:29).

Message variants form a tree with parent ids and an active leaf, serialised by a row lock (apps/web/app/api/chat/conversations/[id]/messages/lib/message-thread.ts:29; apps/web/db/neon/0156_message_thread_variants.sql).

forkConversation copies a conversation up to a message into a new conversation, is idempotent by request id, and caps 50 branches per fork point and 100 fork points per conversation (apps/web/lib/services/conversation-branch-service.ts:49-50,194).

Context manifests are written with insert-or-update by turn id; an update applies only when the stored user is the same user (packages/platform/context-engine/src/manifest-store.ts:55). The manifest carries a temporary_chat flag.

Memory push applies each change only when the client's base version equals the server version, otherwise returns a conflict with the current record; deletes are allowed even when memory is off (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:211).
Memory text passes exclusion and admission gates before it is stored (apps/web/lib/services/managed-memory-context-service.ts:721).
Temporary chats are flagged is_temporary and purged by a cron with a 30-day retention (apps/web/db/neon/0050_temporary_chat_retention.sql:1; apps/web/app/api/cron/purge-temporary-chats/route.ts).
incomplete: Memory provenance columns source_conversation_id, source_turn_id and provenance are written by managed-memory-context-service.ts:820 but the sync push SQL does not set them (apps/web/app/api/memory/sync/route.ts:211), so a memory pushed from an app carries no source conversation. Migration header says not applied (apps/web/db/neon/0285_user_memories_provenance.sql:4).
disconnected_or_disabled: Migrations 0252 (context manifests) and 0285 (memory provenance) carry 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' headers (apps/web/db/neon/0252_context_manifests_and_source_policy.sql; apps/web/db/neon/0285_user_memories_provenance.sql:4). Applied state: unknown. The file 0285 is titled 'Migration 0284' inside.
not_available: Server storage of Local-mode chats: not written by the apps unless in cloud mode (mobile evidence: apps/mobile/services/cloudSyncEngine.ts:101); for desktop, CLI and VS Code: unknown.

established.statement: Conversations and their turns are durably stored and classified.
Message versions and conversation branches are stored and classified with their conversation.
Context manifests (what went into each turn's context) are durably recorded and classified.
Memory items and their provenance (source conversation and turn) are durably stored and classified.
A conversation joins a project only if the user owns it and it is not archived or deleted.
Temporary chats never read or save memory.

acceptance_criteria: POST a conversation with another user's project id: 404 'Project not found'.
POST a temporary conversation with a project id: validation refusal.
Push a memory with a stale base version: response has a conflict containing the server copy and the server copy is unchanged.
Fork a conversation twice with the same request id: one new conversation.
Fork the 51st branch from one message: refused with the maximum message.
Write a manifest for a turn id owned by another user: the other user's manifest is unchanged.
After 30 days a temporary conversation is removed by the purge job.
A memory created by the model records its source conversation and turn.
inferred: A memory typed by hand has no source conversation [inferred from nullable columns in 0285].
proposed: [proposed] Pass source conversation and turn through the memory sync contract so app-made memories carry provenance.
[proposed] Show the person which memory came from which chat.

steps.what_happens: App sends a message to create or update the conversation; server validates project and free allowance and upserts the row.
The turn's context is assembled and a manifest row is written.
The model call itself is handled by the chat pipeline (SYS-chat-turn-pipeline); here only the stored result matters.
Mobile pushes dirty messages and memories when mode is cloud.

features.summary: Server records for projects (instructions and knowledge files), uploaded and generated files in a Library, references to outside resources such as Drive files, repositories and connectors, and the search index built from text extracted from those sources. Library folders as such were not found in code. Bytes sit in object storage, rows in the database.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores projects and their knowledge files with extracted text (apps/web/db/neon/0006_projects.sql:1), a catalog of uploaded and generated files (media_assets, apps/web/db/neon/0036_media_assets.sql:9), a canonical reference row per outside resource (apps/web/db/neon/0322_external_resource_references.sql:28), and a full-text and vector search index over the extracted text (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:48,116).
purpose.why_it_exists: So a person can give the assistant lasting instructions and sources, find earlier files in one place on every app, and have answers and search draw on their own material. Brief items S103.11 to S103.16 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who organise work into projects, and anyone who uploads or generates files.
problems_solved: One duplicate of a project with its sources (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/duplicate/route.ts:114)
One list of files across apps (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts)
Each outside resource having one identity instead of private copies (apps/web/db/neon/0322_external_resource_references.sql:1)
Keyword and meaning search over own material (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:1)
use_cases: Create a project, add a PDF as knowledge, chat with it.
Duplicate a project to try different instructions.
Open Library to find an image generated last week.
Link a Google Drive file to a project as a reference.

where_to_find_it: Web: /chat/projects and /chat/library, tab title 'Library' (apps/web/app/chat/library/layout.tsx:5; apps/web/app/chat/projects).
Desktop: DesktopLibrary (apps/desktop/src/features/library/DesktopLibrary.tsx).
Mobile: library client (apps/mobile/src/features/library/libraryClient.ts).
CLI: cloud library client (apps/cli/src/cloud/library.rs).
VS Code and Chrome: not found in this pass.
prerequisites: Signed-in Cloud account for server storage; plan with file storage and project allowance.
screens_and_controls: Project list and project page with instructions and knowledge files.
Library view with preview, open, delete and restore (apps/web/features/library/components/LibraryView.tsx).
Project duplicate action.
journey: 1. Create a project with instructions.
2. Upload a file; the server stores it, extracts text and creates an index entry.
3. A new upload with the same file name supersedes the earlier version.
4. Chat in the project; retrieval searches the indexed chunks.
5. Duplicate copies the live files into a new project.
feedback_and_outputs: Project limit: 'Your <plan> plan includes N project folders. Upgrade your plan to add more, or delete an existing folder to make room.' (apps/web/lib/services/free-plan-entitlements.ts:54).

Storage limit: '<plan> accounts include X of file storage, shared by your Library and project sources. Delete a file or upgrade to add another.' (apps/web/lib/services/free-plan-entitlements.ts:40-46).
Indexing failure shows: 'The embedding provider did not respond; keyword search still works and indexing retries automatically.' (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-index-service.ts:118).
Library items show file name, kind, size, preview flag, origin uploaded or generated and a recovery date for deleted items (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts).
settings: Project instructions and color.
Temporary chat attachments are kept out of the Library (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:326).

working: Project duplicate copies the project row and live, non-superseded knowledge files in one transaction with a plan quota guard (apps/web/app/api/projects/[id]/duplicate/route.ts:114,158).
Knowledge upload replaces the same file name by marking the earlier row superseded and bumping the version (apps/web/lib/server/project-knowledge-files.ts:416).
Library list excludes files from temporary chats (not temporary_chat) and deleted files, and a deleted view lists items inside a 30-day window (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:326,432-433).
The temporary flag is derived from the conversation, not trusted from the caller (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts:78).
Content hash is stored so the same content is stored and billed once (apps/web/lib/server/media-assets.ts InsertMediaAssetParams contentSha256).

External references: canonical identity key per account and workspace; Drive, custom connector, Code session, project knowledge and assistant-turn persistence call into it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md S103.14 code list; apps/web/lib/server/external-resource-references.ts:76).

Retrieval index: one document per source, chunks with weighted text search and a vector column, states pending, indexing, indexed, stale, failed, drained by a cron (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:1-30; apps/web/app/api/cron/index-retrieval-documents).
If embedding fails, chunks are stored for keyword search only (apps/web/lib/services/retrieval-index-service.ts:511).
incomplete: Files and versions: versions exist for knowledge files (superseded_at, version used by code) while the generic version and parent-version columns for media assets come from migration 0257, headed not applied (apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:4).
disconnected_or_disabled: Migrations 0202, 0257 headed 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' (apps/web/db/neon/0202_retrieval_index.sql:4; apps/web/db/neon/0257_file_versions_and_lineage.sql:4). Applied state: unknown.
not_available: Library folders: no folder store or folder parameter was found in the Library route or the media_assets schema (apps/web/app/api/library/route.ts; apps/web/db/neon/0036_media_assets.sql). Chat folders (chat_folders, apps/web/db/neon/0022_chat_features.sql) and the word 'folder' for projects in plan messages exist, but they are not Library folders.
Library on VS Code and Chrome: not found.

established.statement: Projects with their instructions and knowledge are durably stored and classified.
Files, their versions and derivation lineage are durably stored and classified.
Library entries and folders are durably stored and classified.
References to external resources are stored as canonical, classified references.
Text extracted from sources is durably stored for reuse and classified.
Search and vector indexes are stored and classified with the content they index.
Files uploaded into temporary chats are kept out of the Library and purged with the chat.

acceptance_criteria: Upload a file with the same name twice: one live row, the older one superseded.
Duplicate a project: new project has the same live files and not the superseded ones.
Duplicate over the plan project limit: refused with the plan message.
A file uploaded in a temporary chat does not appear in Library.
After a source's text changes, its index state becomes stale then indexed again.
With the embedding service down, a search by keyword still finds the file.
Link the same Drive file twice: one reference row.
inferred: Folder behaviour for the Library is not yet specified in code, so the brief status 'done' for S103.13 cannot be confirmed [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether Library folders are a product requirement and, if so, add a folder table and API.
[proposed] Show index state per file in every app, as the knowledge panel does on web.

features.summary: Server records for things the assistant produces and the person shares: research reports with their citations, artifacts with version history, published pages, image and video jobs with their assets, and shared chat links with expiry. Share links expire in 1, 7 or 30 days. Published pages have no expiry and stay until unpublished. All runs on our servers.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps citations inside research reports (apps/web/db/neon/0094_research_reports.sql:28), artifacts and their versions (web_artifacts, web_artifact_versions, apps/web/db/neon/0039_artifact_cloud_sync.sql:59), published pages by token (apps/web/db/neon/0095_published_artifacts.sql:47), durable image and video jobs (apps/web/db/neon/0226_durable_image_generation_jobs.sql:32; apps/web/db/neon/0105_durable_video_generation_jobs.sql), and shared chat snapshots (apps/web/db/neon/0051_shared_sessions.sql:1).

established.statement: Citations and source locators are persisted with the answers that use them and classified.

acceptance_criteria: Create a share with expiry 7: expires_at is 7 days ahead; a request with expiry 3 is refused.
After expiry, the share page refuses and a refresh gets the 'create a new link' message.
Revoke removes the link and the page stops loading.

Run research, kill the request: a row exists with status interrupted or failed and the retry updates the same row.
Start an image job, close the tab: the job and its assets are readable by id later.

proposed: [proposed] Keep revoked links as rows with a revoked time so audit can show them.

features.summary: Server records of agent work: each run and its event journal, each model or tool operation with its attempt count, plans, resumable checkpoints for approval and input, coding sessions tied to a repository, installed skills and plugins, schedules and triggers. Approval decisions are written to the audit trail, not on the checkpoint row. All on our servers.

purpose.what_it_does: Records managed agent runs and their ordered events (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9), each provider or tool operation with attempt, retry safety and stored result (apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:20), task plans (work_plans, work_plan_steps, work_plan_revisions listed in apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts), approval checkpoints (apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:8), connector call outcomes (apps/web/db/neon/0223_connector_call_events.sql:32), coding sessions (apps/web/db/neon/0075_cloud_code_sessions.sql:7), user skills (apps/web/db/neon/0157_user_skills.sql:19), plugin installations (apps/web/db/neon/0109_web_plugin_installations.sql:53) and scheduled tasks and runs (apps/web/db/neon/0009_scheduling.sql:1,34; apps/web/db/neon/0210_event_triggers.sql:38).
purpose.why_it_exists: So long agent work can pause for a person, resume after a restart without repeating an action that already happened, show what the agent did, and run unattended on a schedule. Brief items S103.08, S103.21 to S103.25, S103.28, S103.29 (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/103-data-and-persistence-categories.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: People who run agent tasks, coding sessions or schedules; admins reviewing activity.
problems_solved: Doing a paid or side-effecting step twice after a retry (apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:1-10)
Losing a paused run when the client goes away (apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:1-6)
Knowing whether a connector is answering (apps/web/db/neon/0223_connector_call_events.sql:4-20)
Missed or failed scheduled runs (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:2102)
use_cases: An agent asks to run a tool; the person approves later and the run resumes.
A coding session attaches to a repository and keeps a terminal journal.
A person schedules a daily agent task that retries with backoff.
A person installs a plugin and a custom skill.

where_to_find_it: Web: /chat/agents, /chat/code, /chat/schedules, plugin and skill pages (apps/web/app/chat; apps/web/app/api/plugins; apps/web/app/api/skills). Exact visible labels: unknown, not opened.
Run origins accepted: web, desktop, mobile, chrome, vscode, api (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9 origin_surface). CLI is not in that list.
Per-app screens: not traced.
prerequisites: Cloud account with a plan that allows the feature; schedules need a plan with scheduled tasks (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:877).
screens_and_controls: Approve, reject, or approve-always on a pending tool call (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts).
Run list, cancel, pause, steer (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1174,2727,2798).
Schedule create, edit, enable, run now (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:994-1495).
Coding session create and attach (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions).
journey: 1. Person starts an agent task; a run row is created with the request id.
2. The run emits ordered events; each model or tool step claims an operation row.
3. If a tool needs approval the run saves a checkpoint and waits.
4. The person decides; the server claims the checkpoint under a lease, resumes, and records the decision in the audit trail.
5. The run completes, fails or is cancelled and its state is stored.
feedback_and_outputs: Schedule limit: '<plan> plans do not include scheduled tasks. Upgrade to schedule unattended runs.' or '<plan> plans can have up to N scheduled tasks. Delete one or upgrade to add another.' (apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:877).
Approval mismatch: 'Approval decisions do not match the pending tool calls.' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts:142).
Policy block: 'This tool must be approved once under the current conversation and workspace policy.' (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts:390).
Run state names: queued, running, awaiting_input, ready_for_review, completed, failed, cancelled, paused, archived (apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9).
settings: Autonomous tool approvals preference, allowed only when the workspace allows (apps/web/app/api/settings/preferences/route.ts).
Network access for coding sessions: none, trusted, full (apps/web/db/neon/0075_cloud_code_sessions.sql:7).

working: createCloudAgentRun is idempotent by user and request id (unique constraint in apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:756).
Events are appended with a sequence per run (cloud_agent_events in apps/web/db/neon/0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9; appendCloudAgentEvents at apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:841).

claimCloudAgentExecutionOperation takes a lease, records attempt, retry safety safe or unsafe and a result; a completed operation replays its stored result and an unsafe lapsed lease becomes outcome_unknown (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-execution-service.ts:206; apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:20).

Approval checkpoints store the transcript, up to 32 pending tool calls and an event cursor, in states pending, resuming, resolved, failed, claimed under a short lease (apps/web/db/neon/0062_cloud_agent_approval_checkpoints.sql:8; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1908,2000).
The client decides only approve or reject; the decision is recorded as audit event tool_approval_decided with status per tool (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/approve/route.ts:638).
Other checkpoint kinds exist for caller input, device steps and pause (apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:1645,2090,2429,2928).
Task plans are created and settled for a run (apps/web/lib/services/work-plan-service.ts:372,422).

Connector call outcomes (succeeded, failed, blocked, duration) are logged without waiting on the call and read back up to 100 entries to judge health (apps/web/lib/services/connector-call-log-service.ts:52,97; caller apps/web/lib/connectors/health.ts).
Coding sessions store title, repository url, network access, state and terminal entries (apps/web/db/neon/0075_cloud_code_sessions.sql:7; apps/web/lib/services/cloud-code-session-service.ts:1196).

Schedules: runs have status running, success, failed, timeout, cancelled and source schedule, manual, webhook, api (apps/web/db/neon/0009_scheduling.sql:34); attempt count (apps/web/db/neon/0057_durable_scheduling.sql:11) and retry backoff and missed-run policy (apps/web/db/neon/0209_scheduled_task_rules_and_policies.sql:16; apps/web/lib/services/schedule-service.ts:1643,2102).
User skills and plugin installations have create, update, delete, enable services (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-service.ts:261-321; apps/web/lib/services/plugin-installation-service.ts:346-448).
incomplete: Tool receipts: the connector call log keeps tool name and outcome only, not arguments or result (apps/web/lib/services/connector-call-log-service.ts:52). The full result is kept per operation in cloud_agent_execution_operations.result (apps/web/db/neon/0063_cloud_agent_execution_operations.sql:20). A single receipt record that joins both: not found.
disconnected_or_disabled: Migrations 0223 (connector call events) and 0235 (autonomous tool approvals workspace switch) carry 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only' headers (apps/web/db/neon/0223_connector_call_events.sql:4; apps/web/db/neon/0235_autonomous_tool_approvals_workspace_switch.sql). 0061, 0062, 0063, 0075 and 0009 do not show that header in the lines opened. Applied state: unknown.

The legacy table agent_approval_requests (status pending, approved, denied, expired, cancelled) exists (apps/web/db/neon/0077_gateway_compatibility_tables.sql:86) and is named in the erasure lists; no code writing it was found in this pass.
not_available: Run origin 'cli' is not allowed by the 0061 constraint; how CLI runs are recorded: unknown.

established.statement: Each execution attempt (operation, run, retry count) is durably recorded and classified.
Agent runs and task plans (with revisions) are durably stored and classified.
Tool invocations and their receipts are durably recorded and classified.
Approval requests and the decisions made on them are durably recorded and classified.
Resumable checkpoints of long-running work are durably stored and classified.
Coding sessions and their repository bindings are durably stored and classified.
Skills and plugin installations are durably stored and classified.
Schedules and trigger definitions are durably stored and classified.
A client decides only whether a pending tool call may run; transcript and arguments stay on the server and are claimed once under a lease.

acceptance_criteria: Start two runs with the same request id: one run row.
Retry a tool operation after a crash: a completed operation returns its stored result and does not run again.
An unsafe operation whose lease lapsed is marked outcome_unknown, not re-run.
Reject a pending tool call: the run resumes without executing it and an audit event tool_approval_decided with status rejected exists.
Claim the same checkpoint twice: the second claim fails.
Create more schedules than the plan allows: refused with the plan message.
A failed scheduled run retries with backoff up to its retry limit.
A connector tool failure produces one outcome row and never fails the original call.
inferred: An approval decision is not readable from the checkpoint row itself, so an approvals history must read the audit trail [inferred from completeCloudAgentApprovalCheckpoint at apps/web/lib/services/cloud-agent-run-service.ts:2000].
proposed: [proposed] Store the decision, decider and time on the checkpoint or an approvals table so history does not depend on the audit stream.
[proposed] Add one receipt row per tool call joining arguments digest, result digest and outcome.

steps.what_happens: App sends a managed chat turn in agent mode; server creates the run row and starts the tool loop.
Each provider or tool step claims an operation row under a lease and stores its result.
The model call itself goes to a model provider.

features.summary: Server-side storage of the outside accounts a person connects and the secrets behind them. OAuth tokens and custom-connector bearer values are kept encrypted. OAuth sign-in state is kept as a hash with an encrypted verifier. AGI API keys are kept only as argon2 hashes with a lookup prefix. Disconnecting revokes the grant and wipes its tokens.

purpose.what_it_does: Holds which connectors a person switched on, the OAuth grants that let AGI act in their outside accounts, user-added custom connector endpoints with an encrypted bearer value, per-connector on/off states, and the person's AGI API keys. No usable secret is stored in plain text (apps/web/lib/custom-connector-crypto.ts:49; apps/web/db/neon/0097_connector_oauth_broker.sql:92; apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:53).
purpose.why_it_exists: Managed Cloud had no per-user OAuth path: only an enablement flag and a typed-in bearer value. The broker tables hold the state for 'platform runs its own OAuth app, the person clicks Connect, AGI holds their tokens' (apps/web/db/neon/0097_connector_oauth_broker.sql:1-40). API keys let outside code call the AGI cloud API.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people on a paid plan who connect tools; developers who create API keys (needs a plan with managed API access, apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:85); workspace admins via shared connectors [inferred from table organization_shared_connectors in apps/web/lib/services/deletion-manifest.ts:212].
problems_solved: A database read cannot replay a live OAuth flow because only the SHA-256 of state is stored (apps/web/db/neon/0097_connector_oauth_broker.sql:55-60).
A revoked grant physically cannot return a token: a check constraint forces both ciphertext columns to null when revoked_at is set (apps/web/db/neon/0097_connector_oauth_broker.sql:120-124).
A raw API key cannot be recovered from the database; only a hash and the 16-hex key id are stored (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:53-60).
More than one account per connector: personal and work accounts are kept apart (apps/web/db/neon/0253_connector_accounts.sql header).
use_cases: Connect a mailbox through Connect, then let chat read it with approval.
Add a custom connector URL with a bearer value the person typed.
Create an API key named for a script, copy it once, revoke it later.
Disconnect a connector and have its tokens wiped, with a notice if the provider did not confirm revocation (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:489-496).

CLI: apps/cli/src/cloud/connectors.rs lists and disconnects connectors; apps/cli/src/cloud/api_keys.rs lists and revokes keys. A create function was not found there.

(apps/web/features/settings/components/Settings/ApiKeys.tsx:215-419).

journey: Connect: person picks a connector and presses Connect; the app calls GET /api/connectors/oauth/start, which stores a pending authorization and returns the provider URL.
Provider asks for consent; the browser returns to GET /api/connectors/oauth/callback, which exchanges the code and stores encrypted tokens (apps/web/app/api/connectors/oauth/callback/route.ts).
POST /api/connectors/oauth/complete finishes the hand-off with a CSRF check (apps/web/app/api/connectors/oauth/complete/route.ts:24).
API key: open API keys, press add, fill name, scopes, optional project and expiry, confirm step-up check, copy the key shown once, press Done.
Disconnect: DELETE /api/connectors?connectorId=...; grants are revoked, caches purged, tool permissions cleared, audit event written (apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:880-925).
feedback_and_outputs: Disconnect result may include a notice such as 'Disconnected here, but ... did not confirm that it revoked access ...' (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:489-496).
Unreachable provider: 'Couldn't reach <label> just now. It is still connected, so try again in a moment.' (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:480).

Plan refusal for API keys carries code managed_api_plan_required with an upgrade link (apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:85-92).
settings: Per-connector account-wide switch (connector_account_states, migration 0381).
Max API key lifetime configuration name API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS, default 365 days (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:23-33).
Connector token encryption key configuration name CUSTOM_CONNECTOR_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY (value never recorded).

working: OAuth start stores a pending row with state hash and encrypted PKCE verifier, ten minute life (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-store.ts:11,52-90).
Grants stored with encrypted access and refresh tokens; revoke sets revoked_at and nulls both ciphertexts in one statement (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-store.ts:720-745,792-796).

Disconnect revokes locally first, then asks the provider to revoke (best effort), purges caches, clears tool permissions, audits (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:444-461; apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:880-925).
API keys: sk_live_<16 hex id>_<secret>, argon2id hash (64 MB, 3 passes), lookup by key_prefix, revoke is soft (revoked_at) (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:14-21,53-60,237-241,261-282).

API key create: CSRF, plan check, 20 active key cap, step-up auth, rate limit, audit event, developer webhook event; full key returned once as full_key (apps/web/app/api/settings/api-keys/route.ts:71-160).

Account erasure deletes user_connectors, user_custom_connectors, connector_oauth_grants, connector_oauth_authorizations and api_keys, and revokes tokens at the provider best effort (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:93-100,122; apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:425-441).
incomplete: Per-app connect behaviour on desktop, mobile, CLI was not traced end to end; only that code and endpoints exist.

Key expiry: bounded by API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS; keys with no expiry are allowed by the service signature (expiresAt default null, apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:131) while the route validation rule for null was not traced.
disconnected_or_disabled: Provider revocation is skipped when a provider has no revocation endpoint; the notice says access may remain (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:489-496).
not_available: API key creation on CLI: not found (apps/cli/src/cloud/api_keys.rs has list and revoke only).
Connector and API key screens in the VS Code and Chrome extensions: not found.

established.statement: Connectors and connected accounts are durably stored and classified.
Credentials are stored only encrypted or hashed (access_token_enc, key hashes) and classified.
OAuth state is stored as a hash; the code verifier is encrypted; tokens are encrypted columns.
Revoking a grant is not a delete: revoked_at is set and both ciphertexts are nulled together.
Every sensitive store is classified in the retention matrix (api_keys, connector_oauth_grants, connector_oauth_authorizations, user_connectors, user_custom_connectors, connector_account_states).
Never route Local data across a trust boundary silently; registry membership does not authorise it.

acceptance_criteria: After Connect, connector_oauth_grants.access_token_enc holds ciphertext, not the provider token.
connector_oauth_authorizations holds a 64-hex state_hash and an encrypted verifier, no raw state.
After Disconnect, the grant row has revoked_at set and both token columns null; chat can no longer call the connector.
A created API key shows full_key once; later lists show only prefix; api_keys.key_hash starts with an argon2id marker.
The 21st active API key is refused with a message naming the limit of 20.
A Free-plan account is refused API key creation with managed_api_plan_required.
Account erasure leaves no rows for the user in the six connector and key tables.
inferred: Connector features should be unavailable, not silently degraded, when the encryption key is missing [inferred from the refusal at apps/web/app/api/connectors/route.ts:415].

Revoked grants should eventually be deleted; domain retention does this for workspace members when a window is set (apps/web/lib/services/domain-retention-service.ts:452-465) [inferred that personal accounts have no sweep].
proposed: [proposed] Add a maximum age for revoked grants of personal accounts, since the manifest shows no age rule for connector_oauth_grants.
[proposed] Add key creation to the CLI or state that creation is web-only.

steps.what_happens: Person presses Connect; the app asks the server to start an authorization.
Server generates state and PKCE pair, stores state hash and encrypted verifier, returns the provider URL.
Person consents at the provider.
Provider redirects to the callback; server consumes the pending row (single use), exchanges the code, stores encrypted tokens.
On disconnect the server captures and revokes grants in one transaction, then asks the provider to revoke.
API key create: server generates the key, hashes it with argon2id, inserts the hash, returns the raw key once.
API key use: caller sends the key; server finds rows by key_prefix, verifies the hash, updates last_used_at in the background.

features.summary: Server tables for in-app notifications, browser push registrations, feedback and response ratings, and support tickets with replies. Push subscriptions and feedback are classified for account erasure. Feedback screenshots live in private object storage with a cleanup ledger. Web push is web-only; feedback is sent from several apps.

purpose.what_it_does: Stores a notification feed per user, browser Web Push registrations (endpoint and two keys), feedback reports and thumbs ratings with metadata, optional redacted logs and an optional screenshot, and support tickets with replies and escalations (apps/web/db/neon/0016_misc.sql:1-24; apps/web/db/neon/0151_web_push_subscriptions.sql; apps/web/db/neon/0024_support_tickets.sql:9-38).
purpose.why_it_exists: A run that finishes while the person is on web ended silently; push closes that loop (apps/web/db/neon/0151_web_push_subscriptions.sql header). Feedback and ratings tell the team what failed; tickets give a reply channel.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people (feedback also accepts anonymous reports, apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:132); support staff for tickets (apps/web/lib/support/tickets/store.ts:340-400).
problems_solved: Move a push endpoint to the new account when someone signs in on the same browser, so the first account stops getting lock-screen notices (apps/web/db/neon/0151_web_push_subscriptions.sql header; apps/web/app/api/web-push/route.ts:86-96).
Keep dead push endpoints from being retried forever by pruning on 404 or 410 (apps/web/lib/services/web-push-service.ts:49,240-262).
Keep secrets out of feedback by redacting logs before storing (apps/web/app/api/feedback/route.ts:353).
use_cases: Allow browser notifications so a finished run alerts the person.
Send feedback with an optional screenshot from the composer dialog.
Rate an answer up or down and later remove the rating.
Open a support ticket and read staff replies.

features.summary: Server records of what a person pays and uses: the subscription row, the credit account and ledger of every charge, and workspace invoices mirrored from the payment provider. Managed turns write ledger rows; a turn paid from purchased credits is tagged overage so plan windows ignore it. Financial rows follow a retention schedule.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps one subscription row per account (plan tier, status, period), a credit account per period, a signed credit ledger of allocations, deductions, purchases and refunds, a managed usage request record per turn, and for workspaces a copy of Stripe invoices (apps/web/db/neon/0003_subscriptions.sql; apps/web/db/neon/0004_token_credits.sql; apps/web/db/neon/0163_enterprise_billing_contracts.sql:66).
purpose.why_it_exists: The AGI Subscription system needs durable entitlement and usage accounting for managed turns so plan windows, extra usage and refunds are enforced and provable.
purpose.who_uses_it: Every Cloud-mode user (by use), billing admins (invoices), operators (reconciliation crons).
problems_solved: Attribute each managed turn to plan or overage so purchased credits are not charged and then counted again against plan windows (apps/web/lib/server/rolling-usage.ts:25-60).
Never double charge: idempotency keys on settlement (apps/web/lib/billing/financial-record-retention.ts:40-47).
Keep books for the statutory period and drop metadata earlier (apps/web/lib/billing/financial-record-retention.ts:1-8,100-140).
use_cases: Subscribe through checkout; the webhook creates the subscription row.
Send a managed chat turn; reservation and settlement ledger rows are written.
Hit a rolling limit with usage credits on; the turn runs as overage.
A workspace admin reads its invoices.

features.summary: Server records that prove and enforce privacy duties: an append-only security audit trail, consent rows carrying the notice version and surface, data-rights requests with a DPDP reference, legal holds that suspend deletion, retention sweeps recorded per workspace, and a retention matrix describing what each store erases.

purpose.what_it_does: Writes security events to security_audit_logs (and enterprise events for workspaces), records each consent decision as a new row, queues access, correction, erasure, withdrawal, nomination and grievance requests with a DPDP reference, lets workspace admins place legal holds, and runs retention sweeps that record what they deleted or held back (apps/web/lib/security-audit.ts:78-110; apps/web/lib/server/consent-records.ts:83-110; apps/web/lib/server/data-rights-requests.ts:12-20; apps/web/lib/services/retention-service.ts:90-205).
purpose.why_it_exists: To evidence privacy law duties (consent with notice version, rights requests with a clock) and to keep deletion safe: a hold must beat every sweep (docs/compliance/legal-hold-and-ediscovery.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Any visitor or signed-in person (consent, rights requests); workspace owners and admins (legal holds, retention); operators and auditors (audit, queue).
problems_solved: Audit history cannot be edited by the app role; a trigger blocks update and delete (apps/web/db/neon/0123_audit_log_immutability_trigger.sql:65).
Withdrawal is a new row, never an update, so history shows what the person agreed to and when (apps/web/db/neon/0113_dpdp_consent_records.sql comments).
A held subject is never partly erased: account erasure aborts under a hold (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:893-970).
The sweep fails closed if holds cannot be read (apps/web/db/neon/0138_retention_enforcement_and_legal_hold.sql header).
use_cases: Submit an erasure request and receive a DPDP-style reference.
Withdraw product analytics consent.
Admin places a hold on a member during a dispute; the nightly sweep skips that data.
Auditor reads which sweeps deleted or held rows.

where_to_find_it: Web: page /privacy/requests with a rights form and a Consent Centre (apps/web/app/privacy/requests/RightsRequestForm.tsx; ConsentCentre.tsx; YourRightsRequests.tsx).
Rights request types in the form: Access, Correction, Erasure, Withdraw consent, Nomination, Grievance (apps/web/app/privacy/requests/RightsRequestForm.tsx:10-35).

Retention sweep per workspace, opt-in, records outcome deleted, nothing_due, held, aborted or failed in organization_retention_sweeps (apps/web/lib/services/retention-service.ts:182-204); domain sweeps for projects, work, files, artifacts, connector data, notifications and more (apps/web/lib/services/domain-retention-service.ts).

established.statement: Audit events are durably and append-only recorded and classified as audit trail.
Retention sweeps, deletion requests, holds and erasure records are durably stored and classified.
Consent and policy acceptance, with version, are durably recorded and classified.
Audit rows cannot be updated or deleted by the app role; only the owner purges for retention.
A withdrawal is a new row; the newest row per subject and purpose is the live state.
Retention never beats a hold; a hold suspends the sweep for the held data; a refused deletion is itself audited as deletion_blocked_by_legal_hold.
An action a user cannot undo asks first and the question names the consequence.

acceptance_criteria: An UPDATE or DELETE on security_audit_logs by the app role fails with insufficient_privilege.
Granting then withdrawing a purpose gives two rows and hasConsent returns false.
Each consent row stores the current notice version for its purpose and a known surface.
A rights request returns a DPDP-prefixed reference and an audit event privacy_request_submitted.
Posting the same submission token twice returns the same reference with no second row.
With an active hold on a member, the workspace sweep deletes none of that member's held conversations and records outcome held.
Account erasure of a held subject is abandoned and nothing is deleted.
Releasing a hold sets released_at and released_by_user_id and writes legal_hold_released.
inferred: Audit coverage of rights actions is expected on every surface; only web routes were examined [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Add a route or job that moves rights requests through statuses and records the resolution note.
[proposed] Decide whether consent rows should survive account erasure as evidence; today they are erased with the account (apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:152).

steps.what_happens: Person submits a rights request from the web form.
Server checks CSRF and rate limit, validates, inserts the request, then emails the operator inbox through the support email sender.
Email delivery runs at an outside mail service.
Consent decision inserts a new row with notice version and surface.
Admin places a hold; sweeps render the hold exclusion inside their delete statements.
Nightly crons run sweeps and log each outcome.

features.summary: Turns the assistant's streamed text into a readable answer: sanitized Markdown, highlighted code, typeset math and Mermaid diagrams, plus small connector app cards. On web the app card runs in a sandboxed frame on a separate origin; on mobile it shows only the tool's text result. The chat renderer is shared code; each app has its own wiring.

purpose.what_it_does: Parses answer text as Markdown, strips unsafe HTML, highlights code with a Shiki-based highlighter, typesets math with KaTeX, draws Mermaid diagrams on first use, and shows connector 'MCP App' cards in an isolated frame (web) or as plain result text (mobile). (packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/MarkdownContent.tsx:2-5, 57, 820-823)
purpose.why_it_exists: Answers from any model must display the same way and must never run unsafe markup. Connector tools can return small interactive apps; those must run apart from the main app so they cannot read the user's session. (apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/sandbox/route.ts:80-97)
purpose.who_uses_it: Every person reading chat answers on web, the hosted-web desktop window, mobile, the Chrome side panel and the VS Code webview. Connector users see app cards.
problems_solved: Raw Markdown or LaTeX shown as plain symbols.

Unsafe HTML or SVG from a model reaching the page (sanitizer schema: packages/ui/unified-chat/src/components/markdown/markdownSanitizeSchema.ts:1-36; Mermaid output passed through sanitizeSvg: MermaidDiagram.tsx:~232).
Half-written diagrams and formulas flashing errors while an answer streams (MermaidDiagram.tsx looksComplete; MarkdownContent.tsx:748).
Third-party app code touching the host page (iframe sandbox without same-origin: sandbox/route.ts:84).
use_cases: Ask for a worked physics answer and read the formulas typeset.
Ask for a flowchart and read it as a diagram, with the source kept if drawing fails.
Read a code answer with highlighted, copyable code blocks.
A connected tool returns an app; on web the person clicks inside the card; on mobile they read the text result.

Chrome side panel: its own markdown-it pipeline using shared highlighter and math helpers (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/markdown.ts:1-19).
VS Code webview: markdown-it with math helper, html disabled (apps/extension-vscode/src/webview/render.ts:1-24).
prerequisites: A chat answer. Web app cards also need a connector that returns an app and a deployed separate sandbox origin in production (McpAppCard.tsx:111-118).
No subscription is needed to render (none found in the code).

App card: loading text 'Loading MCP App…', an approval prompt before a tool call, and a device-permission ask (McpAppCard.tsx:~404-445).

When the turn finishes, a diagram that is complete is drawn; one that cannot be drawn shows a notice and keeps its source (MermaidDiagram.tsx:~340-352).
If a connector returned an app, the card loads the stored payload, reads the app page, opens the sandbox frame and connects the bridge (McpAppCard.tsx:~225-370).

working: Web: Markdown + raw HTML parsed then sanitized then KaTeX, in that order (MarkdownContent.tsx:818-823).
KaTeX stylesheet imported with the component (MarkdownContent.tsx:57).
Math delimiters normalised so one-line $$ blocks become display math (preprocessMath.ts:1-22).
Shiki highlighter with lazy language loaders and a bounded cache (shikiHighlighter.ts:6-40, 133-160).
Mermaid loaded on first diagram via dynamic import with strict security level, no HTML labels (MermaidDiagram.tsx:~38-50, 135-140).

MCP App flow on web: tool result stored in a table with a 2 MB cap and a 30-day expiry, card fetched by id, resource read, sandbox frame, JSON-RPC bridge, approval for tool calls (apps/web/lib/connectors/mcp-state-store.ts:10-11, 22-60; tool-loop.ts:2969-3000; McpAppCard.tsx:120-370).
Sandbox route: inner frame sandbox 'allow-scripts allow-forms', page CSP built from allow-listed https/wss domains, no-store caching (sandbox/route.ts:49-97, 100-118).
Mobile renders math in a WebView with a locked content policy and embedded KaTeX styles (MathBlock.tsx:21-23; apps/mobile/scripts/vendor-katex-math-styles.cjs).
Chrome extension and VS Code highlight code and typeset math through shared helpers (extension markdown.ts:1-19; vscode render.ts:1-24).
incomplete: Chrome side panel and VS Code webview have no Mermaid rendering in answers; only an artifact-type label for mermaid exists (grep of apps/extension/src and apps/extension-vscode/src: artifactPanel.ts:256-291, artifactPresentation.ts:15,51).
Mobile never opens the app itself; the card only fetches and shows the tool's text (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/cards/McpAppCard.tsx:1-30).
disconnected_or_disabled: In a production web build, if no separate sandbox origin is configured the app card is switched off and falls back to text (McpAppCard.tsx:111-118).
not_available: Interactive MCP App frame on mobile, Chrome and VS Code (mobile shows text; the chat fallback tells people to use a compatible web client: tool-loop.ts:2985-2988). Chrome and VS Code card support: none found in the code (grep 'mcp-app.v1' found only web, mobile, shared packages).

established.statement: S104.03: answers are parsed as Markdown and sanitized before rendering.
S104.02: code blocks are highlighted by a highlighter engine in the mounted renderer.
T07: math is typeset with KaTeX in the mounted chat renderer.
T06: Mermaid code blocks render as diagrams in the mounted chat renderer.
T12: connector tools that return an MCP App render it inline in an isolated sandbox frame driven by a JSON-RPC bridge.
If a capability such as live voice is unavailable, the UI says so without broken controls.
Local mode must fail closed and never silently route to remote compute.

acceptance_criteria: A reply containing <script> or an onerror attribute shows no running script and no broken layout.
A reply with $$ x^2 $$ and \( a+b \) shows typeset math; a malformed formula never leaves a visible error flash while still streaming.
A reply with a closed ```mermaid block shows a diagram with 'Show source', 'Copy diagram source' and 'Expand diagram'.
A reply with an invalid diagram shows 'This diagram could not be drawn' and the source.
A fenced code block with a known language is coloured and copyable; with an unknown language it still shows as plain code.
On web production without a sandbox origin an MCP App card shows the plain tool result and the notice text.
An MCP App tool call from the frame asks the person before it runs.
inferred: Rendering is independent of mode (Local, own key, Cloud) because it runs on the client over text already received [inferred].
A connector app card is only produced in Cloud turns because it is created in the Cloud tool loop on the server [inferred from tool-loop.ts:2969-3000].
proposed: [proposed] Add an empty-state and error-state spec for formulas, since the brief lists it as not verified.
[proposed] Show Mermaid in the Chrome and VS Code answer renderers or label the code block clearly as a diagram source.
[proposed] Let mobile open the app card in a locked WebView or label it 'Open on web'.

steps.what_happens: Answer text arrives over the stream and is held in client state.
Math is normalised, Markdown parsed, raw HTML sanitized, KaTeX applied.
Code is highlighted after the highlighter and language module load.
Mermaid module is imported on first diagram; the SVG is built in an offscreen host, sanitized, cached (32 entries).
Connector tool runs in the Cloud tool loop; if it returns an app, the server stores the payload and adds an 'mcp-app.v1' card to the turn.
The card fetches the payload and reads the app page through the connector endpoint, which contacts the connector's server.
The app runs in an iframe from the sandbox origin; its tool calls go back through the bridge and the connector endpoint, with person approval.

data.what: MCP App payload (tool input and result)
data.synced: Read by the same signed-in user on any web client
data.retained_or_deleted: Expires 30 days after creation (mcp-state-store.ts:10, 54); deletion job: unknown

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Rendering does not call any model or provider. The text it shows can come from any model in any mode. Connector apps come from the connector's own server, not a model provider.

access_and_usage.account: Rendering needs no account. The app card payload route needs a signed-in user (apps/web/app/api/mcp-apps/payload/[payloadId]/route.ts:20-28).
