features.summary: The web side panel where a person opens, edits, versions and exports what the assistant made: rich documents (Tiptap), code (CodeMirror), charts (recharts), slide decks, read-only spreadsheet grids, PDFs, and images with a paint-to-change mask. Real .pptx files come from a separate server tool. Video editing and cell editing are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows each artifact type in its own viewer or editor, keeps versions, and lets the person export or ask the assistant for changes. (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactPreview.tsx:1935-1985, 3291-3340)
purpose.why_it_exists: Long outputs are easier to read and revise beside the chat than inside it; the product requirements list preview, source view, versions, export and share for every artifact. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 9.5)
purpose.who_uses_it: People who ask for documents, code, charts, decks, tables or images.

features.summary: A PDF attached to chat is read on our servers with PDF.js: text per page, page images for scanned pages, size limits and clear errors. Uploads and generated files go to S3-compatible storage, large files in resumable parts. On web a PDF artifact opens in the browser's own viewer; mobile ships its own PDF.js viewer.

purpose.what_it_does: Extracts text and scanned-page images from PDFs so any model can use them, and stores uploaded and generated files in object storage with resumable multipart upload. (apps/web/lib/server/pdf-attachment-content.ts:220-300; apps/web/app/api/files/uploads/resumable-upload.ts)
purpose.why_it_exists: A model route may have no document channel; turning a PDF into text or images works with every route (comment at pdf-attachment-content.ts:146-153). Large files need parts so a dropped connection does not restart the transfer.
purpose.who_uses_it: People attaching documents to Cloud chats and project knowledge.
problems_solved: Chat turn failing because a route cannot take PDF bytes.
Scanned PDFs with no text.
Large uploads that fail midway.
use_cases: Attach a contract and ask for a summary.
Attach a scanned form; pages go in as images.
Upload a 300 MB file in parts on a weak connection.

where_to_find_it: Web composer attach control; the resulting PDF artifact opens in the panel (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2011).
Mobile: viewer opens a PDF in a bundled PDF.js page in a WebView (PdfFileView.tsx).
Desktop: hosted web (AGENTS.md section 5).
CLI: account file uploads (apps/cli/src/app_server/account_uploads.rs exists; behaviour not read).
prerequisites: Signed in for Cloud upload routes (uploads route is user scoped).
screens_and_controls: Panel fallback: 'Inline preview unavailable' or "This PDF couldn't be displayed." with Retry and download (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2022-2040).
Error text for unreadable files: '<name> could not be read as a PDF.' or '<name> is password protected. Remove the password and upload it again.' (pdf-attachment-content.ts:41-44).
journey: Attach a PDF (type application/pdf is in the allowed list: packages/contracts/types/src/attachment-policy.json).
The file is uploaded; large files use parts and a signed session.
On send, the server loads the object, runs PDF.js, builds text with '[Page N]' markers and page images for scanned pages.
The model receives text, images and a note for pages left out (chat-attachment-hydration.ts:681-740).
Ask about the file.
feedback_and_outputs: A truncation notice is raised when pages, scanned pages or text were cut (chat-attachment-hydration.ts:693-699).
A live turn gets a 400 'unreadable_attachment' error; a replayed history degrades the part (chat-attachment-hydration.ts:684-690).
settings: Attachment policy JSON: max 25 MB inline, 20 attachments, large files up to 500 MB, cellular confirm over 50 MB (chat-attachment-policy.json:2-5, 66-70).

working: Server-side extraction with the legacy PDF.js build, up to 250 text pages and 30 scanned page images, 8 MB total image bytes, text truncated to the shared limit (pdf-attachment-content.ts:9-17,144,196-204,229-260).
Encrypted and corrupt files raise a typed error (pdf-attachment-content.ts:51-60,288-295).

Resumable multipart upload with signed sessions, 5 MB parts, 4 MB relay segments, session lifetime equal to the orphan multipart age of 24 hours (resumable-upload.ts:50; upload-contract.json; lifecycle.ts:8).
S3-compatible adapter plus an in-memory adapter and a 'none' provider choice (object-storage/src/types.ts:3; factory.ts; adapters/s3.ts).
Upload routes: POST create, part and complete routes under /api/files/uploads, rate-limited (uploads/route.ts:~224; parts/route.ts).
Intake record table for large chat files (0422_chat_file_intakes.sql:42).
Mobile on-device PDF viewer assembled from a vendored PDF.js (apps/mobile/scripts/vendor-pdfjs-viewer.cjs; PdfFileView.tsx:30-40).
incomplete: Brief says T08 'in-product viewer backed by a rendering engine'. On web the viewer is the browser's built-in viewer through an iframe, not PDF.js on the client (ArtifactPreview.tsx:2011-2018; PDF.js used only in server files, grep of apps/web).
disconnected_or_disabled: Resumable upload throws 'Uploading a file in parts is not available on this deployment.' when private storage or multipart support is not configured (resumable-upload.ts:66-80).
not_available: PDF text extraction on the device for Local chat: none found in the code (extraction is a server module marked server-only).
Client-side PDF.js viewer on web: none found.

established.statement: S104.12: uploaded and generated files are stored in S3-compatible object storage.
T08: PDFs open in an in-product viewer backed by a PDF engine and PDF text is parsed by a PDF engine.
Local files remain local in Local mode; no hidden cloud call.
Object storage is resolved in one place so the host can change by environment.

A scanned PDF produces page images, up to the image cap, and a note for omitted pages.

A non-PDF file renamed .pdf returns 'could not be read as a PDF'.
A 100 MB upload resumes after a dropped connection without restarting.
A deployment with no storage returns the capability-unavailable message instead of failing silently.
inferred: Plan limits on attachment size are defined by shared policy constants (MAX_PLAN_ATTACHMENT_BYTES in billing-catalog.ts:748) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] State clearly in docs that the web PDF view is the browser viewer; add a shared PDF.js viewer if the same look is needed on every app.
[proposed] Add a Local-mode PDF text path on mobile if Local chat should read PDFs.

features.summary: Chat answers stream from the server over server-sent events with a 2-second keepalive. Live voice on web and mobile uses a WebRTC peer connection to a server-created Cloud session. Remote-control pairing returns a signaling address. Several people editing one document at once is not built; no CRDT code exists.

purpose.what_it_does: Streams model output as it is produced, runs a spoken two-way conversation over WebRTC, and hands a paired phone the signaling address of the relay. (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/sse-heartbeat.ts:29-80; apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:36-58,447; apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:100-140)
purpose.why_it_exists: Long answers feel faster when they stream, proxies drop idle connections, and voice needs real-time audio.
purpose.who_uses_it: Everyone who chats; people who talk to the assistant; people pairing a phone with a desktop.
problems_solved: Idle stream closed by a proxy (heartbeat comment line every 2 s).
Silent loss of a voice session (reconnect and keepalive constants).
A scanned QR joining a stranger's desktop (account check at pairing claim).
use_cases: Watch an answer type out.
Talk with the assistant hands free.
Pair the phone to a desktop for remote control (hidden in v1 per owner decision in memory; the code is present).

where_to_find_it: Streaming: any chat on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile, CLI, Chrome, VS Code.
Live voice: web composer voice mode (VoiceModeSurface.tsx) and mobile live voice bar (LiveVoiceBar tests).
prerequisites: Live voice: Cloud mode, signed in, adult eligibility, microphone permission, a plan that allows voice, a secure server URL on mobile (route.ts:175-300; liveVoiceAvailability.ts:25-50).
screens_and_controls: Web messages: 'Microphone access was denied. Allow the microphone to use voice mode.', 'No microphone is available in this browser.', 'This browser cannot open a voice connection.' (live-voice-session.ts:61-74).
Mobile: 'Live voice runs in AGI Cloud, so Local Mode stays turn based.' and 'Sign in to use live voice; this chat stays turn based.' (liveVoiceAvailability.ts:22-23).

'Voice ran out of included minutes on this plan, so the session ended. Nothing was lost from the conversation.' (line 71-72).
Limit notices '5-hour limit reached', 'Weekly limit reached', 'Monthly limit reached' with reset time (lines 258-268).
settings: Voice choice, language, pace and reasoning are sent to the server (live-voice-session.ts imports live-voices); control locations unknown.

working: SSE with comment keepalives every 2 s, disconnect logging and metric (sse-heartbeat.ts:9,27-80).
Heartbeat wrapper used by the chat completions route, resume routes and approval route (grep of withSseHeartbeat).

features.summary: The desktop app is an Electron shell with a sandboxed window showing the hosted web app. The mobile app is Expo React Native with native modules. The CLI is a Rust program with a ratatui terminal interface and an app-server that serves other clients. The Tauri desktop code is retained internal code.

purpose.what_it_does: Packages the product for each native platform: a privileged Electron main process around a remote web page, an Expo app with native modules, and a Rust terminal app. (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1090-1125; apps/mobile/package.json; apps/cli/Cargo.toml:15-25)
purpose.why_it_exists: Native shells give files, windows, notifications, secure storage and a terminal home that a web page cannot.
purpose.who_uses_it: People installing AGI on Mac or Windows, on a phone, or using the terminal.
problems_solved: One web codebase for desktop chat.
Safe privileged code: renderer is sandboxed with context isolation.
The terminal front end is separated from the agent engine so VS Code and others can reuse it (app_server.rs:1-30).
use_cases: Open AGI Desktop and chat in a window.
Share a window with the assistant.
Run `agi` in a terminal.
Use AGI Mobile offline.

Mobile: installed app with scheme 'agiworkforce' (app.config.js:160).

CLI also serves MCP over stdio (app_server.rs:6-12) and has app-server tests (apps/cli/tests/app_server_stdio.rs, app_server_websocket.rs).
incomplete: Desktop main-process trust boundaries beyond these lines were not read; the dispatcher gates commands by capability (dispatcher.ts:3200-3290).
disconnected_or_disabled: Electron desktop refuses local inference commands by design: 'answers every conversation in the cloud' (dispatcher.ts:3234-3244; docs/decisions/2026-09-15-founder-decisions.md D-2026-09-15-04).
Tauri desktop code under apps/desktop/src and src-tauri is retained internal code (docs/security/security.md:310-320).
not_available: Native shell on web and Chrome: not applicable.

established.statement: S104.09: the desktop app runs as a native Electron shell with a privileged main process.
S104.10: the mobile app is a native Expo React Native app with native modules.
T10: the CLI separates a Rust TUI front end from its agent runtime, which also serves other clients as an app-server.
Electron is the public AGI Workforce desktop; Tauri is not a second public product (partly superseded 2026-10-24).
Desktop chat is Cloud; local coding sessions run the CLI.

A repeated renderer crash shows the crash screen instead of a blank window.

features.summary: AGI Mobile stores chats in an encrypted SQLite database whose 256-bit key sits in device secure storage, and can run a small model on the phone for free without an account. Onboarding checks the device and recommends a model. The Electron desktop does not run on-device models; only the retained Tauri code checks a local model server.

purpose.what_it_does: Keeps mobile data encrypted on the device and runs inference there when the phone supports it. (apps/mobile/storage/db.ts:19-30,130-160; packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts)
purpose.why_it_exists: Local mode must work without an account, keep work on the device and make no hidden cloud calls. (doc: docs/product/requirements.md section 7.1)
purpose.who_uses_it: Mobile users who want private, free, offline chat.
problems_solved: Readable chats if the phone is lost (encryption).
Needing an account or payment for basic chat.
Not knowing whether a device can run a model.
use_cases: Chat on a plane with no network.
Finish onboarding and download a recommended model.
Check tokens per second in Performance settings.

Desktop Tauri build (retained internal): local model server health monitor (App.tsx:746-752).
prerequisites: A supported phone; downloading a model needs storage and network; Local use needs no sign-in (doc: docs/product/requirements.md M-US-001).
screens_and_controls: 'Recommended' badge, 'Pick a different model', 'Continue without downloading', 'Sign in to use Cloud', 'Continue' and 'Skip for now' (onboarding.tsx:648-810).
When unsupported: '<model> is unavailable on this device.', 'Browse local models', 'Continue without a local model' (onboarding.tsx:684-686,777-794).
Download screen: 'The download continues if you leave this screen.', 'Try again', 'Continue to chat' (onboarding.tsx:880-916).

Local data reset notice if the database could not be read (localDataReset.ts; LocalDataResetNotice test).
settings: Performance chip toggle; model picker; installed models store (installedModels.ts).

working: Encrypted SQLite through expo-sqlite with SQLCipher enabled (app.config.js:454); key is 32 random bytes in hex kept in secure storage, this-device-only, id agi_sqlcipher_db_key_v1 (db.ts:23-60).

features.summary: Web search over a person's own chats, projects, files and indexed documents, backed by Neon Postgres. Chat titles and messages match by substring; indexed documents (uploaded knowledge, artifacts, reports) match by full text plus a meaning (vector) search, merged by rank. No separate search engine exists. Mobile calls the same API only in Cloud mode.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a signed-in person find past chats, projects, files, schedules and indexed documents from one search box, and lets the chat pipeline pull relevant passages from uploaded knowledge and past chats into a turn. Chat, project and file rows are matched with case-insensitive substring tests (route.ts:321,339,356,372). Indexed documents are matched by Postgres full text and by vector distance, then fused (retrieval-search-service.ts:187-260; rank.ts:24-30).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires conversations and messages to be searched through an indexed search engine behind a search API (S104.13) and knowledge chunks to carry embeddings in a vector index queried by cosine distance (S104.14). The code answers both inside the database instead of a separate engine (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/104-named-technology-options-not-claims-about-competitor-interna.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in web users (and mobile users in Cloud mode) who search their history, and the chat server code that retrieves knowledge passages for a question.
problems_solved: Finding an old chat or message without scrolling.
Answering from long uploaded files whose text does not fit the prompt, by retrieving only the best passages (project-knowledge-retrieval.ts:1-40).
Matching a question to a passage that uses different words, through the vector leg (retrieval-search-service.ts:187-260).
Keeping results private to the owner and the active workspace (retrieval-search-service.ts:187-205).
use_cases: Press the search control on web, type a chat title word, open the matching chat.
Ask a question in a project that has uploaded files; the answer draws on retrieved passages.
Ask 'what did we decide last week' and have past-chat excerpts retrieved by meaning, with a keyword fallback (past-chat-context-service.ts:365-392).
Filter search by message role or date range.

Search must be allowed for the workspace data region, otherwise the route refuses (route.ts:154-170).
The meaning leg needs indexed documents, an embedding route and managed compute access (retrieval-search-service.ts:152-175; retrieval-embedding-service.ts:226-248).
screens_and_controls: Search input, category tabs, role filter 'All messages', date range, include-archived toggle, recent and popular searches, clear history (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:134-183,568; global-search-service.ts:321-370).
API also accepts mode (strategy), kind, limit up to 100, type=recent|popular|suggestions (route.ts:41-42,262-300,392-412).
journey: Open the search dialog and type a query.
The page calls GET /api/search with the query, category and filters (global-search-service.ts:189).
The server returns chat and message rows, projects, files, schedules and indexed documents with a semantic state (route.ts:618-630).
The person opens a result; the query is recorded in search history unless track=false or the request is cross-site (route.ts:600-615).
feedback_and_outputs: Result lists per category with highlighted matches (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:402).
Stats of chat, message, project, file and document matches (route.ts:590-600).
'Search unavailable / Something went wrong. Please close and try again.' on dialog failure (GlobalSearchDialog.tsx:445-452).

settings: Search history can be cleared (route.ts:660-681).
Temporary chats are excluded from search (route.ts:322-327; retrieval-search-service.ts:240-250).
Per-workspace data region decides whether search is served (route.ts:154-170).

working: Web GET /api/search is rate limited, scoped to user and organization, and bounded: default 50 and maximum 100 results (route.ts:41-42,246-260).

Chat titles, project names and descriptions, file names and prompts, and message content are matched with ilike on trigram indexes (route.ts:321,339,356,372; 0101_sync_and_search_indexes.sql:80-100). Message query is capped at 100 rows (route.ts:466).

Indexed documents are searched in 'hybrid' strategy by default: full text (ts_rank_cd over a stored tsvector, simple config) and vector (cosine distance operator over a 1536-dimension embedding with an HNSW index), fused by reciprocal rank and re-scored (types.ts:177; 0202_retrieval_index.sql:120-148; rank.ts:5-70).
Candidates are min(100, limit x 4); at most 3 hits per source on the search route (retrieval-search-service.ts:41-45,330-390; route.ts:406-415).
The query embedding is metered: entitlement check, daily 'vector_queries' allowance, usage reservation and settle (retrieval-embedding-service.ts:204-330).
If embedding is refused or fails, search falls back to full text only and logs it (retrieval-search-service.ts:177-183).

Chunks are indexed by a cron every 10 minutes that dispatches workflows (vercel.json:61-64; index-retrieval-documents/route.ts:15-37); an embedding failure stores chunks for keyword search and retries (retrieval-index-service.ts:118,511).
Past-chat and project-knowledge retrieval reuse the same provider (past-chat-context-service.ts:278-291; project-knowledge-retrieval.ts:1-40).
Row level security is forced on retrieval tables (0202_retrieval_index.sql:150-156).
incomplete: The indexed-document leg is skipped when a role or date filter is set or the category is Scheduled, so those searches use substring rows only (route.ts:398-401).
Mobile reads only 'results' and 'projects' from the response, so indexed documents are not shown there [inferred] (chatViewStore.ts:250-262).
Mobile past-chat cloud search sends only the first query term (pastChatContext.ts:75-82).
disconnected_or_disabled: Meaning search is off for an account with no embedded chunks ('no_index') or no embedding route (retrieval-search-service.ts:155-166; retrieval-embedding-service.ts:140-146).
not_available: No standalone search engine; none found in the code (retrieval-search-service.ts:187-260).
Desktop, CLI, VS Code and Chrome do not call /api/search: not found in .ts/.tsx; Rust not searched.

established.statement: Conversations and messages are searched through an indexed search engine behind a search API.
Knowledge chunks carry embeddings in a vector index queried by cosine distance.
Data lives in PostgreSQL (Neon) reached through the data-layer adapter.
Queries are scoped to the user.
ChatGPT and Claude search of chat history are product references; verify current pages before material changes.

acceptance_criteria: A query matching a chat title returns that chat in Sessions for its owner and never for another user.
A query for a phrase present only in an uploaded document returns the document in 'documents' with semantic state 'used' when embeddings exist.
With the embedding route unavailable, the same query still returns full-text hits and semantic state 'unavailable'.
limit above 100 is rejected or bounded; default is 50.
A role, startDate or endDate filter returns message rows and no indexed documents.
Temporary chats and deleted chats never appear.
Free account at its daily vector-query allowance still gets keyword results.
inferred: Mobile Local mode searches only on-device data and sends nothing to /api/search [inferred] (chatViewStore.ts:244-250).

Substring search over messages is the only path for chat messages; the vector index covers documents, artifacts and reports, not every message [inferred] (route.ts:372; retrieval-search-service.ts:240-250).
proposed: [proposed] Show indexed-document hits in the mobile Cloud search UI.
[proposed] Tell the person when a filter turned meaning search off.

steps.what_happens: Web sends GET /api/search with q, category and filters.
Server rate limits, resolves user, organization and region, and refuses if the region cannot be served.
Substring queries run against chats, messages, projects and files in Postgres.
Unless a filter forbids it, the indexed-document search starts in hybrid mode: checks the account has embedded chunks.
The query text (first 2000 characters) is embedded through the managed embedding route after entitlement, allowance and reservation checks.
One SQL statement runs a full-text leg and a vector leg, merges them, then the code reranks, removes near-duplicates and caps hits per source.
Response returns rows, documents, semantic state and stats; the query is logged to search history.

aliases: Background jobs and durable agent runs
features.summary: Two separate server mechanisms. A queue in the database holds small jobs (notifications, email, deletion, exports) that a cron route drains every five minutes. Cloud agent turns run on the Vercel Workflow engine, are journaled in the database, and can be reattached from the Tasks page after a tab closes.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs long or retried work off the request: queued jobs with retries and dead letters (job-service.ts:231-540) and durable cloud agent turns that wait for a person's device up to an hour (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:14-65).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires background jobs queued and drained by a scheduled worker (S104.15) and long agent and indexing runs on a durable workflow engine (S104.16). Agent turns that die with the browser connection lose work.
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users who start cloud agent tasks; desktop and mobile users whose cloud runs show in Tasks; operators who watch dead jobs in admin.
problems_solved: Work survives a closed tab, because the run is journaled and attached to a workflow (0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:1-45; start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:150-194).
Transient failures retry with backoff; permanent failures stop (job-service.ts:454-496).
A sleeping device is waited for, not failed (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:14-65).
use_cases: Start an Agi Work task, close the tab, return to Tasks and read the result.
An account erasure or data export runs in the queue.
A schedule-completed email is sent with retry.
A device-revoke message to the relay is retried until it answers (job-handlers.ts:300-340).

where_to_find_it: Web: the Tasks page (apps/web/app/tasks/page.tsx) with filters Active, Needs you, All, Archived and layouts List and Board (TasksPage.tsx:70-81).
Desktop shell code has a Tasks view and cloud runtime, but the public Electron window shows the hosted web app, so treat the web page as what desktop users get (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
Mobile: settings row 'Cloud agent' with statuses Available, Not available on this server, Not included in your account, Status unavailable (CloudAgentStatus.tsx:15-21).
Job queue itself has no user screen; operators use the admin background-jobs endpoint (app/api/admin/background-jobs).
prerequisites: Signed in with a Managed Cloud account.
For Work mode, the Work capability must be admitted (start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:84-92).
Durable start must not be switched off (durable-initial-turns.ts:1-20).
screens_and_controls: Tasks list with cancel, pause, resume, archive and approval actions (TasksPage.tsx:340-490).
Run snapshot, journal and steer endpoints under /api/llm/v1/chat/completions/runs.
journey: Send an agent turn in chat; the server creates a run row and starts the workflow.
The stream is read live; the person may close the tab.
Later open Tasks; the run list is read from the runs API and the journal replays.
Resolve any approval, or read the result.
feedback_and_outputs: Run states queued, running, awaiting_input, ready_for_review, completed, failed, cancelled, paused, archived (0061_cloud_agent_runs.sql:9-25).
Device wait notices 'waiting', 'back', 'withdrawn' (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:19-64).

working: vercel.json schedules drain-background-jobs every 5 minutes (vercel.json:149-152).

The drain verifies cron authentication, honors low-power mode, runs project-knowledge cleanup, then drains with a 250-second budget and at most 12 jobs in flight (drain-background-jobs/route.ts:17-50).
Low power (AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1) skips only after minute 15 of each hour, so the first 15 minutes still run (cron-low-power.ts:5-20).
Nine queue policies set concurrency, attempts, backoff, lease and retention, e.g. email 8 attempts, data-deletion 12 (job-queues.ts:19-100).
Backoff is exponential with jitter, capped per queue (job-queues.ts:135-152).
A PermanentJobError dead-letters at once; exhausted attempts also dead-letter; expired leases are reaped (job-service.ts:116-121,454-540).
Seventeen job kinds map to queues; the handler registry covers 17 handlers (job-queues.ts:108-128; job-handlers.ts:340-367).
Cloud agent turns start through start() from the workflow package and the run is attached to its workflow id; if attach fails the workflow is cancelled (start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:150-194).
The workflow waits up to 60 minutes for the device in 'retryInMs' steps, then withdraws device tools and continues (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:14-65).
Work-plan settle and stream close run on success and on failure (cloud-agent-workflow.ts:67-100).
If durable transport is unavailable the turn can run inline, request-scoped (start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:196-262).
incomplete: When the kill switch AGI_DURABLE_INITIAL_TURNS is 0, false or off, new turns die with the connection (durable-initial-turns.ts:8-18).
Admin view of dead jobs exists, but user-facing display of job failure was not found (unknown).
disconnected_or_disabled: Agent runs are not queue jobs: no agent kind exists in the job registry (job-queues.ts:108-128).
not_available: Mobile and desktop handling of runs not fully read; mobile shows only a cloud-agent availability row (CloudAgentStatus.tsx:15-50).

established.statement: Background jobs are queued and drained by a scheduled worker.
Long agent and indexing runs execute on a durable workflow engine.
Rate limits and limits are configuration; design for bounded resources and backpressure.
Dead letters carrying Google user data are kept no longer than 30 days.
Background mode is non-ZDR because it needs stored response data.

acceptance_criteria: Cron without valid auth returns 401.
With AGI_DB_LOW_POWER=1 after minute 15 the drain returns skipped 'db_low_power' and touches nothing.
A job throwing PermanentJobError becomes dead on its first attempt.
A job failing transiently is requeued with a delay not above the queue maximum and dead after max attempts.
Closing the tab during a cloud agent turn does not cancel it; Tasks later shows its result.
A device that is offline holds the run for up to 60 minutes, then continues without device tools.
With the kill switch on, the turn still completes inline and the run is recorded.
inferred: Free-trial turns use the same durable path since the transport no longer depends on tier [inferred] (start-cloud-agent-workflow.ts:206-262 comment).
proposed: [proposed] Show the person the reason when a run degraded to inline.
[proposed] Expose failed job reasons to the owner of the job where Google data rules allow.

steps.what_happens: Vercel cron calls the drain route on schedule.
Route checks cron auth and low-power skip, then reaps expired leases and claims jobs per queue.
Each handler runs; success completes, failure retries with backoff or dead-letters.
For an agent turn, the chat route builds the workflow input, starts the workflow and attaches its id to the run row.
Workflow checks device presence, runs each model/tool invocation as a step, loops on 'continue', then closes the stream.
The client reconnects through the runs API and replays journal events by sequence.

aliases: Cloud code sandbox and browser automation
features.summary: Two features. On the web, Cloud Code and code execution tools run in a hosted sandbox, available only when the deployment turns it on and the plan includes it. In the Chrome extension, a signed-in agent drives a real tab through the Chrome debugger protocol, with per-site approval and permission modes.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs model-written code in an isolated hosted sandbox (web), and clicks, types, navigates and reads pages in the person's browser through the debugger protocol (Chrome extension).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires cloud code to run in a hosted sandbox provider (S104.24, status partial) and the agent to drive a real browser through an automation engine (S104.25) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/104-named-technology-options-not-claims-about-competitor-interna.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web users on a plan that includes Cloud Code; Chrome extension users who approve browser tasks.
problems_solved: Running code safely away from the user's machine.
Doing multi-step web tasks in a signed-in session.
Controlling risk: sensitive sites, purchases and uploads always ask (approvalPolicy.ts:3-35; spAutonomyFullAccessTooltip).
use_cases: Open a Cloud Code session and run commands.
Ask chat to run Python and get a chart file back.
In the side panel, ask the agent to fill a form on an approved site.
Run an unattended task with the YOLO permission mode on approved sites.

where_to_find_it: Web: Cloud Code page at /code (CloudCodePage.tsx); notices explain why it is unavailable (CloudCodePage.tsx:2067-2073).
Chrome: side panel autonomy menu 'How should AGI act in your browser?' with Ask first, Auto, Full access, YOLO (_locales/en/messages.json keys spAutonomy*).
Mobile: settings row 'Cloud agent' shows availability for cloud code (CloudAgentStatus.tsx:15-21).
Desktop, CLI, VS Code: not read for this feature.
prerequisites: Web sandbox: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1, a sandbox key and a priceable compute rate on the server, and a plan that includes Cloud Code (gate.ts:20-28; sessions/route.ts:55-66).
Chrome: signed-in extension, host permission for the site, browser-control consent for the origin (browserControlConsent.ts:4-17).
Chrome debugger permission is in the manifest (manifest.json:22).

Chrome: permission mode menu, approval prompts, consent text 'This grants full DevTools-Protocol control' (browserControlConsent.ts:6).
journey: Web: open /code; the page reads availability; if enabled and entitled, create a session; run commands or the agent.
Chrome: type a task; the agent selects a model through Managed Cloud; before each action the policy decides ask or act; Chrome shows its debugging banner while attached.
feedback_and_outputs: Web notice when unavailable, with an upgrade link when the plan lacks it (CloudCodePage.tsx:2067-2105).
Model-facing sentence per refusal cause: not configured, no capacity, policy, over quota, provider error (unavailability.ts:10-30).
Chrome approval cards and action descriptions (describeAction.ts).

Chrome per-site allowlist and one-time grants (oneTimeSiteGrants.ts; browserControlConsent.ts).

working: Three gates exist: e2bExecutionEnabled is true if a key is set OR the flag is 1; e2bCutoverEnabled needs the flag equal to 1; e2bProvisioningReady needs flag, key and a priceable rate (gate.ts:9-28).
The runtime refuses with 'not-configured' only if the loose gate is false (runtime.ts:796); it also fail-closes when compute has no resolvable rate (runtime.ts:880-889).

Chat execution tools check the strict cutover flag (tool-loop.ts:2802); the chat code-runs route does the same (code-runs/route.ts:76); Cloud Code routes use the provisioning gate (sessions/route.ts:61; agent/route.ts:101).
Session list returns availability {deploymentEnabled, planEntitled, planTier, maxSessions} (sessions/route.ts:55-66); plan inclusion comes from plan limits (billing-catalog.ts:801-841).
Chrome attaches the debugger per tab with a hold count and queues attach and detach operations (debuggerSession.ts:62-72,110-128,185-230).
User-cancelled detach and any detach drop holds and notify handlers (debuggerSession.ts:151-175).
CDP commands check ownership before and after each command, and Runtime.evaluate is limited to an isolated world (cdpDriver.ts:296-330).
Approval policy always asks for download, upload, sensitive input, sensitive sites, payment, publish and more; modes ask, auto, full, yolo (approvalPolicy.ts:3-35; askBeforeActing.ts:5-52).
Browser tasks call the Managed Cloud gateway and pick models by account access (cloudAgentClient.ts:47-110,312-317).
incomplete: Sandbox gate code is looser than the documented rule: a key alone enables the runtime path even with the flag at 0 (gate.ts:9-14; gate.test.ts:69-104).
S104.24 is partial: the brief says production should switch it on (doc: brief S104.24).
disconnected_or_disabled: Sandbox is off by default: apps/web/.env.example ships AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=0 (.env.example:382-386).
When the sandbox is off, code execution uses the provider-native interpreter instead (hosted-code-execution.ts:37-44; doc: brief S104.24).
not_available: Chrome automation has no own-key or Local model path: only Managed Cloud models are admitted (cloudAgentClient.ts:84-92).
Desktop, CLI, VS Code automation not read.

established.statement: Cloud code runs in a hosted sandbox provider.
The agent drives a real browser through an automation engine (CDP).
Sandbox is built but off unless AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1; turn it on in production.
Documentation availability stays separate from account, region and route availability; sandboxing is a harness feature, not a model capability.
Security behavior fails closed and permissions are least-privilege.

acceptance_criteria: With flag 0 and no key, a chat execution tool call returns 'not available' and the model tells the user why.
With flag 1 and key but no compute rate, session creation is refused and the page says it is not available on this server.
A plan without Cloud Code sees the plan-not-entitled notice and an upgrade path.
Session count never exceeds the plan maximum; the next create reports 'no-capacity'.
In Chrome, a click on a purchase button never completes without the person, in any mode.
Cancelling the Chrome debugging banner stops the run.
An upload or download always asks.
inferred: The loose gate may let a key-only deployment reach the sandbox from the runtime while routes still refuse [inferred] (gate.ts:9-28).
proposed: [proposed] Make runtime.ts use the strict gate so all callers agree.
[proposed] Show the unavailable cause on the web page, not only to the model.

Commands and agent turns run inside the sandbox; results and files return to the page.

aliases: Accounts, payments, encryption keys, monitoring and release builds
features.summary: Six platform services around the product. Sign-in goes through a hosted identity provider behind a port. Checkout creates payment sessions and verifies webhooks. Enterprise workspaces can wrap keys with AWS, GCP or Azure key services. Errors and traces export when configured. Flags live in the database. Releases are signed in CI.

purpose.what_it_does: Provides sign-in (web and mobile), paid-plan checkout and webhooks, customer-managed encryption keys, error and trace export, per-user feature flags and entitlement bundles, and signed desktop, Windows and mobile builds.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief names these as the product's account, payment, key, monitoring, flag and release layers (S104.19 to S104.23, S104.27) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/104-named-technology-options-not-claims-about-competitor-interna.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Every signed-in person (sign-in, flags), buyers (checkout), enterprise admins (keys), developers and operators (monitoring, CI).
problems_solved: Secure account identity without custom passwords code.
Reliable plan changes from verified payment events.
Enterprise control of data keys.
Seeing production errors with the build that caused them.
Turning features on and off per user or workspace.
Shipping installers that operating systems trust.
use_cases: Sign in on web or mobile.
An admin attaches a customer-managed key to the workspace.
A developer reads an error in the error tracker.
Staff turn a capability off with a kill switch.

working: Identity is chosen in one place through a port, so the provider can change by configuration plus an adapter (identity.ts:11-30). The web client provider is Clerk with telemetry off (Provider.tsx:24-30) and loads only on routes that need it (BrowserIdentityBoundary.tsx:7-20). The proxy builds its middleware from the port (proxy.ts:30).
Mobile uses the Clerk Expo provider with a token cache (apps/mobile/app/_layout.tsx:58-59,994).

Checkout checks CSRF, the enabled gate, rate limit and plan-change rules, reuses or creates a customer, refuses a second live subscription, and creates a subscription-mode session (checkout/route.ts:169-200,372-500).
Webhooks verify the signature with a 60-second tolerance, check idempotency, then dispatch about 20 event types (verify.ts:14-45; stripe-webhook/route.ts:48-76).

Key providers: AWS, GCP and Azure providers are built only if their credentials exist, so an unconfigured one cannot answer; a local provider exists outside production only (kms-providers.ts:13-14,353-370; organization-encryption-keys.ts:231-242).
Keys are Enterprise-gated and owner-gated for revoke (keys-access.ts:25-60).
Error tracking starts only in production with a DSN; trace export starts only with an endpoint; platform keys are preloaded at boot (instrumentation.ts:80-125; sentry-shared.ts:23-25).

Flag definitions are read from feature_flag_definitions with a cache of 30 seconds by default and a fail-closed mode (flag-store.ts:111-170; flag-config.ts:18); /api/me evaluates flags and kill switches per subject (me/route.ts:236-300).

Desktop macOS release signs, notarizes and staples installers with App Store Connect credentials (release-desktop-cloud.yml:212-236,272); Windows release uses Azure artifact signing (build-windows-release.yml:136,229); CI has jobs for guards, lint, typecheck, build, security, E2E (ci.yml:22-1833).
incomplete: Checkout may be off in an environment: the example env sets it false (.env.example:232).
Own checkout flow on Local and BYOK: not required, they are free (checkout/route.ts:178-181).
disconnected_or_disabled: Monitoring does nothing without a DSN or endpoint (sentry-shared.ts:23-25; instrumentation.ts:96-120).
Mobile and extension have no error-tracking package in their manifests; desktop has one (apps/desktop/package.json:93) - mobile, extension: none found.
not_available: CLI, VS Code and Chrome sign-in providers not read here.

established.statement: Encryption keys are held in a key ring and can be wrapped by a cloud KMS (AWS, GCP, Azure).
Sign-in on web and mobile goes through a hosted authentication provider behind an identity port.
Payments run through a payment provider with checkout sessions and verified webhooks.
Errors and traces are exported to an observability platform.
Features are gated by a server-side flag system with stored definitions and per-subject evaluation.
CI builds and tests every change; release pipelines sign and notarize installers.
Secrets are never committed; security behavior fails closed.
No mock production paths, silent failures or unused abstractions.

acceptance_criteria: A webhook with a bad signature gets 400 and an audit entry; a valid one is processed once even if sent twice.
Checkout with the gate off returns the 'not available yet' message and creates no session.
A second checkout for an account with a live subscription is refused.
With no AWS credentials, an organization key using AWS cannot be resolved rather than falling back.
A non-Enterprise workspace is refused when provisioning a key.
With no DSN in production no error client starts and boot succeeds.
A flag kill switch removes the capability in /api/me.
inferred: Local and BYOK users need no payment because they are free [inferred] (checkout/route.ts:178-181).
Sign-in is required for Cloud only; whether it is required for Local on each app is a separate question: unknown.
proposed: [proposed] Add a monitoring path for mobile and extension if required.
[proposed] Record the signing identity check in a runbook.

features.summary: A developer project groups API keys so they share one monthly usage count and an optional monthly credit limit. It is managed from the Projects card in the web Developer console. At the limit the gateway refuses the project's keys until the UTC month ends. Archiving a project revokes its keys. No organization can be created here.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a signed-in person create named projects, edit a project's name and monthly credit limit, archive a project, and see each project's key count and this month's credit use. A key can be placed in a project when it is created (F105-02). Keys with no project belong to a built-in 'Default project' row [ProjectsPanel.tsx:517-523]. For a key in a capped project, the chat gateway and the audio transcription gateway refuse the request with HTTP 429 and code project_spend_limit_reached once the month's spend reaches the limit (apps/web/lib/developer-api/project-spend.ts:73-84; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:290-293).
purpose.why_it_exists: Before projects, every API key belonged to the whole account, so a developer could not keep staging and production apart, see what each integration spent, or cap one integration (apps/web/db/neon/0321_developer_projects.sql:4-9, header comment). The brief asks for organizations and projects that scope keys, usage and limits (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/105-developer-platform-and-console.md, S105.01).
purpose.who_uses_it: A developer or small team lead on the web app who calls the managed gateway with API keys, and who wants a spending cap per integration.
problems_solved: One shared key and one shared bill for every integration.
No way to stop a runaway integration from spending all of the account's credits.
No per-project view of usage and key counts.
use_cases: Create a project named for a staging app with a small monthly limit so a test loop cannot spend real credit.
Archive a project when an integration is retired, which revokes all of its keys in one step.
Raise a project's limit mid-month after receiving the project.spend_limit_reached webhook (project-spend.ts:64-71).

journey: Open Developer console and find the Projects card.
Choose 'New project', type a name (1 to 100 characters), optionally type a whole number of credits above 0, choose 'Create project'.
The project appears with '0 keys' and its usage line, for example '<n> of <limit> this month'.
Create keys in it from the API Keys card by choosing the project (F105-02).
To change the name or limit choose 'Edit' then 'Save'. An empty limit removes the limit (parseLimit, ProjectsPanel.tsx:69-74).
To stop a project choose 'Archive' and confirm; its keys are revoked and it moves to the archived list.
feedback_and_outputs: Usage line per row: '<spent> of <limit> this month' or '<spent> this month, no monthly limit' (ProjectsPanel.tsx:96-98).
Key line: '<n> key(s)' (ProjectsPanel.tsx:79-85).
Toast '<name> is archived.' (ProjectsPanel.tsx:415).

Inline error text under the dialog or card; message 'We could not confirm whether the project was updated. Check the project state before repeating this action.' when a write may or may not have reached the server (ProjectsPanel.tsx:64-65).
API refusal for a capped key: HTTP 429, error code project_spend_limit_reached, with project_id and reset_at (project-spend.ts:73-83).
settings: Monthly credit limit per project (1 to 1,000,000,000, DEVELOPER_PROJECT_CREDIT_LIMIT_MAX, developer-project-service.ts:9).
Maximum 100 live projects per account (developer-project-service.ts:7).
Rate limits: developer-console 60 per minute, developer-console-write 20 per minute (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:701-710).

working: Create, list, update and archive routes exist with CSRF and rate-limit checks and per-user scoped database (apps/web/app/api/developers/projects/route.ts:30-67; apps/web/app/api/developers/projects/[projectId]/route.ts:44-96).
Create is serialized by an advisory lock and refuses at 100 live projects (developer-project-service.ts:100-131).

Names are unique per account among live projects, ignoring case, and a duplicate returns a conflict 'You already have a project named <name>.' (apps/web/db/neon/0321_developer_projects.sql:42-44; developer-project-service.ts:43-45).

Archive is one transaction: it sets archived_at and revokes every unrevoked key in the project (developer-project-service.ts:170-197). The route then writes one api_key_revoked audit event and one api_key.revoked webhook per key (projects/[projectId]/route.ts:73-90).
A key whose project is archived fails verification even if not revoked (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:244-262, project exists-clause in verifyKey).

Spend cap: the gateway looks up the key's project, sums this UTC month's spend (settled actual cost plus estimated cost of unsettled requests) and refuses at or above the limit (project-spend.ts:35-52; developer-usage-service.ts developerProjectSpendMicrousd). It queues one project.spend_limit_reached webhook per month (project-spend.ts:54-71).
Usage per key and per project is read from managed_usage_requests joined to api_keys (developer-usage-service.ts readDeveloperUsage; GET /api/developers/usage).
The card shows 'Loading usage', 'Usage unavailable', 'Loading key count', 'Key count unavailable' and never a zero for an unreadable value (ProjectsPanel.tsx:76-99, 207-216).
incomplete: No organization can be created from this feature although the brief says 'organization and projects'; the code has projects only (doc: area brief S105.01; table has user_id and no organization column, 0321 migration line 25-32).
Project update (PATCH) writes no audit event; create does (projects/route.ts:52-62; projects/[projectId]/route.ts:44-60). Archive audits per key, not the project itself [inferred from route code].
The cap is checked before the request runs, so one request can pass the limit by its own cost [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: The cap is enforced only on API-key requests to chat completions and audio transcriptions (auth-gate.ts:290-293; apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:302). Other key-authenticated routes were not checked (unknown).
not_available: Mobile, CLI, VS Code extension and Chrome extension have no developer projects [no code found].
Restoring an archived project: not available; the dialog says it cannot be restored (ProjectsPanel.tsx:397-403).

established.statement: A developer can create projects that scope API keys, usage and limits.
Brief status is web done, desktop done.
A project at its monthly limit refuses its keys with HTTP 429 and code project_spend_limit_reached until the month resets.
Archiving asks first and states that keys are revoked and the project cannot be restored.
Unreadable usage or key counts are labelled unavailable, never shown as zero.
The Desktop shows the hosted web app, so a web change reaches the Desktop window.

acceptance_criteria: Creating a project with a 1 to 100 character name and a blank limit succeeds and the row shows 'no monthly limit'.
A name of 101 characters, an empty name, a decimal limit, zero, or a negative limit is refused (Create schema, projects/route.ts:19-28).
A second live project with the same name in a different letter case is refused with the duplicate-name message.
Archive shows the confirm dialog first; after confirming, every key of the project stops working and the project appears under 'Archived'.
A key in a project whose month spend is at or above the limit gets HTTP 429 with code project_spend_limit_reached on chat completions; after the UTC month turns it works again.
While usage or key counts are loading or failed, the card shows the 'Loading ...' or '... unavailable' text and the Archive button is disabled until key counts are ready (ProjectsPanel.tsx:556).
The 101st live project is refused with 'You can have 100 projects at once. Archive one to make another.'
inferred: Projects are per account, not per workspace: the table has no organization column and every query filters by user_id (developer-project-service.ts:51-57). The workspace id is only sent as a request header (use-developer-projects.ts:62-64) [inferred].
Desktop and web behave the same because the Desktop loads the hosted page [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 5].
proposed: [proposed] Add an audit event for project update and for the archive itself.
[proposed] Show the per-project reset date next to the usage line.
[proposed] Either build organizations or change the brief wording to projects only.

steps.what_happens: The person opens the Projects card; the browser reads projects, API keys and usage in three requests.
The person saves the dialog; the browser fetches a CSRF token and sends POST or PATCH with the workspace header.
The server checks CSRF and rate limit, validates the body, and writes developer_projects under the person's scoped database; creation takes a per-user lock and counts live projects.
Archive: one transaction marks the project archived and revokes its keys; the route writes audit events and queues api_key.revoked webhooks.
Later, an API-key request reaches the chat gateway; the gate sums the project's month spend and either returns 429 or continues to subscription checks.

features.summary: A person creates scoped API keys for the managed gateway, each with a name, one or more scopes, an optional expiry and an optional project. The full secret is shown once. Keys are listed masked with last use and expiry, and can be deleted. Creation needs a plan with Cloud API access and a fresh sign-in check.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates, lists and revokes personal API keys that authenticate calls to the OpenAI-compatible gateway at /api/llm/v1 (chat completions, audio transcriptions, model list, usage). Keys carry scopes models:read, inference:write, usage:read (apps/web/lib/api-key-scopes.ts:1). Only an argon2id hash of the secret is stored (apps/web/lib/services/api-key-service.ts:12-17, 116-123 region).
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers need credentials for scripts, servers and tools that cannot use a browser session, with limited permissions and a way to stop them (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/105-developer-platform-and-console.md S105.02; decision doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md section 'Managed API Key Scopes').
purpose.who_uses_it: A developer on a plan that includes Cloud API access (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise in code: packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:341, 358), on the web app or the CLI.
problems_solved: Calling the gateway from code without sharing a login.
Limiting what a leaked key can do and for how long.
Stopping one integration without touching others.
use_cases: Create a key with only 'Read model catalog' to let a tool list models.
Create a 30 day key with 'Run inference' for a build job.
List keys from the terminal with 'agi keys' and revoke one that leaked.

where_to_find_it: Web: card 'API Keys' on /developers (first card, DeveloperConsolePage.tsx:68) and in the Account settings section (AccountSection.tsx mounts ApiKeysManager).
Desktop: brief marks done; same hosted screens expected [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 5]; not opened.

CLI: 'agi keys' (alias list), 'agi keys list [--json]', 'agi keys revoke <id or name> [-y]', 'agi keys create' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1061-1065, 2221-2235, 7687-7740). The brief did not list it; the code has it.
Mobile, VS Code extension, Chrome extension: none found.
prerequisites: Signed in.

A plan with Cloud API access; otherwise the card shows 'No API keys yet' with the upgrade message and the New Key button is replaced by an upgrade action (ApiKeys.tsx:195-241; server refuses with a 403 and recovery link, api-keys/route.ts:85-92).
A fresh sign-in check (step-up) at creation (api-keys/route.ts:111-117).
screens_and_controls: Button 'New Key' (ApiKeys.tsx:195-207 region) opens the dialog 'Generate New API Key'.

Fields: 'Key Name' (max 100), 'Scopes' checkboxes 'Read model catalog', 'Run inference', 'Read usage' (api-key-scopes.ts:10-24), 'Project' (choose a live project or default), 'Expires' with choices Never, 30 days, 90 days, 1 year (settings-validation.ts:43-52).
After creation the dialog becomes 'API Key Generated' with the warning 'Save this key now. You will not be able to see it again!' and button 'Copy to Clipboard' (ApiKeys.tsx:300-318 region).

Each list row: name, prefix followed by '...', project name or 'Default project', optional usage line, scope labels, 'Created: <date> - Last used: <date> - Expires/Expired: <date>' or 'Never expires' (ApiKeys.tsx:252-276).
Trash button labelled 'Delete <name>' and confirm 'Delete Key' (ApiKeys.tsx:284, 734).
journey: Open API Keys and choose 'New Key'.
Enter a name, tick at least one scope, pick an expiry and optionally a project.
Confirm the fresh sign-in check when asked (step-up dialog).
Copy the full key from the one-time screen and close it; the key is never shown again.
Use it as 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' against the gateway.
To stop it, choose the trash button on its row and confirm 'Delete Key'; the server marks it revoked.
feedback_and_outputs: Toast 'API key copied to clipboard' or 'Could not copy the API key' (ApiKeys.tsx:762-764).
Toast 'API key deleted' (ApiKeys.tsx:745).
Inline form error with role alert when creation fails (ApiKeys.tsx:441).
Gateway responses for keys: 401 invalid_api_key, 403 insufficient_scope, 429 project_spend_limit_reached (auth-gate.ts:240-263, project-spend.ts:78).
Webhook events api_key.created and api_key.revoked (api-keys/route.ts:147; [keyId]/route.ts:59).
settings: API_KEY_MAX_LIFETIME_DAYS environment setting (default 365) bounds a chosen expiry (api-key-service.ts:21-37).
Maximum 20 active keys per account (api-keys/route.ts:26, 105).
Rate limits api-keys-list, api-keys-create, api-keys-delete (delete 10 per minute, fail closed; rate-limit.ts:696-700).

working: Create: validates name 1-100, at least one unique scope from the three, optional ISO expiry, optional project id (api-keys/route.ts:28-37); refuses without managed_api (85-92); refuses a missing or archived project (96-98); refuses the 21st active key (100-109); requires step-up (111-117); inserts the key in a transaction after admitting the project (api-key-service.ts:126-143).
Secret format sk_live_<16 hex>_<48 hex>, argon2id hashed; the raw key is returned once in full_key (api-key-service.ts:50-57 region; api-keys/route.ts:156-162).
List returns active keys only, masked, up to 100 (api-keys/route.ts:52-69).

Revoke: DELETE /api/settings/api-keys/[keyId] checks ownership, returns 'API key was already revoked' for a revoked key, otherwise sets revoked_at, audits and queues api_key.revoked ([keyId]/route.ts:16-67).
Verification refuses revoked, expired and archived-project keys (api-key-service.ts:244-262) and updates last_used_at in the background.

Expiry must be in the future and within the configured maximum (api-key-service.ts:39-47); 'Never' stores no expiry and such a key keeps verifying (test: app/api/settings/api-keys/__tests__/key-expiry.test.ts 'is the default and still verifies...').

CLI lists and revokes through the same routes (apps/cli/src/cloud/api_keys.rs:5, 27-35, 73); create opens the account settings page in the browser because creation needs the fresh sign-in check (lib.rs:7727-7739).
A key rotate service exists, used by a support action (apps/web/lib/support/actions/executors/regenerate-api-key.ts:38-40).
incomplete: Revoking has no step-up check; only creation does (api-keys/[keyId]/route.ts has no requireStepUp; api-keys/route.ts:111). The earlier draft said both did; the code says creation only.
The button and dialog say 'Delete', the route and brief say revoke; wording differs (ApiKeys.tsx:284, 734).
No UI to edit a key's name, scopes or project after creation (not found in ApiKeys.tsx).
disconnected_or_disabled: rotateApiKey is reachable only from a support action, not from the Account settings card or the CLI (searched web app, lib and features; CLI has no rotate subcommand in the KeysSubcommand enum, lib.rs:2221-2235).
not_available: Mobile, VS Code extension and Chrome extension: no key management found.
CLI cannot create a key inline; it hands off to the browser (lib.rs:7727-7739).

established.statement: A developer can create scoped API keys with expiry, see them masked with last-used time, and revoke them.
New keys require one or more of models:read, inference:write, usage:read; the picker submits and shows those grants.
established.source: doc: docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md section 'Managed API Key Scopes' (2026-07-30)

established.statement: At most 20 active keys per user; the 21st is refused with a validation error.
Expired keys stop working.
An expiry must be in the future and not beyond the configured maximum lifetime.
Revoking an already revoked key returns 'API key was already revoked'.
Creating a key needs a plan with the managed_api capability.

acceptance_criteria: Creating with no scope is refused ('Select at least one scope'); duplicate scopes are refused.
The full key appears once; reopening the list shows only the prefix.
A key with 'Expires: 30 days' stops verifying after that time; a past expiry is refused at creation.
The 21st active key is refused with the 20-key message.
On a plan without Cloud API access creation returns 403 and the card shows the upgrade message.
Deleting a key makes the next gateway call with it return 401; deleting it again returns 'API key was already revoked'.
A key without 'models:read' calling GET /api/llm/v1/models gets 403 insufficient_scope.
'agi keys revoke <name>' asks for confirmation unless -y is given.
inferred: Because only creation asks for step-up, a stolen session could revoke keys without a fresh check [inferred].
Expiry 'Never' can exceed the configured maximum lifetime because the bound is applied only when an expiry is given (api-key-service.ts insertApiKey) [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Align the word Delete with Revoke across the card, dialog and CLI.
[proposed] Offer rotate in the card and the CLI.
[proposed] Decide whether 'Never' should be allowed given a maximum lifetime setting.

steps.what_happens: Person fills the dialog; the browser validates with the form schema and starts the step-up prompt if needed.
Browser sends POST /api/settings/api-keys with a CSRF token.
Server checks plan capability, project, active-key count and step-up, then hashes a new secret and inserts the row.
Server returns api_key (masked) and full_key once, writes an audit event and queues a webhook.
A later gateway call presents the key; the server looks up by prefix, checks revoked, expiry and project, verifies the hash, then checks scope and spend cap.
CLI 'agi keys' calls the same list and delete routes with the saved sign-in.

data.what: Key row: name, prefix, argon2id hash, scopes, project, expiry, last_used_at, revoked_at
data.retained_or_deleted: Revoked rows stay with revoked_at set; hidden from the list (api-keys/route.ts:58-66).

data.where_stored: Not stored; shown once in the browser and held in page state until dismissed (ApiKeys.tsx:762 uses lane.secret).

features.summary: In a shared workspace, an admin can see non-human service identities that own workspace API keys, and disable or re-enable them. Disabling stops all of its keys at once. A principal is created by issuing a workspace key without naming one. Workspace keys carry workspace permissions, not model-gateway scopes.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows a 'Service principals' card on the workspace Identity page and a 'Workspace API keys' card on the workspace audit page. A workspace admin can issue and revoke workspace API keys, each owned by a service principal that is bounded by a ceiling of workspace permissions, and can disable or enable a principal (apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/admin-api-keys/route.ts:106-208; apps/web/app/api/settings/organization/service-principals/route.ts:51-86).
purpose.why_it_exists: Automations such as audit export or member sync need credentials that outlive any one person and can be switched off together (apps/web/lib/server/service-principal.ts:27-31, 100-110 comments; doc: area brief S105.03).
purpose.who_uses_it: A workspace admin or owner on a Team or Enterprise workspace.
problems_solved: Keys tied to a departed employee stop working.
One switch stops an automation whose keys live in many systems.
Keys cannot exceed the permissions of the principal or the creator.
use_cases: Issue a key that only reads the audit trail for a compliance export job.
Disable a principal during an incident and enable it after.
Narrow a principal's ceiling so keys already issued lose reach.

established.statement: A workspace admin can create non-human service identities with scoped keys, list them and disable or revoke them.
Creating a workspace key for a disabled principal is refused.
A key can only carry scopes within the principal's ceiling; others are refused and named.
Disabling asks first and names the consequence; enabling does not ask.
A service principal cannot perform actions that act on behalf of a person.

acceptance_criteria: With a role lacking identity.manage, creating a key returns 403 'Your workspace role does not allow creating workspace API keys.' and the card shows no Disable control.
Creating a key without servicePrincipalId makes a new principal whose ceiling equals the requested scopes.
Disabling a principal makes its keys fail on the next call; enabling restores them.
Naming a disabled principal at key creation is refused with the re-enable message.
Requesting a scope above the principal's ceiling is refused and the response names the scope.
Create and revoke each write an audit event; create carries subjectRef service_principal:<id>.
Retrying creation with the same Idempotency-Key replays the first response and does not make a second key.
inferred: The workspace key list is limited to Team or Enterprise because requireTeamAdminAccess demands that subscription [inferred from team-admin-access.ts:70-88].
Desktop parity relies on the hosted web pages [inferred from doc: AGENTS.md section 5].
proposed: [proposed] Add an explicit 'New service principal' control and route.
[proposed] Add the principal reference to the revoke audit event.
[proposed] Show each principal's keys on its row.

steps.what_happens: The Identity page loads principals with the person's bearer token.
Server resolves the caller as member or key, applies the route access table and returns principals and reachable routes.
Disable: browser sends PATCH with principalId and disabled flag; server updates disabled_at and writes an audit event.
Create key: server checks team admin access, permission, scope grant, step-up, then in one transaction mints or reads the principal and inserts the key.
Automation presents the key; the verifier updates last_used_at, refuses revoked, expired or disabled-principal keys and intersects scopes with the ceiling.

features.summary: The gateway endpoint GET /api/llm/v1/models returns the models the caller's plan can run, with context size, capabilities and a deprecation_date that is null until a retirement is scheduled. Operators can hide models with a kill switch. The API docs page lists scheduled retirements; the CLI shows a live managed list without dates.

purpose.what_it_does: Returns an OpenAI-style list of models for the caller (id, owner, tier, context window, max output, capabilities, deprecation_date, accepted request parameters) plus an x_agi_workforce block with user_tier, total_available, allowed_auto_modes, routing_profiles and temporarily_unavailable (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/models/route.ts:41-61, 203-217). The console links to the Models page and to the Deprecations section of the API docs (DeveloperConsolePage.tsx:32-41).
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers must know which models their key can call and when a pinned model will leave, so they can move before it stops working (doc: area brief S105.04 and S105.27; apps/web/app/api-docs/page.tsx:342-368).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers calling the gateway, the web console playground and prompts (use-gateway-models.ts), and the CLI's managed model picker.
problems_solved: Guessing which model ids work on a plan.
Surprise outages when a model is retired.
Routing clients that need to know which models are temporarily down.
use_cases: curl the list with a key that has models:read before choosing a model id.
Watch deprecation_date to schedule a migration.
Run 'agi --list-models' to see the live managed models for the signed-in account.

established.statement: Developers can browse the models their key can call, with capabilities and context size.
Developers are told ahead of time when a model or API is deprecated.
Every listed model carries deprecation_date, null until a retirement is scheduled.
A model whose switch is closed, or whose every provider route is closed, is not listed.
A failed credential is refused, not downgraded to the anonymous list.
CLI shows 'managed model discovery is temporarily unavailable' on HTTP 503.

acceptance_criteria: GET with no Authorization returns the public free catalog (object list).
GET with an invalid Bearer returns 401 invalid_api_key; with a key lacking models:read returns 403 insufficient_scope.
GET with a valid key returns only models of the key owner's plan; each has context_window above 0 and a deprecation_date string or null.
Flipping a model's kill switch removes it from the next response without a deploy.
A model with every route degraded appears in x_agi_workforce.temporarily_unavailable and not in data.
On a developer-surface credential whose plan excludes the surface, data is empty.
API docs page lists every model with a scheduled retirement date, soonest first.
agi --list-models prints a managed section for a pro-or-above account and an explanatory line for lower tiers.
inferred: Retirement dates are the only deprecation signal; no API deprecation (non-model) is listed anywhere I read [inferred].
The models page and the endpoint draw on the same catalogue code (buildCatalogueEntries) [inferred from imports; /models page not opened].

[proposed] Send a notice in the console when a model the account used recently is within a set number of days of retirement.

steps.what_happens: Client sends GET with or without Authorization; server applies the default rate limit.
Server authenticates with scope models:read; on failure maps to a typed refusal.
Server resolves the account's entitled plan tier.
Server builds catalogue entries for the tier, drops those outside the surface profile or switched off, separates temporarily unavailable ones.
Server returns JSON with CORS headers.
CLI fetches the same endpoint with its saved JWT, bounds and validates the response, caches it per account and shows it.

Rate limit headers, when present, show remaining and limit.

features.summary: The web console card 'Prompts and evaluations' stores prompts as versioned templates with {{variable}} slots, lets a developer compare versions and save an old one as the newest, builds test cases by hand or CSV, runs a version over all cases through the gateway, and shows pass, fail, diffs and 1 to 5 grades. Separate custom commands cover reusable prompts in web settings and the CLI.

purpose.what_it_does: Part A, console prompts: a signed-in developer creates a named prompt, saves versions (system prompt, template, model, max_tokens, temperature, note), adds up to 500 test cases, runs a chosen version across them with a check, and reads per-case output, latency, tokens and a diff against the expected text. Part B, custom commands: the web 'Custom commands' settings list and the CLI markdown commands are the reusable prompt templates with arguments that the brief item S105.12 points at (apps/web/features/settings/components/CustomCommandsSettings.tsx; apps/cli/src/custom_commands.rs).
purpose.why_it_exists: The console could send one request and nothing more; developers had nowhere to keep a prompt, compare two versions or check a change against known cases (apps/web/db/neon/0371_developer_prompts_and_evals.sql:4-11 header).

Retyping the same prompt with different inputs.

Roll back by loading an old version and saving it as the next version.

established.statement: Developers can save reusable prompt templates with arguments and invoke them (S105.12).
Prompt templates keep versions that can be compared and rolled back (S105.13).
Developers can build evaluation datasets, run them against a model and prompt, and see per-case results with scores and diffs (S105.14 to S105.16).
Versions are append-only; each save is the next number and an old one can be saved again as the newest.
A run costs what its gateway calls cost, and everything belongs to one account.
Deleting a prompt deletes its versions, cases, runs and grades and cannot be recovered.
Deleting a case asks first; recorded results keep their output.

acceptance_criteria: A new prompt starts at version 1 with template {{input}} and model auto.
Save as version is disabled until the draft differs from the latest version and the template is not empty.
Compare with latest shows added and removed lines for system prompt, template, and model and parameters.
CSV with a header of variable names and an 'expected' column creates one case per row; a header name that is not a valid variable name is refused; over 500 cases is refused.
A run needs at least one case ('Add at least one test case first.') and shows 'Running x of y' while in progress.
A case whose gateway call fails is recorded as Error, not dropped.
Cases changed after a run started do not change that run's expected output or verdict.
Grades 1 to 5 persist after reloading the run.
inferred: Argument handling for CLI commands is verified in code and unit tests (custom_commands.rs tests at 408-444), unlike the draft's 'not verified'.
The console prompts and custom commands are two unrelated stores [inferred: different tables, files and syntax].

steps.what_happens: Person saves a version; browser posts it to the versions route.
Server validates the model, takes the next number and stores the version; a concurrent save returns a conflict message.
Person starts a run; server checks the version and cases, stores the run and freezes the cases in one transaction.
Browser renders each template with the case variables and sends it to the chat gateway, three at a time.
Gateway routes each call to a model and provider chosen for the version's model or 'auto'.
Browser records each output or error; server grades against the frozen expected output and stores the verdict.
Person grades or opens earlier runs; server returns stored results.

features.summary: On the web Developer console, the Request logs card lists recent requests made with a person's API keys, newest first, with a step timeline, tokens and credits. Separately, Settings, Usage shows settled credits by day, week or month and by model. The CLI prints a usage summary. Desktop shows the hosted web app.

purpose.what_it_does: Request logs show each call made with an AGI API key: model, status, key name, time, step timeline (Received, Sent to the model, Model answered, Delivered to your client, Billed), token counts, server-side tool counts and credits (apps/web/features/developers/components/RequestLogsPanel.tsx:22-38, :57-107). The usage history shows settled credits over time and by product area, model and project, with a CSV download (apps/web/features/settings/sections/UsageSection.tsx:1070-1200).
purpose.why_it_exists: A developer who calls the managed gateway needs to see what each call did and cost, and whether a call is still settling. The card says prompts and answers are not stored (RequestLogsPanel.tsx:119-123). [inferred] The two views let a developer tie a bill to requests.
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in developer who holds API keys (web Developer console at /developers), any paid-plan account owner reading usage in Settings, and a CLI user running agi usage.
problems_solved: Finding which API request failed, was declined or was never confirmed (status labels, RequestLogsPanel.tsx:30-38).
Seeing where credits went by model, product area and project (UsageSection.tsx:1130-1156).
Spotting requests still settling that are not yet counted (UsageSection.tsx:1157-1170).
use_cases: A developer opens Developer console, Request logs, opens a row and reads that the model answered 400 ms after it was sent.
A developer opens Settings, Usage, picks Weeks, and reads credits by model.
A CLI user runs agi usage and reads the last days of usage by model (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:776-845).
A developer sees a project line such as '3 of 10 this month' in the Projects card (apps/web/features/developers/components/ProjectsPanel.tsx:90-98).

where_to_find_it: Web: /developers, card titled 'Request logs' (apps/web/features/developers/components/DeveloperConsolePage.tsx:72; apps/web/app/developers/page.tsx:13-22).
Web: Settings, Usage, card 'Where your usage went' (UsageSection.tsx:1101). The console Reference card links to it as 'Usage' (DeveloperConsolePage.tsx:42-46).

Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so the same pages (doc: AGENTS.md section 5). No desktop source file refers to these routes (grep of apps/desktop/src and apps/desktop/electron found nothing).
CLI: command agi usage (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:7680-7686) and slash command /usage (apps/cli/src/repl/slash_commands.rs:316).
Mobile (not in the brief): Cloud usage settings call the same history endpoint (apps/mobile/services/usage.ts:93-98; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-usage/index.tsx:641).
prerequisites: Sign in. The logs and usage routes read the signed-in user's database scope (apps/web/app/api/developers/logs/route.ts:33).
Request logs only list requests made with an API key, so at least one key request must exist (apps/web/lib/services/developer-request-log-service.ts:122-123).
The usage history card shows only for accounts that are not Free and not contract priced (UsageSection.tsx:1224-1225, :1451).
The CLI needs a signed-in managed account and a Cloud session; Local and own-key sessions are refused before any request (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:914-932).
screens_and_controls: Request logs card: description line, list of rows, each row a button with aria-expanded showing model, status, time and key name, total ms; 'Show older' button; 'Try again' button on errors (RequestLogsPanel.tsx:109-206).

Opened row: 'Timeline' list with +ms per step, and facts: Requested model, Served by, Error, Input tokens, Output tokens, Reasoning tokens, Cached input tokens, Web searches, Pages fetched, Code runs, Credits (RequestLogsPanel.tsx:57-107).

established.statement: Developers can browse traces/logs of their API requests with timing and steps.
Developers can see usage and cost over time, broken down by model.
A request with no answer shows 'Outcome unknown' rather than a guess.
Prompts and answers are not stored in the logs.
Usage counts only settled requests and says how many are still settling.

acceptance_criteria: After a call with an API key, the Request logs card lists it with the requested model, status and time.
Opening a row shows the steps that have a timestamp, in order, with +ms from Received.
A request that is declined shows 'Declined'; one without a final answer shows 'Outcome unknown'.
With more than 50 requests, 'Show older' loads the next page without repeating rows.
A failed load shows an alert and 'Try again'; a successful retry replaces it.
Settings, Usage shows credits By model for the chosen period and excludes requests still settling.
A Free account does not see the usage history card.
agi usage in a Local or own-key session says it needs a managed account and sends no request.
inferred: [inferred] Logs are per user, not per workspace: the SQL filters on user_id only (developer-request-log-service.ts:122) even though the request sends a workspace header (use-developer-request-logs.ts:40-43).
[inferred] Playground requests are sent with the session credential, so they have no api_key_id and do not appear in the logs (RequestPlayground.tsx:181-193; developer-request-log-service.ts:123).
proposed: [proposed] Add filters by key, model, status and time range, and a CSV export for logs, as the usage card already has.
[proposed] Add a per-model cost view inside the console so a developer need not leave for Settings.
[proposed] Show the request id so a log row can be matched to /api/usage/turns/{requestId}.

steps.what_happens: The browser calls GET /api/developers/logs with the workspace header; the hook checks the signed-in owner and workspace are admitted first.
The route applies the developer-console rate limit, validates the optional before cursor, and opens a user-scoped database connection.
The service reads up to 51 rows of managed_usage_requests that have an api_key_id for the user, joined to the key name, and maps timestamps to steps.
The page is validated against the contract schema and returned with no-store caching; the card renders it.
Usage history: the Settings card calls GET /api/usage/history; the server sums settled rows by period, workload, model and project.
CLI: agi usage checks the privacy mode, reads the stored sign-in token, and calls /api/usage and /api/usage/history with a 5 second timeout.
