features.summary: The Developer console lists rate limits per endpoint, and responses carry X-RateLimit headers. A workspace owner sets a monthly credit cap that the gateway checks before each turn. A project cap refuses that project's API keys. The CLI has a per-session spend stop. Desktop shows the hosted web app.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows limits per gateway endpoint (apps/web/features/developers/components/RateLimitsPanel.tsx:27-58), returns X-RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset headers (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:1091-1093), lets a workspace admin set a monthly cap with Off, Notify or Block (apps/web/features/workspace-console/components/WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:262-271), lets a project carry a monthly credit limit (apps/web/lib/developer-api/project-spend.ts:30-45), and lets a CLI run stop at a USD budget (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:489-492).
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers need to pace clients before being refused, and owners need to bound spend that automated callers can run up. The migration says an owner asked to approve an AI budget wants a stop, not only a report (apps/web/db/neon/0142_organization_spend_limits.sql:3-6).
purpose.who_uses_it: API developers (limits and project cap), workspace owners and admins on Team or Enterprise (workspace cap), CLI users running unattended jobs (budget flag).
problems_solved: Clients hitting 429 without warning (headers and the limits card).
Runaway spend by a key or a workspace (project cap, workspace Block mode).
Unattended CLI loops that cost more than intended (--max-budget-usd).
use_cases: A developer reads that POST /chat/completions allows 30 requests per minute and reads the remaining count in the 'Try a request' result.
An admin sets a cap of N credits with Block; members' Cloud turns are refused at the cap.
A developer sets a monthly limit on a project; its keys then answer 429 project_spend_limit_reached.
A CI user runs the CLI with --max-budget-usd so the agent stops at the cap.

working: Rate limits card is built from configuration at the server and passed to the page (apps/web/app/developers/page.tsx:15-21; apps/web/lib/developer-api/rate-limit-summary.ts:6-25).

Headers are attached to six gateway routes through withAdmittedRateLimitHeaders (chat completions route.ts:1527; models route.ts:327; embeddings route.ts:283; route/preview route.ts:201; credits/balance route.ts:144; audio/transcriptions route.ts:853).
Workspace cap: GET, PUT, DELETE route with CSRF, rate limit, permission check and audit event (spend-limit/route.ts:56-175).
Gateway checks the workspace cap before processRequest (chat/completions/route.ts:446-455).
Project cap is checked for API-key requests in the chat gate and the transcription route (chat/completions/lib/auth-gate.ts:290-293; audio/transcriptions/route.ts:302).
A crossing queues the webhook project.spend_limit_reached once per month (project-spend.ts:51-71).

incomplete: The card shows static limits only; remaining calls appear only in response headers and in the playground line (RateLimitsPanel.tsx:39-53; RequestPlayground.tsx:430-440).
The workspace cap is eventual, not exact: decisions are cached for 60 seconds (spend-limit-service.ts:58, :168-169), and the card says so (WorkspaceSpendLimit.tsx:79).

The card's limits are computed without a plan tier, so they equal the base value times the scale (rate-limit-summary.ts:21; rate-limit.ts:961-966); the gateway's own user check also passes no tier (auth-gate.ts:273-275). Other routes may scale by plan; not checked.
disconnected_or_disabled: Notify and Off modes never refuse a turn (spend-limit-service.ts:150-155).
The CLI budget event is written only when JSON events or JSON-line output is on (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:9244-9251, :9277).

Mobile, VS Code, Chrome: n/a per brief; no code found for spend-limit in apps/mobile, apps/extension, apps/extension-vscode.

established.statement: Developers can see their rate limits and how close they are to them.
An owner can set a spend cap that the API enforces.
Block is the only mode that refuses; Notify and Off never do; a newly created limit defaults to Notify so saving a number never starts refusing work.
Enforcement is eventual and the console says so.
If the spend state cannot be read the request runs ungoverned.
The budget is resolved against the funding organization, never the workspace the request picked.
Only a holder of policy.manage may change the cap; any change is audited, Block at critical severity.

acceptance_criteria: The Rate limits card lists POST /chat/completions, GET /models, POST /embeddings, POST /audio/transcriptions and GET /credits/balance with limit and window.
A gateway response carries X-RateLimit-Limit, -Remaining and -Reset; a refused one also carries Retry-After.
A member without policy.manage sees the card read-only or not at all and PUT returns a refusal.
With enforcement Block and spend at or above the cap, a Cloud turn is refused with HTTP 402 before any credit is reserved.
With Notify, the same turn runs.
Raising the cap frees the workspace at once (cache is cleared on save).
A project with a monthly limit refuses its keys with 429 project_spend_limit_reached once spend reaches it; another project's keys still work.
The CLI stops with 'Budget cap reached' once --max-budget-usd is exceeded.
inferred: [inferred] The Rate limits card and the gateway agree for chat completions because both read the base bucket without a plan tier.
[inferred] --max-budget-usd uses the CLI's locally priced cost ledger, so it works in every privacy mode (apps/cli/src/usage_summary.rs:874-880 labels it 'priced locally').
proposed: [proposed] Show live remaining and reset on the Rate limits card, using the headers already returned.
[proposed] Make a failed cap lookup visible to the admin instead of silently running ungoverned.
[proposed] Offer the project cap and the workspace cap on one page.

steps.what_happens: The page server renders rate limits from configuration and passes them to the card.
Each gateway call is counted in the bucket for its route; the response carries the headers.
A key call is checked for the project cap, then the subscription lookup runs.
Before processRequest the gateway evaluates the workspace cap and returns 402 on Block and over cap.
An admin PUT stores the cap, clears the cached decision and writes an audit event.
CLI: after each model response the engine compares cumulative cost to the cap and stops further tool calls.

data.where_stored: Process memory and the local cost ledger

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The caps count credits regardless of model or provider. Credits come from provider cost converted by the managed ledger. Own-key (BYOK) and Local sessions never reach this gateway, so the workspace and project caps do not apply to them (doc: docs/product/definition.md not opened; code: AGENTS.md section 6 states the three modes are separate boundaries).

features.summary: In the web Developer console a developer registers an https endpoint, chooses events, copies a signing secret shown once, sends a test event, reads delivery history and resends a delivery. Our servers sign each POST, retry failures for about three days, and keep a log. Desktop shows the hosted web app.

purpose.what_it_does: Sends signed event messages from the platform to a developer's https address when an API key is created or revoked, a project spend limit is reached, or a task run completes, fails or needs approval (apps/web/lib/developer-api/webhook-events.ts:3-35), and keeps a delivery log with Resend (apps/web/features/developers/components/WebhooksPanel.tsx:367-410).
purpose.why_it_exists: Developers want to react to events without polling. The card says 'Add one to receive events without polling.' (WebhooksPanel.tsx:869-871).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in developer or automation owner who runs a public https service.
problems_solved: Missing a key revocation or a limit hit.
Knowing when a scheduled task finished or needs approval.
Proving a message is genuine (signature).
use_cases: Alert a chat channel when a project spend limit is reached.
Start a follow-up job when a task run completes.
Audit key creation in an external log.
Debug a receiver by sending a test event and resending a failed delivery.

established.statement: Developers can register a webhook endpoint and choose which events it receives.
Developers can see a history of webhook deliveries with status and can redeliver.
Up to 10 endpoints per user.
URLs must be https, carry no credentials and resolve to a public address.
The secret is stored encrypted; without secret storage webhooks are unavailable.
A delivery times out after 10 seconds and is attempted up to 20 times with exponential backoff capped at 6 hours.
Requests follow Standard Webhooks headers webhook-id, webhook-timestamp, webhook-signature.

Turning an endpoint off stops new events being queued to it.

steps.what_happens: The person adds an endpoint; the browser POSTs url, description and events with CSRF.
The server checks https, credentials, DNS to a public address, seals a new whsec_ secret, takes a per-user lock and inserts if under 10 endpoints.
The secret is returned once in the 201 body and shown in a dialog.
When an event happens, matching enabled endpoints get a delivery row and a queue job; the first attempt runs after the response.
The job decrypts the secret, signs the JSON body, and POSTs to the developer's URL with a 10 second timeout and no redirects.
Status, attempts, response status and error are written; a non-2xx result leaves it pending until the final attempt, then failed.
Resend copies the stored payload into a new delivery with redelivery_of set and attempts once after the response.

features.summary: On the web, a developer uploads a plugin zip into their own account to try it, then submits a version for review. A platform operator approves, rejects or suspends it in the admin Plugins page; approved plugins appear in the community directory. The CLI installs plugins from a local folder or git onto the device only.

purpose.what_it_does: Upload plugin stores a zip as an account-owned plugin source, installs it for that account only and registers its connectors (apps/web/app/api/plugins/uploads/route.ts:51-94). Submit to the directory scans the stored files and queues a submission with status pending (apps/web/lib/services/plugin-submission-service.ts:198-262). An operator decides it (apps/web/app/api/admin/plugin-submissions/[id]/route.ts:60-105). Only approved submissions are listed to others (plugin-submission-service.ts:420-432).
purpose.why_it_exists: Migration 0328 says only platform administrators could publish, so a developer could install their own plugin privately but never list it; the leaders take a submission, review it and publish it (apps/web/db/neon/0328_plugin_submissions.sql:3-8).
purpose.who_uses_it: A signed-in plugin developer, a platform operator who reviews, and users who install approved plugins.
problems_solved: Trying an unpublished plugin before release.
Getting a reviewed, scanned listing.
Shipping an update that moves existing installs to the new version (0328 migration comment).
use_cases: Upload a zip with a skills folder, test it in chat.
Submit the tested version for review.
Operator approves; users find it in the directory.
Developer withdraws it; everyone who installed it loses it.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (hosted web app): Directory panel, Plugins section, button 'Upload plugin' (packages/ui/ui/src/directory/DirectoryPanel.tsx:463-468; packages/ui/ui/src/directory/constants.ts:402). Desktop shows the hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).

Mobile (not in the brief): a Plugin sources screen lists submissions (apps/mobile/src/features/plugins/sourcesService.ts:98).
prerequisites: Signed in, plugins enabled for the workspace and plugin policy allowing the plugin key (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/install-gate.ts:21-50).
Uploading authors skills, which can be turned off by the deployment switch AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING=0 (apps/web/lib/services/user-skill-authoring.ts:6-17).

established.statement: A developer can load an unpublished custom plugin into their own account to try it.
A developer can submit a plugin or app for review and publish versions to users.
At most one version of a plugin is in review and one approved; approving a new version withdraws the one it replaces and moves its installs onto it.
A submission snapshot of its files is what review and installs see.
Only an approved plugin can be suspended; only a pending one can be approved or rejected.
A rejection carries a note.
Files the server omits are listed back to the uploader.

acceptance_criteria: A valid zip uploads and the plugin appears installed for that account only.
A zip the policy forbids stores nothing and returns a refusal.
The result lists omitted files when the server skipped any.
Submitting needs a verified email; without one the request is refused.
Submitting a plugin the user did not upload or create returns 'not one you uploaded or created'.
A second submission of the same plugin withdraws the earlier pending one.
Only an operator can approve; a non-operator gets 404.
After approval the plugin is listed to other signed-in users; after withdrawal it is not.
inferred: [inferred] 'Publish versions' is met by submitting each new version; there is no separate publish action (service lines 198-262).
[inferred] The moderation page needs platform operator status, not workspace admin, since the route calls requirePlatformAdmin.
proposed: [proposed] Show the scan findings to the developer before they submit.
[proposed] Add a CLI command that uploads a folder to the account.
[proposed] Link approved submissions to the registry version section.

steps.what_happens: The person picks a zip; the browser posts it with a CSRF token.
The server rate-limits, reads the archive, applies workspace feature and plugin policy, plans dependencies, stores the plugin as an owned upload and registers connectors.
The person presses Submit; the server finds the owned entry, scans its files and writes a pending submission with a file snapshot, withdrawing any earlier pending one.
An operator decides; the status, reviewer and time are written, an audit event is recorded and the submitter is notified.
Approved submissions are returned by the community listing and can be installed by others.
CLI: agi plugin install copies a local folder or clones a git URL into the device plugin folder, verifying integrity and signature.

established.statement: Developers can watch the raw streamed events of an API call in an inspector.
Developers can inspect the tool calls (arguments, results) made during an API request.
Developers can author and validate a structured-output JSON schema in the console.
Developers can upload files once through the API or console and reuse them by id across requests.
Developers can create and manage retrieval collections and query them from API calls.
A structured reply is validated before it is returned, so json_object and json_schema need stream false.

acceptance_criteria: Tool-call view: with a tools array and a prompt that triggers a call, the card lists the call name, id and arguments.
Stream inspector (not built): a streamed call would show each event in order with timestamps.
Schema editor (not built): an invalid schema would be flagged before sending.
File reuse (not built): a file uploaded once would be usable by id in two requests.
Retrieval (not built): a collection would be queryable from a request.
Gateway: a json_schema request whose reply does not match returns 502 json_schema_not_satisfied.

[inferred] A file store for the gateway needs a new API-key scope, since only three scopes exist (api-key-scopes.ts:1).
proposed: [proposed] Add a stream switch to the playground and a raw event pane.
[proposed] Show tool results by adding a follow-up turn in the playground.
[proposed] Add a schema box that validates against the limits in json-schema-mode.ts before sending.

Approve and Deny buttons in Slack when an answer needs approval (slack-messages.ts:263-270).
journey: 1. Owner adds the app from Settings, Slack app, Add to Slack.
2. Person opens the AGI app in Slack and sends a message.
3. If not linked, a private message with a 'Connect account' button appears; the link works once and expires in 15 minutes (slack-config.ts:28; slack-messages.ts:201-205).
4. Person opens the link, signs in to AGI, picks a workspace if offered and confirms (app/slack/link/page.tsx).
5. Slack posts 'Your Slack account is now connected to AGI...' (slack-messages.ts:213-217).
6. Person sends the message again. An eyes reaction is added to the message while it runs and removed after (slack-assistant.ts:113-128, 232, 256).
7. The answer arrives in the DM as formatted blocks.
feedback_and_outputs: Answer posted in the DM; DM answers carry a footer with the model display name and no requester name (slack-messages.ts:159-166 with requesterId null for DMs at slack-assistant.ts:152).

Notices: 'I could not finish that answer. Please try again.' (slack-assistant.ts:60); rate limit notice 'You are sending messages faster than AGI can answer them. Wait a minute, then try again.' (slack-assistant.ts:64-65); account unavailable (66-67); workspace left with an Open Settings button (68-70, 333).
Refusals with links: plan required (See plans), quota messages with Add credits, Upgrade or View usage (slack-assistant-turn.ts:167-172, 590-594).
Approval card with Approve, Deny and Review in AGI (slack-messages.ts:234-278); an in-app notification 'A Slack answer is waiting for your approval' (slack-assistant.ts:193-204).
settings: Settings, Slack app: disconnect an account, remove a workspace, manage channel policies (channel policies apply to channels only, not DMs: slack-assistant.ts:349-353).
Memory is applied to DM answers: direct messages load account memory (slack-assistant-turn.ts:521-522).

working: Event receiver with signature check and replay window, url_verification handshake, 413 for bodies over 256 KB (apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts:36-72).

DM event parsing: only direct messages (and app mentions) are read; bot messages, other subtypes, empty messages and bare verification codes are ignored (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts:67-70, 84-85).
Account link request, preview, one-time consume, and link creation (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-links.ts:102-225; apps/web/app/api/slack/link/route.ts).
Managed answer turn with entitlement check, access check, model route admission, content screening, memory, usage reservation and settle (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:408-715).
Per workspace and per user rate limits: 120 and 12 per minute (apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:479-488).
Answer budget: the turn is aborted after the chat tool-loop budget, 240 seconds (slack-assistant.ts:234; apps/web/lib/deadline-policy.ts:1-6).
Approval in Slack with Approve and Deny buttons, 24-hour expiry (slack-config.ts:30; apps/web/lib/slack/slack-interactions.ts:91-160).
Uninstall and token-revoked events delete the installation (slack-assistant.ts:426-447).
incomplete: Files attached in Slack are not opened: the model is told 'I attached files in Slack that you cannot open' with file names only (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-context.ts:241-243).
Tool use in DMs needs approval handled by the person; no approval means the run waits (slack-assistant-turn.ts:98-104).
disconnected_or_disabled: Everything is off until the Slack app is configured: events return 503 without the signing secret (route.ts:48-52), and Settings shows 'AGI in Slack is not set up on this service yet.' (SlackSection.tsx:545-549).

The brief says migration 0333 must be applied before deploy; the migration file exists in the chain (apps/web/db/neon/0333_slack_run_cancel_and_delete.sql). Whether it is applied in production is not recorded in the code.

steps.what_happens: Slack sends the event to /api/webhooks/slack; rate limit and 256 KB cap checked; signature and five minute window verified.
The event is read; direct messages become an assistant event that runs after the response is sent, so Slack gets its acknowledgment in time.
Installation is found, the Slack user is checked against the account link; an unlinked user gets a one-time link prompt.
Per workspace and per user rate limits are checked; over the limit gives one notice.
The bot adds the eyes reaction, reads earlier DM messages and names from Slack, and builds the conversation.
Entitlement, access, model route, content screening, secret check, memory and usage reservation are applied, then the model runs with the allowed tools; cost is settled.
The model call goes to the provider chosen by managed routing.
The answer is converted to Slack blocks and posted in the DM with the bot token; the reaction is removed; the run is marked completed.

features.summary: A person mentions the AGI app in a Slack channel it was invited to. It answers in the thread, or, when the person can use AGI Work and the channel allows it, runs the mention as a task with a link to the task. It posts as the app, not as the person. Web service only; setup needed.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads app mentions in channels, builds thread context, applies the channel's mode and tool allow-list, runs an answer or an AGI Work task on the mentioner's account, and replies in the thread as the Slack app (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant.ts:349-417; slack-channel-policies.ts:60-67; slack-tasks.ts:147-241).
purpose.why_it_exists: Briefs S106.14, S106.16 and S106.21 require a channel agent, mention-to-task and a bot identity distinct from the human. Replies read by a whole channel need stricter safety than a DM, so the code treats other people's messages as information, not instructions (slack-assistant-turn.ts:109-112).
purpose.who_uses_it: Teams in Slack. Installers set channel modes; any linked member can mention the app.
problems_solved: Getting work done where the team already talks.
Keeping a record: task mentions become AGI Work tasks the person can review.
Clear authorship: the app posts, with a footer naming who asked.
use_cases: @AGI summarise this thread.
@AGI research this topic as a task, then open the task link.
Installer sets a channel to 'Answers only' so no tasks start.
Installer turns a channel Off.

where_to_find_it: Slack channel: invite the app (/invite) and type @AGI plus the request (SlackSection.tsx workspace card text: 'Add the app, then /invite it to channels. Anyone there can link their account.').
Web: Settings, Slack app, card 'Slack workspaces you added', per-channel controls (apps/web/features/slack/components/SlackChannelPolicies.tsx).
Desktop: Cloud settings, Slack, button 'Open Slack app settings' opens the web page (apps/desktop/src/features/settings/cloud/CloudSlackSection.tsx:45). No Slack logic on desktop.
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: nothing found.
prerequisites: App installed in the workspace and the app invited to the channel.
The mentioner has linked their Slack account (same as F106-05) and is on a plan with Chat in Slack; task mode also needs a plan with AGI Work (slack-assistant-turn.ts:422-428).
For task mode: the Work capability is available and managed compute access allows it (slack-tasks.ts:45-76).
screens_and_controls: Per channel select, label 'What AGI may do in <channel>' with options 'Answers and runs tasks', 'Answers only, never starts a task', 'Off: does not answer here' (SlackChannelPolicies.tsx:22-26, 259); a default option when nothing is saved.
Per channel checkboxes: 'Search and read the web', 'Run code', 'Use connected apps and integrations' (SlackChannelPolicies.tsx:27-31).
In Slack: answer blocks with a 'View task' button in task mode (slack-messages.ts:177-179).
Approval card visible only to the asker (ephemeral in channels) with Approve, Deny and 'Review in AGI' (slack-assistant.ts:80-97).
journey: 1. Installer adds the app and invites it to a channel; optionally sets the channel's mode and tools in Settings.
2. A linked person types @AGI and the request in the channel. Unlinked people get a private prompt to connect.
3. The bot adds an eyes reaction to the message.
4. The app reads the thread, or the last 10 channel messages, as context information (slack-config.ts:34-41).
5. With no saved policy, the run is a task if tasks are available, else an answer; with a saved mode the mode decides (slack-channel-policies.ts:60-67).
6. The reply is posted in the thread (the mention's own thread if it was top level) with a footer 'For @requester' and a model name.
7. In task mode a 'View task' button opens the task in AGI Work.
feedback_and_outputs: Thread reply as the app, text split into blocks of at most 2,900 characters, 4 sections per message (slack-messages.ts:26-28, 159-184).
'AGI is turned off in this channel by the person who added it to Slack. You can still message it directly.' shown privately to the asker when the mode is off (slack-assistant.ts:61-62, 363-365).
'You stopped this task in AGI, so it has no answer to post.' if the task was stopped (slack-assistant.ts:63).
The failure notice and rate limit notice as in DMs, sent privately (ephemeral) in channels (slack-assistant.ts:80-97).
A task conversation and run appear in AGI Work (slack-tasks.ts:167-192).
settings: Channel mode and tool allow-list per channel, stored per installation and channel (slack_channel_policies, migrations 0374 and 0385).
Plan and workspace: the person picks which AGI workspace answers when linking (app/slack/link/page.tsx).

working: App mention events are parsed; mentions in direct message channels are ignored (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts:68, 80).
Channel mode lookup and 'off' notice (slack-assistant.ts:349-366); mode choice function (slack-channel-policies.ts:60-67).

Task mode: creates or reuses a conversation, saves the request, creates a cloud agent run, journals events, honors stop, saves the answer and moves the run to ready for review (slack-tasks.ts:147-241).
Thread continuity: a follow-up in the same thread reuses the first task's conversation (slack-tasks.ts:93-119; test slack-tasks.thread.test.ts).
Bot identity: replies use the bot token (slack-api.ts:175-197; encrypted token at slack-installations.ts:87); footer names the requester (slack-messages.ts:165-167).
Per-channel tool allow-list: web, code and apps; empty list when policy unreadable (slack-channel-policies.ts:44-58; slack-assistant-turn.ts:482-503).
Approve or deny in Slack by the asker only (slack-interactions.ts:88-120).
Settings UI to set channel mode and tools (SlackChannelPolicies.tsx).
Channel text from other people is fenced as untrusted context (slack-context.ts:175-196; slack-assistant-turn.ts:246).
incomplete: Channel list in Settings shows channel ids (aria-label uses channel.channelId), not names (SlackChannelPolicies.tsx:259); a channel appears only after the app has been mentioned there or a policy exists (slack-channel-policies.ts:103-113).
Connectors are not offered in channels unless the allow-list includes apps; channel runs start with no connectors (slack-assistant-turn.ts:491).
Memory is not loaded in channel answers (slack-assistant-turn.ts:521-522).
disconnected_or_disabled: Off until the Slack app is configured and the plan allows it (same as F106-05).

not_available: Plain channel messages without a mention are not answered by the assistant (slack-events.ts:67-69). Routines can still fire on other Slack events if subscribed (docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md).
Desktop, mobile, CLI, VS Code and Chrome have no Slack runtime.
Local and own-key modes (managed routing only).

Mentioning the assistant in a channel message turns that message into a task the agent runs.
In channels the agent acts under its own bot identity, distinct from the human user.
The Slack app uses bot scopes only; event subscriptions include app_mention.

A follow-up in the same thread continues the same task conversation.
A message in the channel without a mention gets no reply.
With 'Run code' unchecked the run is not offered code tools.
Only the asker can approve a pending step.

Installation and account link are resolved; unlinked users get a private link prompt in the thread.
The channel's saved mode is read; with no saved policy the system checks whether tasks are available (Work capability and compute access).
A run row is written; the bot adds the eyes reaction.
The thread or last 10 channel messages are read from Slack and fenced as untrusted context.
The turn checks plan, access, route, screening and usage; builds the tool plan using the channel allow-list; runs the model.
In task mode a conversation and cloud agent run are created at routing time and events are journaled; the final text is saved as the assistant message and the run set to ready for review.
The reply is posted in the thread with the bot token, with a footer naming the requester and a View task button in task mode.

aliases: What AGI may do in a channel
features.summary: The person who added the AGI app to a Slack workspace picks, per channel, whether AGI is off, answers only, or runs tasks, and which tool groups it may use. When a Slack answer or task needs approval, Approve and Deny buttons appear in Slack. Web only; Teams and email approvals do not exist.

purpose.what_it_does: Two linked controls for the AGI Slack app on web. (1) Per-channel policy: mode (off, answer, task) and a tool allow-list (web, code, apps) stored per Slack channel and read on every message (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-channel-policies.ts:28-67). (2) Approval in the channel: when the tool loop pauses for a sensitive step, AGI posts the request with Approve and Deny buttons in Slack and resumes when the linked requester clicks (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-messages.ts:234-280; apps/web/lib/slack/slack-interactions.ts:91-160).
purpose.why_it_exists: Admins need to limit where and how far an assistant acts in shared channels, and a person needs to approve risky steps where the conversation happens. The migration says AGI used to answer the same way in every channel and cites Claude in Slack and ChatGPT as references (apps/web/db/neon/0374_slack_channel_policy_and_agent_credit_cap.sql:1-12).
purpose.who_uses_it: The installer (the AGI user who added the app to the Slack workspace) sets policies. The requester (a Slack user linked to their AGI account) approves or denies their own pending steps (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-interactions.ts:88-89, 118-120).
problems_solved: AGI answering or acting in channels where it should be quiet
AGI using web, code or connected apps in a channel that should not allow them
Having to leave Slack to approve a step
A stale or forged approval click resuming the wrong step
use_cases: An installer turns AGI off in a private HR channel and leaves it on elsewhere
An installer allows answers but no code in a customer channel
A requester mentions AGI in a channel; it needs approval for a connected-app action; the requester clicks Approve in Slack
A requester ignores a request and the approval expires after 24 hours

established.statement: When an agent needs approval, the request appears in a channel (Slack, Teams or email) and can be approved there.
Admins or users can set what the agent may do per channel (which channels it may read, post in or act on).
Approvals are shown in Slack and also as an in-app notification.
A missing policy row means the default: answers and runs tasks when task is available.
An unreadable tool list gives the run no tools.
A pending approval expires after 24 hours.

acceptance_criteria: Setting a channel to off makes a mention there return the 'turned off' notice and creates no run.
Setting a channel to answer never opens a task conversation even when the plan allows tasks.
Unticking 'Run code' removes code tools from the next turn in that channel; ticking all three stores null (all tools).
Only the installer can read-write policies for that workspace; another AGI user gets 'That Slack workspace is not one you installed'.
A step needing approval posts Approve and Deny; clicking as the requester resumes; clicking as another Slack user is refused.
Clicking an old card after a newer checkpoint is refused as out of date.
After 24 hours, Approve returns 'This approval expired'.
Denying resumes the answer without that step.
inferred: Per-channel read or post restrictions (which channels AGI may read) are not modelled; only off/answer/task and tool groups exist, so S106.22 is covered in part [inferred].
Approver is always the requester; an admin cannot approve for someone else [inferred from NOT_YOURS check].

steps.what_happens: Installer changes a channel setting; browser sends PUT with CSRF; server checks the caller installed the workspace and writes the row; audit event recorded.
Slack sends a mention event; AGI verifies the link, rate limits, reads the channel row and resolves mode.
Turn checks plan and compute access, picks a model route, builds a tool plan limited to allowed groups.
Run parks with checkpoint and expiry; card posted via Slack API privately; in-app notification recorded.
Slack delivers button click to the interactions endpoint; signature verified; decision claimed in a locked transaction; audit event; run resumes after the response.
Slack message and card are held by Slack; the card text is replaced through response_url.

features.summary: In a Slack channel, when a person mentions AGI again inside a thread where AGI already ran a task for them, the new message continues the same AGI conversation. Answer-mode and direct-message runs keep no session; they rebuild context from Slack history. Web only; desktop shows the same hosted app.

purpose.what_it_does: Maps a Slack thread to one AGI conversation for task-mode runs, so follow-ups add to the same conversation (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-tasks.ts:93-119,167-174). For answers, it re-reads the Slack thread or recent history on each message (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-context.ts:92-122).
purpose.why_it_exists: S106.23 requires each channel thread to map to one persistent agent session so follow-ups continue it. Without it each mention would start a fresh conversation with no memory of the task.
purpose.who_uses_it: A linked Slack user working with AGI in a channel thread.
problems_solved: Losing earlier work when asking a follow-up
Many one-off conversations for one thread
Repeating context in each message
use_cases: Ask AGI to draft a report, then reply in the thread 'make it shorter' with a mention
Ask a question in a thread and follow up; AGI reads the thread to see earlier messages
Open the single AGI conversation to see the whole thread's work

where_to_find_it: Slack: reply in the thread of an earlier AGI task and mention the app. A plain reply without a mention is not read: only app_mention and direct-message events are taken up (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts:67-68).
Web: the one conversation appears in the normal conversation list; Desktop shows the same hosted web app (doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
prerequisites: Channel mode is task (or default) and task is available for the account (slack-assistant.ts:354-362)
The first message in the thread ran in task mode and created an agent run (slack-tasks.ts:169-192)
Same AGI person, workspace, installation and channel (slack-tasks.ts:105-117)
screens_and_controls: No dedicated control. The thread itself is the control.
journey: Person mentions AGI in a channel; task mode starts and a conversation is created titled from the first line (slack-tasks.ts:39-43,171-174).
AGI replies in the thread (slack-assistant.ts:99-101).
Person mentions AGI again in that thread.
AGI looks for the earliest earlier run in the same thread by the same person and reuses its conversation (slack-tasks.ts:93-119).
The new request is saved as a user message and a new agent run is created in that conversation (slack-tasks.ts:175-189).
AGI answers in the thread.
feedback_and_outputs: The answer in the thread with a link to the task (slack-assistant.ts:151-155)
The AGI conversation grows with each follow-up (slack-tasks.ts:175-179,216-222)
settings: Per-channel mode (F106-07): answer mode disables sessions
No setting for context sizes; they are constants (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-config.ts:32-41)

working: Task runs find an earlier run in the same thread and reuse its conversation; otherwise create one (slack-tasks.ts:167-174).

Lookup matches thread root as earlier.thread_ts or earlier.message_ts, excludes the current run, and requires same user, organization, installation, channel and a non-deleted conversation (slack-tasks.ts:98-117).
Answer-mode and DM runs read Slack: thread up to 40 messages (20 in DMs), DM history up to 20 messages within 12 hours, channel history last 10 (slack-context.ts:92-122; slack-config.ts:32-41).
incomplete: Only task-mode runs get a persistent AGI conversation; answer-mode runs have none (slack-assistant.ts:401; slack-tasks.ts).
Continuity is per person: another person mentioning AGI in the same thread gets their own conversation, because the lookup requires the same user_id (slack-tasks.ts:109).
A follow-up needs a mention; thread replies without a mention are ignored (slack-events.ts:67-68).
Direct messages never use task mode (slackRunModeFor with no policy and task unavailable for DMs, slack-assistant.ts:354-362), so DM threads are answer-only [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Brief says missing; the code exists for task mode, so the brief is out of date [inferred].
not_available: Teams and email thread continuity: no code (F106-09, F106-10)
Mobile, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: n/a per brief

established.statement: Each channel conversation or thread maps to one persistent agent session, so follow-ups in the thread continue it.
Only task-mode runs are linked to a conversation; the lookup reuses an earlier run's conversation in the same thread.
Answer-mode runs rebuild context from Slack history each message.

acceptance_criteria: Two mentions in one thread by one person in task mode produce one conversation with both requests.
A mention in a new thread or a top-level message creates a new conversation.
Another Slack workspace or channel never reuses the conversation.
A deleted conversation is not reused; a new one is created.
In answer mode no conversation is created and the second answer sees earlier thread messages.
Two people in one thread each get their own conversation.
inferred: The thread should survive the first run failing: a run with no agent_run_id is skipped by the join [inferred from the join on cloud_agent_runs].
proposed: [proposed] Share one conversation per thread across people in the same workspace, if the product wants that.
[proposed] Also read unmentioned thread replies once AGI has joined a thread.

Would let a person correct the feed when it is wrong [inferred].

Press 'not interested' on a story to see fewer like it (would-be, unbuilt).

established.statement: A signed-in user sees a feed of stories, research or content chosen for their interests.

acceptance_criteria: A signed-in user on Web, Desktop and Mobile can open a feed.
A user can follow and unfollow a topic and the choice survives reload and sign-in on another device.

aliases: Artifacts gallery (page title 'Gallery: artifacts built with AGI')
features.summary: The web page /gallery shows six hand-written example artifacts to anyone, signed in or not. A visitor opens one example page and presses 'Build one like it' to start a chat with a prompt in the composer. Signed-in users also see their own artifacts and artifacts shared with them. Mobile has no curated gallery.

purpose.what_it_does: Shows curated example artifacts (six static entries) on a public gallery, opens each on its own page at /gallery/<id>, and hands the example's description to chat as a starter prompt (apps/web/app/gallery/inspiration.ts, apps/web/app/gallery/[templateId]/page.tsx). For signed-in users the same page also lists their own artifacts, artifacts shared with them, and a guided 'New artifact' flow (apps/web/app/gallery/GalleryClient.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S107.04 asks that signed-out visitors can browse curated public pages built by the team, and S107.12 that a visitor reuses a public example's prompt so it lands in the composer.
purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-out visitors judging the product; signed-in users looking for ideas or their own artifacts.
problems_solved: Shows what the product can make without signing up.
Removes the blank-page problem by pre-filling a prompt.
Gives search engines indexable example pages (sitemap lists them) (apps/web/app/sitemap.ts).
use_cases: A visitor opens /gallery, picks 'Flow chart: CI pipeline', reads the diagram, and presses 'Build one like it'.
A signed-in user filters by type 'Code' and opens one of their own artifacts in the side panel.
A signed-in user opens 'Shared with you' to find an artifact someone invited them to.

where_to_find_it: Web: public route /gallery (apps/web/app/gallery/page.tsx), linked from the sitemap page as 'Gallery' (apps/web/app/sitemap-page/page.tsx:40). Example pages at /gallery/<id>.

Web signed-in: /chat/artifacts redirects to /chat/library?surface=artifact, so the in-app Library shows artifacts; the public /gallery stays separate (apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.tsx; apps/web/app/chat/artifacts/page.test.tsx:57).

Mobile: no curated gallery. The mobile 'artifacts' screen is the user's own artifacts (apps/mobile/app/(app)/artifacts/index.tsx, apps/mobile/src/features/artifacts/index.tsx). Brief S107.04 and S107.12: mobile missing.
Desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no gallery code found by search; the public Desktop shows the hosted web app per AGENTS.md section 5, so it may show this page [inferred].
prerequisites: Viewing /gallery and /gallery/<id>: none; no sign-in needed (page has no auth check, apps/web/app/gallery/page.tsx).
Own artifacts and 'Shared with you': signed in; shared list also needs a verified primary email (apps/web/app/api/artifacts/shared-with-me/route.ts).
Prompt reuse landing in the composer: /chat requires sign-in or guest chat (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx).
screens_and_controls: Gallery page: heading 'Artifacts', eyebrow 'Gallery', search box labelled 'Search artifacts', filter menu labelled 'Filter by' with 'Type' (All types plus types) and 'Created' options, primary button 'New artifact', segmented group 'Show artifacts' with 'All', 'Yours', and (signed in only) 'Shared with you' (GalleryClient.tsx:1480-1525).
Sections under All: 'Shared with you' and 'Inspiration' (GalleryClient.tsx:1681,1692).

Card click opens a side drawer (dialog) with the artifact, a language badge, 'Open page' (for examples) or 'Open chat' (for the user's own artifact with a source chat) and a close button labelled 'Close artifact panel' (GalleryClient.tsx:830-950).

New artifact opens 'Choose artifact type' (categories including Documents, Games, Productivity tools, Creative projects, Quiz or survey, Start from scratch) then a 3-step wizard 'Describe your idea' / 'Who is it for?' / 'Any extra requirements?' with a close button 'Close wizard' (GalleryClient.tsx:60-100,611-730).
Example page: eyebrow 'Gallery example', title, description, buttons 'Build one like it' and 'Back to the gallery', and a preview (apps/web/app/gallery/[templateId]/page.tsx).
journey: 1. Open /gallery (no sign-in).
2. Search or filter; cards for the six examples show under 'Inspiration'.
3. Click a card; a drawer shows the example (live preview or source).
4. Press 'Open page' to go to /gallery/<id>.
5. Press 'Build one like it' to go to /chat?starterPrompt=<text> where the text is: Build something like the "<title>" example from the gallery: <description>.
6. In the chat page the prompt lands in the composer; the parameter is removed from the address bar (apps/web/features/chat/pages/WebChatPage.tsx:1322-1327).
7. The visitor edits and sends.
feedback_and_outputs: Skeleton cards while loading the user's list (GalleryClient.tsx:217,1259).
'No matches' state with a clear action when filters match nothing (GalleryClient.tsx:170).
Empty state 'Artifacts you create in conversations will appear here.' with a 'New artifact' button.
Shared tab notices: 'Verify your email to see artifacts shared with you.', 'Artifacts people share with you will appear here.', a failure message with 'Try again', and 'Load more'.
Unknown example id: the not-found page.
settings: None found in the code for the gallery itself.

working: Static registry of six examples: animated gradient button, CI pipeline flow chart, SVG wordmark, Python data pipeline, responsive card grid, SQL accounts schema (apps/web/app/gallery/inspiration.ts).
Public gallery page and example pages, with static params so all six are pre-built and unknown ids call notFound() (apps/web/app/gallery/[templateId]/page.tsx).
Build one like it link to /chat?starterPrompt=... and composer prefill consumed once on the chat page (WebChatPage.tsx:1146,1322-1327).
Search, type filter, date filter, scope tabs, drawer, creation wizard (GalleryClient.tsx).
Account artifact index merged with locally derived artifacts (GalleryClient.tsx:1195-1245; apps/web/features/chat/hooks/use-artifact-index.ts).
Shared with you list with pages and retry (apps/web/app/gallery/use-shared-with-you.ts; apps/web/app/api/artifacts/shared-with-me/route.ts).
Sitemap lists /gallery and each example (apps/web/app/sitemap.ts:6,64).
incomplete: Example cards in the drawer offer 'Open page' only; there is no prompt-reuse button on the card or drawer. Prompt reuse is on the example page. The brief cites GalleryClient.tsx:1119 for it; that line is in the SharedNotice component, so the brief citation is stale (GalleryClient.tsx:1071-1120).
The 'New artifact' wizard builds a prompt from the category and answers; it is not reuse of an example's prompt (GalleryClient.tsx:631-660,1345).

Signed-out visitors who press 'Build one like it' land on /chat: guest chat if open and no session cookie, else sign-in with the path and query kept as the return address (apps/web/app/chat/layout.tsx). A search of GuestChat.tsx for search params, prefill or starter found nothing, so prefill for guests is unverified and probably absent [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Desktop image gallery and style presets were cut because they had no production import path (docs/decisions/wire-or-cut.md:26); that is a different, removed feature.
not_available: Mobile: no curated gallery or prompt reuse (brief S107.04, S107.12).

steps.what_happens: Browser requests /gallery; server renders header and footer; GalleryClient hydrates.
Client filters the six static examples in memory; no network is needed for them.
If signed in, the client fetches /api/artifacts/index and /api/artifacts/shared-with-me with the session token and merges results with the local store.
Pressing 'Build one like it' navigates to /chat?starterPrompt=<encoded text>.

The chat layout lets guests into guest chat when open, sends signed-out visitors with a session cookie or no guest access to sign-in, else shows chat; WebChatPage moves the parameter into the composer.
The visitor presses send; the chat turn then uses whichever mode and provider the account has.

features.summary: A person can open a shared-chat link and read the chat without an account. Signed-in people can press Open in AGI to copy the chat into a new conversation in their own workspace and keep working. The page shows title, model, message count, expiry and, for workspace shares, who shared it.

purpose.what_it_does: Serves a read-only snapshot of a chat at /share/[token] and offers a copy-into-my-account step at /chat/from-share/[token] on web. On mobile, a separate 'Continue in a new chat' action in the Shared with you screen does a similar copy (title and text only) (apps/web/app/share/[token]/page.tsx:96-123; apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/ContinueSharedSession.tsx:99-165; apps/mobile/src/features/projects/components/SharedWithYouScreen.tsx:193-225).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief item S107.11 says a viewer should be able to copy a public shared conversation into their own account and keep working on it, and S107.13 says shared content shows who made it and where it came from (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/107-discovery-social-and-public-content-products.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone holding a share link (readers, signed-out or signed-in); signed-in users who want to continue the chat; workspace members who receive a workspace-only share.
problems_solved: A chat can be shown to someone without an account.
A reader can turn a read-only snapshot into their own editable chat.
A workspace-only share is not readable by anyone holding the link outside the workspace (apps/web/lib/services/org-shared-session-service.ts:196-247).
use_cases: A colleague sends a link; the reader skims it signed out, then signs up and continues it.
A signed-in user opens a shared chat and presses Open in AGI to get their own copy.
A workspace member opens a workspace-only share and sees 'Shared by <name>'.
On a phone, a user opens Shared with you, picks a chat and chooses Continue in a new chat.

where_to_find_it: Web: open /share/<24-character token>; header button 'Open in AGI' (apps/web/features/chat/components/share/SharedSessionViewer.tsx:93-99).
Web: /chat/from-share/<token> is the copy step (apps/web/app/chat/from-share/[token]/page.tsx:1-12).

steps.what_happens: Browser requests /share/<token>; server checks the 24-character token pattern.
Server reads the public row; if none, reads through the caller's row-security connection and runs the workspace admission check.
Server drops system messages, hides the page if expired, renders the viewer.
Viewer presses Open in AGI; browser loads /chat/from-share/<token> and fetches the workspace list, then /api/share/<token>.
Browser creates a conversation, posts message batches to /api/chat/conversations/<id>/messages/bulk, stores artifacts in the local artifacts store and navigates.
On failure the browser sends DELETE for the new conversation.

features.summary: People can report an AI answer or a shared item. On web, a menu item sends a report at once with category harmful. On mobile, a sheet lets the person choose a category and add a note; the report is sent to our servers, kept on the device if sending fails, and can also be emailed.

features.summary: Platform staff review content reports and rights notices in admin screens, record a decision with a note, and unpublish a shared chat or published artifact through a separate takedown action. Every decision writes an audit event. Only platform admins can use it.

purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S107.23: platform staff review reported public content, decide on it and take it down. Reports need a state and a reviewer, not just a log (apps/web/db/neon/0124_content_report_triage.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Platform administrators only.
problems_solved: Reports do not sit unread forever.
An anonymous allegation cannot by itself unpublish someone's content.
Every removal leaves an audit entry.
use_cases: Claim a harmful-content report and mark it actioned with a note.
Reject a rights notice.

Record a notice as unpublished when the copy is already gone.

steps.what_happens: Admin opens the panel; browser fetches the queue with a session token.
Server checks admin identity, rate limit, reads rows.
Admin writes a note and picks a decision; browser posts with a CSRF header.
For Unpublish, panel posts takedown first; server writes a required audit event, then deletes the row.
Panel then posts the notice disposition; server updates the notice and writes an audit event.

features.summary: A signed-in web person links a US bank through Plaid and sees balances, spending by category and recent transactions on the Finances page (/chat/finance). Chat can also read balances and transactions through two read-only bank tools. Both are switched off in code today by the connector release state, and by missing Plaid setup.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person link one or more US bank accounts read-only through Plaid. It shows accounts, spending, income and recent transactions on one page, and lets chat answer money questions from live bank data. It cannot move money (apps/web/features/finance/components/FinanceDashboard.tsx:358; apps/web/lib/connectors/bank-accounts.ts:583-643).
purpose.why_it_exists: The founder decision D-2026-09-28-08 says bank accounts connect read-only like the leaders' personal finance experience, opt-in, US only, never used for training, and stay off until the owner signs the vendor agreement and a lawyer confirms the rules (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:198-215).
purpose.who_uses_it: A person on a paid plan, in the United States, on the web app (and the Desktop window that shows the hosted web app, per doc: AGENTS.md section 5).
problems_solved: Seeing balances and spending across banks without opening each bank
Asking chat about spending without pasting statements
Hiding one account from chat and the page without unlinking the bank
Removing a bank and ending the vendor's access to it
use_cases: Open Finances, pick Last 90 days, read where money went
Ask chat what the checking balance is
Untick a savings account so chat never sees it
Remove a bank after switching banks

where_to_find_it: Web: page /chat/finance titled 'Finances' (apps/web/app/chat/finance/page.tsx:6-17). It has no entry in the left rail; the rail list has no Finance item (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:90-170). It is reached from the toast 'See your finances' after linking (apps/web/features/finance/lib/announce-bank-connected.ts:5-10), from the URL, or from the 'Connect a bank account' link on the page.

Web: linking starts from the connector named 'Bank accounts' in Settings, Connections (the page links to /settings/connections: FinanceDashboard.tsx:30,104) and the connector directory (apps/web/features/directory/hooks/useDirectoryAdapter.ts:1277-1281).

Desktop: the public Desktop shows the hosted web app, so the same page [doc: AGENTS.md section 5]; /chat/finance is listed as a chat section path (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/adjacent-chat.ts:22).
Mobile: not offered; the Bank accounts detail screen redirects away while the flag is off (apps/mobile/app/(app)/connectors/[id].tsx:11-13).
Chrome extension, CLI, VS Code: no bank or finance code found (git grep for plaid, healthex in apps/extension returned nothing).

A plan that includes Connectors: any paid tier, not Free (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:351; connector-policy-gate.ts:179-186).

Deployment configured with PLAID_CLIENT_ID, PLAID_SECRET and PLAID_ENV (apps/web/lib/connectors/plaid-config.ts:52-58).

Connectors released for bank-accounts. Today the release state is 'coming_soon' and bank-accounts is not in the released list, so linking is refused (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14-30; connector-policy-gate.ts:147-154).

working: The page, the overview endpoint, the linked-banks list, per-account exclusion and bank removal are implemented and connected on web (FinanceDashboard.tsx:326-408; apps/web/app/api/finance/overview/route.ts:20-38; LinkedBanks.tsx:37-174).

Spending math: pending transactions are left out; transfers, loan payments and income are not counted as spending; income counts only negative amounts in the INCOME category; totals use the most common currency (apps/web/lib/services/finance-overview-service.ts:17-22,64-117).
Overview reads up to 2,000 transactions in pages of 500 (bank-accounts.ts:828-829,862-911).
Two read-only chat tools with validated arguments, results fenced as untrusted data (bank-accounts.ts:55-57,106-120,652-654,682-788).
Several banks per person, each removable alone; an earlier single-link grant is carried over (bank-accounts.ts:307-355,380-412,483-497; migration apps/web/db/neon/0350_bank_account_items.sql).
Account erasure and connector disconnect remove the Plaid item (apps/web/lib/connectors/oauth-access.ts:449; apps/web/lib/server/account-erasure.ts:1044).
After a bank tool returns data, save_memory is refused for the rest of the turn (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/chat/completions/lib/tool-loop.ts:2531-2536,5642-5644).
Plaid script, frame and API origins are added to the Content Security Policy only while PLAID_ENV is set (plaid-config.ts:64-72; apps/web/proxy.ts:51).
incomplete: No budgets, net worth, credit or document explanation (see F108-02).

The finance overview and linked-banks list endpoints do not check plan, region or connector release; they check sign-in, active account and rate limit only (apps/web/app/api/finance/overview/route.ts:20-36; apps/web/app/api/connectors/bank-accounts/items/route.ts:14-22) [inferred: a person who already has linked rows keeps seeing data after a plan change].
The setup doc says linking again replaces the previous item, but the code keeps several banks (doc: docs/development/connectors-setup.md:597-632 versus bank-accounts.ts:433-454).
disconnected_or_disabled: Connector release state is 'coming_soon' and the released list holds 13 other connectors; bank-accounts is not in it and a test names it as not released (packages/contracts/types/src/connector-release.ts:14-30; packages/contracts/types/src/__tests__/connector-release.test.ts:36-48). So the link and exchange endpoints refuse with 'Connectors are coming soon.' even with Plaid configured (connector-policy-gate.ts:147-154; link/route.ts:42-50).
Chat bank tools are never added to a turn while bank-accounts is unreleased (apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:2478-2485).
Plaid is also unconfigured until the owner sets the three variables; the brief says the owner has said bank stays off for now (brief S108.01; docs/development/connectors-setup.md:597-632).

Mobile: bank code exists (apps/mobile/services/connectors.ts:317-358; apps/mobile/src/features/settings/cloud-connectors/LinkedBanks.tsx) but FEATURES.bankLinking is false (apps/mobile/lib/v1FeatureFlags.ts:30), and the server removes bank tools from mobile turns (plaid-config.ts:13-19).
not_available: Chrome extension, CLI and VS Code: no code.
Mobile: not offered to users.
Local mode: nothing runs on the device; every step needs our servers and Plaid.

established.statement: A personal-finance dashboard shows accounts, balances and spending in one product view.
The user links bank, card and investment accounts so the assistant can read balances and transactions.
The product analyses transactions by category and period and shows where money goes.

Bank connections are opt-in, read-only, United States only, never written to memory or used for training, removed with their stored tokens on disconnect, and stay off until the owner signs the vendor agreement and a lawyer confirms the rules.
Disconnect or account erasure calls Plaid item removal and erases the stored token; the Content Security Policy admits Plaid only while PLAID_ENV is set; set all three variables or none.
An irreversible action asks first and names the consequence (bank removal uses useConfirmAction).

acceptance_criteria: With Plaid sandbox set, connectors released for bank-accounts, a paid account in the US: linking a sandbox bank adds it to 'Linked banks' and shows its accounts.
With no bank linked, /chat/finance shows 'Connect a bank account to see your balances and spending here.'
Switching period changes the totals and the date range returned by /api/finance/overview?period=30d|90d|12m; any other period is refused.
Unticking an account removes it from totals, from the accounts list and from chat tool results.
Remove bank asks for confirmation and, once confirmed, the bank disappears and Plaid item removal is called; a Plaid failure keeps the bank and shows the removal-failed message.
A Free account, or a request from outside the US, cannot start linking and sees a refusal message.
A mobile-started chat turn never receives the bank tools.
After a bank tool returns data in a turn, save_memory is refused in that turn.
inferred: Finance overview and linked-banks list should apply the same plan, region and release rules as linking, so a downgraded or moved account does not keep reading live bank data [inferred from connector-policy-gate.ts:147-186 versus overview/route.ts:20-36].
The Finances page should be reachable from the rail or Settings once bank linking opens [inferred: no rail item exists].
proposed: [proposed] Add a rail or Settings entry for Finances when the connector is released.
[proposed] Gate the overview and items GET routes with the connector policy gate.
[proposed] Update docs/development/connectors-setup.md to describe several banks per person.
[proposed] Add category budgets and net worth on top of the overview (see F108-02).

steps.what_happens: Person opens /chat/finance; the page asks GET /api/finance/overview for the chosen period with cookies.
Server checks sign-in, active account and rate limit, then answers 'unavailable' with the setup message when Plaid variables are missing.
Server reads the person's bank rows and opens each sealed token.
Server asks Plaid for accounts and pages of transactions for the date range, then sums spending, income, categories and months.
To link: the server creates a Plaid link token; the browser loads Plaid Link from cdn.plaid.com; the person signs in to the bank in Plaid's window.
The browser posts the public token; the server exchanges it at Plaid, seals the access token, stores the item, and records the connector grant.
In chat, when the connector is released, connected and not denied, the two bank tool definitions join the turn; a model call runs the tool, which asks Plaid live and returns fenced JSON.

Mobile hosted link (flag off): server asks Plaid for a hosted link URL and stores a pending authorization; the exchange call checks the session and answers 409 'not_finished' text when no bank was added.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Page and linking use no model. The chat tools are offered to whichever model serves the turn through the shared tool loop; no model or provider rule is specific to them (user-connector-tools.ts:2478-2485). Plaid is the data provider and sits outside packages/ai/providers. Tools are skipped for a model whose capability 'tools' is false (route.ts:~812-815) [inferred from the guard comment].

access_and_usage.account: Signed in with an active account; confirmed email required to link (overview/route.ts:21-22; connector-policy-gate.ts:155-158).
access_and_usage.permissions: Workspace connector policy can block bank-accounts at link time (link/route.ts:42-50; tests link route test 177-198). Linking is refused inside no organisation rule specifically beyond that policy. Bank rows are per user with row-level security (0350 migration).
access_and_usage.subscription: Connectors capability, paid tiers only: basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise (billing-catalog.ts:351; connector-policy-gate.ts:179-186). Overview and items reads do not check the plan (overview/route.ts:20-36).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit bucket 'chat-conversation' for link, exchange and items; 'finance-overview' per user for the overview (link/route.ts:28,33; overview/route.ts:23). Up to 20 account ids and 500 transactions per tool call; overview reads at most 2,000 transactions (bank-accounts.ts:51-53,828-829). Plaid bills the balance call per use (doc: docs/development/connectors-setup.md:610-615). No credit or quota counter found in the code for this feature.

access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Any model that can call tools; models flagged without tools get none. No model identifier is named in the code for this feature.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Plaid is required; US institutions only (plaid-config PLAID_COUNTRY_CODES US in bank-accounts.ts:42). Mobile-started turns never get bank tools (plaid-config.ts:13-19).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Not available. Linking and reading need our servers and Plaid; no on-device path exists in the code. Own-key mode: unknown (not examined).

features.summary: One general Deep Research run serves the finance, company, legal and science items. Compare a market or instrument with sources

steps.what_happens: Person switches Deep Research on and sends; the client sends research:true to the chat endpoint.
Server refuses with plan_upgrade_required when the plan lacks deep_research.
Server enters research mode for a paid, non-trial turn and starts a run record; the first request stops after planning.
After 'Start research' the approved steps return in a second request; durable workflow or request-scoped loop runs.
Each gathering round asks the chosen provider with a search tool; searches may be a provider-native tool or our own web_search function; admitted searches reserve a charge.
Pages are read through url_fetch (up to 8) and merged into a deduplicated, numbered source list; blocked domains are dropped.
A synthesis turn writes the report; the report is saved to research_reports and a notification is sent.
The client shows the report, sources panel and gallery; mobile reads the list from the API.

Web search comes from a provider-native tool or our generic backend; the search charge feature is named for Perplexity (research-loop.ts:1815-1822), so provider:perplexity matters for metering. A managed failover plan can rotate the serving provider (route.ts:605-614).

features.summary: A personal Health space: one private project per person, kept out of other chats and training, where a read-only HealthEx connector would let chat read the person's own records. The space, availability checks and guards exist, but HealthEx cannot be connected today because it is unreleased and has no configured sign-in.

purpose.what_it_does: Creates a single Health project per person whose chats and files stay apart from other chats, allows only models that keep chats out of training, and offers HealthEx read tools only inside it (apps/web/lib/services/health-space-service.ts:46-58; apps/web/lib/user-connector-tools.ts:2515-2540,2657-2659).
purpose.why_it_exists: Founder decision D-2026-09-28-08: health records connect like the leaders' health experiences, opt-in, read-only, US only, never used for training, and stay off until the owner signs the vendor agreement and a lawyer reviews the FTC rule (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:198-215).
purpose.who_uses_it: A person in the United States on a personal (not organisation) account, once the connector opens.
problems_solved: Keeping health talk out of ordinary chats and search sharing
Asking questions about the person's own records
Making sure health chats avoid models that may train
use_cases: Ask for a summary of conditions and medications
Ask about lab values
Prepare questions for a doctor visit from records
Keep health notes and files in one private place

steps.what_happens: Page shell asks GET /api/health-space once per user and shows the Health rail item only if 'available'.
Server computes availability: configured OAuth provider, US country header, personal account.
Opening /chat/health reads then POSTs to create the project row once, then redirects.
Person connects HealthEx through OAuth with PKCE; sign-in happens at HealthEx.
A chat turn in the Health project looks up the space, forces no-training routing and passes healthSpace to the tool catalog.
The model calls a HealthEx read tool at the HealthEx MCP server; the answer returns into chat.
After a health read, save_memory is refused for the rest of the turn.

features.summary: Contract review is a vendored skill named review-contract. The person gives a contract and the model reviews it clause by clause, flags deviations, suggests redlines and summarises business impact. It runs in chat on web, desktop (hosted web), mobile and Chrome. Filing documents by client and matter is not built on any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Contract review: the review-contract skill tells the model to accept a contract (file, URL or pasted text), ask which side the person is on, load a playbook if one exists, go through a fixed list of clause categories, flag each as GREEN/YELLOW/RED, write redline text with fallbacks, and give a business impact summary (.agents/skills/review-contract/SKILL.md:26-60, :210-300, :345-382). Matter organisation (client/matter records, per-matter files and history) is the second item of this feature and has no code (audit/missing/108-specialist-workspaces.md:67-73; grep of apps and packages for matter-id / client-matter terms found nothing relevant).
purpose.why_it_exists: To compete with Claude and ChatGPT on legal-work workflows: the brief wants a review flow that checks clauses, flags risks and suggests redlines against a playbook (S108.19), and a matter-based filing system (S108.18) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: In-house legal teams, business people who receive vendor or customer contracts, and sales staff who need a first pass before counsel looks. The skill says it is not legal advice and that qualified lawyers must review (.agents/skills/review-contract/SKILL.md:12-14).
problems_solved: A first-pass clause review of a long agreement takes hours by hand.
Positions are inconsistent when each reviewer decides what is acceptable; the skill compares against a playbook or, if none, generic commercial standards (SKILL.md:47-63).
Redlines and fallback positions are written for the person to paste into a negotiation (SKILL.md:263-295).
use_cases: Paste a vendor SaaS agreement and ask for a review as the customer.
Upload an NDA and run the sibling triage-nda skill to classify it GREEN, YELLOW or RED (.agents/skills/triage-nda/SKILL.md:3).
Ask for redlines on the limitation-of-liability clause of a services contract.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (hosted web app): a bundled skill in the managed catalog; the Skills page is at route /skills (apps/web/app/skills/page.tsx exists) and the composer offers an installed-skill mention palette (apps/web/features/chat/components/Composer/ChatComposerNew.tsx:2902-2907). features.summary: A Code session on the web can be created on the Code Interpreter image and shown as a notebook. The person edits code and markdown cells, runs one cell or all cells in a cloud sandbox, uploads and downloads files, and each run is logged with code, network policy and from-the-top flag. Desktop shows the same hosted page. Mobile and Chrome have none.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs notebook cells (python, javascript, typescript, r, java, bash) in a managed sandbox attached to a Code session, shows ordered outputs, and records each executed cell with a code hash so a result can be traced to code and network policy (apps/web/app/api/code/sessions/[sessionId]/notebook/execute/route.ts:30-90; packages/contracts/types/src/cloud-code.ts:449-455; apps/web/db/neon/0254_notebook_runs.sql:29-46).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S108.22 wants a research environment that runs code or notebooks in a pinned environment that can be re-run to reproduce results (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md). The migration says a result left nothing behind but the browser output (0254_notebook_runs.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Analysts, students and researchers who want to run Python or other code without installing anything.
problems_solved: No local setup: the sandbox image provides Python, Jupyter, pandas, numpy and plotting (apps/web/lib/e2b/templates.ts:141-148).
Order dependence: Run all runs every cell from the top and stops at the first failure (run-all/route.ts:216).
Provenance: who, when, which code, which network policy (0254_notebook_runs.sql header).
use_cases: Load a CSV by upload and plot it.
Run a data-cleaning notebook top to bottom and see where it fails.
Run a bash cell to inspect the sandbox, with network access set to none.

where_to_find_it: Web: the Code area (apps/web/features/code/CloudCodePage.tsx); when the selected session's runtime is the Code Interpreter template the page shows a panel labelled 'Notebook' (CloudCodePage.tsx:2090, :2665; NotebookPanel.tsx:135).
Desktop: hosted web app, same page (doc: AGENTS.md §5 'The public Desktop shows the hosted web app') [inferred for this feature].
Mobile: not available; mobile 'notebook' code is a project knowledge-sources screen, a different thing (apps/mobile/src/features/notebook/service.ts:1-30).
Chrome, CLI, VS Code: not available for notebooks (no notebook code found in apps/extension; surface list in brief).
prerequisites: Signed in on web.
Managed Code enabled on the deployment and priceable: AGI_E2B_EXECUTION on, a sandbox provider key set and a compute rate present (apps/web/lib/e2b/gate.ts:20-27).

Managed compute private beta not switched off (apps/web/lib/managed-compute-gate.ts:40-58; error 'Managed compute is temporarily unavailable. Use Local or BYOK in the meantime, or try again shortly.' execute/route.ts:52-56).
A Code session created on the notebook template and in state ready (cloud-code-session-service.ts:1781-1800).
screens_and_controls: Toolbar buttons 'Add cell', 'Add markdown', 'Run all', 'Upload file' (NotebookPanel.tsx:145-168).
Per-cell 'Run cell N' button and language/kind selectors (NotebookCellView.tsx:132).

Status line under the toolbar: 'Cells build on what ran before them. Run all runs every cell from the top.' or 'Ran N cells from the top at <time>, stopped at the first error.' (NotebookPanel.tsx:182-191).
File list with 'Download <name>' buttons (NotebookPanel.tsx:249).
journey: Open the Code page and create a session using the Code Interpreter runtime with a network setting of none, trusted or full (full needs acknowledgement) (cloud-code-session-service.ts:714-717; templates.ts:141).
The Notebook panel appears once the session is ready.
Edit cells; press Run cell, or Shift+Enter to run and add a new cell (apps/web/e2e/notebook.spec.ts:175).
Or press Run all; cells run in order and stop at the first failed cell.
Optionally Upload file (limit 10 MB) and download generated files (cloud-code-session-service.ts:92).
Read outputs: text, images, tables, or error output.
feedback_and_outputs: Ordered cell outputs (text, image, table) and error output (e2e/notebook.spec.ts:144-164).
Run provenance line with count and 'from the top' or 'in place'.

Errors: 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment', 'Code session is busy; wait and try again', 'Closed Code sessions cannot run cells', 'Failed Code sessions must be closed and recreated', 'Managed Code environment could not be attached' (execute/route.ts:49-51; cloud-code-session-service.ts:1781-1830).
Unconfirmed result in run-all: 'The execution result could not be confirmed. Code may have run. Check the sandbox state before running it again.' (run-all/route.ts:35-36).
settings: Session network access none/trusted/full and extra hosts (cloud-code-session-service.ts:714-717, :370).
Optional requireNetworkAccess in a run request: a run refuses a session wider than it asked for (notebook-runs.ts:10-60).

working: Execute endpoint: rate limit, CSRF, deployment gate, beta gate, managed-compute access, session ownership, network policy, run, provenance write (execute/route.ts:44-90).
Run-all endpoint: up to 100 cells, validated up front, stops at first failure, groups rows by run_id (run-all/route.ts:34, :99-100, :144, :216, :225).
Notebook panel with cells, run, upload and download (NotebookPanel.tsx; notebook-workspace.ts).
Provenance writer records code, SHA-256 digest, network policy, from_top, ok, error (notebook-runs.ts:70-100).
Template list names the Code Interpreter image and is also the allowlist for client-named templates (templates.ts header comment, :141).
incomplete: 'Pinned environment' is not established: the code names a template id but no package or version capture or lock was found, so re-running reproduces the same code, not necessarily the same environment [inferred].
Single-cell runs record cell_index 0 and from_top false regardless of position (execute/route.ts:81-95).

Notebook cell contents are kept in an in-memory workspace; no browser-storage or server save of the notebook document was found in notebook-workspace.ts, notebook-api.ts or hooks (grep for localStorage/sessionStorage/persist found none), so cells may be lost on reload [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Provenance migration 0254 header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only'; whether it is applied is unknown. If not, recordNotebookRun only logs an error and the run still returns (notebook-runs.ts:70-105).
Whole feature is off unless AGI_E2B_EXECUTION=1 with a key and a compute rate (gate.ts:20-27).
not_available: Mobile and Chrome notebooks.
Notebook cell history viewer: table exists but no reader route was found [inferred from file listing of notebook routes: execute, run-all, files only].

established.statement: S108.22 Should: a research environment runs code/notebooks in a pinned environment that can be re-run to reproduce results. Brief status: web done, desktop done, mobile missing, Chrome missing.
Execute checks managed compute access for the code surface and session ownership.
A client may only name a template present in the merged template list.
A run may refuse a session whose network access is wider than the run requested.
Managed compute is a Cloud capability; Local and own-key are the alternatives the error points to.

acceptance_criteria: Run cell on a ready session returns outputs in order and an ok flag.
Run all with a failing second cell stops there and the response says completed false.
A run requesting network none against a full-network session is refused with a conflict message.
With the beta gate off, execute returns the 'temporarily unavailable' message.
A closed or failed session cannot run cells.
After a run, a notebook_runs row exists with code, digest and network_access (when migration applied).
Cell code over 50,000 characters or containing a null byte is rejected.
inferred: Reproducibility needs recorded environment versions, not just code [inferred].
Notebook documents should survive reload [inferred].
proposed: [proposed] Capture package versions per run and show a run history with a 're-run' control.
[proposed] Persist the notebook document with the session.
