aliases: Learn it / Practise it / Revise it
features.summary: Study turns a chat into a tutoring session on one topic. The person picks a topic, a way (Learn it, Practise it, Revise it) and a level, optionally course material from a project and a starting study plan. The server then adds teaching instructions to every turn. Web and desktop (hosted) have a Study page; mobile has Study and learn, Cloud mode only.

purpose.what_it_does: Marks a conversation as a study session and injects a teaching instruction (one idea at a time, hints, worked examples, quizzes and flashcards as artifacts) into each model turn while the session is open (apps/web/features/study/server/study-session-store.ts:86-99, :114-141; apps/web/features/study/lib/study-session.ts:47-68).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S108.23 asks for an education workspace for teachers and learners (classes, assignments, guided study) and S108.24 for curriculum and lesson generation as structured output (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md). The migration says Study is a way of working through a subject, not a second kind of chat (apps/web/db/neon/0247_study_sessions.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: Learners; the shipped flow is learner-side. No teacher, class or assignment feature was found.
problems_solved: Chat answers dump a whole topic; Study makes the model teach one idea, check understanding, and wait (study-session.ts:22-26).

Practice without a quiz tool: quizzes and flashcards come out as artifacts the app renders (study-session.ts:47-56; apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/study/QuizView.tsx, FlashcardsView.tsx).
Finding a session again: sessions are listed and resumable (StudyPage.tsx:128-146).
use_cases: Learn eigenvalues from scratch with a worked example and a check question.
Practise German dative case with short exercises corrected one by one.
Revise a unit using attached course notes from a project and a personal study plan.

where_to_find_it: Web (and desktop via the hosted web app): left navigation item 'Study' to /chat/study (apps/web/shared/components/layout/app-nav-items.ts:144-150; hideable) and a 'Study' row in the composer plus-menu (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:188, :873). Page heading 'Study'.

Mobile: composer add sheet row 'Study and learn', shown only in Cloud mode (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/AddToChatSheet.tsx:584-588, :1256-1261); screen titled 'Study and learn' (apps/mobile/src/features/study/StudyScreen.tsx:177, :207); route apps/mobile/app/(app)/study.tsx hidden from the drawer (_layout.tsx:105).
Chrome, CLI, VS Code: not available (brief; doc: docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:64, :289).
prerequisites: Signed in on web; on mobile the app must be in Cloud mode, else the screen says 'Study runs in AGI Cloud' with 'Switch to Cloud mode' (StudyScreen.tsx:177-197).
The conversation must be a live, non-temporary chat of the caller in the active workspace (study-session-store.ts:125-133).
screens_and_controls: Web Study page: 'What are you studying?' text box (max 200 characters), 'How' radio group with 'Learn it', 'Practise it', 'Revise it', 'Where you are with it' select with 'New to it', 'Some background', 'Know it well', 'Course material' select (only if projects exist), checkbox 'Start with a personal study plan', button 'Start studying', list 'Your sessions' with 'Leave study mode' and a resume control (StudyPage.tsx:103-146, :248, :285-289, :339-344; packages/contracts/types/src/study.ts:7, :19-35).

In a study chat: indicator 'Studying: <topic> · <mode>' and button 'Leave study mode' with note 'Turns off tutoring for this chat. The chat and its messages stay.' (StudyModeIndicator.tsx:8-9, :36-60).
Mobile: topic field (label 'What do you want to study?'), mode and level choices, 'Start studying', history with retry (StudyScreen.tsx:218, :239-269, :314-317).
journey: Open Study.
Type a topic, choose how and level, optionally pick course material and tick the study plan box.
Press Start studying; the app creates a conversation titled from topic and mode, then registers the study session on it (StudyPage.tsx:103-126).
If the plan box was ticked a plan request is placed in the chat draft (studyPlanRequest: order, time per part, checks, ask time per week) (study-session.ts:115-121).
Chat with the model; each turn carries the study instruction.
Quizzes and flashcards appear as artifact blocks the person can answer.
Press Leave study mode to end tutoring; the chat stays. Resume from 'Your sessions'.
feedback_and_outputs: Spinner 'Starting the study session' and error alerts such as 'The study session could not be started.' (StudyPage.tsx:121-124).
'Nothing yet. Subjects you study show up here.' for an empty history; 'Your study history could not be loaded.' on failure (StudyPage.tsx:93-99).
Quiz and flashcard artifacts; study set print helper (study-print.ts).
settings: Course material comes from the person's projects (StudyPage.tsx:248).
Account instruction and project instruction still apply: study instruction is a 'developer' layer ordered with project and personalized layers (request-processor.ts:2111-2125).

working: API: GET list or by conversationId, POST start (strict schema: conversationId uuid, topic 1-200 chars, mode, level), DELETE end (apps/web/app/api/study/sessions/route.ts:28-35, :50-114).
Store: start upserts on conversation_id and re-opens an ended session; ends set ended_at; list joins live conversations in the active workspace (study-session-store.ts:46-62, :114-158).
Server injects the instruction in the managed chat request and in the free-quota turn path (request-processor.ts:3820; apps/web/lib/server/free-quota-turn.ts:1074).
Web page and in-chat indicator (StudyPage.tsx; StudyModeIndicator.tsx).
Mobile screen with Cloud gating, history and retry (StudyScreen.tsx).

Curriculum and lesson-plan output (S108.24) has no dedicated generator; it relies on the prompt text and plan request (study-session.ts:47-56, :115-121). Brief cites connector directory lines for it (vendor-directory.json:1028, :1728), not verified here.
disconnected_or_disabled: composeStudyPrompt, the function that ranks the study instruction against account instruction and current request, has no production caller; only its own test and the feature index use it (grep over apps and packages: apps/web/features/study/index.ts:16 and study-session.test.ts). The live path uses composeStudyInstruction placed in the 'developer' layer (request-processor.ts:2111-2122).
Migration 0247 header says 'NOT YET APPLIED : draft only'; applied state unknown.
not_available: Chrome, CLI, VS Code.

The surface matrix lists desktop and mobile as absent (docs/product/surface-feature-matrix.md:64, :285-286); that conflicts with code for mobile (apps/mobile/src/features/study exists) and is a documentation error by AGENTS.md §2.

established.statement: S108.23 Should: an education workspace for teachers and learners (classes, assignments, guided study). Brief status: web done, desktop done, mobile missing, Chrome missing.
S108.24 Should: curricula and lesson plans (objectives, activities, materials) generated as structured output. Brief status as S108.23.
Starting a session needs a topic, mode and level validated by a strict schema.
One conversation holds one study session; a second start reopens it with the new topic.
Ending Study keeps the chat; nothing a user wrote is thrown away.
Precedence of instructions is decided by the shared resolver, not by Study.

steps.what_happens: Person fills the form and presses Start studying; the app creates a conversation through the chat conversations endpoint.
App posts the session; the server inserts or reopens one row per conversation after checking ownership, workspace, not deleted, not temporary.
App opens the chat; a ticked plan box leaves a plan request in the draft.
On each chat turn the server reads the open session and builds the study instruction into the system preamble.
The chosen model replies, writing quiz or flashcards blocks as artifacts.
Leave study mode sets ended_at.

aliases: Sales, support, HR and marketing skills
features.summary: These workflows are vendored skills the model follows in chat: pipeline and deal review for sales, ticket triage, replies and escalations for support, recruiting pipeline and interview plans for HR, and about forty marketing skills. They read or write outside systems only through connectors the person has connected, and fall back to uploaded or pasted data.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the model step-by-step instructions for common business tasks, for example 'Stage-by-stage pipeline health check from CRM opportunity data' (.agents/skills/pipeline-review/SKILL.md:3), 'Triage and prioritize a support ticket' (ticket-triage/SKILL.md:3), 'Create structured interview plans' (interview-prep/SKILL.md:3). Each skill is a directory in .agents/skills marked audience product in skills-lock.json.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants sales/CRM, support, HR and marketing workflows runnable from the product (S108.26 to S108.29) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md). Skills reuse the chat, connectors and approval system instead of building separate workspaces.
purpose.who_uses_it: Sales reps and managers, support agents, recruiters and hiring managers, and marketers.
problems_solved: Repeated analysis (pipeline coverage, aging, at-risk deals) is done the same way each time.
Support triage gets a consistent priority and routing.
Interview plans come with competency questions and scorecards.
Marketing tasks (ads, SEO audit, copywriting, pricing) have ready procedures.
use_cases: Ask 'review my pipeline' with a CRM connected.
Paste a ticket and run ticket-triage, then draft-response.
Ask for an interview plan for a role.
Run seo-audit or copywriting on a landing page.

where_to_find_it: Web (and desktop via hosted web app): Skills page at /skills (apps/web/app/skills/page.tsx), composer mention palette over installed skills (ChatComposerNew.tsx:2902-2907), or just describe the task so the server may offer matching skills (request-processor.ts:1086-1109). The plus-menu 'Skills' row lists only the person's own skills (ComposerPlusMenu.tsx:1248-1251).
Mobile: Skills screen (Managed Cloud catalog) with Install/Uninstall, Details and 'Use in chat' (SkillsScreen.tsx:365-383).
Chrome: side-panel skill menu lists only the person's own skills (skillsClient.ts:36-43); bundled workflow skills can still be offered by the server by prompt match [inferred].
CLI, VS Code: not offered (request-processor.ts:1073).

features.summary: In chat the model can show a comparison card of two to four products (price, store, buy link, specs, all tied to pages found this turn) or an itinerary card of up to twelve stops numbered on a map with Google Maps route links. Places lookups are charged. The tools do not book or buy. Web, desktop (hosted), mobile and Chrome render the cards.

purpose.what_it_does: Two model tools that build typed cards. compare_products turns web-search findings into a side-by-side table; plan_itinerary looks up each stop through a places provider and builds a numbered itinerary with route legs that open in Google Maps (apps/web/lib/services/product-comparison-tool-service.ts:85, :369; apps/web/lib/places/itinerary-tool.ts:102, :336, :493).
purpose.why_it_exists: Brief S108.31 (shopping comparisons), S108.33 (travel planning and reservations) and S108.34 (commerce checkout, not applicable) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/108-specialist-workspaces.md). Cards give a structured result instead of a long text answer.
purpose.who_uses_it: Shoppers deciding between products and travellers planning a day or trip.
problems_solved: Prices and links cannot be invented: every price source, buy link and source must be a URL returned by a search or fetch in the same turn (product-comparison-tool-service.ts:85-100 description, :224-227).
Stops are looked up as real places so the map pins and route are real (itinerary-tool.ts:264-300, :536-560).
Booking is not faked: the model is told to use a booking connector or point the person to Settings > Connectors (itinerary-tool.ts:217-220).
use_cases: 'Compare these three laptops under $1000.'
'Plan a day in Lisbon with a walking route.'
'Book a table for stop 3' leads to a connector hint.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (hosted web app): chat. The cards appear above the model's reply (cards: apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/cards/ProductComparisonCard.tsx, ItineraryCard.tsx; dispatcher InteractiveCardBlock.tsx).

Mobile: chat; renderers ProductComparisonCard.tsx and the itinerary map in InteractiveCardBlock.tsx; the phone declares support for itinerary.v1 and product-comparison.v1 and sends it with each managed chat request (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/utils/clarifyCard.ts:7-18; apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3442).

Chrome: side-panel chat; card builders buildItineraryCard and buildProductComparisonCard (apps/extension/src/features/side-panel/interactiveCards.ts:109, :316); capability list sent in freeTrialClient.ts:1581-1590.
CLI, VS Code: not offered; the card tools are limited to web, desktop, mobile, chrome surfaces (request-processor.ts:1357-1362).
prerequisites: Cloud chat, streaming on, tool-capable model (request-processor.ts:1371-1382, :1410-1417).
The app must declare card support in the request (x_interactive_cards).
Shopping: a web-search tool must be attached to the turn (request-processor.ts:1414).
Travel: a places provider configured on the server and, on the Free trial path, a window that can cover a places search (request-processor.ts:5518-5520).
The message must look like the intent: shopping needs a purchase word and a choice word; travel needs an itinerary-type phrase (product-comparison-tool-service.ts:36-47; itinerary-tool.ts:57-68).
screens_and_controls: Comparison card: product columns with price, 'Buy at <merchant>' or 'View product' links, spec rows, sources (ProductComparisonCard.tsx:111).
Itinerary card: numbered stops on a map, time labels, notes, route buttons by leg ('Full route' or 'Stops 1 to 5') (itinerary-tool.ts:356-376).
journey: Type a request such as 'compare headphones under $400' or 'plan a weekend in Rome'.
The server checks surface, tool support, streaming, card support and intent, then offers the tool to the model.
For shopping the model first searches the web, then calls compare_products with products and spec labels.
For travel the model calls plan_itinerary with stops; the server looks each stop up and builds the card.
The card renders above the reply; the model adds a short note without repeating the table.
For booking the model uses a connected booking connector or tells the person to connect one.
feedback_and_outputs: Card with fallback text if the app cannot render it (fallback headline and text, itinerary-tool.ts:457-465; product-comparison buildCard :338).
Model-side messages when unavailable: no places provider, no credits, lookup failed, too large (itinerary-tool.ts:200-216).
Omitted prices or links with a note when no URL came from this turn (product-comparison-tool-service.ts:168-177).
Prices stamped 'as of' a check date and the model is told to say they can change (:200).
settings: Connectors: a travel or booking connector in Settings, Connectors (itinerary-tool.ts:217-220).
No shopping or travel specific settings found.

working: Product comparison: input schema 2-4 products with limits, grounded-URL check, size fitting in three budget steps, card and model summary (product-comparison-tool-service.ts:55-83, :224-227, :338-352, :369).

Itinerary: up to 12 stops, routes in legs of 5 stops, Google Maps directions URLs, reservation and settlement of charged places searches, card fitting (itinerary-tool.ts:264-334, :336-380, :457-493; packages/contracts/types/src/interactive-cards.ts:207-210).
Offers wired into the request and tool loop (request-processor.ts:1364-1420; tool-loop.ts:2643-2675).
Renderers on web, mobile, Chrome.
incomplete: Neither tool completes a booking or purchase; reservations depend on external connectors the person must connect (itinerary-tool.ts:217-220).

Itinerary needs a Google places backend key set on the server (apps/web/lib/places/places-config.ts:7 names the env GOOGLE_PLACES_API_KEY); without it the tool is not offered (request-processor.ts:5518).
Desktop: no desktop-specific card code; relies on hosted web app [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Card tools are not offered on cli, vscode or api (request-processor.ts:1357-1362).
No dedicated itinerary-tool test file was found; the tool name appears in request-processor.stable-tools.test.ts and chat-tool-provider-schemas.test.ts.

Booking inside the product with no connector.

steps.what_happens: App sends the chat request with the list of card kinds it can render and streaming on.
Server tests surface, tool support, stream, card support, intent and (for travel) places availability, then adds the tool to the turn.
Shopping: web search results are fetched; the model calls compare_products; the server keeps only URLs retrieved this turn and builds the card.
Travel: the model calls plan_itinerary; the server reserves a charge for each distinct stop lookup, calls the places provider, settles the charge, builds stops and route URLs.
The card is streamed to the app and rendered; route buttons open Google Maps.

features.summary: A menu-bar icon on macOS, or a tray icon on Windows and Linux, in AGI Desktop (Electron). One click starts a new chat, opens Quick Ask, takes a screenshot or window capture, starts dictation, stops running agents, or changes the shortcut keys. Mobile has no menu bar; its quick actions are F109-05.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop adds a small menu to the system menu bar or tray. It lists running and waiting coding sessions, a Stop All Agents item, the four ambient actions (Quick Ask, Screenshot to Chat, Window to Chat, Dictation) with their keys, and a Shortcuts submenu for choosing keys. (apps/desktop/electron/tray.ts:166-206)
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief says a quick menu should offer one-click AGI actions such as new chat, quick ask, screenshot and voice (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md S109.03). The code also states the tray is one of two ways to stop an agent from outside its window, the Stop Agents shortcut being the other (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1851-1857 comment above trayNeeded at :1858).
purpose.who_uses_it: People using AGI Desktop who want AGI actions without bringing the main window forward, and people who need to stop an agent that is using their screen.
problems_solved: Starting AGI actions without finding and focusing the main window.
Seeing which coding sessions run or wait for approval, and opening one.
Stopping agents and revoking computer-use access from outside the app window.
Learning which shortcut key does what, and fixing a key another app already holds.
use_cases: Click the menu-bar icon, then New Chat, to open a fresh conversation.
Click Quick Ask to raise the compact panel (F109-03) without remembering the key.
See 'Waiting for Approval' and open the session that needs a decision.
Open Shortcuts and pick another key for Screenshot to Chat when the default clashes with another app.

where_to_find_it: Desktop on macOS: the icon in the menu bar. Desktop on Windows and Linux: the tray icon; a left click opens the main window (apps/desktop/electron/tray.ts:216-218). On macOS the code names it 'menu bar', elsewhere 'tray menu' (apps/desktop/electron/shortcuts.ts:38-40).

features.summary: On AGI Desktop, one global key captures the whole display under the pointer and another captures the app window in front. The picture is put on the clipboard and pasted into the main chat composer, then the old clipboard is restored. In Chrome, a separate key sends the visible tab to Desktop's chat.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop captures a screen or one other app's window with Electron's capturer, copies the PNG to the clipboard, focuses the main chat composer and pastes (apps/desktop/electron/screenshot.ts:142-244). Chrome's 'capture_page' key sends the visible tab picture to Desktop, which pastes it the same way (apps/extension/src/background.ts:7764-7821; apps/desktop/electron/browserHandoff.ts:33-60).
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief requires a shortcut that captures the screen, or one chosen window, and attaches it to an AGI chat (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md S109.09, S109.10).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users asking AGI about what is on screen; Chrome users with Desktop paired who want a page picture in a Desktop chat.
problems_solved: Taking a screenshot, saving it and attaching it by hand.
Capturing one window rather than the whole screen.
Leaving a screen picture on the clipboard where every app can read it.
use_cases: Press the Screenshot key while reading an error and ask AGI to explain it.
Press the Window key while a design tool is in front to send only that window.
In Chrome press the capture key to hand the page to the Desktop chat.
Capture while Quick Ask is up: the panel is hidden first so it is not in the picture.

where_to_find_it: Desktop: global keys, defaults 'CommandOrControl+Shift+2' (Screenshot to Chat) and 'CommandOrControl+Shift+1' (Window to Chat) (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:161-168); also the menu items in the tray (F109-01) and an app-menu entry (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts, not read in detail).

Chrome: command 'capture_page', suggested Alt+Shift+Y, Command+Shift+Y on Mac, description from locale string commandCapturePage (apps/extension/manifest.json:75-80).
Web, mobile, CLI, VS Code: not present.

journey: Press the key.
Desktop hides Quick Ask and the main window (screen capture only), waits 300 ms, captures the display under the cursor (screenshot.ts:205-213).
The PNG goes on the clipboard; the main window is shown and focused, the composer is focused and the image pasted (screenshot.ts:109-140).
One second later the clipboard is put back: prior text restored, or cleared (screenshot.ts:92-107,235-238).

The paste target is the chat page that was open at press time; if the page changed or is not the trusted product page nothing is pasted (screenshot.ts:59-72,126-134).
The clipboard is restored only if it still holds the capture, so text the user copied since is kept (screenshot.ts:92-107).

A shortcut takes only a chord the shell offers; Screenshot on the paste chord captured the screen at every paste, which is why choices are restricted.

[proposed] Offer a window picker if 'chosen window' must mean choice.

features.summary: A small always-on-top window on AGI Desktop, opened with a global key, that takes one prompt over any other app. It shows the hosted compact chat page and hands longer work to the main window. Chrome has a matching in-page panel on approved sites. Mobile has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop keeps a hidden 480 by 620 frameless window loaded with the hosted /quick-ask page (apps/desktop/electron/quickAsk.ts:6-10,52-126). A key press shows it in the upper centre of the display under the cursor. In Chrome, a launcher button and slide-in panel are added to approved web pages for one question about the page (apps/extension/src/inPagePanel/setup.ts:44-66).
purpose.why_it_exists: A compact assistant should float over other content and take a prompt without opening the full app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md S109.05). The code comment compares it to the ChatGPT and Claude companion windows (quickAsk.ts:43-47).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who want a fast question without switching windows; Chrome users who want a question about the page they are on.
problems_solved: Switching to the main app for a one-line question.
Losing the current context to open a full chat.
Page questions without leaving the page (Chrome).
use_cases: Press the Quick Ask key, ask for a command, Escape.
Ask a question, then follow a link in the answer that belongs in the main window.
In Chrome, click the launcher on a page and ask 'Summarize this'.
Open Quick Ask, then press the dictation key to speak the question (F109-04).

where_to_find_it: Desktop: global key default 'Alt+Shift+Space' (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:162); tray item 'Quick Ask' (F109-01); app menu items 'Quick Ask' (apps/desktop/electron/appMenu.ts:183,621); dock menu toggle (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:2622-2626). Settings row 'Quick Ask shortcut': 'Message AGI from anywhere on your desktop.' (DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:92-96).

Chrome: round launcher button with label 'Open AGI' and tooltip 'Ask AGI' (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/launcher.ts:114,120) and a panel with textarea placeholder 'Ask one question about this page…' and button 'Open in side panel' (apps/extension/src/features/content/in-page-panel/panel.ts, composer and footer built around lines 130-180).

features.summary: On AGI Desktop, a global key starts and stops dictation from any app: it speaks into Quick Ask or the main window composer, or, if switched on, into the app in front. On mobile the only established route is a widget or shortcut that opens the in-app voice screen. Chrome has none.

purpose.what_it_does: Desktop routes the key press to Quick Ask if visible, else a visible main window, else raises Quick Ask, and sends a toggle message to the page, which records and transcribes (apps/desktop/electron/voiceDictation.ts:34-49,58-78). With the setting on, a press over another app opens a small bar and types the transcript into that app (apps/desktop/electron/main.ts:1921-1930; apps/desktop/electron/dictationElsewhere.ts:89-170).
purpose.why_it_exists: Dictation should start from anywhere on the device without first opening the app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md S109.07). The spec describes it as an OS-global dictation shortcut (doc: docs/specs/desktop-global-voice/spec.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Desktop users who prefer speaking to typing; phone users reaching voice mode from the home screen.
problems_solved: Opening AGI and clicking the microphone before speaking.
Typing the spoken text into another app by hand (macOS, when the setting is on).
use_cases: Press the key over a browser, say a question, press again, and the text lands in the Quick Ask composer.
With 'Dictate into the app you are using' on, dictate an email sentence straight into the mail app.
On the phone, tap Voice on the home-screen widget to start voice mode.
Press the key while the main window is hidden: Quick Ask opens and starts listening.

where_to_find_it: Desktop: key default 'Alt+Shift+V' (packages/contracts/local-runtime/src/host-bridge.ts:166); tray item 'Dictation' (F109-01); settings row 'Voice shortcut': 'Speak to AGI from anywhere on your desktop.' and row 'Dictate into the app you are using' with its hint (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/DesktopSettingsSection.tsx:57-59,114-117).
Dictation bar page: /quick-ask/dictate (apps/web/app/quick-ask/dictate/page.tsx).
Mobile: widget button 'Voice', Android launcher shortcut 'voice', or link agiworkforce://intent/voice (see F109-05); Settings, Quick Access (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/index.tsx:715).
Chrome: none (brief: missing).

steps.what_happens: Global key calls dictateFromShortcut.
Target window is chosen and the composer focused; a toggle message is sent.
The page records audio from the microphone.
The recording is posted to /api/voice/transcribe.
The server checks kill switch, rate limit, 25 MB size, privacy setting and plan allowance, then calls an OpenAI speech-to-text model and settles voice minutes.
Text returns to the composer, or to the shell, which types it into the app in front once.

data.where_stored: In memory in the page; sent to the server and the transcription provider, dropped afterwards (comment: 'nothing stores' it, apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:467)
Composer draft on the device; typed into another app or on the clipboard

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: The transcription slot must resolve to a live OpenAI speech-to-text model, else the route throws (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:495-503). The provider folder is packages/ai/providers/openai. The model is chosen by the catalog slot, not by this feature. Mobile voice recognition runs on the device (voiceInput.ts:306-311); the reply model follows the app's mode (apps/mobile/app/(app)/voice.tsx:201,442).

access_and_usage.account: Desktop: signed-in account needed for the hosted page and for transcription. Mobile: voice screen is in the (app) area; sign-in need for Local mode was not traced.
access_and_usage.permissions: Microphone; macOS Accessibility for typing into other apps (main.ts:2256); the app-in-front lookup depends on the macOS helper [inferred].
access_and_usage.subscription: Voice minutes are metered per plan with a free allowance (apps/web/app/api/llm/v1/audio/transcriptions/route.ts:594-601). Exact per-plan numbers: unknown (not read).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit 'audio-transcription' (route.ts:294); 25 MB per file (route.ts:398); 10-minute bar session (dictationElsewhere.ts:51); voice_minutes allowance.
access_and_usage.flags: DICTATION_CAPABILITY kill switch (apps/web/app/api/voice/transcribe/route.ts:19-26); dictationEnabled setting; dictateIntoFocusedApp preference.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Speech-to-text model only; the slot must be an OpenAI STT model.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: The user's privacy setting can refuse the provider: 'Voice transcription uses a provider that may train on what you send...' (transcriptions/route.ts:506-515).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Desktop: this path posts to the server, so it needs the cloud; no local alternative found on this route (unknown for other desktop paths). Mobile: recognition is on the device, with a refusal rather than a quiet switch to server recognition (voiceInput.ts:306-311).

purpose.why_it_exists: Brief items: a home-screen widget that starts an action (S109.01) and a hardware button such as the iPhone Action Button that triggers AGI actions (S109.11) (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md). features.summary: On iPhone, saying 'Ask AGI Mobile' to Siri sends the question to AGI Cloud with a stored token and reads the answer aloud without opening the app. It must be switched on in Settings, Security and login, in Cloud mode. No headset-button code exists; headsets work only through Siri. Desktop, Chrome, Android: none.

purpose.what_it_does: An iOS App Intent posts the question to /api/mobile/intent/ask with a bearer token from the keychain; the server answers with one short model reply, charges usage, saves it as a chat and returns text that Siri speaks (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AskAGIIntent.swift:24-70; apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:116-255).
purpose.why_it_exists: The user should start talking to AGI from headphones, earbuds or a voice command without touching the phone (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md S109.13). The migration says the intent runs without the app open, so it has no identity session and needs its own token (apps/web/db/neon/0349_mobile_intent_tokens.sql header).
purpose.who_uses_it: iPhone users who use Siri by voice, including through connected earbuds [inferred].
problems_solved: Getting an answer when hands or eyes are busy.
Unlocking and opening the app for a quick question.
Running an AI request from Siri with the account's limits and policies applied.
use_cases: Say 'Ask AGI Mobile' then the question with earbuds on [inferred].
Run the Ask AGI shortcut from the Shortcuts app.
Open the saved chat later in the app to read the answer.

where_to_find_it: iOS only. In the app: Settings, 'Security and login', switch 'Ask from Siri' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/account-security/index.tsx:537,579; apps/mobile/src/features/siri/AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:59-71).
Siri phrases: 'Ask AGI Mobile', 'AGI Mobile answer my question', 'Talk to AGI Mobile' (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIAppIntents/AppShortcuts.swift) with the app name filled in by the system [inferred].
Setup guide: Settings, Quick Access, 'Siri & Shortcuts' (apps/mobile/src/features/widget-setup/index.tsx:169).
Android, desktop, Chrome: not present (apps/mobile/__tests__/WidgetSetupPage.test.tsx:91 says the Android guide makes no Assistant claims).
prerequisites: iOS (askFromSiriSupported is iOS only: apps/mobile/src/features/siri/askIntentToken.ts:113-115).
AGI Cloud mode and a signed-in account; in Local mode the switch is disabled with 'Needs AGI Cloud. Switch to Cloud mode to turn it on.' (AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:61-64,69).
Permission to share with AI providers (enableAskFromSiri calls ensureCloudSendConsent, askIntentToken.ts:188-193).
The phone registered to the account (apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent-token/route.ts:35-46).
screens_and_controls: Switch 'Ask from Siri' with description 'Ask AGI through Siri and hear the answer, saved as a chat.'
Alert titles 'Ask from Siri was not turned on' and 'Ask from Siri was not fully turned off' (AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:47-50).
Siri parameter 'Question' with prompt 'What do you want to ask?' (AskAGIIntent.swift:13-18).
journey: Switch on Ask from Siri in Cloud mode and allow sharing with AI providers.
The app asks the server for a token for this install and stores it in the keychain (askIntentToken.ts:144-170).
Say or type the question to Siri.
The intent trims it, refuses empty or over 2,000 characters, and posts it (AskAGIIntent.swift:44-56).
Siri speaks the answer; the same text is returned as the result (AskAGIIntent.swift:24-27).
feedback_and_outputs: Spoken answer.

Spoken errors: 'Ask a shorter question.', 'Ask from Siri is off. Open AGI Mobile in AGI Cloud, sign in if asked, and turn on Ask from Siri in Settings, Security and login.', 'Ask from Siri needs to be set up again...' on 401, server messages, or 'AGI Mobile could not answer right now. Try again in the app.' (AskAGIIntent.swift:33-37,43-69).
A saved chat titled by the first 60 characters of the question (mobile-intent.ts:38,60-96).
settings: Ask from Siri switch (storage key ask-from-siri-enabled-v1, askIntentToken.ts:27).
Token default model captured from the app's model choice at enable time (askIntentToken.ts:128-137).

working: Intent, shortcut phrases, keychain read and the HTTPS post (AskAGIIntent.swift:30-97). The Swift keychain service ends with ':no-auth', which expo-secure-store appends to the service when no authentication is required (apps/mobile/node_modules/expo-secure-store/ios/SecureStoreModule.swift:175), so it matches the TypeScript service name.
Token issue and revoke endpoints with CSRF check, rate limit, device registration check and audit events (apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent-token/route.ts:23-103).

Ask route: bearer token lookup, rate limit 6 per minute failing closed, MFA policy, IP allow list, body check, answer, error mapping (apps/web/app/api/mobile/intent/ask/route.ts:26-71; apps/web/lib/rate-limit.ts:112-116).

Server checks in order: account status, terms, adult eligibility, content moderation, secret handling, entitlement bundle, chat capability for the 'mobile' surface, managed compute access, route choice, cost estimate, usage reservation, model call, usage settle, conversation save with two attempts (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent.ts:123-255).

Token: prefix agi_it_, SHA-256 hash stored, one live token per install, 30 days, revoked on sign-out, switch-off or device removal, rotated on app launch (apps/web/lib/server/mobile-intent-tokens.ts:11-60; apps/web/db/neon/0349_mobile_intent_tokens.sql header).
Timeouts: server 50 s with maxDuration 60, phone 55 s (route.ts:17,20; AskAGIIntent.swift:51).
incomplete: Revocation and rotation race cases are source-reviewed only (doc: audit/registers/known-flaws.md:292-293, MOBILE-SIRI-ROTATION-RETRY-01 and MOBILE-SIRI-ROTATION-DISABLE-01).
A small window can leave a token on the device after a kill (doc: audit/registers/known-flaws.md:343 MOBILE-SIRI-TOKEN-KILL-WINDOW-01).
The server keeps no record of the provider-sharing permission and does not check it on this route (doc: audit/registers/known-flaws.md:205 WEB-PROVIDER-SHARING-SERVER-RECORD-01).
disconnected_or_disabled: In Local mode the switch cannot be turned on, but a token that is already on keeps answering through AGI Cloud (doc: audit/registers/known-flaws.md:342 MOBILE-SIRI-LOCAL-MODE-01; AskFromSiriSetting.tsx:61-69).
not_available: Headset or earbud button handling: no code found; nothing in apps/mobile/native handles media buttons (search of native, src, services found only voice audio-route files).
Android equivalent: none found.
Desktop and Chrome: not present (brief).

established.statement: The user can start talking to AGI from a headset or earbuds (button or voice command) without touching the phone or computer.
Ask from Siri sends the question to AGI Cloud; this is the one path where content reaches the managed cloud in Local mode, recorded as a deviation.
The ask route applies the account's workspace MFA and IP allow list to the token owner and answers nothing when refused.
The iOS intent must not promise where the AI runs.

acceptance_criteria: With Ask from Siri on in Cloud mode, 'Ask AGI Mobile' plus a question returns a spoken answer and a saved chat.
With the switch off, Siri says Ask from Siri is off and names Settings, Security and login.
An empty question or one over 2,000 characters is refused on the phone and by the server (400).
A revoked or expired token gives 401 and the 'set up again' message.
A request beyond 6 per minute is rate limited; a workspace needing MFA or limiting IPs is refused.
An account with no model access gets a 403 with a reason and no model call or usage reservation.
Turning the switch off revokes the token on the server.
inferred: Earbuds and headsets work only because Siri routes their voice command to the intent [inferred]; there is no AGI code for a headset button.
proposed: [proposed] Decide whether switching to Local mode turns Ask from Siri off (open owner question in MOBILE-SIRI-LOCAL-MODE-01).
[proposed] Add a server record of the provider-sharing permission and check it on this route.
[proposed] Decide if an Android equivalent is wanted.

steps.what_happens: Person turns on the switch; the app asks for consent and requests a token for this install.
Token is stored in the iOS keychain, readable after first unlock, this device only.
Siri runs the intent; it posts the question with the bearer token over HTTPS.
Server resolves the token, rate limits, checks MFA and IP, validates the body.
Server checks account, terms, age, moderation, secrets, plan and managed compute access, picks a route and reserves usage.
Server calls the model provider, settles usage and saves the chat.
The phone speaks the returned text.

features.summary: Remote Control lets a paid account pair a phone with a computer running AGI Desktop (or the AGI VS Code extension). The phone then follows coding sessions, reads diffs and answers the agent's approval requests. The computer owner must allow each phone. The phone side is switched off in the current mobile build.

purpose.what_it_does: The computer (Desktop app, or VS Code) asks our server for a short-lived pairing code and QR code. The phone scans it and claims the pairing through the same server. A relay then carries messages between the two. The phone can list coding sessions on the computer, start or interrupt a turn, read the working-tree diff and answer approval and question prompts [inferred from the host callbacks: listSessions, startTurn, interruptTurn, answerApproval, answerQuestion, readDiff, startSession] (apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:219-262).
purpose.why_it_exists: A person who starts a long coding task on a computer wants to leave the desk and still unblock the agent from a phone. The brief states that a desktop companion pairs with the phone so desktop work can be started, watched or approved from it (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md, S109.04).
purpose.who_uses_it: Paying users who run coding sessions in AGI Desktop or the VS Code extension and own the phone app. Free accounts are refused (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:352).
problems_solved: The agent stops and waits for an approval while the person is away from the computer.
No way to see how a long coding session is going from a phone.
Needing to be at the computer to send the next instruction.
use_cases: Start Remote Control on Desktop, scan the QR code with the phone, and approve a file change from the sofa.
Watch a test run and read the diff on the phone while the computer works.
Pair the VS Code extension so the phone gets a push when a session needs approval or finishes (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/remoteControlService.ts:141-152).

where_to_find_it: Web (inside the Desktop app window, which shows the hosted web app): Settings, Capabilities section, block headed 'Remote Control'. It renders only when the page runs inside the desktop host and the host supports it (apps/web/features/desktop-host/components/RemoteControlSection.tsx:37, :166-171; apps/web/features/settings/sections/CapabilitiesSection.tsx).
Desktop: a separate window titled 'Pair a phone' shows the QR code, the code text, 'Copy code' and 'Refresh code' (apps/desktop/electron/remote/pairingWindow.ts:14-22).

VS Code: command 'agi-workforce.remoteControl' (start or show), 'agi-workforce.stopRemoteControl', 'agi-workforce.copyRemoteControlLink', plus a status bar item (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/remote-control/index.ts:10-12, :139).

Mobile (hidden in this build): Settings, group 'Remote control', row 'Connections' opens the 'Remote control' screen; the companion screen is under app/(app)/companion. journey: 1. On Desktop (web settings page) or VS Code, the person presses 'Pair a phone'.

2. The app asks the server to create a pairing (POST /api/pair/initiate with initiator desktop) and gets a 12-character code, an expiry and a private token (apps/web/features/desktop-host/lib/remote-pairing.ts:34-60).
3. Desktop opens the 'Pair a phone' window with the QR code and the code.
4. On the phone, the person scans the QR code in the companion screen. The phone claims the pairing through POST /api/pair/claim (apps/mobile/services/manualPairing.ts:165).
5. The computer shows 'Allow this phone?' with the pairing code. The person confirms only if it is the phone they just used.
6. The phone lists sessions, opens one, sends a prompt or answers approvals.
7. If the agent needs an allow that the computer reserves, the computer opens a dialog and the phone is told to wait; the person has two minutes to answer there.
8. The person stops Remote Control (Disconnect phone, Stop Remote Control or Cancel pairing) to end it.

established.statement: A desktop companion pairs with the user's phone so desktop work can be started, watched or approved from the phone.
A pairing is refused when the screen-share switch is closed, the plan is not paid, or the plan cannot be read, and the refusal says why.
A pairing is rechecked while live, so it does not outlive the reasons that would have refused it.
Revoking a pairing must take effect on the next request, and the controlled device must show that it is being controlled for as long as it is.
The Remote Control feature is experimental, requires a desktop host, and is gated by entitlement 'developer_surfaces' and policy 'remote_control'.

acceptance_criteria: A free account pressing 'Pair a phone' (or calling POST /api/pair/initiate) gets a refusal with the paid-plan message and no code is created.
A paid account gets a code, expiry and QR; the code expires after 300 seconds by default, and a ttlSeconds outside 30 to 900 is rejected with 400.
With the screen-share switch closed, pairing is refused with the switch's message.
The computer shows 'Allow this phone?' with the pairing code before any session is shared; choosing 'Cancel' keeps the phone out.
An approval that the computer reserves is not applied until the computer owner allows it; after 120 seconds with no answer the phone is told nobody answered and the agent keeps waiting.
'Stop Remote Control' or 'Disconnect phone' ends the link and the phone can no longer read sessions.
With companion and dispatch flags false, no Remote control row or companion screen is reachable in the mobile build.
inferred: The phone side can only be accepted when the mobile flags are turned on in a future build; until then no end-to-end pairing with a real phone is possible in the shipped build [inferred].
A phone is limited to folders the agent may already run in on the computer [inferred from remoteRefusal].
proposed: [proposed] Show the remaining validity time of the code in the Desktop pairing window.
[proposed] Add a list of paired phones with a revoke button on the web settings page, not only a single Disconnect action.
[proposed] Decide and record whether pairing in Local mode is allowed at all, since it needs our servers.

steps.what_happens: Person presses 'Pair a phone'; the web page in Desktop posts to /api/pair/initiate with initiator desktop.
Server checks CSRF, sign-in, rate limit ('device-link'), workspace policy, plan and kill switch.
Server calls the signaling relay (SIGNALING_HTTP_URL, secret SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET) to mint code and tokens; 10 second timeout; refuses non-secure relay URLs.
Server marks the device remote_enabled and writes an audit event, then returns code, expiry, QR text and the desktop token.
Desktop host opens a WebSocket to the relay, draws the QR in a script-free window and waits.
Phone claims the pairing through /api/pair/claim; server asks the relay to mint the mobile token only for the same account.
Computer asks 'Allow this phone?'; if allowed, the phone's session requests are served after a per-folder check.
Messages between phone and computer flow through the relay; the agent runs on the computer with its own configured model.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Remote Control carries no model choice. It relays a coding session that the computer's agent runs; which model or provider that session uses is decided in the Desktop or VS Code session, not here (apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:219-262). Pairing itself needs our servers and so is not available in pure Local mode.

access_and_usage.account: A signed-in account is required on the web and computer side (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:46-60); the phone claim also needs the same account (apps/web/app/api/pair/claim/route.ts:35-47).
access_and_usage.permissions: The computer owner must allow each phone in a dialog; the phone reaches only folders the agent is approved for; allows reserved by the computer need a second dialog; credential paths are removed from diffs (apps/desktop/electron/remote/remoteControlService.ts:66-79, :255-258).
access_and_usage.subscription: Capability remote_control is allowed on the paid tiers basic, pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise; free is refused with code plan_upgrade_required (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:332-353; apps/web/lib/feature-flags/remote-control-gate.ts:57-80). The feature registry also names entitlement developer_surfaces (feature-registry.json:175-198).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit bucket 'device-link' on initiate; code lifetime 30 to 900 seconds; approval confirmation 120 seconds. No usage metering or credit use for pairing was found in the code (apps/web/app/api/pair/initiate/route.ts:63-107).
access_and_usage.flags: Mobile flags companion and dispatch (both false). Kill switch 'screen_share'. Workspace policy 'remote_control'. Environment names SIGNALING_HTTP_URL, SIGNALING_INTERNAL_SECRET, SIGNALING_PAIRING_TTL (names only).
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Not applicable; no model is chosen by this feature.
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: None found in the code.
access_and_usage.local_mode: Pairing needs our server and the relay, so it does not work offline or in a Local-only setup. The computer's own agent may still run on a local model; whether the relay works for such a session was not verified [unknown].

The phone shows 'This QR code was made by an older Desktop version...' and asks to update.

features.summary: On AGI Mobile, a person picks an on-device model in the model picker, confirms a download, watches progress, and can cancel. Settings, Storage lists each downloaded model with its size and a Delete button. Downloads need Wi-Fi unless the cellular switch is on, and need free space. CLI and VS Code have no equivalent.

purpose.what_it_does: Lists on-device models from a built-in catalog, downloads a chosen model file over HTTPS with a checksum check, records it as installed, and lets the person delete it later to free space (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts:432-566, :633-670).
purpose.why_it_exists: Local models are free of any subscription and work without our servers once downloaded, but the files are several gigabytes, so the person needs control over data use and storage. The brief requires browse, download with progress and pause or cancel, and a storage view with delete (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md, S109.18 and S109.19).
purpose.who_uses_it: Phone users who want private, offline or free chat on the device.
problems_solved: Surprise mobile-data bills from a multi-gigabyte download.
Failed downloads that fill the phone without warning.
Corrupt files: the file hash is checked.
No way to see what the models use or remove them.
use_cases: Download the default on-device model on Wi-Fi at home and chat offline later.
Cancel a download that was started by mistake.
Delete a model in Settings, Storage to free space before a trip.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: the model picker sheet and the 'Models' screen, where on-device models sit in a group titled 'On device' (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/components/ModelPickerSheet.tsx:937; apps/mobile/app/(app)/models.tsx:321). Settings, General, row 'Models' opens it (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx:176-182).
Mobile: Settings, General, row 'Storage' opens 'Storage' with 'Download over cellular' and 'Downloaded Models' (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/storage.tsx:389, :409).
Onboarding also shows the picker with local scope (apps/mobile/app/(public)/onboarding.tsx:476).
CLI and VS Code: not available (area brief S109.18, S109.19).
prerequisites: Enough free space: model size plus 256 MB headroom (modelDownload.ts:189, :213-227).
Wi-Fi, or the cellular switch on (modelDownload.ts:193-211).
No sign-in or plan check was found in the download code (apps/mobile/services/modelDownload.ts, whole file).
screens_and_controls: Model row: tap a model marked 'download required' to start; rows say 'Tap to download, long press to favorite', 'Model download is in progress', 'Tap to retry download' (ModelRow.tsx accessibility hints).

Confirmation alert 'Download <name>?' with 'Cancel' and 'Download'; on mobile data without consent the alert 'Wi-Fi needed' appears with 'OK' (apps/mobile/src/features/model-picker/downloadConfirmation.ts:29-70).
'Cancel download' button under a downloading row, accessibility label 'Cancel downloading <name>' (ModelRow.tsx:324-331).

Storage: switch 'Download over cellular' (hint 'Off waits for Wi-Fi. Models are several gigabytes.'), card 'Downloaded Models' with 'Estimated <size>' per model, trash button 'Delete <name>' (storage.tsx:385-451).
Delete confirmation 'Delete <name>?' with 'This removes the downloaded model files. You can re-download the model later.' (storage.tsx:246-249).
journey: 1. Open the model picker or Settings, General, Models.
2. Choose a model in the 'On device' group that is not downloaded.
3. Read the 'Download <name>?' alert (size, mobile-data note) and tap 'Download'.
4. The store checks network and free space, then downloads; the row shows a percentage.
5. Optionally tap 'Cancel download'; the row returns to 'download required'.
6. On finish the file hash is checked, the model is recorded as installed and the picker selects it.
7. Later, open Settings, General, Storage; tap the trash icon next to the model and confirm 'Delete'.
feedback_and_outputs: Progress percentage in the row; a 'Loading models…' indicator while installed models are read (ModelPickerSheet.tsx:355-358, :876-883).

Error texts: 'This download needs Wi-Fi. Connect to Wi-Fi, or turn on Settings, Storage, Download over cellular to use mobile data.'; 'This device is offline, so the download cannot start. Reconnect and try again.'; 'This model needs <size> free and this device has <size>. Free up space and try again.'; 'Integrity check failed for <name>. The downloaded file is corrupt. Please try again.'; 'Download was cancelled.' (modelDownload.ts:193-227, :522, :544).

Delete errors: 'Model removal failed' with 'This model is replying now. Try again when it finishes.' for ExecuTorch busy case, otherwise 'Could not remove the model. Refresh Storage and try again.' (storage.tsx:262-272; modelDownload.ts:68).
settings: 'Download over cellular' switch, stored as allowCellularDownloads in persisted store 'agi-model-install-v1', default off, and pushed to native code for the system model (installStore.ts:382-385, :639-641).
Model files are kept out of device backup (modelDownload.ts:100-107).

working: Download of a GGUF model file with HTTPS-only URL, SHA-256 hex check, resume data saved on failure, backup exclusion and install record (modelDownload.ts:120-170, :313-420, :432-566).
Optional vision projector file downloaded and verified with the model (modelDownload.ts:490-526).
ExecuTorch presets download through the same network and space gate (installStore.ts:521-545).
Cancel clears the job, bumps a generation counter so late progress is ignored, and pauses the download (modelDownload.ts:303-311; installStore.ts:597-612).
Storage screen lists installed models, estimated sizes, free space and cache, with retry on read failure and delete (storage.tsx:186-451).
Deletion removes the model directory only when the stored record still matches (modelDownload.ts:633-670).
incomplete: A cancelled download may not keep its resume data: on pause, the resume file is written only in the error path, while the cancel path throws before it (modelDownload.ts:341-388) [inferred]. Whether a cancelled GGUF download truly resumes later is not verified.

The 'model is replying' block exists for ExecuTorch models (releaseExecutorchPreset fails). deleteDownloadedModel for a GGUF model removes the folder without an in-use check (modelDownload.ts:633-670, :608-631) [inferred].
Sizes shown are estimates taken from catalog numbers, labelled 'Estimated' (storage.tsx:409-440).
getModelStorageBytes reads the size of a directory entry and may not give the real total; the Storage screen uses getDirectorySizeBytes instead (modelDownload.ts:672-676; storage.tsx:32) [inferred].
disconnected_or_disabled: Models with availability 'locked' or non-local surface do not start a download; they show a lock reason (installStore.ts:432-445).
Multimodal models are blocked on low-RAM devices with a stated reason (installStore.ts:117-134).
not_available: CLI: no download command; 'agi models' only lists, probes and sets models in local servers (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1861-1887).
VS Code: no on-device model download; its Local model note refers to Ollama and LM Studio running on the computer (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts:1600-1601).
Desktop and Chrome: not listed in the brief; no code was searched for them beyond the brief [unknown].

established.statement: The user can browse, download (with progress, pause or cancel) and install local models from inside the app.
The user can see how much space each local model uses and delete models to free storage.
Downloads check free space and Wi-Fi or cellular consent before they start.
Model files are excluded from device backup.
Failures are reported with a kind: wifi_required, offline, checksum_mismatch, storage_full, network_error, cancelled, already_installed.
Local inference on mobile is free of any paid subscription (project requirement stated in the task).

acceptance_criteria: On cellular with the switch off, choosing a download shows 'Wi-Fi needed' and nothing downloads.
With less free space than size plus 256 MB, the error names both numbers and nothing is written.
While downloading, 'Cancel download' returns the row to 'download required' and no model is marked installed.
A finished download whose file hash differs is deleted and 'Integrity check failed' is shown.
After a successful install, Settings, Storage lists the model with an estimated size, and Delete removes it and the picker stops saying ready.
Model files are marked excluded from device backup after a download.
Starting a second download of the same model while one runs is refused (already downloading).
inferred: Download needs no sign-in because the code has no account check [inferred]; a separate app-level gate (first-run age check or terms) might still apply and was not traced.

steps.what_happens: Person taps a model; the app asks 'Download <name>?' and checks whether the device is on mobile data.
prepareModel sets the job to 'downloading', reads the cellular consent and calls downloadModel.
Checks offline, Wi-Fi and free space (size plus 256 MB headroom) before writing.
File is fetched over HTTPS from the catalog URL (Hugging Face hosting in the catalog), resumable, in a model folder under the app's documents.
SHA-256 of the file is computed in chunks and compared with the catalog value; mismatch deletes the file.
A record is inserted into installed_models and the store marks the model ready; backup exclusion is applied.
Delete: Storage screen calls deleteDownloadedModel, then deleteInstalledModel and updates the store.

features.summary: On AGI Mobile, Settings, General, Performance shows the phone's RAM, thermal state, the local runtime tier it can use and what is loaded in memory. The person can load or unload an on-device model and run a benchmark. Errors from the local runtime become plain messages. CLI and VS Code only probe local servers.

purpose.what_it_does: Reads device capability (RAM, which system model runtime exists, whether the ExecuTorch tier is available), shows the tier and thermal state, lets the person load or unload a model, and runs a timed benchmark (apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/performance.tsx:74-110, :503-545).
purpose.why_it_exists: On-device models depend on phone hardware; people need to know what will run, free memory on demand and see why local chat fails. The brief lists a hardware panel, load and unload controls and runtime health (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md, S109.20-S109.22).
purpose.who_uses_it: Phone users running local models, and testers checking device support.
problems_solved: Not knowing why a local model will not run.
A loaded model holding memory.
Unclear failures such as heat or out-of-memory.
use_cases: Check whether a phone gets the system model, the hardware-accelerated tier or the general tier.
Unload models to free RAM before another app.
Run a benchmark after downloading a model.

where_to_find_it: Mobile: Settings, General, row 'Performance' (apps/mobile/src/features/settings/general/index.tsx:183-190). Screen header 'Performance' (performance.tsx).
CLI: 'agi models status' and 'agi models scan' (apps/cli/src/lib.rs:1868-1879) show local model servers, not on-device models.
VS Code: no load or health panel found; settings text only mentions Ollama and LM Studio (apps/extension-vscode/src/features/settings/settingsWebviewContent.ts:1600-1601).
prerequisites: A selected on-device model for Load and benchmark; a downloaded model for most (see F109-08).
System-managed models (built-in) need no load and show no button.
screens_and_controls: 'Device Tier' card: label 'Tier 1', 'Tier 2' or 'Tier 3' with description, rows 'RAM', 'Thermal', 'Capabilities' (performance.tsx:594-690).

'Active Model' card: model name, size or 'System managed', status line and button 'Load' or 'Unload local models'; accessibility labels 'Load model now' and 'Unload local models from memory' (performance.tsx:701-790).
Stat chips 'avg tok/s', 'avg TTFT', 'mem peak'.
'Benchmark This Device' card with button 'Run Benchmark' (shows 'Benchmarking…' while running) (performance.tsx:940-977).
Toggle 'Show performance chip in chat' (performance.tsx:1077).
journey: 1. Open Settings, General, Performance.
2. Read the tier card and the RAM and thermal rows.
3. In 'Active Model', tap 'Load' to put the selected model in memory, or 'Unload local models' to free it.
4. Tap 'Run Benchmark'; the app announces 'Running benchmark. Please wait.'
5. Read the last benchmark result.
feedback_and_outputs: Status text: 'Loaded in memory', 'Another local model is loaded in memory', 'Not loaded; an installed model loads on use', 'Working…', 'Managed by the system; availability is checked on use' (performance.tsx:732-753).
Load failure: 'Failed to load: Try again, or choose a smaller model.'; unload failure: 'Failed to unload: Wait for any active response to finish, then try again.' (performance.tsx:503-545).
Benchmark with no available model: 'Choose an available on-device model in Models before running a benchmark. Download it first if needed.' also announced to screen readers (performance.tsx:420-426).
AICore note: 'AICore is downloading its model. This device moves to Tier 1 when done.' (performance.tsx:67-72).

In chat, local failures read: 'Your device is too warm to run the on-device model. Let it cool down, then try again.' and 'This device ran out of memory for the on-device model. Close other apps, or choose a smaller model.' (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:1389-1416).
settings: 'Show performance chip in chat' stored under key perf-show-chip-v1, default on (performance.tsx:53, :309).
Model selection comes from the model picker (F109-08).

working: Capability detection: RAM and thermal flag from the system-model native modules, tier 2 available at 3500 MB or more (or unknown RAM with ExecuTorch present), tier 3 always (packages/platform/local-llm/src/capabilities.ts:4, :34-86; types.ts).
loadLocalModel, unloadLocalModels and loadedLocalModel in the local-llm package (packages/platform/local-llm/src/selector.ts:165-196).
Performance screen load and unload with busy guard, failure messages and live status (performance.tsx:503-545).
Benchmark records tokens per second, first-token time, peak memory and thermal state (apps/mobile/services/performanceMonitor.ts:123-170).
Plain-language local error mapping in chat (chatExecutionStore.ts:1371-1416).
Thermal refusal in the runtime: 'Device is thermally throttled, inference paused.' (selector.ts:36-38, :110-112).
incomplete: Thermal state shows only 'nominal' or 'serious', because getThermalState maps a single boolean (performanceMonitor.ts:42-44) [fair and critical values exist in the type but are not produced].
There is no separate 'runtime health' view; health is the tier card, thermal row and the Active Model status text [inferred].

The brief marks S109.22 done for CLI and VS Code, but the cited lines do not show health for on-device models: the CLI probes Ollama and LM Studio (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:175-290) and the VS Code lines cited in the brief are chat state code unrelated to health (ChatStateManager.ts:1441, :3863).
disconnected_or_disabled: No load button for system-managed models (fileSizeBytes 0), by design (performance.tsx:724-732, :761).
not_available: CLI and VS Code: no hardware panel and no load or unload of on-device models. CLI has a probe of local servers: Running, Unreachable, Faulty or Blocked per provider (apps/cli/src/local_models.rs:21-26, :377-402).
Desktop and Chrome: not covered by the brief.

established.statement: The app shows the device's hardware capability for local models (RAM, accelerators, supported runtimes).
The user can load a local model into memory and unload it to free resources.
The app shows whether the local model runtime is running and healthy, with errors when it is not.
Capabilities come from the local-llm package; loadedLocalModel reports what is in memory.
A benchmark without an installed model shows the 'Choose an available on-device model in Models...' message and announces it.

acceptance_criteria: The tier card shows Tier 1, 2 or 3 matching the device, with RAM in the 'RAM' row.
'Load' on a downloaded model changes the status to 'Loaded in memory'; 'Unload local models' returns it to 'Not loaded; an installed model loads on use'.
Load failure shows 'Failed to load' text in the live region; the button stays usable after.
'Run Benchmark' with no installed model shows the Models message and no result is saved.
A successful benchmark updates 'Last benchmark result' and is announced to screen readers.
With a throttled device, a local chat shows 'Your device is too warm to run the on-device model...'.
Buttons are disabled while a load, unload or benchmark runs.
inferred: System-managed models need no load control because the OS manages them [inferred from performance.tsx:724-732].
proposed: [proposed] Show all four thermal levels reported by the OS.
[proposed] Add a runtime health row that names the active runtime and its last error.
[proposed] Give the CLI and VS Code a clear 'on-device models are mobile only' statement rather than 'partial'.

features.summary: After each on-device reply, AGI Mobile records speed in tokens per second, time to first token, peak memory and thermal state. Settings, General, Performance shows averages, two seven-day charts and a benchmark result. An optional chip under replies shows the speed. CLI and VS Code have nothing like it.

purpose.what_it_does: Measures every local reply, stores up to 500 events, and draws them on the Performance screen as averages and charts (apps/mobile/services/performanceMonitor.ts:38-100; apps/mobile/app/(app)/settings/performance.tsx:795-935).
purpose.why_it_exists: Local model speed varies by phone, model and heat. People and testers need numbers to choose a model and to see slowdowns. The brief asks for speed, latency, memory and thermal state over time (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md, S109.25).
purpose.who_uses_it: Phone users on local models and engineers checking device performance.
problems_solved: No evidence why local chat feels slow.
Hard to compare models on one phone.
use_cases: See that replies slow when the phone warms up.
Pick a faster model after comparing tokens per second.
Hide the speed chip to keep chat clean.

Mobile chat: chip under an on-device assistant reply (apps/mobile/src/features/chat/components/MessageBubble.tsx:3115-3125).
CLI and VS Code: not available (area brief S109.25).
prerequisites: At least one on-device reply with more than one token (chatExecutionStore.ts:3138-3149).
Rows 'avg tok/s' show '--' until at least one event exists (performance.tsx:795-815).
screens_and_controls: Stat chips 'avg tok/s', 'avg TTFT', 'mem peak', and text 'Rolling average over last N inferences'.
Text 'The app is using NMB of memory now' refreshed every 2 seconds (performance.tsx:371-385).
Chart cards 'Tok/s, Last 7 Days' with 'N events' and 'First-Token Latency, Last 7 Days' (performance.tsx:889-935).
'Last benchmark result' block with tok/s, TTFT, mem peak and thermal.
Toggle 'Show performance chip in chat' with sublabel 'Shows tok/s under on-device replies' (performance.tsx:1077-1078).
journey: 1. Send a message with an on-device model selected.
2. When the reply completes, the app records one event.
3. Open Settings, General, Performance.
4. Read the averages and the two charts, or run a benchmark.
feedback_and_outputs: Averages over the last 100 events; charts over 7 days; chart accessibility labels such as 'Tokens per second over the last 7 days. N data points. Most recent: X t/s.' (performance.tsx:907, :930).
Chip under each local reply when the toggle is on.
settings: Toggle 'Show performance chip in chat' (key perf-show-chip-v1, default on).

working: One event is recorded per completed local reply when decode time is above zero and more than one token arrived: tokens per second equals count over decode time, rounded to 0.1 (apps/mobile/stores/chat/chatExecutionStore.ts:3138-3149).
First-token latency is the time from the start of generation to the first token (chatExecutionStore.ts:3143-3149).
Thermal state is recorded from getThermalState (performanceMonitor.ts:42-44).

Peak memory is now sampled once a second during the reply through native modules on iOS and Android and recorded (chatExecutionStore.ts:3094-3112, :3146; apps/mobile/services/processFootprint.ts:16-45; apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIFoundationModels.swift:117-129; apps/mobile/native/android/AGIAICoreModule.kt:85-89). The brief's note that peak memory stays 0 is out of date.
Events are stored in MMKV, capped at 500, filtered to 7 days for charts (performanceMonitor.ts:38-86).
Dashboard view exists: averages, charts and benchmark (performance.tsx:795-935). The brief's 'not sure' about a view is answered: it exists.
incomplete: Peak memory is the whole app's footprint, not the model's [inferred from phys_footprint and process PSS in the native code].
Tokens are counted per token callback, not by a tokenizer, so tokens per second is approximate [inferred from localTokenCount += 1 at chatExecutionStore.ts:3109].
First-token latency starts before the model loads, so it can include load time [inferred from localStartedAt at :3093].
Thermal state has only two values (performanceMonitor.ts:42-44).
If memory modules are missing, readMemoryFootprintMB returns null and peak stays 0 (processFootprint.ts:16-27).
No call to clearPerfData outside its definition was found, so there is no 'clear' control (performanceMonitor.ts:116).
disconnected_or_disabled: none found.
not_available: CLI and VS Code: no resource dashboard (area brief S109.25).
Cloud or server-side aggregation of local performance: none found.

established.statement: A dashboard shows local compute use: speed (tokens per second), latency, memory and thermal state over time.
Tokens per second equals tokens divided by decode time, rounded to 0.1.
The performance chip is controlled by a user toggle that defaults to on.

acceptance_criteria: After one local reply of several tokens, the Performance screen shows 'avg tok/s' with a number, and the chart card shows '1 events'.

After 500 events the oldest are dropped.
Peak memory shows a positive number on a device where the native module answers.
Running a benchmark adds a point to the last benchmark block.

steps.what_happens: A local turn starts a memory sampler and records start time.
The local runtime generates; each token callback records the first token time and increments a counter.
On finish the sampler stops and returns the peak.
Speed is computed and recordPerfEvent stores the event.
The Performance screen reads events and shows them.
