features.summary: A group of ways to reach AGI from outside the main apps. Slack is built in code: a signed event receiver and an assistant that answers direct messages and mentions, but it needs owner setup. Lock-screen widget, selected-text rewrite, phone calls, other messengers, wearables and spatial interfaces were not found in code.

purpose.what_it_does: Slack: after a workspace installs the AGI app and a person links their account, AGI answers direct messages and channel mentions in Slack on that person's plan (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant.ts:420-449; apps/web/db/neon/0330_slack_app.sql header). The other channels do nothing today.
purpose.why_it_exists: People want AGI where they already work or with hands free, as the leading assistants offer. The brief lists these as ambient extensions (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/109-optional-native-and-ambient-extensions.md, S109.02, S109.08, S109.12, S109.15, S109.16, S109.17).
purpose.who_uses_it: Slack: team members on plans that include 'Chat in Slack' (pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium, enterprise). Others: nobody yet.
problems_solved: Leaving the chat tool to ask AGI a question.
Agent approvals needed while in Slack (approval through web or desktop).
use_cases: Direct message AGI in Slack to summarise a thread.
Mention AGI in a channel and get a threaded answer or an AGI Work task.
Approve a tool step on the web page while Slack waits (apps/web/app/api/slack/runs/[runId]/approval/route.ts).

where_to_find_it: Web: Settings, section 'Slack' (apps/web/features/settings/sections/SlackSection.tsx; apps/web/features/settings/lib/web-settings-sections.ts:39). The owner installs from there; each person then links their Slack account through /slack/link (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-config.ts:30-31).
Slack itself: direct message the AGI app or mention it in a channel.
Mobile, desktop, CLI, VS Code, Chrome: no Slack screen found.

Lock screen: an iOS 18 control named 'Open AGI Mobile' says in its description that it can be placed on the Lock Screen, Control Center or Action Button (apps/mobile/native/ios/AGIWidgets/AGIWidgets.swift:90-99). It opens the app; whether it works on a locked phone is unknown.
prerequisites: Slack: Slack app created and configured by the owner; signing secret, client id and client secret set; NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL set to a secure origin; connector token storage available (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-config.ts:62-70).
Slack: a plan with 'slack_app' (pro or higher) (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:360; apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:415-421).
Slack: migration 0330 applied; the brief also says 0333 must be applied before deploy (apps/web/db/neon/0330_slack_app.sql; 0333_slack_run_cancel_and_delete.sql).
screens_and_controls: Settings, Slack: add to Slack, installed workspaces, channel policies, linked accounts, disconnect, approval decisions (SlackSection.tsx; apps/web/features/slack/components/SlackChannelPolicies.tsx).

In Slack: an 'eyes' reaction while working (slack-config.ts:50), a link message for unlinked people, notices such as 'AGI is turned off in this channel by the person who added it to Slack. You can still message it directly.' (slack-assistant.ts:50-51).
Settings messages: 'AGI was added to Slack. Send it a message there to start.' and 'AGI in Slack is not available right now.' (SlackSection.tsx:46-50).
journey: 1. The owner creates the Slack app and sets its secrets (owner task, per docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md section 3).
2. A workspace admin opens Settings, Slack and adds the app (one workspace at a time).
3. A person messages AGI in Slack and receives a link to connect their AGI account (15 minute link).
4. After linking, AGI replies in the thread; a tool step may wait for approval on web or desktop.
5. The person disconnects in Settings, Slack, which also deletes their run records.
feedback_and_outputs: Answers posted in Slack; 'I could not finish that answer. Please try again.'; rate limit notice 'You are sending messages faster than AGI can answer them. Wait a minute, then try again.'; plan notice 'AGI in Slack is available on <plans> plans.' with a 'See plans' link (slack-assistant.ts:49-55; slack-assistant-turn.ts:415-421).
settings: Per-channel mode and tools policy (slack_channel_policies, migrations 0374 and 0385).
Slack bot scopes are listed in code (slack-config.ts:12-20).

working: Slack events route: rate limit, 256 KB body cap, signature check that fails closed (503 when the signing secret is unset), url_verification, then answer and trigger ingest (apps/web/app/api/webhooks/slack/route.ts:21-129).
Assistant handles direct messages, mentions, uninstall and token revoke events (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-events.ts:57-99; slack-assistant.ts:420-449).
Install, OAuth callback, account link, runs approval and channel policy routes exist under apps/web/app/api/slack.
Answers run through managed cloud routing with plan and compute checks (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:334-437).

Tables slack_installations, slack_link_requests, slack_account_links, slack_assistant_runs, slack_channel_policies (apps/web/db/neon/0330_slack_app.sql:31-140; 0374_slack_channel_policy_and_agent_credit_cap.sql:28).
Nine test files in apps/web/lib/slack plus route tests exist.
incomplete: Setup depends on the owner: Slack app creation, secrets and applying migrations (brief; docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:296-320).
The brief cites apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:253 as the evidence for messaging; that route handles review requests, not chat. The real Slack code is the slack route and lib/slack.
The brief's status 'web partial' for Slack is based on the unfinished owner setup, not on missing code.
Teams, WhatsApp and Telegram chat access: no route found (a search of apps/web/app and apps/web/lib matched only connector catalog files and Microsoft Graph).
disconnected_or_disabled: Slack answers nothing until SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_SECRET and a secure app origin exist; Settings says the app is not set up (slack-config.ts:62-70; docs/runbooks/connector-oauth-apps.md:318-320).
Mobile, desktop and Chrome have no Slack entry.
not_available: Lock-screen widget (S109.02): no code found beyond the iOS control noted above.

Selected-text rewrite shortcut (S109.08): none found in Desktop; the 'selected_text' matches in desktop code belong to agentic event handling in the Tauri build, not a rewrite shortcut (apps/desktop/src/hooks/useAgenticEvents.ts:396).
Wearable voice (S109.12), telephone access (S109.15), spatial or XR (S109.17): no code found in desktop, mobile or web.
Other messaging platforms (Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram): not found.

established.statement: The phone lock screen can show an AGI widget or start an AGI action without unlocking.
Text selected in any app can be rewritten by AGI with a shortcut and the result put back in place.
The user can talk to AGI from a smartwatch or other wearable.
The user can reach AGI by calling or texting a phone number.
The user can talk to AGI from a messaging platform (Slack, Teams, WhatsApp, Telegram) and get answers there.
AGI offers a spatial or XR interface.

Slack bot scopes only; the owner creates the app, sets SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_SECRET and SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, subscribes to app_mention and message.im; migration 0333 applied before deploy.

acceptance_criteria: A Slack event without a valid signature gets 401; with the secret unset gets 503.
A direct message from an unlinked person gets a link message, not an answer.
A linked person on a plan below pro gets 'AGI in Slack is available on ... plans.'
A channel set to 'off' answers 'AGI is turned off in this channel...' only when mentioned, and runs nothing.
Disconnecting a Slack account deletes its run records.
Removing the app in Slack deletes the installation and its links.
For each unbuilt channel, no entry is shown anywhere in the apps.
inferred: Slack answers use the same plan, credits and model policy as web chat because they pass through managed cloud admission [inferred from slack-assistant-turn.ts:334-437].
proposed: [proposed] Mark S109.16 as 'built, awaiting owner setup' rather than partial.
[proposed] Ship a lock-screen widget family before wearables.
[proposed] Decide product scope for Teams, WhatsApp and Telegram before any build.

steps.what_happens: Slack posts an event to /api/webhooks/slack; the server rate-limits, caps size and verifies the signature.
The route acknowledges at once and schedules the assistant work after the response; it also offers the event to the trigger ingest.
The assistant finds the installation, resolves the person's AGI link and the channel policy, and records a run.
The turn checks plan 'slack_app', admits a managed cloud route, checks compute access, then calls the model.
The answer is posted back to Slack with the bot token.
A step needing approval is parked; the person decides on web or desktop; the run resumes.

execution_and_data_flow.models_and_providers: Slack answers use managed cloud routing and the person's plan model policy; the model is chosen by the route admission, not by Slack (apps/web/lib/slack/slack-assistant-turn.ts:334-437, :45-50). No on-device model takes part. The other channels have no model path.

access_and_usage.account: Slack needs an AGI account linked to the Slack user; the app is installed once per Slack workspace by an AGI account (apps/web/db/neon/0330_slack_app.sql header).
access_and_usage.permissions: Slack bot scopes limited to those in slack-config; channel owners set per-channel mode and tools; approvals by the linked account.
access_and_usage.subscription: Capability slack_app, label 'Chat in Slack', allowed on pro, max, max_15x, team, team_premium and enterprise (packages/contracts/types/src/billing-catalog.ts:360, :418). Refusal code slack_plan_required (slack-assistant-turn.ts:415-421).
access_and_usage.limits_and_metering: Rate limit 'trigger-webhook' on the endpoint; per-person answer rate limit; body 256 KB; context limits in SLACK_CONTEXT_LIMITS; agent credit cap migration 0374; managed usage accounting is imported by the turn (slack-assistant-turn.ts:60-75).
access_and_usage.flags: Readiness depends on environment names SLACK_SIGNING_SECRET, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_ID, SLACK_APP_CLIENT_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (names only). No feature flag found.
access_and_usage.model_compatibility: Whatever the managed route admits for the plan; some models may be refused when the plan keeps chats out of training (slack-assistant-turn.ts:128).
access_and_usage.provider_restrictions: Content-safety and training opt-out checks apply to the managed route (slack-assistant-turn.ts:45, :53, :125-128).
access_and_usage.local_mode: Slack is a Cloud feature and has no Local mode. The unbuilt channels have none either.

features.summary: A document the assistant writes in chat opens in the Artifacts panel. On web it can be edited in a rich editor and saved as a new version. On the phone it is edited as plain Markdown source. The assistant can also make real Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV files, which appear as file cards.

purpose.what_it_does: Two linked jobs. (1) Chat to editable document: a Markdown document the assistant writes becomes a stored artifact. On web the person edits it in a rich text editor, or as Markdown source when the text cannot survive a round trip, and each saved change adds a version (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/ArtifactDocumentEditor.tsx:21-22, 53-72; packages/platform/artifacts/src/artifact-store.ts:69-120). (2) Document to presentation: the assistant calls one server tool that builds a real .pptx from an ordered slide outline, and can also build .docx, .xlsx, .pdf and .csv (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts:138-188, 233-260). Web also has an in-app deck artifact (Markdown slides) with its own editor (apps/web/features/chat/components/artifacts/presentation/PresentationWorkspace.tsx).
purpose.why_it_exists: Competing assistants let a person work on a written answer like a document and ask for a real file. Without this, answers stay as chat text. The requirements document lists Markdown documents, spreadsheets and presentations among artifact types and 'slide deck ... export where the generated format supports it' (doc: docs/product/requirements.md:1440-1448, 1488).
purpose.who_uses_it: People on web and the desktop app (which shows the hosted web app, doc: AGENTS.md section 5) who write or revise documents and decks; people on the phone who receive generated files; Chrome extension users who receive generated files in the side panel.
problems_solved: A chat answer cannot be tweaked without copy and paste
Edits would overwrite the assistant's text with no history
People need a file they can send (Word, PowerPoint) instead of chat text
A document with unsupported formatting would be corrupted by a rich editor
use_cases: Ask for a project brief, open it, fix a paragraph in the rich editor, press Save to keep it as version 2
Pick Output > Presentation in the web composer and ask for a 10 slide pitch; open the .pptx card
Upload a Word file and ask the assistant to replace text in it, keeping the other parts of the file
On the phone, open a generated deck from a Project's 'Slide deck' output and share the file

established.statement: A document the assistant writes in chat opens as an artifact the user can edit as a document and save back as a new version.
A document (chat artifact or uploaded file) is turned into a presentation the user can open and keep working on.
A document opens in the rich editor only when its text survives a round trip; otherwise it opens as Markdown source with a notice.
A saved content change adds the next version and older versions stay listed.
A deck is built from an ordered outline of at most 40 slides.
The office tool edits an existing Word or Excel file; a PowerPoint file cannot be the source.
Presentations, reports and images are versioned objects.

acceptance_criteria: Given a Markdown document with only headings, lists, tables and links, 'Edit document' opens the rich editor and 'Save' adds exactly one version.
Given a document containing math, a footnote or raw HTML, the editor shows Markdown source and the notice text.
Pressing 'Save' with unchanged text adds no version; 'Cancel' leaves the stored artifact unchanged.
Reloading during an edit offers the kept draft and the toast 'Restored your unsaved edits to this artifact'.
Choosing Output > Presentation and asking for a deck returns a .pptx card with no more than 40 slides.
Attaching a .docx and asking for a wording change returns a new .docx and leaves the original attachment untouched.
On a Free plan chat the Output row is disabled.
On mobile in Local mode the 'Create file' row is not shown.

A deck made in chat should keep editing after it is exported as a file [inferred from S110.02 'keep working on']

features.summary: A person attaches a spreadsheet and asks for analysis, a chart and a Word report. Code running in a cloud sandbox can read the file and draw charts. The office file tool can write Excel files that contain native charts. Putting that chart inside a Word report has no direct tool; it depends on sandbox code and an unverified template.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets the assistant read an uploaded .xlsx, compute on it, draw a chart, and deliver files. Two routes exist. Route A: the managed office tool writes or edits Excel files and can add a bar, line or pie chart drawn from the sheet's own cells (apps/web/lib/services/managed-office-file-service.ts:81-91, 163-188; managed-workbook-builder.ts:5-17, 97-113). Route B: the cloud code sandbox runs Python on the staged attachment and may save a chart image or a Word file (apps/web/lib/e2b/attachment-staging.ts:1-12; apps/web/lib/e2b/python-figure-provenance.ts:1-40).
purpose.why_it_exists: Competing assistants analyse spreadsheets and return charts and reports. Data work needs real computation, not a model guess.
purpose.who_uses_it: Analysts and office workers on web and Desktop (hosted web app); phone users who see chart artifacts.
problems_solved: Models cannot reliably calculate on large tables without running code
A chart should be a real object, not text
Reports need the chart inside the document

A chart-into-Word request returns a .docx that contains the chart image (to be verified live).
On the phone, a chart artifact renders as a chart, not as raw JSON.
On the Free plan the request is refused or the toggle is off.

features.summary: In live voice, the voice model can hand a goal to the chat as an AGI Work task, or make a Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF or CSV file that appears as an 'Open' link or card. Works on web (and desktop through the hosted app) and on the phone in Cloud mode. CLI voice only turns speech into a typed prompt.

purpose.what_it_does: Gives the live voice session two tools. 'agi_work' hands a goal to the chat client, which sends it as an AGI Work turn (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tools.ts:343-362, 400-402; apps/web/features/chat/lib/live-voice-session.ts:746-770). The office file tool builds a document and the session lists it as an openable file (apps/web/lib/voice/live-voice-tool-runner.ts:151-190; apps/web/features/chat/components/Voice/VoiceModeSurface.tsx:471-500).
purpose.why_it_exists: Competing assistants let a person talk and have work done. Retyping a spoken request defeats voice mode.
purpose.who_uses_it: People who talk to the assistant on web, Desktop or the phone; terminal users who dictate.
problems_solved: Spoken requests for long work need a durable run, not a spoken answer
A spoken request for a document needs a file
Voice sessions end; the task must outlive them
use_cases: Say 'research competitors and write me a report' and a background AGI Work task starts in the chat
Say 'make a one page PDF of these notes' and tap 'Open'
On the phone, ask for a spreadsheet and open it with the system share sheet
In the terminal, press push-to-talk, review the text, send it to the agent

journey: 1. Start voice mode; the app opens a live session and passes the list of client hand-offs.
2. Speak the request.
3. For long work the voice model calls 'agi_work' with the goal. The tool needs approval (requiresApproval true). The server replies it was handed off.
4. The client starts a work-mode send into the chat with the goal; the session shows 'An Work task started in the chat for: <goal>...' as a note (live-voice-session.ts:763-767).
5. For a document the voice model calls the office tool; the server builds it and returns a file with a link under /api/files.
6. Tap 'Open' (web opens a new tab; phone downloads then opens the share sheet).
7. The work task continues in the chat after the call ends.

established.statement: A request made in voice mode becomes a durable AGI Work task (runs in background, tracked in Tasks) without the user retyping it.
A spoken request produces a document (docx, pdf, markdown artifact) the user can open from the voice session.
The voice model gets the work task tool only when the client listed it and the plan has agi_work; the office file tool is in the list when tools are allowed.
If the work task fails to start the user is told.
Live voice must be separate from dictation; if unavailable the UI says so without broken controls.
The app says whether audio is local or provider/cloud.

acceptance_criteria: On a plan with agi_work, speaking a multi-step request starts one work-mode send in the chat with the spoken goal.
On a plan without agi_work the voice model is not offered the task tool.
If the chat cannot send, the voice model is told the task did not start.
A spoken request for a PDF yields an 'Open' link that opens the file.
The 'Open' link appears only for /api/files paths.
On the phone in Local mode live voice is unavailable with the stated reason.
CLI /voice in a Local session without a local speech program and without the opt-in refuses to send audio to the cloud.

steps.what_happens: Client creates a live session, sending the list of client hand-offs ('agi_work' when it can start a work task).
Server checks sign-in, plan voice allowance, tenant, billing hold; picks the live model from the voice_live routing slot; builds the tool list.
Audio flows between the device and the live voice provider over a real-time connection created by the server.
The voice model calls a tool; the client posts it to the tools route; approval is applied for write-risk tools.
For agi_work the server only returns 'handed off'; the client then starts a work-mode send with the goal in the chat.
The chat turn runs as an AGI Work request on our servers (work_mode agiwork).

features.summary: After finishing work in chat, a person can turn it into a reusable skill (web, desktop, CLI) or a scheduled routine (web menu, CLI). On web and desktop the model writes a draft card with Save buttons; nothing is stored until the person saves. Turning a custom assistant into a plugin does not exist in any app.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets a person capture a task they just finished as something reusable. On web and desktop the model proposes a plugin or skill in a draft card, and the person saves it into their Skills. On web the message menu can also open the Schedules form with the earlier prompt filled in. On the CLI, slash commands tell the agent to write a SKILL.md file or to create a hosted schedule.
purpose.why_it_exists: Claude and ChatGPT let people keep a good workflow instead of retyping it. The brief lists the Should lines as: after a task the user saves it as a Skill that appears in Skills; after a task the user turns it into a scheduled routine; the user converts a custom assistant into a plugin (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.14, S110.15, S110.16).
purpose.who_uses_it: Web and desktop chat users on an account that may author skills; CLI users; people with a plan that allows scheduled tasks (routines).
problems_solved: Retyping the same instructions for repeat work
Keeping a working method in a form the model loads later
Running the same task on a clock without opening the app
use_cases: After a research chat, press Save as skill in the message menu, review the draft card, press Save as a skill.
Ask in chat to turn the work into a plugin with two skills, then press Save plugin.
On the web, choose Run this on a schedule on an answer and finish the Schedules form.
In the CLI after a fix, type /save-routine every weekday at 9 and approve the cron_create call.

where_to_find_it: Web and desktop (the desktop window shows the hosted web app, AGENTS.md section 5): the three-dots menu on an assistant message has 'Save as skill' and 'Run this on a schedule' (apps/web/features/chat/components/messages/MessageBubble.tsx:4050-4060). The draft card appears under the assistant reply (MessageBubble.tsx:2956).
Web and desktop: saved skills open at Settings > Skills; a saved plugin opens at Settings > Plugins through the Open link on the card (PluginDraftCard.tsx:64-68).

established.statement: After a task completes, the user saves it as a reusable Skill that appears in their Skills and can be invoked later.
After a task completes, the user turns it into a scheduled routine that later runs the same work on its schedule.
The user converts an existing custom assistant into a plugin with instructions, knowledge and tools carried over, and installs or shares it.
Nothing is saved until the user presses a save button.
The draft card is offered only on web and desktop.

acceptance_criteria: On web, with skill authoring on, an answer's menu shows 'Save as skill'; choosing it makes a draft card with a 'Save plugin' button and, for one skill, a 'Save as a skill' button.
Pressing 'Save as a skill' creates the skill, shows 'Saved as a skill. It is on in your chats.', and the skill is listed in Settings > Skills.
Before any button is pressed, no skill or plugin exists for that draft.
With AGI_USER_SKILL_AUTHORING=0 the menu item and the card are not offered and POST /api/skills is refused with 'Skill authoring is not available.'.
In a temporary chat the 'Save as skill' menu item is absent.
On a free account the 'Run this on a schedule' menu item is absent; on a plan with a nonzero allowance it opens /chat/schedules with the prompt filled in.
In the CLI in Managed mode, /save-routine leads to a cron_create call that creates a schedule; in Local or BYOK mode the call is refused with the not-managed message.
A failed save shows 'This draft could not be saved. Try again.' and the draft stays unsaved.
inferred: A routine made from a finished task should store a prompt that works without the chat; the CLI prompt says so explicitly (claude_parity.rs:901-908) [inferred as the requirement for web too].
Plugin conversion should carry instructions, knowledge and tools, per the brief; no field model for an old custom assistant was found, so its source data is unknown.
proposed: [proposed] Show the saved skill's name in the card and link to it in Settings > Skills (the card already links by name for skills).
[proposed] Let the draft card also save a routine, so web matches the CLI's one-step routine creation.

[proposed] Add a draft-card equivalent on mobile, VS Code and Chrome, or record a decision that they stay out, as the VS Code and Chrome decisions record other omissions (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:362, 391).

steps.what_happens: Person asks for a skill/plugin or picks 'Save as skill'; the browser sends a streaming chat request.
The server checks surface, tool-capable model, streaming, non-temporary chat, skill authoring switch and workspace gates, then adds draft_plugin to the model request.
The chosen model (platform route or the user's own key) writes the draft by calling the tool; the server validates it and returns it to the client.
steps.evidence: plugin-draft-tool.ts:107-143 (validation on our servers); the model call itself goes to the model provider [inferred from the chat-completions route]

steps.what_happens: The card renders from the tool result; the person presses Save, the browser posts to /api/plugins/authored or /api/skills.
The server stores the skill (table user_skills) and the card shows the saved state.
Web routine: the browser navigates to the Schedules page with the prompt in the URL; the person finishes and saves the schedule.
CLI: the prompt goes to the active model; the agent writes SKILL.md in the project folder, or calls cron_create, which posts to /api/schedules.

aliases: Email and GitHub mentions start tracked work
features.summary: A new email (Gmail trigger) or an @agi-workforce comment on a GitHub issue or pull request starts an agent run on our servers. Gmail triggers are currently refused because connectors are marked coming soon. GitHub mentions start a review or a cloud coding session and reply on GitHub, but only when sandbox switches and the installation's review setting are on.

purpose.what_it_does: Turns an outside event into tracked agent work. A Gmail trigger runs a saved schedule's prompt for each new message in a connected mailbox. A GitHub mention by a repository member starts a pull request review or a cloud coding session and posts progress and the result back as a comment.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants an email thread to become a tracked agent task, and a team mention to open a coding session that the team can follow and whose result posts back (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.10, S110.11). The founder decision says neither leader offers an address to forward email to an agent, so no forward address is built (doc: docs/decisions/2026-09-27-founder-decisions.md:164-168).
purpose.who_uses_it: Individuals and teams with a connected Gmail account (when released) or a GitHub App installation on their repositories.
problems_solved: Copying email content into chat by hand
Asking for code changes or reviews from inside GitHub without opening the app
Giving the team one place (the session link) to follow the work
use_cases: A routine summarises every new email from a mailbox.
A maintainer writes '@agi-workforce fix the failing check' on a pull request.
A reviewer writes '@agi-workforce' alone on a pull request to start a review.
A team follows the linked cloud session from the issue comment.

GitHub: comment on an issue or pull request in a repository where the AGI GitHub App is installed (apps/web/app/api/github/webhook/route.ts:200-266).

Mobile, Chrome: not found. VS Code: no email intake found; the cited localRuntimeClient lines are a thread-reconnect schema (apps/extension-vscode/src/integrations/localRuntimeClient.ts:1150-1165).

GitHub: the comment itself; replies are posted by the bot as issue comments.
journey: Email: create or choose a schedule (its prompt describes the work).
Open the triggers panel, choose Gmail, enter the mailbox address, save. The server starts a Gmail watch (api/triggers/route.ts:101).
Gmail pushes a notice to our Pub/Sub endpoint; the server lists new inbox messages and ingests one event per message (webhooks/gmail/route.ts:49-95; gmail-watch.ts:414-440).
A background job creates a schedule run with the event data appended to the prompt as data, and the agent runs (trigger-fire.ts:59-75, 85-160).
The run appears in the schedule's run history; the trigger delivery is marked fired, filtered, failed or dead (trigger-fire.ts:110-195).

GitHub: a member comments '@agi-workforce <task>' on an issue or pull request. The webhook verifies the signature, drops duplicates and bots, checks the commenter's standing, then queues a review (empty text or a review request on a pull request) or a coding task (route.ts:70-266).

The bot comments 'AGI Code is working on this. Follow along or step in here:' with the session link, then posts the final message and opened pull request number, or a pause, stop or failure message (cloud-code-github-task.ts:61-75, 289-345).
feedback_and_outputs: GitHub comments with the session link and result (TASK_COPY strings, cloud-code-github-task.ts:61-75).
Webhook JSON replies such as {received:true, task:'queued'} or review:'queued' (route.ts:261-267).
Trigger delivery statuses and run history in the schedule (trigger-fire.ts:110-195).

Per-installation pr_review_enabled column (cloud-code-github-task.ts:191-206).

steps.what_happens: Gmail sends a mailbox-changed notice to Google Pub/Sub, which pushes it to POST /api/webhooks/gmail with a signed token.
The server verifies the token against the configured audience and service account, decodes the notice (mailbox and history id only).
For each trigger on that mailbox, the server lists new inbox messages through the owner's Gmail grant (metadata and snippet) and ingests one event each.
A background job loads the trigger, creates a schedule run, appends the event block to the prompt and runs the scheduled-agent executor.
The agent works with the model route set for the schedule; the result lands in run history and the delivery is settled.
GitHub sends a webhook; the server verifies x-hub-signature-256, records the delivery id once, and routes the comment event.
The server checks sender and commenter standing, then runs a review or a coding task in the background (after()), calling GitHub's API with an installation token.
A cloud coding session runs in a managed sandbox; the final changes are committed, pushed and a pull request is opened; the bot comments the result.

aliases: Local work to explicit cloud handoff (S110.22)
features.summary: A coding session can run in a managed cloud sandbox on a GitHub repository. A local session can be handed to it from the CLI (agi code handoff) or from VS Code (Code: Continue in the Cloud), and a cloud branch can be brought back with agi resume --teleport or VS Code's Bring the branch in. It works only when managed Code is switched on. Design-to-code and review decks are not built.

purpose.what_it_does: Runs a coding agent in a cloud sandbox on a repository branch, lets the person follow it on web, mobile, CLI or VS Code, approve its steps, open a pull request, and move work between the local checkout and the cloud.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants an explicit local-to-cloud hand-off, a cloud result brought into the local checkout with review, a design implemented in the user's repo and a repository turned into a review deck (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.12, S110.13, S110.22, S110.23). The cloud parity spec says cloud sessions must match Claude's (doc: docs/specs/agi-code-cloud-parity/spec.md).
purpose.who_uses_it: Developers on a plan that includes AGI Code, on a repository hosted on GitHub.
problems_solved: Long coding tasks tying up a laptop
Continuing a terminal session somewhere that keeps running
Getting a cloud branch into the local editor without copy and paste
use_cases: From the CLI: push the branch, run agi code handoff, review what moves, confirm.
In VS Code run 'Code: Continue in the Cloud', type a task, confirm the review.
On web open /code, pick a repository and start a task.
In VS Code pick a cloud session and choose 'Bring the branch in'.

Changes and commit routes also check e2bProvisioningReady (changes/route.ts:32; commit/route.ts:47).

established.statement: The user explicitly hands a local coding session (history, repo state, pending work) to cloud execution and it continues in a cloud session.
A cloud session's result (diff, branch or files) is brought into the local checkout from a product control, with review before applying.

A local session sent to the cloud starts a new cloud session from the pushed branch with a new task, as claude --cloud does; history comes back only when a cloud session is pulled local. VS Code S110.22 is met at parity once cloud sessions are on.
A cloud session's result comes local through the CLI and VS Code; the desktop app adds no native pull.
A cloud session is refused when sandbox switches are off, and when managed compute is switched off.
CLI hand-off sends only a Managed session, and refuses Local or BYOK sessions with an explanation.

acceptance_criteria: With switches off, POST /api/code/sessions returns the 'Managed Code is not enabled for this deployment' error and the VS Code and CLI actions show a refusal.
With switches on and a plan that includes AGI Code, starting a session on a repository returns a session with a branch.
agi code handoff with unpushed commits stops and tells the user to push first.
agi code handoff from a Local-mode session refuses and names /continue-with-cloud.
agi code handoff of a Managed session shows what moves and what stays, then creates a session; uncommitted changes produce the warning.
agi resume --teleport in a checkout with uncommitted changes refuses and asks to commit or stash.
In VS Code, Bring the branch in with local changes asks before switching and does nothing if declined.
In VS Code, Continue in the Cloud when signed out shows 'sign in to AGI Cloud to continue work in the cloud'.
inferred: The brief's 'review before applying' for S110.23 is met only partly by a dirty-tree confirmation; a diff view of the cloud result before checkout is not present [inferred from index.ts:87-133].
Web should show a visible reason when managed Code is off; the sessions list returns availability.deploymentEnabled and planEntitled for that (code/sessions/route.ts:57-62) [inferred use].
proposed: [proposed] Add a review step (diff summary) before Bring the branch in.
[proposed] Show the same what-moves and what-stays review on web and mobile when they gain a hand-off.
[proposed] Treat design-to-code as a record-or-build decision per app, as the CLI has already ruled it out.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets work follow the person across devices: a web chat shows on the phone and replies sync back; a terminal coding session is listed and resumable in the desktop app and in VS Code; the phone can send a task to a paired computer under that computer's approvals.

purpose.who_uses_it: Signed-in people with more than one AGI app; developers who switch between terminal, desktop and editor.

steps.what_happens: Web or mobile writes messages; mobile marks them for sync and the loop pushes them to POST /api/chat/sync.
The server gate checks workspace policy and stores rows with a server_version.
The other device pulls rows with server_version greater than its cursor, in pages, and advances the cursor.
Desktop or VS Code starts the CLI as a local app server and asks it to list or resume threads.
Phone dispatch (switched off) would pair via a relay host and send the task to the computer, which asks for approvals locally.

features.summary: When usage runs out the apps show the next step: switch model if one is eligible, wait or be notified at reset, buy credits, upgrade, or use your own key. When a connected account expires, a connect or reconnect card appears and the person sends the request again, because the turn is not resumed automatically (by decision).

purpose.what_it_does: Turns a refusal into a way forward. The server sends a structured refusal (reason, reset time, recovery action, optional alternative model); the app renders a card or banner. For connectors, the tool result carries a connect request with a link so the person can reconnect and ask again.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants one-step recovery from usage exhaustion and a reconnect prompt when a connected account expires mid-task (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.26, S110.27).
purpose.who_uses_it: Anyone who hits a plan or free-lane limit, and anyone whose connected app login has expired.
problems_solved: A dead-end error when usage is gone
Not knowing when the limit resets
Silent tool failures after an expired connection
use_cases: A free user hits the daily limit on one model and presses 'Switch to <model>'.
A paid user presses 'Buy credits' or 'Notify me when it resets'.
A chat tool call says Gmail needs reconnecting; the user presses Reconnect Gmail and sends the message again.
A CLI user sees a hint to run agi usage or use their own provider.

features.summary: A published artifact keeps its link when republished; each publish records a version and an older version can be put live again. A viewer can save a copy of a shared artifact or continue a shared conversation as a private chat. In workspace settings a user can share projects (read-only or can-edit), artifacts, conversations and connectors; skills are not shared there.

purpose.what_it_does: Lets people publish an artifact at a link, update it in place with a history they can roll back, unpublish it, let viewers copy or fork what was shared, and share their own resources with their workspace.
purpose.why_it_exists: The brief wants versioned updates in place, private forks of public creations, workspace sharing with access levels, and a viewer-authorized connected app (doc: knowledge-base/data/area-briefs/110-cross-product-experiences-to-include-in-the-product-map.md, S110.17, S110.28, S110.29, S110.30).
purpose.who_uses_it: Creators who publish artifacts or apps; viewers of shared links; workspace members and sharing managers.
problems_solved: Sending a new link for every edit
Fixing a bad update without losing the old one
Viewers wanting to keep and extend what they saw
Teams needing a shared place for projects and artifacts
use_cases: Republish an artifact and keep the same URL.
Put an older version live from Settings.
Open a shared chat link and press 'Open in AGI' to continue it privately.
Share a project with the organization as read-only.

established.statement: A published output is updated in place: the user changes it, republishes to the same link, and the new version is recorded and reversible.
A viewer of a public or shared creation can make a private copy in their own account and continue it.
A user explicitly shares a resource they own (project, conversation, artifact, skill) into their workspace with an access level, and members find and open it.
A viewer opening a shared artifact or app signs in with their own account so the app uses the viewer's connected services with their permissions.
Unpublish cannot be undone and deletes visitor data.
Artifacts that use connected apps are refused on public shares.

acceptance_criteria: Publishing the same artifact twice keeps the same token and URL and adds a second version.
The history lists versions newest first and marks exactly one as 'Live now'.
'Put live' on version N makes the public page show version N's content and adds a new version; the older versions remain.
Unpublish asks for confirmation, then the link stops working.
A signed-out viewer pressing 'Save a copy to my chats' is sent to sign in; a signed-in viewer ends in a new chat containing the artifact.
Opening /chat/from-share/<token> signed in creates a new conversation with the shared messages; an expired share shows 'This shared conversation has expired.'
Sharing a project with the organization as read-only is visible to members; 'Stop sharing' removes it.
An artifact that uses connected apps cannot be published at 'Anyone with the link' and shows the public-share message.
inferred: A restored version should keep the same visibility and token [inferred from the update statement at published-artifact-service.ts:513-519].

Skills should be shareable to a workspace per S110.30, but no entry exists; the plugin directory may carry workspace skills through a workspace_plugin marker (apps/web/features/plugins/server/directory/workspace-skill.ts:1-12) [inferred, not opened further].
proposed: [proposed] Add skills to workspace sharing or record that workspace plugins are the route.
[proposed] Mirror 'Put live' on mobile for published versions.
[proposed] Run a live end-to-end check of a viewer-authorized connected app on a non-public share.

steps.what_happens: The client posts the artifact to /api/artifacts/publish; the server checks ownership, content size and policy, upserts the publication and records a version.
A viewer opens the link; the server renders it (sandboxed for html and react kinds).
Put live: the server reads the snapshot, prepares the publication, rewrites the row and records a version in one transaction, and logs an audit event.
Save a copy: the viewer's browser creates a conversation and saves the artifact as a message through the normal chat API.
Continue a shared chat: the browser reads /api/share/<token>, creates a conversation, and posts the messages in batches; on failure it deletes the partial conversation.
A viewer-run app calls the runtime routes as the signed-in viewer; the model call runs with the viewer's connected apps if the publisher declared them and the share is not public.
